mflorin@newscorp.com (Michael Florin, Investor Relations, News Corp)

notes: Aged 95; avoid succession topics. Corporate comms at News Corp is the only published route; no personal office contact found.

name: Warren Edward Buffett
current_role: Director, Berkshire Hathaway (stepped down as CEO at end-2025 and as chairman in Sept 2026; Greg Abel is CEO, Howard Buffett chairman)
profile: The 'Oracle of Omaha' turned failing textile maker Berkshire Hathaway, which he took control of in the 1960s, into a conglomerate spanning insurance (GEICO), BNSF railroad, Berkshire Hathaway Energy and big stakes in Apple and others. He handed the CEO role to Greg Abel on Jan 1, 2026, gave up the chairmanship in Sept 2026, and continues giving most of his fortune away.
interesting_fact: As a high-school sophomore in 1945 he and a friend spent $25 on a used pinball machine for a barber shop; they soon had machines in three Omaha barber shops and sold the business in 1947 for $1,200.
deep_cut_fact: On his first income-tax return, in 1944 at age 13, he took a $35 deduction for the use of his bicycle and watch on his paper route.
notes: Age 96; notoriously does not use email and has no social accounts; Berkshire has no PR department. Only realistic route is a letter to Berkshire's Omaha office. Energy angle: Berkshire Hathaway Energy (utilities, PacifiCorp, MidAmerican). Also a lifelong ukulele player (Wikipedia).

name: Greg Brockman
current_role: Co-founder and President, OpenAI (also leads product strategy since May 2026, plus AI infrastructure)
profile: North Dakota-raised programmer who left Harvard/MIT to join Stripe, becoming its first CTO (grew it from 4 to 250 people). Co-founded OpenAI in 2015; his stake made him a multi-billionaire. In 2026 he took charge of OpenAI's unified product team (ChatGPT, Codex, API) alongside its compute/data-center buildout.
interesting_fact: Won a silver medal at the 2006 International Chemistry Olympiad and was the first North Dakotan Intel Science Talent Search finalist since 1973.
deep_cut_fact: His first-ever paid job was an acting gig: as a scrawny ninth grader he auditioned to be a marching tin-soldier extra in a Mannheim Steamroller Christmas concert in Grand Forks. After high school he took a gap year and wrote ~100 pages of a first-principles chemistry textbook, still unfinished on his site.
notes: Publishes his own email on his homepage (obfuscated as greg [at] gregbrockman [dot] com). Very active on X as @gdb. Strong fit for AI compute/data-center topics (oversees OpenAI infrastructure). 'substack' entry is actually his personal blog.

name: Chen Tianshi
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Cambricon Technologies (SSE: 688256)
profile: Born 1985 in Nanchang, Chen entered USTC's gifted 'Special Class for the Young' as a teen and earned a CS PhD by 2010. After research at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Computing Technology, he co-founded AI-chip maker Cambricon in 2016 ('China's Nvidia'); its shares soared from 2024 on demand for domestic AI accelerators.
interesting_fact: Cambricon grew out of academic papers co-written by Chen and his elder brother Chen Yunji; both entered USTC's gifted-youth program and had CS doctorates by 24. The CAS Institute of Computing Technology still holds a minority stake.
deep_cut_fact: He was lead author of 'DianNao' (ASPLOS 2014), an early deep-learning accelerator paper reporting ~118x speedup and ~21x energy savings vs a SIMD CPU; his ICT homepage lists it as an ASPLOS'14 Best Paper Award winner, and it seeded Cambricon's chip line.
notes: No published IR/press email found on company site; investor contact is via Shanghai Stock Exchange (688256) disclosures. Media-shy; rarely gives interviews.

name: Gennady Timchenko
current_role: Founder/owner, Volga Group (private investment firm); Chairman of the Board, Kontinental Hockey League (KHL); President, SKA Saint Petersburg
profile: Russian billionaire (born 1952, Leninakan/Gyumri) who co-founded oil trader Gunvor in 1997 and built Volga Group, which holds major stakes in gas producer Novatek and petrochemical group Sibur. A close Putin associate, he is sanctioned by the US (2014) and EU/UK (2022); he sold his Gunvor stake the day before US sanctions hit.
interesting_fact: In 1998 he co-founded the Yawara-Neva judo club in Saint Petersburg (with the Rotenberg brothers; Putin is honorary president), and he has chaired the KHL hockey league since 2012.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an electrical engineer (Leningrad Mechanical Institute, 1976) and started in 1977 at the Izhorsky plant near Saint Petersburg, which built power generators; as a child he lived in East Germany (1959-65) and learned German.
notes: Sanctioned by US, EU and UK; outreach/interviews may raise legal/sanctions-compliance issues for the podcast. Contacts are for the Elena and Gennady Timchenko Foundation (Moscow), not him personally. Volga Group has no reachable public press contact found.

name: Henry Nicholas III
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Broadcom; founder of the Henry T. Nicholas, III Foundation and backer of Marsy's Law for All
profile: Electrical engineer (UCLA BS/MS/PhD) who worked at TRW and PairGain before cofounding fabless chipmaker Broadcom with Henry Samueli in 1991. He took it public in 1998 and stepped down as CEO in 2003; Broadcom's later merger with Avago drives his wealth. He now focuses on crime-victims' rights via Marsy's Law, named for his sister, and on education philanthropy.
interesting_fact: A music enthusiast, Nicholas has said his inspiration for Broadcom came from Pink Floyd lyrics; Broadcom itself was started in 1991 in a spare bedroom of his Redondo Beach home.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 he co-founded the Nicholas Academic Centers with retired Orange County Superior Court Judge Jack K. Mandel to give academic support to under-resourced Santa Ana high schoolers; he has given $57.7M and the centers have graduated 2,070 students, nearly all going on to post-secondary education.

public_contacts.value: Ted Varipatis, Serra Public Affairs - ted@serrapublicaffairs.com (press contact listed for Marsy's Law campaign)

notes: Has had widely reported legal/drug issues (2008 indictment later dismissed; 2019 Las Vegas case) - avoid. Best route is via the Marsy's Law for All organisation / its PR firm; the press contact found is on the Maine campaign page. His PhD (UCLA) was awarded in 1998.

name: Andrey Melnichenko
current_role: Founder of EuroChem (fertilizers) and SUEK (coal); left both boards in March 2022 and stepped back as beneficiary after sanctions
profile: Belarus-born Russian industrialist who started with a campus currency-exchange booth, co-founded MDM Bank at 21 (1993), then built fertilizer giant EuroChem and coal/energy company SUEK through MDM Group. Sanctioned by EU/UK/US in 2022, which he disputes; his wife became trust beneficiary of the stakes. Holds UAE citizenship since 2021.
interesting_fact: His Philippe Starck-designed Sailing Yacht A, the world's largest sail-assisted yacht, was frozen by Italian authorities in Trieste in 2022; he also collects Impressionist art including Monet.
deep_cut_fact: Studied physics at Moscow State University. At 14 he was evacuated after Chernobyl; he later called that his 'freest and most interesting summer' and wrote in The Economist (2026) it taught him 'a complex system containing enormous amounts of energy does not forgive miscalculation or arrogance.'
notes: Sanctioned by EU, UK and US (2022) - check legal/compliance before any engagement. Best route is the Andrey Melnichenko Foundation media inbox (foundation also runs the Mendeleev Chemistry Olympiad support). Has written essays for The Economist on energy/civilisation, so is open to long-form media.

name: Wang Chuanfu
current_role: Founder, Chairman and President, BYD Company Ltd.
profile: Chemist-turned-entrepreneur born 1966 in Wuwei, Anhui, who founded BYD in Shenzhen in 1995 as a rechargeable-battery maker. BYD entered autos in 2003 and is now the world's largest plug-in/EV maker, also making batteries (FinDreams/Blade), buses, energy storage and electronics; Berkshire Hathaway was an early investor (2008).
interesting_fact: Before BYD, Wang was general manager of a Shenzhen battery venture set up in 1993 by his Beijing research institute; he left in 1995 to found BYD at 29 with a CN¥250,000 loan from his cousin Lu Xiangyang.
deep_cut_fact: BYD's very first employee card, issued in 1995, belongs to Wang himself, bearing employee number 00001. He studied metallurgical physical chemistry at Central South University (grad. 1987) and earned a master's at the Beijing Non-Ferrous Metal General Research Institute (now GRINM) in 1990.
notes: SEC insider match (Lion Group Holding LGHL chairman/CEO) appears to be a different person with a similar name; ignore it. BYD IR email db@byd.com is the board-secretary/IR mailbox listed on CNInfo (Shenzhen exchange). Wang rarely gives Western interviews.

name: Jason Chang CS
current_role: Chairman, ASE Technology Holding (Taiwan; world's largest chip packaging & testing group)
profile: Jason Chang Chien-sheng (b. 1944, Shanghai; family from Wenzhou) cofounded Advanced Semiconductor Engineering (ASE) in Kaohsiung in 1984 with his brother Richard and built it into the world's largest outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider, now ASE Technology Holding (NYSE: ASX), a key player in advanced packaging for AI chips. He holds Singapore citizenship.
interesting_fact: Educated at National Taiwan University (BS) and the Illinois Institute of Technology (MS) before building ASE; Hurun lists him under China but he is Taiwanese-Singaporean.
deep_cut_fact: In September 2015 he received a SEMI Award recognising his 'significant achievements in the development and commercialization of copper wire in the IC assembly process' - an industry-wide switch from gold to copper bonding wire that ASE pushed early.
notes: Aged 82 and low-profile; skipped the June 2025 AGM. Hurun lists country as China but he is Taiwan-based with Singapore citizenship. Best route is ASE corporate PR/IR. corp_comms@aseglobal.com also published on the contact page.

name: Vinod Shantilal Adani
current_role: Dubai-based investor; runs a family investment office; part of the Adani Group promoter group (no formal executive title)
profile: Born 1949 in Gujarat, Vinod Adani is the elder brother of Gautam Adani. He started a textile business in Mumbai, traded commodities from Singapore from 1989 and has lived in Dubai since 1994, where he runs a family investment office. He is a Cypriot citizen, and the Adani Group lists him as a member of its promoter group.
interesting_fact: The IIFL Wealth Hurun India Rich List 2022 named him the richest NRI (non-resident Indian) and the sixth-richest Indian overall.
deep_cut_fact: He started out on his own long before Dubai. In 1976 he founded a textile business, VR Textile, in Mumbai, then moved to Singapore in 1989 to trade commodities.
notes: Very private: he keeps a low profile and has no public website or social accounts. He is central to the 2023 Hindenburg allegations and earlier DRI probes, so outreach is sensitive. If attempted at all, the realistic route is the Adani Group corporate communications office. Net-worth figures vary widely by source.

name: Dang Yanbao
current_role: Chairman, Ningxia Baofeng Energy Group (Shanghai-listed coal-to-chemicals/olefins producer); controlling holder of Baofeng Energy Storage
profile: Born 1973, Dang worked in building materials, trading and investment before founding Baofeng Energy in Ningxia in 2005, turning coal into olefins and other chemicals. In 2025 Baofeng started a $6.7B Inner Mongolia olefins plant, lifting capacity to 5.2M t/yr; a sister firm began trial output at a 100GWh battery/storage plant in Yinchuan in 2024.
interesting_fact: Baofeng's Inner Mongolia coal-to-olefins complex, which started up in 2025 at a cost of about $6.7 billion, is among the largest olefins plants in the world, raising company capacity to 5.2 million tons a year.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Yanchi County, Ningxia, and in 2011 he and his wife set up the Ningxia Yanbao Charity Foundation for education and poverty relief; by 2021 it had financially helped about 256,700 young students (he gave RMB 302M to it in 2019).
notes: IR email is the board-secretary/securities affairs contact listed in Baofeng Energy's 2025 interim report summary (China Securities Journal). Chinese-language outreach recommended; low international media profile.

name: Philip Anschutz
current_role: Owner, Chairman and CEO, The Anschutz Corporation (Denver); owner of Anschutz Entertainment Group (AEG)
profile: Kansas-born Denver billionaire who built fortunes in oil (from 1960s Wyoming wildcatting), railroads (Southern Pacific), telecom (Qwest), real estate and entertainment. Through AEG he owns 70+ arenas/venues, the LA Kings and a Galaxy stake; his Power Company of Wyoming is developing the Chokecherry and Sierra Madre wind project with the TransWest Express transmission line.
interesting_fact: On 320,000 acres of his Wyoming ranch land he is building one of the world's biggest wind farms (Chokecherry and Sierra Madre, ~3 GW), paired with a transmission line to carry the power to the Southwest.
deep_cut_fact: His early oil career was saved by Hollywood: when his Wyoming well near Gillette caught fire in the late 1960s, he sold Universal Studios exclusive rights to film the blaze for its John Wayne/Red Adair movie 'Hellfighters' for $100,000, which paid Adair to put it out.

public_contacts.value: mroth@aegworldwide.com (Michael Roth, AEG VP Communications, per Jan 2025 release)

notes: Famously private; has given almost no interviews in decades. The Anschutz Corporation publishes no press contact; AEG communications is the only published route. Energy angle: Chokecherry/Sierra Madre wind + TransWest Express line. Kool-Aid stand anecdote (age 6) in Forbes bio.

name: Huang Shilin
current_role: Co-founder and ~9-10% shareholder of CATL (left vice-chair/board in Aug 2022); reported chairman of Contemporary Nebula Technology Energy (CNTE, Fujian)
profile: Huang Shilin (b. 1967) co-founded battery giant CATL with Robin Zeng and was its vice chairman until resigning in August 2022 to pursue solar-storage, charging and inspection businesses. He remains CATL's third-largest shareholder (~10% before a ~1% block sale in Nov 2025) and is linked to CNTE, a CATL-affiliated energy-storage/charging-station maker in Fuzhou.
interesting_fact: When he quit CATL in 2022, the company said he would explore solar, energy storage, charging and inspection businesses and might form 'strategic synergy' with CATL in future; CATL holds ~20% of CNTE, the storage/charging firm he chairs.
deep_cut_fact: He and CATL chairman Robin Zeng (Zeng Yuqun) were high-school classmates; a Hefei University of Technology graduate, Huang was R&D director at Dongguan ATL (Amperex) and Ningde ATL before co-founding CATL.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal accounts found. The listed email is CNTE's general company inbox (not personal). CATL's English contact page blocks scripted access; CATL IR via catl.com investor pages.

name: Harold Hamm
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Continental Resources (private since 2022); founder of the Hamm Institute for American Energy at Oklahoma State University
profile: Oklahoma sharecroppers' son who turned a water-hauling trucking business into Continental Resources, pioneering horizontal drilling and fracking in North Dakota's Bakken. He took Continental private in a 2022 buyout. Now focuses on energy policy and the Hamm Institute, which in 2026 got Google.org funding for research on reliable power for AI.
interesting_fact: Hamm was the 13th and youngest child of Oklahoma cotton sharecroppers. In 2012 Time named him one of the world's 100 most influential people, and he was Mitt Romney's energy adviser that year.
deep_cut_fact: Hamm started work at 16 at a gas station, then mucked out oil tanks at a refinery. He founded his first company, Shelly Dean Oil Co. (later Continental), in 1967, and went back to finish college at Phillips University in Enid only after he struck oil.
notes: Strong fit: the Hamm Institute now does research on powering AI/data centers. The press email (Kristin Thomas, Continental's SVP/Chief Communications Officer) comes from a 2018 release, so check it is still current. Politically prominent (major Trump fundraiser); 2026 reports linked him to an oil trade-association role and interest in a U.S. Senate seat.

name: Jason Chang
current_role: Chairman (and CEO per company releases), ASE Technology Holding Co. (TWSE: 3711, NYSE: ASX)
profile: Taiwan-born, Singapore-based co-founder of ASE, the world's largest outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider, which he started with brother Richard in 1984. ASE (incl. SPIL and USI) is a key advanced-packaging/heterogeneous-integration supplier for AI chips. The brothers also invest in real estate developer Sino Horizon.
interesting_fact: He founded ASE in 1984 betting early that the rise of the fabless model would let Taiwan become a global IC manufacturing hub; the company lacked technology and resources in its early years but he kept investing heavily in advanced packaging R&D.
deep_cut_fact: Trained as an engineer: electronics engineering degree from National Taiwan University and an M.S. in industrial engineering from the Illinois Institute of Technology; National Cheng Kung University gave him an honorary doctorate in July 2022 (ASE and NCKU have collaborated on packaging R&D since 2012).
notes: Low public profile; route via ASE corporate PR/IR. Avoid succession topics (his son Rutherford, a presumed successor, died recently).

name: Edwin Chen
current_role: Founder & CEO, Surge AI
profile: Edwin Chen founded Surge AI in 2020 to supply high-quality human data, RL environments and evals for training frontier AI models. Bootstrapped with no outside funding, Surge passed $1B+ revenue in 2024 with under ~100 staff (customers include Google and Anthropic); Chen owns an estimated ~75%. Earlier he was a data/research scientist at Twitter, Google and Facebook.
interesting_fact: At MIT, where he studied math, computer science and linguistics, Chen researched how to decode the Inca khipu, a 'language' recorded via knots tied in rope.
deep_cut_fact: As a Twitter data scientist in 2012, Chen mapped geotagged tweets to show where Americans say 'soda', 'pop' or 'coke' (soda on the coasts, pop in the Midwest, coke in the South); the post on his personal blog went viral via Bloomberg, Gizmodo and FlowingData.
notes: Does long-form podcasts (Lenny's Podcast Dec 2025, 20VC, No Priors) — receptive to podcast format. Strong views on AI benchmarks, RL environments and anti-'blitzscale' company building; press@surgehq.ai is the published press route.

name: Khalif bin zayed an Nahyas
profile: Listed name matches Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the UAE and Ruler of Abu Dhabi (2004-2022), who died on 13 May 2022. Record skipped per instructions.
notes: Died 13 May 2022 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khalifa_bin_Zayed_Al_Nahyan). Caveat: the listed 'S B K Holdings' (SBK Holding) is the private holding company of his eldest son Sheikh Sultan bin Khalifa Al Nahyan (https://sbkholding.com), so the Hurun 2014 entry may conflate father and son. If the journalist wants the living SBK owner, research Sultan bin Khalifa separately.

name: Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan
profile: Former President of the UAE and Ruler of Abu Dhabi (2004-2022). Died 13 May 2022, aged 73; succeeded by his half-brother Mohamed bin Zayed.
notes: Deceased 13 May 2022 (source: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/uaes-long-ailing-leader-sheikh-khalifa-bin-zayed-has-died). Not a viable podcast guest.

name: Paolo Rocca
current_role: Chairman of Techint Group and Chairman of Tenaris (stepped down as Tenaris CEO in May 2026, succeeded by Gabriel Podskubka).
profile: Milan-born (1952) grandson of Techint founder Agostino Rocca, Paolo Rocca runs the Italo-Argentine Techint conglomerate (Tenaris seamless steel pipes for oil & gas, Ternium steel, engineering). As CEO from 2002 he merged mills in Argentina, Italy, Mexico and Japan into the NYSE-listed Tenaris brand. Wealth is shared with his brother Gianfelice Rocca.
interesting_fact: He took Tenaris through more than two decades as CEO, unifying acquired pipe mills across several countries under a single global brand listed in New York; in 2013 Columbia Business School gave him its Deming Cup for operational excellence.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business, in the late 1970s he settled on a remote farm in Chubut, Patagonia, raising sheep and living austerely; he also worked as an executive assistant at the World Bank before formally entering Techint in 1985.

public_contacts.value: Tenaris Media Relations team contact (via Media resources page)

notes: Input name was just 'Paolo' (Techint, shared with Gianfelice Mario Rocca) = Paolo Rocca. Low public profile; best route is Tenaris/Techint media relations. Was indicted in Argentina's 2018 'cuadernos' graft case — avoid in outreach.

name: Kwong Siu-hing
current_role: Largest shareholder (via family trust) of Sun Hung Kai Properties; former SHKP chairman (2008–2011)
profile: Kwong Siu-hing (鄺肖卿, b. 1929) is the widow of Kwok Tak-seng, who co-founded Sun Hung Kai Properties in 1958 and died in 1990. Through a family trust she controls the largest stake in SHKP, one of Hong Kong's biggest property developers, and she is long ranked Hong Kong's richest woman. She chaired SHKP from 2008 to 2011; her son Raymond Kwok is now chairman.
interesting_fact: She left Guangdong for Hong Kong in 1947 and married Kwok Tak-seng at 20. Sun Hung Kai, which he started with Fung King-hey and Lee Shau Kee in 1958, went public in 1972 and became one of Hong Kong's largest developers.
deep_cut_fact: Her ancestral home is Huashan town in Hua County (now Huadu District, Guangzhou). According to the SCMP, before becoming SHKP chairwoman at 78 in 2008 she 'had never sat on the board of a Hong Kong company'.
notes: She is about 96 and entirely private, with no public role or interviews; she is not a realistic podcast guest. Any approach would go through SHKP corporate communications. Avoid family-feud topics.

name: Jaime Gilinski Bacal
current_role: Head of the Gilinski Group (Banco GNB Sudameris, Grupo Nutresa control stake, Panama Pacifico real estate); listed as Grupo Nutresa chairman since 2024
profile: Colombian banker and developer (Georgia Tech industrial engineering, Harvard MBA, ex-Morgan Stanley M&A) who built a Latin American banking empire through acquisitions, including Banco Andino and GNB Sudameris. In 2021–24 he won control of food giant Grupo Nutresa after a long takeover battle, and co-develops Panama Pacifico on a former US Air Force base.
interesting_fact: In the 1990s he bought the Colombian assets of collapsed BCCI for a nominal sum, rebuilt them as Banco Andino, and sold it about four years later for a reported $70 million.
deep_cut_fact: Before banking he spent nine years building consumer-products and snack-food businesses in South America; the family group still owns Yupi snacks. He sits on the International Advisory Board of Oxford's Blavatnik School of Government, and funds an HBS fellowship for Colombian and Panamanian MBA students.
notes: Lives primarily in Panama/London; private, rarely interviewed in English. No dedicated Gilinski Group press contact found. Nutresa control story is contentious in Colombia (rivalry with GEA) — avoid. Fellowship HBS detail from Wikipedia.

name: Enrique Razon Jr.
current_role: Chairman and President, International Container Terminal Services Inc. (ICTSI); chairman of Bloomberry Resorts (Solaire) and Prime Infrastructure Capital (Prime Infra)
profile: Enrique 'Ricky' Razon Jr. turned the Manila port business his grandfather started in 1916 into ICTSI, a global terminal operator spanning Asia-Pacific, Africa, Europe and the Americas. He also built the Solaire casino resorts and, via Prime Infra, has moved into utilities and energy: Manila Water, the Malampaya offshore gas field, gas-fired plants bought from the Lopez Group in 2025, and large solar-plus-battery projects.
interesting_fact: Razon left school at 17 to take a minimum-wage job in the family's cargo-loading business and worked his way up through the ranks.
deep_cut_fact: Associates describe him as a former junior golfer whose real handicap is closer to two than the six he claims; he set up the Philippine Golf Tour Foundation, and one of his favourite sports is kiteboarding.

public_contacts.value: https://ictsi.com/contact (routes General / Investor Relations / CSR inquiries)

notes: Rarely grants interviews. Energy angle is strong (Prime Infra: Malampaya gas, gas plants, MTerra Solar solar+storage). investor@ictsi.com and info@ictsi.com appear as routing addresses in ICTSI's contact form source; foundation@ictsi.com is for ICTSI Foundation/CSR.

name: Mikhail Fridman
current_role: Co-founder of Alfa Group; shareholder (no board role) in Luxembourg-based investment group LetterOne
profile: Lviv-born co-founder of Alfa Group (Alfa-Bank, Alfa-Eco) who made his fortune in banking, telecom and oil, including the TNK-BP venture sold for $14bn in 2013. Sanctioned after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, he stepped back from LetterOne, sold his Alfa-Bank stake in 2025 and has spent 2025-26 fighting EU sanctions and seeking compensation for frozen assets.
interesting_fact: He lived in Western Ukraine until he was 17 and has called Lviv, where his parents lived, his 'favorite city'; in 2011 he founded the Alfa Jazz Fest there.
deep_cut_fact: As a student at the Moscow Institute of Steel and Alloys he washed windows and co-founded a student discotheque called 'Strawberry Fields', and organised students to queue for theatre tickets used to barter for scarce goods.
notes: Highly sensitive subject: sanctioned (UK; EU status contested/partly lifted in 2026 per reports), on Ukraine's wanted list, litigation against several states. No published personal/office contact found; he no longer has a formal LetterOne role. Reputational risk for outreach.

name: Murali Divi
current_role: Founder and Managing Director, Divi's Laboratories Ltd (Hyderabad)
profile: Pharmaceutical scientist (PhD, Kakatiya University) who worked in US specialty-chemical firms before founding Divi's Research Centre in 1990, which became Divi's Laboratories, now one of the world's top three makers of active pharmaceutical ingredients plus custom synthesis and nutraceuticals, with ~90% of revenue from exports. Divi's is investing in peptides including GLP-1 ingredients.
interesting_fact: A fitness fanatic, he built a yoga center at Divi's headquarters in Hyderabad and spends weekends at his organic farm near the city.
deep_cut_fact: His first career step was as a trainee at Warner Hindustan in 1975; before starting Divi's he partnered with Dr. Kallam Anji Reddy (later Dr. Reddy's founder) to acquire Cheminor Drugs in 1984.
notes: Low-profile, rarely gives interviews. Company general inbox is the only published route.

name: George R. Roberts
current_role: Co-Executive Chairman and co-founder, KKR & Co. Inc. (Menlo Park/San Francisco)
profile: Houston-born George Roberts co-founded leveraged-buyout pioneer Kohlberg Kravis Roberts in 1976 with his cousin Henry Kravis and Jerome Kohlberg, after the trio's 'bootstrap' deals at Bear Stearns, where he made partner at 29. He and Kravis handed the CEO roles to Joe Bae and Scott Nuttall in 2021 and remain co-executive chairmen; KKR is now a major infrastructure and data-center investor.
interesting_fact: He founded and chairs REDF (Roberts Enterprise Development Fund), a pioneer of 'employment social enterprise' that funds businesses hiring people facing major barriers to work; he has also given $190M to Claremont McKenna ($50M in 2012, $140M in 2022).
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from Culver Military Academy in Indiana in 1962 and the school named him its 'Man of the Year' in 1998; he still serves as a Culver trustee.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews (Kravis is the public face). Best route is KKR media relations. Data-center/energy angle: KKR is a big investor in digital infrastructure and energy transition.

name: Sarath Ratanavadi
current_role: Founder and CEO, Gulf Development PCL (Thailand)
profile: Thai engineer often called Thailand's 'energy king' and its richest person. He founded Gulf Electric in 1994 during power-sector liberalisation, grew Gulf Energy Development into a major IPP, took it public in 2017 and in 2025 merged it with telecom holding Intouch (AIS) to form Gulf Development, spanning power, telecom, data centers (JV with Singtel) and a Kasikornbank stake.
interesting_fact: Gulf Energy's 2017 IPO raised over 25 billion baht, Thailand's biggest IPO in a decade; Gulf later co-launched a crypto exchange in Thailand with Binance.
deep_cut_fact: A keen golfer and former managing director of the Thailand Golf Championship, he opened Stonehill, a 340+ acre private golf club outside Bangkok designed by architect Kyle Phillips, in 2022.
notes: Born 1965 Bangkok; Chulalongkorn civil engineering, USC MS engineering management. Data-center angle via Gulf's JV with Singtel (GSA). Avoid USC donation/admissions topic. Best route: Gulf corporate contact/IR.

name: George Kaiser
current_role: President/CEO and primary owner of GBK Corp (parent of Kaiser-Francis Oil); chairman and majority owner of BOK Financial; founder, George Kaiser Family Foundation
profile: Tulsa-born son of refugees from Nazi Germany who took over the small family oil prospector Kaiser-Francis Oil in 1969 and grew it into an international E&P firm. Bought Bank of Oklahoma out of federal receivership in 1991 (now BOK Financial, ~63% owned) and holds ~72% of LNG firm Excelerate Energy; his GKFF has paid out $2.5bn+, focused on Tulsa.
interesting_fact: In 2018 he opened The Gathering Place, a 66-acre Tulsa riverfront park that is the largest public park in the US built with private funds.
deep_cut_fact: His foundation, jointly with the University of Tulsa, acquired Bob Dylan's 6,000+ item archive in 2016 (reportedly $15-20m), after earlier buying the Woody Guthrie archive; both now anchor Tulsa's Brady Arts District (Bob Dylan Center, Woody Guthrie Center).
notes: Famously low-profile; rarely gives interviews. Best route is GKFF media office. Also a good energy angle: Kaiser-Francis (gas) and Excelerate Energy (LNG regasification). Giving Pledge signer (2010).

name: Lu Xiangyang
current_role: Vice chairman, BYD Company; chairman of Youngy Group (融捷集团) and chairman/president of listed Youngy Co., Ltd. (002192.SZ)
profile: Born 1962 in Wuwei, Anhui, Lu worked at a local People's Bank of China branch before moving to Guangdong in the early 1990s. In 1995 he backed his cousin Wang Chuanfu's new battery firm BYD, now one of the world's largest EV makers, where he is vice chairman. He also runs his own Youngy (Rongjie) investment group, with lithium assets.
interesting_fact: His initial stake in BYD came from investing a few million renminbi in his cousin Wang Chuanfu's newly formed battery start-up in 1995; that stake is the source of most of his roughly $15bn fortune.
deep_cut_fact: Through Youngy Co. (融捷股份), which he chairs, Lu controls Rongda Lithium, holder of the mining right to the No. 134 spodumene vein at Jiajika in Kangding, Sichuan, one of China's largest hard-rock lithium deposits. In 2024 it agreed a project to add 350,000 t/yr of ore-processing capacity at the mine.
notes: Very low public profile and rarely gives interviews. socialmediaglobal@byd.com is the general contact email BYD publishes for its global HQ; PressEU@byd.com is BYD Europe's press contact. Youngy Co. investor-relations contacts are listed in its SZSE filings (002192). Sources disagree slightly on his initial BYD investment (RMB 2.5m vs 5m).

name: Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud
current_role: King of Saudi Arabia and Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques (since January 2015)
profile: Salman bin Abdulaziz (born 1935) is King of Saudi Arabia; his listed wealth reflects royal/state oil-linked fortune rather than a business he built. He governed Riyadh province for nearly five decades before becoming defence minister, crown prince and, in 2015, king. Day-to-day government is now led by his son Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who chairs the cabinet.
interesting_fact: Before taking the throne he served as Governor of Riyadh for roughly 48 years (1963-2011), overseeing its growth from a mid-sized town into a city of millions.
deep_cut_fact: He is a keen amateur historian: he long chaired Darah (the King Abdulaziz Foundation for Research and Archives), and his personal library is known for its rare manuscripts and books on Arabian history.
notes: Reigning head of state (aged ~90; hospital tests Jan 2026, still chairing cabinet per Aug 2026 reports). Not a realistic podcast guest; any approach would go via the Saudi Royal Court / embassy media offices. Wikipedia was rate-limited during research.

name: Jeffery Hildebrand
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Hilcorp Energy Company (Houston); Chairman, Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission (named 2023)
profile: Texas-born geologist/petroleum engineer (UT Austin BS 1981, MS 1985) who founded Hilcorp in 1989-90 after stints at Exxon and Dan A. Hughes Co. He built it into America's largest private oil producer by buying and revitalising mature fields, incl. BP's Alaska assets ($5.6B, 2020). Stepped down as CEO in 2018; remains executive chairman.
interesting_fact: In December 2015 Hilcorp gave each of its ~1,380 employees a $100,000 bonus after the staff hit a five-year goal of doubling the company's size.
deep_cut_fact: His alma mater's department is now the 'Hildebrand Department of Petroleum and Geosystems Engineering' at UT Austin, renamed in Nov 2017 after he and wife Mindy gave $25M; as a student he was in Pi Epsilon Tau, the petroleum engineering honor society.
notes: Very private, rarely gives interviews. Hilcorp's contact form has a dedicated Media option (asks for outlet and deadline). Also reachable in public capacity via Texas Parks & Wildlife Commission. Bio with board roles: https://krirm.tamuk.edu/jeff-hildebrand/

name: Sam McCandlish
current_role: Co-Founder and Chief Architect, Anthropic (CTO until Oct 2025)
profile: Theoretical physicist (Brandeis BS/MS, Stanford PhD under Eva Silverstein) who moved into AI at OpenAI, where he worked on scaling laws, then co-founded Anthropic in 2021. His wealth comes from his Anthropic stake. After serving as CTO, he became Chief Architect in Oct 2025, leading pretraining, large-scale model training, research productivity and RL infrastructure.
interesting_fact: He was lead author of OpenAI's 2018 paper 'An Empirical Model of Large-Batch Training' (with Jared Kaplan, Dario Amodei), which introduced the 'gradient noise scale' to predict how far training can be parallelised; he later co-authored the 2020 scaling-laws paper.
deep_cut_fact: His 2012 DOE Office of Science Graduate Fellowship profile (High Energy Theory, hometown Pittsburgh) notes he spent a summer at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics studying gravitational microlensing, and that outside physics he enjoys climbing trees and playing jazz piano.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews. Title change to Chief Architect confirmed by TechCrunch (Oct 2025) and Anthropic leadership page. Best route is via Anthropic press.

name: Tom Brown
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Compute Officer, Anthropic
profile: Co-founder of Anthropic (2021), where he runs compute, the infrastructure that trains and serves Claude. He was previously a research engineer at OpenAI and first author of the GPT-3 paper. Before AI he worked as an engineer at YC startups including MoPub and the group-dating app Grouper. His wealth comes from his Anthropic stake.
interesting_fact: He is the first-listed author of 'Language Models are Few-Shot Learners' (2020), the GPT-3 paper that kicked off the large-language-model era.
deep_cut_fact: His route into OpenAI went through Grouper: Greg Brockman was a regular Grouper user. Brown spent six months teaching himself ML (Coursera, Kaggle, a GPU bought with YC credits), then messaged Brockman: 'I got a B- in linear algebra... I'm happy to mop floors.'
notes: Chief Compute Officer title per July 2026 reporting (https://thenextweb.com/news/tom-blomfield-monzo-founder-anthropic-compute). He spoke openly about his career on YC's Lightcone podcast (Aug 2025) and answered Business Insider by email. No personal contact published; go through Anthropic press.

name: Christopher Olah
current_role: Cofounder and interpretability research lead, Anthropic
profile: Canadian AI researcher who cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI staff and leads its interpretability research (understanding the internals of neural networks). Previously at Google Brain and OpenAI; cofounded the Distill journal. His Anthropic stake (company valued at $380B in Feb 2026) makes him a billionaire despite never finishing college.
interesting_fact: Olah skipped college and became a Thiel Fellow in 2012 at 19; in 2020 he wrote a blog post to help others decide whether to follow a similar no-degree path.
deep_cut_fact: Before AI, he was a 3D-printing hacker: in early 2012 he started ImplicitCAD, an open-source programmatic CAD tool written entirely in Haskell (inspired by OpenSCAD) that exports STL and G-code for 3D printers.
notes: Research-focused, rarely does business press; most active via his blog and X (@ch402). Anthropic press route for formal requests.

name: Daniela Amodei
current_role: Co-founder and President, Anthropic
profile: Co-founded AI lab Anthropic (maker of the Claude models) in 2021 with her brother Dario and five other ex-OpenAI staff; as president she runs day-to-day operations. Earlier: a Pennsylvania congressional campaign and Rep. Matt Cartwright's office, an early hire at Stripe (2013), then OpenAI (2018-2020) as VP of safety and policy. Anthropic was privately valued at ~$965B in May 2026.
interesting_fact: Before tech she worked in politics on Matt Cartwright's successful 2012 Pennsylvania congressional campaign and then in his Washington office; she and Dario were both named to the 2023 Time100 AI list.
deep_cut_fact: She went to UC Santa Cruz on a classical flute scholarship and studied liberal arts and music, graduating in English literature, and at OpenAI she managed the team during GPT-2's development before moving into safety and policy.
notes: Anthropic press office (press@anthropic.com) is the standard route. Lowell High School (San Francisco) alumna. Note: this research was compiled by Claude, an Anthropic model; facts drawn from public sources only.

name: Jack Clark
current_role: Co-founder and Head of Public Benefit, Anthropic (leads the Anthropic Institute, since March 2026)
profile: British-born former tech journalist (The Register, Bloomberg) who became OpenAI's policy director in 2016 and co-founded Anthropic in 2021 with six ex-OpenAI researchers. His wealth comes from his Anthropic stake. He ran Anthropic's policy team until March 2026, when he became Head of Public Benefit leading the new Anthropic Institute; he still writes the Import AI newsletter.
interesting_fact: Clark was a founding member of Stanford's AI Index (2017-2024) and an inaugural member of the US National AI Advisory Committee (2021-2024); his Import AI newsletter is read by ~70,000 people each week.
deep_cut_fact: Before AI policy he was a technical journalist covering distributed systems and quantum computers; in 2016 he told his Bloomberg editor Alistair Barr, on a bench overlooking SF Bay, he was quitting to join OpenAI - Barr told him it was a terrible idea. He also writes short science-fiction stories in Import AI.
notes: Very public and accessible via Import AI newsletter and X; podcast-friendly (frequent interviewee). Forbes bio's 'head of policy' title is outdated as of March 2026.

name: Jared Kaplan
current_role: Cofounder and Chief Science Officer, Anthropic (on leave as associate professor of physics, Johns Hopkins University)
profile: Theoretical physicist (Stanford BS, Harvard PhD under Nima Arkani-Hamed) who worked on quantum gravity and holography at Johns Hopkins from 2012, joined OpenAI in 2019 and cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI staff. Anthropic was valued at $380B in Feb 2026; Kaplan leads its science work and served as its Responsible Scaling Officer.
interesting_fact: Lead author of 'Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models' (2020), the paper showing LLM performance improves predictably with model size, data and compute; he also co-authored the GPT-3 paper. Named to the Time100 AI list in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from the Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy (IMSA) in 2001, and in 2026 IMSA's Board of Trustees gave him its alumni Trailblazer Award. His 2009 Harvard PhD thesis was titled 'Aspects of holography'.
notes: Reach via Anthropic press team. Strong physics-to-AI story; scaling laws link directly to data-center/compute demand theme.

name: George Roberts
current_role: Co-Founder and Co-Executive Chairman, KKR & Co. Inc.
profile: George R. Roberts (b. 1943, Houston) co-founded KKR in 1976 with cousin Henry Kravis and Jerome Kohlberg after their Bear Stearns buyout work. KKR pioneered the leveraged buyout (RJR Nabisco, 1988), went public in 2010, and now has 250+ portfolio companies, including energy holdings like Crescent Energy. Roberts and Kravis became co-executive chairmen in 2021; he is based in the Bay Area.
interesting_fact: Roberts and his wife sit on the boards of the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco and SFMOMA; his nonprofit REDF (now Redefine Alliance) invests in businesses that train and employ people facing barriers to work.
deep_cut_fact: Roberts graduated from Culver Military Academy in Indiana in 1962 and received its 'Man of the Year' award in 1998. He became a Bear Stearns partner at 29. He also founded REDF in 1997 (originally the Roberts Enterprise Development Fund), an early backer of employment social enterprises; he still chairs its board.
notes: Very low public profile and rarely gives interviews. Best route is KKR Media (media@kkr.com). Redefine Alliance (formerly REDF), which he chairs, offers a philanthropic angle. KKR has a large energy/infrastructure book (e.g. Crescent Energy), relevant to the podcast.

name: Dario Amodei
current_role: Cofounder & CEO, Anthropic PBC
profile: San Francisco-born physicist turned AI researcher who led research at OpenAI (GPT-2/GPT-3, co-inventor of RLHF) before cofounding Anthropic in 2021 with his sister Daniela and five other ex-OpenAI staff. Anthropic, maker of Claude, filed its S-1 for an IPO in Oct 2026 and launched its roadshow in Nov 2026.
interesting_fact: Writes long-form essays on AI's future on his personal site, notably 'Machines of Loving Grace' (2024) and 'The Adolescence of Technology'; he earned his Princeton biophysics PhD as a Hertz Fellow.
deep_cut_fact: Before AI he was a neuroscientist: his 2011 Princeton PhD thesis, 'Network-Scale Electrophysiology: Measuring and Understanding the Collective Behavior of Neural Circuits' (advisors Michael Berry and William Bialek), built devices to record neural circuits. He was also on the 2000 USA Physics Olympiad team.
notes: Anthropic is in its IPO roadshow (Nov 2026), so expect quiet-period limits on executive media. Has done many long-form podcasts (Lex Fridman, Dwarkesh, Ezra Klein, Cheeky Pint), listed on darioamodei.com. Physics Olympiad detail per Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dario_Amodei).

name: Li Shuirong
current_role: Chairman, Zhejiang Rongsheng Holding Group and Rongsheng Petrochemical (SZSE: 002493)
profile: Li Shuirong (b. 1956) built Hangzhou-based Rongsheng from a 1989 polyester cloth workshop into one of China's largest private petrochemical groups, spanning refining, chemicals, logistics and property. He chairs Rongsheng Petrochemical, whose Zhoushan refinery is a strategic partner of Saudi Aramco (which paid $3.4bn for 10% in 2023).
interesting_fact: Before going into business Li tried to make a living as a carpenter; in 2020 Rongsheng became the first private Chinese refiner granted government permission to export refined oil products.
deep_cut_fact: His first business, founded in 1989, was the Yinong Network Chemical Fiber Factory in Yinong town (Xiaoshan, Hangzhou), making polyester fibre cloth; he only moved upstream into petrochemicals as the polyester industry shifted.
notes: Emails are Rongsheng Petrochemical board secretary (Quan Weiying) and securities affairs rep, from the 2026 interim report. Son-in-law Xiang Jiongjiong is GM of the listed arm. Low media profile; Chinese-language approach advisable.

name: Barry Lin Bai-Li
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Quanta Computer (Taiwan)
profile: Shanghai-born (1949), Hong Kong-raised, NTU-trained electrical engineer Barry Lam (Lin Pai-li) co-founded calculator maker Kinpo in 1973, then founded Quanta Computer in 1988, building it into the world's largest notebook ODM. Quanta is now a major AI-server builder (incl. Nvidia GB200 racks for hyperscalers), which drove his fortune to the top of Taiwan's rich lists.
interesting_fact: He started Quanta in 1988 with colleague C.C. Leung on under US$900,000 of capital; it became a Fortune Global 500 company and the original design manufacturer of the One Laptop per Child XO-1.
deep_cut_fact: A major collector of Chinese painting and calligraphy, he owns more than 250 works by Zhang Daqian and sponsors the Zhang Daqian Museum in the artist's former home; he also built an art-and-technology museum into Quanta's HQ.
notes: Known as Barry Lam in English. Low-profile; route via Quanta corporate spokesperson/IR (TWSE: 2382). Quanta ESG reports reportedly list a CSR contact (qci.csr@quantatw.com) but I could not reverify the PDF. Also funds NTU's Barry Lam Hall (EECS).

name: Oeri Paul Sacher
profile: This 1996 Forbes entry ($13.1B, shared with the Hoffmann family) appears to be the Hoffmann-Oeri-Sacher Roche founding-family fortune headed by Paul Sacher (1906–1999). Sacher was the Swiss conductor and new-music patron who became Roche's main shareholder through his wife Maja Hoffmann. He died 26 May 1999 in Switzerland, aged 93.
notes: Deceased (Paul Sacher, d. 26 May 1999; NYT obituary https://www.nytimes.com/1999/05/27/arts/paul-sacher-is-dead-at-93-conductor-and-arts-patron.html ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Sacher). The name merges 'Oeri' (Roche heirs Vera Oeri-Hoffmann / Jakob Oeri line) with Sacher. Living Roche-family heirs (e.g. André Hoffmann, Maja Oeri) would be separate profiles.

name: Family Hoffman
current_role: Family entry (Hoffmann/Oeri heirs of Roche founder Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche); public face: André Hoffmann, Vice-Chairman of Roche Holding
profile: A 1996 Forbes family entry for the Swiss Hoffmann-Oeri clan (shared with Paul Sacher and the Oeris), heirs of Roche founder Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche. Through a pooled voting bloc the family holds ~9% of Roche capital but a majority of votes; André Hoffmann (b.1958) has sat on Roche's board since 1996 and is vice-chairman, alongside cousin-line member Jörg Duschmalé.
interesting_fact: André Hoffmann is also Co-Chair of the World Economic Forum's Board of Trustees and a leading voice on 'sustainable capitalism'; he received the WWF Duke of Edinburgh Conservation Medal in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: André grew up in France's Camargue wetlands at the Tour du Valat biological station founded in 1954 by his father Luc Hoffmann (a WWF co-founder); in 1983 he left its board to work as acting administrator of the research station, and he now presides over Fondation Tour du Valat and the MAVA Foundation.
notes: This is a family entry, not one person; profile uses André Hoffmann (Roche Vice-Chairman, term to 2027) as the representative since he is the family's public figure. Other branches: Oeri (e.g. Maja Oeri, Andreas Oeri) and the late Paul Sacher's heirs. Confirm which family member the journalist wants before outreach.

name: R. Budi Hartono
current_role: Co-owner and head of Djarum Group (clove cigarettes, Bank Central Asia stake, Polytron, Blibli/Global Digital Niaga, Como 1907)
profile: Robert Budi Hartono (b. 1941, Semarang) and brother Michael inherited Djarum after their father's 1963 death and a factory fire, growing it into one of the world's largest clove-cigarette makers. Their biggest asset is a controlling stake in Bank Central Asia, bought after the 1997-98 crisis; holdings also include Polytron (now making EVs), Blibli (IPO 2022), Jakarta property and Italian football club Como 1907.
interesting_fact: Their father Oei Wie Gwan bought a bankrupt cigarette company in 1950 and renamed it Djarum ('needle') after the needle of a gramophone.
deep_cut_fact: PB Djarum, Indonesia's famous badminton club, began on a court at the Djarum factory in Kudus where Budi Hartono encouraged employees to play; spotting young Liem Swie King's talent, he formalised the club, and 7 of the 8 players on Indonesia's 1984 Thomas Cup-winning team came from PB Djarum.
notes: Very private; no personal or family-office contact published. Note: the 2018 Asian Games bridge bronze medal belongs to his brother Michael, not Budi. Route via Djarum Group / Djarum Foundation corporate channels.

name: Michael Sabel
current_role: CEO and Executive Co-Chairman, Venture Global (NYSE: VG), Arlington, Virginia
profile: Former investment banker (Friedman Billings Ramsey, Sandler O'Neil) who co-founded LNG exporter Venture Global with finance lawyer Bob Pender in 2013; together they own 80%+ of the company, which IPO'd in Jan 2025. Sole CEO since 2020, he is building a third Louisiana export plant (CP2) and the company made its Fortune 500 debut in 2026.
interesting_fact: Venture Global's edge was building LNG plants from small, factory-made modular liquefaction trains (with Baker Hughes) snapped together 'like Legos' — Sabel called shrinking the scale 'our Eureka moment'.
deep_cut_fact: Before LNG, Sabel and Pender tried in 2009 to develop a coal power plant in Sri Lanka; it didn't happen, and the LNG idea came while studying how Haiti could import small volumes of gas.
notes: Company is in high-profile arbitration disputes (BP won in Oct 2025); avoid that topic in outreach. Best route is Venture Global Public Affairs (press@). Frequent speaker at Gastech / LNG conferences.

name: Robert Pender
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Co-Chairman, Venture Global, Inc. (NYSE: VG)
profile: Bob Pender is a former Hogan Lovells project-finance partner who cofounded LNG exporter Venture Global with ex-banker Mike Sabel in 2013. The pair own more than 80% of the company, which IPO'd in January 2025 at a near-$60B valuation. Pender was co-CEO until 2020 and is now executive co-chairman.
interesting_fact: Before LNG, Pender spent 28 years as an energy finance lawyer and worked on more than $35 billion of energy, infrastructure and power projects, from cogeneration, biomass and geothermal to LNG and nuclear, including representing the Government of India and the People's Republic of China.
deep_cut_fact: Pro bono, he gave legal support to the Interim Haiti Recovery Commission and then served as a counselor to Haiti's Minister Delegate for Energy Security. He also helped the American Red Cross with South Asia tsunami relief and Accion with microfinance projects in Africa.
notes: Low public profile compared with co-chair Mike Sabel, who does most of the media. The best route is Venture Global's press office in Arlington, VA. He sits on the Memorial Sloan Kettering board of trustees.

name: Ian Henrick Lundin
current_role: Lundin family member/beneficiary; former Chairman of Lundin Petroleum/Lundin Energy (until 2022). Holds no current listed-board seat per Lundin Group site.
profile: Swedish-Canadian (b. 1960), son of Lundin Group founder Adolf H. Lundin, based near Geneva. Ran International Petroleum Corp/Lundin Oil and chaired Lundin Petroleum (later Lundin Energy, sold to Aker BP in 2022). Family wealth is held via trusts/Nemesia S.à r.l., a major holder in Lundin Mining, Lundin Gold, IPC and others.
interesting_fact: The Lundin family controls a stable of separately listed resource companies (Lundin Mining, Lundin Gold, IPC, Orrön Energy, Lucara, etc.) through a family trust; Nemesia held ~20% of Lundin Mining in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he was a drilling engineer for Wintershall (BASF) on offshore fields in northern Greece, then joined International Petroleum Corp in 1984 as operations manager in Dubai; he holds a 1982 B.Sc. in Petroleum Engineering from the University of Tulsa.
notes: Sensitive: Ian Lundin is on trial in Stockholm for alleged complicity in war crimes in Sudan (1999-2003); hearings ended and a verdict is expected around Dec 2026. He denies wrongdoing. Very private; no personal channels. Hurun's $13B figure likely reflects the whole Lundin family trust (Nemesia).

name: Haji Hassanal Bolkiah
current_role: Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan of Brunei Darussalam; also Prime Minister, Defence, Finance and Foreign Minister
profile: Hassanal Bolkiah has been Sultan of Brunei since his father abdicated on 5 Oct 1967, making him one of the world's longest-reigning monarchs. His wealth derives from Brunei's oil and gas revenues, managed via the Brunei Investment Agency (BIA), the sovereign fund that also owns the Dorchester Collection hotels. He still heads state and government.
interesting_fact: Educated at Victoria Institution in Kuala Lumpur, he trained as an officer cadet at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst (enrolled Jan 1966) before being called home to take the throne in 1967.
deep_cut_fact: He is a qualified pilot who flies his own aircraft: in March 2013 he personally piloted his Boeing 747 to Washington for his meeting with President Obama.
notes: Reigning head of state; Hurun ranks him via the Brunei Investment Agency (state wealth). Realistic route is the Prime Minister's Office (general inbox) or Brunei embassy press channels; a podcast booking is very unlikely.

name: Richard Kinder
current_role: Executive Chairman and co-founder, Kinder Morgan, Inc.; Chairman, Kinder Foundation
profile: Missouri-born lawyer who rose to president/COO of Enron, left in 1996 and with college friend Bill Morgan bought Enron's liquids pipelines for ~$40M, building Kinder Morgan into one of North America's largest energy-infrastructure firms. CEO until 2015, now Executive Chairman and top shareholder; funds Houston parks, education and pediatric cancer via the Kinder Foundation.
interesting_fact: He takes a salary of $1 a year from Kinder Morgan; his wealth comes from being its largest shareholder.
deep_cut_fact: A University of Missouri BA/JD alumnus (and Sigma Nu), he funded Mizzou's Kinder Institute on Constitutional Democracy with $25M in 2015, later raising total giving to the institute to $60M. Houston's Kinder Land Bridge over Memorial Drive in Memorial Park (2023) is also named for him and Nancy.
notes: Kinder Foundation site says it cannot respond to every inquiry and has no published email. Best route for an energy podcast is via Kinder Morgan media relations. Age 82.

name: Henry Kravis
current_role: Co-Executive Chairman, KKR & Co. Inc.
profile: Henry Kravis co-founded KKR in 1976 with cousin George Roberts and Jerome Kohlberg, pioneering the leveraged buyout. He and Roberts handed the co-CEO roles to successors in 2021 and serve as co-executive chairs; KKR (public since 2010) manages $650B+ across PE, infrastructure, energy and credit. He is a major donor to Columbia Business School.
interesting_fact: In 1989 KKR orchestrated the $25 billion buyout of RJR Nabisco, the deal behind the bestseller 'Barbarians at the Gate.'
deep_cut_fact: Born in Tulsa, Oklahoma, the son of an oil-industry engineer, Kravis captained the Claremont Men's College golf team as a senior in 1967, finishing his last season with an undefeated conference record; CMC's Kravis Center and Kravis Leadership Institute bear his name.
notes: Best route is KKR global communications (media@kkr.com). Energy angle: father Raymond Kravis was a Tulsa petroleum engineer/consultant (Tulsa Historical Society); KKR is a big infrastructure/energy investor.

name: Pei Zhenhua
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Suzhou Tianhua New Energy (formerly TA&A Ultra Clean Technology, SZ:300390)
profile: Born 1959 in Yixing, Jiangsu, Pei founded Suzhou TA&A (cleanroom/antistatic products) in 1997, later pivoting it into lithium battery materials as Tianhua New Energy. Most of his fortune comes from an early stake in battery giant CATL held via Ningbo United Innovation; in 2025 he sold a 12.95% Tianhua stake to CATL, making it a major shareholder.
interesting_fact: In 2015 the Ningbo United Innovation partnership bought 15% of CATL's predecessor for RMB 89 million; Pei was its biggest LP (79.9%). A decade later it was selling CATL shares worth tens of billions of yuan.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur, Pei worked at the Jiangsu Textile Research Institute, first in its knitting research lab and then in its new-products business department, before founding TA&A in November 1997.
notes: Low public profile; rarely interviewed. Best route is Tianhua New Energy's board secretary office (IR email from its 2026 interim report). Spouse Rong Jianfen is co-controller of Tianhua.

name: Carrie Perrodo
current_role: Owner (with family) of Perenco, the family-owned Anglo-French oil & gas producer; son François Perrodo is chairman
profile: Born Ka Yee Wong, a former top model who married Perenco founder Hubert Perrodo in 1974; she inherited the company when he died in a 2006 ski-touring accident. Perenco is one of the world's largest family-owned oil producers (Gabon, Cameroon, Peru, Vietnam, UK North Sea etc.). Son François chairs it; daughter Nathalie oversees the family's Bordeaux wine estates. She is reported to live in London.
interesting_fact: A 1970s top model, she met Hubert Perrodo while he was travelling the world in search of oil and gas; she also launched her own agency, Carrie's Models, which she later sold but which is still active in Singapore.
deep_cut_fact: Her Chinese name is 黃嘉兒; she was born in Hong Kong and moved to Singapore to pursue modelling before founding Carrie's Models. Her late husband Hubert was also a polo player and noted art collector.
notes: Extremely private; no personal public profile or social accounts. Forbes says 'native of Singapore' while Wikipedia says Hong Kong-born, moved to Singapore. Best route is via Perenco's PR agency Celicourt or pitching son François Perrodo (chairman).

name: Terrence Pegula
current_role: Owner, CEO & President, Buffalo Bills and Buffalo Sabres (Pegula Sports & Entertainment); runs JKLM Energy, Pittsburgh
profile: Penn State petroleum & natural gas engineering grad who founded Appalachian driller East Resources in 1983 and sold its assets to Royal Dutch Shell in 2010 (~$4.7B). He then bought the Sabres (2011) and Bills (2014) with wife Kim, and still produces Pennsylvania gas through JKLM Energy, staffed largely by ex-East Resources people.
interesting_fact: The Pegulas' $102M gift to Penn State built Pegula Ice Arena and created Division I hockey there, helping trigger the formation of the Big Ten hockey conference.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Carbondale, PA (Scranton Prep '69), he entered Penn State as a math major; his first job was with Getty Oil in Victoria, Texas, and Felmont Oil brought him to Olean, NY in 1975. He started East Resources in 1983 with $7,500 borrowed from family and friends.
notes: Best route is probably via Pegula Sports & Entertainment / Bills communications, or JKLM Energy (his active gas company) for an energy angle. Family business office in Boca Raton, FL. Avoid Kim Pegula's health as a topic.

name: Randa Duncan Williams
current_role: Non-executive Chairman, Enterprise Products Partners (general partner) and Chairman of EPCO / Enterprise Products Company
profile: Daughter of Enterprise Products co-founder Dan Duncan (d. 2010); the only one of four sibling heirs active in the pipeline business, which runs 50,000+ miles of pipelines plus Gulf Coast processing and storage. Joined in 1994, was CEO 2001, and has been non-executive chairman since 2013; also owns Texas Monthly.
interesting_fact: Before joining the family business she practised law for about six years (from 1988) on toxic-tort and property-liability cases; in 2019 she bought Texas Monthly magazine.
deep_cut_fact: A Houston Museum of Natural Science trustee since 1995 and former board chair, she also served on the board of the Manned Space Flight Education Foundation (the nonprofit behind Space Center Houston).

public_contacts.value: rrainey@eprod.com (Rick Rainey, Media Relations, Enterprise Products; tel (713) 381-3635)

notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Enterprise media relations (Rick Rainey) or via Texas Monthly ownership. IR site blocks automated fetches; contact emails taken from 2026 press releases as indexed by search.

name: Dannine Avara
current_role: Private investor; co-heir to the Duncan family's controlling stake in Enterprise Products Partners
profile: Dannine Avara (nee Duncan, b. 1964) is one of four children of the late Dan Duncan, who co-founded Houston pipeline giant Enterprise Products in 1968 with $10,000 and a truck. She inherited her stake when he died in 2010; Enterprise now owns 50,000+ miles of gas, oil and petrochemical pipelines. She keeps a very low profile and lives in Houston.
interesting_fact: Her father built Enterprise Products from a $10,000, one-truck propane business in 1968 into one of the largest US midstream companies; he was once Houston's richest man.

public_contacts.value: rrainey@eprod.com (Rick Rainey, Media Relations, Enterprise Products)

notes: Very private; no public role, interviews or social accounts found. Sister Randa Duncan Williams is the only sibling on Enterprise's board and is the family's public face; company media relations is the only published route.

name: Milane Frantz
current_role: Investor; heir and shareholder in Enterprise Products Partners (Duncan family); director, Duncan Family Foundation
profile: Milane Duncan Frantz (b. 1970) is one of four children of Dan Duncan, who founded Houston pipeline giant Enterprise Products Partners in 1968 and took it public in 1998. She inherited a stake after his 2010 death but is not active in the business (sister Randa Duncan Williams is). She lives in Houston, sits on the Hermann Park Conservancy board and is a director of the Duncan Family Foundation.
interesting_fact: Because Dan Duncan died in 2010, the one year the US federal estate tax was temporarily repealed, his heirs became the first American billionaire heirs to pay no estate tax since it was enacted.
deep_cut_fact: She studied at the University of Houston, and her family's Duncan Family Foundation is credited as a leadership donor to Houston's Hermann Park Conservancy, whose board she sits on.
notes: Very private, low public profile; no personal channels found. Best indirect route may be via Enterprise Products Partners (Houston) or the Hermann Park Conservancy. Avoid mentioning her late husband.

name: Zhu Yiming
current_role: Chairman, GigaDevice Semiconductor (603986.SH / HK) and Chairman, ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT)
profile: Zhu Yiming founded GigaDevice in Silicon Valley in 2005 and moved it to Beijing, building a NOR-flash and MCU champion listed in Shanghai in 2016 (and Hong Kong in 2026). With the Hefei government he set up CXMT, now China's largest DRAM maker, which listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on July 27, 2026, lifting his fortune above $10bn.
interesting_fact: CXMT is China's leading bid to compete with Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron in DRAM; Zhu stepped back from GigaDevice's CEO role to lead the Hefei memory project. He is credited with 50+ patents.
deep_cut_fact: Born 1972 in Funing County, Jiangsu, he studied physics at Tsinghua and moonlighted as a programmer for Zhongguancun firms. He went to Stony Brook for a physics PhD (where Nobel laureate C.N. Yang taught) but switched to an EE master's to pursue Silicon Valley.
notes: Low public profile in Western media; outreach best via GigaDevice board office / IR (Chinese-language). info@cxmt.com is CXMT's general corporate inbox, not a personal channel.

name: John C. Malone
current_role: Chairman Emeritus and strategic adviser, Liberty Media (since Jan 1, 2026); major shareholder across Liberty companies
profile: John Malone, the 'Cable Cowboy', ran Tele-Communications Inc. (TCI) from 1973 to 1996 and built it into a cable giant later sold to AT&T. He then assembled the Liberty empire: Liberty Media (Formula 1, Live Nation stake), Liberty Global, QVC Group, plus big stakes in Charter and Warner Bros. Discovery. He stepped down as chairman of Liberty Media and Liberty Global at the start of 2026 but remains a key shareholder and adviser.
interesting_fact: From 2011 to 2021 Malone was the largest private landowner in the United States, with about 2.2 million acres of ranches and forests.
deep_cut_fact: Malone started his career in 1963 at Bell Labs doing economic planning and R&D, then earned a Johns Hopkins Ph.D. in operations research. He became famous as a huge retail Tesla investor, later trimming his stake and moving into Treasuries.
interesting_fact: At one point he claimed to be Tesla's third-largest individual shareholder after selling Baidu and Nvidia shares at the start of the pandemic to buy long-dated Tesla call options.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond the KoGuan School of Law at Shanghai Jiao Tong ($30M, 2008), he gave $28M to Peking University, which named a law-school building after him (the Leo KoGuan Building); his Chinese name is Liao Kaiyuan (廖凯原).
notes: Active and outspoken on X (posts about Tesla/Musk/markets), but handle not verified from an official page here. SHI recently acted as lead integrator for a New Jersey AI supercomputer initiative (data-center angle). SHI press has used agency Gregory FCA; no current verified press email found.

name: Alexei Kuzmichev
current_role: Co-founder/shareholder, Alfa Group Consortium (listed as supervisory board member); stepped down from LetterOne board in 2022
profile: Russian businessman (b. 1962, Kirov) who co-founded Alfa Group with Mikhail Fridman and German Khan, later LetterOne. Wealth from oil (TNK-BP stake sold to Rosneft in 2013), Alfa-Bank, VimpelCom and X5 Retail. Sanctioned by the EU/UK (2022) and US (2023); sold his Alfa-Bank stake in 2023 and has been under French investigation since Oct 2023.
interesting_fact: He is friends with photographer Trevor Paglen and owns one of Paglen's most famous works, the night photograph of the NSA headquarters.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alfa, he served 1980-82 as an army radio operator on the Soviet-Chinese border; in 1988 he, Fridman and Khan started Alfa Photo, a business importing photo chemicals, the seed of Alfa Group.
notes: Sanctioned by UK, EU, US (OFAC SDN, Aug 2023), Canada and Australia; French money-laundering/sanctions-evasion charges pending. Any engagement may raise legal/compliance issues. No published personal or office contact found; former Alfa Group/LetterOne bio pages are offline.

name: Guan Yamei
current_role: Chairman (president) of Tongwei Group, Chengdu; long-time executive alongside board chairman Liu Hanyuan
profile: Guan Yamei (管亚梅) is a senior leader of Tongwei Group, the Chengdu conglomerate that grew from aquafeed into one of the world's largest polysilicon and solar cell makers (Tongwei Co., 600438.SH). Hurun lists her wealth jointly with Tongwei founder Liu Hanyuan; she has served as Tongwei Co. president and later as Tongwei Group chairman.
interesting_fact: Tongwei, which she helps lead, started in fish feed and is now one of the world's largest producers of high-purity polysilicon and solar cells, while still running a major aquaculture/feed business.
deep_cut_fact: In October 2009, as president of Tongwei Co., she was named one of 'China's 100 Meritorious Persons in Agriculture Industrialization' - one of only three entrepreneurs from Sichuan to receive the honour that year.
notes: Very low public profile; almost all coverage centres on Liu Hanyuan. English spelling varies (Guan Yawei in a 2009 Tongwei release). IR email zqb@tongwei.com is the securities dept (board secretary Yan Ke) per Tongwei's investor-briefing notice. Best route is via Tongwei Group corporate/securities office.

name: Pavel Tykac
current_role: Owner, Sev.en Global Investments / Sev.en Group (coal, power, steel, oil & gas; Prague)
profile: Czech investor who began as a computer distributor, co-founded takeover firm Motoinvest in 1992, then built Sev.en Energy (Czech coal mines, power plants, 50% of InterGen). Via Sev.en Global Investments he now buys ESG-shunned assets abroad: Celsa UK/Nordic steel, Texas oil and gas wells, a stake in Vietnam's Mong Duong 2 plant.
interesting_fact: His group openly runs a contrarian strategy of buying companies that institutional investors are dumping over ESG concerns, betting coal and heavy industry stay profitable longer than markets assume.
deep_cut_fact: He is a native of Čelákovice, a small town near Prague, and Forbes Czech names his real passion as football club SK Slavia Prague, which it lists among his holdings.
notes: Very low public profile and rarely gives interviews; CEO Alan Svoboda usually speaks for the group. Best route is the Sev.en GI media team (Veronika Diamantová; communications director Gabriela Sáričková Benešová). The site shows emails through JS anti-spam markup (decoded with the site's own script).

name: Guo Jinshu
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Inner Mongolia Huineng Coal & Electricity Group (Ordos)
profile: Guo Jinshu (郭金树), a former head of the Ordos municipal coal bureau, founded Huineng in the early 1990s from restructured small coal mines. It grew into a private coal, coal-to-gas/LNG, coal chemicals and power group with >RMB100bn in assets; he is now pushing into solar, new materials and acquisitions (e.g. Asia-Potash stake, ST Xinchao bid).
interesting_fact: Huineng began as a company of 600+ laid-off coal workers who pooled their own money; Guo says those who didn't take buyouts all became shareholders. Its Ordos coal-to-natural-gas plant became a national demonstration project.
deep_cut_fact: Guo explains the name: 汇 'gather' + 能 meaning energy, power, talent and ability, and preaches four qualities for running a business: 定力, 控制力, 穿透力, 平衡力 (composure, control, penetration, balance). In his 70s (2023) he still targeted RMB250bn in assets by 2030.
notes: Input's SEC link (Luckin Coffee CEO) is a mismatch: Luckin's CEO is Guo Jinyi, a different person. Very low-profile private Chinese coal tycoon; no published personal contacts found. Company site reportedly huinenggroup.com (unreachable, unverified). 2025 Asia-Potash filings name him as Huineng's sole actual controller.

name: Ray Lee Hunt
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Hunt Consolidated, Inc. (Dallas; oil & gas, LNG, real estate, investments)
profile: Son of wildcatter H.L. Hunt, Ray Hunt (b. 1943, SMU grad) took over Hunt Oil after his father's 1974 death and built Hunt Consolidated into a conglomerate spanning oil and gas, Peru LNG, power/infrastructure and real estate (Hunt Realty, Reunion in Dallas). Now chairman emeritus; son Hunter Hunt runs the energy and infrastructure businesses.
interesting_fact: Hunt Oil was one of the first companies to land an exploration deal in Iraq's Kurdistan region after the fall of Saddam Hussein (2007), and it holds stakes in Peru's natural gas fields and its gas liquefaction plant.
deep_cut_fact: Hunt and John Scovell were 20-somethings who 'didn't know rebar from structural steel' when they started the Reunion project in 1972; Hunt made Scovell president of Woodbine Development as its only employee, and at 32 refused even to read the $35M construction contract, trusting him. Reunion Tower opened April 15, 1978.
notes: Very private family company. Best route is Hunt Consolidated public affairs (media line (214) 978-8534 published on same page). Also trustee/director emeritus at SMU and George W. Bush Presidential Center; son Hunter Hunt is the operational lead for energy/infrastructure.

name: Sri Prakash Lohia
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Indorama Corporation
profile: Kolkata-born (1952) Indonesian billionaire who moved to Indonesia in 1973 with his father to start Indorama Synthetics (spun yarns, 1976). He built Indorama Corporation into a diversified petrochemicals, fertilizer, polyester and gloves group; his 2006 purchase of a Nigerian olefins plant became West Africa's largest petrochemical complex. Son Amit is vice chairman.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he acquired a struggling integrated olefin plant in Nigeria and turned it into the largest petrochemical company in West Africa; Indorama marked its 50th anniversary (Golden Jubilee) in Dubai in late 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He started buying a few old hand-coloured 'colour plate' books around 2008 as a hobby; it grew into one of the world's premier private collections of the genre (21,500+ images), which he had digitised and made freely viewable online so anyone, regardless of language, can enjoy the plates.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Brother-in-law of Lakshmi Mittal. Son Amit Lohia (vice chairman) is the more public face. Not to be confused with brother Aloke Lohia of Indorama Ventures (Thailand).

name: Li Yanhong
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Baidu Inc.
profile: Li Yanhong (Robin Li) co-founded Baidu in 2000 with Eric Xu after search-engine stints at IDD/Dow Jones and Infoseek in the US. Baidu became China's dominant search engine; Li has since steered it into AI (ERNIE large models, AI cloud) and Apollo/Apollo Go autonomous driving.
interesting_fact: Before Baidu, Li built RankDex (1996), an early search engine that ranked pages by the links pointing to them, a link-analysis idea that predated Google's PageRank.
deep_cut_fact: Li is the named inventor on US patent 5,920,859, 'Hypertext Document Retrieval System and Method' (filed Feb 1997, issued July 1999), written while he was at IDD Information Services, a Dow Jones unit where he also worked on software for the online Wall Street Journal.
notes: Known in English as Robin Li. The listed SEC insider roles (Datadog CPO, Equinix director) belong to a different person, Yanbing Li; this is a name-match error, not Robin Li. Best route is via Baidu corporate/IR.

name: Cao Renxian
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd. (300274.SZ)
profile: Cao Renxian (曹仁贤) grew up in a poor rural family, studied industrial automation at Hefei University of Technology and taught there before founding Sungrow in 1997. Sungrow became one of the world's largest makers of solar PV inverters and energy storage systems, selling into the Middle East, Southeast Asia, Europe and the U.S. He remains chairman of the Shenzhen-listed company.
interesting_fact: Sungrow, founded by a university lecturer in renewable-energy power electronics, grew into what it calls the world's leading inverter and energy storage system supplier, with over 269 GW of inverters installed worldwide by mid-2022.
deep_cut_fact: Cao launched Sungrow on 28 November 1997 in a humble rented house in Anhui at age 30, quitting his secure university teaching job while newly married, and funded it with about 80,000 yuan of his own savings plus money from friends and relatives.
notes: No personal social accounts found. Best route is Sungrow corporate communications or IR (the IR email is the company's published investor contact). Deep-cut source for the rented-house date is Sungrow's 25th-anniversary release (aap.com.au link); the savings figure comes from Wikipedia.

name: Sudhir Mehta
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Torrent Group (Torrent Pharmaceuticals, Torrent Power), Ahmedabad
profile: Elder son of Torrent founder U.N. Mehta, Sudhir Mehta became group chairman in 1998 and built Torrent from a pharma firm (Trinity Laboratories) into a pharma-power-gas conglomerate. He handed the chair to brother Samir in the 2010s and stepped off the Torrent Pharma board in March 2024, remaining Chairman Emeritus.
interesting_fact: He pushed Torrent Pharma into exports, entering Russia during its 1990s political turmoil; Torrent later built a strong presence in Europe, Russia and Brazil. Business Standard describes him as extremely media-shy, avoiding interviews and press briefings.
deep_cut_fact: When India opened power to private players in 1991, he began quietly buying shares of Ahmedabad Electricity Co. and Surat Electricity Co., taking majority stakes by the late 1990s - the origin of Torrent Power, which went on to build the 1,147.5 MW Sugen gas-fired plant.
notes: Very media-shy; largely retired from active business. Brother Samir Mehta is group chairman; approach via Torrent corporate/company secretary channels. Group energy arm (Torrent Power, Torrent Gas) is the podcast-relevant angle.

name: Samir Mehta
current_role: Chairman, Torrent Group; Executive Chairman, Torrent Pharmaceuticals (reappointed for 5 years from Apr 2025)
profile: Ahmedabad-based chairman of the Torrent Group (pharmaceuticals, power, and more), founded by his father U.N. Mehta. He succeeded his elder brother Sudhir as group chairman in 2014 and has grown Torrent Pharma into a global generics player in ~40 countries, while Torrent Power is a major Indian power utility/generator.
interesting_fact: In March 2025 the Torrent Group completed the purchase of a 67% majority stake in IPL cricket franchise Gujarat Titans from CVC-controlled Irelia, reportedly for about Rs 5,035 crore.
deep_cut_fact: Besides running Torrent, he serves as President of the Indian Pharmaceutical Alliance (IPA), the lobby group of India's largest research-based drugmakers, where his bio highlights his push for an employee-centric workplace promoting equality and fairness.
notes: Energy angle is Torrent Power (Ahmedabad/Surat utility, renewables, pumped storage). Low public profile; route via Torrent corporate communications/IR.

name: Michael Kadoorie
current_role: Non-executive Chairman, CLP Holdings; Non-executive Chairman, The Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels (Peninsula Hotels)
profile: Sir Michael Kadoorie (b. 1941) heads the Kadoorie family interests in Hong Kong: CLP Holdings, the power utility the family co-founded that serves ~80% of Hong Kong, and Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels, owner of The Peninsula hotels. Still chairing CLP in 2026, he opened its May 2026 AGM and is overseeing power investment for the Northern Metropolis.
interesting_fact: He is the scion of a Baghdadi-Jewish family whose grandfather Elly Kadoorie settled in Shanghai in 1880; he is also a keen photographer and classic-car collector (Bugatti Type 57, Hispano-Suiza J12, Lamborghini Miura).
deep_cut_fact: He is a helicopter pilot: Heliservices (HK) was founded in 1978 after he bought Hong Kong's first private helicopter. He still chairs it, and it flies from the Peninsula's rooftop helipad and washes power-line insulators for HK utilities.
