notes: Very private, aged 85; no personal social media. CLP press office (named contact changes per release) or the HSH/Peninsula corporate office are the realistic routes. Aviation (Heliservices, Metrojet) is a good conversational hook.

name: Rinat Akhmetov
current_role: Founder and owner, System Capital Management (SCM) group (Metinvest, DTEK); president of FC Shakhtar Donetsk
profile: Ukraine's richest person and the son of a Donetsk coal miner. He built SCM by buying mining and steel assets during 1990s privatisation; it now holds steelmaker Metinvest and energy company DTEK, Ukraine's largest private power producer. His plants and substations have been heavily damaged in the war, but he has stayed in Ukraine and funds reconstruction and aid.
interesting_fact: Through SCM's 'Steel Front' initiative, his companies make fortifications and other defensive equipment for Ukraine's military, including protection for US-supplied Abrams tanks.
deep_cut_fact: His 'Heart of Azovstal' project began with a call to Azovstal commander Denys Prokopenko 15 minutes before the defenders left the plant. Prokopenko asked him to 'take care of my men', and Akhmetov launched the project in January 2023 with $25M for Mariupol defenders and families of fallen soldiers.
notes: Very private; speaks mainly through SCM press statements. SCM's communications director is Natalia Yemchenko (Kyiv Post). DTEK (energy arm) is the most relevant angle for an energy podcast. scm.com.ua and dtek.com sit behind bot protection, so their contact pages could not be verified. Avoid oligarch/politics framing.

name: Li Ping
current_role: Vice Chairman, Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. (CATL)
profile: Li Ping (b. 1968) is vice chairman and co-controlling shareholder (with chairman Robin Zeng) of CATL, the world's largest EV battery maker, founded in 2011 and dual-listed in Shenzhen and Hong Kong; he holds ~4.3% of the company. He previously worked at electrical engineering firms and holds a Fudan degree and a CEIBS MBA. CATL licenses tech to Ford's Michigan battery plant, completed June 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2025 Li and his wife Liao Mei donated 4.05 million CATL shares (about 1 billion yuan) to their alma mater Fudan University; the transfer was registered on July 10, 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Li studied polymers at Fudan (class of 1985), while his wife Liao Mei was a Fudan history major (class of 1986); their 1-billion-yuan gift funds Fudan's new Xue Min Institute of Advanced Studies.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews (some speeches at CATL events). The only route is CATL corporate (IR/media). Sources disagree on when he became vice chairman (2015 or 2017).

name: Oleg Deripaska
current_role: Founder, Basic Element; major shareholder of En+ Group (which controls Rusal)
profile: Russian industrialist who built Siberian Aluminium in the 1990s and merged it with Abramovich's assets in 2000 to form Rusal. Founder of Basic Element (metals, energy, construction, agriculture). Sanctioned by the US (2018), UK and EU; his En+/Rusal stake was cut to resolve US sanctions on the companies in 2019. In 2026 he is a vocal commentator on Russia's economy.
interesting_fact: Through his Volnoe Delo foundation he has funded the Phanagoria excavation since 2004, which made him Russia's single biggest donor to archaeology and Phanagoria the country's best-financed dig.
deep_cut_fact: He enrolled in physics at Moscow State University in 1985 and graduated with honours in 1993. Before that he served in the Soviet Strategic Missile Forces in Trans-Baikal from 1986 to 1989. Shrinking academic funding ended his plan to become a theoretical physicist, and he moved into metals trading.
notes: Sanctioned by the US, UK, EU, Canada and Australia, so check compliance and legal issues before any outreach. He posts on an official Telegram channel that the press quotes often, but I could not verify the exact handle. His official site deripaska.com and the Basic Element site basel.ru were unreachable from this environment.

name: Mikhail Gutseriev
current_role: Founder and main shareholder / chairman, Safmar Group (oil, coal, real estate, retail; Russia)
profile: Russian-Ingush billionaire (b. 1958, Akmolinsk) who ran Slavneft, then founded oil producer RussNeft in 2002; fled to London in 2007 amid tax charges and returned in 2010. Built Safmar Group (RussNeft, Russian Coal, Neftisa, A101 developer). Sanctioned by UK and EU in 2021 over ties to Lukashenko; in 2022 transferred assets to a relative.
interesting_fact: He owns Moscow's Hotel National, where Donald Trump stayed on his first Russia trip in 1987, owns radio stations incl. Radio Shanson, and writes song lyrics performed by well-known Russian singers.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil, he trained in 'Leather and Fur Technology' (Dzhambul Technological Institute, 1981) and worked as a process engineer in Grozny; in 2005 he funded the rebuilding of his old Grozny high school No. 23, destroyed in the First Chechen War.
notes: Contact is the SAFMAR Charitable Foundation (his foundation) site, which looks dated (c.2014). Subject to UK sanctions (EU sanctions litigated; EU General Court annulled some listings 2025-26). Reputational/legal sensitivity for any engagement.

name: Mike Brown
current_role: Owner and President, Cincinnati Bengals (NFL)
profile: Mike Brown (b. 1935) is the son of coaching legend Paul Brown. He helped his father found the Cincinnati Bengals in 1967–68, served as assistant GM, and took over as owner after Paul's death in 1991. The Brown family still runs the team, with daughter Katie Blackburn as executive VP. Forbes valued the Bengals at more than $5B in 2025.
interesting_fact: The Bengals reached Super Bowl LVI under Brown's ownership in the 2021 season. That run brought the franchise's first playoff win since 1990 and its first-ever road playoff win.
deep_cut_fact: Brown played quarterback at Dartmouth (class of 1957) and graduated from Harvard Law School in 1960. As a young man he had a summer job as a deck hand at Kinsman Marine Transit, hired by George Steinbrenner long before either of them owned a pro sports team.
notes: He is 91 and rarely gives interviews beyond team press events. Bengals media relations (bengals.com/news/media) is the professional route. He is a poor fit for an energy/data-center angle.

name: Daniel Nadler
current_role: Cofounder & CEO, OpenEvidence
profile: Canadian-born AI entrepreneur with a Harvard Ph.D. in economics. Cofounded Kensho (AI for financial analytics), sold to S&P Global for $550M in 2018. In 2022 cofounded OpenEvidence, an AI medical-search tool free for verified doctors and ad-supported; valued at ~$12B in early 2026, with Nadler owning nearly 60%.
interesting_fact: OpenEvidence has signed up more than 758,000 doctors and was adding ~55,000 per month; it is free for verified clinicians and earns money from advertising.
deep_cut_fact: He is a published poet: his debut collection 'Lacunae: 100 Imagined Ancient Love Poems' (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2016) presents short poems as imagined translations of lost ancient texts. He studied poetry at Harvard under Pulitzer winner Jorie Graham.
notes: contact@openevidence.com is the general company contact in the site footer, not a dedicated press line. Poetry is a good angle for outreach; Forbes notes his Ph.D. thesis was on credit-derivative pricing.

name: JK Irving
profile: James K. (J.K.) Irving, longtime chairman of J.D. Irving Ltd. and eldest son of K.C. Irving, died June 21, 2024 in Saint John, New Brunswick, aged 96.
interesting_fact: He was the last surviving son of Irving Group founder K.C. Irving; his brother Arthur (Irving Oil) died about a month before him.
notes: Deceased (June 21, 2024). Source: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-06-21/james-k-irving-canadian-forestry-billionaire-dies-at-96 . His son Robert K. Irving, co-CEO of JDI, reportedly died May 2026; Jim (J.D.) Irving remains co-CEO.

name: Maximilian Viessmann
current_role: CEO & President, Viessmann Generations Group GmbH & Co. KG; board member, Carrier Global
profile: Fourth-generation heir (b. 1989) of the Viessmann heating dynasty. Ex-BCG consultant who joined in 2015 and became CEO; sold Viessmann Climate Solutions to Carrier for ~EUR 12bn (agreed 2023, closed Jan 2024) and joined Carrier's board. Now runs family investor Viessmann Generations Group (2026: AI push, FC Bayern stake).
interesting_fact: The Viessmann brand stayed with the family: Viessmann Generations Group owns it and licenses it to Carrier after the EUR 12bn sale of Viessmann Climate Solutions.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the Advisory Council of the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), and before joining the family firm he was an angel investor in Europe and Asia as well as a BCG consultant.
notes: Press contact named on 2026 VGG releases is Nicola Boya (byan@viessmann.com). Group communications inbox listed in imprint. Very relevant for energy/heat-pump angle.

name: Luo Jinhong
current_role: Co-actual controller and major shareholder of EVE Energy (Huizhou); holds 50% of controlling shareholder Tibet EVE Holding (not a director/officer)
profile: Luo Jinhong (骆锦红) co-founded EVE Energy in 2001 with her husband, chairman Liu Jincheng, after both worked at Desay Energy in Huizhou. EVE grew from lithium primary cells into a top Chinese EV and energy-storage battery maker. The couple are joint actual controllers; Hurun 2025 put their joint wealth at RMB 52.5B.
interesting_fact: In EVE's 2022 private placement the couple personally subscribed RMB 6B (Luo 4B, Liu 2B) alongside RMB 3B from their holding company, a large founder bet on capacity expansion.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding EVE she worked at three battery makers in Huizhou: Huizhou Bohui Battery, Times Battery and Desay Energy Technology; EVE's first entity (2001) was set up via relatives' nominee shareholding while Liu was still Desay's deputy GM.
notes: Very low public profile; she is not an executive and gives no interviews found. Husband Liu Jincheng is the public face (gives English-language interviews, e.g. electrive 2025). Route via EVE securities department (IR email).

name: Jayshree Ullal
current_role: Chairperson and CEO, Arista Networks; director, Snowflake
profile: London-born, Delhi-raised engineer (SFSU, Santa Clara) who ran Cisco's switching business before becoming CEO of Arista Networks in 2008, when it had no revenue and under 50 employees. Arista now sells $9B+ a year of high-speed Ethernet switches, a core supplier to cloud and AI data-center buildouts; she owns roughly 2% of the stock.
interesting_fact: She joined Arista as CEO when the startup had no revenue and fewer than 50 employees; it now generates more than $9 billion in annual revenue.
deep_cut_fact: Early in her career at AMD she designed high-speed memory chips for IBM and Hitachi; she joined Cisco in 1993 when it bought Crescendo Communications, Cisco's very first acquisition, and built the Catalyst switching business.
notes: Press email is Arista corporate communications (Amanda Jaramillo) as listed on 2026 releases. No verified personal social accounts found. Frequently speaks about AI networking/back-end AI clusters; strong data-center fit.

name: Maria Fernanda Amorim
current_role: Matriarch/co-owner (with daughters Paula, Marta, Luisa) of the Americo Amorim Group; no executive role
profile: Widow of cork magnate Americo Amorim (d. 2017); she and her three daughters inherited his fortune and top Forbes Portugal's rich list (~EUR 5.8B, Jan 2026). The core asset is the family's control of Amorim Energia, which owns ~37.5% of oil & gas group Galp (chaired by eldest daughter Paula), plus Corticeira Amorim stakes, Amorim Luxury and real estate.
interesting_fact: Forbes notes she has founded two museums: one dedicated to Port wine and another, in Grijo, focused on arts and crafts.
notes: Very private, elderly, no public profile or interviews found. The family's public face is daughter Paula Amorim (chair of Galp and Amorim Energia) - for an energy podcast she is the realistic guest; route via the Americo Amorim Group general email or Galp media relations. Couldn't verify the museum names independently.

name: Albert Avdolyan
current_role: Owner, A-Property (holding behind ELSI / Elga coal complex, Pacific Railway, Yakut Fuel & Energy Co.)
profile: Krasnodar-born (1970) investor who co-founded Russian telecom Scartel/Yota with Sergey Adoniev, then sold out of the MegaFon-linked holding in 2013. Through A-Property he bought the giant Elga coking-coal deposit in Yakutia (2020), merged coal assets into ELSI (2022), owns gas producer YATEC and is building the ~530 km private Pacific Railway to a Sea of Okhotsk port.
interesting_fact: The Pacific Railway he is building from Elga to Port Elga on the Sea of Okhotsk is ~531 km long (626 km of track with junctions), a record for a private railway in Russia.
deep_cut_fact: In 2013 he founded the 'New Home' charitable foundation, which builds 'Point of the Future' (Tochka Budushchego) in Irkutsk: a free school for 1,000 pupils plus a village of cottages for foster families with orphaned and disabled children; a second complex began in Yakutia in 2022.
notes: Sanctions sensitivity: US Treasury sanctioned Elga coal entities (June 2024) and Sibanthracite; a news report says he was personally added to the EU sanctions list (unverified here). Russian company sites (elsi-group.ru) were unreachable from this environment so no press email was confirmed. Very low public profile.

name: Robert Bass
current_role: President, Keystone Group LP (Fort Worth family investment holding company); founder of the Oak Hill investment funds
profile: Fort Worth-born Yale (1971) and Stanford MBA (1974) investor, one of the four Bass brothers whose fortune traces to great-uncle Sid Richardson's oil. Built his own wealth through Keystone and the Oak Hill family of funds (Oak Hill Capital, Oak Hill Advisors), plus 1980s deals such as Taft Broadcasting and American Savings. Major donor to Stanford, Duke, Yale and Brookings.
interesting_fact: Bass sold New York's Plaza Hotel to Donald Trump in 1988 for $390 million.
deep_cut_fact: He began his business career at Wells Fargo after Yale, and is a past chairman of both Stanford's board of trustees and the National Trust for Historic Preservation.
notes: Very private; no published personal/office contact found. Keystone Group LP (Fort Worth) is his office; Oak Hill Advisors/Oak Hill Capital press offices are an indirect route. Founder of the defunct supersonic-jet firm Aerion (avoid as an opener).

name: Walther Moreira Salles
current_role: Filmmaker and co-founder of production company VideoFilmes; Itaú Unibanco heir (Moreira Salles family holding)
profile: This is most likely Walter (Walther) Moreira Salles Júnior (b. 1956), son of banker-diplomat Walther Moreira Salles. With his brothers he shares the family's controlling stake in Itaú Unibanco, Brazil's largest private bank, via the family holding. He is best known as an acclaimed director: Central Station, The Motorcycle Diaries, and I'm Still Here, which won Brazil's Oscar for Best International Feature in 2025.
interesting_fact: Thanks to his Itaú stake he is often described as the world's third-richest filmmaker, behind Steven Spielberg and George Lucas. His film I'm Still Here brought Brazil its first Academy Award for Best International Feature.
deep_cut_fact: Salles spent about ten years making non-fiction documentaries before switching to fiction. He was drawn to his 2001 film Behind the Sun after his younger brother handed him Ismail Kadare's novel Broken April, saying 'If I know you well, this will touch you.'
notes: Hurun's 'Walther Moreira Salles' (Itaú, 2014–2026) must be a living heir; the father of that name died in 2001. It is almost certainly the filmmaker son, whose legal name is Walther/Walter Moreira Salles Júnior. Brothers Fernando, Pedro (Itaú chairman) and João are listed separately. He is a filmmaker rather than a business operator, so his fit for an energy/data-center podcast is limited.

name: Yang Zhiling
current_role: Founder and CEO, Moonshot AI (Beijing; maker of the Kimi chatbot and open-weight Kimi models)
profile: Yang Zhilin (b. 1992, Shantou) studied CS at Tsinghua and did a CMU PhD under Ruslan Salakhutdinov and William Cohen, co-authoring Transformer-XL and XLNet. After founding Recurrent AI, he co-founded Moonshot AI in 2023 with Tsinghua classmates; it raised ~$2B at a $20B+ valuation in May 2026 and has reportedly raised more since, ahead of a planned Hong Kong IPO.
interesting_fact: A prog-rock devotee, he named Moonshot AI in honour of Pink Floyd's album The Dark Side of the Moon; a white piano reportedly stands prominently in the Beijing office.
deep_cut_fact: At Tsinghua he was the drummer in a campus band called Splay and organised music competitions; he won admission there after taking first prize in China's National Olympiad in Informatics.
notes: Name usually romanised Yang Zhilin (杨植麟). Keeps a low profile: rarely gives interviews and has no public personal social-media account (Caixin). Best route is Moonshot's global PR address; X handle is the company's, not his.

name: Zhu Hongmei
current_role: Co-actual controller of Shenghong Group / Eastern Shenghong (000301.SZ); director of controlling shareholder Jiangsu Shenghong Technology
profile: Zhu Hongmei (朱红梅) is the wife and business partner of Miao Hangen, founder of Suzhou-based Shenghong Group; the couple are joint actual controllers of Eastern Shenghong. Shenghong grew over ~30 years from printing and dyeing in Shengze, Wujiang into polyester fibre, refining and petrochemicals (Shenghong Petrochemical in Lianyungang) and new-energy materials. She holds no executive post at the listed company.
interesting_fact: The couple took Shenghong public via a 2018 backdoor listing into Wujiang state-owned 'Oriental Market' (renamed Eastern Shenghong), reported as the largest A-share asset restructuring of 2018 and a mixed-ownership reform test case.
notes: Very private; virtually no personal public profile or interviews. Husband Miao Hangen (chairman of Shenghong/Eastern Shenghong) is the public face; best route is Eastern Shenghong's securities/IR office in Shengze, Suzhou (board secretary Wang Jun). Hurun lists wealth jointly with Miao Hangen.

name: Tench Coxe
current_role: Director, NVIDIA (since 1993; audit and compensation committees); former Managing Director, Sutter Hill Ventures
profile: Venture capitalist who joined Sutter Hill Ventures in 1987 and was managing director 1989-2020, focused on IT investments. Sutter Hill backed Nvidia at its founding and Coxe has sat on Nvidia's board since 1993; his stake made him a billionaire as Nvidia became the AI-datacenter giant. Now Austin-based, he is a philanthropist and was an Artisan Partners director until 2025.
interesting_fact: In January 2026 he and his wife Simone gave $100M, unrestricted, to launch UT Austin's new academic medical center (with an MD Anderson expansion) - one of the largest gifts in the university's history.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he was Director of Marketing and MIS at Digital Communication Associates; he holds an economics BA from Dartmouth and a Harvard MBA. In 2025 he also became a minority owner of MLS club Austin FC.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Austin FC ownership: https://austinfc.com/news/austin-fc-announces-additions-to-clubs-ownership-group. Best formal route is Nvidia corporate PR; Austin philanthropy (UT/Dell Med) is a friendly hook.

name: Mike Adenuga
current_role: Chairman, Globacom (Glo) and Conoil; founder of Conoil Producing
profile: Nigerian tycoon (b. 1953) who made his first million at 26 trading lace and distributing soft drinks, then built Conoil Producing (oil blocks in the Niger Delta) and Globacom, a top-three Nigerian mobile operator that also built the Glo-1 submarine cable to the UK. Also owns 74% of listed fuel marketer Conoil and a stake in Sterling Financial Holdings.
interesting_fact: He paid his way through an MBA at Pace University in New York by working as a taxi driver; his Glo-1 cable runs about 6,100 miles from Nigeria to the UK via Ghana and Portugal.
deep_cut_fact: He personally funded the new Alliance Française de Lagos 'Mike Adenuga Centre' at 9 Osborne Road, Ikoyi: Emmanuel Macron inaugurated its first phase in July 2018 and it fully opened in May 2019, with an auditorium, library, art gallery and outdoor amphitheatre.
notes: Famously media-shy; rarely gives interviews and speaks via Globacom statements. No personal social accounts found. Turned 73 in April 2026. NCC has required Globacom to appoint a separate CEO (2025), so leadership structure may change; route via Globacom corporate communications.

name: Wang Qingtao
current_role: Founder/Chairman, Zhongrong Xinda Group (中融新大集团, formerly Shandong Coking Group), Qingdao — group in court-ordered bankruptcy restructuring since 2023
profile: Shandong-born (1962, Zouping) coal and coking entrepreneur known as the 'coking king'. Built Shandong Tiexiong Energy Coal Chemical from 2003, co-founded Shandong's largest coal-chemical park with Shagang in 2007, then renamed his group Zhongrong Xinda in 2016 and pivoted into bank stakes and mining (incl. a Peru iron mine). The group entered bankruptcy restructuring in 2023.
interesting_fact: Ranked Shandong's richest person on the 2021 New Fortune 500 list (RMB 59.65B), and was vice-chairman of the China Coking Industry Association.
deep_cut_fact: To win steel magnate Shen Wenrong's (Shagang) backing, he visited him in Jiangsu more than a dozen times in three months, telling him: 'You build the biggest steel mill, I'll build the biggest coking plant.' Earlier he served in the army and worked at the Zouping materials bureau before quitting to trade coal.
notes: Group in bankruptcy restructuring (Zibo Intermediate Court, 2023) and he reportedly faces numerous consumption-restriction orders; sensitive subject, not a likely podcast guest. No published personal/office contacts found. Also credited with a patented coke-oven smoke/dust removal device (cnpp.cn/focus/30788.html).

name: Eric Lefkofsky
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chairman, Tempus AI, Inc. (Nasdaq: TEM); cofounder of Lightbank
profile: Serial Chicago entrepreneur who made his fortune cofounding Groupon (2008) with Andrew Mason and longtime partner Brad Keywell, after earlier ventures including Starbelly, InnerWorkings, Echo Global Logistics and MediaOcean. Since 2015 he has run Tempus, which applies AI and molecular data to cancer care; it IPO'd in 2024 at about $6B, his fourth IPO. He also cofounded VC firm Lightbank.
interesting_fact: After a girlfriend dumped him in college at Michigan, he started his first business selling carpets, which he estimates generated hundreds of thousands of dollars in sales.
deep_cut_fact: He is a published author and longtime teacher: his 2007 book 'Accelerated Disruption' (Easton Studio Press) is about how technology reshapes business, and he has taught entrepreneurship/disruptive business models at Kellogg, DePaul and Chicago Booth.
notes: Personal site lefkofsky.com links his X and LinkedIn. Tempus media route is media@tempus.com. Strong AI/data angle (multimodal foundation models, large genomic datasets). Avoid personal/family health topics.

name: Xu Xin
current_role: Non-independent director (since July 2024) and co-actual controller, Hangzhou Changchuan Technology (300604.SZ)
profile: Xu Xin (徐昕, b. 1976) is co-actual controller, with chairman Zhao Yi (reported as her husband), of Hangzhou Changchuan Technology, a ChiNext-listed maker of chip test equipment (testers, handlers, AOI) founded 2008, listed 2017. She joined at founding as finance manager, later CFO and assistant GM; director since 2024.
interesting_fact: Changchuan has grown by buying foreign tool makers: Singapore AOI maker STI, the semiconductor division of Japan's SATO and Malaysia's test-equipment maker EXIS; it now employs about 4,500 people.
deep_cut_fact: Before Changchuan, she spent 1999-2005 as a sales clerk at Hangzhou Weili Trading; a Zhejiang Shuren University graduate, she joined Changchuan at its April 2008 founding as finance manager and ran its finances as CFO in 2015.
notes: Low public profile; husband Zhao Yi (ex-Silan Microelectronics production director, founder/chairman) is the public face. Best route is the company IR/board secretary office (secretary Shao Jingyang). Contacts are company-level, not personal.

name: Zhao Yi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Hangzhou Changchuan Technology (CCTech, SZSE: 300604)
profile: Zhao Yi (b. 1976, Weiyuan, Neijiang, Sichuan) spent 1997-2007 at Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics, rising to production director, then founded Changchuan Technology in 2008 to make chip test and handling equipment (testers, handlers, probers, AOI). CCTech listed in Shenzhen in 2017; AI-driven demand for memory/advanced-packaging test pushed its market cap to ~CNY180B, and it is now pursuing a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: CCTech was billed as China's first listed semiconductor test-equipment company (Shenzhen ChiNext IPO, April 2017, at CNY9.94/share); its value rose from ~CNY27.7B to ~CNY180B in about 18 months to 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He started CCTech in April 2008 with just CNY500,000 in seed capital, launched its first gravity-type test handler that same year, and its in-house analog tester CTA8200 in 2009. The name 'Changchuan' combines the hometowns of the two co-founders: Changxing (Zhejiang) and Sichuan.
notes: Described in Chinese press as low-profile; co-founder and wife Xu Xin is a director (Hurun lists the fortune jointly). Board secretary Shao Jingyang handles investor contact. Hometown-name detail is from Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_Changchuan_Technology).

name: Rakesh Gangwal
current_role: Director, Southwest Airlines (chairman Nov 2024–Aug 2025); co-founder of InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo)
profile: Kolkata-born, IIT Kanpur- and Wharton-educated airline veteran. Gangwal rose through United Airlines and Air France, ran US Airways as CEO and chairman (1998–2001) and then Worldspan. In 2006 he co-founded IndiGo with Rahul Bhatia, starting with one aircraft; it is now India's largest airline. He left IndiGo's board in 2022 and is selling down his stake. He joined Southwest's board in 2024 and still serves as a director after a stint as chairman.
interesting_fact: IndiGo started in 2006 with a single aircraft and grew into India's largest airline by market share. Gangwal's stake in it is the source of his multibillion-dollar fortune.
deep_cut_fact: In April 2022 Gangwal gave ₹100 crore to his alma mater IIT Kanpur to set up the Gangwal School of Medical Sciences and Technology, a planned medical school with a super-speciality hospital on campus. He also joined the school's advisory board. Earlier in his career he was a production and planning engineer at Philips India and a financial analyst at Ford.
notes: Low public profile; he is Miami-based. Avoid the IndiGo governance dispute with Bhatia. No personal social accounts were found. The IIT Kanpur medical school philanthropy is the warmest angle.

name: Paul-Louis Halley
profile: French retail entrepreneur who co-founded Promodès in 1961 with his father and brother; it merged with Carrefour in 1999, leaving him its principal shareholder (~11%). He died on 6 December 2003 in a TBM 700 plane crash on approach to Oxford Airport.
notes: Deceased 6 Dec 2003 (plane crash near Oxford, UK). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul-Louis_Halley. Skip for outreach.

name: John Catsimatidis
current_role: Owner, Chairman and CEO, Red Apple Group (Gristedes/D'Agostino, United Refining, WABC radio); director, Turning Point Brands
profile: Greek-born (Nisyros, 1948), Harlem-raised grocer who dropped out of NYU to buy into the store he clerked at, opened the first Red Apple in 1971 and later bought Gristedes. In 1986 he acquired Pennsylvania refiner United Refining (Warren, PA), now the core of his energy holdings, alongside NYC real estate. Since 2020 he has owned WABC radio, where he hosts 'The Cats Roundtable'.
interesting_fact: He hosts a weekly political talk-radio show, The Cats Roundtable, and bought the station that airs it (WABC 770 AM) in 2020; he ran for NYC mayor as a Republican in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil he dabbled in aviation: he invested in charter carrier Capitol Air in 1984 and in 1992 launched his own charter airline, Capitol Air Express, which flew from 1993 to 1996 in the old Capitol Air livery. He studied electrical engineering at NYU (Brooklyn Tech '66) before quitting 8 credits short.

public_contacts.value: The Cats Roundtable (WABC 770 AM) - linked from his official site

notes: Very media-friendly; hosts his own radio show and does many interviews, so a guest-swap/radio angle may work. Red Apple Group HQ is 800 Third Ave, NYC (no published press email found). Wrote a memoir, 'How Far Do You Want to Go?' (listed on his site).

name: Trevor Rees-Jones
current_role: Founder, Chief Oil & Gas (Dallas); co-founder of The Rees-Jones Foundation
profile: Dallas oil-and-gas bankruptcy lawyer (Thompson & Knight) who switched to investing in wells in 1984 and founded Chief Oil & Gas in 1994. Chief was an early Barnett Shale and Marcellus driller; he sold Barnett assets to Devon in 2006 and Chief's Marcellus business to Chesapeake in 2022, and remains active in oil, gas and mining ventures plus large North Texas philanthropy.
interesting_fact: By 2005 Chief Oil & Gas was the second-largest producer in the Barnett Shale, having drilled more than 250 wells, and its 2006 Barnett sale to Devon and Crosstex brought roughly $2.6 billion in cash.
deep_cut_fact: He earned Eagle Scout with Troop 70 in 1966, and the Circle Ten Council's Trevor Rees-Jones Scout Camp is named after him; his foundation also funded the Rees-Jones Foundation Leadership Veranda at the Boy Scouts' Summit Bechtel Reserve.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews but did several with Hart Energy and D CEO. Foundation emails were taken from search snippets of the official contact page (site blocked direct fetch) - re-verify before use. Also a Dartmouth trustee (2010-14) and TCU trustee.

name: Lin Shu-hong
current_role: Co-founder and President (總裁) of Chang Chun Group, Taiwan petrochemicals (stepped down as chairman end-2013)
profile: Lin Shu-hong (林書鴻, also Suhon Lin, b. 1928) co-founded Chang Chun Group in 1949 with classmates Tseng Shin-yi and M.K. Liao on about $100. It grew into one of Asia's largest private petrochemical groups (resins, chemicals, electronic materials) with plants in Taiwan, China and SE Asia. Though he left the chairmanship in 2013, in his mid-90s he still toured plants weekly.
interesting_fact: Called 'the Edison of petrochemicals': in the early days he ran 5-6 experiments a day to perfect a plywood adhesive that won over 60+ Taiwanese plywood makers and was even sold to the US military. He was elected to ITRI's first class of Fellows (2012) and won a National S&T contribution award (2016).
deep_cut_fact: At 94 he still visited the Hsinchu, Miaoli, Mailiao, Changhua and Kaohsiung plants every week, read nightly before bed, and recommended Kazuo Inamori's book on work, which he had covered in sticky tabs and notes.
notes: Born 1 Aug 1928 (age ~98); Forbes 2026 still lists him and no death report found, but confirm before outreach. Famously low-profile; group is private with no press/IR desk found (website behind Cloudflare). Any approach would go via Chang Chun Group corporate office in Taipei.

name: Carlos Bulgheroni
current_role: Deceased (died 3 September 2016, aged 71, in the United States)
profile: Argentine oil and gas magnate who, with brother Alejandro, built Bridas (founded by their father) into Argentina's leading private energy group, later partnering with BP and CNOOC in Pan American Energy. He died of cancer in September 2016; Alejandro now leads the family business.
notes: Deceased: died 3 Sep 2016 (sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Bulgheroni ; https://www.pagina12.com.ar/diario/economia/2-308544-2016-09-04.html). Wealth was shared with brother Alejandro Bulgheroni (alive, chairman of Pan American Energy Group) - he would be the relevant outreach target instead.

name: Vladimir Kim
current_role: Major shareholder, KAZ Minerals (private copper miner, Kazakhstan/Kyrgyzstan); former chairman of Kazakhmys/KAZ Minerals
profile: Vladimir Kim joined Zhezkazgantsvetmet, later Kazakhmys, in 1995 and chaired Kazakhmys from 2005. It became the first Kazakh company listed in London. After the 2014 split he kept a big stake in copper producer KAZ Minerals, which he and Oleg Novachuk took private in 2021; it runs the Aktogay and Bozshakol mines. In 2025 he sold his majority stake in Kazakhmys Corp. to Nurlan Artykbaev.
interesting_fact: He is descended from Koreans whom Stalin deported to Kazakhstan, and for years he was ranked Kazakhstan's richest person.
deep_cut_fact: Kim was born on 29 October 1960 in the village of Slavyanka (now Myrzakent) in South Kazakhstan. He trained as an architect, graduating from the Almaty Architecture and Construction Institute in 1982, and holds a Candidate of Technical Sciences degree. After independence he did business internships in Germany, Switzerland and South Korea.
notes: Very private; he gives no interviews and has no social presence. Copper for electrification and data centers is a relevant angle. Approach only via KAZ Minerals corporate communications (head office now in Dubai). Politically connected, so avoid political topics.

name: Liu Hanyuan
current_role: Chairman, Tongwei Group; NPC deputy and vice chairman of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce
profile: Liu left a job at the Meishan county hydropower bureau in Sichuan to build a fish-feed business (founded 1986) that became Tongwei Group, a global leader in aquafeed. Tongwei later moved into polysilicon and solar cells, becoming one of the world's largest PV manufacturers. He is a prominent lawmaker-advocate for solar and renewable-energy policy.
interesting_fact: Tongwei ranks among the world's largest players in two unrelated industries at once: aquaculture feed and solar (polysilicon/cells). Liu regularly files NPC/CPPCC proposals pushing PV, e.g. solar to cut smog and tax cuts for the PV industry.
deep_cut_fact: In spring 1983, aged ~18, he pooled 200 yuan savings plus money from his parents selling two pigs (500 yuan total) to build a 64 m2 submerged fish cage in a Meishan canal; stocking 185 kg of carp yielded 1,390 kg by autumn, reportedly a Sichuan record for fish yield per unit area.
notes: ir_email is the published board-secretary (Yan Ke) contact of listed Tongwei Co. (600438) per its 2024 annual report summary; Tongwei's English site publishes many news items about Liu's policy proposals, a good angle for an energy podcast.

name: Gordon Getty
current_role: Composer and philanthropist (Gordon P. Getty Family Foundation); Getty Oil heir
profile: Son of oil tycoon J. Paul Getty, he led the 1984 sale of Getty Oil to Texaco for $10.1B and in 1985 split the family trust into separate trusts. Now in his 90s, he is a working classical composer (operas Plump Jack, Usher House, The Canterville Ghost, Goodbye, Mr. Chips) and a major San Francisco arts donor; he co-founded PlumpJack Winery with Gavin Newsom in 1995.
interesting_fact: He has given more than $450 million to his philanthropic foundation since 2008, and New Century Chamber Orchestra dedicated its entire 2025-26 season in his honor; he was one of ten inaugural inductees into Opera America's Opera Hall of Fame (2020).
deep_cut_fact: An English-literature graduate of the University of San Francisco and longtime poet, he writes his own librettos; his most-performed vocal work is The White Election (1981), a cycle setting 31 Emily Dickinson poems for soprano and piano, performed at Lincoln Center and the Hermitage Theatre.

public_contacts.value: Nancy Shear Arts Services - sheararts@gmail.com (PR/press for his music only)
mail@rorkmusic.com (Rork Music, his publisher; music inquiries only)

notes: Born 1933; very old and private on business matters. Only published routes are music-related (publisher Rork Music, PR via Nancy Shear Arts Services); his site says funding requests are discarded. An energy-angle pitch is a stretch; an arts/legacy framing fits better. Wikipedia notes 2026-released documents showing past Epstein correspondence - sensitive topic.

name: Li Min
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Rockchip Electronics Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603893), Fuzhou
profile: Li Min cofounded Rockchip in Fuzhou in 2001 with Huang Xu and remains chairman (reappointed general manager in Jan 2025). Rockchip designs SoCs for AIoT devices, tablets and edge-AI products and listed in Shanghai in 2020; Li holds roughly 37% of the company, the source of his fortune.
interesting_fact: Rockchip, a Fuzhou chip designer, counts Intel, Samsung and Google among its customers and focuses on intelligent IoT and edge-AI processors.
deep_cut_fact: In December 2025 he donated 175,000 Rockchip shares (worth roughly RMB 31M at the time) to the education foundation of his alma mater, Fuzhou No. 1 Middle School (福州一中), 'to give back to his alma mater'.
notes: Low media profile; English name in Chinese is 励民. Best route is via Rockchip's securities/IR department. Some unofficial sites say he was born 1965 and graduated Zhejiang University 1991 - not verified.

name: Steven Hao
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Cognition (maker of the Devin AI software-engineering agent)
profile: MIT-trained competitive programmer and former early engineer at Scale AI who co-founded Cognition in late 2023 with Scott Wu and Walden Yan. Cognition's Devin autonomous coding agent (and its 2025 acquisition of Windsurf) drove rapid valuation jumps, making Hao a billionaire per Forbes.
interesting_fact: All three Cognition co-founders were International Olympiad in Informatics competitors; Forbes reported that the company's rapid growth made CTO Hao a billionaire within about two years of founding.
deep_cut_fact: At IOI 2014 in Taipei he placed 6th in the world for the United States, scoring perfect 100s on five of six problems (525/600) to win a gold medal.
notes: No published press email found; only company social accounts. CEO Scott Wu is the usual public face; Hao is the technical lead and appears at engineering conferences (e.g. GitNation speaker profile), a possible route.

name: Fan Hongwei
current_role: Chairman, Hengli Petrochemical Co. (SSE: 600346); Vice Chairman, Hengli Group
profile: Born 1967 in Wujiang, Suzhou, Fan co-founded what became Hengli Group with her husband Chen Jianhua, starting in textiles in 1994 and integrating upstream into polyester, PTA and a giant refinery-petrochemical complex on Changxing Island, Dalian. She chairs listed Hengli Petrochemical; Hengli Group posted 2024 revenue of RMB 871.5bn (Fortune Global 500 #81).
interesting_fact: Hengli's integrated 'from a drop of oil to a bolt of cloth' chain helped break foreign dominance of PX and PTA feedstocks in China; in July 2025 Fan was one of 100 private entrepreneurs given a national 'outstanding builder' award in Beijing.
deep_cut_fact: Hengli began in 1994 as the Wujiang Chemical Fiber Weaving Factory in Shengze, Suzhou, with just 27 employees; when Hengli Group was formally set up in 2003, Fan became its general manager running production and operations.
notes: hlzq@hengli.com is Hengli Petrochemical's board-office/investor mailbox (listed in 2025 and 2026 earnings-call notices); Chinese-language approach advisable. Very low international media profile.

name: Carlos
profile: Carlos Alberto Bulgheroni (1945-2016), Argentine co-owner (with brother Alejandro) of the family energy group Bridas, died on 3 September 2016. Record matched via source of wealth Bridas and shared_with Alejandro Bulgheroni.
notes: DECEASED 3 Sep 2016 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Bulgheroni). Name field is truncated ('Carlos'); country listed as Spain is wrong - he was Argentine. For Bridas/Pan American Energy, the living family principal is his brother Alejandro Bulgheroni.

name: Romesh Wadhwani
current_role: Founder & Chairman, SAIGroup (SymphonyAI, ConcertAI); Founder & Chairman, Wadhwani Foundation
profile: Born in Karachi in 1947 and educated at IIT Bombay and Carnegie Mellon (PhD), Wadhwani made his fortune founding Aspect Development and later ran software PE firm Symphony Technology Group. He now heads SAIGroup, which includes SymphonyAI (backed by his $1B commitment) and ConcertAI. His Wadhwani Foundation funds entrepreneurship and AI-for-good work in India.
interesting_fact: Aspect Development, which he founded in 1991, was acquired by i2 Technologies in 1999 for $9.3 billion in stock. In 2020 India awarded him the Padma Shri.
deep_cut_fact: Before Aspect, he spent a decade running two startups. One was American Robot Corporation, which made computer-integrated manufacturing software. The other was Compu-Guard Corporation, an early technology-enabled energy-management company.

public_contacts.value: Chris Gale (Gale Strategies), SymphonyAI media contact: Chris@GaleStrategies.com

notes: The Compu-Guard energy-management startup is a natural hook for an energy-focused podcast. He also sits on the boards of trustees of CSIS and the Kennedy Center. The best route is SymphonyAI's PR contact.

name: Paul Foster
current_role: Founder & CEO, Franklin Mountain Investments (El Paso, TX); former founder/chairman of Western Refining
profile: A Baylor-trained CPA who kept the books for small Southwest refineries, Foster took over bankrupt El Paso Refining with partners in 1992, built Western Refining and sold it to Tesoro in 2017 ($6.4B deal). Via Franklin Mountain Investments he holds 30+ businesses (real estate, restaurants, sports); in 2025 he sold Franklin Mountain Energy for about $2.5B.
interesting_fact: He is part owner of the El Paso Chihuahuas Triple-A baseball team (via MountainStar Sports Group) and in 2007 gave $50M to help create the Paul L. Foster School of Medicine at Texas Tech in El Paso.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Lovington, New Mexico (class of 1975), he earned an accounting degree from Baylor in 1979 and then started out working at the local refinery back in Lovington before moving to El Paso.
notes: Very relevant to energy angle: serves on the Dallas Fed Energy Advisory Council and was appointed by Gov. Abbott to the ERCOT board selection committee (https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-appoints-foster-to-ercot-board-selection-committee). Best route is Franklin Mountain Investments' general inbox.

name: Torbjorn Tornqvist
current_role: Former co-founder and CEO of Gunvor Group (oil trader, since renamed Centalion); stepped down Dec 2025 in a management buyout; head of Artemis Racing sailing team
profile: Stockholm-born (1953), Geneva-based oil trader who co-founded Gunvor in 1997 and grew it into one of the world's largest independent energy traders. He bought out co-founder Gennady Timchenko's stake in 2014. In Dec 2025 he resigned as CEO and agreed to sell his ~86% stake to ~60 senior employees, partly vendor-financed; the firm has since rebranded as Centalion.
interesting_fact: He founded the Artemis Racing sailing team in 2006, which reached the Louis Vuitton Cup final in the 2013 America's Cup challenger series and helped bring Sweden back into the America's Cup.
deep_cut_fact: He came to competitive sailing late: he started crewing with Russell Coutts at the Swan Worlds, Coutts 'talked me into a TP52', and they won the MedCup and the championship in the same season, after only about three years of sailing. He still helms his own RC44 on the 44Cup circuit.
notes: No personal or office contacts published. He has left Gunvor/Centalion, so company press office is no longer a route to him. Artemis Racing (sailing) is the only active public affiliation. Avoid Russia/Timchenko/US Treasury topics; they are the context of his exit.

name: Pyotr Aven
current_role: Co-founder/shareholder of LetterOne (L1) and Alfa Group; former chairman of Alfa-Bank (2011-2022); art collector based in Surrey, UK
profile: Moscow-born economist Pyotr (Petr) Aven was Russia's minister of foreign economic relations in 1992 before joining Alfa-Bank, which he ran as president (1994-2011) and chairman until 2022. With Mikhail Fridman and partners he co-owns Alfa Group and LetterOne. Sanctioned by the EU/UK in 2022, he stepped off LetterOne's board and now focuses on his art collection and writing.
interesting_fact: He owns what is described as the largest/best private collection of Russian art (Goncharova, Petrov-Vodkin, Chagall, Kandinsky), lent to Tate, the Royal Academy, MoMA and Fondation Louis Vuitton; in 2022 he bought a building in Riga for a planned private museum.
deep_cut_fact: His collecting began in childhood with stamps and toy cars; the first painting he bought was a 1920s still life by Pavel Kuznetsov. As a young economist he was seconded to IIASA in Laxenburg, Austria, and he has lectured at Moscow's Higher School of Economics since 2007.
notes: Under EU/UK/US sanctions since 2022 - check legal/editorial implications before any engagement. petraven.info describes itself as his website (email appears in its schema.org metadata); appears to be a reputation-style site, so treat accounts linked there with some caution. Books: 'The Age of Berezovsky', 'Gaidar's Revolution' (free at petr-aven-books.com).

name: Liu Debing
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director & Chairman, Knowledge Atlas Technology / Zhipu AI (Z.ai), HKEX: 2513
profile: Co-founder and chairman of Zhipu AI, the Beijing developer of the GLM large language models, spun out of Tsinghua University's knowledge-engineering lab (AMiner) in 2019. He handles fundraising and business decisions. Zhipu listed in Hong Kong in January 2026, billed as the world's first listed LLM company, raising about $560M, and in 2026 changed its English short name to Z.AI.
interesting_fact: Speaking to Bloomberg TV on the day Zhipu listed, Liu said the AI price war would go global: if Zhipu can keep its prices at about one-seventh of its rivals', international customers will have to accept it.
deep_cut_fact: Before Zhipu, Liu earned a computer science PhD at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Computing Technology, then worked at Technicolor's China research institute before joining Tsinghua as a senior engineer. He was one of Zhipu's six founders.
notes: Zhipu is on the U.S. Entity List (added 2025). No dedicated IR or press email found in its HKEX filings; best route is the company website or its HK IR channel. Chinese-language outreach is advisable.

name: Cho Jyh-jer
current_role: Retired; former Vice Chairman of MediaTek (retired June 2015)
profile: MediaTek co-founding veteran who joined as president in 1997 when the chip designer was spun off from United Microelectronics (UMC), and was promoted to vice chairman in 2005 to focus on new products and strategy. He retired in June 2015; his wealth comes mainly from his MediaTek stake. No public role since retirement was found.
interesting_fact: One of the founding veterans who fought alongside MediaTek chairman Tsai Ming-kai from the company's optical-disc-drive chip days, before MediaTek became one of the world's top smartphone chip designers.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer from National Chiao Tung University (communication engineering), he came out of NCTU's famed 'Lab 307' under Prof. Wu Chung-yu, one of the first master's cohorts in a lab that produced many of Taiwan's IC-design leaders.
notes: Very private, retired since 2015; no published personal/office contact found. Deep-cut fact taken from search-indexed text of GVM/NYCU pages (gvm.com.tw not fetchable here) - double-check before use. Alive status not confirmed but no death report found; still on 2026 Forbes real-time list.

name: N. Murray Edwards
current_role: Executive Chairman, Canadian Natural Resources Ltd.; owner, Edco Financial Holdings; chairman/co-owner, Calgary Sports & Entertainment Corp. (Calgary Flames)
profile: Regina-born lawyer-turned-financier who built his fortune backing and running Canadian energy companies, above all oil-sands giant Canadian Natural Resources (executive chairman), plus Ensign Energy, Magellan Aerospace and Imperial Metals. He also leads the Calgary Flames ownership group and owns Resorts of the Canadian Rockies. He moved his residency from Calgary to London in 2016.
interesting_fact: In high school Edwards worked four nights a week as a hockey referee; he also worked on a garbage crew and had a summer job at a beer factory with unlimited beer on breaks.
deep_cut_fact: A keen investor as a student, Edwards rang the bell on Oct 3, 2002 to launch the 'N. Murray Edwards MarketWatch' stock-ticker board he donated to his alma mater's business school in Saskatoon, years before it was renamed the Edwards School of Business (2007).

public_contacts.value: https://www.cnrl.com/contact (Canadian Natural contact page incl. Investor Relations link)

notes: Very low public profile; rarely gives interviews. Best route is likely via Canadian Natural's investor relations or the Edwards School of Business (USask), where he sits on the Dean's Advisory Council. Lives primarily in London (UK) since 2016.

name: James
profile: Most likely James K. 'J.K.' Irving, chairman of J.D. Irving Ltd. and brother of Arthur Irving (Irving Oil), with whom the Hurun 2014 entry is shared. He died on 21 June 2024, aged 96, in Saint John, New Brunswick. Record skipped per instructions.
notes: Entry gives only the first name 'James' (Irving Group, shared with Arthur Irving), so identity is inferred. J.K. Irving died 21 June 2024 (https://www.cbc.ca/1.7243426); Arthur Irving died in May 2024. If the entry meant J.K.'s son James D. 'Jim' Irving (co-CEO of J.D. Irving Ltd.), he is alive and would need separate research.

name: Alejandro Bulgheroni
current_role: Chairman, Pan American Energy Group (Argentina); owner of Bulgheroni family wine estates incl. Bodega Garzón (Uruguay)
profile: Argentine industrial engineer (b. 1943, Rufino) who joined his father's Bridas Corp. in 1965 and ran it with brother Carlos from 1985; sold 50% to CNOOC and in 2017 merged with BP's Argentine assets to form Pan American Energy Group, Argentina's largest private integrated energy firm. Lives in Uruguay; owns 10+ wineries worldwide and a large dairy complex.
interesting_fact: In 1992 he secured some of the first gas exploration concessions Turkmenistan granted to a foreign energy company. His Garzón wine club membership reportedly costs $200,000.
deep_cut_fact: His wine empire began as an energy idea: in 2006 he stood on a windy Uruguayan hilltop scouting a wind-farm site, advisers suggested vines instead, and when told quality would take 6-8 years he quipped, 'How old do you think I am?' (Wine Spectator, 2018).
notes: The PAE email is the company's general 'otras consultas' inbox, not a press desk. Son Marcos Bulgheroni is PAE Group CEO. The wine/energy angle (wind farm turned vineyard) is a natural hook.

name: Li Chunan
current_role: Chairman of Dalian Linton NC Machine Co. (Linton Technologies, BSE: 835368); cofounder and major shareholder of Longi Green Energy.
profile: Li Chunan (b. 1968, Nanyang, Henan) cofounded Longi Green Energy, one of the world's largest solar wafer and module makers, with Lanzhou University classmates Li Zhenguo and Zhong Baoshen. He also chairs Dalian-based Linton, which makes crystal-growing, wafer-slicing and other equipment for the solar and semiconductor industries.
interesting_fact: Longi's three cofounders were college friends from undergraduate days at Lanzhou University; Li studied in its physics department (entered 1986) and serves as a trustee of the Lanzhou University Education Foundation.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar, he was an inventor of magnetic separation gear: he holds a 1997 Chinese utility-model patent for a 'suspended permanent-magnet iron remover' (ZL97233990.6) and a 2010 invention patent for a circulating-oil-cooled electromagnetic iron remover, from his Fushun magnet-electric company days (cofounded 1993).
notes: IR email is the Linton board office contact (named staffer Jin Yao, tel 0411-62638881) published in an Aug 2025 shareholder-meeting notice. Deep-cut source is a user-contributed Chinese bio page (patent numbers are checkable on CNIPA). Avoid: 2024 CSRC Liaoning fine for insider-info leak.

name: Nikolai Buinov
current_role: Co-founder, chairman of the board and majority shareholder, Irkutsk Oil Company (INK)
profile: Krasnoyarsk-born (1967) founder of Irkutsk Oil Company, Russia's largest independent private oil producer. He started in timber, co-founded fuel supplier Bodaibo Energy with his father in 1995, bought his first oil licence in 1997, and in 2022 bought back Goldman Sachs' stake in INK. INK is now moving into petrochemicals with its Irkutsk Polymer Plant near Ust-Kut.
interesting_fact: In 2025 INK began launching the Irkutsk Polymer Plant near Ust-Kut, the first polymer plant in Eastern Siberia and the company's largest investment project.
deep_cut_fact: A transport-university graduate (St Petersburg, 1990), he financed the restoration of the historic Wawelberg Bank building on Nevsky Prospekt, a long-stalled St Petersburg project completed in 2021 and now operating as a hotel.
notes: Low public profile, based in Irkutsk. Best route is likely INK's press service via irkutskoil.ru (site unreachable from here, so no contact verified). Russian energy company; check sanctions exposure before outreach.

name: Otto Toto Sugiri
current_role: Cofounder and President Director (CEO), PT DCI Indonesia Tbk
profile: Indonesian tech pioneer (b. 1953, Bandung; RWTH Aachen grad) dubbed Indonesia's 'Bill Gates'. After running IT at Bank Bali from 1983 he founded Sigma Cipta Caraka (1989, now Telkomsigma) and cofounded Indonet (1994), Indonesia's first ISP. He has led DCI Indonesia, the country's largest data-center operator, which listed in 2021.
interesting_fact: DCI was the first data center in Southeast Asia to earn Uptime Institute's Tier IV Certification of Constructed Facility (2020); he was EY World Entrepreneur of the Year Indonesia 2023.
deep_cut_fact: In 1999 he founded Balicamp (PT Sigma Karya Sempurna), an export-oriented software development campus in Pacung village, Bali, meant to let young Indonesian programmers compete internationally.
notes: Received Bintang Jasa Utama from President Jokowi (Aug 2024). Several Bank Bali colleagues (e.g. Marina Budiman) are his long-time cofounders. Low-profile; route via DCI corporate secretary.

name: Sid Bass
current_role: Private investor, Fort Worth, Texas (Bass family oil and investment fortune)
profile: Sid Richardson Bass (b. 1942; Yale, Stanford GSB) took charge of the Fort Worth family oil fortune of great-uncle Sid W. Richardson and father Perry Bass in the late 1960s, growing a ~$50m company into a multibillion-dollar investment group. Now a low-profile private investor and arts philanthropist.
interesting_fact: He and the Bass family were the largest shareholders in The Walt Disney Company from 1984, backing the arrival of Michael Eisner's management team; his 2006 $25m gift to the Metropolitan Opera was then the largest individual gift in its history.
deep_cut_fact: In 1970, at about 27, he recruited his Stanford business-school classmate Richard Rainwater (then 26, at Goldman Sachs) to manage the Bass family investments - a partnership that ran until 1986 and made Rainwater one of the era's legendary dealmakers.
notes: Extremely private; no published office/press contact found. Only realistic route is via Fort Worth institutions he supports or a warm intro. Net worth ~$3.9-4.6bn.

name: Thomas Siebel
current_role: Chairman and CEO, C3 AI (NYSE: AI); resumed the CEO role in May 2026
profile: Chicago-born Tom Siebel was an Oracle executive, then founded CRM pioneer Siebel Systems, which Oracle bought for $5.8bn in 2006. In 2009 he founded C3 AI (originally C3 Energy), an enterprise-AI software company that started out serving utilities. He stepped back to executive chairman in 2025 and returned as CEO in May 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2019 he set up a C3 AI programme that pays for employees to earn the University of Illinois online Master of Computer Science. Graduates get a 15% raise, a $25,000 bonus and extra stock options.
deep_cut_fact: Before he had a computer-science degree he earned a BA in history at Illinois, and he later endowed a Thomas M. Siebel Chair in the History of Science there. In 2015 his foundation launched the Siebel Energy Institute to fund research on managing power-grid data.
notes: A natural fit for an energy/AI podcast: C3 started as C3 Energy, serving utilities, and he wrote the book 'Digital Transformation' (2019). He stepped back from the CEO role in 2025 for health reasons and returned in May 2026; don't raise health in outreach. He also founded the Montana Meth Project and the Siebel Scholars programme.

name: Yang Yazhen
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Yang Weidong) of Satellite Chemical Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002648), Jiaxing, Zhejiang
profile: Yang Yazhen (registered in filings as YANG YA ZHEN) and her husband Yang Weidong are the actual controllers of Satellite Chemical, the Jiaxing-based maker of acrylic acid/esters, polymers and C2/C3 petrochemicals; she held about 11.7% directly as of 2020, with the couple controlling ~50% in total. Her husband is chairman and president; she keeps a low public profile.
interesting_fact: Satellite Chemical, which grew from a business Yang Weidong founded in 1992, is now a leading global acrylic acid producer and in Nov 2026 announced a ~$3.1bn propylene and downstream materials project in Lianyungang including a 2 million t/yr propane dehydrogenation unit.
notes: Very private; no interviews or personal bio found. Not an executive per recent filings (VP & board secretary is Shen Xiaowei). Best route is via the company's board office/IR (IR@weixing.com.cn, as published in the 2024 annual report summary). Identity per SZSE equity-change report 2020: https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk02/finalpage/2020-11-21/fcfe55cd-8d27-417f-8476-d827510808cb.PDF

name: George Bishop
current_role: Founder & Chairman/CEO, GeoSouthern Energy (The Woodlands, Texas)
profile: Mississippi-born petroleum geologist (MSU 1958) who founded GeoSouthern Energy in 1981 and became a billionaire when it sold its early Eagle Ford acreage to Devon for $6B in 2013. He redeployed into Haynesville gas via JVs with Blackstone Credit (sold 2021, $1.85B) and Williams (GEP Haynesville II, which sold a majority interest in its South Mansfield assets to Japan's JERA in Oct 2025).
interesting_fact: He and wife Kathy gave Mississippi State University $100 million in 2023 for scholarships, the largest gift to a higher-education institution in Mississippi's history.
deep_cut_fact: Received an honorary Doctor of Public Service from MSU in May 2019. On his giving he said: 'Mississippi State opened many doors for me... I especially want to help students that have the desire to work but don't have the funds.' He also owns the Eagleford Restaurant in Cuero, Texas, near his ranch.
notes: Born 1937 (about 89). Extremely private; GeoSouthern's website (geosouthern.com) is a placeholder with no contact info. Possible warm route via Mississippi State University Foundation, where he is a major donor and former board member. Kirkland & Ellis advised GEP Haynesville II on the 2025 JERA deal.

name: Lynn Schusterman
current_role: Co-Founder and Chair Emerita, Charles and Lynn Schusterman Family Philanthropies (Tulsa)
profile: Tulsa philanthropist (b. 1939, Kansas City) whose fortune comes from Samson Resources, the oil & gas firm her late husband Charles founded in 1971; most assets were sold to a KKR-led group for $7.2B in 2011, with some oil & gas holdings kept in Samson Energy. She led the family foundation 2000-2018 and is now chair emerita; the family has given away $3.5B+.
interesting_fact: She and Stacy Schusterman (the foundation's current chair) received the Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy in 2022 (alongside Dolly Parton), and in 2026 both were named to the TIME100 Philanthropy list.
deep_cut_fact: She began volunteering with the National Council of Jewish Women in the early 1960s; after Charles died in 2000 she became the first woman to lead a large Jewish philanthropic organization, and in 1994 she helped found Hillel in the former Soviet Union.
notes: Aged 87; energy link is legacy (Samson Resources/Samson Energy). Best route is the foundation's media inbox. Hillel-FSU detail is cited on her Wikipedia page (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynn_Schusterman); NCJW/first-woman details from JWA. Spoke at ROI's final summit in Jerusalem, June 2026.

name: Chey Tae-won
current_role: Chairman, SK Group (SK Inc.); Chairman, Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry
profile: Has chaired SK Group since 1998. SK is one of Korea's largest conglomerates, spanning energy and refining (SK Innovation), telecom (SK Telecom) and memory chips (SK Hynix, a key HBM supplier for AI data centers). He has pushed SK hard into AI, batteries and clean energy, and has chaired the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry since 2021.
interesting_fact: He has championed 'social value' as a business metric. Under his 'Double Bottom Line' initiative (2018), SK companies measure and report their social impact in monetary terms alongside profit.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a physics degree from Korea University, completed the economics PhD program at the University of Chicago, co-authored a 2019 Stanford business case on SK's Double Bottom Line, and has twice been elected President of the Korea Handball Federation.
notes: Sources disagree on the Chicago degree. SK's site says he holds a PhD; other bios say he completed the PhD program. Avoid his 2013 conviction and his divorce case. Given SK Hynix (HBM) and SK's energy businesses, he fits both the data-center and energy themes. Best route is SK's US media team; KCCI is an alternative.

name: Liu Jincheng
current_role: Founder and chairman, EVE Energy (亿纬锂能, Shenzhen-listed 300014), Huizhou
profile: Hubei-born battery engineer (PhD) who studied electrochemistry at Wuhan University and founded EVE Energy around 2000-01. EVE makes consumer, EV (incl. BMW Neue Klasse cylindrical cells) and storage batteries, ranked No. 2 in energy-storage cell shipments in 2025, and now pitches itself as an 'energy base for the AI world'.
interesting_fact: At EVE's 25th anniversary he recalled that China's smart-meter procurement rules once explicitly banned domestic batteries; EVE ran hundreds of battery-explosion tests to break the import monopoly. His motto: 'Lithium battery, I love you' is 'a lifelong mission, not a slogan'.
deep_cut_fact: He describes himself as the first engineer in China to do lithium-battery safety research, some 40 years ago; EVE also funds a named 'EVE Energy Chair Professor' at his alma mater Wuhan University.
notes: No personal social accounts found. Best route is EVE's board office / IR (board secretary Jiang Min per company IR page). Chinese-language outreach advisable. Company says it was founded 2001 (Forbes says 2000).

name: Ray Davis
current_role: Managing Partner, Majority Owner and Board Chairman, Texas Rangers; Chairman & CEO, Avatar Investments L.P.
profile: Born 1941 in Overton, Texas, Davis co-founded pipeline giant Energy Transfer with Kelcy Warren in the mid-1990s and was co-CEO until retiring in 2007 (left the board 2022). He now runs family investment firm Avatar Investments in Dallas and is managing partner of the Texas Rangers, which his group bought in 2010 and which won the 2023 World Series.
interesting_fact: Under his ownership the Rangers won the first World Series title in the franchise's 63-year history (2023) and opened the $1.25B retractable-roof Globe Life Field in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: He received the Navy SEAL Foundation's 'Fire in the Gut' Award in 2024 and the BENS Eisenhower Award in 2017; his listed interests are ranching, bird hunting and reading.
notes: Famously press-shy ('doesn't grant interviews'; called his 2015 Dallas Morning News interview possibly his last). Best route is via Texas Rangers communications. Energy Transfer roots make him relevant to the energy angle.

name: Francois Perrodo
current_role: Chairman, Perenco (Franco-British independent oil & gas producer)
profile: French businessman (b. 1977, Singapore) who chairs Perenco, the oil and gas company founded by his late father Hubert, which specialises in extending the life of mature fields the majors have left. The family (with mother Carrie) also owns Bordeaux wine estates such as Chateau Labegorce and is diversifying via its London family office BNF Capital and PE firm Perwyn.
interesting_fact: A serious amateur endurance racer and car collector: he races for AF Corse at Le Mans/ELMS and owns a Ferrari 250 GTO (bought in 2016 for ~$56.4m) plus several McLaren F1s and the only privately owned Toyota TS020 Le Mans car.
deep_cut_fact: He read physics at St Peter's College, Oxford, where he captained the University polo team in 1999, then earned an engineering degree from the French petroleum school IFP School (2002) and an INSEAD MBA in Singapore, his birthplace.
notes: Private; best route is Perenco's media agency Celicourt. His Instagram (fanchracing) covers cars/racing - motorsport is a good rapport hook. Note: Sunday Times entry is shared with mother Carrie Perrodo.

name: Americo Amorim
profile: Américo Amorim (1934-2017), Portugal's richest man at his death, built the family cork business Corticeira Amorim into the world's largest cork producer and held energy (Galp) and banking interests. He died on 13 July 2017. His daughter Paula Amorim now leads the family's interests.
notes: Deceased 13 July 2017 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Am%C3%A9rico_Amorim ; AP via https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/americo-amorim-thought-portugals-richest-man-dies-48614152). Energy-related successor is Paula Amorim (Galp chair).

name: Zhang Hong
current_role: Co-owner, with her husband Lin Jianhua (chairman), of Hangzhou First Applied Material Co. (Fu Si Te, SSE: 603806)
profile: Zhang Hong appears on the Hurun lists jointly with her husband Lin Jianhua as the couple behind Hangzhou First Applied Material (福斯特). The company was founded in 2003 and is the world's largest maker of EVA encapsulant film for solar modules. Lin is chairman and controlling shareholder; Zhang has no public executive role at the company.
interesting_fact: First Applied Material was the lead drafter of China's national standards for EVA and co-extruded encapsulant film used in solar modules (GB/T 29848, GB/T 45939).
notes: Very private, with no individual public profile; Hurun lists the wealth as '林建华、张虹夫妇' (2022 list, No. 83). Outreach would go to the company's securities department (fst-zqb@firstpvm.com). Her husband Lin Jianhua is the public face.

name: Saban Cemil Kazanci
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Kazancı Holding; Chairman, Aksa Energy and Aksa Electricity
profile: Istanbul-born (1961) son of Ali Metin Kazancı, he started in the family's generator-making business and drove its growth into Aksa Energy (1997) and the broader Kazancı Holding (generators, power, gas and electricity distribution). Aksa Energy now runs gas and renewable plants in Turkey, Central Asia and Africa, and is widely ranked Turkey's richest person.
interesting_fact: Aksa Energy is the largest Turkish investor in Uzbekistan's power sector (1,220 MW after the 430 MW Talimercan plant) and is building out Africa, incl. an 825 MW Takoradi plant in Ghana.
deep_cut_fact: He has been awarded Uzbekistan's Order of Friendship (Dustlik), recognising Aksa's power-plant investments there.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Aksa Energy corporate communications (the press_email is listed as Corporate Communications) or Kazancı Holding general contact. Aksa IR site: https://www.aksainvestorrelations.com/investor-relations/contact.

name: Chen Weiliang
current_role: Chairman and CEO, MetaX Integrated Circuits (Shanghai) Co. (SSE STAR: 688802)
profile: Chen Weiliang is a GPU engineer who spent over a decade at AMD in China, latterly leading GPU/GPGPU SoC design, before co-founding MetaX with ex-AMD colleagues Peng Li and Yang Jian in Shanghai in September 2020. MetaX builds GPGPUs for AI training and inference; its December 2025 STAR Market IPO raised ~$593m and shares jumped ~700% on debut, making him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: MetaX shares soared roughly 693% on their December 2025 Shanghai debut, one of the biggest first-day pops of China's AI-chip IPO wave, turning the ex-AMD engineer into a billionaire overnight.
deep_cut_fact: MetaX was founded on 14 September 2020 and in 2024 alone filed more than 210 patent applications, with over 120 granted, 97% of them invention patents.
notes: Business@ is the company's general business inbox (not personal). Reports differ on AMD tenure (13-15 years). Data-center/AI angle: domestic Nvidia alternative under US export controls.

name: Todd Wanek
current_role: President & CEO, Ashley Furniture Industries (Arcadia, Wisconsin)
profile: Son of founder Ron Wanek, Todd Wanek has been CEO of Ashley Furniture since 2002, after running its Taiwan factory for five years and becoming COO in 1996. Ashley is the world's largest home furnishings manufacturer and North America's largest furniture store brand; his father remains chairman.
interesting_fact: As a teen and college student he worked odd jobs at Ashley, including on the production line and shipping furniture, and after college spent five years living in Asia managing the company's Taiwan factory.
deep_cut_fact: He was named a 2026 Tampa Bay Father of the Year by the National Father's Day Council (June 2026 luncheon benefiting Big Brothers Big Sisters). Ashley's Hope to Dream program, which he describes as starting to help local kids who needed a mattress, passed 200,000 donated beds.

public_contacts.value: Sharon Okaah, Flytevu - sharon.okaah@flytevu.com (campaign media contact on Ashley press release)

notes: Best route is Ashley corporate PR (publicrelations@ashleyfurniture.com). Hope to Dream bed-donation program is a good warm hook. Flytevu contact appears campaign-specific.

name: Mark Pears
current_role: Chief Executive, William Pears Group (since 1984); Chairman, Talisman Global Asset Management; trustee, Pears Foundation
profile: London property billionaire who has run the family's privately held William Pears Group, founded in 1952 by his grandfather Bernard and father Clive, since his father's death in 1984 when he was 21. He runs it with brothers Trevor and David; together they co-founded Pears Foundation (1992), one of the UK's largest family foundations.
interesting_fact: Appointed CBE in 2014 'for services to Business and to Charity'; he has been a trustee of the British Museum and the homelessness charity St Mungo's.
deep_cut_fact: In 2000 he co-founded Telereal, which became the UK's largest property outsourcing company, managing estates for British Telecom, the DWP, the DVLA and Royal Mail assets.
notes: Low public profile; family business is private. Foundation is invitation-only and asks not to receive funding requests; general foundation inbox is the only published route found.

name: Weili Dai
current_role: Co-founder & Board Director, Silicon Box (Singapore chiplet packaging); co-founder of Marvell Technology
profile: Shanghai-born, UC Berkeley CS grad Weili Dai co-founded Marvell Technology with Sehat Sutardja in 1995 and served as its president until 2016. Based in Las Vegas, she now invests in tech and real estate and has co-founded several startups, including AI firm MeetKai (2018) and Silicon Box (2021), which runs a ~$2B chiplet-packaging fab in Singapore aimed at AI customers.
interesting_fact: She is often described as the only woman co-founder of a major semiconductor company, and is reportedly the first woman to give the commencement address at UC Berkeley's engineering school, where Sutardja Dai Hall (home of CITRIS) bears her name.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager in Shanghai, before emigrating to the US at 17, Dai played semi-professional basketball.
notes: Also linked to DreamBig Semiconductor (co-founder/chair title reported) and inherited a stake in Alphawave (acquired by Qualcomm). Her husband and co-founder Sehat Sutardja died in 2024; treat sensitively. Avoid Marvell 2016 exit topic.

name: Pansy Ho
current_role: Group Executive Chairman and Managing Director, Shun Tak Holdings; co-chairperson, MGM China Holdings
profile: Daughter of the late Macau gaming magnate Stanley Ho, Pansy Ho runs Shun Tak Holdings (property, hotels and the Hong Kong-Macau TurboJET ferries) and holds stakes in MGM China and SJM Holdings. She made more than $1.5bn from MGM China's 2011 IPO and is now a prominent global tourism advocate, serving as a UN Tourism Ambassador.
interesting_fact: She dabbled in Hong Kong show business as an actress in the 1980s and helped promote her sister Josie Ho's acting and singing career.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 she founded the Global Tourism Economy Research Centre, which organises the annual Global Tourism Economy Forum in Macau; she was named a UNWTO Tourism Ambassador in 2018 and became the first official PATA Foundation Ambassador.
notes: Shun Tak has issued a statement warning about false AI-generated content about the group online, so check sources carefully. Her sister Maisy Ho, an executive director, died in April 2026; avoid that topic. Tourism (GTEF, UN Tourism) is the most natural hook. Shun Tak's site blocked scraping, so no email was verified.

name: Angela Bennett
current_role: Head of Wright Prospecting; principal of AMB Holdings (family investment company), Perth
profile: Australian iron-ore heiress whose wealth comes from Wright Prospecting's share of the Rio Tinto royalty negotiated by her father Peter Wright with Lang Hancock. She took over Wright Prospecting with her brother Michael after their father's 1985 death; in Dec 2025 sold a 15% stake in the Rhodes Ridge project to Mitsui in a ~$2B deal. Son Todd runs AMB Holdings.
interesting_fact: Her wealth stems from a royalty on every tonne of iron ore Rio Tinto mines in parts of Western Australia, negotiated decades ago by her father and Lang Hancock (father of Gina Rinehart).
deep_cut_fact: Ruah's 11-storey Perth shelter for homeless women and children is named the Angela Wright Bennett Centre after her donation; her foundation also gave $250,000 to autism research at the Kids Research Institute in 2015.
notes: Described as reclusive and rarely seen in public; no personal/public channels found. Angela Wright Bennett Foundation (program director David MacKenzie) funds climate/nature work; best route likely via AMB Holdings / foundation. Avoid the Rinehart litigation and family disputes in outreach.

name: Antti Herlin
current_role: Chairman of the Board, KONE Corporation (Helsinki)
profile: Finland's richest person and fourth-generation controlling owner of elevator/escalator maker KONE, which his great-grandfather invested in in 1924. He was KONE CEO 1996-2006 and has chaired the board since 2003. In April 2026 KONE agreed to combine with TK Elevator; Herlin is to remain chairman with over 50% of KONE's voting rights.
interesting_fact: KONE tests its elevators underground: in 2017 it expanded its Tytyri test facility to 350 m (1,150 ft) deep inside a working limestone mine in Lohja, Finland.
deep_cut_fact: Herlin owns a farm in Kirkkonummi, his birthplace west of Helsinki, where he raises Hereford and Aberdeen Angus beef cattle.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Best route is KONE Global Head of Media Relations (Gia Forsman-Härkönen). KONE-TKE combination announced Apr 2026 (https://www.tkelevator.com/global-en/newsroom/press-releases/kone-and-tke-to-combine-creating-a-world-class-company-in-the-elevator-and-escalator-industry-197696.html) is a timely hook.

name: Anne Beaufour
current_role: Board member of Ipsen (representing family holding Highrock S.à r.l.); director of family holding Mayroy
profile: Granddaughter of Dr. Henri Beaufour, founder of the labs that became French pharma group Ipsen. After her father Albert died in 2000 she and brother Henri controlled ~52-57% of Ipsen via Luxembourg holdings (Mayroy, Highrock, Beech Tree). Switzerland-based; Henri died in Nov 2025, his stake passing to a foundation.
interesting_fact: Ipsen traces back to the Beaufour laboratories founded in 1929 by her grandfather; she holds a geology degree from the University of Paris-Sud (Orsay).
notes: Extremely private; declines comment via Ipsen spokesperson. Brother Henri Beaufour died 28 Nov 2025 - avoid as an outreach topic. Best route is Ipsen corporate communications.

name: Adarsh Hiremath
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Mercor (San Francisco)
profile: Co-founded Mercor in 2023 with high-school debate partners Brendan Foody and Surya Midha after dropping out of Harvard (CS) as a sophomore. Mercor recruits domain experts who train and evaluate models for the big AI labs; a $10B valuation in Oct 2025 made the three, then 22, the youngest self-made billionaires. He leads Mercor's technology as CTO.
interesting_fact: Mercor's annualized revenue went from $100M in March 2025 to $500M by September 2025, and the three cofounders each own roughly 22% of the company.
deep_cut_fact: At Bellarmine College Preparatory in San Jose he was one of the school's top debaters and a debate-team captain; even after leaving for Harvard, he and his cofounders came back to volunteer as Bellarmine debate coaches.
notes: No published press email found (support@mercor.com is a contractor support line only). CEO Brendan Foody is the usual public face; Hiremath has appeared on a Felicis fireside podcast. Avoid the March 2026 data-breach topic.

name: Brendan Foody
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Mercor (San Francisco)
profile: In 2023 Brendan Foody cofounded Mercor with two Bellarmine high school friends, Adarsh Hiremath and Surya Midha. The company supplies expert contractors who help the big AI labs train and evaluate their models. A $10B valuation in October 2025 made the three of them the world's youngest self-made billionaires at 22. Mercor reported $500M in annualized revenue in September 2025.
interesting_fact: Foody and his cofounders were Thiel Fellows, and he left Georgetown to build Mercor. Mercor grew from about $100M in annualized revenue in March 2025 to $500M by September 2025.
deep_cut_fact: His first business was an 8th-grade donut stand. He bought Safeway donuts at $5 a dozen and sold them at his middle school for $2 each. When a rival started selling Chuck's donuts, he cut his price to $1 to run them out. After the principal banned the stand, he moved it about 20 feet off campus. He told the story on 20VC.
notes: He does a lot of podcasts (20VC, Conversations with Tyler) and would likely be receptive to a podcast invite. Mercor's site lists only a support@ inbox, with no press email. I could not confirm his personal X handle from an official source, so reach him via LinkedIn/X DM or Mercor's press page.

name: Surya Midha
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Mercor (stepped back from COO role Oct 2025)
