Wu Yan has almost no public profile of her own and the details are mostly about her husband. Identity is marked uncertain on the person level; the source of wealth ('Hakim' = 汉鼎宇佑) matches. No published contacts found.

name: Yu Renrong
current_role: Founder, chairman and controlling shareholder, OmniVision Group (formerly Will Semiconductor, Shanghai-listed)
profile: Ningbo-born Tsinghua electronic-engineering graduate (1990) who worked as an engineer at Inspur and in electronic-component distribution before founding chip designer Will Semiconductor in 2007. In 2019 it bought US image-sensor maker OmniVision for about $2.2bn, making it the world's No. 3 CMOS image-sensor supplier; he now also funds a new research university in Ningbo.
interesting_fact: In February 2025 he was the only semiconductor executive to speak at Xi Jinping's private-sector symposium, alongside Ren Zhengfei, Lei Jun and Wang Chuanfu; Will Semi shares hit the 10% daily limit the next day.
deep_cut_fact: His education foundation is co-building the Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo, in his hometown (CNY 10bn from his foundation vs CNY 16bn from the city); in Dec 2025 he gave another 30 million Will Semi shares (~2.5% of the company) to its foundation. Hurun named him China's most generous donor.
notes: Company now trades as OmniVision Group (豪威集团); IR email above is from 2025 earnings-call notices (securities investment dept). Board secretary listed as Ms Ren Bing. Chinese-language outreach likely more effective; the Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo is an alternate angle.

name: Erramon Aboitiz
current_role: Director, Aboitiz Equity Ventures; Chairman, Union Bank of the Philippines; Chairman of the Board of Trustees, Asian Institute of Management
profile: Erramon 'Montxu' Aboitiz is a fifth-generation leader of the Philippines' Aboitiz Group, a century-old conglomerate in power (AboitizPower), banking (UnionBank), food, cement and infrastructure. He was AEV president and CEO from 2009 to 2019 and briefly CEO of Aboitiz Power in 2018; he now sits on the AEV board, chairs UnionBank and, since 2023, chairs the AIM board.
interesting_fact: In 2011 he was named Management Man of the Year by the Management Association of the Philippines and Entrepreneur of the Year by Ernst & Young; AIM later gave him an honorary doctorate in management.
deep_cut_fact: He studied in the US Pacific Northwest, earning a BS in Business Administration (Accounting and Finance) from Gonzaga University in Spokane, Washington; in 2023 he became only the 7th chairman of the Asian Institute of Management, succeeding Peter Garrucho.
notes: Goes by 'Montxu'. Fits energy angle via AboitizPower. AEV chairmanship has passed to other family members (reports name Enrique/Endika); verify before outreach. Board bio: https://aboitiz.com/board_member/erramon-i-aboitiz-4

name: Michael Intrator
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, CoreWeave, Inc. (NASDAQ: CRWV)
profile: Co-founded CoreWeave in 2017 with Brian Venturo and Brannin McBee as a GPU crypto-mining outfit (Atlantic Crypto) and pivoted it into an AI cloud whose customers include Microsoft, Meta and OpenAI. CoreWeave IPO'd in 2025 at ~$23B valuation; he owns roughly 12%. Previously he ran natural-gas hedge fund Hudson Ridge Asset Management.
interesting_fact: CoreWeave started life mining Ethereum with GPUs; the founders repurposed that GPU fleet for AI compute, and the company now powers nine of the ten leading foundation-model providers and signed a $14B compute deal with Meta running to 2031.
deep_cut_fact: Before natural-gas trading and AI, he spent years at Natsource Asset Management working in environmental/carbon markets, and he holds an MPA from Columbia SIPA (plus a BA from Binghamton). He received the Research & Development Council of New Jersey's Science & Technology Medal.
notes: High-profile public-company CEO, does frequent conference/podcast appearances (London Tech Week, GTC). Energy/data-center angle is a natural fit: background in natural-gas and carbon markets. Route via press@coreweave.com.

name: Akihiko Otsuka
profile: Former chairman of Otsuka Holdings and longtime president of Otsuka Pharmaceutical (1976-2000). Died November 28, 2014, aged 77, while serving as representative director and chairman, per Otsuka Holdings' official notice.
notes: Deceased (source: Otsuka Holdings TSE disclosure https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/45780/140120141201087645.pdf ; https://www.yakuji.co.jp/?p=40292). Current chairman is Ichiro Otsuka. Remove from outreach list.

name: Ziff, Dirk, Robert And Daniel
current_role: Co-founders/principals of Ziff Brothers Investments, the family's private investment office
profile: The three sons of publisher William B. Ziff Jr. inherited their fortune after the family sold most of Ziff-Davis/Ziff Communications in 1994 (a 1998 joint Forbes listing). They formed Ziff Brothers Investments, a famously discreet family office investing across equities, debt, real estate, commodities, private equity and hedge funds; they now are listed individually.
interesting_fact: Ziff Brothers Investments provided early seed capital to Daniel Och's hedge fund, which became Och-Ziff Capital Management and went public in 2007 (Wikipedia flags this as needing a citation).
deep_cut_fact: Robert Ziff studied electrical and computer engineering at Harvard (magna cum laude), graduated first in his class at Cornell Law School where he edited the Cornell Law Review, and in 2008 endowed the Robert D. Ziff Professorship of Law at Cornell. Dirk and Daniel gave $2m in 2018 to Columbia's Center for Climate and Life.
notes: Family/group entry (1998 Forbes list) covering three brothers; each is now profiled separately. Very private family office with no public website or published contact; outreach would need a warm intro.

name: Gabriele Volkmann
current_role: Shareholder (heir) in Brose Fahrzeugteile SE & Co. KG, Coburg; no public operating role found
profile: According to Forbes (2018), Gabriele Volkmann is an heir to Brose, the family-owned German auto-parts supplier founded by her great-grandfather Max Brose and built into a global player by her uncle Michael Stoschek. Brose is split between the Stoschek and Volkmann family lines; her mother Christine Volkmann is a shareholder.
interesting_fact: Brose makes mechatronic parts such as window regulators, seat adjusters, door systems and e-bike motors, components that are 'largely invisible to drivers' yet fitted to cars worldwide. It is among the largest family-owned automotive suppliers.
notes: Very private; she appeared on Forbes only in 2018, and almost nothing is published about her personally. German press says the shareholders include Christine Volkmann 'and her eldest daughter', which may be her, but this is unconfirmed. Brose is chaired by Maximilian Stoschek, and he or the Brose press office is the realistic route. Brose's site has no scrapeable press email.

name: Howard Schultz
current_role: Lifelong Chairman Emeritus, Starbucks; co-founder, Schultz Family Foundation; investor via Maveron
profile: Brooklyn-raised entrepreneur who joined Starbucks in 1982, founded Il Giornale, then bought and scaled Starbucks from 11 stores to 35,000+ worldwide over three stints as CEO (last ended 2023). He left the board in 2023 as lifelong chairman emeritus, invests in consumer startups through Maveron, and funds veteran and youth job programs via the Schultz Family Foundation.
interesting_fact: He grew up in a Brooklyn housing project and was the first in his family to graduate from college, attending Northern Michigan University on a football scholarship.
deep_cut_fact: Before Starbucks he sold Xerox machines in New York, then ran US operations for Swedish housewares maker Hammarplast; noticing a small Seattle shop ordering unusually many drip coffeemakers led him to visit Starbucks in 1981.
notes: Reported in 2026 to have moved from Washington state to Florida for a 'retirement phase' (verify). He posts occasionally on LinkedIn. Foundation site blocks automated fetches, so no foundation email was verified.

name: Jean Coutu
current_role: Founder, The Jean Coutu Group (now part of Metro Inc.); co-founder, Marcelle and Jean Coutu Foundation
profile: Montreal pharmacist (born 1927) who opened a discount pharmacy with partner Louis Michaud in 1969 and built The Jean Coutu Group into Quebec's dominant drugstore chain via franchising and acquisitions, including a large US arm. The family sold the company to Metro in 2017-18 for about C$4.5bn; he now focuses on philanthropy through the family foundation.
interesting_fact: His 1969 store pioneered the 'pharm-escompte' format in Quebec: low prices, broad non-pharmacy merchandise and long opening hours, which became the template for the franchise network launched in 1973.
deep_cut_fact: The first Pharm-Escompte Jean Coutu opened in June 1969 on avenue du Mont-Royal at the corner of rue Garnier in Montreal's Plateau; he reportedly put his life savings of about C$250,000 into it.
notes: Aged ~99; alive per latest available sources (no death report found as of Nov 2026, but verify before outreach). Not active in business; family foundation (fmjc.org, Montreal, supports Quebec causes and projects in Mali and Haiti) is the most plausible route. Life-savings figure from encyclopedia.com company history.

name: Zhou Jianping
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder (via Hailan Group), HLA Group Corp. (Shanghai 600398); son Zhou Lichen is chairman
profile: Founder of HLA Group (Heilan Home), one of China's largest menswear makers and retailers. Starting from a small-town photo studio, he took over a collective wool mill in Xinqiao, Jiangyin in 1988 and launched the HLA retail brand around 2002 on a self-service, Uniqlo-style model; he has since handed the chairmanship to his son.
interesting_fact: He never attended university; the money for his first wool-mill venture came from running a photo studio.
deep_cut_fact: In 1984 he opened the first photo studio in his hometown of Xinqiao, Jiangyin; it sat opposite a wool mill, which is how he learned the textile trade before taking over the town's collective mill for 300,000 yuan in 1988.
notes: Very low profile; communicates via HLA's board secretary (Tang Yong). No published personal contact found; route via HLA Group investor relations / SSE roadshow platform.

name: Brian Acton
current_role: Executive Chairman, Signal Technology Foundation (co-founded 2018); also listed as interim CEO of Signal Messenger LLC
profile: Stanford computer scientist and early Yahoo engineer who co-founded WhatsApp with Jan Koum in 2009. Facebook bought it in 2014 for about $19-22bn. He left in 2017, put $50m into creating the Signal Foundation, and with his wife Tegan runs Wildcard Giving, Sunlight Giving and related charities holding over $1bn.
interesting_fact: In 2009 both Twitter (May) and Facebook (August) turned him down for jobs. Five years later Facebook bought WhatsApp for about $19bn. He had tweeted that Twitter's rejection was 'ok' because it would have been a long commute.
deep_cut_fact: Before Yahoo, he grew up in Michigan and Central Florida (Lake Howell High School). In 1992 he worked as a systems administrator at Rockwell International, then did product testing at Apple and Adobe. He joined Yahoo in 1996.
notes: His $50m to Signal was structured as an interest-free loan. I found no published press email for Signal (privacy@signal.org is for data requests only). He's privacy-minded and rarely gives interviews, so the best route is probably via the Signal Foundation or his X account.

name: Dennis Bastas
current_role: Chairman and Group CEO, DBG Health (Melbourne)
profile: Melbourne-born son of Greek migrants who started in logistics at Coles Myer, founded generics maker Genepharm Australasia in the early 2000s and sold it to Watson in 2012 for $252M. His DBG Health bought Arrotex Pharmaceuticals and others in 2023, and in 2025 BDT & MSD Partners bought a stake in DBG's holding company for $1B, valuing it at over $4.7B.
interesting_fact: DBG Health's 2023 deals, worth $671M, included Arrotex Pharmaceuticals, Australia's largest pharmaceutical company by market share.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an industrial designer, graduating in Engineering & Industrial Design from Monash University in 1988 and hoping to design cars overseas. The early-1990s recession changed his plans and he took a logistics job at Coles Myer instead.
notes: DBG's contact form explicitly accepts media/press enquiries; state the purpose in the form. Car design and industrial design are a natural conversation opener. Coles Myer detail also in the ReadyMedia profile https://content.readymedia.com.au/video/dennis-bastas

name: Li Zhengguo
current_role: Founder and Chief Technology Officer, LONGi Green Energy Technology (head of Central R&D Institute; stepped down as president May 2025)
profile: Li Zhenguo (李振国, b. 1968; listed here as 'Li Zhengguo') co-founded Xi'an-based LONGi in 2000 with Lanzhou University classmates, turning a reprocessed-silicon supplier into the world's largest monocrystalline solar wafer/module maker. In May 2025 he handed the presidency to Zhong Baoshen and now leads R&D as CTO, pushing back-contact (BC) cell technology.
interesting_fact: He received a Lifetime Achievement Award at the S&P Global Energy Awards, and has predicted back-contact (BC) cells will exceed 30% market share by 2028.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating in physics/semiconductors from Lanzhou University, his first job was at the Huashan Semiconductor Materials Factory; he later ran the crystal-growing base of Xi'an University of Technology's factory before founding LONGi.
notes: Name spelled Li Zhenguo in English sources. Wealth shared with wife Li Xiyan (co-founder). Frequent speaker at WEF, COP30, UNCCD COP17 - conference circuits are a realistic approach route; route requests via LONGi corporate communications.

name: Li Xiyan
current_role: Major shareholder (~5%) and co-controlling party, LONGi Green Energy Technology (with husband Li Zhenguo)
profile: Li Xiyan is the wife of LONGi founder Li Zhenguo and, with him, a controlling shareholder of LONGi Green Energy, the Xi'an-based maker of monocrystalline silicon wafers and solar modules founded in 2000. She holds about 5% of LONGi directly (third-largest holder) and keeps a low public profile; she has no executive role.
interesting_fact: LONGi is named after Jiang Longji, a former president of Lanzhou University, where Li Zhenguo and his co-founding classmates studied semiconductor materials; the couple have been ranked Shaanxi's richest on the Hurun list.
notes: Very private; virtually no public interviews. Hurun lists wealth jointly with Li Zhenguo (input says 'Li Zhengguo'). Best route is LONGi board office (Xi'an). Beware a different Li Xiyan (Chongqing law professor) in search results.

name: Chen Danian
current_role: Founder and CEO, Zenmen / LinkSure (WiFi Master Key)
profile: Born in 1978 and educated at Fudan University, Chen co-founded online-games company Shanda Interactive with his brother Chen Tianqiao in 1999 and served as its COO; Shanda listed on NASDAQ in 2004. He later founded Zenmen/LinkSure, maker of WiFi Master Key, a crowd-sourced Wi-Fi sharing app that reached about 900 million users.
interesting_fact: WiFi Master Key added 100 million users in three months in early 2017, passing 900 million users. It is one of the largest Wi-Fi sharing apps in the world.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager in Shanghai in 1996, Chen applied for commercial ChinaNET dial-up access, which took a household register booklet and 'a pile of administrative forms'. In 1998 he wrote an article for ICPCW predicting the internet's impact would be 'no less than the invention of the steam engine'.
notes: Also known as Danny Chen. The company's international PR has historically gone through PR Newswire releases. No published email found; Chinese-language outreach through Zenmen corporate communications is likely needed.

profile: Listed by Hurun China 2026 with wealth from Accton Technology (Taiwan, TWSE: 2345), a Hsinchu-based maker of network switches whose revenue has surged on AI data-centre demand. Searches in English and Chinese found no public source tying this name to Accton's board or major shareholders.

name: Peter Hargreaves
current_role: Co-founder of Hargreaves Lansdown; backer/partner of Blue Whale Capital (left HL board Oct 2025; son Robert took his seat)
profile: Clitheroe-born chartered accountant who co-founded Hargreaves Lansdown with Stephen Lansdown from a Bristol spare bedroom in 1981, building the UK's largest retail investment platform. HL was taken private in a £5.4bn takeover in 2025, and he remains a major shareholder. He seeded fund manager Blue Whale Capital in 2017 and is the main stakeholder in satellite ground-station firm GomSpace.

notes: Outspoken and interview-friendly in the UK financial press. His energy and space investments (ITM Power hydrogen, GomSpace satellites) fit the podcast's angle. Blue Whale is the best route to him. Brexit donations are politically sensitive, so avoid leading with them.

name: Jeff Rothschild
current_role: Private investor; Facebook founding infrastructure executive (retired 2015); vice chair, Vanderbilt University Board of Trust; director, Pure Storage (joined 2018)
profile: Rothschild co-founded storage-software company Veritas Software (1988; sold to Symantec for $13.5B in 2004) and online-gaming network Mpath Interactive (1995). He joined Facebook in 2005 as VP of infrastructure engineering, building out its backend systems, moved to an advisory role around 2010 and left in 2015; his fortune comes mainly from Facebook stock.
interesting_fact: When Facebook hired him in 2005 he was 50 years old, making him the company's oldest executive at the time.
deep_cut_fact: Before Facebook he co-founded Mpath Interactive in 1995, an early internet multiplayer-gaming/voice company that went public in 1999, and he is a co-inventor on several of its patents; he began his career as an engineer at Honeywell and Intel.
notes: Low public profile, no personal social channels found. Strong data-center/infra angle (ran Facebook infrastructure in its scale-up years, storage background). Possible routes: via Vanderbilt or Pure Storage board, but no published contact for him personally. Not related to the banking Rothschilds.

name: William Wrigley Jr
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Wrigley Management (Chicago single-family office) and WWJr. Enterprises (venture/PE vehicle)
profile: William "Beau" Wrigley Jr., great-grandson of the gum company's founder, ran Wm. Wrigley Jr. Co. from 1999, bought Altoids and Life Savers in 2005 and sold the firm to Mars for $23 billion in 2008. He later led cannabis firm Surterra/Parallel (2018 to ~2022) and now invests through his family office.
interesting_fact: His great-grandfather originally sold baking soda and switched to gum after noticing the gum he gave away as a premium was more popular than the product.
deep_cut_fact: He is a trustee of Conservation International, where he co-chairs its Ocean Health Council, and sits on the National Geographic Society's Council of Advisors.
notes: No published email or contact form found for Wrigley Management. Was an early chairman/investor in health-kiosk startup higi (MobiHealthNews 2016). Avoid Parallel lawsuits topic.

name: Jonathan Nelson
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Providence Equity Partners
profile: Jonathan M. Nelson (Brown '77) co-founded Providence Equity Partners in Providence, RI in 1989. It has since backed more than 180 media, communications, education and information companies. Wins include selling PADI in 2017 for over $700M and roughly sextupling a $300M 2007 stake in ZeniMax when Microsoft bought it for $7.5B. He is now executive chairman and a trustee of Rockefeller University.
interesting_fact: In college he worked at a commercial radio station, hosting the 'Jazz After Hours' program. Today he sits on the board of the Newport Festival Foundation, which runs the Newport Folk and Jazz Festivals.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 his $25 million gift created the Jonathan M. Nelson Center for Entrepreneurship at his alma mater, Brown. He had earlier funded Brown's Nelson Fitness Center, and he serves as a Fellow of the Brown Corporation.

public_contacts.value: Pro-Providence@profileadvisors.com (Profile Advisors, listed as Providence Equity media contact)

notes: Media enquiries go through the PR firm Profile Advisors. The Brown entrepreneurship center and his jazz/Newport interests make good outreach hooks. Providence invests in communications infrastructure, which is relevant to data centers.

name: Romano Minozzi
current_role: Founder of Iris Ceramica Group; controlling shareholder (via Finanziaria Ceramica Castellarano) of GranitiFiandre; major investor in Eni, Snam, Enel
profile: Italian industrialist (b. 1935) who in 1961 bought a struggling ceramics maker in the Modena tile district, renamed it Iris and grew it into an international surfaces group. He has since built a large portfolio in Italian energy and utility stocks (Terna, Snam, Italgas, Enel, Eni); daughter Federica has run Iris as CEO since 2017.
interesting_fact: In May 2025 his group's holdings passed 3% of Eni, making him one of the oil major's largest shareholders; earlier he bought 4.2% of grid operator Terna for ~$173M in 2010 and sold three years later for ~$465M.
deep_cut_fact: An economics graduate of the University of Bologna, he began his career at a bank in Modena, where he got hooked on the stock market; he bought his ceramics company in 1961 with a 300-million-lira loan from Mediobanca and later served a three-year term on Ferrari's board.
notes: Aged ~91 and very private; no personal channels. Iris contact page's HTML contains a press-office email (press@digital-mind.it, agency Digital Mind, Milan) but that block is commented out/possibly outdated. Strong energy-investor angle (Eni/Snam/Terna/Enel).

name: Olivier Pomel
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Datadog, Inc. (NASDAQ: DDOG)
profile: French-born engineer who co-founded cloud monitoring/observability company Datadog in 2010 with Ecole Centrale Paris classmate Alexis Le-Quoc after both worked at Wireless Generation (acquired by News Corp). Datadog IPO'd on Nasdaq in 2019; Pomel still runs it as CEO and owns 2%+ of the stock.
interesting_fact: Pomel and co-founder Alexis Le-Quoc met as undergraduates at Ecole Centrale Paris and became billionaires in 2020 after a blockbuster Datadog earnings release sent shares soaring.
deep_cut_fact: He is one of the original authors of the open-source VLC media player, from his student days at Ecole Centrale Paris; before Datadog he also worked as a software engineer at IBM Research.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (DASH, Slush, HumanX) - good podcast prospect; route via Datadog press team.

name: Jacques D'Amours
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder (about 6%), Alimentation Couche-Tard; retired from the board in 2023
profile: Montreal-based co-founder of Alimentation Couche-Tard (Circle K), which started from one Quebec convenience store in 1980 and grew through acquisitions into a global chain of more than 17,000 stores. He worked at the company for 34 years, retiring as VP of administration in 2014, and left the board in 2023. He remains its second-largest shareholder.
interesting_fact: He was the youngest of Couche-Tard's four co-founders, alongside Alain Bouchard, Richard Fortin and Réal Plourde, and has been a billionaire since 2005.
deep_cut_fact: In the mid-1980s, aged about 28, he ran operations with Réal Plourde in Couche-Tard's small early office. The company's very first employee remembered him as 'more of an introvert' than his co-founders. His roles over the years included manager of technical services and VP of sales.
notes: Low-profile and retired from the company. Couche-Tard media relations may forward a request but does not represent him personally. Co-founder Alain Bouchard is the public face.

name: Kwon Hyuk-bin
current_role: Founder and Chief Vision Officer (CVO), Smilegate Holdings; chairman of Smilegate Hope Studio foundation
profile: Kwon founded Smilegate in 2002 and owns it outright. A 2008 publishing deal with Tencent turned its shooter CrossFire into a global hit in China, and the later MMORPG Lost Ark followed. Smilegate is among Korea's largest game companies. He became CVO in 2020 and backs startups through the Orange Planet Entrepreneurship Foundation and charity work through Smilegate Hope Studio.
interesting_fact: In 2020 he became the first person from Korea's game industry to receive a national Order of Cultural Merit (cultural medal).
deep_cut_fact: Smilegate's very first game was not CrossFire but an FPS called Headshot Online, finished around 2005. Its official launch was cancelled when the publisher, Yahoo Korea, left the games business. As a student he took part in Samsung's Software Membership developer program.
notes: Rarely speaks publicly. His 2026 divorce litigation, which affects Smilegate's ownership, is in the news; avoid it. Orange Planet, the startup foundation, is a natural entrepreneurship angle for a podcast. The Samsung Software Membership fact is from the Forbes facts and a Wikipedia mirror.

name: Alexis Lê-Quôc
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Datadog (NASDAQ: DDOG)
profile: French-born engineer who co-founded cloud monitoring/observability company Datadog in New York in 2010 with CEO Olivier Pomel, after years at IBM Research and as director of operations at edtech firm Wireless Generation. Datadog IPO'd on Nasdaq in 2019; he owns roughly 3% and remains CTO, also doing angel investing.
interesting_fact: He and Pomel met as students at Ecole Centrale Paris and then worked together for nine years at Wireless Generation (acquired by News Corp in 2010) before founding Datadog, which debuted at a 2010 SeedStart demo day.
deep_cut_fact: He 'first met' Olivier Pomel in college: while Nmap-scanning the campus network on a fresh Linux install, he was disconnected for being too curious, and Pomel was one of the people who cut him off. His first computer was a Sinclair ZX Spectrum his parents (university teachers) bought.
notes: Frequent conference/podcast guest (Modern CTO #146, Zero Prime E09, Software Engineering Daily 2018), so podcast-friendly. Best route is Datadog press team.

name: George Lindemann Sr
current_role: Deceased (died 21 June 2018, aged 82); former chairman & CEO of Southern Union Co.
notes: Died June 21, 2018 at age 82 per Wharton Magazine obituary (https://magazine.wharton.upenn.edu/obituaries/george-lindemann-w58) and Wikipedia (citing Palm Beach Daily News). Founder of Metro Mobile (sold to Bell Atlantic), later ran pipeline firm Southern Union (sold to Energy Transfer, 2012). Profile skipped per instructions.

name: Ian Livingstone
current_role: Co-Executive Chairman, London & Regional Properties (with brother Richard Livingstone)
profile: Input lists only 'Ian'; the David Clulow chain shared with Richard Livingstone points to Ian Livingstone (b. 1962). With his brother he founded London & Regional Properties in 1987, buying distressed assets in the property crash; holdings have included David Lloyd Leisure and London hotels. He chaired the Optika Clulow optician chain until its 2011 sale.
interesting_fact: With Colombian banker Jaime Gilinski the brothers have developed Panama Pacifico, a $700m project on the former Howard US Air Force Base in Panama.
deep_cut_fact: Before property he trained as an optometrist: he earned an optometry degree from City University London and qualified in 1984, which led to his optical-retail chain before L&R took off.
notes: Name matched via the David Clulow / Richard Livingstone link (not fully confirmed). Very private; L&R has no reachable website or press contact. Trustee of the Mayor's Fund for London (https://www.mayorsfundforlondon.org.uk/people/ian-livingstone/). Real estate/leisure, not energy or data centers.

name: Zhu Yuqin
current_role: No public executive role found; Hurun lists her jointly with husband Tang Jinkui, co-founder, vice chairman & GM of Shenghong Group
profile: Zhu Yuqin appears on Hurun lists together with her husband Tang Jinkui (b. 1955, Suzhou), co-founder of Shenghong Group, a Suzhou conglomerate that grew from textile dyeing (founded 1992) into polyester fibre and a 16 Mt/yr refining-petrochemical complex in Lianyungang (listed arm: Eastern Shenghong, 000301.SZ). Hurun ranked the couple at RMB 23bn in 2023.
interesting_fact: Shenghong grew in three decade-long steps: dyeing (now 2.4bn+ metres/yr capacity), then differentiated fibres (3.6 Mt/yr, called a 'global differentiated-fibre expert'), then a 16 Mt/yr integrated refinery in Lianyungang; it entered the Fortune Global 500 in 2020.
notes: Essentially no public footprint of her own; facts found relate to husband Tang Jinkui (who has patents in dyeing-wastewater membrane treatment and sludge incineration) and the company. Any approach should go via Shenghong / Eastern Shenghong. Alive status not confirmed by a source. Listed focus 'data_center_ai' looks mis-tagged; business is petrochemicals/fibre.

name: Richard H. P. Chang
current_role: Vice Chairman and President, ASE Technology Holding Co. (Kaohsiung, Taiwan; NYSE: ASX) — per most recent SEC filing found
profile: Richard H.P. Chang (張洪本) co-founded Advanced Semiconductor Engineering (ASE) in Kaohsiung in 1984 with his brother, chairman Jason C.S. Chang. ASE became the world's largest outsourced chip packaging and test (OSAT) group, merging with SPIL in 2018 to form ASE Technology Holding, where he serves as vice chairman and president; advanced packaging is now central to AI chips.
interesting_fact: He was president of ASE from its founding in March 1984, became vice chairman in 1999, and served as ASE's CEO from July 2000 to April 2003 before taking his current vice chairman/president role at the holding company created in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Before helping build the world's biggest chip packaging-and-test group, he trained as an industrial engineer: his bachelor's degree is in Industrial Engineering from Chung Yuan Christian University in Taiwan.
notes: Hurun lists him under China; he is Taiwanese (ASE HQ Kaohsiung). Low public profile vs. brother Jason Chang. Route via ASE public relations (ASEH_PR@aseglobal.com). Current title taken from FY2021 20-F; confirm in the latest 20-F.

name: Chen Lu
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Skyverse Technology (Shenzhen Zhongke Feice, SSE STAR: 688361)
profile: Physicist who worked as a senior scientist at Rudolph Technologies and KLA in the US, returned to China in 2010 via the CAS 'Hundred Talents' program at the Institute of Microelectronics, and in Dec 2014 spun out Skyverse in Shenzhen. Skyverse makes semiconductor inspection/metrology tools for SMIC, YMTC and CXMT, listed on the STAR Market in May 2023, and aims to be China's answer to KLA.
interesting_fact: Skyverse's patterned-less wafer defect inspection tool passed SMIC production-line validation in 2017 - billed as a 'zero-to-one' breakthrough for Chinese high-end inspection equipment; Huawei's Hubble is among its investors.
deep_cut_fact: Entered the University of Science and Technology of China's Special Class for the Gifted Young at 15 to study physics, went abroad at 20 and earned a PhD in optical physics from Brown University at 26.
notes: Wealth shared with Ha Chengshu per Hurun. Company is on the US Entity List (Dec 2024) - sensitive for a US podcast. Best route is the board secretary's office (IR@skyverse.cn); Chinese-language outreach recommended.

name: Ha Chengshu
current_role: Director and co-actual controller, Shenzhen Skyverse Technology (中科飞测, SSE STAR: 688361)
profile: Hong Kong-national co-founder and, with her husband, Skyverse chairman/CEO Chen Lu (ex-KLA scientist), actual controller of Skyverse, a Shenzhen maker of semiconductor wafer defect-inspection and metrology equipment that listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023. She served as VP, then GM (2022-23) and is now a board director.
interesting_fact: Skyverse is one of China's few domestic suppliers of wafer inspection/metrology tools, a segment long dominated by KLA, where Chen Lu worked as a senior scientist before co-founding the company with her.
deep_cut_fact: Before chips she had a finance/VC career in the US: a Yale master's in international & development economics and a US law doctorate (Univ. of Washington), then senior tax analyst at Deloitte (US) 2007-11 and a manager at venture firm GSR Ventures (金沙江创投) in California 2011-16, before joining Skyverse as VP in 2016.
notes: Wealth is held jointly with husband Chen Lu (chairman/GM, the more public face). Low media profile; IR mailbox (board secretary office) is the realistic route. Fluent English given US education.

name: Ma Yunsheng
current_role: Chairman, Chambroad Holding Group (Boxing County, Binzhou, Shandong) - per Forbes
profile: Ma Yunsheng chairs Chambroad Holding, a private Shandong group in petrochemicals, specialty chemicals, high-performance materials and agribusiness. A former government official, he joined the business in 1982 when it was a collective and grew it into a diversified group reporting 110.8bn yuan of 2025 sales and ~11,000 staff.
interesting_fact: Chambroad funds the Chambroad Technology Award, a national science prize for young researchers launched in 2019 that has drawn 100+ academicians into its selection and honored 504 awardees.
notes: Very low English-language profile; no recent interviews found and current chairmanship confirmed only via Forbes. Alive status inferred from his 2026 Forbes real-time listing. Best route is the Chambroad corporate contact form.

name: Wei Xuefeng
current_role: Director, Hangzhou Jinjiang Group (杭州锦江集团); legal representative of Zhejiang Hengjia Holdings, a Jinjiang Group shareholder
profile: Wei Xuefeng (尉雪凤) is the wife and business partner of Dou Zhenggang, founder of Hangzhou Jinjiang Group, a Lin'an-born private group in waste-to-energy power, alumina/aluminium and chemicals. Hurun lists the couple jointly (Jinjiang, energy & chemicals). In 2025 Jinjiang moved to inject Sanmenxia Aluminum (~RMB 319bn deal) into listed Jiaozuo Wanfang (000612.SZ).
interesting_fact: Jinjiang Group started in Lin'an, Zhejiang in 1983 and moved through textiles, paper, cables and pharma before settling on waste-to-energy, non-ferrous metals and chemicals; it developed circulating-fluidized-bed garbage-incineration power technology.
deep_cut_fact: She is the legal representative and sole owner of Zhejiang Hengjia Holdings (浙江恒嘉控股, formerly Zhejiang Xin Jinjiang Investment Management, est. 2003 in Lin'an), one of the holding companies that owns Hangzhou Jinjiang Group alongside Dou Zhenggang.
notes: Identity confirmed via Hurun API record (2018-2022 lists '钭正刚、尉雪凤 / Dou Zhenggang & Wei Xuefeng, Jinjiang, couple') and Securities Times/Sohu 2017 report naming the couple as actual controllers in a Jinjiang share deal (https://m.sohu.com/a/206405956_115433). No interviews or personal channels found; she keeps a very low profile. Route is via Jinjiang Group (Hangzhou HQ; site lists contact page). Not to be confused with Jin Jiang hotels (Shanghai).

name: Wang Guangxi
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Wintime Energy Group (永泰能源, 600157.SH); founder and controller of Yongtai (Wintime) Group
profile: Wang Guangxi (王广西), born 1969 in Jiangsu, founded Yongtai Group in 2003 as a real-estate business, then in 2007 took control of listed Lurun Shares, renamed Wintime Energy in 2010, and built it into one of Shanxi's largest private coal and power producers. He and his wife Guo Tianshu are ranked among Shanxi's richest people.
interesting_fact: A Jiangsu native with an MBA, he became known as Shanxi's richest man (with wife Guo Tianshu) by turning a Shandong-listed shell into a coal-mining and power-generation group in Shanxi.
deep_cut_fact: Before coal, he made his first fortune in property: his Jiangsu Yongtai Real Estate Group became the largest shareholder of Lurun Shares in early 2007, the shell that later became Wintime Energy - his first A-share listed company.
notes: Emails are the board-secretary (wteclzqb@126.com) and company general (wteclbg@126.com) addresses published in Wintime Energy's 2025 half-year report. Avoid referencing the June 2026 regulatory fine over Haide Shares disclosures (sources used here also report it). Very private; no personal media presence.

name: Guo Tianshu
current_role: 20% shareholder of Yongtai Investment Holding (Wintime Group), parent of Shanxi-listed Wintime Energy (600157.SH); no public executive title found
profile: Guo Tianshu is the wife of Wang Guangxi, who founded Yongtai Investment Holding in 2003. Wang owns 80% and Guo 20%. The group took over lubricant maker Lurun in 2007 and renamed it Wintime Energy in 2010. By consolidating 15+ coal mines it became one of Shanxi's largest private coal and power groups, now adding vanadium-battery storage.
interesting_fact: On the 2025 New Fortune 500 rich list, Wang Guangxi and Guo Tianshu ranked as Shanxi province's richest people, with 16.43bn yuan.
notes: Guo has almost no public profile; husband Wang Guangxi fronts the business and left Wintime's chairmanship in 2026. In 2025-26 regulators investigated and fined Wang over disclosures at group company Haide. Only route found is Wintime's board-secretary email. Use Chinese-language outreach.

name: Bradley Jacobs
current_role: Chairman & CEO, QXO (building products distribution); also to be chairman & CEO of new acquisition platform CKX
profile: Serial roll-up builder: United Waste (sold 1997 for $1.9B), United Rentals, then XPO Logistics (2011), which he split into XPO, GXO and RXO. Since 2024 he has run QXO, buying Beacon Roofing, Kodiak ($2.25B) and TopBuild (~$17B, closed July 2026), aiming for $50B revenue; in Nov 2026 he announced a second $1B-backed platform, CKX.
interesting_fact: A trained classical pianist, he studied math and music at Brown before dropping out; he has written two books, 'How to Make a Few Billion Dollars' (2024) and a 2025 sequel.
deep_cut_fact: His first company was Amerex Oil Associates, an oil brokerage he co-founded in 1979 and ran until its 1983 sale; he then moved to London and founded oil trader Hamilton Resources, and often credits financier Ludwig Jesselson as a mentor.
notes: Very media-friendly (books, frequent interviews). Best route: QXO media contact Joe Checkler. New CKX platform's target industry undisclosed - possible podcast hook.

name: Juan March Delgado
current_role: President of the board of trustees, Fundación Juan March (and of the Instituto Juan March)
profile: Grandson of Juan March Ordinas, who founded Banca March in Palma de Mallorca in 1926. With his brother Carlos he controls Banca March, Spain's only 100% family-owned bank, and a large stake in investment group Corporación Financiera Alba, which he co-chaired until 2018. He left the Banca March board in 2021 after 27 years and now focuses on the family foundation, which is arts-focused.
interesting_fact: He sat on Banca March's board from 1994 until July 2021, when his daughter Catalina March Juan took his seat as part of a planned handover to the family's next generation.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Palma de Mallorca in 1940, he is a trained engineer, holding a Doctorate in Industrial Engineering from Madrid's Universidad Politécnica.
notes: Aged about 86 and private. The best route is via Fundación Juan March (Madrid); march.es blocked automated fetching, so its press/contact page could not be checked. Note: Juan March de la Lastra (a different person, a cousin's line) chairs Banca March and Alba.

name: Warren Stephens
current_role: 68th U.S. Ambassador to the United Kingdom (since May 2025); chairman of family investment bank Stephens Inc. (Little Rock)
profile: Son of Jackson Stephens, he grew up in Little Rock's Stephens Inc. (founded by his uncle Witt in 1933, underwriter of Walmart's 1970 IPO), became CEO in 1986 and bought out his cousins in 2006. He stepped back as CEO in January 2025, with his sons named co-CEOs, to serve as Trump's ambassador in London.
interesting_fact: A golf nut, he built the Tom Fazio-designed Alotian Club overlooking Lake Maumelle, Arkansas (opened 2004), ranked #37 in Golf Digest's 2025 list of America's greatest courses.
deep_cut_fact: He contributed land and financing for Dickey-Stephens Park, the North Little Rock minor-league ballpark opened in 2007 that is named jointly for the Stephens brothers and baseball's Dickey brothers (Yankees Hall of Famer Bill Dickey).

public_contacts.value: https://uk.usembassy.gov/ (U.S. Embassy London, his official office)

notes: As a serving ambassador, podcast requests would go through the U.S. Embassy London press office; he is unlikely to discuss business while in post. Washington and Lee BA (1979), Wake Forest MBA (1981).

name: Jack Cockwell
current_role: Former President & CEO of Brookfield (1991-2002); shareholder of Partners Ltd, which holds Brookfield's controlling voting shares
profile: South African-born accountant (born East London, 1941) who joined Touche Ross in Cape Town and was sent to Montreal in 1966. He joined the Bronfmans' Edper in 1968 and built it into the Brookfield empire, handing over to Bruce Flatt in 2002. His wealth comes largely from Brookfield shares held through the Partners partnership. He is a Member of the Order of Canada.
interesting_fact: In 2008 he gave $5m to Ryerson (now Toronto Metropolitan University) nursing school, renamed the Daphne Cockwell School of Nursing after his mother. In 2011 he gave $10m toward George Brown College's Limberlost Place, a 10-storey mass-timber building.
deep_cut_fact: In the mid-1980s he bought land near Huntsville, Ontario, and created the Limberlost Forest and Wildlife Reserve, now over 10,000 acres and open to the public. As a teenager he represented his Scout troop at the 9th World Scout Jamboree in England (1957).
notes: In his 80s and keeps a low profile. The Brookfield press email is a corporate route, and the Limberlost email is for the reserve he founded (it's a general inquiry address). I couldn't confirm whether he is still on any Brookfield board in 2026.

name: Ron Burkle
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, The Yucaipa Companies (Los Angeles); co-owner, Pittsburgh Penguins
profile: Pomona-born son of a Stater Bros. store manager who founded Yucaipa in 1986 and made his fortune buying and merging supermarket chains (Fred Meyer, Ralphs, Food4Less, Dominick's). He now invests mainly in food-trade logistics, cold storage and food safety, and in 2026 led a group that took Soho House private.
interesting_fact: He bought Jesse Owens' 1936 Berlin Olympic gold medal at auction for about $1.4-1.5 million in 2013, and with Mario Lemieux he brought the Pittsburgh Penguins out of bankruptcy in 1999.
deep_cut_fact: By age 13 he had joined the grocery workers' union, UFCW Local 770, while stocking shelves at his father's store. He finished high school at 16 and went to Cal Poly Pomona to study dentistry before leaving for the grocery business.
notes: Yucaipa press relations email is the best published route. Also co-chairs UCLA's Burkle Center for International Relations. Avoid Epstein/Clinton-related topics.

name: Arvind Tiku
current_role: Founder & Chairman, AT Group / AT Capital (Singapore); Chairman & founder, Juniper Green Energy
profile: Indian-born, Singapore-based Arvind Tiku left India at 18 to study mechanical engineering in Russia, traded commodities in London, then made his fortune in Kazakh oil and gas. Through AT Holdings/AT Capital he now invests in property in Europe and India and in Juniper Green Energy, a wind/solar developer (Vitol holds 25%) that filed for an Indian IPO in 2025.
interesting_fact: Although he owns a private jet, Forbes notes he prefers to use Uber on overseas business trips; in 2021 he also took a minority stake in Swedish payments firm Klarna.
deep_cut_fact: Tiku stresses Juniper's hybrid strategy: he has said about 83% of its portfolio is wind, wind-solar hybrid and firm-and-dispatchable (FDRE) projects and only ~17% plain solar, which management says earns better tariffs.
notes: Low media profile; best route is likely via Juniper Green Energy (an Indian renewables IPP, fits the energy angle). AT Capital's site atcapital.com.sg returned an error when checked. Emails are general Juniper company inboxes, not his own.

name: Mohamed Alabbar
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Eagle Hills; Chairman, Americana Restaurants; founder of Noon.com
profile: Alabbar founded Emaar Properties in 1997, which built the Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall, and chaired it until 2020. Most of his fortune is his roughly 33% stake in Americana Restaurants. He now runs Abu Dhabi developer Eagle Hills, active in about 10 countries, and holds stakes in Noon.com and Zand Bank.
interesting_fact: The son of a dhow boat captain, Alabbar took his first job after college at the UAE's central bank.
deep_cut_fact: The eldest of 12 children, Alabbar studied finance and business at Seattle University's Albers School on a government scholarship (graduated 1981). In 1992 he became the founding director general of Dubai's Department of Economic Development.
notes: Media-friendly and active on social media; his own site links his X, Instagram and LinkedIn. Primary sources for the scholarship detail: BusinessWeek 2007 'The Master Builder of the Middle East' (archived) and Wikipedia.

name: Alceu Elias Feldmann
current_role: Founder, Chairman and President, Grupo Fertipar (Curitiba, Brazil)
profile: Santa Catarina-born agronomist (Federal University of Parana) who founded Fertipar in Paranagua, Parana, in 1980. He grew it into one of Brazil's largest fertilizer groups (~$3.9B revenue in 2021), a dozen-plus companies across Brazil's farm belts plus affiliated port terminal Fospar; he and his three children keep it private and he still runs it.
interesting_fact: Fertipar expanded region by region through separately branded companies: Fertigran (1984), Fertilizantes Piratini in Rio Grande do Sul (1985), then the Northeast in the 1990s, Fertipar Sudeste (1998) and Bandeirantes (2000).
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Fertipar he worked in sales at fertilizer maker Ultrafertil, travelling widely to talk with farm professionals; that region-by-region view of the sector became the basis for his own company.
notes: Very low profile; rarely gives interviews. Best route is Fertipar's corporate contact page (HQ in Curitiba). Older son of the same name is a Stock Car Brasil driver. Birthplace reported inconsistently in Brazilian press (SC vs PR).

name: Richard Chang
current_role: Vice Chairman and President, ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. (Taiwan)
profile: Richard H.P. Chang co-founded Advanced Semiconductor Engineering (ASE) in Kaohsiung in 1984 with his elder brother Jason; it is now ASE Technology Holding, the world's largest provider of chip assembly, packaging and test services, a key beneficiary of advanced packaging demand for AI chips. He is vice chairman/president, and with Jason a main investor in developer Sino Horizon.
interesting_fact: In the early 1980s the Chang family was already successful in property, but Richard argued Taiwan's nascent electronics industry was the bigger long-term bet; their mother sold properties to cover ASE's losses in its first three years.
deep_cut_fact: He was ASE's founding President from March 1984 (when the first Kaohsiung plant started with about 200 people) until becoming Vice Chairman in 1999, and holds an industrial engineering degree from Chung Yuan Christian University in Taiwan.
notes: Taiwanese family but Forbes lists him under Hong Kong. Low public profile; brother Jason Chang (chairman) is the public face. Best route is ASE corporate PR. ASE is highly relevant to AI/data-center chip packaging (CoWoS-type capacity).

name: Hsieh Wen-Ta
current_role: Chairman, Hon. Precision Inc. (鴻勁精密, TWSE: 7769), Taichung, Taiwan
profile: Hsieh Wen-Ta (謝旼達) founded Hon. Precision's predecessor in 1999 to build IC test handlers; the company now holds about a third of that market and adds active thermal control and liquid-cooling plates, supplying TSMC, Nvidia and ASE. AI/HPC orders drive about 70% of sales. He took it public on the Taiwan Stock Exchange on Nov 27, 2025.
interesting_fact: Hon. Precision's Nov 2025 TWSE debut set Taiwan listing records: it opened at NT$1,495 (an all-time high listing price) and jumped NT$1,445 on its first day, briefly pushing its market cap near UMC's.
deep_cut_fact: A machine-design graduate of Taipei Institute of Technology (台北工專機械設計科), Hsieh came out of Taiwan's machine-tool trade. Commentator Hsieh Chin-ho noted he wears work clothes on the floor of his Taichung factory, tucked in a lane off Daya Road, so visitors may not realise he's the boss.
notes: Very low-profile engineer-founder; rarely interviewed. Hon Precision is unrelated to Hon Hai/Foxconn despite the name. The SEC insider roles listed (Amprius, Ambiq, Desktop Metal director) belong to a different person, Wen Hsieh (a US venture capitalist), not this Hsieh Wen-Ta. Route via company IR.

name: Zhang Shuangwang
current_role: Founder of Inner Mongolia Yitai Group; legal representative of Inner Mongolia Yitai Investment Co., the de facto controller of Yitai Coal (per 2022 annual report)
profile: Zhang Shuangwang (张双旺), born 1943 in Jungar Banner, Inner Mongolia, was a local government official before founding Yitai in 1988. Yitai grew into a large Ordos-based group spanning coal mining, coal railways and coal-to-liquids, controlling listed Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal (SSE B-shares/HKEX). He is recorded as responsible person of the group's holding company, Yitai Investment.
interesting_fact: Yitai Coal's ultimate controller, Inner Mongolia Yitai Investment Co., is itself owned by 2,315 individual shareholders rather than one family vehicle; Zhang Shuangwang is its legal representative.
deep_cut_fact: In March 1988 Zhang gave up his post as deputy head of the Ikh Ju League (now Ordos) township-enterprise office and led 21 surplus government staff out of the civil service to start Yitai; he was later named a National Model Worker (1995).
notes: Born 1943 (about 83). No death reports found and he is still on Hurun lists through 2026, but there is no recent public activity, so alive is marked unknown. Wealth is shared with Zhang Donghai, former Yitai Coal chairman. Very low public profile; the only route is Yitai Coal's board secretary/IR office. Current day-to-day chairman of Yitai Coal is Zhang Jingquan.

name: Zhang Donghai
current_role: Reported as president/director of Inner Mongolia Yitai Group; chaired listed Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal until late 2019 (current group title not confirmed by official source)
profile: Zhang Donghai is the son of Zhang Shuangwang, who founded Ordos-based coal producer Yitai Group in 1988. Donghai joined in 2001, became group general manager in 2004 and long chaired Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal, which expanded into railways and coal-to-liquids. Zhang Jingquan succeeded him as Yitai Coal chairman in Dec 2019; the family shares the fortune.
interesting_fact: Yitai began in 1988 when his father quit a government post and led 21 surplus civil servants to start the company; Yitai Coal later became China's first coal company listed via B shares and expanded into coal-to-liquid fuels.
deep_cut_fact: In 2001, during Yitai's hardest period, he resigned a division-level post in the Inner Mongolia regional government to join a Yitai subsidiary as general manager; cost controls in his first year alone added about RMB 12 million, and he launched the 'Yitai clean coal' brand with national research institutes.
notes: Low public profile; little recent English-language coverage. Fortune shared with father Zhang Shuangwang (Hurun). No verified published personal/office contact found; Yitai corporate websites did not load. Best route is likely Yitai Coal's company secretary/IR via HKEX or SSE filings.

name: Ding Hui
current_role: Chairman and co-controlling shareholder (~26%), Shenzhen JLC Technology Group (嘉立创, SZSE: 001232)
profile: Born 1979 in Xuzhou, Jiangsu, Ding Hui moved to Shenzhen at 17, rose from electronics-factory apprentice to supervisor, then founded PCB trader Zhongxinhua. He and his brother invested in Yuan Jiangtao's JLC from 2012 and merged their businesses in 2021; JLC (PCB prototyping, component e-commerce, EDA) listed on the Shenzhen main board on 4 Aug 2026 at a market cap above RMB100bn.
interesting_fact: JLC serves engineers' small-batch PCB orders at scale: over 21 million orders a year and 9.5m+ registered online users by end-2025; CATL subscribed as a strategic investor in its 2026 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: In 2002 he started out in a ~20 sq m rented room in an urban village on Shenzhen's outskirts selling electronics; he recalled having 'no money and no goods' and taking any customer that earned a few hundred yuan just to survive.
notes: Dataset lists industry as semiconductors; JLC is actually PCB/electronics manufacturing platform (hardware supply chain for AI/data-center prototyping). Very low media profile; route via board secretary office.

name: Ding Huixiang
current_role: Co-founder and co-controlling shareholder (26.25% pre-IPO), Shenzhen JLC Technology Group (嘉立创 / JLCPCB); listed as director and deputy GM in the prospectus (one report says he left those posts in April 2026)
profile: Ding Huixiang (b. 1982, Suining, Xuzhou, Jiangsu) is a co-founder of JLC, the PCB prototyping and electronics-components platform behind JLCPCB, LCSC and EasyEDA, with his elder brother Ding Hui and Yuan Jiangtao. JLC listed on the Shenzhen main board on 4 Aug 2026 at RMB 84.46/share and topped RMB 100bn market cap; 2025 revenue was RMB 10.2bn.
interesting_fact: All three JLC founders hold only junior-college (dazhuan) diplomas; the business grew from a shared counter less than one metre wide in Shenzhen's Huaqiangbei electronics market into a 100-billion-yuan listed company with ~9.6m registered engineer users.
deep_cut_fact: Before JLC, he joined his brother's PCB maker Zhongxinhua (founded 2004). In Dec 2012 he personally put RMB 600,000 into Yuan Jiangtao's then-small JLC for a 60% stake, later passing half to his brother; this deal merged the two founding lines.
notes: Low public profile; brother Ding Hui (chairman) and Yuan Jiangtao (GM) are the public faces. Reports conflict on whether he still holds director/VP posts after April 2026; check latest SZSE filings. Best route is JLC's board-secretary/IR office via its SZSE disclosures.

name: Ryan Smith
current_role: Co-founder and board member of Qualtrics; chairman of Smith Entertainment Group (owner of the Utah Jazz and Utah Mammoth)
profile: Utah tech billionaire who co-founded survey and experience-management software firm Qualtrics with his father and brother while at BYU. SAP bought it for $8B in 2019 and later spun it off, and Silver Lake took it private in 2023. He now runs Smith Entertainment Group, which owns the NBA's Utah Jazz and the NHL's Utah Mammoth, and remains a Qualtrics shareholder.
interesting_fact: He brought the NHL to Utah: in 2024 the league granted him an expansion franchise, and he paid $1.2B for the Arizona Coyotes' hockey assets. The team became the Utah Mammoth.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of BYU's Marriott School in his junior year to build Qualtrics. He went back and finished his degree in 2016, when he was already a billionaire CEO. Before that he served a two-year church mission in Mexico.
notes: In Feb 2026 Qualtrics named Jason Maynard CEO, with Jim Whitehurst as executive chairman. Older sources still call Smith executive chairman, so describe him as co-founder. He sold his stake in Real Salt Lake in 2025. X handle @RyanSmith belongs to a different person. For sports or media topics, the best route is probably SEG or Utah Jazz communications.

name: Michelle Zatlyn
current_role: Co-founder, President and Board Co-Chair, Cloudflare, Inc. (NYSE: NET); director, Atlassian
profile: Canadian-born Zatlyn co-founded internet infrastructure and security company Cloudflare in 2009 with Harvard Business School classmate Matthew Prince (and Lee Holloway). Cloudflare IPO'd in 2019 and hit $2.2B revenue in 2025; she owns ~2% and is president and board co-chair. Earlier: Google intern, Toshiba product manager, founding team of Achievers (I Love Rewards).
interesting_fact: She studied chemistry at McGill (BSc 2001) before her HBS MBA, and was named to Fortune's 40 Under 40 (2017) and C100's 2019 'Icon of Canadian Entrepreneurship'.
deep_cut_fact: She grew up in Prince Albert, Saskatchewan, attending Ecole Holy Cross and Carlton Comprehensive High School, where she was captain of the basketball team; she has urged Saskatchewan entrepreneurs to 'lean in' to tech.
notes: Talks to media often about Cloudflare, AI crawler and bot policy, and internet infrastructure, so she is a good fit for the data-center and AI angle. The best route is Cloudflare press. Her X handle is not verified, so it is left out.

name: Alexandr Wang
current_role: Chief AI Officer, Meta Platforms (leads Meta Superintelligence Labs); board member, Scale AI
profile: Wang co-founded Scale AI in 2016 at age 19, after dropping out of MIT. Scale became the leading data-labelling and model-evaluation supplier to AI labs and the Pentagon. In June 2025 Meta bought 49% of Scale for $14.3B, and Wang left as CEO to become Meta's Chief AI Officer. Mid-2026 reporting still had him in that role, leading Meta's frontier-model (TBD Lab) work.
interesting_fact: He grew up in Los Alamos, New Mexico, the son of two Los Alamos National Laboratory physicists. As a teen he was a USACO finalist and made the 2014 US Physics Team, then took full-time engineering jobs at Addepar and Quora at 17.
deep_cut_fact: In March 2025 he co-wrote 'Superintelligence Strategy' with Dan Hendrycks and Eric Schmidt. The paper introduced 'Mutual Assured AI Malfunction' (MAIM), a deterrence idea modelled on nuclear MAD that explicitly covers the sabotage of rivals' datacenters.
notes: Very high-demand executive. The Meta communications/newsroom team is the likely route. His Superintelligence Strategy paper fits the podcast's data-center/energy angle.

name: Micree Zhan
current_role: Co-founder and controlling shareholder (CEO/legal representative since 2021), Bitmain Technologies, Beijing
profile: Chinese electronics engineer (b. 1979, Fujian) who co-founded Bitmain with Jihan Wu in 2013 and designed the ASIC chips behind its Antminer rigs, making it the largest bitcoin-mining hardware maker. Ousted in 2019, he regained control in a 2021 settlement, buying out Wu's camp for ~$600m. Late-2025 crypto-press reports of a fine/detention are unconfirmed.
interesting_fact: Forbes reports he first met cofounder Jihan Wu via a chance encounter on a Beijing street while working on a TV set-top-box startup; in 2018 Hurun named him the world's richest crypto entrepreneur.
deep_cut_fact: After a microelectronics master's at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Microelectronics (2004), he was an engineer at Tsinghua University's IT Research Institute, then ran DivaIP, a set-top-box startup, before Bitmain. He grew up in Minhou County, Fujian (Minhou No.1 High School).
notes: Very private; no personal channels found. Dec 2025 crypto-media rumors of regulatory fines/detention unverified - check status before outreach. Bitmain publishes only sales/supplier emails (sales.apac@bitmain.com) on its homepage, no press email.

name: Li Zhaoting
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder of Tunghsu Group (Dongxu Group); barred from China's securities markets for life
profile: Hebei-born (1965) engineer and former NPC deputy who built Tunghsu Group (Shijiazhuang) into a glass-substrate, optoelectronics, solar and EV conglomerate with three listed firms. After 2019–20 bond defaults, regulators found multiyear financial fraud, fined the group and Li personally and banned him from the market for life.
interesting_fact: Before founding Tunghsu he spent years at the Shijiazhuang Diesel Engine Factory after graduating in mechanical engineering in 1986, rising from technician to deputy general manager.
notes: Not recommended for outreach. Hebei regulators fined him personally about US$870M (reported) and imposed a lifetime market ban over the Tunghsu fraud. Caixin covered the auditor's record penalty in April 2026. No sign he has died, but there are no recent public appearances. No public contact routes found.

name: Li Qing
profile: Li Qing (李青) was listed by Hurun (2019-2021) jointly with Li Zhaoting, founder of Shijiazhuang-based Tunghsu Group (东旭集团), a maker of LCD glass substrates, optoelectronics and solar businesses. No public information about Li Qing's own role could be found; Hurun pairings like this usually denote a spouse or family member.
interesting_fact: Li Zhaoting founded Tunghsu's predecessor in 1997 after quitting a state job, taking 20-odd former subordinates and his wife's entire savings with him.
notes: Not a good outreach target: Tunghsu group has been in a prolonged debt crisis, and a Feb 2026 filing by Shanghai Challenge Textile (嘉麟杰) said Li Zhaoting had been detained by Shijiazhuang police (https://www.cls.cn/detail/2290214). Li Qing has no public profile; identity unconfirmed.

name: Yang Yafei
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Shenzhen DapuStor Microelectronics (大普微, SZSE ChiNext: 301666)
profile: Born 1979, BUPT-trained engineer with a PhD from the University of Rhode Island who spent years at Qualcomm before returning to China in 2016 to found DapuStor in Shenzhen, making enterprise SSD controller chips and SSDs for data centers. DapuStor listed on ChiNext in April 2026 as the board's first unprofitable IPO, surging ~350% on day one to a >RMB100bn market cap.
interesting_fact: DapuStor was the first loss-making company ever to list on Shenzhen's ChiNext board (April 2026); its shares opened up nearly 350% and the market cap passed RMB 100 billion on day one.
deep_cut_fact: He studied industrial automation at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (class of 1998), earned an EE PhD at the University of Rhode Island in 2008, then rose from senior to senior staff engineer at Qualcomm; he chose Longgang because Shenzhen is hardware's 'China Silicon Valley'.
notes: Strong data-center storage angle (enterprise SSDs/controllers for AI servers). IR email from 2025 annual report summary; IR phone 0755-89932506 also published there. Chinese-language outreach likely needed.

name: CC Leung
current_role: Co-founder and Vice Chairman, Quanta Computer (Taiwan)
profile: C.C. (Chee-Chun) Leung (梁次震) co-founded Quanta Computer in 1988 with fellow NTU alumnus Barry Lam, after serving as a VP at Kinpo Electronics. Quanta became the world's largest contract notebook maker and is now a leading builder of AI servers and racks for hyperscalers. He remains vice chairman and comments on the AI server outlook.
interesting_fact: A physics graduate of National Taiwan University (unlike EE-trained co-founder Barry Lam), Leung gave NT$205 million to his alma mater to support basic research.
deep_cut_fact: National Taiwan University's Leung Center for Cosmology and Particle Astrophysics (LeCosPA), founded in 2007, was created with his donation; in July 2025 it became host of the new Max Planck-IAS-NTU Center for particle physics, cosmology and geometry.
notes: Low-profile; speaks to Taiwanese press mainly at Quanta AGMs/events. No published personal or IR email found; Quanta routes media via designated spokespersons (contact via quantatw.com). LeCosPA physics connection is a strong conversation opener.

name: Rajeev Juneja
current_role: Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Mankind Pharma (New Delhi); President, PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (2025-26)
profile: Co-founded Mankind Pharma with elder brother Ramesh Juneja (company started 1991 with ~20 staff and INR 5M seed capital; incorporated 1995). Mankind sells affordable generics plus consumer brands (Manforce condoms, Prega News). He led its May 2023 IPO and the 2024 INR 13,630 crore acquisition of Bharat Serums and Vaccines.
interesting_fact: He and his younger brother were born on the same date, ten years apart; Amitabh Bachchan is Mankind's brand ambassador.
deep_cut_fact: He credits Mankind's growth to a 'startup culture' and the mantra of staying dynamic: 'In a fast-changing world, you cannot remain stationary... Every day is a new day.' He also said of the IPO: 'It makes you more responsible.'
notes: Also reachable via PHDCCI (industry chamber) in his presidency role. Company also lists investors@mankindpharma.com.

name: Matteo Danieli
current_role: Co-founder, Bending Spoons (Milan); has served as VP of Product / former Chief Product Officer
profile: Italian engineer who co-founded Bending Spoons in 2013 with Luca Ferrari, Francesco Patarnello and Luca Querella after their note-taking startup Evertale failed. Largely bootstrapped until 2022, Bending Spoons buys apps with loyal users and overhauls them (Evernote, Meetup, WeTransfer, Eventbrite, Vimeo, AOL) and was valued at ~$11B in October 2025, Italy's most valuable startup.
interesting_fact: The four cofounders met while studying in Copenhagen; their first venture, Evertale, failed before they relaunched as Bending Spoons and later moved to Milan.
deep_cut_fact: Born in 1984, he graduated with honours in Information Engineering from the University of Padua through the T.I.M.E. double-degree programme with the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), where the Copenhagen connection began; he was Evertale's CTO.
notes: Lower-profile than CEO Luca Ferrari. Reportedly stepped down from the CPO role because he felt someone else could add more value, in line with the company's meritocracy culture (per a Sourcery interview summary, unverified). Has appeared on podcasts, so he may be open to one.

name: Lin Jianhua
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Hangzhou First Applied Material (Shanghai: 603806)
profile: Co-founded Hangzhou First Applied Material in 2003 with his wife Zhang Hong after 12 years at a state-owned fertilizer factory in Zhejiang. First became the world's largest supplier of solar-module encapsulant film (EVA/POE), with over half of the global market, plus backsheets; it has since expanded into electronic-circuit and battery materials.
interesting_fact: Before founding a solar-materials giant he spent 1982-1994 working at a state-owned fertilizer factory in Zhejiang Province.
deep_cut_fact: First did not start in solar: its early product was hot-melt adhesive web film for the textile industry, and moving into EVA solar film was what the company calls its first transformation, from textiles into new energy. It now supplies over 50% of the world's PV encapsulant film.
notes: Low public profile; rarely interviewed, company communications usually come from the board secretary (Zhang Ying). Best route is the securities/IR department email; Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Anton Osika
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Lovable (Stockholm)
profile: Swedish engineer (b. 1990) who co-founded 'vibe coding' startup Lovable with CTO Fabian Hedin in 2023 after his open-source GPT-Engineer project went viral. Lovable launched in Nov 2024, hit $100M ARR in eight months and was valued at $13.3B in Aug 2026; Forbes estimates he owns ~24%. Earlier he was first employee at Sana Labs and co-founder/CTO of Depict.ai.
interesting_fact: Lovable reached $100M in annualized subscription revenue just eight months after launch - which Forbes calls the fastest-growing software startup in history; he and Hedin pledged 50% of exit proceeds to charity via Founders Pledge.
deep_cut_fact: Before startups he was a physicist: he earned a physics BSc at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, then an MSc in engineering physics at KTH, and did research tied to the ATLAS experiment at CERN.
notes: Very accessible and media-friendly; posts constantly on X and LinkedIn and does lots of podcasts/conference talks. Best route: press@lovable.dev or a DM on X. AI-software angle more than data centers/energy.

name: Fabian Hedin
current_role: Cofounder and Chief Technology Officer, Lovable (Stockholm)
profile: Swedish engineer who, after founding small startups (Tentium, TenFAST) and leading frontend at Depict.ai, was recruited by Anton Osika to cofound Lovable out of the open-source GPT Engineer project. Lovable's 'vibe coding' platform lets non-coders build apps by prompt; it hit $100M ARR eight months after its Nov 2024 launch and was valued at $13.3B in Aug 2026. He owns ~24%.
interesting_fact: Lovable reached $100M in annualized subscription revenue just eight months after launch, which Forbes calls the fastest-growing software startup in history; Hedin and Osika have pledged 50% of exit proceeds to charity.
deep_cut_fact: His path into building software started with running his own Minecraft servers in high school, a story he told on Notion's 'First Block' founder series; Lovable also dogfoods heavily, building its own internal tools (office CRM, ops software) in Lovable.
notes: Accessible, technical founder who does podcasts/conference talks (Notion First Block, Google Cloud Next, HumanX). Best route: Lovable press@ or via conference speaker circuits. Personal X/LinkedIn not verified here (web-search budget ran out).

name: Edward Bass
current_role: President, Fine Line, Inc. (Fort Worth private investment and venture capital firm); owner/developer of Sundance Square
profile: Fort Worth-born Bass brother (Yale 1967) whose share of the Sid Richardson oil inheritance grew through oil, pipelines and investments; the brothers sold their oil company to ExxonMobil in 2017 for $5.6B in stock. Best known for remaking downtown Fort Worth via Sundance Square, Bass Performance Hall and Dickies Arena, and for funding Biosphere 2; pledged $160M to Yale's Peabody Museum.
interesting_fact: In 1991 he spent about $150 million backing Biosphere 2 in Arizona, the sealed experimental ecosystem meant to show humans could live in enclosed habitats such as those in space.
deep_cut_fact: He won the 2007 Henry Hope Reed Award (given alongside Notre Dame's Driehaus Prize) for championing traditional architecture and urbanism; as chairman of Performing Arts Fort Worth he led the building of the Bass Performance Hall, which opened in 1998.
notes: Private; no published personal/office email found. Natural routes are via Fine Line, Inc. or Sundance Square (Fort Worth). Strong interest in architecture/urbanism and ecology (Biosphere 2); emeritus Yale Corporation trustee.

name: Scott Lin
current_role: Co-founder, Largan Precision; chairman of Mao Yu Memorial Co. (Maoyu), Largan's largest single corporate shareholder (no executive role at Largan)
profile: Scott Lin (Lin Yao-ying, b. 1933) co-founded Taichung-based Largan Precision with Tony Chen in 1987; it became the world's leading smartphone-lens maker and a major Apple supplier. Largan is now run by his sons; in 2020 he moved family shares into the locked holding company Maoyu. Forbes puts his fortune at about $3B.
interesting_fact: At 93, 16 years after handing over the reins, he still goes into Largan six days a week and closely follows its push into co-packaged optics (CPO) for AI data centres, studying AI alongside staff.
deep_cut_fact: An agricultural-chemistry graduate of National Chung Hsing University, he was a middle-school chemistry teacher and worked at Taiwan Sugar and a provincial ammonium-sulfate company before moving into optics; he started Largan at about 47 with no optics background.
notes: Chinese name 林耀英. Aged 93; very low profile, Chinese-language media only. 'office_email' is Largan's general company address. Outreach likely best via Largan IR or in Mandarin; CPO/data-centre optics angle is topical.

name: John Paul DeJoria
current_role: Co-founder and chairman, John Paul Mitchell Systems; co-founder of Patron Spirits (sold to Bacardi 2018); >10% holder of HighPeak Energy
profile: Born 1944 in Echo Park, LA, DeJoria sold encyclopedias and shampoo door-to-door and was at times homeless before co-founding John Paul Mitchell Systems with Paul Mitchell in 1980 on a $700 loan. He co-founded Patron in 1989 and sold it to Bacardi in 2018 ($5.1B deal). He now invests across ventures incl. West Texas oil producer HighPeak Energy (~12% stake) and runs a family foundation.
interesting_fact: Sea Shepherd-linked Captain Paul Watson Foundation named its first anti-whaling ship the 'John Paul DeJoria II' (2022); he also bought the former McDonald's HQ campus incl. Hamburger University for $40M in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the U.S. Navy at 17 straight out of high school and served on the aircraft carrier USS Hornet; in 2012 the U.S. Navy Memorial gave him its Lone Sailor Award, and he credited the Hornet with teaching him the people-management and teamwork skills he later used in business.
notes: Very public, media-friendly speaker (Shark Tank guest, documentaries, memoir). Energy angle: HighPeak Energy 13D holder plus past interests in solar and natural gas ventures. Foundation (JP's Peace, Love & Happiness) website/Instagram are the cleanest routes; no published personal or press email found. Avoid ROKiT bankruptcies as a topic.

name: Zhu Guodong
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder (~7%) of Suzhou TFC Optical Communication (300394.SZ); no board or executive role since Nov 2023
profile: Zhu Guodong (朱国栋) is the technical co-founder of TFC Optical, set up in Suzhou in 2005 with Zou Zhinong and Ou Yang as a ceramic-ferrule maker (Zhu held 25%). TFC grew into a supplier of passive optical components and optical engines for AI data centers. Zhu was a director and VP until the 2023 board election and remains a top shareholder.
interesting_fact: TFC started with a single rice-grain-sized ceramic ferrule, a part then dominated by Japanese makers; the team produced roughly a million rejects before cracking nano-zirconia sintering and cut the price by nearly two-thirds versus imports.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, Zhu graduated from Tsinghua University in welding technology and equipment, holds Singapore permanent residency, and spent about 10 years at foreign firms, working as an engineer at Singapore's Sharikat Kian Tong Pte Ltd and Aston Air Control Pte Ltd before co-founding TFC.
notes: Very low profile; English sources almost nil. He is no longer an officer, so TFC's securities/IR office (zhengquan@tfcsz.com) is only an indirect route. Sold ~1.27% of TFC via inquiry transfer in Aug 2025. Chairman/face of TFC is Zou Zhinong.

name: Mário Araripe
current_role: Founder and majority owner, Casa dos Ventos (shares leadership with CEO Lucas Araripe)
profile: Ceará-born ITA-trained engineer who ran textile, real-estate and auto businesses (bought jeep maker Troller and sold it to Ford in 2006), then founded Casa dos Ventos in 2007, now Brazil's largest renewable developer (about a third of the country's operating wind farms). TotalEnergies owns 34% of its generation JV. The firm is now pivoting to powering data centers, incl. a large campus at Pecém.
interesting_fact: Casa dos Ventos calls data centers its main growth vector: it signed a ~US$500M renewable supply deal with Ascenty (Jan 2026) and is exclusive power supplier to a large data-center campus at the port of Pecém, Ceará, linked to ByteDance/TikTok.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Crato, Ceará, son of an engineer in Brazil's federal anti-drought works department; he trained as an aeronautical-mechanical engineer at ITA. The wind idea came from ITA classmate Odilon Camargo, who urged him to be first to map Brazil's wind potential; he then used the Troller sale cash to prospect the Northeast.
notes: Company accounts, not personal. Son Lucas Araripe is CEO and the public face for data-center strategy; Mário gives occasional interviews (Forbes Brasil, Diário do Nordeste). Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Contact form is commercially oriented; no published press email found.

name: Gao Guangrong
current_role: Chairman, Eoptolink Technology Inc. (新易盛, SZSE: 300502), Chengdu
profile: Sichuan-born (1969) optical-communications engineer who co-founded Eoptolink with five partners in 2008 and listed it on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2016. Eoptolink makes high-speed optical transceivers (400G/800G/1.6T) for AI clusters and cloud data centers and has boomed with AI build-outs, making him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Eoptolink, once focused on domestic telecom, only broke into overseas hyperscaler (e.g. Amazon) supply chains around 2019; with Innolight and TFC it is nicknamed one of China's 'Yi-Zhong-Tian' AI optical-module trio, and its market cap passed RMB 350B in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: A technical-school graduate (industrial electrical automation, Chengdu Radio Machinery School), he joined the optical-communications branch of Leshan Radio Factory at 20 as a technician and stayed 10 years, then rotated through tech, purchasing, sales and management jobs before founding Eoptolink at 39.

public_contacts.value: daniel.wang@eoptolink.com (Wang Cheng, board secretary); vivi.wei@eoptolink.com (securities affairs rep)

notes: Low public profile; route via board secretary/IR. Note: CSRC issued an administrative penalty in Feb 2025 over his 2023 share sales (avoid in outreach). Strong data-center/AI angle.

name: Lisa Su
current_role: Chair, President and CEO, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)
profile: Taiwan-born, Bronx Science- and MIT-trained (BS/MS/PhD EE) semiconductor engineer who worked at Texas Instruments, IBM and Freescale before joining AMD in 2012 and becoming CEO in 2014. She led one of tech's great turnarounds; her wealth comes from AMD stock. Now she is pushing AMD's Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs into AI data centers, including a 2025 compute partnership with OpenAI, against Nvidia.
interesting_fact: At IBM she played a key role in developing the 'recipe' to replace aluminum interconnects with copper on chips without contaminating them, a technology launched in 1998 that yielded chips up to ~20% faster.
deep_cut_fact: As an MIT freshman her UROP job was 'pure grunt work' making two-inch wafers in Hank Smith's semiconductor lab in Building 39 for x-ray lithography research; that plus summer jobs at Analog Devices hooked her on semiconductors. Her PhD was among the earliest work on silicon-on-insulator (SOI).
notes: Extremely high-demand speaker; formal route is AMD Corporate Communications (corporate.pressinquiry@amd.com). Active on X (@LisaSu). Natural fit for AI data-center compute/power topics. Distant relative of Nvidia's Jensen Huang (often raised; she downplays it).

name: Cristiano Crippa
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Technoprobe S.p.A. (Euronext Milan: TPRO), since 2017
profile: Cristiano Crippa co-founded Technoprobe with his father Giuseppe Crippa (an ex-SGS/STMicroelectronics manager, d. 2025), which makes probe cards that test microchips; it is now the world's No. 2 probe-card maker with ~2,700 staff. Technoprobe listed in Milan in 2022 and later joined the FTSE MIB; Cristiano owns about 18% and has chaired the board since 2017.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Technoprobe became the first company in Italy to open a COVID vaccination hub for the general public inside its premises: a 4,300 m2 space where 160,000 doses were given to local residents over six months.
