deep_cut_fact: Technoprobe started in the garage and attic of the Crippa family home in Merate (Lecco), while his father was still working at SGS/ST; in 1997 it bought its first building in nearby Cernusco Lombardone and moved in with about 10 employees.
notes: Founding year differs by source (Forbes: 1989 with his father; company history: garage start 1993, incorporated 1996). Family-run, low media profile; press@technoprobe.com is the published route. Father Giuseppe died July 2025 - avoid leading with that.

name: Roberto Crippa
current_role: Vice President (and Vice Chairman of the Board), Technoprobe S.p.A.
profile: Roberto Crippa is the son of the late Giuseppe Crippa (d. 2025), who founded probe-card maker Technoprobe in his garage in 1989. Roberto joined in 2002, ran Italian operations and has been Vice President since 2013; Technoprobe, whose probe cards test chips before packaging (including for AI processors), listed on Euronext Milan in 2022 and Roberto owns about 18%.
interesting_fact: Technoprobe began in 1989 in Giuseppe Crippa's garage and attic while he was still working at STMicroelectronics; it became a global top probe-card supplier and made the founder a billionaire in his late 80s.
deep_cut_fact: A chemical engineer from Politecnico di Milano, he started in a technical product-development role and is author or co-author of numerous international patents; in 2018 he and brother Cristiano led the 100% acquisition of hydraulics-components engineer DA-TOR, starting a diversification into an Italian industrial hub.
notes: Forbes named him among Italy's top 100 managers in 2019. Gave a 2023 interview to Corriere della Sera's L'Economia (https://technoprobe.com/news-and-press/news-events-publications/leconomia-interview-with-roberto-crippa). Company is in Cernusco Lombardone (Lecco). info@ is a general company address.

name: Michael S. Smith
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Freeport LNG (Houston); director, Teledyne Technologies
profile: Made his first fortune with Basin Exploration, an E&P company he founded in Fort Collins in 1981 and sold to Stone Energy in 2001 for ~$428M. He founded Freeport LNG in 2002 as an import terminal, then flipped it to exports when shale arrived, raising $15B+ of debt to build three liquefaction trains in Freeport, Texas (~15 Mtpa). He still runs it and speaks publicly on U.S. LNG export economics.
interesting_fact: Freeport LNG was designed to import gas; when the shale boom hit he turned the strategy 180 degrees and built one of the largest U.S. LNG export terminals instead.
deep_cut_fact: Though he left CSU just shy of a chemistry degree, his 2016 $13M gift to Colorado State created 50 full-tuition business scholarships for the college's 50th anniversary and completed funding for the Michael Smith Natural Resources Building; he credited 'strong science and mathematics' at CSU for teaching him the oil business.
notes: Company is private. Freeport LNG press releases list media contact Heather Browne, Director Corporate Communications (phone 713-980-2888, office line), e.g. https://freeportlng.com/files/docs/FINAL-Restart-Press-Release-022123-2.pdf. Info@ email dates from a 2018 release. Speaks at CERAWeek/Milken - conference route possible.

name: Ravi Ruia
current_role: Co-founder and Vice Chairman, Essar Group (senior family figure since brother Shashi's death in Nov 2024)
profile: Co-founded Essar with elder brother Shashi in 1969, growing it from a Chennai port construction contract into a conglomerate spanning steel, oil refining, power, ports and telecom. Essar bought the Stanlow refinery (Essar Oil UK, now EET Fuels) from Shell in 2011 and sold its Indian refiner to a Rosneft-led group for $12.9bn in 2017; it now pursues energy-transition projects at Stanlow.
interesting_fact: The name Essar comes from the brothers' initials, 'S' and 'R' (Shashi and Ravi); the group's first job was a 1969 contract worth about Rs 2.3 crore to build an outer breakwater for Chennai (Madras) Port.
deep_cut_fact: He is a mechanical engineer by training, a graduate of the College of Engineering, Guindy in Chennai - India's oldest engineering college (founded 1794) - and was singled out as one of its six most notable alumni when it turned 225 in 2018.
notes: Essar's corporate press contacts are on essar.com press releases (Essar Capital corporate affairs) and EET Fuels (Stanlow) releases, but those sites blocked automated fetching, so no email was verified. Forbes profile is joint with Shashi Ruia (died 2024). Best route: Essar corporate affairs office.

name: Walter Faria
current_role: Owner and controlling shareholder, Grupo Petrópolis (Itaipava, Crystal, Petra, Black Princess beers), Brazil
profile: Brazilian brewer (b. 1955, Pedranópolis, SP) who went from a cotton gin to Brazil's largest Schincariol distributor, then bought Cervejaria Petrópolis in 1998 at ~2% market share; by 2013 Itaipava made it Brazil's No. 2 brewer. The group also makes TNT energy drink - likely the source of the 'energy' tag, not the energy sector.
interesting_fact: Under Faria, Grupo Petrópolis grew from about 2% of Brazil's beer sales in 1998 to over 11% and the No. 2 national brand in 2013, largely through aggressive marketing and low prices.
deep_cut_fact: At 13, in the Macedônia district of Fernandópolis (SP), he sold eggs and piglets around town using a horse cart - a cart he kept as a keepsake. His savings then funded a coffee-processing business with a brother.

public_contacts.value: VCRP Brasil (press relations for Grupo Petrópolis, South/Southeast, appointed 2024)

notes: Very private, gives no interviews. Carries significant legal baggage (Lava Jato 2019 arrest; group filed for judicial recovery in 2023) - poor fit and sensitive; avoid these topics. Weak link to the energy theme (beverages only). Company site blocks automated access; press route is via the group's PR agencies.

name: Garibaldi Thohir
current_role: Vice President Commissioner, PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (formerly Adaro Energy; stepped down as President Director at the June 2025 AGM)
profile: Garibaldi 'Boy' Thohir, son of Astra co-founder Teddy Thohir and brother of Erick Thohir, led the 2005 takeover of coal miner Adaro and ran it for ~2 decades, steering it toward aluminium smelting, minerals and renewables (now AlamTri; coal spun off as AADI in 2024). He is also a tech investor (ex-Gojek commissioner).
interesting_fact: He served as president commissioner of Gojek after founder Nadiem Makarim joined the cabinet in 2019, and has said he advised Nadiem informally for years before Gojek scaled.
deep_cut_fact: Back from his US MBA, he wanted a $2,000-a-month job at Citibank, but his father refused and told him to be an entrepreneur. His first venture (1991) was a plan to build a rental office on a 3,000 m2 plot along the new Saharjo-Kuningan road in Jakarta; it stalled because land clearances required at least 1 hectare.
notes: Widely known as 'Boy Thohir'. corsec@ is AlamTri's corporate secretary (company office, not personal). Some data sites still list him as President Director - outdated since June 2025. Energy-transition angle: AlamTri is building an aluminium smelter and hydro/renewables in North Kalimantan.

name: Semahat Arsel
current_role: Chair, Vehbi Koç Foundation board & executive committee; board member, Koç Holding; chair, Divan Group
profile: Semahat Sevim Arsel (b. 1928, Ankara) is the eldest child of Koç Group founder Vehbi Koç and holds a stake in Koç Holding, Turkey's largest conglomerate (energy via Tüpraş, Aygaz, autos, appliances, banking). On Koç's board since 1964, she built its tourism/hospitality arm and leads the family's main foundation.
interesting_fact: Turkey's only postgraduate nursing education center, SANERC (founded 1992 at the American Hospital, Istanbul), is named after her; she has chaired the Vehbi Koç Foundation's Nursing Committee since its nursing fund began in 1974.
deep_cut_fact: In 1972 she took charge of renovating Istanbul's Divan Hotel in Elmadağ and went on to turn 'Divan' into a luxury hospitality brand; she also co-founded TUGEV, a foundation for tourism training, and lived in Germany in 1959-60, studying at the Goethe Institute.
notes: Aged 98 and very private; no personal public channels. Best route is via the Vehbi Koç Foundation or Koç Holding corporate communications. Koç's energy link (Tüpraş refining, Aygaz, Entek power) is the podcast angle.

name: Lukas Henrik Lundin
profile: Swedish-Canadian resource financier who chaired the Lundin Group of mining and energy companies for 25+ years (Lundin Mining, Lucara Diamond, Filo Mining, NGEx etc.); family holdings were held via the Nemesia trust vehicle. He died on 26 July 2022 in Geneva, aged 64, after a two-year battle with brain cancer.
notes: Deceased 26 July 2022 (sources: https://www.mining.com/?p=1096241 ; https://filomining.mediaroom.com/2022-07-27-Filo-Minings-Founder-and-Former-Chairman-Lukas-H-Lundin-Passes-Away). Sons Adam and Jack Lundin now lead Lundin Group companies; the Lundin family remains long-term shareholders.

name: Guo Jianjun
current_role: Former general manager of Inner Mongolia Huineng Group (汇能集团); left Huineng's management and shareholding in July 2025
profile: Guo Jianjun (郭建军) is the son of Guo Jinshu, who quit as head of the Ordos coal bureau in 2004 to found Huineng Group (coal, coal-to-gas/power, roads, property). As Huineng's GM he led its capital-markets push, including a stake in Asia-Potash International and an offer for ST Xinchao (oil & gas). Hurun listed him 2019-2024; a July 2025 filing says he exited Huineng.
interesting_fact: Hurun ranked him alone under Huineng (coal, roads & bridges, property, Ordos), at No. 224 in 2024 with RMB 22bn, while his father Guo Jinshu remains Huineng's chairman.
deep_cut_fact: In his first media interview he said Huineng would enter capital markets 'in a long-term, good-faith, professional way' and would not take over companies 'like a barbarian' (不会选择'野蛮人'的方式入主).
notes: Identity confirmed (Hurun API: 郭建军/Huineng/Ordos; Sohu Aug 2026). Prior pass confused him with father Guo Jinshu. Per an Asia-Potash filing (July 2025) he left Huineng management/ownership after being penalised for disclosure violations in the ST Xinchao bid, so avoid that topic. No published personal contacts; Huineng is the only org route.

name: Hilmi Panigoro
current_role: President Director, PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MedcoEnergi), Jakarta
profile: Bandung-born geologist and younger brother of Medco founder Arifin Panigoro. Joined Medco as a director in 1998 and has run or overseen it since (President Director 2001-08 and again from 2015). MedcoEnergi spans oil & gas across Southeast Asia, power (incl. geothermal/solar) and a stake in copper-gold miner Amman Mineral.
interesting_fact: Holds an ITB geological engineering degree (1981), Thunderbird MBA core program (1984) and an MSc from the Colorado School of Mines (1988); he has over four decades in oil and gas and leads a company that has set net-zero targets.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 1981 as a wellsite geologist at Huffco/Vico Indonesia, rising to VP & Director of Business Process Reengineering before his brother invited him to join Medco as a director in 1998.
notes: Regular speaker at energy conferences (SPE, Singapore International Energy Week) and has given interviews on energy transition, so reachable via MedcoEnergi corporate communications/IR.

name: Sandra Irving
current_role: Philanthropist; co-owner of Irving Oil family interests; advisory board member, Arthur L. Irving Institute for Energy and Society (Dartmouth)
profile: Saint John, New Brunswick-born widow of Arthur L. Irving (d. May 2024), longtime chairman of Irving Oil, the private refiner/marketer that runs Canada's largest refinery in Saint John; their daughter Sarah Irving is now the family's leader at the company. Sandra is a major donor to education and medical research in Atlantic Canada and the US.
interesting_fact: With Arthur and Sarah, she co-funded the $80M lead gift that created Dartmouth's Arthur L. Irving Institute for Energy and Society, and she sits on its advisory board; she and Arthur were adopted as honorary members of Dartmouth's Class of 1972.
deep_cut_fact: She holds a BA with distinction from the University of New Brunswick and an MA in Political Science from the University of Toronto, and is an honorary Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada; with Arthur she endowed chairs in cardiology and oncology at Massachusetts General Hospital.

public_contacts.value: https://irvingoil.com/en-CA/press-room (Irving Oil press room; media contact listed as Sam Robinson, Public Affairs)

notes: Very private; no personal public channels. Arthur Irving died May 13, 2024. Most plausible routes are Irving Oil Public Affairs or the Dartmouth Irving Institute (energy/society angle fits the podcast).

name: Ilya Sutskever
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI), Palo Alto / Tel Aviv
profile: Soviet-born Israeli-Canadian AI scientist (b. 1986) who co-created AlexNet with Hinton and Krizhevsky, co-founded OpenAI and served as chief scientist through GPT/ChatGPT and o1-style reasoning. He left in 2024 to co-found SSI, which raised $3B+ at a ~$32B valuation; CEO since July 2025. In July 2026 SSI announced an NVIDIA partnership to scale its compute 10x.
interesting_fact: He won the NeurIPS Test of Time Award three years in a row (2022-2024) and received the National Academy of Sciences Award for the Industrial Application of Science in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Jerusalem he began taking Open University of Israel classes in eighth grade; after moving to Canada at 16 he spent only about a month in high school before the University of Toronto admitted him straight into third year.
notes: Very media-shy; rare interviews (e.g. Dwarkesh Podcast, Nov 2025). SSI is compute-heavy (NVIDIA deal, earlier Google Cloud TPUs) - relevant data-center angle. comms@ssi.inc is the only published inquiry address.

name: Andre Desmarais
current_role: Deputy Chairman, Power Corporation of Canada and Power Financial Corporation
profile: André Desmarais (b. 1956, Ottawa) is the youngest son of Paul Desmarais Sr. He and his brother Paul Jr. were co-CEOs of Power Corporation, the Montreal financial holding company, for about 24 years until 2020. He remains deputy chairman and sits on group boards including Great-West Lifeco, IGM Financial and Power Sustainable, the group's renewables arm.
interesting_fact: He is honorary chairman of the Canada China Business Council and served on the Hong Kong Chief Executive's Council of International Advisers from 1998 to 2007.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career at Campeau Corporation in 1979 and was a special assistant to Canada's Minister of Justice in 1980-81 before joining Power Corp in 1983. He also started and owned an experimental farm in Canada.

public_contacts.value: Media requests: Stéphane Lemay, VP, General Counsel & Secretary, Power Corporation of Canada (phone listed on contact page; no email published)

notes: No personal social accounts were found. The best route is Power Corporation's media-requests contact. For the energy angle, Power Sustainable (renewables and energy infrastructure) is the relevant group company. The first contact entry is a named media contact with a published phone number only; no email is published.

name: Paul Desmarais Jr.
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Power Corporation of Canada (and Power Financial); also long-time chairman of Groupe Bruxelles Lambert
profile: Eldest son of Power Corp builder Paul Desmarais Sr. (born Sudbury, 1954; McGill BComm, INSEAD MBA). He joined Power Corp in 1981, led the creation of Power Financial in 1984 and was co-CEO of Power Corp from 1996 until stepping back in 2020; he remains chairman. Power's holdings span Great-West Lifeco, IGM Financial, GBL, Sagard and Power Sustainable.
interesting_fact: He sat on the boards of major European energy groups, serving as a director of GDF Suez (2008-2014) and of Total until 2017, via the family's stakes held through Pargesa/Groupe Bruxelles Lambert.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm in 1981 he cut his teeth at S.G. Warburg & Co. in London and at Standard Brands in New York; in 1984 he led the creation of Power Financial Corporation.
notes: Energy angle is Power Sustainable (renewables/infrastructure; media pr@powersustainable.com per its 2025 release, https://powersustainable.com/en/news/power-sustainable-announces-plan-to-invest-and-mobilize-more-than-10-billion-into-canadian-infrastructure-and-related-companies/). Power Corp releases name Stephane Lemay (VP, General Counsel) as contact. Not to be confused with son Paul Desmarais III.

name: Surender Pal Singh Saluja
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Premier Energies Ltd (Hyderabad solar cell & module maker; listed NSE/BSE 2024)
profile: Mechanical engineer who founded Premier Energies in Hyderabad in 1995, starting with solar lanterns and streetlights. The company grew into one of India's largest integrated solar cell and module manufacturers and listed in Sept 2024, making him a billionaire. His son Chiranjeev Singh Saluja is MD; the firm is expanding cell, module and storage capacity.
interesting_fact: Premier Energies began in 1995 selling small solar products such as lanterns and streetlights, decades before India's solar-manufacturing boom; it is now among the country's largest makers of solar cells and modules.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated in mechanical engineering from Karnatak University, Dharwad, in 1969 and ran small ventures before solar; he has said his one slight regret is never having worked as an employee at a corporation early in his career.

public_contacts.value: mohit.chawla@premierenergies.com (Mohit Chawla, Marketing & Communications, Premier Energies)

notes: Name also spelled Surendar Singh Saluja. Day-to-day public face of the company is son and MD Chiranjeev Saluja; route through company communications. Strong energy/solar-manufacturing fit.

name: Lee Bass
current_role: Private investor (Lee M. Bass, Inc., Fort Worth); rancher and conservationist; Chairman Emeritus, The Peregrine Fund
profile: Lee M. Bass is one of the four Fort Worth Bass brothers who turned an inheritance from oilman uncle Sid Richardson into multibillion-dollar fortunes through oil and investing; in 2017 the brothers sold their oil company to ExxonMobil for $5.6B in stock. He runs his own investments, raises longhorns on South Texas ranches and is a leading Texas conservation philanthropist.
interesting_fact: He chaired the Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission (named chair by Gov. George W. Bush; chairman emeritus since 2001) and with wife Ramona funded the reintroduction of the endangered Aplomado falcon in South Texas; they entered the Texas Conservation Hall of Fame in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: He is a founding member of the International Rhino Foundation, and he and Ramona helped found 'South Texas Natives' (now the Texas Native Seeds Program) at the Caesar Kleberg Wildlife Research Institute; he has also chaired the TPWD White-Tailed Deer Advisory Committee.
notes: Very private; no personal website or social accounts found. Plausible indirect routes: The Peregrine Fund (peregrinefund.org) or Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation, where he holds honorary/emeritus roles - neither publishes a contact for him personally.

name: Wang Hui (David H. Wang)
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, ACM Research Inc. (Nasdaq: ACMR); chairman of its Shanghai-listed subsidiary ACM Research (Shanghai) / Shengmei Semiconductor (盛美上海)
profile: Tsinghua- and Osaka-trained engineer who founded ACM Research in Silicon Valley in 1998, then built it out in Shanghai as a maker of wafer-cleaning, electroplating, furnace and PECVD equipment for chip fabs. His wealth comes mainly from the Shanghai STAR-listed unit. He still runs the company, which is expanding into advanced-packaging tools.
interesting_fact: EY's 2023 World Entrepreneur Of The Year program (Chinese mainland) credits Wang with inventing stress-free copper polishing and holding more than 100 patents. It says his cleaning technologies can cut use of hazardous chemicals such as sulfuric acid by 50-80%.
deep_cut_fact: Wang entered Tsinghua's precision instruments department in 1978. He first went to Japan to study industrial robotics at the University of Tokyo but was referred to Osaka University because his assigned professor was retiring. After a postdoc at the University of Cincinnati, he worked at Quester Technology (1993-98) before founding ACM.
notes: Known in English as David H. Wang. The IR contacts are at The Blueshirt Group (Steven Pelayo, US; Gary Dvorchak, China). Media contact is Alyssa Lundeen at Bodewell Group. Relevant to AI/data-center chip supply chains.

name: Carl Icahn
current_role: Chairman and controlling holder, Icahn Enterprises L.P. (Nasdaq: IEP); large holder in CVR Energy, CVR Partners, Southwest Gas, Centuri, Monro
profile: Veteran activist investor from Far Rockaway, Queens, who went from Dreyfus stockbroker to buying an NYSE seat in 1968 and became one of Wall Street's most famous corporate raiders. He invests mainly through Icahn Enterprises, whose energy arm CVR Energy (refining, fertilizer) is a core holding; Ted Papapostolou became IEP CEO in May 2026.
interesting_fact: His mother pushed him into medical school; he dropped out of NYU med school after two years because he hated it, joined the Army Reserve, and ended up on Wall Street. He has given about $200M to what is now the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai.
deep_cut_fact: His Princeton philosophy thesis, 'The Problem of Formulating an Adequate Explication of the Empiricist Criterion of Meaning,' won the McCosh Prize; he called writing it 'exhilarating,' said it was the most rewarding part of Princeton, and still keeps a copy. He also worked on the business side of The Daily Princetonian.
notes: Age ~90, now based in Florida (IEP moved HQ to Sunny Isles Beach). IR@ielp.com was the IEP investor contact in Feb 2026 releases; after May 2026 releases list only phone for CEO Ted Papapostolou. X account rarely used recently. Energy angle: CVR Energy/CVR Partners, Southwest Gas.

name: Marina Budiman
current_role: Co-founder & President Commissioner, PT DCI Indonesia Tbk (DCII)
profile: Indonesian tech entrepreneur who co-founded DCI Indonesia in 2011 with Otto Toto Sugiri and Han Arming Hanafia; DCI runs Southeast Asia's first Tier IV data center and leads Indonesia's colocation market. Earlier: Bank Bali banker, CFO of Sigma Cipta Caraka (2000-08), Indonet co-founder (1994). DCI president director 2012-16, president commissioner since.
interesting_fact: Named one of Forbes Asia's 20 'Asia's Power Businesswomen' in 2021; by 2025 she was ranked among Indonesia's 10 richest people and the country's richest woman.
deep_cut_fact: She has no tech degree (University of Toronto, finance/economics) and planned to be a banker; a 1985 software-installation project at Bank Bali convinced her tech could power business. Her line: 'You will never get bored with the tech sector.'
notes: Rarely interviewed; little personal media presence. DCI is central to Indonesia's AI/hyperscale data-center build-out, a strong podcast angle. Best route via DCI corporate secretary. Net worth figures vary widely with DCII's volatile share price.

name: Fernando Augusto Zobel de Ayala
current_role: Vice Chairman, Ayala Corporation; Chairman, AC Health; director of Ayala Land and BPI (as of 2025)
profile: Fernando Zobel de Ayala (b. 1960), seventh generation of the family behind Ayala Corporation, the Philippine conglomerate spanning property, banking, telecoms and energy (ACEN). He was Ayala's President/COO for 15 years and CEO 2021-2022, stepped back in 2022, and has since returned to board roles, chairing AC Health and Ayala Foundation.
interesting_fact: Long active in Habitat for Humanity: he was Vice Chairman of Habitat for Humanity International and chaired its Asia-Pacific capital campaign steering committee.
deep_cut_fact: A serious arts patron: he helped the founders develop Art Fair Philippines in its early days, sits on international advisory committees of Tate Modern, the Met and Art SG, and in 2025 funded CIMAM travel grants for Philippine curators and museum professionals.
notes: Input middle name 'Augusto' looks like a mix-up with his brother Jaime Augusto; he is Fernando Miranda Zobel de Ayala. Ayala's energy arm is ACEN. Route via Ayala Corporation corporate communications (ayala.com contact page); I could not verify a published press email. He took a medical leave in 2022, so avoid the topic.

name: Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala
current_role: Chairman, Ayala Corporation (Philippines); also chairs BPI and ACEN (formerly AC Energy)
profile: Eldest son of the Zobel de Ayala family (b. 1959; Harvard AB '81, MBA '87); succeeded his father as Ayala Corp. CEO in 1994 and led the conglomerate (property, banking, telecom, energy) as chairman & CEO 2006-2021. Now non-executive chairman; Ayala's ACEN is a major SE Asian renewables platform.
interesting_fact: In 2007 he became the first Filipino to receive Harvard Business School's Alumni Achievement Award, its highest honour; in 2017 the UN Global Compact named him the first Southeast Asian SDG Pioneer.
deep_cut_fact: A rugby devotee who played county-level rugby in Sussex as a teen at English boarding school, he flew to France for the 2007 World Cup to cheer the All Blacks; at Harvard he rowed lightweight crew briefly and calls quitting 'one of my big regrets.'
notes: Correct spelling is Jaime (not Jamie). Wikipedia links an official Facebook page for him. Best route is Ayala Corp. corporate communications; ACEN is the energy angle.

name: Peter Shu
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Transcend Information Inc. (TWSE: 2451), Taipei.
profile: Peter Shu (Shu Chung-won, b. 1954) is a National Cheng Kung University electrical-engineering graduate and ex-HP engineer who founded Transcend in 1988-89. He built it into a major global brand of memory modules, flash cards, SSDs and USB drives with thousands of niche SKUs. In 2026 he was again named among Harvard Business Review's Taiwan Top 100 CEOs as memory prices surged.
interesting_fact: Transcend has made more than 2,000 specialised memory and board products and served 5,000+ long-term customers; Shu said in 2026 the company had not borrowed from banks in 17 years.
deep_cut_fact: Transcend began with Chinese printing: as an HP engineer Shu had worked on Chinese support for HP's LaserJet; after leaving he wrote the Chinese printer software alone in 3-4 months working 13-14 hour days. It sold 12,000 sets in year one at NT$2,500 royalty each, funding the company.
notes: Taiwan-based (listed as China in input). IR email per Transcend's shareholder-services page and 2024 annual report (spokesperson listed as Chen Po-Shou); company sites were not reachable by curl from here, so verified via search snippets. Early product was the Key Pro software-protection dongle.

name: Hal Jackman
current_role: Patriarch / largest family shareholder of E-L Financial Corporation (Toronto); former Lieutenant Governor of Ontario
profile: Henry N.R. 'Hal' Jackman (b. 1932) expanded the insurance and investment empire built by his father Harry Jackman, chairing National Trust and Empire Life; the family controls TSX-listed E-L Financial, now run by his son Duncan. He was Ontario's 25th Lieutenant Governor (1991-97) and U of T chancellor (1997-2003). In 2025 he gave $80M to U of T law, renamed the Henry N.R. Jackman Faculty of Law.
interesting_fact: His September 2025 $80 million gift was the largest ever to a Canadian law school, bringing his giving to U of T's law faculty to $100 million; the school was renamed the Henry N.R. Jackman Faculty of Law.
deep_cut_fact: While Lieutenant Governor in 1991, Jackman donated his historic collection of toy soldiers (over 650 figures) to the Royal Ontario Museum; he also served as honorary colonel of the Governor General's Horse Guards, a Toronto militia unit.
notes: Aged 94; no personal public channels. E-L Financial press releases name CFO Scott F. Ewert as the contact (published business line (416) 947-2578). Honorary-colonel detail from U of T/Victoria College sources: https://vic.utoronto.ca/henry-n-r-jackman-honoured-with-international-business-lnew-news-page

name: Safra Catz
current_role: Executive Vice Chair of the Board, Oracle Corporation (CEO 2014-Sept 2025); director, Paramount Skydance
profile: Israeli-born American executive who joined Oracle from investment bank DLJ in 1999 and rose to president, CFO and CEO (co-CEO with Mark Hurd from 2014, sole CEO from 2019). Her wealth is largely Oracle stock. In Sept 2025, amid Oracle's AI data-center build-out, she handed over to co-CEOs Clay Magouyrk and Mike Sicilia and became executive vice chair.
interesting_fact: She is credited with driving Oracle's $10.3bn hostile takeover of PeopleSoft in 2005, and in 2011 was the highest-paid woman among Fortune 1000 companies.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Holon, Israel, she moved to Brookline, Massachusetts at age six and graduated from Brookline High School; alongside running Oracle she has been a lecturer in accounting at Stanford Graduate School of Business.
notes: SEC insider data still lists her as CEO; she became Executive Vice Chair on 22 Sept 2025. Very press-shy; best route is Oracle corporate communications.

name: Adebayo Ogunlesi
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Global Infrastructure Partners (a part of BlackRock); Senior Managing Director, BlackRock; OpenAI board member
profile: Nigerian-born lawyer turned banker and infrastructure investor. After Cravath and 23 years at Credit Suisse, he cofounded Global Infrastructure Partners in 2006, building it to $100B+ AUM across energy, transport, digital infrastructure and water before selling it to BlackRock for $12.5B in 2024. He joined OpenAI's board in January 2025.
interesting_fact: Early in his career he clerked for Justice Thurgood Marshall, the first Black U.S. Supreme Court justice; he holds degrees from Oxford (BA), Harvard Law (JD) and Harvard Business School (MBA).
deep_cut_fact: Alongside his dealmaking he has taught courses on transnational investment projects at Harvard Law School, Yale Law School and the Yale School of Management.
notes: Very strong energy + AI data-center angle (GIP owns energy/digital infra; OpenAI board; GIP part of the BlackRock/MGX/Microsoft AI Infrastructure Partnership). Also director of Kosmos Energy and Topgolf Callaway. Route via BlackRock Americas corporate communications.

name: Qian Peixin
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Wang Liping) of Jiangsu Hengli Hydraulic Co. (SSE: 601100)
profile: Qian Peixin (钱佩新) is co-actual controller, with husband and chairman Wang Liping, of Jiangsu Hengli Hydraulic, a Changzhou maker of hydraulic cylinders, pumps and valves for excavators and machinery. The family controls ~64% of the Shanghai-listed firm. She is not a public-facing executive.
interesting_fact: Hurun lists her among the world's self-made women billionaires (2020-2025) on the strength of the family's stake in Hengli Hydraulic, a key supplier of hydraulic components to excavator makers.
notes: Very low public profile; virtually no interviews. Only route is Hengli's board-secretary office (hlzqb@hengli.net, from 2025 annual report). Note: in March 2026 Hengli disclosed a provincial supervisory commission action concerning chairman Wang Liping; on 13 Apr 2026 it said he had resumed duties. Weak fit for an energy podcast.

name: Shen Xiqiang
current_role: Vice chairman and major shareholder, Jiangsu Yoke Technology Co. (雅克科技, 002409.SZ)
profile: Shen Xiqiang (沈锡强, about 78) co-founded Jiangsu Yoke in Yixing, Jiangsu in 1997 as a flame-retardant chemicals maker; it listed in Shenzhen in 2010. Yoke now makes semiconductor precursors, photoresists and specialty gases, plus LNG cryogenic insulation panels. His elder son Shen Qi is chairman and his younger son Shen Fu is deputy GM.
interesting_fact: Yoke is both a chip-materials and an LNG-shipping supplier. Its insulation panels went into the world's first large Mark III Flex LNG carrier, and its LNG panel business grew 57% in 2025, while its high-k precursors go into DRAM, 3D NAND and AI advanced-packaging chips.
notes: Very low profile; no interviews found. The family business is now run by his sons, so Yoke's IR office (board secretary Qin Hongjian, per the 2025 annual report) is the realistic route. Bridges both of the podcast's themes: LNG energy shipping and semiconductor materials for AI chips.

notes: Died 27 Sep 2015 at his Fort Worth home (announced by the Rainwater Charitable Foundation). name: Nitin Sandesara
current_role: Promoter, Sandesara Group; owner of Sterling Oil Exploration & Energy Production Co. (SEEPCO), Nigeria
profile: Gujarat-born promoter of the Sandesara Group (Sterling Biotech, gelatin/pharma, energy). Since the mid-2000s the group's main asset has been Nigerian upstream producer SEEPCO, which holds OML 143 (Okwuibome field). Lived abroad from 2017 amid an Indian bank-fraud case; India's Supreme Court let criminal proceedings be closed in 2025-26 after a settlement with lenders.

deep_cut_fact: In July 2015 Africa Oil & Gas Report called the Sandesara venture Sterling Energy 'the busiest company on rig sites in Nigeria', with five rigs active at once. SEEPCO won OML 143 (then OPL 280) in Nigeria's 2005 bid round.

Hurun figure (2015) is dated. Only route found is SEEPCO's press-release media contact.

name: Xu Yanming (徐延铭)
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Zhuhai CosMX Battery Co. (珠海冠宇, SSE STAR 688772); deputy to China's National People's Congress
profile: Harbin Institute of Technology graduate who has worked on batteries for nearly 30 years. He led a team from Harbin's Guangyu group to Zhuhai in 2007 to found what became CosMX, a maker of polymer lithium-ion batteries for laptops, tablets and phones, listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021. Per TSR data, CosMX ranked No.1 globally in laptop battery shipments in 2024.
interesting_fact: CosMX ranked first worldwide in notebook-PC lithium battery shipments and second in tablet batteries in 2024 (Techno Systems Research data), and held 2,400+ granted patents by mid-2025.
deep_cut_fact: At the 2026 Two Sessions he proposed that China's lithium-battery makers copy the solar industry's playbook: a cross-supply-chain patent pool led by top firms and a 'next-generation battery technology innovation alliance' to co-develop high-silicon anodes and solid-state batteries, replacing 'litigation instead of competition'.
notes: Chinese-language outreach advisable. Chaired CosMX board meeting March 30, 2026 per SSE filing. Founding story (Harbin Guangyu spin-out, HIT alumnus) from Chinese press profiles (cnstock); verify details before quoting. No personal social accounts found.

name: Li Xue
current_role: Shareholder and member of the controlling Lee family group of Yunnan Energy New Material (SEMCORP / 恩捷股份, 002812.SZ); no executive post
profile: Li Xue (李雪), registered as Sherry Lee, is one of six members of the Paul Xiaoming Lee family who jointly control Yunnan Energy New Material (Enjie/SEMCORP), the Yuxi-based world leader in wet-process lithium-battery separator film that grew out of a cigarette-packaging printer. Hurun's 2022 Self-Made Women list ranked her No. 33 with RMB 19.5bn. She holds no management role at the company.

deep_cut_fact: She has been a direct shareholder since about 2010, when the Lee family moved stakes in the predecessor Chuangxin Color Printing from the offshore Newston vehicle to Heyi Investment, Li Xue and other family members.
notes: Identity confirmed: Hurun API (2022 women list: 李雪, Energy New Material/恩捷股份, Yuxi) plus Sina Finance naming 'Sherry Lee (李雪)' among Enjie's six actual controllers. She is Paul Xiaoming Lee's daughter (prior pass wrongly linked her to Li Xiaohua). Very private; no interviews or accounts found. Route only via Enjie's securities office.

name: Martin Viessmann
current_role: Non-executive member of the Board of Directors, Viessmann Generations Group (family investment holding, Battenberg/Allendorf, Germany)
profile: Grandson of founder Johann Viessmann (1917); led the heating-systems maker as managing partner/CEO from 1989 and pushed it into renewables and efficiency. After the 2024 sale of Viessmann Climate Solutions to Carrier, the family runs Viessmann Generations Group, an investment company 'co-creating living spaces for future generations', with son Max as co-CEO; Martin now sits on its board.
interesting_fact: A fitness buff and passionate skier, he holds a professional pilot's license and an honorary doctorate from the University of Wisconsin; Viessmann is a major winter-sports sponsor.
deep_cut_fact: In Dec 2012 he and wife Annette endowed UW Oshkosh's first-ever endowed chair, the Viessmann Endowed Chair in Sustainable Technology, capping a partnership that in 2011 opened the Western Hemisphere's first dry-fermentation anaerobic biodigester on that campus.

public_contacts.value: phiv@viessmann.com (Philine von Hardenberg, Director Corporate Communications, Viessmann Generations Group)

notes: Forbes bio calling him chairman of the executive board is outdated: group site lists him as non-executive board member; son Max Viessmann leads. Best route is Generations Group corporate communications. Strong US tie via UW Oshkosh partnership.

name: Susan Ocampo
current_role: Director, MACOM Technology Solutions (MTSI); co-founder, VP, Secretary & Treasurer of GaAs Labs LLC
profile: Filipino-American co-founder (with her late husband John Ocampo) of RF chipmaker Sirenza Microdevices in 1984 and of investment fund GaAs Labs in 2008, which bought MACOM in 2009. She is MACOM's largest individual shareholder (10%+ owner) and a board member; John died in November 2023. name: Irwin Jacobs
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman Emeritus, Qualcomm; philanthropist (San Diego)
profile: MIT/UCSD electrical-engineering professor who co-founded Linkabit (1968) and then Qualcomm (1985), commercialising CDMA, the technology underlying modern cellular networks; CEO until 2005 and chairman until 2009, he left the board in 2012. Now in his 90s, he remains a major San Diego philanthropist and still appears at events (TechCon Fellows Lifetime Achievement Award, April 2026).

name: Mikail Gutseriyev
current_role: Founder and owner of the SAFMAR group (Russneft, Neftisa, Russian Coal, A101 and media assets). He left the Russneft board after EU sanctions in 2021.

name: Shouliang Miao
current_role: Chairman and President, Shenzhen Fuyuan Group (深圳市富源实业(集团)有限公司)
profile: Miao Shouliang (缪寿良, b. 1955, Wuhua, Meizhou) came to Bao'an, Shenzhen in 1987 with RMB 2,000 and ~30 fellow villagers to run a quarry that supplied Shenzhen's airport and expressways. notes: Known in English as Li Shui-po; company 新莱应材 / Kinglai Group. IR emails belong to the board secretary (Zhu Mengyong) and securities rep (Wang Mengdie) per the 2025 annual report summary. Tagged 'Green Energy' but the business is ultra-clean materials for semiconductor/biopharma - a chip supply-chain angle.

name: Ding Feng
current_role: Non-executive director and co-controlling shareholder, Wanbang Digital Energy (Star Charge), Changzhou
profile: Ding Feng is the husband of Star Charge founder Shao Danwei; together they control about 87% of Wanbang Digital Energy (Star Charge), a Changzhou-based maker of EV chargers, microgrid and storage systems that has shipped 2M+ chargers to ~70 countries and filed for a Hong Kong IPO in Jan 2026. He keeps a low profile behind his wife.
interesting_fact: Per the 2026 HK prospectus, Ding and Shao each hold 1.36% directly and own 50/50 the Wanbang Investment Group, which holds 84.44%; the loss-making charging-network operation was spun out to another company they control before the IPO.
notes: Common name; identity inferred from Hurun 'shared with Shao Danwei' + Star Charge. Reports call him a behind-the-scenes adviser; some say he earlier founded a Wanbang auto business (unverified). Shao Danwei is the public face; approach via Star Charge corporate contact.

name: Shao Danwei
current_role: Founder, executive director and CEO, Wanbang Digital Energy (Star Charge / 星星充电), Changzhou; chairman since Dec 2017
profile: Changzhou-born founder (age ~43, Nanjing University of Finance & Economics) of Star Charge, China's No. 2 public EV-charging network (15.7% share, Nov 2025) with 2M+ chargers delivered to ~70 countries. She and husband Ding Feng control ~87% of parent Wanbang Digital Energy, which filed for a Hong Kong IPO in January 2026 after earlier listing attempts.
interesting_fact: Before starting Star Charge in 2014 she ran a car-dealership business, serving as executive director and CEO of Jiangsu Wanbang Jinzhixing auto investment group (2012-2014); she has been vice chair of the Jiangsu General Chamber of Commerce since July 2022.
deep_cut_fact: She says Star Charge began after an August 2014 dinner in Laoshan with TELD chairman Yu Dexiang: she wanted to buy his chargers, his quote was too high, so she built her own - joking in 2024, 'If you had given me a cheaper price, there would be no runner-up today.'
notes: No personal channels found; route via Star Charge corporate/international team. Company is mid-IPO process in Hong Kong (filed Jan 2026), which may limit media availability. Chinese-language outreach likely more effective.

name: Huang Xiaonan
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, DeepZero (深演智能, HKEX: 2723), Beijing
profile: Peking University alumna and ex-McKinsey manager who cofounded ad-tech firm iPinYou (品友互动) with Xie Peng in April 2009. Renamed DeepZero, it now sells decision-AI agents for marketing and sales to large enterprises and listed in Hong Kong in May 2026, where the retail tranche was ~5,480x oversubscribed and shares nearly tripled on debut.
interesting_fact: DeepZero's Hong Kong IPO in May 2026 was ~5,480x oversubscribed in the public tranche; shares priced at HK$55.5 opened at HK$155 (+179%), turning a 2009 ad-tech startup into one of the year's hottest AI listings.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding iPinYou she worked at Procter & Gamble in the 1990s, running decisions on Nielsen retail-audit 'small data', then was a project manager at McKinsey Beijing; her cofounder Xie Peng was a P&G Guangzhou regional sales manager.

public_contacts.value: marketing@ipinyou.com (company contact email listed on DeepZero site)

notes: Gives media interviews (e.g. Shanghai Securities News, Sept 2026) on enterprise AI agents - a natural fit for the podcast. Her name is sometimes romanized Huang Xiaonan / Xiao Nan Huang; some sources render it 黄晓楠.

name: Folorunsho Alakija
current_role: Executive Vice Chairman, Famfa Oil Ltd; Group Managing Director, Rose of Sharon Group
profile: Nigerian businesswoman who moved from secretarial and banking jobs into fashion (Supreme Stitches, later Rose of Sharon House of Fashion), then won an oil prospecting licence in 1993 for the offshore block containing the Agbami field, developed with Chevron. Now focused on philanthropy, ministry and writing; served as Chancellor of Osun State University 2016-2026.
interesting_fact: In 2025 she funded and donated a 250-bed teaching hospital (the Modupe and Folorunso Alakija Medical Research and Training Hospital) to Osun State University, reportedly worth N34 billion.
deep_cut_fact: Her career began in 1974 as an executive secretary at Sijuade Enterprises in Lagos after secretarial studies at Pitman Central College, London; she later served as president of the Fashion Designers Association of Nigeria and remains a trustee.
notes: Name often spelled Folorunso. Her official site has a 'Let's Talk' contact form and a Press section; she is publicly active as an author and Christian minister, so the personal site is the best route.

name: Stefan Schoerghuber
profile: Owner and CEO of Munich's Schörghuber Unternehmensgruppe (construction/real estate, brewing via Paulaner/BrauHolding, hotels), which he took over after his father Josef died in 1995. Died unexpectedly 25 November 2008 aged 47; widow Alexandra Schörghuber later led the group.
notes: Deceased (25 Nov 2008, per Wikipedia and Brauwelt https://brauwelt.com/en/international-report/europe-russia/626074-brewer-and-hotelier-stefan-schrghuber-dies-at-47). Skip.

name: Eugenio Garza Laguera
notes: Eugenio Garza Laguera, longtime chairman of FEMSA and of the Tec de Monterrey board, died May 24, 2008 in Monterrey at age 84. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugenio_Garza_Lag%C3%BCera ; https://www.femsa.com/en/press-room/press-release/fundacion-paz-es-a-b-p-recognizes-the-life-and-legacy-of-eugenio-garza-laguera/

name: Jean Claude Gandur
current_role: Founder & Chairman, AOG (Addax & Oryx Group, owner of Oryx Energies); Founder, Fondation Gandur pour l'Art
profile: Grasse-born (1949) Swiss oil entrepreneur who founded the Addax & Oryx Group in 1987, built Addax Petroleum into a major Nigeria-focused producer and sold it to Sinopec in 2009 for about US$7.3bn. He then launched Toronto-listed Oryx Petroleum (Iraqi Kurdistan; left board after 2020 change of control) and now chairs AOG while focusing on his art foundation.
interesting_fact: His collection of Egyptian antiquities is one of the largest still in private hands; his Fondation Gandur pour l'Art (est. 2010) is planning a museum in Caen, France, on a 51,000 m² site.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Alexandria, Egypt until age 12, studied law and political science at Lausanne and history at the Sorbonne, and started in 1976 at commodities trader Philipp Brothers (Phibro), spending eight years at its Zug subsidiary before founding AOG.
notes: Listed country UK but based in Geneva/Switzerland. info@fg-art.org is the general mailbox of his art foundation; Oryx Energies (AOG's African downstream energy arm, Geneva) is the business route. Hurun/Forbes listings stale since ~2016.

name: Alexander Knaster
current_role: Founder, Pamplona Capital Management (London); majority owner of Pisa SC; founder of The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research
profile: Moscow-born (1959) financier who emigrated to the US at 16, studied EE/maths at Carnegie Mellon and got a Harvard MBA, ran CSFB Russia and then Alfa-Bank (1998-2004) before founding Pamplona Capital in 2004, a London private-equity/TMT manager (~$15B AUM in 2021). He bought 75% of Italian club Pisa in 2021 (promoted to Serie A in 2025) and has put the bulk of his assets into The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research.
interesting_fact: He named Pamplona Capital after the San Fermin festival in Pamplona, which he attended after graduating from Harvard Business School.
deep_cut_fact: Energy roots: in 1980, fresh out of Carnegie Mellon, he took a job as an engineer with Schlumberger working on oil platforms in the Gulf of Mexico. He later endowed the Alexander M. Knaster Scholarship Fund (1993) for CMU electrical & computer engineering undergrads.

public_contacts.value: ed.orlebar@tbcardew.com (Tavistock/TB Cardew - media enquiries for Pamplona)
info@themarkfoundation.org (The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research)

notes: Wikipedia article flagged for possible COI editing; facts used are biographical basics. Political donor (UK Conservatives) - avoid. Pamplona has moved away from energy; his podcast hooks are the Schlumberger start, Alfa-Bank era and Pisa football. Best route: Pamplona media contact at TB Cardew.

name: Sanjay Singal
current_role: Former chairman & managing director / promoter, Bhushan Power & Steel Ltd (company now owned by JSW Steel)
profile: Sanjay Singal, from the family behind the Bhushan steel businesses, built Bhushan Power & Steel into a large integrated steelmaker with operations in Odisha. The company went into insolvency in 2017, and JSW Steel took it over through a resolution plan (₹19,700 crore). He no longer controls the business and has spent recent years contesting the process in court.
interesting_fact: In September 2025 the Supreme Court of India upheld JSW Steel's ₹19,700 crore resolution plan for Bhushan Power & Steel, after briefly ordering liquidation in May 2025 at the former promoters' urging.
notes: He is a low-value and sensitive outreach target: he lost control of BPSL in insolvency, faced ED/CBI fraud proceedings, and the Supreme Court criticised the former promoters in 2025. No published contacts or public profile were found. No positive, sourced deep-cut fact was found.

name: Lin Zhiqiang
current_role: Chairman, Sanan Optoelectronics Co. (SSE: 600703), Xiamen; director at Fujian Sanan Group
profile: Eldest son of Sanan Group founder Lin Xiucheng (Hurun lists the fortune jointly). Born 1974 in Anxi, Fujian, he joined the family group in 1996, became Sanan Optoelectronics' general manager in 2011 and chairman in July 2017. Sanan is China's largest LED chip maker and is expanding into SiC/GaN compound semiconductors for EVs, inverters and power electronics.
interesting_fact: Sanan reached the stock market via a 2008 backdoor listing into the suspended, loss-making Tianyi Technology, which was turned into China's LED chip leader after the family injected Sanan Electronics' LED wafer and chip assets.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economic management at the PLA Naval Command College and has served as a local people's congress deputy in Anxi County and in Xiamen's Siming District.
notes: IR email is the board-secretary contact in Sanan's 2025 annual report summary. Sensitive timing: in 2026 Sanan disclosed that founder Lin Xiucheng and vice-chairman Lin Kechuang were placed under investigation, and the company swung to losses. Deep-cut source is a secondary Chinese profile site; verify before use.

name: John B Hess
current_role: Director, Chevron Corp (since July 2025, after Chevron's $53B acquisition of Hess Corp); director, Goldman Sachs
profile: Son of Hess founder Leon Hess, he joined the family firm as a trainee in 1976 and was CEO from 1995 until 2025, turning Hess into an exploration-and-production company with a stake in Guyana's giant Stabroek oil discoveries and the Bakken. Chevron bought Hess for ~$53B (closed July 18, 2025) and he joined Chevron's board and its Public Policy & Sustainability Committee.
interesting_fact: Hess's 30% stake in Guyana's Stabroek block, one of the biggest oil finds of the past decade, was the main prize in Chevron's $53B takeover, which was delayed over a year by an arbitration with ExxonMobil.
deep_cut_fact: Despite growing up wealthy he pumped gas at the family's Hess stations, joined his father on foreign oil fields at age seven, and as a Harvard undergraduate studied in Beirut, becoming fluent in Arabic and Farsi.
notes: No personal or family-office contact published; Hess Corp no longer exists as a separate company, so Chevron (board) is the institutional route. Recent CEO talks frame oil and gas as needed alongside AI-driven power demand, a good podcast hook.

name: Thomas Kurian
current_role: CEO, Google Cloud (Alphabet), since January 2019
profile: Kerala-born, Princeton-trained engineer Thomas Kurian spent 22 years at Oracle, rising to president of product development over a ~35,000-person engineering org, which made him wealthy via Oracle equity. Since 2019 he has run Google Cloud, turning it into a profitable, fast-growing business at the centre of Google's AI infrastructure and data-center buildout.
interesting_fact: His identical twin George Kurian is CEO of NetApp; in 1996 the twins effectively swapped careers - George moved from Oracle to McKinsey while Thomas left McKinsey to join Oracle.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Pampady, Kottayam, he and his twin boarded at Jesuit-run St Joseph's Boys' High School in Bangalore; both got into IIT Madras but took the SAT there and won partial scholarships to Princeton, moving to the US at 17. He graduated summa cum laude in electrical engineering.
notes: Wealth listed by Hurun is attributed to Oracle; he now runs Google Cloud - highly relevant for a data-center/AI podcast. Route via Google Cloud press team. X handle @ThomasOrTK ('CEO of @GoogleCloud') confirmed only via an aggregator; he is also active on LinkedIn.

name: Mahabir Prasad Agarwal
current_role: Chairman Emeritus (advisory), Shyam Metalics and Energy Ltd (NSE: SHYAMMETL); stepped down as chairman in May 2025
profile: Kolkata-based first-generation steel entrepreneur and co-promoter of Shyam Metalics and Energy, an integrated maker of ferro alloys, steel, aluminium foil and captive power, listed in 2021. He chaired the company until May 2025, when he resigned citing his age. Brij Bhushan Agarwal became chairman and MD, and Mahabir Prasad Agarwal stayed on as chairman emeritus.
interesting_fact: When he stepped down as chairman in May 2025, Shyam Metalics kept him on as chairman emeritus in an advisory role rather than letting him retire outright.
notes: Elderly and retired from the chair, so a low public profile. The company's Head of IR is Pankaj Harlalka, per the Nov 2026 earnings-call transcript. Unverified social posts say he started as a steel trader around 1970 and opened a sponge-iron plant in Sambalpur in 1990; these are not used as facts. The current chairman and MD, Brij Bhushan Agarwal, is the more active spokesman.

name: Stefan Fuchs
current_role: CEO (Chairman of the Executive Board), FUCHS SE, Mannheim (contract extended to June 2029)
profile: Third-generation family leader of FUCHS (formerly Fuchs Petrolub), founded in 1931 in Mannheim and now the world's largest independent lubricants supplier with ~6,000 staff in 50+ countries. He joined in 1996, entered the Executive Board in 1999 and has been CEO since 2004; the board extended his contract in Oct 2025 to 2029. (Input name 'Stefan Fuch' is a misspelling.)
interesting_fact: FUCHS has grown from a 1931 Mannheim family business into the world's largest independent supplier of lubrication solutions, independent of the oil majors; Stefan Fuchs has run it for more than 20 years.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he spent two years as an auditing assistant at Wollert-Elmendorff Deutsche Industrie-Treuhand in Mannheim, then was posted (1997-99) to Fuchs Lubricants Co. in Harvey, Illinois, responsible for Argentina, Brazil and Mexico. He also sits on the supervisory board of machine-tool maker TRUMPF.
notes: Input name misspelled ('Stefan Fuch'). Press contact Tina Vogel (FUCHS SE Public Relations) per July 2026 release. Born 1968; Mannheim University business graduate.

name: W Brett Welson
current_role: Chairman, Prairie Merchant Corporation (private merchant bank); co-founder (ret.) of FirstEnergy Capital
profile: W. Brett Wilson (input spelling 'Welson' is a typo) is a Saskatchewan-born investment banker who co-founded Calgary energy investment bank FirstEnergy Capital in 1993 (with Murray Edwards and others) and chaired it until 2008. He was a Dragons' Den panellist (seasons 3-5) and now invests via Prairie Merchant in energy, real estate, agriculture and sports (incl. a Nashville Predators stake).
interesting_fact: He bills himself as the all-time lead deal-making 'dragon' on CBC's Dragons' Den, and wrote the 2012 Penguin book 'Redefining Success: Still Making Mistakes'.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance, Wilson earned a civil engineering degree and spent three years working the oilfields of Western Canada for Imperial Oil, then did an MBA in entrepreneurship at the University of Calgary (1985) and started at McLeod Young Weir.
notes: Hurun $2B figure looks inflated (other estimates far lower). Very active and outspoken on social media; has had public controversies over posts (2018, 2020) - be aware. Prolific philanthropist (prostate cancer, domestic-abuse research, mental health) and regular podcast guest, so likely receptive.

name: Ronald Mc Aulay
current_role: Director, Sir Elly Kadoorie & Sons Ltd (Kadoorie family office); former long-time director of CLP Holdings and Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels
profile: Ronald McAulay (b. 1935/36), a Scottish-born Hong Kong businessman, married into the Kadoorie family. His wealth stems mainly from a roughly 10% stake, held through trusts, in CLP Holdings, Hong Kong's biggest power utility. He sat on CLP's board 1968-2016 and on Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels' board 1972-c.2017.
interesting_fact: He joined the board of CLP, Hong Kong's main power utility, in 1968 at age 32 and served nearly half a century, leaving on 1 October 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the Kadoorie businesses he trained as an accountant: he is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Scotland, holds a master's degree from the University of Glasgow, and was schooled at Gordonstoun.
notes: Very private and about 90 years old. I found no death report, and Wikipedia (edited 2026) lists him as living. No published personal contact; the only route is via the Kadoorie family office (Sir Elly Kadoorie & Sons, Hong Kong) or CLP corporate communications. Input lists the country as China (Hong Kong); he is a British citizen.

name: Catherine Lozinck
profile: Catherine Lozick (correct spelling), daughter of Swagelok co-founder Fred A. Lennon, inherited a majority stake in the Solon, Ohio valve and fittings maker. Forbes reports she died in January 2025 at age 79. Swagelok is now led by Fred Lennon's grandson Thomas F. Lozick as chairman and CEO.
notes: Deceased January 2025 per Forbes profile (https://www.forbes.com/profile/catherine-lozick/). Input name is misspelled ('Lozinck'). Family remains very private; Swagelok is run by Thomas F. Lozick (https://swagelok.com/en/about/news/swagelok-announces-election-of-directors).

name: Maria del Carmen Sundblad Beccar Varela
current_role: Matriarch and shareholder of the Perez Companc Family Group (Argentina); founder of Munchi's ice cream and driving force behind Temaikèn.
profile: Born 1942, 'Munchi' Sundblad is the widow of Gregorio Pérez Companc (d. 2024), whose family controls Pecom (oil & gas services/production, expanding in Argentine upstream), Molinos Río de la Plata food and farmland. She built her own businesses: the Munchi's ice-cream chain, a Jersey dairy herd, and the Temaikèn bioparque in Escobar.
interesting_fact: She personally decided to build Temaikèn in Escobar, which opened in 2002 as Latin America's largest theme/bioparque, and she weighed in on the family's historic 2002 sale of Pecom Energía to Petrobras for about US$1bn.
deep_cut_fact: Her ice-cream brand Munchi's is named after her own childhood nickname; she also raises prize Jersey cattle at the family's San Isidro Labrador cabaña in Escobar, which she visited weekly, and La Nación wrote she only raises her voice when her bulls win at a rural show.
notes: Extremely private family ('extremists of anonymity'); no personal channels. Alive status presumed (on Hurun Global 2025-26 lists, no obituary found; would be 84). Contacts are company forms only (Munchi's, Pecom). Husband Gregorio died June 2024.

name: Giannis Vardinogiannis
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Motor Oil (Hellas) Corinth Refineries; Chairman & CEO, Avin Oil
profile: Eldest son of the late Vardis Vardinoyannis and head of the Vardinoyannis group, which controls Greek refiner Motor Oil Hellas. CEO since 2021 and chairman since Nov 2024, he has pushed the refiner into renewables (2.2 GW via the 2024 Anemos RES deal), waste/circular economy and banking (Optima Bank, listed 2023), with interests in shipping, upstream and hospitality.
interesting_fact: He ran Panathinaikos FC from 2000, taking the club to the Champions League quarter-finals in 2001-02, and was a founding member and later president of Greece's Super League.
deep_cut_fact: A Vassar economics graduate, he won the Greek Rally championship six straight times (1987-1992) in a Lancia Delta with co-driver Kostas Stefanis, and in 2024 founded the private team Cyclon Rally Sport.
notes: Also spelled Yannis/Ioannis Vardinoyannis. No published personal or press email verified (moh.gr blocked automated access); Motor Oil IR officer listed as Mary Psyllaki on market-data sites.

name: Robin Khuda
current_role: Founder and CEO, AirTrunk
profile: Dhaka-born accountant who moved to Sydney at 18, worked at Fujitsu, PIPE Networks and NEXTDC (as CFO), then founded hyperscale data-center operator AirTrunk in 2015. Blackstone and CPP Investments bought AirTrunk in 2024 in a A$24B (~US$16B) deal; he remains CEO and is expanding across APAC, the Middle East and India (a ~US$30B India plan announced in 2026).
interesting_fact: In AirTrunk's early days he dipped into his retirement savings to keep it afloat and came close to bankruptcy; in 2024 he was named AFR Business Person of the Year. In 2025 he gave A$100M to the University of Sydney for a 20-year women-in-STEM program.
deep_cut_fact: Right before founding AirTrunk he left NEXTDC to become CEO of Mint Wireless, a telecom payments company; he says he had been watching the cloud boom since 2010-11 and planning his own data-center business.
notes: Elected Fellow of ATSE in 2026. Runs the Khuda Family Foundation (women in tech, mental health). Also founded luxury developer Ondas. Excellent fit for the data-center podcast; route via AirTrunk media.

name: Amjad Masad
current_role: Cofounder and CEO, Replit
profile: Jordan-raised son of refugees who moved to the US in 2012 as an early engineer at Codecademy, then worked on Facebook's JavaScript infrastructure before cofounding Replit in 2016 with his wife Haya Odeh. Replit became a leader in AI 'vibe coding' agents and was valued at $9bn after a $400m round in March 2026.
interesting_fact: As a teenager in Jordan he made money building software management systems for local internet cafes; Replit's backers now include a16z, Coatue, Shaquille O'Neal, Jared Leto and Qatar's QIA.
deep_cut_fact: Before Replit he was tech lead on Facebook's JavaScript infrastructure team, which built or maintained the Babel compiler, Jest and the React Native packager; before that he was Codecademy's #1 employee, briefly at Yahoo, and worked in cybersecurity while in college.
notes: Very active and accessible on X (@amasad); has done many podcasts, so a direct X reply/DM plus press@replit.com is the best route. Strong AI/data-center angle (compute-hungry coding agents).

name: Zhu Gongshan
current_role: Founder, chairman and joint CEO of GCL Technology Holdings (3800.HK); chairman of GCL Group (Golden Concord)
profile: Born 1958 in Funing, Yancheng, Jiangsu, Zhu founded GCL in Hong Kong in 1990, first building cogeneration power plants, then moving into solar-grade polysilicon from 2006. GCL Tech became one of the world's largest polysilicon makers and is now pushing low-energy FBR granular silicon. He also chairs the Asian Photovoltaic Industry Association and the Global Green Energy Industry Council.
interesting_fact: Zhu trained as a power engineer, graduating from Nanjing Electric Power College (now Nanjing Institute of Technology) in 1981. GCL's first business was thermal and cogeneration power plants, years before it became a solar-materials giant.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding GCL he worked ordinary jobs from 1978, including as a shop sales clerk. He later chaired the SNEC Hydrogen Energy Industry Alliance Council and was named one of the 'Ten Outstanding Contributors to New China's New Energy Industry' in its 70th year.
notes: ESG@gcl-power.com is the corporate contact printed in GCL Tech's 2025 annual/ESG report (Suzhou HQ, tel +86 512 6853 3900); no dedicated press email was found. He speaks often at SNEC and global solar forums, so a conference is a plausible route. The sales-clerk detail comes from an ifeng profile (https://finance.ifeng.com/people/comchief/zhugongshan.shtml); the award and hydrogen role from the HKEX annual report.

name: William Koch
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Oxbow Corporation / Oxbow Carbon (West Palm Beach, Florida)
profile: William 'Bill' Koch, one of the four sons of Koch Industries co-founder Fred Koch, founded Oxbow in 1983 after leaving the family business; it grew into a major trader and processor of petroleum coke, coal, sulphur and other carbon products. He remains chairman, and is also a big collector of art, wine and Old West memorabilia.
interesting_fact: He won the 1992 America's Cup with his America3 syndicate, then in 1995 entered 'Mighty Mary', a boat crewed mostly by women, in the next Cup.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2011 he paid about $2.3m at Brian Lebel's Old West auction in Denver for the 'Upham tintype', the only authenticated photo of Billy the Kid; it joined his Wild West collection that includes Custer's rifle and Remington bronzes.
notes: Born 1940; listed on Forbes real-time 2026, no death reports found. Oxbow is private; a 2015 Oxbow press release listed a Corporate Communications Office in West Palm Beach (phone 561-907-5422, Director Corporate Affairs Brad Goldstein) - may be outdated. oxbow.com did not respond to direct fetch. Avoid the Koch-brothers feud and Oxbow litigation topics.

name: Mariarosa Lavelli
current_role: Major shareholder (~11%) of Technoprobe S.p.A. (Euronext Milan); co-founder of the Fondazione Mariarosa e Giuseppe Crippa
profile: Widow of Giuseppe Crippa (d. July 2025), an ex-STMicroelectronics engineer who founded Technoprobe, now a global leader in probe cards for chip testing used by Nvidia, Apple, TSMC and others. She handled the administration from the start and was still reported in 2022 to follow the family company's accounts. Owns ~11% since the 2022 IPO.
interesting_fact: Technoprobe started in the garage and attic of the Crippa family home in Merate (Lecco). In 1993 the nucleus was Giuseppe, son Cristiano, Mariarosa on administration and two employees. It moved to its first building in 1996 with about 10 staff.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2023 she and Giuseppe set up the Fondazione Mariarosa e Giuseppe Crippa to give structure to the family's and Technoprobe's philanthropy. Il Giorno noted she 'still follows the accounts' of the family firm even after it made Giuseppe a billionaire at 87.
notes: Recently widowed (July 2025), so be sensitive. Never gives interviews; route via Technoprobe press office. The family (son Cristiano Crippa, CEO Stefano Felici) is the public face. The foundation's start date is given as May 2023 in Technoprobe materials.

name: Li Jianli (励建立)
current_role: Chairman, Shenzhen Kedali Industry Co. (科达利, SZSE 002850)
profile: Ningbo-born mould designer who co-founded Kedali in Shenzhen in 1996 with his brother using ~RMB 20,000 of savings. Kedali moved from stamping dies to phone-battery parts and, from 2007, to precision structural parts for EV batteries; it listed in Shenzhen in 2017 and supplies CATL, BYD, CALB, EVE, Panasonic and LG, with ~32% global share in 2023.
interesting_fact: In 2007, as iPhone-era pouch cells threatened his phone-battery parts business, he put more than half its profits into EV battery structural parts; R&D succeeded by 2010 and the segment grew from RMB 66m revenue (2013) to RMB 930m (2016).
deep_cut_fact: He studied mould design at a technical secondary school, graduated in 1991 and went to Shenzhen as a die designer at a Hong Kong-owned firm. Kedali's break came in 1999 when BYD asked it to co-develop phone-battery parts: after 20+ attempts in a year it matched Japanese imports at about a third of the price.
notes: Low media profile; Chinese-language outreach advisable. No published email found on company site; best route is Kedali's investor-interaction page (cninfo IRM, linked from its website) or the company contact page https://www.kedali.com.cn/contact.html. Brother Li Jianju (励建炬) is president.

name: Airat Shaimiev
current_role: Head (CEO) of JSC Tatavtodor, Tatarstan's state road-construction company; co-owner of TAIF shareholders' stake in Sibur
profile: Son of Tatarstan's first president, Mintimer Shaimiev. He built his fortune as a co-owner of TAIF Group, a Tatarstan holding with refining and petrochemical assets that merged into Sibur in 2021; TAIF shareholders received 15% of Sibur. He still runs Tatavtodor, the regional road builder, which reported 2025 contracts worth billions of rubles.
interesting_fact: With his brother Radik and his son Timur he also owns MNKT, a small oil producer in Tatarstan (per Forbes).
deep_cut_fact: He practiced karate in Soviet times, when the sport was banned in the USSR. After it was legalised he won the Kazan championship, then took up motor racing; he and his brother raced in the first events at the Vysokaya Gora autodrome in 1996.
notes: He is under UK sanctions (OpenSanctions entry gb-hmt-15608), so outreach may raise compliance and reputational issues. The only published contact is Tatavtodor's general company email. He gives few interviews.

name: Wang Nan
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Puya Semiconductor (普冉股份, Shanghai STAR Market 688766)
profile: Born 1976; SJTU physics graduate who spent 14 years at Hua Hong NEC (engineer to senior director) before founding Puya in 2012/2016. Puya makes NOR Flash, EEPROM and MCUs, listed in 2021, bought SLC-NAND maker SkyHigh Memory, saw H1 2026 profit jump ~19x on AI-driven memory demand, and plans a Hong Kong listing.
interesting_fact: He bet on an unfashionable process: Puya was the first to build general-purpose NOR Flash on the SONOS charge-trap process (instead of incumbents' ETOX), whose low power and tiny die size rode the TWS-earbud boom into Xiaomi, Samsung, OPPO and vivo products.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a double bachelor's in physics and applied electronics from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and, while still at Hua Hong NEC, earned an EMBA (2011) from Washington University in St. Louis' Olin Business School.
notes: Low-profile; few personal interviews. Route via board secretary / IR (ir@puyasemi.com). Hurun lists name as Wang Nan (王楠). Company announced H-share HK listing plans in Nov 2026.

name: Yao Lijun
current_role: Founder, Chairman (and CTO), Konfoong Materials International Co. (SZSE: 300666), Yuyao/Ningbo, Zhejiang
profile: Materials scientist with doctorates from Harbin Institute of Technology and Hiroshima University who returned from abroad and in 2005 co-founded Konfoong Materials with six partners in Yuyao, Zhejiang. Konfoong makes ultra-high-purity metal sputtering targets used by 100+ chip fabs worldwide, a key domestic supplier in China's semiconductor supply chain; he aims for a 30% global share.
interesting_fact: Konfoong's sputtering targets are used by more than 100 chip factories worldwide, and Yao has said his goal is a 30% global market share in target materials.
deep_cut_fact: He launched Konfoong in April 2005 alongside returned Chinese scientists plus Japanese and American experts, shipping in 20 containers of imported equipment to Yuyao; he credits reform and opening-up with 'four opportunities' including his Japanese doctoral scholarship.
notes: Thousand Talents Program recipient; won Zhejiang provincial science & technology award (2018). No published IR email found; Konfoong's board secretary (Zou Junwei, appointed 2025) and securities dept. handle investor queries via SZSE Interactive (irm.cninfo.com.cn). Company site was not reachable from here; URL taken from public listings.

name: Farris Wilks
current_role: Co-owner, Wilks Brothers LLC (family investment office, Cisco, Texas); 10%+ shareholder in ProFrac Holding Corp. (ACDC)
profile: Texas stonemason-turned-fracking billionaire: with brother Dan he founded Wilks Masonry (1995) and Frac Tech (2002), selling to a Temasek-led group in 2011 for $3.5bn pretax. Via Wilks Brothers they invest in oilfield services (ProFrac, U.S. Well Services, Dawson Geophysical) and own ~672,000 acres in six states.
interesting_fact: Farris is pastor of his own church, the Assembly of Yahweh Seventh Day Church near Cisco, Texas - the congregation his father Voy led from 1952.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil, the brothers were bricklayers like their father and ran Wilks Masonry; they launched Frac Tech in 2002 out of tiny Cisco, Texas (Eastland County), where both still live, and grew it into one of the largest US fracking firms in under a decade.
notes: Very private; Wilks Brothers site publishes no contact. ProFrac (chaired by Dan's son Matt Wilks) is an indirect route only - Farris is a shareholder, not an executive. Politically prominent (major conservative donor), so expect media caution.

name: Tseng Shin-yi
profile: Most likely Cheng Hsin-yi (鄭信義, b. 1928), one of three cofounders in 1949 of Taiwan's Chang Chun Group, the island's No. 2 petrochemical group after Formosa Plastics. Chinese Wikipedia records his death on 28 January 2016.
notes: Caproasia's 2017 Forbes-based list has 'Tseng Shin-yi', 90, Chang Chun Group; this matches cofounder 鄭信義, who died 28 Jan 2016 per https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%84%AD%E4%BF%A1%E7%BE%A9 and https://www.cmoney.tw/notes/note-detail.aspx?nid=49860. Romanization match not 100% confirmed; treat as deceased.

name: Vladimir Gridin
current_role: Retired co-founder of Siberian Business Union (SDS) holding, Kemerovo; exited the business from 2016 to 2019
profile: Vladimir Gridin co-founded Siberian Business Union (SDS) with Mikhail Fedyaev in the mid-1990s and built it into a large Kuzbass coal, chemicals and engineering holding (registered 2004). He was a State Duma deputy for Kemerovo region from 2011. He later stepped back, reportedly moved to Monaco, and from about 2016 to 2019 sold his stakes to Fedyaev and Roman Trotsenko.
interesting_fact: SDS grew into Russia's third-largest producer of thermal (power-station) coal, with interests in mining, rail transport, chemicals, machine building and radio stations.
deep_cut_fact: The partners' first major asset in the mid-1990s was the Chernigovets open-pit coal mine in Kuzbass. When SDS was formally registered in Kemerovo in 2004, it already brought together more than 20 businesses in coal, machinery, building materials and utilities.
notes: Out of public life since around 2015; last on the Forbes list in 2013. He has largely exited SDS and reportedly lives in Monaco (dataset says UK). No current public contact found; alive status is unconfirmed, with no death reports found. Russian coal ties carry sanctions sensitivity, so check before outreach.

name: Sanjeev Soosaipillai
current_role: Founder, chairman & CEO of Prax Group (UK oil refining/fuel group); key UK units in administration since June 2025
profile: Sanjeev Kumar (Winston) Soosaipillai cofounded Prax with his wife Arani in 1999, growing from petrol retailing into wholesale fuel (2002), then buying the Lindsey Oil Refinery on the Humber and a stake in South Africa's Natref refinery. Parent State Oil and the Lindsey refinery entered administration/liquidation in June 2025; retail, upstream and international arms continue to trade.
interesting_fact: Prax grew from a two-person operation in 1999 into the owner of one of the UK's six major refineries (Lindsey), a rare case of a privately held, founder-owned UK refiner.
notes: Sensitive: Prax's UK refining collapse (June 2025) is under Insolvency Service investigation, with a reported asset freeze. The only press contact is the administrators' (Teneo) media desk, not him personally. Most bio coverage is sponsored content. Probably not a suitable guest now.

name: Arani Soosaipillai
current_role: Co-owner (with husband Sanjeev Kumar/Winston Soosaipillai) of Prax Group, UK oil refining and trading group now in insolvency
profile: Arani Soosaipillai and her husband built London-based Prax Group (founded 1999), an oil trading, distribution and refining group that bought the Lindsey oil refinery. Reports name her as joint ultimate controlling party alongside her husband, who was sole director. Prax's main companies entered administration/liquidation in mid-2025 and Lindsey refinery ceased operations.
interesting_fact: Prax grew from a 1999 London fuel-trading start-up into an integrated group owning the Lindsey refinery in Lincolnshire, one of only a handful of UK refineries.
notes: Not a good outreach target: Prax collapsed in June 2025 (administration/liquidation, refinery closure, UK government demands for investigation, High Court asset freeze on her husband). Hurun $1.9bn figure is pre-collapse and stale. No public role or contact for her found.

name: Wang Junshi
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder, Ginlong Technologies (Solis inverters); stepped down as director/deputy GM in 2021
profile: Wang Junshi (age ~77, Ningbo) co-founded Ginlong Technologies in 2005 with his wife Lin Yibei and son Wang Yiming; the company, sold under the Solis brand, became one of the world's largest string solar-inverter makers and listed in Shenzhen (300763) in 2019. He left the board in 2021; his son now chairs the firm, which has expanded into energy storage.
interesting_fact: Ginlong/Solis says it was only the second inverter company worldwide to obtain the UK's G83 grid-connection certification, in 2006, a year after its founding, an early bet on export markets.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding a multibillion-dollar solar-inverter business, Wang Junshi worked as a high school teacher.
notes: Very low public profile; elderly and retired from management. Best route is via Ginlong/Solis corporate (son Wang Yiming is chairman and the public face). No published press/IR email found on Solis site (only sales/service addresses).

name: Tan Dong
current_role: Director (non-independent), Guangdong Kingshine Electronic Technology Co. (科翔股份, SZSE: 300903); GM of subsidiary Huayu Huayuan
profile: Tan Dong (b. 1969, postgraduate degree) co-founded Huizhou-based PCB maker Kingshine (Dayawan Kexiang) in 2001 with Zheng Xiaorong, now chairwoman; the pair are its controlling shareholders and share the Hurun fortune. Kingshine listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in Nov 2020 and makes HDI, multilayer, flex and ceramic-substrate boards for autos, servers, optical modules and mmWave radar.
interesting_fact: Before Kingshine, Tan Dong was general manager (1996-2001) of Shenzhen Shunjiaxing Electronics, where Zheng Xiaorong was executive director; they then moved together to found Dayawan Kexiang in July 2001, the origin of today's listed group.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1993 as an engineer in the technical department of Guangdong Macro (Wanjiale) Communication Equipment Co., before moving into PCB manufacturing.
notes: Hurun English name 'Kingshine' = 科翔股份 (not Kinwong/景旺). Low public profile; no interviews found. Company securities dept (board secretary Zheng Haitao) is the formal route; IR email published in company filings (shown via Eastmoney F10).

name: Zheng Xiaorong
current_role: Chairwoman, Guangdong Kingshine Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (科翔股份, SZ:300903), a Huizhou PCB maker
profile: Zheng Xiaorong (b. 1972) and her husband Tan Dong are the controlling shareholders of Kingshine Electronic (科翔股份). The company makes high-density PCBs, including HDI boards for AI servers and 800G optical modules, at plants in Huizhou and Jiangxi. She has run the business since 2001 and was general manager until October 2025. She holds about 15% directly.
interesting_fact: In 2009 she bought a near-bankrupt factory, turned it profitable within three months, and passed RMB 100M in output the next year. Around 2012 she set up an HDI division while most peers held back, and that bet now underpins Kingshine's AI-server boards.
deep_cut_fact: She began her career in 1992 as marketing department manager at Shenzhen Kerong Electronics' subsidiary factory. In 1997 she became executive director of Shenzhen Shunjiaxing Electronics, before founding Daya Bay Kexiang (Kingshine's predecessor) in 2001.
