deep_cut_fact: He was one of the primary sponsors and the first executive director-general of the China Red Ribbon Foundation, a special fund for HIV/AIDS prevention and treatment in China.
notes: NOT a viable outreach target: reportedly in police custody since Dec 2022 (Caixin/SCMP Jan 2023); no trial outcome found. Hanergy is defunct as a public company; HK SFC 8-year director ban. Avoid.

name: Malone Mitchell
current_role: Chairman & CEO, TransAtlantic Petroleum LLC (Turkey/Bulgaria E&P, now private); owner of Mitchell Group / Longfellow Energy
profile: West Texas oilman N. Malone Mitchell 3rd built Riata Energy (1985-2006) into one of the largest private US energy companies, then sold control to Tom Ward for about $500M; it became SandRidge Energy. He then founded Mitchell Group (Riata Management, Longfellow Energy) and has led TransAtlantic Petroleum, which produces oil and gas in Turkey.
interesting_fact: He is one of America's biggest landowners: the Land Report ranked him No. 22 with 384,000 acres, including the 350,000-acre Longfellow Ranch near his hometown of Sanderson, Texas, known for elk and mule deer hunts.
deep_cut_fact: Before Riata he worked in oilfield services and in his family's ranching and aviation businesses; he graduated from Oklahoma State University in 1983 and, while running TransAtlantic, spent much of his time on the ground in Turkey, Bulgaria and Romania.
notes: Formally N. Malone Mitchell 3rd (some filings: Noah Malone Mitchell). TransAtlantic is now an LLC (taken private), so there is no IR team; a 2013 Wall Street Transcript CEO interview exists. Last on Forbes in 2010-2011.

name: Mohammed Al Barwani
current_role: Founder and Chairman, MB Holding Company LLC (Muscat, Oman)
profile: Omani petroleum engineer (b. 1951) who founded MB Holding in 1982 as an oilfield-services firm, then expanded into oil & gas E&P (Petrogas), engineering and mining (Mawarid). He owned superyacht builder Oceanco 2010-2025 and was named Oman Air chairman in 2020.
interesting_fact: He bought superyacht builder Oceanco in 2010 after first visiting it in 2009, and sold it in 2025 to Valve founder Gabe Newell; MB's Mawarid Mining was the first private company to explore for copper and gold in Oman.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding MB he spent a decade (1976-86) as a reservoir engineer at Petroleum Development Oman (the Shell/government JV); he studied at Miami University (Ohio), UT Austin (chemical engineering) and Heriot-Watt, which gave him an honorary doctorate in petroleum engineering in 2010.
notes: mboman@ is MB Holding's general corporate inbox, not personal. Sons run MB's mining and E&P arms (Usama Al Barwani listed as CEO). Current Oman Air chair status not re-verified.

name: Kang Qiao
profile: Listed by Hurun (2014-2018) as the businessman behind Searainbow (medical e-commerce, digital entertainment, high-tech chemical fibre). Searainbow Holding (Shenzhen 000503, now Guoxin Health) is still ~24% held by Zhonghai Heng Industrial per 2026 data, but no public profile confirming his current role was found.
notes: Extremely low public profile; dropped off rich lists after 2018. Link to Searainbow/000503 is from Hurun data and not independently confirmed via a source naming him. Not recommended without further verification.

name: Armon Dadgar
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, HashiCorp (an IBM company, within IBM Software)
profile: Co-founded HashiCorp in 2012 with University of Washington classmate Mitchell Hashimoto, building infrastructure-automation tools Terraform, Vault, Consul and Nomad. HashiCorp IPO'd in 2021 and was acquired by IBM for $6.4B in Feb 2025; Dadgar stayed on as CTO, working on Terraform/Ansible integration within IBM Software.
interesting_fact: He co-founded HashiCorp at about 24; the company name is a portmanteau of co-founder Hashimoto's surname and 'Corp', and it sold to IBM for $6.4B in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: As a student he interned at Amazon Web Services when it had only ~250 people and 'the whole thing fit on one floor' (Andy Jassy welcomed the interns). He first learned to program from a Visual Basic box set with five install CDs and a 600-page book.
notes: Press email is from 2024 HashiCorp releases (pre-IBM); post-acquisition press may route through IBM communications. Before HashiCorp he was an academic researcher at the University of Washington. Frequent podcast guest (Logan Bartlett Show ep. 102, Open Source Underdogs ep. 58).

name: Daniel Jaeggi
current_role: Co-founder & President, Mercuria Energy Group (Geneva)
profile: Swiss commodities trader (also spelled Jäggi) who co-founded Geneva-based Mercuria with Marco Dunand in 2004; it has grown into one of the world's five largest independent energy traders, spanning crude, products, gas, LNG, power and increasingly energy-transition assets. He and Dunand control the majority of the privately held firm.
interesting_fact: Mercuria's 2014 purchase of JPMorgan's physical commodities business vaulted the then 10-year-old firm into the elite club of global commodity trading houses alongside Vitol, Glencore and Trafigura.
deep_cut_fact: Jaeggi and Dunand began their careers together at Cargill International, then moved through trading roles at Goldman Sachs's J. Aron unit, Salomon Brothers (Phibro) and Sempra Energy before launching Mercuria together in 2004 - a partnership spanning roughly four decades.
notes: Very low public profile; rarely gives interviews (Dunand is the usual public face). Mercuria's contact page lists a Geneva switchboard; 2025 releases name Matt J. Lauer as press contact (no email published). Best route is Mercuria corporate communications via the contact form.

name: Marco Dunand
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Mercuria Energy Group (Geneva)
profile: Swiss commodities trader and University of Geneva economics graduate who co-founded Mercuria in Geneva in 2004 with Daniel Jaeggi after stints at Cargill, Goldman Sachs' J. Aron and Phibro/Salomon. Mercuria grew into one of the world's largest independent energy traders and is pushing into critical minerals and energy-transition assets; Dunand speaks frequently at FT, Reuters and WEF events.
interesting_fact: Bloomberg in 2014 dubbed Mercuria 'the $100 billion commodity empire that few know'; it went from startup to one of the top five independent oil traders within a decade.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Daniel Jaeggi started their careers together at Cargill in Geneva, then both moved into oil trading at Goldman Sachs' J. Aron unit, decades before founding Mercuria together.
notes: Accessible on the conference circuit (FT Commodities Summit, Reuters Events, WEF, World Government Summit) — a good podcast candidate on energy trading and transition. Mercuria site was not reachable from this session to confirm a press email; use contact form or Geneva HQ switchboard.

name: Eugene Shvidler
current_role: Private investor and owner of Château Thénac winery (France); formerly chairman of Millhouse LLC (stepped down March 2022)
profile: Born in Ufa (1964), Gubkin-trained mathematician and Fordham MBA who worked at Deloitte in New York before partnering with Roman Abramovich. He was president of Sibneft from 1998 until its $13bn sale to Gazprom in 2005, later held about 5% of steelmaker Evraz and chaired Abramovich's Millhouse. He holds British and US citizenship.
interesting_fact: As Sibneft president (1998-2005) he ran what was, for most of his tenure, Russia's fastest-growing oil company by production and its most profitable per barrel, before Gazprom bought it for $13bn.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serious winemaker: in 2000 he bought Château Thénac near Bergerac, built on the ruins of a monastery founded in 1109, and told The Guardian he wanted 'first-class wine that will rival anything neighbouring Bordeaux has to offer'.
notes: High-risk outreach: under UK sanctions since March 2022 (High Court 2023 and Court of Appeal 2024 rejected his challenges). Does not like being called an oligarch. Very private; no personal press office found. The winery is the only published channel. Listing says energy/Evraz but he is no longer active in Russian energy.

name: Ge Zhiyong
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Wuxi Autowell Technology (ATW; Shanghai STAR Market 688516)
profile: Ge Zhiyong (葛志勇) is the controlling shareholder (with concert party Li Wen), chairman and GM of Wuxi Autowell, founded 2010. It makes automation equipment for solar module and cell production (notably cell stringers), plus lithium-battery and semiconductor equipment. Hurun listed him as a billionaire 2021-23 at the peak of the solar boom.
interesting_fact: Autowell only entered the PV business in 2012, yet its flagship multi-busbar (MBB) cell soldering stringer now claims over 70% market share, with customers including Jinko, JA Solar, Trina, Longi, Tongwei and India's Tata and Adani (company claim).
notes: Low media profile; no sourced personal biography found online. Not on Hurun since 2023 (solar equipment downturn). Best route: company IR mailbox (listed in the 2024 annual report summary; board secretary Zhou Yongxiu).

name: Rusteem Sulteev
current_role: Former co-owner and first deputy general director of TAIF Group (Kazan); TAIF was merged into SIBUR in 2021 (now Sibur-RT) - current formal role unclear
profile: Kazan-born (1954) civil engineer who joined TAIF as first deputy general director in 1995 and became a co-owner, alongside Albert Shigabutdinov and Radik Shaimiev, of the Tatarstan oil, gas and petrochemicals group (Kazanorgsintez, Nizhnekamskneftekhim, TGK-16). Through TAIF's 2021 combination with SIBUR he became a SIBUR shareholder; he also co-owns Kazan's Avers Bank.
interesting_fact: TAIF, which he co-owned, was one of Russia's largest private petrochemical groups before its 2021 merger with SIBUR; its shareholders received a stake in SIBUR Holding in the deal.
deep_cut_fact: He started out as a construction foreman after graduating from the Kazan Institute of Civil Engineering in 1976; one of his first major projects was building a factory for the bread and baking industry, and in 1984 he was deputy director for construction of Kazan's second bakery plant.
notes: Name usually spelled Rustem Sulteev. Very private; no public contact channels found. Listed in sanctions databases (OpenSanctions: https://opensanctions.org/entities/Q55759794) - check legal/sanctions implications before any outreach. Alive status not confirmed by recent news (no death reports found).

name: Tang Jinkui
current_role: Vice Chairman, Shenghong Group (盛虹集团), Suzhou; shareholder in Jiangsu Eastern Shenghong (SZSE: 000301)
profile: Suzhou-based self-made businessman (age ~71) and long-time No. 2 to chairman Miao Hangen at Shenghong Group, which grew from a Shengze silk-weaving/dyeing mill into a polyester-fibre and petrochemicals conglomerate. Its fibre arm backdoor-listed in Shanghai/Shenzhen in 2018 as Jiangsu Eastern Shenghong.
interesting_fact: Eastern Shenghong now runs a 16 Mt/yr integrated refining-petrochemical complex plus methanol-to-olefins and propane dehydrogenation units, and markets itself as moving into 'new energy new materials' such as EVA for solar panels.
notes: Very low public profile; Forbes lists him as 'Tang Jinkui & family', vice chairman of Shenghong Group (Forbes profile). Miao Hangen is the group's public face. Only realistic route is Eastern Shenghong's securities-affairs mailbox. No verifiable personal anecdotes found.

name: Roland Duchatelet
current_role: Non-executive director, X-FAB Silicon Foundries SE; co-controlling shareholder (via Elex) of Melexis and X-FAB
profile: Belgian engineer-entrepreneur (b. 1946, Merksem) who in 1989 formed holding Elex with Rudi De Winter and Francoise Chombar, taking over automotive-sensor maker Melexis (1994) and specialty foundry X-FAB (1999); the families still jointly control both listed firms. He founded the Vivant party, was a senator 2007-10, and has owned several football clubs.
interesting_fact: He has owned a string of football clubs - Sint-Truiden, Standard Liege, Charlton Athletic, AD Alcorcon and Ujpest - and remains main shareholder of Germany's FC Carl Zeiss Jena.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Elex he was a marketing manager at German chipmaker Elmos Semiconductor (1985-89); his 1993 book 'NV Belgie, verslag aan de aandeelhouders' (Belgium Inc., a report to the shareholders) spent ten weeks in Belgium's non-fiction top ten and argued for a basic income.
notes: X-FAB's published IR & PR contact (Uta Steinbrecher) is the cleanest corporate route; Melexis also has an IR page (melexis.com/en/investors). Avoid leading with his football-ownership era, which was contentious with fans (Charlton, Standard).

name: Liu Jianfang
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Jiangsu Gao Kai Precision Fluid Technology (Shanghai STAR: 688835)
profile: Former Jilin University mechanical engineering professor who founded Gao Kai in Wujin, Changzhou in 2013 to commercialise piezoelectric drive and precision fluid-control technology (flow controllers, jet dispensing, coating) used in chip and electronics manufacturing; customers include BYD, CATL and Foxconn. Gao Kai listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in Aug 2026, jumping ~240% on debut.
interesting_fact: He left a tenured professorship at 38, taking several graduate students with him, and started the company with just 2 million yuan of registered capital to attack a market then almost monopolised by foreign piezo-jet dispensing brands.
deep_cut_fact: During his PhD (Jilin, 2002-05) he spent a year at Yamagata University in Japan studying piezoelectric drive and vibration control under Katsumi Watanabe and Katsuyoshi Suzuki; his research line traces to his mentor Prof. Yang Zhigang, who pioneered Jilin's piezo-drive work in 1992.
notes: Newly minted billionaire (Aug 2026 IPO). No personal/press contact found in this pass; company IR/board-secretary contacts should be in the STAR Market prospectus or SSE filings for 688835. Some English sources call the company 'Gaoke'/'Gaokai'.

name: Aluru Jagadish Prasad
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, HBL Engineering Ltd (formerly HBL Power Systems), Hyderabad
profile: Dr. Aluru Jagadish Prasad founded what is now HBL Engineering in 1977 in Hyderabad, starting with aircraft batteries for the Indian Air Force. The company now makes specialised batteries (for aircraft, data centres, submarines, missiles and tanks), defence electronics, e-mobility drivetrains and the Kavach train collision-avoidance system for Indian Railways; he remains CMD.
interesting_fact: HBL's batteries go into aircraft, data centres, submarines, missiles and battle tanks, and the company also builds train collision-avoidance systems for Indian Railways - a mix of defence, rail and backup-power tech that started with one IAF aircraft battery in 1977.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting HBL he worked at the Administrative Staff College of India in Hyderabad; he holds a B.Tech from IIT Kharagpur, an MS in Management from MIT and a doctorate in international business from Columbia University (per HBL's 2023-24 annual report).
notes: Aged about 78 in 2024. HBL's battery energy storage (BESS) and data-centre battery lines fit the podcast's energy/data-centre angle. Best route is the company's general address contact@hbl.in or investor@hbl.in (company secretary).

name: Wu Ming
current_role: Co-founder and part of the controlling shareholder group of Fourth Paradigm (4Paradigm, HKEX-listed AI company); not listed in current executive team
profile: Wu Ming (吴茗, Phairy Wu) co-founded enterprise-AI company Fourth Paradigm in 2014 with her husband Dai Wenyuan (ex-Baidu, Huawei Noah's Ark) and AI scholar Yang Qiang. It listed in Hong Kong in 2023. Before the IPO, Dai, Wu and affiliated vehicles controlled about 41% of the company.
interesting_fact: Fourth Paradigm was the first AI startup to win investment from all five of China's big state banks (ICBC, ABC, BOC, CCB and BoCom), and raised a $700M Series D in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Fourth Paradigm she studied at Huazhong University of Science and Technology in Wuhan and worked at Baidu, the same company where Dai Wenyuan ran the Fengchao ad-ranking system.
notes: Low public profile; 36Kr marks her as a former co-founder who has left operating roles. Her husband Dai Wenyuan (chairman/CEO) is the public face. Approach via Fourth Paradigm PR/IR. One source describes her as also an investment partner at Sequoia China, but the wording is ambiguous and unverified.

name: Cheng Wei
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, DiDi Global (Beijing Xiaoju Technology)
profile: Cheng Wei (程维, b. 1983, Shangrao, Jiangxi) spent about eight years at Alibaba, rising to a deputy GM role in Alipay's B2C unit, before founding ride-hailing app Didi Dache in 2012 at age 29. Didi merged with Kuaidi, drove Uber out of China in 2016 and expanded into robotaxis, EV and mobility services; it delisted from NYSE in 2022 and trades OTC.
interesting_fact: Didi famously 'tamed Uber': in 2016 Uber sold its China business to Didi in exchange for a stake in the combined company, after a costly subsidy war.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alibaba he drifted through odd jobs, including as an assistant to the head of a foot-massage chain; he was ill on the day of China's gaokao but still won a place at Beijing University of Chemical Technology, studying administration.
notes: Input's SEC link (TSMC Chairman & CEO) is a mismatch: that is C.C. Wei (Wei Che-chia) of TSMC, a different person. Cheng Wei keeps a low media profile post-2021 regulatory crackdown; route via DiDi corporate/IR.

name: Hu Wei
current_role: Director and Vice General Manager, StarPower Semiconductor (Jiaxing; SSE: 603290)
profile: Hu Wei (female) co-founded StarPower Semiconductor in Jiaxing, Zhejiang, in 2005 with husband and chairman Shen Hua after both returned from the US. StarPower makes IGBT and SiC power-semiconductor chips and modules for EVs, solar/storage and industrial drives; listed in Shanghai in 2020. The couple jointly control ~41.7%.
interesting_fact: StarPower was ranked fifth in the global IGBT module market by Omdia (2023), a field that was dominated by foreign firms when the couple started the company in 2005.
deep_cut_fact: She earned a master's in Engineering-Economic Systems from Stanford in 1994, then spent 1995-2001 at US credit-card issuer Providian Financial as marketing director, assistant to an executive SVP and corporate strategy manager before co-founding StarPower.
notes: Wealth is shared with husband Shen Hua (chairman/GM, the public face). Both reportedly hold US nationality. Route via StarPower board secretary/IR (Jiaxing HQ). Highly relevant to EV/solar/data-center power electronics.

name: Zhong Fenghao
current_role: Director and early co-founding shareholder, Hangzhou Changchuan Technology Co., Ltd. (300604.SZ)
profile: Zhong Fenghao (钟锋浩) is a director and long-time major shareholder (~5%) of Hangzhou Changchuan Technology, founded in 2008 by Zhao Yi, which makes semiconductor test equipment (testers and handlers) used by Chinese packaging/test houses such as JCET and Tongfu. The company's market value surged in 2025-26 on chip/AI demand and it is pursuing a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: Changchuan's equipment sits at the last step of chip mass production: every chip is tested and sorted before shipping, and Changchuan builds the machines for both steps; four of its original six non-independent directors came from Silan Microelectronics.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Changchuan, he was manager of the test-equipment development department at Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics, the chipmaker where founder Zhao Yi was production director; Silan later became a Changchuan customer.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal channels found. Not the chairman (founder Zhao Yi controls the company). Best route is company IR/board secretary. Sold ~0.97m shares in Jan 2026, dropping below 5%; not relevant to outreach.

name: brother
profile: Not a named person. This is a parsing artifact of the Forbes entry 'Mikhail Gutseriev & brother' (Forbes 2021). The profile URL now redirects to Mikhail Gutseriev (age 68, Moscow), founder and main shareholder of Safmar Group (oil, coal, real estate, retail), #487 on Forbes' 2026 list.
interesting_fact: Per Forbes, Mikhail Gutseriev owns Moscow's Hotel National, where Donald Trump stayed on his first visit to Russia in 1987, and he writes lyrics for songs performed by famous Russian singers.
notes: Not a separate person: the unnamed 'brother' is most likely Sait-Salam Gutseriev, Mikhail's brother and long-time partner, but Forbes doesn't name him here. Mikhail Gutseriev is sanctioned by the UK, EU and others (2021, Lukashenko ties), so this is a poor fit for outreach. Duplicate of the Gutseriev family entry.

name: Liu Zhenfeng
current_role: Co-founder and Director, Yantai Jereh Oilfield Services Group Co., Ltd. (002353.SZ)
profile: Liu Zhenfeng (刘贞峰, b. 1961) co-founded Jereh in 1999 with Sun Weijie and Wang Kunxiao, and has served as its vice president, director and 'meritorious adviser'. Jereh grew from a parts trader into a major maker of fracturing and oilfield equipment, listed in Shenzhen in 2010, and is now selling gas-fired power generation to data centers. He was re-elected to Jereh's board in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: Jereh, best known for oilfield fracturing equipment, won a US$100 million order for generator sets from a North American data center in November 2025, a sign of oilfield-equipment makers moving into AI power.
deep_cut_fact: Liu trained in computer science at the University of Science and Technology Beijing. Jereh started in 1999 as Yantai Jereh Equipment, a small trader in imported mining spare parts, long before it built its own oilfield machinery.
notes: Low public profile. The computer-science detail comes from his exchange-filed resume (Eastmoney F10: emweb.securities.eastmoney.com ... code=SZ002353). zqb@jereh.com is Jereh's registered securities-affairs office email. Chairman is Li Zhiyong and president is Sun Weijie.

name: Jack Cogen
current_role: Private investor; early backer and director of CoreWeave from Sept 2017 until he chose not to stand for re-election at the June 8, 2026 annual meeting
profile: Jack D. Cogen founded and ran Natsource Asset Management (1994-2014), one of the largest private greenhouse-gas/environmental-markets asset managers. Two later CoreWeave cofounders (incl. CEO Michael Intrator) worked at Natsource and at gas hedge fund Hudson Ridge, where he was a director; he became an early CoreWeave investor and board member, owning ~5% at its 2025 IPO.
interesting_fact: CoreWeave started in 2017 as a crypto-mining operation run by former natural-gas/carbon traders before pivoting to GPU cloud for AI customers such as Microsoft and OpenAI; Cogen backed and served on its board for more than eight years.
deep_cut_fact: He chaired the International Emissions Trading Association (IETA) from 2008 to 2011 and remains an IETA Fellow; academically he holds an M.S. in Mathematics as well as an MBA from NYU, plus a B.A. from Rutgers.
notes: Left CoreWeave's board in June 2026, so CoreWeave channels are now indirect; no personal/family-office contact published. Great podcast angle: carbon markets -> natural gas -> AI data centers. Low public profile.

name: Wang Lekang
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Shenzhen Sunmoon Microelectronics (明微电子, SSE STAR: 688699); re-elected Oct 2025
profile: Born 1966, Wang Lekang is a senior electronics engineer who founded Shenzhen Sunmoon Microelectronics in October 2003, a fabless designer of LED display/lighting driver ICs now listed on Shanghai's STAR Market. He controls about 38% of the company directly and via holding company Shenzhen Mingwei Technology, and was re-elected chairman and GM in October 2025.
interesting_fact: He remains both founder-chairman and general manager more than two decades after starting Sunmoon, holding ~9.8% directly and ~27.9% indirectly as actual controller.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Sunmoon he worked as an engineer at SAST Shenfei Laser Optical Systems (先科深飞激光光学系统), then at Guowei Technology (国微科技) as office director, sales director and assistant to the GM.
notes: Low public profile; best route is the board secretary/IR office (Ir@chinaasic.com). Company website domain chinaasic.com.

name: Liu Chengyu
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Kstar Science & Technology (科士达, SZSE: 002518)
profile: Liu Chengyu joined Kstar's predecessor in 1993 and rose to run and control it. Kstar, listed in Shenzhen since 2010, makes UPS systems, data-center power and cooling infrastructure, solar inverters and energy-storage systems. He remains chairman and GM, and was renominated to the board in late 2025.
interesting_fact: Kstar sits right at the podcast's intersection: it supplies uninterruptible power, precision cooling and modular data-center infrastructure, and also builds PV inverters and battery storage.
deep_cut_fact: After university he taught at Xiapu No. 6 Middle School in Fujian. Kstar began as Fujian Xiapu Kstar Electronics in that coastal county before moving to Shenzhen. He later earned an EMBA at Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.

public_contacts.value: stock@kstar.com.cn (company IR mailbox; board secretary Fan Tao fantao1@kstar.com.cn, tel 0755-86168479)

notes: Fellow director Liu Ling (also a former Xiapu schoolteacher) is co-controller. Low media profile; IR mailbox/board secretary is the formal route. Data-center power angle makes him a strong fit.

name: Andrei Kuzyaev
current_role: President and CEO, ER-Telecom Holding (Dom.ru); main owner and chairman of Luch Capital (formerly Perm Financial and Industrial Group)
profile: Perm-born economist turned oil and telecom magnate. In the 1990s his Perm Financial and Industrial Group bought into Permneft, and he ran Lukoil-Perm before selling the stake to Lukoil in 2003. He then led Lukoil Overseas, Lukoil's international upstream arm, and was a Lukoil vice-president. Since 2015 he has run ER-Telecom, Russia's third-largest broadband provider (Dom.ru).
interesting_fact: He was a Lukoil veteran who ran its international upstream division, Lukoil Overseas, from December 2000 and was a Lukoil vice-president. In 2015 he switched to running ER-Telecom full time.
deep_cut_fact: As a Perm State University economics student he set up his own student work brigade, 'Sever', which collected logs washed onto the banks of the Vishera river and shipped them to a pulp mill. He also created Perm's first student research squad doing contract research, and graduated in 1987 with honours.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK since Feb 2025 under the Russia regime, and earlier by Ukraine; outreach may raise compliance issues. ER-Telecom's press pages render in JavaScript and list no email. A 2020 release named a Dom.ru press secretary, but that contact is outdated and personal, so it is not listed. He also founded Perm's Stroganov Club and chaired the Russia-Venezuela business council.

name: Wang Yuxian
profile: Hurun China 2026 lists Wang Yuxian (王育贤) with wealth of about $1.3B from 'Semight'. That most likely means Semight Instruments (联讯仪器, SSE STAR 688808), a Suzhou optical-communication and semiconductor test-equipment maker that listed in April 2026. But its disclosed controllers are Hu Haiyang, Huang Jianjun and Yang Jian, and I found no public source linking a Wang Yuxian to it.
notes: Identity unresolved. Searches in Chinese and English (王育贤 + 联讯仪器/Semight/胡润) found nothing, and Semight's broker reports name only Hu, Huang and Yang as controllers. Check the Hurun listing itself before any outreach; the name may be a romanization or matching error.

name: Houshan Bai
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Ningbo Ronbay New Energy Technology (688005.SH); Chairman, Beijing Ronbay Investment Holding
profile: Bai Houshan (白厚善) is a metallurgical engineer who founded two Chinese lithium-battery cathode makers. He built Beijing Easpring into a ChiNext-listed company (IPO 2010) and left in 2013. That year he started Ronbay, which became China's leading high-nickel cathode supplier and listed on the STAR Market in 2019.
interesting_fact: After leaving Easpring in 2013, he built Ronbay into a company that overtook his former employer within a few years. By 2021 Ronbay held close to half of China's high-nickel cathode shipments, and its market value approached RMB 60B.
deep_cut_fact: His career as a founder began in 1992, leading a research group at Beijing's BGRIMM. The group first made electronic-ceramic additives and only moved into lithium cobalt oxide in 2001, becoming Easpring. Before that he was a technician at the Shenyang Research Institute of Mining & Metallurgy.
notes: The website is the company's, not his personal site, and I found no published email. In April 2026 the Ningbo office of the CSRC warned and fined him RMB 3M over misleading contract disclosures by Ronbay (csrc.gov.cn). Be aware of this before outreach. The formal route is the Ronbay board secretary office.

name: Yu Bangping
current_role: Chairman, executive director and controlling shareholder, Perennial Energy Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 2798), Guizhou coal miner
profile: Guizhou coal entrepreneur with 30+ years in mining who built the Hongguo, Baogushan and Xiejiahegou underground coal mines in Panzhou, Guizhou, grouped under Perennial Energy (久泰邦达), listed in Hong Kong in 2019. He was CEO 2018-2023 and remains chairman; Forbes listed him as a billionaire in 2021 on the coal-price boom.
interesting_fact: In Feb 2024 the group's Baogushan mine won Guizhou safety permits to double annual capacity from 600,000 to 1.2 million tonnes, with a similar expansion planned for the Hongguo mine.
deep_cut_fact: He founded the Hongguo coal mine back in November 1990, then the Baogushan mine in April 2004 - long before the 2019 Hong Kong IPO of the group.
notes: Very low profile; no media/social presence found. Company website listed in filings did not return content; best route is via company secretary / HK office listed in HKEX filings. Deep-cut source is a data aggregator quoting the company bio (not independently verified in a filing).

name: Lim Oon Kuin
current_role: Former founder of Hin Leong Trading (collapsed 2020); serving a prison sentence in Singapore
profile: Lim Oon Kuin ('OK Lim') founded Hin Leong Trading in 1963 and built it into one of Singapore's largest independent oil traders, with the Ocean Tankers fleet. Hin Leong collapsed in 2020 with billions in debt. He was convicted of abetting cheating and forgery, and in March 2026 the High Court cut his sentence on appeal to 13.5 years.
interesting_fact: He started Hin Leong in 1963, at age 20, with a single truck delivering diesel to fishermen and small rural power producers. 'Hin Leong' means 'prosperity' in Chinese.
notes: Not suitable for outreach: he is in prison (see SCMP, March 2026: https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/southeast-asia/article/3345339/singapore-court-reduces-oil-tycoon-ok-lims-prison-sentence-13-1/2-years-appeal). The Forbes bio is outdated; Hin Leong no longer operates. No public contact routes.

name: Gao Don
current_role: Founder and President, Positec Group (Worx, Kress)
profile: Don Gao founded Positec in Suzhou in 1994 as an OEM power-tool maker for brands like Black & Decker, then built his own brands, launching Worx in 2004 and later Kress. Positec now sells cordless tools, battery outdoor equipment and robotic mowers in ~70 countries with 4,000+ staff; in April 2026 it took a strategic investment from Bain Capital.
interesting_fact: Positec once shipped 700,000 angle grinders in a single year to Black & Decker; when the tool giant decided to make them in-house, Gao resolved to 'control his own destiny' and build branded products.
deep_cut_fact: Gao hired Vicenza, Italy-based designer Paolo Andriolo to style Positec tools, and the company's Australian design office originated the JawSaw, a 'safe chainsaw' whose chain is exposed only when cutting.
notes: Forbes lists him as 'Gao Don'; he uses Don Gao. Low public profile. Bain Capital deal (Apr 2026) press release: https://positec-europe.com/es/news/positec-gibt-strategische-partnerschaft-mit-bain-capital-bekannt/ . Energy angle: battery platforms and electrification/robotics of outdoor equipment. No published press email found.

name: Manoj Bhargava
current_role: Founder/owner, Innovation Ventures / Living Essentials (5-hour Energy); founder, Stage 2 Innovations & Billions in Change
profile: Lucknow-born (1953) entrepreneur who spent over a decade at an Indian ashram, ran his family's plastics business, then launched 5-hour Energy in 2004 and made it the dominant US energy shot. Giving Pledge signatory; funds Stage 2 Innovations/Billions in Change (Free Electric bike, water purifiers) and India's Hans Foundation.
interesting_fact: Through Stage 2 Innovations he developed the HANS Free Electric bike, a pedal generator meant to supply off-grid households with electricity, alongside the 'Rain Maker' water purifier — pitched as inventions for 'the unlucky third of the world'.
deep_cut_fact: Long before 5-hour Energy, his first venture's early product was 'Chaser', an anti-hangover pill; he had earlier won a scholarship to The Hill School for maths and spent one year at Princeton (1972) before leaving for India.
notes: Reclusive ('mystery monk'). Journalist should be aware of reputational issues: WSJ (Oct 2024) and CNBC reported a US federal tax probe involving him and his philanthropy, plus past 5-hour Energy regulatory suits and the 2023 Arena Group/Sports Illustrated dispute. Energy angle = Free Electric/off-grid power inventions.

name: Alexander Vagin
current_role: Former co-owner and chairman of Raspadskaya (Kuzbass coking-coal miner); exited 2012-2013, current activity unknown
profile: Alexander Stepanovich Vagin (Kuzbass State Technical University, 1981) rose from the mine floor to co-control Raspadskaya, a top Russian coking-coal miner, with partner Gennady Kozovoi after its 1991 privatisation; partnered with Evraz from 2004 and IPO'd in 2006. Forbes put him at $1.3B in 2011. In 2012 the pair sold out to Evraz for $202M plus 11% of Evraz.
interesting_fact: Raspadskaya was one of the first Soviet 'people's enterprises', corporatised in December 1991 with miners as shareholders; Vagin, then the mine's production director, was elected chairman of the shareholders' council and with Kozovoi gradually bought out the miners' shares.
deep_cut_fact: Forbes estimated that Vagin and Kozovoi, who started at the mine in the 1970s as mechanics (slesari), took about $1.8B gross out of Raspadskaya over two decades through asset swaps, its 2006 IPO, dividends and the 2012 Evraz deal.
notes: Appears only on Forbes 2011 list; essentially no public profile since exiting Raspadskaya (MarketScreener lists his chairmanship ending 2013). No published contacts found; Russian national, so sanctions/compliance context may matter. Raspadskaya had a fatal 2010 mine disaster; avoid as an opener.

name: Li Xipeng
profile: Listed by Hurun (China list 2013-2019, Global list 2018-2020) with wealth from 'Shengrun', a private group in real estate, electric power and infrastructure. The group's exact Chinese name, location and his current role could not be verified from sources reachable in this pass.
notes: Not linked to any listed company found; Chinese encyclopedia sites (Baidu Baike, Baike.com) were blocked and the web search budget was exhausted, so identity is unconfirmed. Off Hurun lists since 2020. Needs a Chinese-language follow-up search before any outreach.

name: Shu Pujuan
current_role: Co-owner (49% shareholder) of Henan Shengrun Holding Group (河南盛润控股集团), Zhengzhou
profile: Shu Pujuan (舒蒲娟, b. ~1965) is the wife and business partner of Li Xipeng (李喜朋), founder of Zhengzhou-based Shengrun Holding (盛润控股), a group in real estate, power/energy and urban infrastructure (toll expressways). Hurun listed the couple jointly (2013-2020). She keeps no public profile of her own.
interesting_fact: A 2011 SEC filing by Nasdaq-listed China Infrastructure Investment Corp (CEO/chairman Li Xipeng, which ran the Pingdingshan-Linru expressway in Henan) states that Li owns 51% and his wife Shu Pujuan 49% of Henan Shengrun.
deep_cut_fact: Shengrun's ties to US markets: through China Infrastructure Investment Corp, the family's toll-road business (Pingdingshan Pinglin Expressway) was listed on Nasdaq, and in 2011 a Shengrun subsidiary, Zhengzhou Simian Real Estate, was folded into the listed company via VIE agreements.
notes: Hurun romanises husband's name as Li Xipeng (李喜朋, not 李西鹏). Hurun data: Shengrun Holding, Zhengzhou, Henan; Shu b. 1965. Company site www.srkg.com.cn did not respond. No personal public channels found; any outreach would go via Li Xipeng / Shengrun Holding. Baidu/Sogou blocked automated access, so Chinese news coverage was only partly checked.

name: Cai Di'e
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2022-2024) jointly with Wang Mingwang as a source of Sunwoda wealth; personal role at Sunwoda not confirmed
profile: Appears on the Hurun Global list 2022-2024 together with Wang Mingwang, co-founder (with Wang Wei) of Shenzhen-based Sunwoda Electronic (SZSE: 300207), a major lithium-ion battery maker for phones/laptops, EVs and energy storage. Her own role and relationship to the company could not be confirmed from public sources checked.
interesting_fact: Sunwoda, the source of this fortune, was the world's largest supplier of batteries for smartphones, laptops and tablets by 2024 shipments, with a 34.3% share of mobile-phone batteries.
notes: Identity uncertain: could not find a public bio or Chinese name for Cai Di'e (web-search budget exhausted mid-lane). Any approach would go through Sunwoda corporate/IR; Wang Mingwang or chairman Wang Wei are the public faces. Energy-storage/EV battery fit is good.

name: Vladimir Shmunis
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, RingCentral (NYSE: RNG)
profile: Ukraine-born engineer (SF State BS/MS in computer science) who founded RingCentral in 1999 and built it into a cloud business-communications company with over $2B in revenue. After a brief stint as executive chairman in 2023 he returned as CEO in December 2023 and has pushed AI-focused products; supports Stanford cancer research and Tel Aviv University's Shmunis School of Biomedicine.
interesting_fact: UC Today dubbed him 'the godfather of UCaaS'; RingCentral has been a Gartner Magic Quadrant leader for UCaaS for 12 straight years, and he received the Ellis Island Honors Society Award in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Before RingCentral he founded Ring Zero Systems, a pioneer of desktop business-communications software that shipped more than 25 million copies bundled by PC makers such as IBM, HP, Sony and Toshiba, and was later acquired by Motorola.
notes: Goes by 'Vlad'. Best route is RingCentral media relations (named PR contact on 2026 releases). Named inventor on several US patents.

name: Lin Jiangwei
current_role: Founder and largest individual shareholder (~13.4%), Suzhou Jolywood (Zhonglai) Photovoltaic New Materials (300393.SZ); no longer a director or executive
profile: Lin Jianwei (林建伟; listed as Lin Jiangwei) founded Jolywood (Zhonglai) in Suzhou, Jiangsu in 2008, building it into the world's top solar-backsheet maker and an early mass producer of n-type TOPCon cells. In Feb 2023 state-owned Zhejiang Energy's listed arm Zheneng Electric Power took control; he remains the largest individual holder alongside Zhang Yuzheng (~2.75%).
interesting_fact: Jolywood's FFC double-sided coated backsheet broke a foreign technology monopoly in China, and the company says it was No.1 globally in PV backsheet shipments four years running (2021-2024), with over 210 GW shipped cumulatively.
notes: Correct Chinese spelling is 林建伟 (Lin Jianwei). Not on Jolywood's current board (chairman Zhang Chengyu); company now controlled by Zhejiang SASAC via Zheneng. Very low public profile; no personal channels found. Alive status not independently confirmed (still listed as shareholder at 30 Sep 2026). Web search budget exhausted before deep-cut research.

name: Zhang Yuzheng
current_role: Co-founder of Suzhou Jolywood (Zhonglai) Photovoltaic (300393.SZ); no current board or management role found
profile: Zhang Yuzheng (张育政) co-founded the predecessor of Jolywood/Zhonglai, Suzhou Zhonglai Solar Materials Technology, in Changshu in March 2008. The company grew from PV backsheets into N-type TOPCon cells and modules and listed on ChiNext in Sept 2014. Hurun listed this wealth jointly (to 2022) with Lin Jianwei. Control has since passed to state-owned Zhejiang Zheneng Electric Power, and Lin waived his voting rights in 2026.
interesting_fact: Jolywood went from a 2008 backsheet start-up to a ChiNext listing in only six years (Sept 2014), then became an early mass producer of N-type bifacial cells before Zhejiang Energy took control.
deep_cut_fact: Company filings name her as one of just two founding investors (with Dai Enqi) of Suzhou Zhonglai Solar Materials Technology, registered in Changshu on 7 March 2008.
notes: Very private; no interviews found. The founding family no longer controls Jolywood (Zheneng Electric is now the controlling shareholder), so the company is not a route to Zhang. Last Hurun appearance was 2022; current wealth probably much lower. Avoid the change of control and losses as topics.

name: Zang Jianjun
current_role: Unknown; formerly Executive Chairman of SGX-listed CEFC International Ltd and a senior executive of the Huaxin/CEFC China Energy group
profile: Zang Jianjun (臧建军, b. ~1974) is a petrochemical-trading executive from the Shanghai Huaxin (华信) / CEFC China Energy group founded by Ye Jianming; Hurun listed him (2015-2017) under 'Huaxin Petroleum'. He ran Hua Xin Energy Holdings 2006-2011, then became CEO (2012) and Executive Chairman (2013) of Singapore-listed CEFC International. CEFC China Energy collapsed in 2018 and was declared bankrupt in 2020; his current activity is not public.
interesting_fact: He joined CEFC International's board in January 2012, became CEO in December 2012 and Executive Chairman in December 2013, handing the CEO role to ex-PetroChina finance manager Lu Dachuan in February 2015.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in Hebei trading: business manager at Hebei Baoding International Trading Co (1995-96), international trading manager at Hebei Lixiang Corp (1996-99), then chemical business unit GM and deputy GM at DaGang Petro Chemical (1999-2006) before Huaxin.
notes: Identity: Hurun 2015/2017 entries list 臧建军, b. 1974, Shanghai, company 华信石油 / Huaxin (oil & chemicals), which matches the CEFC (华信) group. The CEFC group collapsed after chairman Ye Jianming was detained in 2018 (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CEFC_China_Energy). No current role, channels or contacts found. Approach with care given the group's history.

name: Lin Haifeng (林海峰)
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Risen Energy Co. (东方日升, SZSE: 300118)
profile: Born 1975, founder of Risen Energy, a Ningbo (Ninghai)-based solar manufacturer founded in 2002 that makes PV cells and modules and builds solar plants, with sales offices in Australia, India, the US and Japan; listed in Shenzhen in 2010. Chairman since at least 2021 and holds ~283M shares; the company is pushing heterojunction (HJT) modules.
interesting_fact: Risen set up a 'Global PV Research Institute' in Nov 2023 to drive integrated cell/module R&D, and its 2023 revenue reached about RMB 35.3bn with net profit up ~46%, helped by its heterojunction technology.
deep_cut_fact: His official company bio notes he holds an EMBA from Ningbo University and has been named one of Ningbo's 'Ten Outstanding Young People' and 'Ten Charity Stars', as well as a 'Changzhou Star Entrepreneur'.
notes: Low international profile; no personal accounts found. Board secretary is Zhou Yinning. Web-search budget ran out mid-lane, so profile relies on exchange-data and company pages. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Zhang Jinfang
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Chipone Technology (Beijing) Co. (集创北方); since Jan 2026 also actual controller of Silicon-valley display-chip firm Analogix/硅数股份
profile: Born 1985 in Shuozhou, Shanxi; PhD in circuits and systems from Beijing Jiaotong University. Founded display-driver chip designer Chipone in 2008 while a first-year master's student; it became a ~RMB 31B unicorn backed by Xiaomi, vivo, Huawei Hubble and BOE, and is preparing a STAR Market IPO. In 2026 he took control of display-chip maker Analogix (硅数股份).
interesting_fact: Chipone's chips are behind the 16K wraparound LED display of the Las Vegas Sphere, and it holds over 45% of the global LED display-driver chip market.
deep_cut_fact: He started Chipone in 2008 with four classmates in a ~40 sqm rented room in Zhongguancun; within a year the five-person team shipped its first product, a phone-charger power-management chip, before moving into LED driver and touch chips.
notes: Young (b. 1985) chip founder; IPO-in-preparation context means company may limit his media. Best route: Chipone public affairs (pr@). Display-chip focus is more consumer electronics than data center.

name: Radik Shaimiev
current_role: Businessman, Kazan; one of the main shareholders of the TAIF group (Tatarstan petrochemicals, merged into SIBUR in 2021); long-time Tatneft board member
profile: Son of Tatarstan's first president Mintimer Shaimiev (listed spelling 'Shaimev'). Trained as a civil engineer, he joined Kazan investment firm TAIF in 1992; TAIF became the holding company for Tatarstan's big petrochemical, refining and power assets, and he has sat on Tatneft's board since 1998. Also an internationally ranked rally/autocross driver and was named president of FC Rubin Kazan in 2017.
interesting_fact: A Master of Sport (international class) in motorsport, he won the 2003 European Autocross Championship in the touring-car class, with his own brother Airat as main title rival, and still competes in classic rallies, including World Championship rounds.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he trained as an architect-engineer: after Marine service in Vladivostok (1982-84) and graduating from the Kazan Civil Engineering Institute in 1989, he worked as an engineer in architectural-planning workshop No. 2 of the Kazgrazhdanproekt institute.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contact found. Sanctioned by Ukraine (Oct 2022) and Canada (June 2025), which makes outreach/booking legally and reputationally sensitive for a Western podcast. Only data point is Hurun 2014; TAIF has since been folded into SIBUR.

name: Mikhail Fedyaev
current_role: Co-owner and president of Siberian Business Union (SDS) holding, Kemerovo (coal, fertilizers, engineering, transport)
profile: Kemerovo businessman (b. 1962, Prokopyevsk) who started as a car-factory mechanic. With partner Vladimir Gridin he won control of the Chernigovets coal pit in 1999 and in 2004 formed Siberian Business Union (SDS), now spanning coal mining, fertilizers/chemicals, engineering, transport and construction in Kuzbass. He has been SDS president since 2007.
interesting_fact: He was elected chairman of a production-and-construction cooperative in 1989, one of the first Soviet-era private ventures, and in the 1990s ran the Kemerovo office of MirInvest, where he met his long-time partner Vladimir Gridin.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a mechanical engineer in 'Automobiles and motor transport' at the Kuzbass Polytechnic Institute (1985), rose to deputy head of a truck column, and in 1996 was general director of Partner-Grundfos, a Kemerovo venture tied to the Danish pump maker, before going into coal.
notes: Sensitive: owner of the Listvyazhnaya mine where a 2021 methane explosion killed 51; he was arrested in 2021 and given a suspended sentence in 2025. No published personal or press contact found. Russian-language, regionally focused; likely a poor fit for outreach.

name: Gao Jifan
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Trina Solar Co., Ltd. (SSE STAR: 688599), Changzhou
profile: Gao Jifan, a Changzhou native with chemistry degrees from Nanjing University and Jilin University, founded Trina Solar in 1997. Trina listed on the NYSE in 2006, went private in 2017 and relisted on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020; it is now one of the world's largest PV module makers and has expanded into energy storage, trackers and digital energy services, with plants in China, Vietnam and Thailand.
interesting_fact: Trina was named the first solar 'Industry Shaper' by the World Economic Forum in Davos, and was the first PV and energy-storage company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market.
deep_cut_fact: Trina says Gao was inspired to found the company by the Kyoto Protocol and the US 'Million Solar Roofs' initiative (both 1997); academically he is a physical chemist - MSc in physical chemistry from Jilin University (1988) after a Nanjing University chemistry BSc (1985).
notes: Frequent Davos/industry-forum speaker, so conference panels are a natural route. Son Gao Haichun became co-chairman in 2025 (succession under way). Could not verify a published press/IR email (web-search budget exhausted).

name: Wang Dong
current_role: Co-founder and Executive President, Moore Threads Technology (Beijing GPU maker; STAR Market 688795)
profile: Per Forbes, Wang Dong spent more than a decade as a sales director at Nvidia before co-founding Moore Threads in 2020 with former Nvidia China head Zhang Jianzhong. Moore Threads designs full-function GPUs for AI training/inference and graphics as a domestic Chinese alternative to Nvidia; it listed in Shanghai in December 2025, raising about $1.1B.
interesting_fact: Moore Threads' shares jumped about 468% on their Shanghai trading debut on 5 Dec 2025, with DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng's High-Flyer reported among institutional investors.
deep_cut_fact: At the July 2026 World AI Conference in Shanghai he argued the inference market has no 'universal chip' - only combinations of solutions - because inference scenarios are highly fragmented and no single company can monopolize them; he also noted Chinese frontier models' cost advantage.
notes: Common name; matched via Forbes URL (wang-dong-1 = Moore Threads cofounder, $1.4B on 2026 list). Input's 'Hurun China 2007-2021' entries predate Moore Threads (2020) and likely belong to another Wang Dong. Public speaker at WAIC - route via Moore Threads marketing (mkt@) or IR.

name: Cao Zheng
current_role: Major shareholder (wealth shared with chairman Cao Ji) of Zhejiang Hangke Technology (688006.SH); director and VP of the company until Dec 2021
profile: Cao Zheng (b. 1983) built his career inside Hangke, the Hangzhou maker of formation and grading equipment used in the back-end of lithium-ion battery production lines, rising from purchasing staff to director, deputy GM and head of sales. Hangke listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in July 2019; Hurun lists his fortune jointly with Cao Ji, Hangke's founder and chairman.
interesting_fact: Hangke was one of the first batch of companies to list on Shanghai's STAR Market (July 2019), and its post-processing equipment for EV battery cells is sold to major battery makers in China and abroad.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he spent 2005-2008 as an assistant engineer at STATS ChipPAC, the Singapore-based semiconductor packaging and test company; he holds Singapore permanent residency and a master's degree.
notes: No longer on Hangke's board (term ended Dec 2021), so current role is unclear; alive status not independently confirmed (no reports of death found, but web search budget ran out). The IR email is the company's board-secretary mailbox. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Li Chen
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (founding-shareholder group with Li Zhen and Guoxuan Holding) of Gotion High-Tech (国轩高科, SZSE: 002074); holds ~1.57% directly and sits on boards of group-related companies
profile: Li Chen (李晨) is the son of Gotion High-Tech founder-chairman Li Zhen and, with him and Nanjing Guoxuan Holding, one of the company's acting-in-concert controlling shareholders. Hefei-based Gotion (formerly Anhui Guoxuan) makes LFP and other lithium-ion cells for EVs and grid energy storage, with Volkswagen China as a major strategic shareholder.
interesting_fact: Although Volkswagen (China) is a top shareholder, under its shareholder agreement VW irrevocably waives part of its voting rights so that its voting power stays at least 5 points below that of the founding shareholders - Guoxuan Holding, Li Zhen and Li Chen.
notes: Wealth listing is shared with father Li Zhen, the public face of Gotion; Li Chen keeps a low profile and his executive title (if any) is not confirmed in the 2026 interim report. Strong energy-storage fit, but the better interview target is likely Li Zhen. Contact via Gotion IR/board office.

name: Lu Weidong
current_role: Deputy General Manager, Inner Mongolia Erdos Resources Co. (鄂尔多斯, SSE: 600295 / 900936); previously a company director
profile: Lu Weidong is a long-serving senior executive of the Erdos group in Ordos, Inner Mongolia, whose listed arm Erdos Resources spans cashmere (the Erdos brand), coal, power and ferroalloy/chemicals. He sat on the listed company's board (still a director in mid-2025) and is listed as Deputy GM in the 2025 pay disclosure; Hurun ranks him for his group shareholding.
interesting_fact: The Erdos group combines one of China's best-known cashmere brands with an energy-and-metallurgy business (coal, power, silicon/ferroalloys) in Ordos, one of China's main coal regions.
notes: Role confirmed in Erdos Resources' Apr 2026 notice on executive pay (Lu Weidong, Deputy GM, 2025 pay RMB1.96M): https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202604141821185338_1.pdf . Chairman is Wang Zhen. No personal channels; formal route would be the board secretary listed in Erdos Resources' annual report.

name: Huang Biliang
current_role: Co-founder, director & general manager, JoulWatt Technology (Hangzhou); co-controlling shareholder with chairman Zhou Xunwei
profile: Huang Biliang (b. 1971, Macau resident) earned BS/MS degrees at Tsinghua and a PhD at Virginia Tech, then spent 2001-2013 at Linear Technology as a design engineer and R&D center manager. He co-founded power-management chipmaker JoulWatt in Hangzhou in 2013 (GM since 2016); it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market and serves data-center/server power.
interesting_fact: Both JoulWatt founders, Huang and Zhou Xunwei, earned PhDs at Virginia Tech under power-electronics pioneer Fred C. Lee, and both later worked at Linear Technology before co-founding JoulWatt; Huang is the named inventor on 99 granted invention patents there.
deep_cut_fact: Per JoulWatt's IPO prospectus, he was the first to propose using coupled inductors to improve power modules' static and dynamic performance, an idea widely adopted by industry, with the work cited 2,000+ times; in 2015 his team was named a Zhejiang 'leading innovation and entrepreneurship team'.
notes: Technical founder, low media profile. Coupled-inductor/VRM power-delivery work is directly relevant to AI server power, a strong podcast angle. JoulWatt filed for a Hong Kong H-share listing in Jan 2026.

name: Kim Sang-beom
current_role: Chairman, ISU Group (ISU Chemical, ISU Petasys, ISU Specialty Chemical), South Korea
profile: Chairman of ISU Group since 2000, succeeding his late father Kim Joon-sung (founder of Daegu Bank, ex-chairman of Samsung Electronics and Daewoo). He became a billionaire in 2025 as AI demand sent shares of ISU Petasys - a Daegu maker of high-layer printed circuit boards for AI servers and 800G switches used by Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft and Cisco - up more than 200%; he holds ~17% directly and indirectly.
interesting_fact: ISU Petasys's most advanced product is 40+-layer multilayer boards for AI network switches; JPMorgan analysts forecast that mix rising from 22% of networking sales in 2025 to 43% in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before running the family group he was a New York lawyer at Debevoise & Plimpton; he holds a JD and an MBA from the University of Michigan and a business degree from Seoul National University.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts found. Route would be via ISU Group / ISU Petasys corporate communications (Korean company sites not reachable from this environment, so no published email verified). Strong data-center/AI-hardware angle (PCBs for AI servers).

name: Wang Xinyang
current_role: Chairman, Gpixel Changchun Microelectronics (长光辰芯, HKEX: 3277)
profile: Wang Xinyang (王欣洋) chairs Gpixel, a Changchun-based fabless maker of high-performance CMOS image sensors for machine vision, scientific, medical and professional imaging, founded in 2012 with subsidiaries in Antwerp and Tokyo. Gpixel listed on the Hong Kong main board on 17 April 2026 (HK$39.88 offer price), which made him a billionaire on Forbes' real-time list.
interesting_fact: Gpixel's very first product, the GMAX3005, was at launch the world's highest-resolution CMOS image sensor (150 megapixels), and it later built the first back-illuminated scientific CMOS sensor, the GSENSE400BSI.

public_contacts.value: info@gpixel.com (general/media contact; media inquiry form on site)

notes: Forbes profile now 404s (dropped off list). Personal bio details not verified from a public source; web-search budget ran out during this lane. Gpixel Europe (Antwerp) handles English-language inquiries: info@gpixel.eu.

name: Cao Kanyu
current_role: Director and President (CEO since April 2023), CXMT Corporation / ChangXin Memory Technologies, Hefei
profile: PhD-trained chip engineer (born 1971) who worked at Philips Semiconductors in the U.S., founded two Beijing chip startups, then ran a NAND flash unit before joining CXMT in 2017. Rose through R&D to CEO/President of CXMT, China's leading DRAM maker and world No.4 by share, which raised about $8.6B in its July 2026 Shanghai STAR Market IPO.
interesting_fact: In October 2026 he publicly unveiled CXMT's progress on a 4F2 DRAM cell architecture at China's Integrated Chips and Chiplets conference, with next-gen DDR5 RDIMM products targeted for year-end.
deep_cut_fact: Before CXMT he was a serial founder: between 2005 and 2013 he set up Beijing Kuntian Kewei Microelectronics and Beijing Fandaxun Technology, then was GM of the NAND flash division at NoVoMem Inc. (2013-17), per CXMT's IPO prospectus.
notes: Chinese state-linked strategic chip company; executives rarely give Western media interviews. Route via board office / IR (board secretary Yuan Yuan). Company is subject to U.S. export-control scrutiny.

name: Daniel Roberts
current_role: Co-Founder, Co-CEO and Director, IREN Ltd (Nasdaq: IREN)
profile: Sydney-based co-founder, with brother Will, of IREN (formerly Iris Energy, founded 2018), which began as a renewable-powered bitcoin miner and now builds AI/HPC data centers, including a 2GW campus in Sweetwater, Texas. IREN signed a five-year, ~$9.7bn AI cloud contract with Microsoft in 2025. Before IREN, Daniel helped grow Palisade Investment Partners in infrastructure.
interesting_fact: The brothers deliberately sought 'stranded' renewable power: their first site was a data center beside a shut pulp mill in Canal Flats, British Columbia, using surplus hydro and rehiring local mill workers.
deep_cut_fact: Daniel first bought bitcoin in 2013 at about US$1,000 and sold at US$500 ('What nonsense is this?'), then joined the Ethereum presale. Scouting sites for Iris Energy, the brothers backpacked through Europe, Iceland and the US, and still laugh about a scuzzy windowless New York hostel.
notes: Wealth shared with brother/co-CEO William Roberts. Forbes AU says Daniel was co-owner of Palisade Investment Partners (helped grow it to ~$6bn infrastructure AUM) while Will was a Macquarie VP, slightly contradicting the Forbes profile that both worked at Macquarie. Highly relevant to energy/data-center podcast.

name: William Roberts
current_role: Co-Founder & Co-CEO, IREN Ltd (Nasdaq: IREN), Sydney
profile: Will Roberts and his older brother Daniel co-founded Iris Energy (renamed IREN in 2024), which listed on Nasdaq in November 2021 as a renewable-powered bitcoin miner and has pivoted to AI cloud/HPC data centers. IREN is building a 2GW, 1,800-acre campus in Sweetwater, Texas, and in 2025 signed a five-year, $9.7B AI cloud contract with Microsoft. Before IREN, Will was a vice president at Macquarie Group, where he co-founded its digital assets team.
interesting_fact: The brothers deliberately named the company Iris Energy rather than something like 'Iris Data' - they measure compute in gigawatts, not gigabytes - and IREN's sites span Texas, Oklahoma and British Columbia.
deep_cut_fact: Will and Daniel first bought bitcoin in 2013 at around US$1,000, sold at US$500 after it crashed ('What nonsense is this?'), then got into the Ethereum presale for next to nothing - years before founding Iris Energy.
notes: Shares Forbes profile with brother Daniel (the more public-facing co-CEO). Ideal podcast fit (bitcoin-to-AI-data-center pivot, 2GW Texas campus, Microsoft deal). Best route: IREN media@iren.com. Avoid referencing Daniel's 2023 health scare mentioned in Forbes AU.

name: Tang Jie
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Scientist, Zhipu AI (Z.ai); Professor of Computer Science, Tsinghua University
profile: Tang Jie (唐杰) is a Tsinghua professor and an ACM, AAAI and IEEE Fellow. He co-founded Zhipu AI in 2019 out of his Knowledge Engineering Group and, as chief scientist, leads its GLM/ChatGLM large-language-model family. Zhipu went public in Hong Kong in January 2026, which made him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: He invented AMiner.org, an academic search and social-network mining system he has built since 2006, which grew to over 30 million users in 220 countries and regions. It became Zhipu's technical foundation.
deep_cut_fact: As a grad student he interned in Microsoft Research Asia's NLC group (2004-05) and at IBM China Research Lab (2004). He was later a visiting scholar at Cornell with John Hopcroft and Jon Kleinberg. His research won the SIGKDD Test-of-Time (ten-year best paper) award.
notes: He is an accessible academic who publishes his own email and gives many keynotes in English. Forbes estimates of his net worth vary widely with Zhipu's share price. For data-center/AI topics, frame the pitch around open models (GLM) and AGI.

name: Yan Junjie
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, MiniMax Group (HKEX-listed Chinese foundation-model/AI company, Shanghai)
profile: Born 1989 in Xiayi County, Henan, Yan earned a PhD at the CAS Institute of Automation, did a Tsinghua postdoc in deep learning, then rose from intern (2015) to vice president at SenseTime. He left in 2021 to found MiniMax (LLMs, Hailuo video, Talkie, speech/music models); its January 2026 Hong Kong IPO made him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: In January 2026 he joined a symposium hosted by Premier Li Qiang, only the second founder of a Chinese foundation-model developer (after DeepSeek's Liang Wenfeng) to attend such a meeting.
deep_cut_fact: A devoted Dota 2 player, he goes by the alias 'IO' (a pun on input/output and the Dota wisp hero); watching OpenAI's bots beat top Dota players in 2019 pushed him from computer vision toward language models. As a PhD student he said his goal was to be a Java developer at IBM.
notes: MiniMax name comes from the minimax algorithm. Gave a Bloomberg Q&A in Jan 2026 (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-01-08/minimax-founder-was-once-dismissed-as-a-fraud-by-big-tech-q-a), so open to English-language press. Gaming link: knows miHoYo CEO Cai Haoyu, an early backer.

name: Oleg Misevra
current_role: Controlling owner and chairman, East Mining Company (VGK / Vostochnaya Gornorudnaya Kompaniya), Sakhalin, Russia
profile: Former USSR/Russian Internal Troops officer who became a top manager and minority partner at MDM Group and president of SUEK (2002-04). In 2004 he bought SUEK's Sakhalin assets, building East Mining Company around the Solntsevsky open-pit coal mine and Shakhtersk port, now one of Russia's fastest-growing thermal coal exporters to Asia.
interesting_fact: He was named Russia's 'Exporter of the Year' in 2019 in the All-Russian People-2019 competition, as VGK ramped Sakhalin coal exports and expanded its Shakhtersk port.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2015 interview he explained that VGK was then Russia's only exporter of brown (lignite) coal, so its real competitor is Indonesia rather than Australia, and that the business is fully self-contained: 'We have everything of our own: the mine, the port, the conveyor line.'

current_role: Director and General Manager, Hubei Dinglong Co. (鼎龙股份, SZSE: 300054), Wuhan; also director of Wuhan Zhongyuan Huadian since Dec 2025

name: Pankaj Doshi
current_role: Promoter-shareholder, Waaree Energies Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Pankaj Doshi is one of four Doshi brothers whose family controls Waaree Energies, India's largest solar-module maker by capacity. name: Liu Shiqi
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hubei Wanrun New Energy Technology Co. (688275.SH)
profile: Liu Shiqi controls Hubei Wanrun New Energy, founded in December 2010 in Shiyan, Hubei. The company makes lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode materials and precursors for EV and energy-storage batteries. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in September 2022, and Liu still runs it as chairman and general manager.
interesting_fact: Liu personally chairs Wanrun's board-level Sustainability Committee. The company has joined the CDP carbon-disclosure programme two years running, scoring B-, and is developing technology to recover lithium carbonate and iron phosphate from waste.
deep_cut_fact: Wanrun funds the 'Wanrun Class' (万润班) at Yunyang High School in Shiyan, the company's hometown: 40 students a year from low-income families get study and living stipends through all three years of high school.

name: Li Fei
current_role: Co-founder, co-controlling shareholder and director (per 2024 filings), Hubei Wanrun New Energy Technology (SSE STAR: 688275)
profile: Li Fei (李菲) and her husband, chairman Liu Shiqi, founded and jointly control Hubei Wanrun New Energy, a top-three global lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode maker based in Shiyan, Hubei. Listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022, it supplies LFP for EV and energy-storage batteries.
interesting_fact: Wanrun grew revenue at a 324% CAGR from 2020 to 2022, reaching RMB 12.35bn in 2022, as LFP displaced other EV battery chemistries and lithium carbonate prices spiked.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wanrun, Li Fei worked at Dongfeng Motor and Shenzhen Zhonghuang Industrial; the founders' first firm, Wanrun Gongmao (2003), made iron-phosphate cathode precursors and got into the supply chain of US battery pioneer A123 before Wanrun New Energy was set up in 2010.

name: Colette Kress
current_role: Interim CEO (since 12 Nov 2026) and EVP & Chief Financial Officer, NVIDIA.
profile: Kress joined Nvidia as CFO in 2013 after ~25 years in tech finance (Texas Instruments, 13 years at Microsoft, CFO of a Cisco division). She steered its finances as sales rose from $4.3bn to $215.9bn and it became the first $5tn company. On 12 Nov 2026 she was named interim CEO after Jensen Huang resigned, while remaining CFO.
interesting_fact: She joined Nvidia partly at the urging of her two young sons, avid gamers who knew the company from the chips in their favourite video games.
deep_cut_fact: Jensen Huang interviewed 22 candidates before hiring her; in her first week she asked how long he'd want her in the role and he answered, 'For as long as we shall live and death do us part.' She holds a finance B.Sc. from the University of Arizona and an MBA from SMU.
notes: Very timely: just became interim CEO amid Huang's sudden 12 Nov 2026 resignation (personal-conduct reports) - avoid that topic; expect heavy media demand. Best route is Nvidia corporate PR (press@nvidia.com). Q3 FY27 earnings 17 Nov 2026.

profile: Hangzhou-based shareholder and supervisor of Zhejiang Rongsheng Holding Group, the private parent of Shenzhen-listed Rongsheng Petrochemical (002493), one of China's largest refining, petrochemical and polyester-fibre groups. Chang Chun is one of Asia's largest petrochemicals-and-plastics makers, with plants in Taiwan, mainland China and Southeast Asia. Forbes previously listed her jointly with her brother Tseng Cheng.

name: Wang Wenjian
current_role: Founder, honorary chairman and non-executive director, Sunny Optical Technology (Group) Co. (HKEX: 2382)
profile: Wang Wenjian (王文鉴, b. ~1947) founded what became Sunny Optical in Yuyao, Zhejiang, in 1984, serving as chairman and CEO before moving to non-executive director in 2012. Sunny is now a global leader in phone camera lenses and modules (1.32bn lenses shipped in 2024) and automotive/AR optics. His son Wang Tan Jiong became board chairman in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: Sunny's largest shareholder is an employee trust (Sunny Group Overseas Employee Trust, ~35.5%) co-administered by Wang, a structure designed to avoid family control; the company pivoted to phone optics in 2000 when phones had no cameras of note.
deep_cut_fact: In 1984 he started the business as a small township optical-instrument factory in Yuyao with just eight high-school graduates and a RMB 60,000 loan; he has also been honorary president of the Yuyao Charity Federation (2003) and a guest professor at Zhejiang University (2005).
notes: Age ~78-79; low public profile. Board bio: https://www.irasia.com/listco/hk/sunnyoptical/onlinereport/2025/e_annual/47/ . Best route is Sunny IR office. Shares the Sunny fortune with co-founders such as Ye Liaoning (P07144).

name: Dasari Uday Kumar Reddy
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO, Tanla Platforms Ltd (Hyderabad)
profile: Uday Reddy founded Tanla in 1999 as an SMS-centre provider for telecom operators and listed it in 2006. Tanla is now a leading Indian CPaaS and enterprise-messaging company, with blockchain-based anti-spam (Trubloq) and anti-phishing (Wisely ATP) platforms. He first joined the Forbes billionaires list in 2022 after Tanla's shares more than doubled in 2021.

deep_cut_fact: At 11 he sold sweets to his whole school. In the late 1980s he sold his only possession, his motorbike, to start a paging business in Hyderabad, camping outside a hardware maker's site in Singapore until he had mastered the technology. He charged per message rather than for hardware.
notes: Not the same person as YuppTV founder Uday Reddy; avoid YourStory or FPJ articles about that Uday Reddy. He did an MBA at Manchester Business School, where seeing UK text-messaging use inspired Tanla. Forbes also notes his first venture was real estate in 1993.

profile: Tang Zhuang (b. 1973) is a co-founder and CTO of Maxscend (卓胜微), a Wuxi-based maker of RF front-end chips (switches, LNAs, filters) for smartphones that listed in Shenzhen in 2019. Shenwu grew into a group with two listed arms (Shenwu Environmental, Shenwu Energy Saving) before a 2017-18 liquidity crisis.

current_role: President, Orion Heritage Co. (private Museum 'Collection', Moscow); founder of InOil (GreenBooster fuel additive)
profile: Tbilisi-born (1957) entrepreneur who cofounded Russian dairy-and-juice giant Wimm-Bill-Dann and chaired it 2001-2010; it sold to PepsiCo for ~$5.7B in 2010-11, netting him ~$600M for his ~10% stake. profile: Zhang Tianren built Tianneng from a debt-laden battery workshop in Changxing, Zhejiang (1986) into China's largest lead-acid battery maker, powering the country's e-bike boom; it listed in Hong Kong in 2007 and its Tianneng Battery arm trades on Shanghai's STAR Market. profile: Long Daqiang (龙大强, b. 1973) and his wife Meng Liye, both from Pei County, Jiangsu, moved from steel trading into solar in 2010, founding cell maker Zhongyu PV and then SolarSpace (中润光能). SolarSpace became the world's No.2 PV-cell maker by 2024 shipments (14.6% share) and in 2025 filed for a Hong Kong IPO, partly to fund a North Carolina cell plant.
