interesting_fact: Fermi's Project Matador in the Texas Panhandle was pitched as one of the world's largest energy-and-data campuses, combining gas, nuclear, solar and grid power to serve hyperscale AI tenants.
deep_cut_fact: Outside energy, his philanthropy has focused on family formation in US inner cities, and abroad he has worked with orphanages in China and helped build and maintain schools in Rwanda and Zambia.
notes: Sensitive timing: he left Fermi as CEO in April 2026, was removed from the board, and has been in a public proxy fight with the company (calling for a sale/special meeting). Avoid the dispute in outreach; his PR firm Collected Strategies issues his statements. Fermi IR is not a good route for him now.

name: Fang Xiaoling
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Maxio Technology (Hangzhou) Co. (STAR Market: 688449).
profile: Fang Xiaoling (b. 1963, US citizen) holds Zhejiang University BS/MS degrees and a University of Utah EE PhD. After co-founding Taiwanese fabless firm JMicron, she founded Maxio in Hangzhou in 2014; it designs SSD/data-storage controller chips and AIoT signal-processing chips, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in late 2024. She controls ~45% of Maxio.
interesting_fact: Surveillance giant Hikvision invested in Maxio in its third year and became its 2nd-largest shareholder (37% with a subsidiary pre-IPO); Maxio's controllers are mass-deployed at YMTC and Longsys.
deep_cut_fact: Before chips for storage, she was a principal engineer at Sonic Innovations, a Salt Lake City hearing-aid maker (then ranked world No. 7), from 1995-2001 right after her Utah PhD; she then cofounded JMicron and ran JMicron USA for 15 years.
notes: Low media profile; best route is Maxio IR (board secretary/CFO Qian Xiaofei). Data-center angle: enterprise SSD controllers.

name: Luo Yungang
current_role: Unknown; Hurun listed him (2017-2018) under Baota Petrochemical (宝塔石化), Yinchuan, Ningxia
profile: Luo Yungang (罗运刚) is listed by Hurun China 2017 (RMB5300m) and 2018 (RMB7000m) with Baota Petrochemical Group (宝塔石化集团), a Yinchuan-based private refiner with ~200 fuel stations that also ran Yinchuan University (hence 'petrochemicals, education'). His exact role or stake could not be independently confirmed.
notes: Hurun API (hurun.net HsRankDetailsList, 2017/2018 lists) gives 罗运刚 / Bao Ta Petrochemical / Ningxia-Yinchuan, with no birth year. Searched Chinese and English web for 罗运刚 plus 宝塔石化 and 泰瑞智本. Read the 2015 SZSE restructuring report of Baota Industry (000595), which lists Baota Petrochemical's shareholders as Sun Hengchao 43.8%, 宁夏泰瑞智本投资 32.1%, 江苏汇金 18.46% and Sun Shulan 5.64%; 罗运刚 is not named, so he may hold his stake indirectly, e.g. via 泰瑞智本 (unverified). The Baota group ran into a debt crisis in 2018. No contacts found. Baidu, Qichacha and Sogou were blocked.

name: Wang Jingliang
current_role: Legal representative of Kunming Huachen Investment Co. (昆明华辰投资), a shareholder of Yunnan Energy New Material / SEMCORP (恩捷股份, 002812.SZ)
profile: Wang Jingliang (王敬良, b. 1963, Kunming) is a Kunming investor whose wealth comes from a stake in Yunnan Energy New Material (恩捷股份), the world's largest lithium-battery separator maker, controlled by the Paul Xiaoming Lee family. Hurun 2021 put his fortune at RMB6.5bn (6th richest in Yunnan). He reportedly heads Kunming Huachen Investment and the Huakun investment partnerships in Hainan and Zhuhai.
interesting_fact: Kunming Huachen Investment held 2.64% (23.4m shares) of Yunnan Energy New Material at end-2020, among its top-10 shareholders alongside the Lee family's vehicles.
deep_cut_fact: Huachen Investment was one of the original holders of Shanghai Energy (上海恩捷, SEMCORP's separator unit). In 2018 it swapped that stake for new shares when packaging maker Yunnan Chuangxin (创新股份) bought Shanghai Energy at RMB24.87/share, turning a cigarette-pack printer into a battery-materials giant.
notes: Hurun 2021: 王敬良, b. 1963-04, Kunming, company 恩捷股份 / Energy New Material ('packaging box production'). His link to 昆明华辰投资 (legal representative) comes from a secondary rich-list article (https://m.maigoo.com/top/399867.html), not a filing. His name does not appear in Enjie's 2020/2024 reports, which only name Huachen. Very private. No contacts found. Enjie IR would be the only institutional route.

name: Ye Liaoning
current_role: Co-founder and consultant, Sunny Optical Technology; chairman until 1 Nov 2025 (retired from the board citing retirement age)
profile: Ye Liaoning (叶辽宁, b. ~1965) joined the Yuyao Chengbei optical-instrument factory that became Sunny Optical in 1984 and is counted among the group's founders. He rose to deputy GM (1995), executive director (2007) and chairman, leading Sunny's growth into a global phone/auto camera-optics leader, then stepped down in Nov 2025 and stays on as a consultant.
interesting_fact: He stepped down as chairman effective 1 Nov 2025 ahead of reaching retirement age in early 2026, handing over to founder Wang Wenjian's son Wang Tan Jiong, and remains a consultant to the group.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the factory in 1984 as a teenager and earned his diploma part-time from Zhejiang Radio & TV University only in 1999; he received China's National May-First Labor Medal (2019) and the title National Model Worker (2020).
notes: Low international profile; now retired from the board. Only published route is Sunny's IR office. Fortune shared with Sunny co-founders (see Wang Wenjian, P05955).

name: Ivan Müller Botelho
current_role: Patriarch of the controlling Botelho family of Energisa S.A. and its long-time former chairman; he is not listed on the board elected in April 2026
profile: An electrical engineer (University of Miami) from Leopoldina, Minas Gerais, Ivan Botelho is the third generation of the family that has controlled Brazilian utility Energisa since 1905. He built it from a regional Cataguases utility into a group with nine state distribution companies, transmission and gas, serving more than 20 million customers. His sons Ricardo (CEO) and Maurício (CFO) now run it.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Energisa, the underdog bidder, won the 2013 creditors' vote for the bankrupt Grupo Rede over CPFL, a deal that changed the group's scale. In 2026, at 92, he published a memoir, 'A jornada da Energia para o futuro', based on his testimony to journalist Plínio Fraga.
deep_cut_fact: He started on the front line, in the lines and power plants. His memoir recalls installing Brazil's first photoelectric cell to switch street lighting on automatically, and a safety-glove demonstration that ended up shutting down power to the whole town. He was also an early backer of the Instituto Liberal think tank.
notes: He is about 92 (per JB, March 2026), so the realistic route is via Energisa IR or his sons; CEO Ricardo Botelho is the active public face. The new memoir (2026) is a natural hook for outreach. Confirm his current board status in Energisa's Formulário de Referência.

name: Muhammed Aziz Khan
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Summit Group (Bangladesh); based in Singapore
profile: Bangladesh-born, Singapore-based Muhammed Aziz Khan (b. 1955, Dhaka IBA MBA) started out as a trader and founded Summit in 1985; it built Bangladesh's first independent power plant (Khulna, 1998) and its first private off-dock port, and now spans power, LNG, ports, fibre optics and real estate. Japan's JERA owns 22% of Summit Power International, run by his daughter Ayesha.
interesting_fact: He told Nikkei Asia Summit plans Bangladesh's first data centre using Summit Power's gas-fired capacity: 'Summit Group's next phase focuses on integrating energy and data, leveraging our LNG and fibre-optic expertise.'
deep_cut_fact: Singapore's Prime Minister's Office awarded him the Public Service Medal (COVID-19) for financially helping Bangladeshi workers in Singapore during the pandemic; he and his wife were also the first Bangladeshis named UNICEF International Council members.

public_contacts.value: enquiry@summitpowerinternational.com (Summit Power International, One Raffles Place, Singapore)

notes: Very good fit: energy + data-centre angle (gas-to-data-centre plan, fibre/LNG). Gives interviews to Bangladeshi press and Nikkei. Best route: Summit Power International Singapore enquiry form (press category).

name: Gennady Kozovoy
current_role: Shareholder (~5.7%) of Evraz plc; former CEO and board member of Raspadskaya coal company (Mezhdurechensk, Kuzbass)
profile: Siberian coal executive who rose through Russia's Raspadskaya mine. In 1993 he was elected general director and, with partner Alexander Vagin, gained control of the company as workers' shares were bought up. Raspadskaya listed in 2006. In 2012 they sold control to Evraz for cash plus Evraz shares, his main asset today. He stepped down as CEO in July 2014.
interesting_fact: Kozovoy and Vagin turned Raspadskaya, once a 'people's enterprise' owned by its miners, into one of Russia's biggest coking-coal producers. They sold their stake to Evraz for about $202M plus roughly 11% of Evraz.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 36 years at Raspadskaya, starting as an electrician-fitter (elektroslesar) at the mine and rising to general director, as the company noted when he handed over the CEO role in 2014.
notes: Very private and gives virtually no press. Russia-based. Evraz was sanctioned by the UK in 2022 (Abramovich link) and is no longer LSE-traded, so outreach may be impractical. Patronymic Ivanovich. No published contact found.

name: Mikhail Abyzov
current_role: None; former Russian Minister for Open Government Affairs (2012-2018), now serving a prison sentence in Russia
profile: Minsk-born Russian energy and engineering businessman (b. 1972) who built his fortune via fuel supply and power assets such as Novosibirskenergo, and chaired engineering group E4. He was Russia's Minister for Open Government Affairs 2012-2018. Arrested in 2019, he was sentenced in Dec 2023 to 12 years; a later RVC-related conviction raised the total to 14 years.
interesting_fact: He set up his first company, Intershops, in 1990 at about 18, selling Turkish consumer goods and later office equipment, before moving into fuel supply and Siberian power utilities.
notes: NOT a viable outreach target: imprisoned in Russia (12-year sentence Dec 2023 per Moscow Times https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2023/12/22/former-russian-minister-sentenced-to-12-years-for-embezzlement-a83522; further cases since, incl. 14-year combined sentence reported by Current Time). He denies the charges. No public contacts; deep-cut fact left empty deliberately.

name: Kirill Shamalov
current_role: Shareholder of PAO SIBUR Holding (about 4% per Forbes); listed by the UK sanctions register as Deputy Chairman of SIBUR's Management Board (current status unverified)
profile: Russian petrochemicals investor and son of Rossiya Bank co-owner Nikolai Shamalov. He joined Sibur as a vice president in 2008, became deputy CEO in 2012 and built up a stake that made him briefly Russia's youngest billionaire. He later sold most of it and is believed to keep about 4% of Sibur. He is under US (2018), UK and EU sanctions.
interesting_fact: Forbes notes he became a vice president of Sibur, Russia's largest petrochemicals company, at age 26, after studying law at Saint Petersburg State University.
deep_cut_fact: According to a Sibur biography cited by Bloomberg, in 2002, at about 20 and still a law student, he was named Gazprom's chief legal counsel for foreign economic activity. He later became chief legal counsel at Gazprombank before joining Sibur in 2008.
notes: High risk: he is sanctioned by the US, UK and EU, and most coverage concerns his former marriage to Putin's daughter and how he got his Sibur shares. He is very private and gives no interviews. The only route is Sibur's corporate press office, and it is unclear whether he still holds a Sibur post. Probably not a suitable podcast guest.

name: Cesar Maklary
current_role: Co-founder and President, Fluidstack (AI cloud / data-center builder, HQ New York)
profile: French co-founder (with Gary Wu and Jamie Cox) of Fluidstack, which grew from an Oxford-born GPU marketplace into a builder/operator of large AI data centers for customers including Anthropic, Google and Meta. A ~$1.5B round led by Jane Street in 2026 valued Fluidstack at over $18B, making the three co-founders billionaires at around 30; he joined in 2020.
interesting_fact: Maklary was the face of Fluidstack's Feb 2025 deal, announced by Emmanuel Macron at the Paris AI Action Summit, to help build an $11.5B AI data center in France ('Nvidia has told me that they will send those chips when we need them'); later that year Jensen Huang signed a Lego model of an Nvidia chip for him and Wu at GTC.
deep_cut_fact: Before data centers he worked on aerodynamics for a Formula One team. He has explained Fluidstack's origin as matching PhD friends starved for compute with 'hardcore cloud gaming friends' whose rigs sat idle most of the week.
notes: Great fit for data-center podcast. Speaks at conferences (e.g. RAISE Summit Paris). France data-center project was reportedly scrapped in 2026 in favour of US sites (avoid framing as failure). Fluidstack declines to comment on valuation/net worth.

name: Gary Wu
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Fluidstack (AI cloud / data-center builder, New York)
profile: Most likely the Gary Wu who co-founded Fluidstack in 2017 while studying economics at Oxford. It began renting idle gamers' GPUs to AI researchers and now builds gigawatt-scale AI data centers, incl. Anthropic's planned $50B build-out on Google TPUs. A Sept 2026 round valued it above $18B, making Wu (31) a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Fluidstack's backers project it managing up to 1.3 GW across 10+ sites in 2026 and aspire to 17+ GW by 2030; it appears to be the first publicly known operator of Google TPU data centers outside Google.
deep_cut_fact: Fluidstack started in 2017 helping gamers make 'beer money' by renting out their idle GPUs to AI researchers; the company never disclosed raising any outside funding until July 2026.
notes: Identity uncertain only because the input lists country 'China' while Fluidstack is UK-founded and now New York-HQ; source of wealth ('AI datacenter builder') and new-billionaire status match strongly. Founders give few interviews; Fluidstack declines press comment. Note Anthropic is a major customer (research compiled by Claude, an Anthropic model).

name: James Dacombe
current_role: Founder & CEO, Olix (OLIX Computing, London AI-inference chip startup); founder & CEO, CoMind (brain monitoring)
profile: British serial founder (b. ~2001) who dropped out of school at 17 to build CoMind, a non-invasive brain-monitoring company, then in 2024 founded Olix (formerly Flux Computing), which designs chips and systems for AI inference. Olix raised $312m in August 2026 at ~$3.3bn, making him Europe's youngest self-made billionaire per Forbes (~30% of Olix, ~12% of CoMind).
interesting_fact: Forbes counts him as one of only 11 self-made billionaires worldwide under 30 - and one of four based outside the US; Olix tripled in value between February and August 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He started programming apps and websites at 13 while at Ashville College in Harrogate, North Yorkshire, then became a Thiel Fellow. He told the Sunday Times in 2024: 'An advantage of starting my business so young was naivety... you just try a lot of things.'
notes: Highly relevant for data-center/AI-infrastructure angle (Olix pitches a 'token factory' rebuild of the datacentre). Olix and CoMind did not respond to Forbes/Fortune comment requests in Aug 2026, so expect a press-office gate; press@olix.com is the best route.

name: Jamie Cox
current_role: Cofounder, Fluidstack (AI cloud / data-center builder, now HQ'd in New York)
profile: British cofounder (with Gary Wu, later Cesar Maklary) of Fluidstack, started in 2017 as a marketplace renting idle gamer GPUs to AI researchers and now a builder/operator of large AI data centers, including custom sites for Anthropic in New York and Texas and a planned 1GW campus in France. A 2026 Jane Street-led $1.5B round valued it at $18B+, making Cox (29) a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Forbes reported Fluidstack appears to be the first publicly known operator of Google TPU data centers outside Google; Macron announced its ~EUR10B, 1-gigawatt French AI data center project in Feb 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He was reading classics at Oxford when he met economics student Gary Wu; he dropped out in 2018 to become a Thiel Fellow, and in 2020 he and Wu started Treecard, a cashback card that funded tree planting, alongside Fluidstack.
notes: Prime fit for the data-center podcast. Specific exec title not published (Wu is CEO, Maklary President). Company declined comment to Forbes on funding; route via press@fluidstack.io.

name: Baoshen Zhong
current_role: Chairman and President (General Manager), LONGi Green Energy Technology Co. (SSE: 601012)
profile: Zhong Baoshen chairs LONGi Green Energy, a global leader in monocrystalline solar wafers, cells and modules. He first built Fushun Magnetic Equipment, then joined Lanzhou University classmate Li Zhenguo at LONGi in 2006 as chairman, adding the CEO role in 2025. He is now steering LONGi through a PV downturn and into energy storage and hydrogen.
interesting_fact: LONGi bet early on monocrystalline silicon when multicrystalline was the industry mainstream, and that bet made mono the dominant solar technology. In 2026 Zhong set a goal of growing LONGi's energy-storage business to a scale close to its PV business within five years.
deep_cut_fact: LONGi's origin story starts with a phone call. In September 2005 Zhong was sightseeing at the Petronas Twin Towers after a business trip to Malaysia when Li Zhenguo, his 1986-entry Lanzhou University physics classmate and fellow Henan native, called about buying used US mono-crystal pullers. Zhong replied: 'Wait for me to come back' (等我回来).
notes: Very visible: NPC deputy, Boao and UN energy forum speaker, regular earnings-call commentator. Best route is LONGi PR (PR@longi.com). Topical hooks: solar-plus-storage ('光储融合') and the anti-'involution' push in Chinese PV. Sources differ on his major (Forbes says metallurgy, Chinese media say physics).

name: Zhang Xuezheng
current_role: Founder and actual controller (via Wentianxia Technology Group) of Wingtech Technology (600745.SH); former chairman of Wingtech (to 2025) and CEO of Nexperia (suspended by Dutch order, Sept 2025)
profile: Born 1975, studied at Guangdong University of Technology, then worked at STMicroelectronics and ZTE before founding Wingtech in 2006. Wingtech became China's top phone ODM (it made Xiaomi's Redmi line), then bought Dutch chipmaker Nexperia in 2019. In 2025 the Dutch government took control of Nexperia, suspending him as CEO; he remains Wingtech's controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Wingtech designed and built Xiaomi's Redmi 1, the first smartphone to retail for under 1,000 yuan (799 yuan), which sold more than 30 million units.
deep_cut_fact: In 2006 he reportedly started Wingtech in Jiaxing with about 30 staff and 100,000 yuan, then went door-to-door in Shenzhen's Huaqiangbei with three salespeople to sell its first phone mainboard, the W100. It went on to ship 18 million units.
notes: Highly sensitive: Nexperia/Dutch government dispute (2025-26), a 2024 CSRC fine, and 2026 share freezes tied to an arbitration. Wingtech denied 'fled' rumours in Sept 2026. Rarely gives interviews. No published press/IR email found on the Wingtech English site. Career timeline (ST 1997-98, ZTE 1998-2002) per https://www.maigoo.com/mingren/24826.html.

name: William Moncrief-jr
current_role: Deceased (died 29 December 2021, Fort Worth, aged 101); formerly head of Moncrief Oil
profile: William Alvin 'Tex' Moncrief Jr., Fort Worth wildcatter who with his father 'Monty' built the Moncrief oil and gas business over 70+ years, died on 29 December 2021 aged 101.
notes: Deceased - death reported by NBC DFW and Hart Energy (Dec 2021). Source for death: https://www.nbcdfw.com/news/local/texas-oil-billionaire-william-tex-moncrief-jr-dead-at-101/2848207/ ; also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Moncrief

name: Randal Nardone
current_role: Director and major shareholder, New Fortress Energy (Nasdaq: NFE); co-founder of Fortress Investment Group
profile: Lawyer-turned-investor Randal Nardone co-founded Fortress Investment Group in 1998, was its CEO 2013-2017 and became a billionaire on its 2007 IPO; SoftBank bought Fortress in 2017. He sits on the board of Wes Edens' LNG-to-power firm New Fortress Energy (~9.6% holder per 2025 proxy).
interesting_fact: Fortress was the first major US private-equity/hedge-fund manager to go public (Feb 2007), which put Nardone on the Forbes billionaires list that year.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance, Nardone was a partner and member of the executive committee at New York law firm Thacher Proffitt & Wood, then a principal at BlackRock Financial Management; he holds a BA from UConn and a JD from Boston University School of Law.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Wes Edens (NFE CEO) is the public face. NFE has been through financial stress/refinancing in 2025-26, so avoid wealth/stock topics. Power-for-data-centers angle: NFE's Oct 2026 300MW turbine lease.

name: Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha
current_role: Chairman and CEO, King Power International (Thailand); Chairman, Leicester City FC
profile: 'Top' (b. 1985) took over Thailand's dominant airport duty-free operator King Power, founded by his late father Vichai in 1989, after Vichai's death in an October 2018 helicopter crash; the family fortune is shared with his mother and siblings. He chairs Leicester City (family-owned; reported in Aug 2026 to be up for sale) and the family also owns OH Leuven and a stake in Bangkok's MahaNakhon tower.
interesting_fact: The family name was a gift: Thailand's late King Bhumibol Adulyadej gave Vichai the surname Srivaddhanaprabha; Aiyawatt was born Aiyawatt Raksriaksorn.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serious polo player who represents Thailand: he won gold in mixed 2-4 goals polo at the 2025 SEA Games in Thailand, and team silver at the 2017 SEA Games in Kuala Lumpur.

public_contacts.value: https://www.lcfc.com (Leicester City FC; chairman statements published here)

notes: Sensitive moment: Leicester relegated to League One (Apr 2026) and reportedly put up for sale (Aug 2026) — avoid in outreach. Only customer-service emails are published by King Power/LCFC; no press contact for him found. Energy-focus tag in input looks weak (duty-free retail).

name: Xu Shijun
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Jiangsu Haili Wind Power Equipment Technology Co., Ltd. (海力风电, SZ:301155)
profile: Xu Shijun (b. 1963) controls Jiangsu Haili Wind Power, a Nantong-based maker of wind-turbine towers, monopiles and other offshore foundation structures, which listed on the Shenzhen ChiNext board in 2021. A trained mechanical engineer and senior economist, he joined Haili in 2009 and has chaired it since. He shares the Hurun listing with Xu Chengchen, a fellow director.
interesting_fact: Haili builds the giant steel towers and pile foundations that hold up China's offshore wind turbines. That made Xu one of the few billionaires whose fortune comes directly from the build-out of offshore wind in the Yellow Sea and East China Sea.
deep_cut_fact: Before wind power he worked his way up at the Rudong County Cotton Machinery Factory (如东县棉机厂) in Jiangsu, first as head of supply and sales and then as factory director. He also still chairs Longteng Machinery (龙腾机械).
notes: 'Haili' here is Jiangsu Haili Wind Power, not the unrelated NEEQ-listed Zhejiang Haili (835787). Xu is low-profile and the IR inbox is the only published route. The listed sector 'Energy' fits: offshore wind supply chain.

name: Mehmet Rustu Basaran
current_role: Chairman, HABAŞ Group (Habaş Sınai ve Tıbbi Gazlar İstihsal Endüstrisi); chairman and part-owner of Anadolubank
profile: Turkish industrialist (b. ~1946/47) who heads Habaş, founded by his father Hamdi Başaran in 1956 in Istanbul as the Topkapı oxygen plant. Habaş grew from industrial/medical gases into one of Turkey's largest steel producers, with LPG/LNG/CNG distribution, storage, shipping and port operations; he also controls Anadolubank.
interesting_fact: Per Forbes, he is a serious car collector whose collection has included a Ferrari 288 GTO, Ferrari F40, McLaren F1, Porsche Carrera GT and Hennessey Venom GT.
notes: HIGHLY SENSITIVE / timing: on 10 Nov 2026 he was reported detained in Istanbul in the probe into a deadly explosion at Habaş's Aliağa (İzmir) steel plant (reported 18 dead). Source: https://www.timeturk.com/habas-patronu-mehmet-rustu-basaran-kartalda-gozaltina-alindi. Forbes says he seldom appears in public and doesn't talk to press. Outreach not advisable now.

name: Yao Lisheng
current_role: Non-independent director and major shareholder, Maxscend Microelectronics (卓胜微, SZSE: 300782), Wuxi
profile: Yao Lisheng (姚立生) is a co-founding shareholder and long-time board member (since 2017) of Maxscend Microelectronics, a Wuxi-based fabless maker of RF front-end chips (switches, LNAs, modules) for smartphones that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in June 2019. His fortune tracks his Maxscend stake; he dropped off Forbes/Hurun lists after 2022 as the shares fell.
interesting_fact: Maxscend's predecessor was set up in August 2012 with RMB10m registered capital by just three backers: CEO Xu Zhihan, Yao Lisheng and Tianjin Xundu.
deep_cut_fact: He studied as an undergraduate at Tsinghua University and did graduate work at the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
notes: Very low public profile; not an executive (chairman/CEO is Xu Zhihan). Education detail comes from an aggregator (MarketScreener); verify against Maxscend's annual report director bios. Route via company general/IR inbox.

name: Ghan Djoe Hiang
current_role: Family shareholder, Baramulti Group (Indonesian coal; listed arm PT Baramulti Suksessarana Tbk, IDX: BSSR)
profile: Jakarta-based widow, about 86, of Athanasius Tossin Suharya (d. 2020), who started the Baramulti group in 1971 as general contractor PT Ensicon Indonesia and moved into coal trading in 1988. Her wealth comes from the family's coal holdings; the group owns 11 coal concessions in Kalimantan and Sumatra. Forbes listed her as a billionaire only in 2023.
interesting_fact: Baramulti grew from a 1971 construction contractor into the owner of 11 coal concessions in Kalimantan and Sumatra; its listed unit BSSR mines near Samarinda, East Kalimantan.
notes: Extremely private: no interviews or public role found. The group's site lists only phone numbers, no email. She dropped off Forbes' list after 2023, and no recent news was found to confirm she is alive (Forbes gave her age as 83 in 2023). Family members such as Daniel Suharya appear on the BSSR board; the company is a better route than her personally.

name: Dai Wenyuan
current_role: Chairman, Executive Director & CEO, 4Paradigm (Beijing Fourth Paradigm Technology, HKEX-listed)
profile: AI researcher-turned-founder who started 4Paradigm in 2014 after serving as chief architect of Baidu's Phoenix Nest ad system and principal scientist at Huawei's Noah's Ark Lab. 4Paradigm sells enterprise machine-learning/AI platforms and is HK-listed; he holds degrees from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and HKUST.
interesting_fact: He is a former ACM-ICPC (international collegiate programming contest) world champion, per 4Paradigm's leadership page, and was named to MIT Technology Review's Innovators Under 35 (China) and Fortune's 40 Under 40.
deep_cut_fact: He is first author of 'Boosting for Transfer Learning' (ICML 2007, with Qiang Yang, Gui-Rong Xue, Yong Yu), which introduced TrAdaBoost, the first boosting-based transfer-learning algorithm and a widely cited classic in the field.
notes: Data-center/AI angle: 4Paradigm builds enterprise AI platforms and compute solutions. Best route is 4Paradigm PR (pr_co@4paradigm.com).

name: Bryan Sheffield
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, Formentera Partners (Austin, TX)
profile: Son of Pioneer Natural Resources CEO Scott Sheffield. In 2008 he founded Parsley Energy on his grandfather's old Midland wells, listed it in 2014 and sold it to Pioneer in 2021 for about $7.6bn including debt. Since 2020 he has run Formentera Partners ($2.8bn+ commitments, about 70,000 boe/d), which is developing Australia's Beetaloo Basin with INPEX.
interesting_fact: Parsley Energy started in 2008 with 109 old wells his grandfather Joe Parsley had drilled around Midland. Bryan had no energy experience, only 'family connections' and a 'trader's taste for risk', per Forbes.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019 he founded the Drop Shot Series, Austin's first professional tennis tournament series, with former world-ranked pro Christo van Rensburg. It grew into the ATX Open, a WTA 250 event and Austin's largest women's pro sporting event. He is also a co-owner of Austin FC.
notes: Good podcast fit: shale plus Australian gas/LNG, with first Beetaloo gas sales in Sept 2026. He speaks at Hart Energy conferences. Firm news goes out via BusinessWire; I found no published press email. The LinkedIn link is the company page, not his own.

name: Liu Fuhai
current_role: Founder/chairman, Shandong Dahai Group (山东大海集团), Dongying (as last reported by Forbes, 2018)
profile: Liu Fuhai (刘福海, b. ~1954) is the self-made founder of Shandong Dahai Group (est. 1988, Guangrao/Dongying, Shandong), a conglomerate spanning textiles, new energy (including PV and copper/energy materials), new materials and trade. Forbes listed him with family at about US$1bn (2017-2018). Hurun listed him 2008-2018.
interesting_fact: Dahai grew into a ~RMB40bn-revenue group by 2017, built on a 'circular economy' model that links textiles with energy and new-materials businesses.

current_role: Founder and majority shareholder of OVO Energy; founder and major shareholder of eVTOL maker Vertical Aerospace (NYSE: EVTL)
profile: Belfast-born ex-City trader who founded OVO Energy in 2009 with £350k of savings; OVO became the UK's fourth-biggest household supplier. He has stepped back from day-to-day running and in 2025 sold the OVO brand to the company for £150M in preference shares. He now backs Vertical Aerospace's electric air taxi.
interesting_fact: He put $50M of his own money into Vertical Aerospace in 2024 to keep its electric air-taxi programme alive. Earlier, in 2015, he bought the collapsed Marussia F1 team out of administration and raced it as Manor.
deep_cut_fact: His first company, founded in 2001 straight after his finance master's at the University of Edinburgh, was The Rental Guide, a property-advertising business, years before OVO.
notes: Good fit for both energy and eVTOL/electrification angles, and he is relatively media-friendly. Vertical's press office is the best route; OVO's press page lists only the general hello@ovoenergy.com. In 2025 he gave up his seat on OVO's holding-company board.

name: Templeton Richard
current_role: Retired former Chairman and CEO, Texas Instruments (retired as executive chairman Dec 31, 2025)
profile: Rich Templeton joined Texas Instruments in 1980 straight out of Union College with an electrical engineering degree and spent 45 years there, becoming CEO in 2004 and chairman in 2008, steering TI's focus on analog and embedded chips and 300mm US fabs. He handed the CEO job to Haviv Ilan in 2023 and retired as executive chairman at end-2025.
interesting_fact: He and his wife Mary, Union College classmates (Class of 1980) who met there, gave the school $51M in 2020, its largest gift ever, creating the Templeton Institute for Engineering and Computer Science, then another $40M in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: The Templetons also gave a 'landmark' $20M gift to SMU's Lyle School of Engineering in 2023, following an earlier $2M endowed chair in electrical engineering and $5M for research.
notes: Input name order reversed (Richard Templeton / 'Rich'). Now retired from TI, so TI media relations may only forward; university partners (Union, SMU) are alternative warm routes. Retirement source: https://investor.ti.com/node/37476/pdf (TI announcement, Oct 2025).

name: Yasuko Uchiyama
current_role: Founding-family shareholder of Lasertec Corp. (TSE: 6920); no executive role found
profile: Uchiyama Yasuko (内山靖子) was a top Lasertec shareholder (4.24% in 2015, 4.44% and #3 in 2020) alongside other Uchiyama family members. Lasertec grew out of the Tokyo ITV Research Institute founded in 1960 by Uchiyama Yasushi (d. 1992) and now dominates EUV mask inspection. She no longer appears in the top-10 list (2025-26). Her exact relationship to the founder is not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Lasertec announced the world's first photomask defect inspection system in 1976 and in 2017 was first to commercialise EUV mask-blank defect inspection; it is described as holding 100% world share in EUV mask inspection, a chokepoint for leading-edge AI chips.
notes: Private individual with no public profile; only appears on Hurun 2022. Shareholder data: https://the-shashi.com/tse/6920/shareholders/ . Only realistic route is Lasertec IR, which is unlikely to forward personal outreach. Consider deprioritising.

name: Fred Mannix
current_role: Chairman/owner, The Mancal Group (Mancal Corporation), Calgary
profile: Frederick Philip Mannix (b. 1942, Calgary), OC, AOE, is the third-generation heir of the Mannix construction and coal dynasty (Loram, Manalta Coal). After the family businesses were split with brother Ron (Coril Holdings), he built the private Mancal Group, active in oil and gas (Mancal Energy), coal, real estate, private capital and ranching; Steve Letwin is CEO.
interesting_fact: At age 12 he was sent by his father to work as a general labourer on a company project in Quebec, and spent later summers as a CAT operator and foreman; in 1998 he and his siblings made what was then the largest single private donation in Canadian history to mark 100 years of Mannix operations.
deep_cut_fact: Troubled by inaccurate media coverage of the 1990s Balkans conflict, he created a 10-day military journalism course at the University of Calgary and Universite de Montreal, saying 'good reporting and strong democracy depend on an informed public.' He also completed National Defence College Course 32 as a civilian in 1979.
notes: Input lists 'Fred and Ron Mannix' jointly; this profile is Fred P. Mannix (Mancal). Brother Ron runs separate Coril Holdings. Very private family. Strong interest in military history, defence/foreign affairs (founder of Canadian Defence and Foreign Affairs Institute) and journalism, a good hook for a journalist. Not to be confused with son Fred Mannix Jr., the polo player.

name: Massimo Moratti
current_role: Former CEO of Saras (sold to Vitol in 2024) and former president/owner of FC Internazionale; private investor
profile: Massimo Moratti (born 16 May 1945, Milan) was a long-time executive and shareholder of Saras, the Sardinian oil refiner his father Angelo founded in 1962. He owned and presided over Inter Milan (1995-2013), winning the 2010 treble. The family sold its remaining 35% of Saras to Vitol in 2024, and he still gives interviews on Inter and Milan life.
interesting_fact: As Inter owner he won the 2010 treble (Serie A, Coppa Italia, Champions League) under José Mourinho, 45 years after his father Angelo's 'Grande Inter' won the European Cup.
deep_cut_fact: At 80 he said his one regret was not running for mayor of Milan: Cardinal Carlo Maria Martini personally urged him to consider it, and he also turned down an approach from Walter Veltroni. He liked the idea of a mayor as 'president of a team: vision and action, day by day.'
notes: Name in input is misspelled 'Moratty'. Saras is now owned by Vitol, so no corporate route remains, and I found no published personal or family-office contact. He is open to press interviews (Italian sports/business outlets); Inter's media office has published his interviews (inter.it). He was hospitalised briefly in 2025; avoid mentioning health.

name: Gao Xuefeng
current_role: Reported head/owner of Jinchengtai (金诚泰) group, Ordos, Inner Mongolia (coal & chemicals), per Hurun; not independently confirmed
profile: Gao Xuefeng (高雪峰, b. ~1958) appears on Hurun China lists (2011-2018) and Hurun Global 2018 as founder/owner of Jinchengtai (金诚泰), an Ordos-based coal and chemicals business (Hurun 2018: RMB6bn). No company website, filings or press coverage could be found to confirm his role or the group's current status.
notes: Hurun API data: 高雪峰, b. 1958, residence Ordos, Inner Mongolia; company 金诚泰 / Jinchengtai, coal & chemicals (2015/2017/2018). Searched Chinese and English for 高雪峰 + 金诚泰 / 鄂尔多斯 / 煤炭 and found nothing. Don't confuse with 准格尔旗金正泰煤炭 (Jinzhengtai, Shandong Energy-owned). Registry sites (Qichacha/Tianyancha), Baidu and Sogou were blocked here. A registry lookup of 金诚泰 entities in Ordos would settle it.

name: Li Wen
current_role: Co-founder, Director, Vice General Manager and Technical Director, Wuxi Autowell Technology (SSE STAR: 688516)
profile: Li Wen (b. c.1969) co-founded Wuxi Autowell in 2010 with chairman Ge Zhiyong; the two are the company's joint actual controllers. Autowell makes high-end automation equipment for the photovoltaic industry (notably solar cell stringers) and has expanded into lithium battery and semiconductor equipment. He remains a director, VP and technical director (term to Sept 2027).
interesting_fact: Autowell is a STAR Market-listed supplier of production equipment to the solar supply chain; Li Wen and Ge Zhiyong are its joint controlling shareholders, putting Li on the Hurun list during the PV equipment boom (2021-2023).
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Autowell he started as an assistant engineer and engineer at the Ministry of Nuclear Industry's Fifth Research and Design Institute, then worked as an engineer at Wuxi Sanbao Industrial and ran Wuxi Tongwei Technology as general manager.
notes: Engineer-founder with very low media profile; name is extremely common, identity tied via Autowell. IR email is from a financial-data page reproducing company filings; verify against Autowell's annual report. Board secretary: Zhou Yongxiu.

name: Peng Jun
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, Pony AI Inc. (Nasdaq: PONY; also Hong Kong-listed)
profile: Peng Jun (James Peng) co-founded robotaxi company Pony.ai in Fremont, California in late 2016 with Lou Tiancheng, after ~7 years at Google and a stint as chief architect of Baidu's autonomous-driving unit. Pony listed on Nasdaq in 2024 (HK in 2025) and runs driverless robotaxis in major Chinese cities, expanding to the Gulf, Singapore and Europe.
interesting_fact: Peng told Fortune (Mar 2026) that Pony had ~1,200 robotaxis on the road targeting 3,000 by year-end, and that one regular rider booked a car right after lunch every day because it was a clean, quiet napping place.
deep_cut_fact: A Tsinghua graduate with an MS from the University at Buffalo and a Stanford engineering PhD, he was one of Baidu's first AI hires in the US, invited by SVP Wang Jing to help start Baidu Research US before becoming its autonomous-driving chief architect in 2015.
notes: Gives English-language interviews (Fortune, CNBC, Bloomberg); a plausible podcast guest on AI/autonomy. Route via Pony.ai IR/communications.

name: Airat Shaimev
current_role: Former co-owner of TAIF Group (Tatarstan); no verified current executive role (TAIF's petrochemical/energy assets were merged into SIBUR in 2021)
profile: Airat Mintimerovich Shaimiev (also spelled Shaimev) is a son of Tatarstan's first president, Mintimer Shaimiev, and was a major shareholder of TAIF, the Kazan-based petrochemicals, refining and power group. In 2021 TAIF's shareholders swapped control of its petrochemical and energy businesses for 15% of SIBUR; TAIF JSC was renamed Sibur-RT in 2022.
interesting_fact: The 2021 TAIF-SIBUR merger created one of the world's largest petrochemical companies, with TAIF's owners receiving a 15% stake in SIBUR.
notes: Subject to sanctions (UK FCDO, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Ukraine) per OpenSanctions: https://www.opensanctions.org/entities/Q110608262/. Only on Hurun Global in 2014. Outreach not advisable without legal review; no public contact channels found.

name: Zhang Xun
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2021-22) with Zhang Yong (章勇) as holding wealth through Shanghai Fudan Microelectronics (688385.SS / 1385.HK), a chip designer. Filings show Zhang Yong indirectly held about 9% of Fudan Micro via Shanghai Zhengben and Shanghai Nianjin. I found no public profile or filing that names Zhang Xun (章训), so his role is unclear.
notes: Identity not confirmed; Zhang Xun is probably a relative or associate of Zhang Yong, the Fudan Micro shareholder. That stake fell below 5% by Sept 2024 through sales and judicial disposals, and the Shanghai Stock Exchange censured Zhang Yong in 2023 over nominee-holding disclosures. Not an officer of Fudan Micro. Low priority; I don't recommend outreach.

name: Vinod Kumar Agarwal
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Agarwal Coal Corporation Pvt. Ltd. (Indore); Chairman, Emerald Developers
profile: Indore-based Vinod Agarwal built Agarwal Coal Group from a family coal-transport business into one of India's largest coal importers (15M+ tonnes a year). It has operations in India, South Africa, Singapore, Nepal and Indonesia and turnover of about ₹15,000 crore. He is diversifying into renewables (50+ MW of wind and solar commissioned) and real estate through Emerald Developers.
interesting_fact: He began running the family coal business at just 15. He was born in Rohtak, Haryana, and raised in Indore, and the IFL Hurun India Rich List 2025 ranked him the richest person in Madhya Pradesh.
deep_cut_fact: Agarwal Coal built its own in-house digital analytics platform, 'Manthan', for real-time market intelligence from procurement to sales. The group aims to grow its solar portfolio to 100-150 MW.
notes: Sometimes spelled Agrawal. He founded the Balaji Sewarth Vinod Agarwal Foundation (2010), and csr@ is its contact. Coal-to-renewables transition is a natural podcast angle. Company site memorialises his late wife (d. Jan 2026), so be sensitive with timing and tone.

name: Sudhir Seth
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Sudhir Group / Sudhir Power Ltd (Gurugram, India)
profile: Sudhir Seth is a first-generation Indian industrialist who founded Sudhir Power in 1973. It is a Gurugram-based maker of Cummins-powered silent diesel gensets, with arms in power distribution, rentals and tools and equipment. His son Rahul Seth runs the business as managing director. Hurun listed him at about $1B in 2026.
interesting_fact: Sudhir Group has a roughly 40-year association with Cummins, plus 15-year and 7-year alliances with Schneider and JLG, and calls itself India's leading maker of silent gensets. These are the backup-power sets used by Indian data centres, hospitals and offices.
notes: Private company with little personal press coverage. Hurun India profiled him in its interview series (hurunindia.com/interviews). The best route is probably via MD Rahul Seth or the company's general inbox. Founding year (1973) comes from data-aggregator profiles.

name: Kenneth Irving
current_role: Private investor/philanthropist; former CEO of Irving Oil (left 2010); no current executive role found
profile: Eldest son of the late Arthur Irving and grandson of industrialist K.C. Irving, Kenneth Irving ran Irving Oil - owner of Canada's largest refinery in Saint John, N.B. - in the 2000s before leaving in 2010. Since then he has kept a low profile, spending much of his time in Maine and supporting clean-water causes; Hurun lists his wealth at ~$1B.
interesting_fact: He was put in charge of Irving Oil around 2000 as the third generation of the K.C. Irving dynasty, and was succeeded in 2010 by Mike Ashar, a Mumbai-born chemical engineer and ex-Suncor executive.
deep_cut_fact: After attending a 2012 Lake Ontario Waterkeeper gala, he donated his ~$2M, 19-hectare Kennebecasis River home in Saint John to Waterkeepers Canada for a national water centre for 'swimmable, drinkable, fishable water'; he says he finds peace in the wilderness, usually on water.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contact found, and he is no longer affiliated with Irving Oil (avoid routing via the company). Sensitive: his 2010 exit followed a well-publicised family rift - do not raise. Clean-water philanthropy (Waterkeeper) is the warmest angle.

name: Emily Irving
profile: Listed with Irving Oil as the source of wealth, so presumably a member of the Arthur Irving branch of New Brunswick's Irving family, which owns Irving Oil (Canada's largest refinery, in Saint John). Searches found no public role, interview or biography. Irving Oil's leadership pages do not list her.
notes: Very private with almost no public footprint. A family-member list on Wikipedia includes an 'Emily Irving' under Arthur Irving's branch, but the entry is unsourced ('citation needed'). If outreach is wanted, Irving Oil's corporate communications is the only plausible route, and it is not her own channel.

name: Jennifer Irving
current_role: Irving Oil family shareholder (no public executive role found)
profile: Jennifer Irving is a daughter of the late Arthur L. Irving (d. May 2024), longtime head of Saint John-based Irving Oil, which runs Canada's largest oil refinery. She appears on the Hurun list via the family's Irving Oil stake; no public business or board role for her could be found. In 2025 Irving Oil said it would remain privately owned.
interesting_fact: Irving Oil, the family business behind her wealth, operates Canada's largest oil refinery in Saint John, New Brunswick.
notes: Very private; named only as one of Arthur Irving's children (from his first marriage to Joan Carlisle) in obituary coverage. Identity marked uncertain because no source ties her individually to the Hurun figure. Contact form is Irving Oil corporate, not personal. Her half-sister Sarah Irving is the public-facing family member at Irving Oil.

name: Sarah Irving
current_role: Director, Arthur and Sandra Irving Foundation; advisory board member, Dartmouth's Arthur L. Irving Institute for Energy and Society (former EVP & Chief Brand Officer, Irving Oil)
profile: Granddaughter of K.C. Irving and daughter and heir of the late Irving Oil chairman Arthur Irving. Dartmouth '10 and Tuck MBA, ex-Deloitte strategy consultant in New York, she was EVP and Chief Brand Officer of Saint John-based Irving Oil (owner of Canada's largest refinery) until 2023. Now a biotech investor and philanthropist based in Saint John.
interesting_fact: She was long seen as heir apparent at Irving Oil, the private refiner behind Canada's largest oil refinery in Saint John, before stepping off the executive team in 2023 during a strategic review of the company.
deep_cut_fact: She sits on the advisory board of Dartmouth's Arthur L. Irving Institute for Energy and Society (named for her father) and describes herself as an early investor in biotech, also advising Mass General Brigham's Cancer Institute Advisory Council.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contact found. Best route may be via the Irving Institute for Energy & Society at Dartmouth or Irving Oil corporate communications. Her listed country is blank in input; she is Canadian (Saint John, NB).

name: Yu Faxin
current_role: Actual controller of Zhejiang Zhenlei Technology (浙江臻镭科技, 'Great Microwave', STAR 688270); professor, Zhejiang University School of Aeronautics and Astronautics
profile: Yu Faxin (郁发新), a Zhejiang University aerospace-electronics professor since 2006, turned chip entrepreneur. He controls Great Microwave (Zhenlei Tech), maker of RF, phased-array and power-management chips mainly for defence communications and radar, listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022. Hurun Global 2026 put him at about $1B.
interesting_fact: He controlled about 43.5% of Great Microwave at its 2021-22 STAR Market IPO, and an earlier chip venture he backed, Chengchang Technology, also went public separately (Shenzhen, 2022).
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 Zhejiang University transferred an analog phased-array T/R chipset design developed by an 8-person team led by Yu to the startup Chengchang; he was the key inventor, receiving about 70% of the inventors' share of the fee, which was converted into equity.
notes: Academic-turned-founder in defence RF chips; no personal public channels. Company shares were tagged 'ST' (special treatment) in 2026 after an SSE public censure over disclosures; avoid as topic. Route via IR mailbox (board secretary).

name: Lucy Gou
current_role: Founder, Passes (creator monetization platform); founder, Backend Capital
profile: Lucy Guo (usual spelling) dropped out of Carnegie Mellon as a Thiel Fellow, designed at Snapchat, then co-founded data-labeling firm Scale AI with Alexandr Wang in 2016, leaving in 2018 but keeping her stake. Meta's 2025 $14.3B investment valuing Scale at $29B+ made her a billionaire; she now runs creator platform Passes and seed fund Backend Capital.
interesting_fact: In April 2025 she displaced Taylor Swift as the world's youngest self-made woman billionaire (a title that passed to Kalshi's Luana Lopes Lara in late 2025).
deep_cut_fact: She taught herself to code as a teenager by writing bots for the online game Neopets and selling the in-game assets for real money; later she was Snapchat's first female designer and helped build Snap Map.
notes: Input spells her name 'Gou'; she is Lucy Guo. Her wealth is from Scale AI but she no longer works there; Scale press would not represent her. Passes and Guo are subject to pending litigation and recent tabloid coverage; vet before outreach. Active on social media but handles not verified here.

name: Jony Ive
current_role: Founder, LoveFrom (with Marc Newson); leads design across OpenAI after OpenAI acquired his device startup io (2025)
profile: British-American designer (b. 1967, Chingford) who as Apple's design chief shaped the iMac, iPod, iPhone and iPad before leaving in 2019 to found LoveFrom in San Francisco. In 2025 OpenAI bought his AI-hardware startup io for ~$6.5B in stock, with Ive and LoveFrom taking creative responsibility across OpenAI; LoveFrom also designed Ferrari's first EV, the Luce (2026).
interesting_fact: LoveFrom became the first non-Italian company to design a Ferrari production car - the all-electric Ferrari Luce, unveiled in May 2026 after five years of work.
deep_cut_fact: As an industrial-design student at Newcastle Polytechnic his designs, including a telephone and a hearing aid, were shown at London's Design Museum; winning the RSA Student Design Award in 1988 and 1989 paid for the trip to San Francisco where he met Robert Brunner, his future route into Apple.
notes: Famously private and rarely gives interviews; no personal social accounts. LoveFrom publishes no press email; the practical route is OpenAI's communications team or LoveFrom via its website. Fit is AI hardware/design rather than energy. Fun aside: LoveFrom's bear mascot 'Montgomery' is named after Montgomery Street, SF.

name: Farukbhai Gulambhai Patel
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, KP Group (KPI Green Energy, KP Energy, KP Green Engineering), Surat, Gujarat
profile: Dr. Faruk G. Patel founded KP Group in Surat in 1994 as a small logistics and construction venture and built it into a renewables conglomerate (solar, wind, hybrid, BESS, green hydrogen) with a 10.6+ GW portfolio. Listed arms include KPI Green Energy and KP Energy; his 'KP 3.0' plan targets 10 GW owned capacity, 10 GW EPC and 10 GWh storage.
interesting_fact: In late Sept 2026 KPI Green signed a binding offer to buy 100% of Saudi Alfanar Group's Indian wind subsidiaries, part of a push into BESS, floating solar, offshore and green hydrogen.
deep_cut_fact: Before renewables he is credited with the 'one tower, multiple networks' telecom-tower sharing idea, and KP was the first to install wind turbines in South Gujarat after three years of research; his group is also building what it calls the world's first old-age home for differently-abled people.
notes: Very media-friendly: personal website, published biography book ('Urja No Ujaas'), Josh Talks and IIM Ahmedabad lectures. Best route: contact form on farukpatel.com or KP Group media (kpgroup.co/media-kit). Strong energy/storage fit.

name: Mira Murati
current_role: Founder and CEO, Thinking Machines Lab
profile: Albanian-born engineer (Colby BA, Dartmouth BEng) who worked on Tesla's Model X and at Leap Motion before joining OpenAI in 2018, rising to CTO and briefly interim CEO in Nov 2023. Left in 2024 and launched Thinking Machines Lab in Feb 2025 with a record ~$2B seed round; its first product, Tinker, lets users fine-tune frontier models.
interesting_fact: Thinking Machines Lab's governance gives Murati a weighted, deciding board vote, an unusual degree of founder control for a lab that raised one of the largest seed rounds in history.
deep_cut_fact: Under her full name, Ermira Murati, she wrote 'Language & Coding Creativity' for the Spring 2022 issue of Daedalus (American Academy of Arts & Sciences), on how NLP engines like GPT-3 change how humans relate to machines.
notes: High-profile and media-selective. No published press email found for Thinking Machines; company X/LinkedIn are the official channels. Born in Vlore, Albania; Albania's government invested $10M in her lab.

name: Pradeep Garg
current_role: Chairman, Kundan Group (gold refining, bullion, minting, mining, Kundan Green Energy), India
profile: Dr. Pradeep Garg chairs the Kundan Group, which grew from a single enterprise founded in 1971 into a diversified group running what it calls India's largest private gold refinery, bullion trading, minting and mining. Its Kundan Green Energy arm has about 350 MW of commissioned hydro, solar and waste-to-energy capacity; Udit and Vidit Garg also sit on the board.
interesting_fact: Beyond gold, the group's Kundan Green Energy has commissioned about 355 MW, mostly hydro (~293 MW) plus ~40 MW solar and waste-to-energy, an energy angle for the podcast.
notes: Group site lists a general email truncated as 'info@kundangroup' (no domain), so not recorded; use the contact page or the group's Delhi switchboard listed there. Director Udit Garg is the public face of Kundan Green Energy in media. Web search budget ran out before deep-cut research.

name: Shahril
current_role: Tan Sri Shahril Shamsuddin, key figure of the family-controlled Sapura Group (Malaysia); retired as President & Group CEO of Sapura Energy in March 2021
profile: Shahril Shamsuddin built Sapura Energy (formerly SapuraKencana, now renamed Vantris Energy) into one of Malaysia's largest offshore oil-and-gas service and drilling groups, and led the wider family conglomerate Sapura Group (energy, engineering, aviation, defence, property). He retired as Sapura Energy's group CEO in March 2021, handing over to Anuar Taib.
interesting_fact: Sapura was founded in 1975 by his father Abdul Kadir Shamsuddin with six staff in a one-room office (starting with telecoms firm Uniphone Works) and was named after Abdul Kadir's wife, Siti Sapura.
notes: Input name is only 'Shahril'; matched to Tan Sri Shahril Shamsuddin via 'Sapura Group'. Last on Hurun in 2014-15; wealth likely much lower now. Avoid Sapura Energy's 2022-24 debt restructuring as a topic. No current published contact found (sapura.com.my pages returned 404). Alive: no report of death found, but not positively confirmed.

name: Peter Smedvig
current_role: Third-generation owner of the Smedvig family business (Smedvig Family Office, Stavanger/London); co-founder of Smedvig Capital (no longer on its listed team)
profile: Peter Thomas Smedvig (b. 1946, Stavanger) is the grandson of Peder Smedvig, who founded the family shipping business in 1915. He took Smedvig ASA into offshore drilling (listed Oslo 1990, NYSE 1996), exited shipping (1996) and drilling (2006), and built the Smedvig Family Office (~US$2.4bn AUM), now owned by the 4th generation.
interesting_fact: In 1996, the same year the family exited shipping, he and Johnny Hewett founded Smedvig Capital in London - one of the early family-office private-equity/venture arms; it still invests in founders via Smedvig Ventures.
deep_cut_fact: He studied in England before Wharton: a bachelor's from Newcastle University (1970) and an MBA from the Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania (1972).
notes: Now ~80 and appears retired from day-to-day roles; the family office says the 4th generation owns it, and the family's philanthropy runs through North Star (founded 2019). Best route is the Smedvig family office general inbox. 'Alive' based on Wikipedia/Wikidata listing him as living; no recent public appearances found.

name: Robert Coyiuto Jr.
current_role: Chairman, Prudential Guarantee and Assurance (PGA); Vice-Chairman, National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP)
profile: Filipino businessman who chairs PGA, one of the Philippines' largest non-life insurers founded by his late father, and is a major shareholder and vice-chairman of NGCP, the private operator of the national power grid, via listed Synergy Grid & Development (SGP). He also holds a stake in Oriental Petroleum & Minerals and runs luxury-car distributor PGA Cars.
interesting_fact: He founded PGA Cars in 1996, the sole Philippine distributor of Audi, Porsche, Lamborghini and Bentley; in 2021 he raised his holding in Synergy Grid via a share swap with his investment firm Pacifica21.
deep_cut_fact: His Coyiuto Foundation set up a biennial literary award in 2014 dedicated to authors of biographies and autobiographies, a rare niche prize in Philippine letters.
notes: Very private; no personal accounts found. Synergy Grid site lists only a corporate office address (Pasig City), no email. NGCP is the grid angle for an energy podcast; NGCP site blocked automated access. Web-search budget ran out mid-lane, so contacts are thin.

name: Gim Seong-gon
current_role: Chairman of the Board and President, CS Wind Corp. (KRX: 112610), Seoul (board term to March 2027)
profile: Korean founder of CS Wind, the world's largest maker of wind-turbine towers. Grew up poor, took a construction job in Saudi Arabia for higher pay, started his own building-materials business there in 1984, and pivoted the company to wind towers in 2003. Goldman Sachs invested ~$40M in 2008; CS Wind now runs plants across Asia, Europe and the US, with day-to-day CEOs under him.
interesting_fact: CS Wind's factory in Pueblo, Colorado, bought from Vestas in 2021, is the world's largest wind-turbine tower plant - a US bet Bloomberg called 'lucky' after the Inflation Reduction Act.
deep_cut_fact: Before making wind towers, his company built industrial chimneys for fossil-fuel power plants; it only switched to wind-turbine towers in 2003, applying the same tall-steel-structure know-how to renewables.
notes: Romanised also as Kim Seong-kwon (김성권); don't confuse with the SNU nephrologist of same Korean name. Operations run by CEOs Bang Seong-hun and Hwang Kyoo-deuk. Avoid the Forbes company-name fact in outreach (it concerns his son).

name: Edward Screven
current_role: Retired (Feb 2025) EVP and Chief Corporate Architect, Oracle; was Oracle's representative on the board of Ampere Computing (acquired by SoftBank in 2025)
profile: Carnegie Mellon computer-science graduate who joined Oracle in 1986 and spent 38+ years there, ending as chief corporate architect steering technology and architecture decisions. His wealth is Oracle stock; Oracle's AI/cloud-infrastructure surge made him a billionaire in 2025. He oversaw open-source programs including Java, Oracle Linux, MySQL and VirtualBox, and represented Oracle on Ampere's board.
interesting_fact: Forbes counted him as one of two new billionaires minted by Oracle's AI-fueled stock surge in September 2025, months after he had retired from the company.
deep_cut_fact: He was responsible for many of Oracle's best-known open-source programs, including Java, Oracle Linux, MySQL and VirtualBox, an unusual brief for an executive at a company long known for proprietary database software.
notes: Low public profile; retired, no personal site or social accounts found and no Oracle route now that he has left. Forbes profile URL now returns 404 (he appears as 'former' billionaire). Ampere/Arm data-center CPU angle is the best hook. Shared search quota ran out, so contact research was limited.

name: Ramachandra Galla
current_role: Founder Chairman, Amara Raja Group (Amara Raja Energy & Mobility; son Jayadev Galla is chairman & MD of the listed company)
profile: After 18 years as an engineering consultant in the US, Ramachandra N. Galla returned to Andhra Pradesh and founded Amara Raja (1984-85), now India's No. 2 lead-acid battery maker (Amaron, PowerZone) that also builds lithium-ion cells and packs in Telangana. In his late 80s, he is founder chairman while his son runs the group.
