As CTO he leads Pony's L4 robotaxi technology.
interesting_fact: Pony.ai launched what it called China's first public robotaxi service in Nansha, Guangzhou on 2 Feb 2018 after a months-long sprint; Lou was said to work about 100 hours a week during that push.
deep_cut_fact: Invited as a guest speaker to the East Asian round of the Topcoder Open in Sept 2020, he gave his talk to 100+ young contestants and then, without telling anyone, entered the contest himself half an hour later.
notes: Engineer-first, gives occasional technical interviews (e.g. PonyWorld 2.0 with Autonomous Vehicle International). Quote: 'The only things truly in your control are focus and hard work.' Route via Pony.ai IR/comms.

name: Steve Sanghi
current_role: President, CEO and Chair of the Board, Microchip Technology (NASDAQ: MCHP); director of Intel and Impinj
profile: Indian-born engineer (b. 1955) who left Intel for Waferscale Integration, then joined near-bankrupt Microchip in 1990 and ran it as CEO 1991-2021, building it into a major microcontroller/analog maker. He returned as CEO in Nov 2024, was made permanent in July 2025 and is leading the turnaround; he joined Intel's board in Dec 2024.
interesting_fact: Northern Arizona University renamed its engineering college the Steve Sanghi College of Engineering in Oct 2024, and in 2026 named the Maria and Steve Sanghi College of Nursing.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote a business-advice column for the Arizona Republic, collected as the book 'Ask Steve' (Oct 2024), after his 2023 memoir 'Up and to the Right'. He holds a 1975 electronics degree from Punjab Engineering College and an MS from UMass Amherst.

public_contacts.value: Investor relations: Sajid Daudi, Head of IR, (480) 792-7385 (no email published)

notes: Publicly engaged author/columnist; his books and the NAU colleges are good hooks. Microchip IR (Sajid Daudi) or corporate communications is the formal route. The ir_email entry is a phone line because no IR email is published.

name: Xu Xinjian
current_role: Chairman, Solareast Holdings (日出东方, 603366.SS) and its controlling shareholder Sunrain Holding Group (太阳雨控股集团)
profile: Founder of the Sunrain (太阳雨) and Micoe (四季沐歌) brands. He built Solareast, based in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, from a small workshop into one of China's largest solar water-heater makers. It is listed in Shanghai, also owns the kitchen-appliance brand Sacon (帅康), and has been moving into air-source heat pumps and other low-carbon heating.
interesting_fact: His solar-thermal company grew from a small workshop in Lianyungang into a leader of China's solar water-heater industry, the world's largest. Its brands Sunrain and Micoe became household names.
deep_cut_fact: On 16 August 2023 he gave the welcome speech at the ground-breaking of Micoe's 'heat-pump zero-carbon laboratory building' at the group's Lianyungang HQ. It is a whole building dedicated to air-source heat-pump R&D, part of his push to move the solar-heater group into heat pumps.
notes: Both IR emails come from the 2025 annual report summary (April 2026): one is the board secretary's (Liu Chidao), the other the securities representative's (Cao Jing). Born 1964 and a Peking University Guanghua alumnus, per a brand-directory site I could not confirm. Low media profile. Good fit for the energy-transition / heat-pump angle.

name: Zhao Kui
current_role: Vice Chairman and director, Erdos Group (鄂尔多斯集团), Inner Mongolia (as of 2023; current status unverified)
profile: Zhao Kui (赵魁, b. 1960) is a long-serving vice chairman of Inner Mongolia's Erdos Group, the cashmere-to-coal, ferroalloy, chemicals and power conglomerate led by Wang Linxiang. Its listed arm, Erdos Resources (600295/900936), reported revenue of 25.7B yuan in 2025. Hurun ranked him among Inner Mongolia's richest: 7.8B yuan in 2021 and 6.1B yuan in 2023.
interesting_fact: A finance professional rather than a founder, he holds an economics degree and is a certified senior accountant. Erdos Group, best known for cashmere, now also produces coal, ferrosilicon, PVC and cement.
notes: Very low public profile; his bio comes from Hurun-derived aggregators. He drops off Hurun lists after 2023, and he is not on the listed company's 2026 board or executive list, so his current role is unclear. The emails belong to Erdos Resources' board secretary (Guo Sheng) and securities representative, as published in the 2025 annual report. They are a group-level route only, not personal contacts for Zhao.

name: Luo Huabing
current_role: Director and one of the seven joint actual controllers, Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics (600460.SH)
profile: Luo Huabing (罗华兵) is one of seven co-founders of Silan Microelectronics, a Hangzhou-based chip designer and maker of power semiconductors (IGBT, MOSFET, SiC, IPM). The seven, led by chairman Chen Xiangdong, are jointly the company's actual controllers. He remained a director as of 2025 filings.
interesting_fact: Silan has become one of China's fastest-moving silicon-carbide players. It started a SiC power-device line in 2022 and by 2024 had capacity above 5,000 wafers a month, serving the EV, solar/storage and industrial markets.
deep_cut_fact: In 1997 Luo was one of six colleagues who joined Chen Xiangdong, then a senior executive at Huayue Microelectronics, in founding Hangzhou Silan Electronics, the forerunner of today's Silan Microelectronics.
notes: Low public profile, and almost all coverage focuses on chairman Chen Xiangdong. His June 2025 share-reduction filing confirms he is still a director. Formal route: the Silan board secretary / IR office.

name: Marianne Odfjell
current_role: Private investor; chair of Ask Invest AS and director of Odfjell Invest / Odfjell Capital (per insider-profile listings)
profile: Norwegian heiress (b. c.1970), London-based, who received ~30% of offshore driller Odfjell Drilling in 2007 when her father Abraham Odfjell passed his shares to her and her sister Helene (70%). She sat on Odfjell Drilling's board 2010-2013 and in 2013 announced plans to sell her stake for about $500m ahead of the company's Oslo listing; she now invests privately.
interesting_fact: In 2007, after the share transfer, she was Norway's fourth-richest woman while her sister Helene was the richest; the family fortune was originally built on Odfjell tankers before the move into offshore drilling.
notes: Very private; no public contact, website or social accounts found. Not currently an executive of Odfjell Drilling (sister Helene is the active family figure there). Role listings come from MarketScreener insider pages (could not be fetched to verify).

name: The Jatania brothers
current_role: Family investors (UK); Danny Jatania's Jatania Group invests in SMEs, public equities and commercial property
profile: Four London-based brothers (Mike, George, Vin, Danny) built Lornamead, an acquisition-led personal-care group (est. 1978) owning brands like Yardley and Harmony Hairspray; it joined Hong Kong's Fung group in Dec 2012. The family now invests via Jatania Group (Jersey) in SMEs, public equities and commercial property.
interesting_fact: Lornamead's strategy was to buy established, sometimes neglected brands; its best-known deal was acquiring the 18th-century British perfumer Yardley. Mike Jatania said Lornamead wanted to build a significant personal-care business through strategic acquisitions.
notes: This is a group entry for four brothers. Jatania Group's site describes it as founded by Danny Jatania and is the only official contact route found. The family is low-profile, and recent Sunday Times Rich Lists show their wealth as flat. Lornamead's sale date comes from lornamead.com.

name: Lu Yonghua
current_role: Actual controller (largest shareholder) of Jiangsu Linyang Energy; stepped down as chairman June 2025
profile: Lu Yonghua (陆永华) built Qidong-based Jiangsu Linyang Energy (SSE: 601222), founded in 1995 as a maker of smart electricity meters for State Grid and China Southern Power Grid. From 2015 he pushed it into solar plant development, PV modules and energy storage. He left the chair in June 2025 but still controls ~39% of the company.
interesting_fact: Under Lu, Linyang evolved from a smart-meter supplier into a solar-farm developer and energy-storage maker; in H1 2026 revenue rose 82% as it sold down PV plants in a shift to an asset-light model.
notes: Now semi-retired; Yin Biao is chairman since June 2025. The IR email is the company board secretary's office (Cui Dongxu), not personal. Chinese-language outreach advised. Forbes shares listing with Mao Caihong.

name: Mao Caihong
current_role: No public executive role found; linked to Jiangsu Linyang Energy (SSE: 601222) alongside controlling shareholder Lu Yonghua
profile: Hurun lists her wealth jointly with Lu Yonghua, chairman/GM and ultimate controller of Jiangsu Linyang Energy (Qidong, Jiangsu), a maker of smart meters, solar power plants and energy storage. Linyang's 2023 annual report names 'Lu Yonghua, Mao Caihong' as joint guarantors of company borrowings, confirming her connection to the company; no other public profile found.
interesting_fact: Linyang Energy is controlled via Qidong Huahong Electronics (90% owned by Lu Yonghua), which held 34.72% of the listed company at end-2023.
notes: Extremely low profile; nature of relationship to Lu Yonghua not stated in sources found (do not assume). Any outreach would go through Linyang's board office (dsh@linyang.com.cn, board secretary Cui Dongxu per 2023 annual report). Lu Yonghua was placed under a supervisory-commission detention in Feb 2021 (NBD report) - sensitive.

name: Liu Manshi
current_role: Founder, chairman and president of Manshi Group (满世投资集团 / Inner Mongolia Manshi Coal Group), Ordos, Inner Mongolia
profile: Liu Manshi (刘满世, b. 1949) is from Zhunge'er Banner, Ordos. He co-founded Manshi Group in the early 1990s; it runs 8 large coal mines producing 25m+ t/yr of low-ash, low-sulphur thermal coal, plus a coal-logistics network, mine-mouth power and overseas projects. Hurun ranked him 9th-richest in Ordos in 2021 (RMB4.1bn).
interesting_fact: The group carries his given name - 'Manshi' (满世) - and its vision slogan '誉满全球 盛世百年' ('fame across the world, a century of prosperity') works both characters in; it ranked 483rd among China's top 500 private firms in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: Manshi took coal abroad under Belt and Road: a 55%-owned open-pit coal mine in Gunung Mas, Central Kalimantan, Indonesia (103.72 km2 concession, ~61.6m t first-phase reserves), with a washery, power plant and barge port, alongside a 2x660MW mine-mouth plant at its Guanzigou mine.
notes: Unlisted private group; no published office/press email or official site verified. Group says it has spent nearly RMB300m on poverty relief and education donations. Identity linked via company profile ('founded by entrepreneur Liu Manshi and others') and Hurun 2021 Ordos list (https://m.maigoo.com/top/420440.html).

name: Hu Liqiang
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Shanghai Bright Power Semiconductor (STAR Market: 688368)
profile: Born 1976, Hu is a chip designer who worked at ON Semiconductor's Shanghai design center and China Resources Siwei before founding Bright Power Semiconductor in Shanghai in 2008. The fabless firm began with LED-lighting driver chips and now sells AC/DC, DC/DC, motor-control and HPC power chips; he is its controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Bright Power has moved from LED lighting drivers into power-management chips for servers, base stations and high-performance computing, a domestic-substitution play in China's AI/data-center supply chain.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was as an assistant engineer at the 704 Research Institute of China Shipbuilding Industry Corp (marine machinery and power systems) before he moved into IC design; he has been named a Shanghai 'Leading Talent' and won the 8th Shanghai Tech Entrepreneur Innovation Award.
notes: Low-profile engineer-founder; route via IR (board secretary Yang Biao). Chinese-language outreach advisable. Relevant angle: Chinese power-management chips for servers/HPC.

name: Liu Jieqian
current_role: Listed by Hurun as co-owner (with Hu Liqiang) of Shanghai Bright Power Semiconductor (晶丰明源, STAR 688368); exact current title not verified
profile: Liu Jieqian (刘洁茜) appears on Hurun China lists 2020-2026 sharing a fortune with Hu Liqiang, chairman and founder of Bright Power Semiconductor. Founded in Shanghai in 2008, Bright Power designs power-management and motor-control chips (AC/DC, DC/DC, LED drivers) and now sells multiphase controllers and fan/pump solutions for AI servers.
interesting_fact: Bright Power started as an LED-lighting driver-chip maker and shipped 7B+ chips in 2021; it now pitches 48V server fan and liquid-cooling pump solutions for AI servers and multiphase digital controllers for high-performance computing.
notes: Very low public profile; I couldn't confirm her role at the company from an official page (company site doesn't name her) and my web-search quota ran out. Hu Liqiang is the public face - route via the IR mailbox. Data-center angle: server power/cooling chips.

name: Ye Huaneng
current_role: Actual controller of Guangdong Baolihua New Energy (宝新能源, SZSE 000690) via parent Guangdong Baolihua Group, which he founded and controls (~90%)
profile: Ye Huaneng (叶华能), from Meixian, Guangdong, left his mountain village in 1972 at 20, made his first money in construction and founded Baolihua Group (1993). Its listed arm (IPO 1997) moved from building/property into power: coal-gangue CFB plants at Meixian Heshuyuan and the Lufeng Jiahu Bay clean-energy base, plus wind. Chairman of the listed company is now Zou Jinkai.
interesting_fact: Baolihua's businesses once ranged from power plants to a men's fashion label ('Shenlang'), a 20% stake in the Meizhou-Shantou expressway and the Yannanfei Tea Field resort in Meixian.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he farmed after high school and worked as a 'minban' (community-funded) teacher in his home village of Changjiao, an old revolutionary-base village in Meixian; he later invested RMB180m to build the Yannanfei Tea Field resort near home.
notes: Not an officer of the listed company; reach via its board-secretary office (Meixian HQ / Guangzhou office). Be aware: in Jan 2026 the Guangdong CSRC bureau fined him over undisclosed nominee holdings and share sales and SZSE publicly reprimanded him (per 2026 interim report) - avoid in outreach.

name: Xu Chen
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, SmartSens Technology (思特威, SSE STAR: 688213)
profile: Xu Chen (徐辰, 'Dr. Richard Xu') is a CMOS image-sensor engineer (Tsinghua BEng; HKUST MPhil/PhD) who founded Shanghai-based SmartSens in 2011. The company has led security-camera image-sensor shipments for years and expanded into automotive, machine vision and smartphones; it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in May 2022.
interesting_fact: SmartSens says it has led the security/surveillance image-sensor market by share eight years running and holds 550+ granted patents; Xu was named a 2025 Forbes China Best CEO.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019 SmartSens became the first Chinese company in the image-sensor field selected for ISSCC (the 'chip Olympics'), presenting the opening paper of the conference's image-sensor session.
notes: Uses the English name Richard Xu. The published 'Marketing and Media' address is the company media/BD contact, not a personal one. Academic background is in CMOS image sensors and high-speed optical receivers.

name: Wen Zhenlin
current_role: Chairman, co-founder and co-controlling shareholder, Jiangsu X-chip Semiconductor Technology (展芯股份, SZSE ChiNext 301707), Nanjing
profile: Wen Zhenlin (温振霖, b. 1981), a Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics power-electronics master's graduate, spent 2009-2018 as an engineer at CETC's 14th Research Institute, then co-founded X-chip in 2018. It designs high-reliability analog/power-management chips and micro-modules for defense/aerospace import substitution; it listed on ChiNext on 7 Aug 2026.
interesting_fact: X-chip's IPO (Aug 2026) sold 41.12m shares at RMB23.45, raising about RMB964m. Pre-IPO, Wen and co-founder Xu Ligang together controlled 54.77% of votes; Wen also held 7.35% directly.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding X-chip he designed power-supply systems for national key radar/weapons programmes at CETC's 14th Institute (the Nanjing radar institute); the prospectus credits that experience with the firm's 'self-defined forward design' approach rather than pin-for-pin copies of imported chips.
notes: Newly listed 2026; shares the Hurun entry with his wife Yu Zhengjing (the prospectus names her as his spouse and concert party). Co-controller Xu Ligang (徐立刚) is general manager. Best route is the company securities department (contact person Zhu Dawei) via ir@semitech.cc.

name: Yu Zhengjing
current_role: Head of the General Affairs and Marketing departments (core employee), Jiangsu X-chip Semiconductor Technology (展芯股份, 301707); concert party of the controlling shareholders
profile: Yu Zhengjing (余正晶, b. 1985) is the wife of X-chip chairman Wen Zhenlin and, per the IPO prospectus, acting-in-concert party of co-controllers Wen and Xu Ligang. She works at the company as head of its general affairs and marketing departments. X-chip, founded in Nanjing in 2018, makes high-reliability analog/power chips for defense and listed on ChiNext in Aug 2026.
interesting_fact: The Hurun 2026 entry is shared with her husband; X-chip raised about RMB964m in its August 2026 ChiNext IPO at RMB23.45 a share.
deep_cut_fact: She is listed among X-chip's 'core employees' in the IPO prospectus, running both its general-affairs (综合部) and marketing (市场部) departments, not just a passive family shareholder.
notes: Low public profile; almost no press. Approach via the company securities department / her husband.

name: Luo Xingshun
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Suzhou UIGreen Micro&Nano Technologies (和林微纳, STAR Market 688661)
profile: Luo Xingshun (骆兴顺, b. 1974, Huai'an, Jiangsu) built the Suzhou precision-parts business that became UIGreen (est. 2012), maker of micro-precision MEMS parts and semiconductor chip-test probes (memory, AI, CPU/GPU) plus EV and medical parts. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021; AI test demand put him on Hurun's 2026 list.
interesting_fact: UIGreen's micro-precision probes and parts are used in semiconductor chip testing for memory, AI and CPU/GPU chips, and the company has set up market teams in the US, Japan, Singapore and Southeast Asia.
deep_cut_fact: He came up through procurement, not engineering: purchasing manager at Knowles Electronics (Suzhou) 2004-06 and briefly purchasing director at Guangzhou audio maker Diffeni (广州市迪芬尼音响) in 2006, before running Helin Precision from 2007; he later did an EMBA at HKUST (2012-14).
notes: Hurun 'Harmonics' = 和林微纳 (UIGreen). Low profile, Chinese-language only. Contacts come from the company's exchange-registered profile (Eastmoney F10 data); IR email is the securities department. Board secretary is Zhao Chuan.

name: Ming Zaiyuan (明再远)
current_role: Chairman, Xinjiang Xintai Natural Gas Co. (新天然气, SSE: 603393)
profile: Born 1963, Ming has chaired Xinjiang Xintai Natural Gas since 2013 and holds ~174M shares. Founded in 2000 and listed in Shanghai in 2016, the company grew from Xinjiang city-gas distribution into an integrated clean-energy group spanning coalbed methane, tight and shale gas, LNG, pipelines (Shanxi) and coal resources.
interesting_fact: Xintai runs three flagship projects: the Kashgar North conventional oil and gas block, the Santanghu coal-chemical project and an underground coal-to-gas (coal gasification) project, alongside unconventional gas in Shanxi.
deep_cut_fact: Before energy he spent four years in the army (1980-84), then 13 years in rural banking in Deyang, Sichuan (1985-98), rising from auditor to deputy president of the local Agricultural Bank branch and head of the credit-cooperative union; he is a certified economist.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts. Board secretary Liu Dong handles investor contact (exchange-registered email above). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Liu Qiang
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Ingenic Semiconductor (北京君正, SZSE: 300223; HKEX: 03223)
profile: Founder and chairman of Beijing-based fabless chip designer Ingenic, set up in 2005 on the founding team's own XBurst CPU design and listed on ChiNext in 2011. Ingenic makes SoCs for smart cameras, AIoT, wearables and education devices, bought US memory maker ISSI (SRAM/DRAM/NOR flash) in 2020, and added a Hong Kong listing in August 2026.
interesting_fact: Ingenic's JZ4770 processor powered the world's first Android 4.0 'Ice Cream Sandwich' tablet in 2011, built on Ingenic's home-grown XBurst MIPS-based CPU core.

public_contacts.value: https://irm.cninfo.com.cn/ircs/company/companyDetail?stockcode=300223&orgId=9900016187 (official investor Q&A platform, linked from Ingenic site)

notes: Very low public profile; common name (刘强) - make sure to reference Ingenic. Biographical detail not verified this pass (web-search budget exhausted); HK listing prospectus (2026) should contain his full bio. Memory (ISSI DRAM) is a modest data-center angle.

name: Gao Jiyang
current_role: Founder & CEO, Galaxea AI (星海图, GALAXEA (Beijing) Artificial Intelligence Technology Co.)
profile: Gao Jiyang (高继扬) studied microelectronics at Tsinghua (2015) and earned a USC PhD in computer vision (2018), then was a tech lead at Waymo and an executive director at Momenta. He founded embodied-AI/robotics company Galaxea AI with Tsinghua's Hang Zhao; it builds general-purpose humanoid and wheeled-arm robots plus its own G0 foundation models, and became a unicorn.
interesting_fact: At the 2026 World Robot Conference Galaxea signed a three-year deal with JD.com and showed what it called the world's first robot-run 'forward warehouse' that takes online orders and picks/packs them autonomously.
deep_cut_fact: At Waymo he was co-first author of VectorNet (CVPR 2020), an influential method for encoding HD maps and agent motion for trajectory prediction, and of TNT (CoRL 2020) with his future Galaxea cofounder Hang Zhao.
notes: Personal email is self-published (written 'jiyanggao1203 at gmail dot com') on his academic homepage, which dates from his Momenta days, so may be less monitored. Robotics rather than data centers, but strong AI-infrastructure/foundation-model angle.

name: Che Chengju
current_role: Second-largest shareholder (~4.3%) of Zibo Qixiang Tengda Chemical (002408.SZ); former chairman and later director/GM, no longer listed among current management
profile: Che Chengju (车成聚, b. 1950), a Qilu Petrochemical veteran, from 1998 built Qixiang into a Zibo C4-chemicals producer, listed in Shenzhen in 2010. After the parent group's restructuring, state-owned Shandong Energy took control (2022); he stepped down as chairman in 2023 and remains a major individual shareholder.
interesting_fact: After losing control to Shandong Energy, he pledged in Sept 2023 to buy RMB 100-120M of Qixiang shares on the open market and did so, lifting his stake to about 4.2-4.3%.
deep_cut_fact: He started work in December 1971 and rose to labour-section chief and deputy director of Qilu Petrochemical's rubber plant before running Qixiang; he has won a Sinopec Science and Technology Progress first prize and was named a Shandong Outstanding Entrepreneur in 2002, 2007 and 2021.
notes: Age ~76 and no longer in management (company now state-controlled under Shandong SASAC), so the IR email reaches the company, not him. Alive status inferred from 2026 shareholder filings that list him as holder. Very low international profile; Chinese-language only.

name: Shen Hao
current_role: Actual controller of Hongyu Investment (now Shenzhen Hongyu Information Technology), a ~5% shareholder of Trina Solar (688599); controlling shareholder and executive director/GM of Jiangsu Huabo Industrial Group (Nanjing)
profile: Shen Hao (沈浩) is a Nanjing-based investor whose vehicle Hangzhou Hongyu Investment bought 6% of Trina Solar during its 2017 return from NYSE to China; Trina's 2020 STAR Market IPO and solar rally put him on the 2021 Hurun list. He also owns 90% of Jiangsu Huabo Industrial Group. Hongyu still held 5.08% of Trina in Oct 2024.
interesting_fact: Trina's 2020 prospectus names him as one of only three non-founder individuals indirectly holding 5%+ of Trina, alongside Zhang Yong (Rongqi) and Zhu Guangping (Qisheng); Hongyu nominated director Dou Yuming to Trina's board in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: Besides Huabo, the prospectus lists him as a director of Shanghai Yingxing Network Technology, Nanjing Laifuxing Communications and Nanjing Guoli Management Consulting, plus controller of supply-chain firm Jiangsu Fengyun (蜂云) and Nanjing Mifeng (Bee) Management Consulting.
notes: Very private financial investor, not a Trina executive; no press profile found. In Oct 2024 his vehicle (Shenzhen Hongyu, 5.08%) planned a block-trade sale of up to 0.5% of Trina but ended early after selling 0.08% (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202410081640203107_1.pdf). No personal/office contact published; Trina IR (IR@trinasolar.com) is not his channel.

name: Lu Xianping
current_role: Chairman and General Manager (president), Shenzhen Chipscreen Biosciences (STAR Market: 688321)
profile: Xianping Lu, a U.S.-citizen scientist, did postdoctoral research at UC San Diego (1989-94), helped found Maxia Pharmaceuticals and Galderma Research, and headed research at Galderma's North American R&D center before returning to China. In 2001 he co-founded Chipscreen in Shenzhen, which developed chidamide (Epidaza), China's first original anti-cancer drug; he still chairs and runs it.
interesting_fact: Chipscreen's chidamide is described as China's first original anti-tumor new drug; Lu received Shenzhen's 2018 Science and Technology 'Mayor's Award'. Note: Chipscreen is a drug developer, not a chip company.
deep_cut_fact: In 2006, short of cash, Chipscreen out-licensed chidamide's patents abroad on a fee-plus-milestones-plus-royalty model - reported as the first time a Chinese original new drug's patent rights were licensed to the U.S. and other developed markets. In 2000 he and five young Chinese scholars decided to return to China to start it.
notes: Still chairman per Chipscreen's 2025 annual report (signed 30 Mar 2026). Career details from the 2024 annual report bio. Mis-tagged as data_center_ai - biotech, low relevance for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Chen Wukui
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Chief Engineer, Shenzhen Topraysolar Co., Ltd (002218.SZ)
profile: Engineer-entrepreneur (b. 1958) who founded Shenzhen Topray Solar in 2002 and has chaired it since, building it into a maker of amorphous, mono- and multi-crystalline silicon solar cells, modules and solar applications. Topray listed in Shenzhen in February 2008; he remains chairman and chief engineer and was re-elected for the 2025-2028 board term.
interesting_fact: He led Topray's industrial park project, which was among China's first batch of national renewable-energy demonstration projects (Ministry of Construction), and the NDRC's 25MW amorphous-silicon PV industrialisation project.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar he worked across an unusual mix of fields - chemicals, magnetic materials, rubber, machinery and electro-vacuum technology - and holds degrees in both mechanical manufacturing and international economics; he still carries the title of chief engineer at the company he chairs.
notes: Last on Hurun China list in 2021; the IR email is the published board-secretary mailbox (Gong Yanping). Chinese-language outreach advisable; no English-language profile or social accounts found.

name: Wang Wenzhi
current_role: Chairman (last reported) of Elion Ecological Restoration Co. (亿利生态修复), part of Wang Wenbiao's Elion Resources Group; former director of Elion Energy / Elion Clean Energy (600277)
profile: Wang Wenzhi (王文治) is a long-time senior executive of Elion Resources Group, the Inner Mongolia chemicals, coal, pharma and desert-greening conglomerate founded by Wang Wenbiao, with whom Hurun co-listed him in 2008-2013. He sat on the board of listed Elion Energy (2011-14 and later) and went on to chair Elion's Beijing-based ecological-restoration arm.
interesting_fact: He chaired Elion Ecological Restoration (founded 2014, Beijing), the group's eco-restoration arm; Elion's Kubuqi Desert greening earned Wang Wenbiao UNEP's Champions of the Earth lifetime-achievement award (https://unep.org/championsofearth/es/node/229).
notes: Family tie to Wang Wenbiao is implied by the shared Hurun entry but not confirmed in any source we found. Avoid: a CSRC penalty decision on Elion Clean Energy handed him a 10-year market ban (Wang Wenbiao got a lifetime ban) - https://www.jiemian.com/article/7011562.html. Tried Elion annual reports (2020, 2023) and board-election notices for a bio; none found. No published contact.

name: Xue Fangquan
current_role: Chairman, Chongqing Minsheng Energy Group (重庆民生能源集团) as of 2015 reporting; current status not re-verified
profile: Xue Fangquan, born in the mid-1950s in Zhengxing, Bishan (Chongqing), went from farmer to railway soldier, teacher and state-firm employee before founding Chongqing Minsheng Energy Group, a private group spanning piped natural gas, energy chemicals, plastic pipes, petrochemical logistics, city buses, property and hotels, with ~3,000 staff and assets over RMB1B.
interesting_fact: Despite his wealth he told Chongqing Morning Post in 2015 that he still lived in an ordinary high-rise flat he had moved into in 1999, saying he liked knowing his neighbours.
deep_cut_fact: A creature of habit from four years as a railway soldier in Hebei, he was up by 6am and in the office before 7:30, where he walked 6,000 steps around the company lobby to music every morning - aiming to have walked the equivalent of a lap of the Earth by age 80.
notes: Source is a 2015 profile; he dropped off Hurun after 2021 and is now around 70, so check he is still active. Told the reporter interviews were welcome any day before 8:30am - an approachable, early-rising type. No published contacts found.

name: Ding Yongqaing

name: Gerald Ronson
current_role: Chief Executive, Heron International (London property developer); founding chairman, Community Security Trust
profile: Sir Gerald Ronson (b. 1939) left school at 15 to join his father's furniture firm Heron and built it into one of Britain's largest private companies, spanning property and petrol retailing. After near-collapse in the early-1990s property crash, Heron rebuilt to develop Heron Tower and The Heron in the City of London; his Rontec consortium bought Total UK's forecourt network. He was knighted in 2024 for philanthropy.

deep_cut_fact: In the mid-1960s Ronson brought the first self-service petrol stations to the United Kingdom - decades before his Rontec consortium acquired Total's UK forecourt business.

No working Heron International contact found (heron domains tried were parked/unreachable). Possible indirect routes: Community Security Trust or JCoSS, where he holds leadership roles.

current_role: Co-founder and director, JinkoSolar (晶科能源, SSE 688223) and JinkoSolar Holding (NYSE: JKS); director of Jinko Power (晶科科技)

current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Sino Geophysical Co., Ltd. (潜能恒信, SZSE: 300191), Beijing

interesting_fact: His seismic-services company turned upstream player: by its 2025 annual report it held interests in 8 petroleum blocks (6 in China, 2 overseas), including Bohai 05/31 where it is optimising the CFD1-2 oilfield development plan with CNOOC Tianjin.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated in 1985 in geophysical prospecting from China University of Petroleum, then spent 1985-1996 processing and interpreting seismic data at CNPC's Bureau of Geophysical Prospecting research institute and at Singapore's Oriental Petroleum Technology, including a secondment to Halliburton in the US.
notes: Low international profile; communications in Chinese via the board secretary office (zqb@sinogeo.com) is the realistic route. Hurun entry is shared with Zhou Zilong. Board includes CAS academician and former CNPC VP Jia Chengzao.

name: Guo Hui
current_role: Cofounder, director and deputy general manager, Shanghai Awinic Technology (SSE STAR: 688798) (per IPO prospectus; verify current title)
profile: Guo Hui (郭辉, b. 1972), a semiconductor-physics engineer, cofounded Shanghai Awinic in 2008 with Sun Hongjun. Awinic designs analog and mixed-signal chips (audio amplifiers, haptic drivers, power management) for smartphones and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021; he held about 13% pre-IPO, the second-largest stake.
interesting_fact: Awinic's founding team largely came from Huawei's chip-design group and then mobile-chip startup Qipai Microelectronics, including Guo and chairman Sun Hongjun.
deep_cut_fact: Before Awinic he spent 1997-2002 as an IC design engineer in Huawei's Central R&D basic-business unit, rising to deputy manager of its digital-analog department, then served as VP of Qipai Microelectronics (Shanghai) 2002-2008.
notes: Low media profile; no interviews found. Route via Awinic securities/board office (securities@awinic.com, also given in its 2024 sustainability report). Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Zhou Zilong
current_role: Major shareholder (acting-in-concert with controlling shareholder Zhou Jinming), Sino Geophysical Co. / 潜能恒信能源技术股份有限公司 (SZSE: 300191)
profile: Zhou Zilong is a top-ten shareholder of Sino Geophysical (潜能恒信), a Beijing oil and gas exploration technology and E&P company founded and controlled by Zhou Jinming. The company's 2025 annual report identifies Zilong as Jinming's child. Hurun listed the family's wealth jointly from 2017 to 2021. He holds no disclosed executive role and has no public profile of his own.
interesting_fact: Sino Geophysical has developed 50+ proprietary seismic-imaging and exploration software packages (e.g. WEFOX, SinoGeoStar) and runs a US subsidiary, Sinogeo E&P Service LLC in Texas.
notes: Passive shareholder with no public persona. Father Zhou Jinming is chairman and the public face. Do not confuse him with an unrelated post-2000 Shanghai startup founder of the same name. The only route is the company securities department.

name: Bahram Akradi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Life Time Group Holdings (NYSE: LTH); Director, Northern Oil and Gas (NOG)
profile: Tehran-born entrepreneur who came to Colorado at 17, began selling memberships at a Nautilus gym, co-led U.S. Swim & Fitness in Minneapolis (1984-89), then founded Life Time in 1992. Life Time runs 180+ 'athletic country club' destinations plus events like Leadville 100 and Unbound Gravel, and returned to the NYSE in 2021. He also sits on the board of oil producer Northern Oil and Gas.
interesting_fact: He has built Life Time into a 'healthy way of life' company spanning clubs, MIORA longevity clinics, LT Work coworking and endurance events, and writes personal essays for the company's Experience Life magazine.
deep_cut_fact: As a boy he wanted to fly for the Iranian air force like his brother Davood, so he majored in electrical engineering at UC Colorado Springs as a route to aerospace. He cooked nights as 'Chef Akradi', outsold the local Nautilus gym's top salesman within 3 months, and drove a U-Haul to Minneapolis in March 1983.
notes: Strong podcast fit (founder story, immigrant entrepreneur), and the NOG directorship gives an energy angle. Writes first-person pieces in Experience Life magazine. Best route is Life Time public relations.

name: Yang Jianliang
current_role: Chairman, Hoyuan Green Energy Co. (formerly Wuxi Shangji Automation; SSE: 603185), Wuxi
profile: Yang Jianliang (b. 1969) co-founded Wuxi Shangji Grinding Machine Co. with his wife Hang Hong in 2002; from 2004 it made grinding and slicing machines for solar, listed in Shanghai in 2018, then expanded into wafers, polysilicon, cells and modules with big bases in Baotou. He was chairman and GM until 2022 and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: In January 2026 Hoyuan (HY Solar) said it produced 40-micron 'engineering-ready' ultra-thin silicon wafers at its Baotou plant using slicing equipment it designed in-house - a nod to its machine-tool roots.
deep_cut_fact: His company began life as a grinding-machine maker and, by its own account, entered PV equipment in 2004 as one of China's earliest dedicated solar-equipment manufacturers. He is a senior economist, a Jiangsu CPPCC member and vice-chair of the Wuxi Energy Industry Association.
notes: IR email is the company securities department (board secretary Zhuang Kejie). Son Yang Hao (b. 1992) has been general manager since 2022 and is a more public, younger face of the company. Solar sector downturn hit results in 2024; keep outreach upbeat.

name: Xue Guanglin
current_role: Founder of Brightoil Petroleum (HKEX: 933); no longer chairman/CEO since 2019 (later named strategic adviser)
profile: Anhui-born Xue Guanglin (Cantonese: Sit Kwong Lam) founded Brightoil in the 1990s, building one of China's largest private oil groups: bunkering and trading, a tanker fleet, storage terminals, Xinjiang gas fields and Bohai Bay oil interests. He made Forbes China's top 60 in 2012-15 and sat on the CPPCC from 2003.
interesting_fact: At its peak Brightoil had about 12 million cubic metres of oil storage capacity and a 3-million-DWT ocean tanker fleet, unusual scale for a private Chinese energy company.
deep_cut_fact: In his chairman's message on Brightoil's website he wrote: 'More than 20 years ago, I had a dream: to build a privately owned Chinese global energy company.' He served as a member of the 10th through 13th CPPCC National Committees.
notes: Not recommended as a guest: Hong Kong High Court declared him bankrupt in April 2019 over ~US$1.4B in personal guarantees for Brightoil debts; he lost his chairman/CEO roles. His listed fortune is out of date. Current status and activities unclear. No published contact found.

name: Wang Yihui
current_role: Chairwoman and General Manager, Zhuhai Jieli Technology (杰理科技, BSE: 920138)
profile: Wang Yihui (b. Oct 1970) founded Zhuhai Jieli Technology in 2010 after seven years as vice-president of Zhuhai chip firm Jianrong; Jieli designs low-cost Bluetooth audio, wearable and IoT SoCs used widely in earbuds and smart devices. She is one of four co-controllers (80%+ of votes); after several earlier attempts, Jieli listed on the Beijing Stock Exchange on 12 Aug 2026, opening up 191% at a RMB 23.8bn market cap.
interesting_fact: Jieli finally went public on its fourth IPO attempt: its Beijing Stock Exchange debut on 12 August 2026 opened 191% higher, valuing the company at about RMB 23.8 billion; Xiaomi is also a shareholder (~2.7%).
deep_cut_fact: She did not start in tech: her first job (1994-97) was as a staff member at Zhuhai Hengtong Shipping Group, followed by six years as head of administration at Zhuhai Xike Network Technology before she moved into chips in 2003.
notes: Wang Yihui is female (filings say 王艺辉女士). Very low media profile. Avoid the 2012-17 trade-secret litigation with former employer Jianrong (withdrawn). Board secretary Hu Xiangjun is the formal IR route; info@ is the company email listed in filings.

name: Yan Hongjia
current_role: Chairman/head of Mingguan New Material (明冠新材, SH:688560); co-founder and controlling figure of Yunnan Yuze New Energy (formerly Yuze Semiconductor), an N-type silicon wafer maker
profile: Born 1980 in Xinzhou, Shanxi, Yan Hongjia co-founded Mingguan New Material (solar backsheets, battery aluminium-plastic film; STAR Market 2020) with his brother Yan Yong in 2007. In 2019 they founded Yuze Semiconductor in Chuxiong, Yunnan, an N-type wafer maker that has raised over RMB 2B and filed for IPO tutoring in 2024.
interesting_fact: Yuze kept a low profile until June 2022, when Tongwei disclosed polysilicon supply contracts with it worth about RMB 38.5B. Yuze is one of a cluster of solar plants that turned Chuxiong in Yunnan into an unlikely new-energy hub.
deep_cut_fact: After high school he skipped university to ease his family's finances and went south to work. In 2003 he and his brother set up Yuntian Electronics in Kunshan, Jiangsu, and made their first money selling computer consumables. In 2006 he moved into new energy in Jiangxi.

public_contacts.value: ir@mg-crown.com (Mingguan New Material board secretary's office)

notes: The 'Yuze' in the dataset is Yuze Semiconductor / Yunnan Yuze New Energy (Chuxiong). The more reliable route is via listed Mingguan (Yichun, Jiangxi), where he is the legal head. He co-controls both companies with his brother Yan Yong. Low profile.

name: Guo Chunxuan
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Xinxiang Richful Lube Additive Co. (瑞丰新材, SZSE: 300910)
profile: Guo Chunxuan (郭春萱, b. 1964) built Richful in Xinxiang, Henan, into China's leading domestic maker of lubricant additives (plus carbonless-paper developer), exporting to North America, Europe and emerging markets. He has chaired the business since 1996 and listed it in Shenzhen in 2020; Richful competes with global additive majors (Lubrizol, Infineum, etc.).
interesting_fact: Richful is regarded as China's leading domestic lubricant-additive maker; in Sept 2026 it launched RF60300, an additive package to help oil blenders meet the new API CL-4/FB-4 performance categories.
deep_cut_fact: He started as a workshop director at Hubei's Echeng Iron & Steel Works (1985-87), then was a technician at the Xinxiang Chemical Research Institute, and is a named inventor on patents for zinc dialkyl dithiophosphate (ZDDP) and dithiocarbamate preparation methods. He also chairs the additives committee of the Shanghai lubricant industry association.
notes: Low profile, technical founder. Best route: securities affairs office (zqb@richful.com, published in a July 2024 board announcement).

name: Xu Ligang
current_role: Co-founder, co-controlling shareholder, Director & General Manager, Jiangsu X-chip Semiconductor (展芯股份, SZSE ChiNext: 301707), Nanjing
profile: Xu Ligang (徐立刚, mid-40s) holds a PhD in power electronics from Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics and co-founded Nanjing-based X-chip in 2018 with fellow NUAA alumnus Wen Zhenlin. X-chip designs high-reliability analog power-management chips and DC/DC micro-modules; it listed on ChiNext on 7 Aug 2026 and surged ~360% on debut.
interesting_fact: X-chip's IPO priced at 23.45 yuan and opened 360% higher on day one (peaking near 129.90 yuan), making Xu and co-founder Wen Zhenlin newly minted chip billionaires in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding X-chip he worked as an engineer at Shenzhen Qingxuan Electronics and at Silergy's Hangzhou arm, then ran the Zhuzhou Zhanxin business unit; X-chip's leadership and independent directors are largely fellow NUAA power-electronics alumni.
notes: Hurun 'X-Chip' = 江苏展芯半导体 (Zhanxin). Chairman is co-founder Wen Zhenlin; Xu is GM. Company focuses on military/high-reliability power chips, so expect low media appetite. Route via IR email.

name: Ou Xinhua
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Shanghai Prisemi Electronics (芯导科技, STAR Market: 688230)
profile: Engineer-founder who set up Shanghai Prisemi in Nov 2009, a fabless designer of power semiconductors (TVS/ESD protection devices, MOSFETs, Schottky diodes, power-management ICs) for consumer electronics, with Xiaomi among its major customers. He controlled 100% of the company before its 2021 STAR Market listing and was re-elected chairman in Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: Prisemi was his first startup, and he kept 100% control of it right up to its STAR Market IPO filing, with no outside VC shareholders.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Prisemi he was an R&D engineer and project manager at Shanghai Guangyu Ruixin Microelectronics and then technical director at Suzhou Jingxun Technology.
notes: Low public profile with no interviews found. Prisemi does power and protection chips, mainly for phones and consumer devices, so the data-center link is indirect.

name: Li Yi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, 51WORLD (Beijing 51World Digital Twin Technology; HKEX-listed)
profile: Li Yi (Archer Li) founded 51WORLD in Beijing in 2015, evolving it from a VR startup into a digital-twin and simulation platform used for autonomous-driving testing, transport hubs, smart factories, water management and energy. Backed by Sky9 Capital from its Series A, 51WORLD listed on the HKEX main board; he now pitches it as a data engine for embodied AI and robotics.
interesting_fact: His stated goal is to build a 'Digital Twin Earth' - a complete virtual replica of the world - by 2030; 51WORLD's simulation platform serves nearly a hundred intelligent-driving customers.
deep_cut_fact: On investor Sky9 Capital's founder page he lists as his favorite quote: 'Pessimists are always right but optimists are more likely to succeed.'
notes: Goes by 'Archer Li' in English. aes@51aes.com is 51WORLD's published customer-service email (no dedicated press address found). Data-center/energy angle: digital twins for energy sites and factories; recent focus on robotics training data.

name: Ao Fengting
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Inner Mongolia Mengtai Group (coal, power, aluminium; Ordos)
profile: Inner Mongolia entrepreneur who founded Mengtai Group (formerly Ordos Mengtai Coal & Power), an integrated coal, power and aluminium producer in Ordos. He has been on the Hurun list every year since 2010 (9th in Inner Mongolia in 2024, RMB 5.3bn) and reportedly is a vice-president of the China Ethnic Trade Promotion Association.
interesting_fact: Mengtai follows the classic Inner Mongolia 'coal-power-aluminium' integration model, using its own mine-mouth coal power to run energy-intensive aluminium smelting.
notes: Very low profile with minimal public information; the biography above comes from a Hurun-derived list (maigoo.com/news/725273.html). I could not reach a company website or published contact. Identity is matched by name and company only.

name: Liang Meizhen
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (acting in concert with Yu Zhong and Zuo Guojun) of Shenzhen S.C New Energy Technology (捷佳伟创, 300724.SZ)
profile: One of three actual controllers of S.C New Energy, a Shenzhen solar-equipment maker founded in 2003 that builds PECVD, diffusion, texturing/etching and automation tools for crystalline-silicon PV cell lines; it listed on ChiNext in 2018. She directly holds about 7% and controls about 11% of voting rights (incl. shares held by her son), per 2025 filings. No executive role found.
interesting_fact: 'SC' in the Hurun listing is S.C New Energy (捷佳伟创), one of China's main suppliers of solar-cell manufacturing equipment, whose PECVD tools deposit anti-reflective and passivation layers on PV cells.
notes: Identity inferred from Hurun 'SC' + green energy and confirmed by S.C New Energy filings naming 梁美珍 as co-actual controller. Appears to be a passive shareholder with no public profile; better interview targets are chairman Zuo Guojun or CEO Yu Zhong.

name: Hu Xinrong
current_role: Chairman, legal representative and core technical staff, Shenzhen Xinyichang Technology (Hoson, SSE STAR: 688383)
profile: Shenzhen engineer who co-founded Xinyichang with Song Changning in 2006; the two are its controlling shareholders. Starting with capacitor aging-test machines, the company became a leading Chinese maker of LED (incl. Mini LED) die bonders and expanded into semiconductor die-attach and lithium-battery equipment. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in April 2021.
interesting_fact: Xinyichang began in 2006 making aluminium electrolytic capacitor aging-test machines, then used that know-how to break into LED die bonders, and later developed six-head high-speed die bonders for Mini LED and chip-packaging die bonders for semiconductors.
deep_cut_fact: He worked his way up from the shop floor: a technician at Shenzhen Huachang Electronics, then technician and equipment supervisor at Shenzhen Datong, before running two small Bao'an workshops (Hengchang machining plant and Yichang electronics factory) that preceded Xinyichang.
notes: Hurun's 'Xinyichang' = 新益昌 (Hoson). Low media profile; route via board secretary Liu Xiaohuan's office (hoson@szhech.com, listed in 2024 interim report). Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Pua Khein Seng
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Phison Electronics Corp. (Hsinchu, Taiwan; NAND flash controllers/SSDs); founder of Malaysian IC-design arm MaiStorage
profile: Malaysian engineer (b. 1974, Sekinchan, Selangor) who studied at National Chiao Tung University and in 2000, aged 27, co-founded Phison with four schoolmates. Phison is credited with the first single-chip USB flash drive controller and now makes NAND controllers and enterprise SSDs, including aiDAPTIV+ for AI workloads. He stepped back as chairman but remains CEO.
interesting_fact: He is widely known in Malaysia as the 'father of the pen drive' for Phison's single-chip USB flash drive, and was made a Dato' by Penang in 2012.
deep_cut_fact: A farming-town boy from Sekinchan, Selangor, he attended Pin Hwa High School in Klang before going to Taiwan for university. He founded Phison in 2000 at 27, and in 2024 the KL20 Summit celebrated his 'homecoming' as he set up MaiStorage to train Malaysian chip designers.
notes: Hurun lists him under China, but he is a Malaysian citizen based in Taiwan. Strong data-centre/AI-storage angle (NAND shortage, aiDAPTIV+). Phison sites block automated fetches; the press email comes from 2026 Business Wire releases as indexed by search. Some releases list spokesperson Antonio Yu instead.

name: Wong Howard
current_role: Executive Director, Chairman and CEO, Hong Kong ZCloud Technology Construction Ltd (9900.HK; formerly Gain Plus Holdings)
profile: Howard Wong (黄晞), about 70, took control of HK construction subcontractor Gain Plus Holdings via his wholly owned Asia General Industries (~32%) and became chairman and CEO in Feb 2025. He renamed it Hong Kong ZCloud Technology Construction to reflect a 'technology construction' focus; the share rerating put him on Hurun's 2026 China list.
interesting_fact: After his takeover the company rebranded from Gain Plus Holdings to Hong Kong ZCloud Technology Construction (ticker 'ZCLOUD TECH CON' from 26 May 2025) and split each share into eight in August 2025.
deep_cut_fact: His earlier career was in retail and trading: from 2000 to 2015 he was an executive director of Chaifa Holdings (stock code 139), whose businesses at times spanned garments, shoes, car audio equipment and early internet ventures.
notes: Very little public profile; no interviews, website contacts or social accounts found. Listed-company announcements on HKEXnews (stock 9900) are the main public record. Company's core business is still HK building subcontracting/RMAA; data-center link is not documented in sources found.

name: Zhang Yuan
current_role: Chairman, legal representative and actual controller, Changchun Zhiyuan New Energy Equipment Co. (SZSE ChiNext: 300985)
profile: Zhang Yuan controls (via Changchun Huifeng New Energy Equipment Group, with Wang Ran and Zhang Yichi) Changchun-based Zhiyuan New Energy, founded 2014 and listed on ChiNext in 2021. It makes vehicle LNG fuel-supply systems, LNG marine fuel systems and cryogenic tanks, and processes graphitized anode material for lithium batteries; revenue was ~RMB 1.7bn in 2025.
interesting_fact: Zhiyuan straddles two energy transitions: LNG fuel systems for heavy trucks and ships (a diesel substitute) and graphitization of anode material for EV lithium-ion batteries.
notes: Very low public profile; little personal biography online. Company filings (cninfo.com.cn, code 300985) are the main source; board secretary is Zhang Shuying. Contact would go through the company's board secretary/IR office. Common name - confirm via company.

name: Liu Xingsheng
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO/President, Focuslight Technologies (炬光科技, 688167.SH), Xi'an
profile: Liu Xingsheng (Victor Liu) left a US laser-industry career to found Xi'an Focuslight in 2007, building high-power semiconductor lasers and micro-optics. Listed on Shanghai's STAR Market, Focuslight bought Germany's LIMO (2017) and SUSS MicroOptics in Switzerland, and is now pushing into optical-communications/co-packaged optics and automotive LiDAR. He holds ~13% of the company.
interesting_fact: After the SUSS MicroOptics deal, Liu is steering Focuslight toward silicon photonics, transceivers and co-packaged optics, a direct link to AI data-center interconnects; it has also supplied LiDAR transmitters to automakers for years.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in rural Suide County, Shaanxi, he earned his Virginia Tech materials-science PhD in just 2 years 8 months (2001), the fastest in the program's history; at Corning, Coherent and nLight he developed what Xinhua called the first flip-chip semiconductor laser. His motto: 'NO COPY'.
notes: Goes by 'Victor Xingsheng Liu' in English materials and gives English-language trade-press interviews, so English outreach is feasible. jgdm@ is the published investor mailbox (board office).

name: Griffin Perry
current_role: Co-founder and ~11% shareholder, Fermi America (Nasdaq: FRMI); Co-Chairman, Granite Ridge Resources (NYSE: GRNT); co-founder, Grey Rock Investment Partners
profile: Son of ex-Texas governor and Energy Secretary Rick Perry; co-founded Fermi America in Jan 2025 with his father and Toby Neugebauer and took it public on Nasdaq nine months later at ~$12.5bn. Fermi's 'Project Matador' is a multi-GW private-power AI campus near Amarillo. He also co-founded Grey Rock and co-chairs Granite Ridge Resources.
interesting_fact: Fermi plans to power its Texas Panhandle AI campus with its own private generation - gas, nuclear and solar - pitched at 11 GW at IPO and now marketed as a 17 GW 'Project Matador'; the stake made Perry a billionaire before the campus had a single customer.
deep_cut_fact: He began as a financial advisor at UBS and Deutsche Bank, was president of Caddis Energy, holds a BA in economics and history from Vanderbilt (plus study at the LSE) and sits on the board of the Cotton Bowl Athletic Association.
notes: Prime fit for an energy + data-centre podcast. Fermi has had leadership turnover (CEO and CFO stepped down) and share-price volatility - handle tactfully. Route via Fermi media email; Granite Ridge IR is an alternative. Deep-cut bio originates from his Grey Rock/Granite Ridge biography (reproduced on insidertrades.com).

name: Zhang Jianjun
current_role: Founder and chairman, Era Group (公元塑业集团), controlling shareholder (with Lu Caifen) of Era Co., Ltd. (公元股份, SZSE: 002641, formerly Yonggao)
profile: Taizhou (Huangyan, Zhejiang) entrepreneur born in 1961 who built Era/Yonggao into one of China's largest plastic-pipe makers, with a solar-module arm (Era Solar). He holds 75% of the parent Era Group and Lu Caifen holds 25%; together they are the actual controllers of the listed Era Co. The listed company's board is now chaired by Lu Zhenyu.
interesting_fact: Era's plastic pipes were used on landmark projects such as the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge and Beijing Daxing International Airport.
deep_cut_fact: After high school he took his mother's place at the Huangyan cannery, starting as a boiler worker; in 1983, aged 22, he borrowed 3,000 yuan, bought five hand-cranked injection-moulding machines and began making washing-machine parts in two rented rooms.
notes: 'China ERA' = 公元 (Era) Group, Taizhou. Off the Hurun list since 2021. Deep-cut and profile details come from a Chinese brand-directory bio (cnpp.cn), which is secondary. The ownership split is from the company's exchange disclosures (sohu 002641 shareholder page). Low international profile; route via the listed company's securities department.

name: Lu Caifen
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Zhang Jianjun) and major shareholder of Gongyuan Co., Ltd. (公元股份, formerly Yonggao, SZ002641); holds no executive post
profile: Lu Caifen (卢彩芬) and her husband Zhang Jianjun are the actual controllers of ERA Group / Gongyuan Co. in Huangyan, Taizhou, Zhejiang, one of China's largest makers of plastic (PVC/PE) pipes, which also runs ERA Solar module making. She owns 25% of parent Gongyuan Plastics Group and is the listed company's second-largest shareholder; as of April 2026 neither she nor her husband holds a board or executive role.
interesting_fact: ERA Group traces back to 1983 and moved into photovoltaics in 2006 with Zhejiang ERA Solar Technology, a module and solar garden-light maker; her brother Lu Zhenyu, once the predecessor company's storage-and-transport section chief, rose to chairman.
notes: Very private; no personal media presence. In an April 2026 investor Q&A the company said the controllers have no plans to return to management. Only realistic route is the board secretary's office (zqb@era.com.cn). ERA founding/solar details partly from exhibitor listings (https://craft.co/zhejiang-era-solar-technology).

name: Liu Jiang
current_role: Legal representative and 93.5% owner of Beijing Dongjia Investment (北京东嘉投资); former actual controller of Guizhou Gas (600903.SH)
profile: Liu Jiang (刘江, b. 1968) controlled city-gas distributor Guizhou Gas Group through his Beijing Dongjia Investment, making the Hurun and Forbes lists in 2018-2023. In 2023 Dongjia agreed to transfer its controlling stake to Guizhou Wujiang Energy Investment, shifting control of Guizhou Gas to the Guizhou provincial SASAC.
interesting_fact: The 2023 deal had Wujiang Energy take 29.99% of Guizhou Gas, with about RMB 1.09bn paid for the purchased shares, handing a privately controlled provincial gas utility to the state.
notes: Very private; no public bio, interviews or personal channels found. Since 2023 he is no longer controller of Guizhou Gas, so company IR is not a route to him. Dongjia Investment is Beijing-based (Zhongguancun).

name: Zhou Yinghuai
current_role: Director and General Manager (CEO), Sichuan Injet Electric Co., Ltd. (英杰电气, SZSE: 300820)
profile: Zhou Yinghuai (b. 1964), a senior engineer, co-founded Deyang-based Injet Electric with chairman Wang Jun in 1996; each controls about a third of it. Injet makes power-control and special power supplies for polysilicon/PV, semiconductor and materials manufacturing, plus EV chargers; Zhou has been GM since 2010.
interesting_fact: Injet's power-control supplies are a key input for solar-grade polysilicon furnaces, tying the company's fortunes to China's PV build-out; it also sells EV charging piles.
deep_cut_fact: Injet started in January 1996 as 'Deyang Sunshine Electric' (德阳市阳光电气), set up by Wang Jun, Zhou Yinghuai and Xiao Lin with just ~RMB 500,100 of registered capital; it took the Injet (英杰) name in 2002. Zhou is also vice-chairman of the Sichuan Power Electronics Society.

public_contacts.value: http://ir.p5w.net (Panorama Network investor-interaction platform used by Injet)

notes: Wang Jun is chairman; Zhou is GM. Very little English coverage. No published IR email found; company website was unreachable from here. Board secretary is Liu Shiwei (per 10jqka). Energy relevance: PV/polysilicon power supplies.

name: Yang Xueyan
current_role: Executive partner of Arctech Solar's employee shareholding platforms (Suzhou Rongbo and Suzhou Zhongzhi Wanbo); wife of Arctech founder/CEO Cai Hao
profile: Co-holder, with husband Cai Hao, of the fortune in Arctech Solar (Jiangsu Zhongxinbo, SSE STAR: 688408), a Kunshan-based maker of solar trackers, fixed-tilt racking and BIPV systems founded in 2009 and listed in 2020. Per Arctech's 2025 annual report she is the managing partner of the company's two employee stock-ownership vehicles.
interesting_fact: Arctech is one of the world's larger solar-tracker suppliers; at SNEC 2026 it said it secured over 3 GW of orders for its 'Tracker+' ecosystem, and it is building a zero-carbon headquarters campus in Kunshan.
notes: Spouse relationship confirmed in Arctech's 2025 annual report summary (shareholder relationship note). No public interviews found; husband Cai Hao (CEO, ~35% holder) is the natural podcast guest - she is best approached jointly via Arctech IR.

name: Wan Yongxing
current_role: Actual controller and legal representative, CCS Supply Chain Management (Ruimaotong, SSE: 600180); controller of Zhengzhou Zhongrui Industrial Group
profile: Wan Yongxing (万永兴) is a Zhengzhou-based entrepreneur who built Ruimaotong (CCS Supply Chain Management), one of China's larger private coal supply-chain and commodity-trading groups, listed in Shanghai. Through holding company Zhengzhou Zhongrui Industrial Group he also controls real-estate developer Hechang Group. He and his holding entity own about 54% of Ruimaotong.
interesting_fact: His group spans two very different businesses: moving coal from mines to power plants and ports via Ruimaotong's supply-chain platform, and residential property development through Hechang Real Estate in Henan.
notes: Hurun's 'Rail holdings' appears to be a rendering of 瑞茂通 (Ruimaotong). Group is in financial distress in 2026: Ruimaotong under delisting-risk warning since 30 Apr 2026, overdue debts and his shares judicially frozen (https://www.mrjjxw.com/articles/2026-09-23/4590522.html). Very low media profile; approach with care, via company IR only.

name: Zou Chenghui
current_role: Founder and (former) chairman / controlling shareholder, Akcome (Zhejiang Akcome New Energy Technology, ex-SZSE 002610)
profile: Chinese solar entrepreneur who founded Akcome in 2006, a maker of solar module components (aluminium frames, EVA) that expanded into PV power plants and heterojunction (HJT) cells; Akcome listed in Shenzhen in 2011 and he was chairman from 2011. Akcome was delisted from the Shenzhen exchange in June 2024, and his current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Akcome was an early Chinese mover in heterojunction (HJT) solar cells: at SNEC 2023 it unveiled a 730 W n-type HJT module (AK iPower 7.0) on 210 mm wafers.
notes: Akcome was delisted in 2024 after its share price fell below exchange thresholds and a CSRC disclosure investigation into the company and Zou - wealth likely far below the Hurun figure; sensitive subject, low-priority outreach target. No current published contacts found. Delisting source: https://pv-magazine.com/2024/06/21/chinese-pv-industry-brief-akcome-confirms-delisting-from-the-shenzhen-stock-market

name: Ou Yang (欧洋)
current_role: Co-founder, Director and General Manager, Suzhou TFC Optical Communication (天孚通信, SZSE: 300394) (GM since Jan 2018 per 2024 reporting)
profile: Co-founder (b. 1968) with husband Zou Zhinong and Zhu Guodong of TFC Optical Communication, a Suzhou maker of passive optical components and high-speed optical-engine packaging. TFC started in 2005 with zirconia ceramic sleeves, listed on ChiNext in 2015 and boomed on AI data-center demand for 800G/1.6T optics; she and Zou are the actual controllers.
interesting_fact: The name 'TFC' (天孚) comes from the English phrase 'Technology First'. TFC's first product, a rice-grain-sized ceramic ferrule sleeve, displaced Japanese imports such as Kyocera's in China's fiber-optic market.
deep_cut_fact: Every TFC production line entrance displays a plaque reading '如履薄冰' ('as if treading on thin ice'). Ou Yang says it reminds staff to treat even the tiniest component 'like a baby' because TFC ships hundreds of millions of ceramic sleeves a year.
notes: Wealth shared with husband Zou Zhinong (chairman). TFC filed for a Hong Kong H-share listing in late 2025. The ir_email is TFC's securities department (证券部). Strong data-center optics angle. Current GM title confirmed only through 2024 reporting.

name: Hsieh Juor-Ming
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Voltronic Power Technology Corp. (旭隼科技, TWSE: 6409), Taipei
profile: Hsieh Juor-Ming (謝卓明, 'Alex Hsieh') founded Voltronic Power with five colleagues during the 2008 financial crisis and built it into the world's largest ODM maker of small/mid-size UPS units, also making solar inverters and DC EV chargers. Profitable every year except its first, it is one of Taiwan's few non-semiconductor 'thousand-dollar' stocks; he now targets large data-center UPS as AI drives demand.
interesting_fact: Voltronic is a classic high-mix, low-volume maker: ~20,000 complete UPS models on the books, shipping 4,000-6,000 different models a month, often only a few dozen units per order - yet it holds 20%+ of global UPS ODM share.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2025 CTEE interview he contrasted himself with Morris Chang's ideal CEO (80% strategy, 20% execution): 'I am not that ideal CEO - I spend 90% on details; details decide victory.' During the 2020-22 chip shortage he personally chaired the shortage meeting every day.
notes: Romanisations vary: Alex Hsieh / Hsieh Jour-Ming / Chuo-Ming Hsieh. Company spokesman listed as Chiehmin Wang (Financial Manager). Strong fit for a data-center power episode (UPS, BBU views, AI demand); he does give occasional Taiwanese press interviews.

name: Sun Junliang
current_role: Director, Shaanxi Beiyuan Chemical Industry Group (北元化工, 601568.SH); acts in concert with major shareholder Shaanxi Hengyuan Investment Group
profile: Shenmu (Yulin, Shaanxi) coal-chemical entrepreneur whose wealth comes from Beiyuan Chemical, a large PVC and caustic-soda producer built on local coal and power, co-owned with state-owned Shaanxi Coal. notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or bio found. Only route is Beiyuan Chemical board office (published email). Hengyuan has been selling down its Beiyuan stake in 2026.

Beiyuan's filings name Sun Heng as controller of Hengyuan Investment, which reported RMB 7.76bn revenue and RMB 2.55bn net profit in 2024.

name: Li Abo
current_role: Director and Honorary Chairman, Yinchuan Weili Transmission Technology (Shenzhen ChiNext 300904)
profile: Li Abo (李阿波, b. 1955), a senior engineer from Ningxia, built Yinchuan Weili Reducer (founded 2003) into Weili Transmission, which makes precision gear reducers and yaw/pitch drives for wind turbines. He chaired the listed company and is now honorary chairman; Li Xiang, with whom Hurun lists the fortune, is chairman and president.
interesting_fact: Weili, a gear-reducer maker in Yinchuan, is building a planned RMB5bn wind-turbine gearbox ('speed-increaser') smart factory, billed as the only large wind-gearbox R&D and production base in western China.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong gearbox engineer, he started at the reducer research institute of Yinchuan Crane Factory, later headed the design office of the Ningxia Reducer Research Institute and served as deputy secretary-general of China's national gear-reducer industry association, before founding Weili and serving as its chief engineer.
notes: Country is blank in the input; he is Chinese (Ningxia). Hurun-listed only in 2023. Day-to-day leader is chairman/president Li Xiang. Route via the IR mailbox in the 2025 annual report.

name: Yao Junqing
current_role: President, Shanxi Meijin Energy Co., Ltd. (Shenzhen: 000723)
profile: Senior executive and member of the Yao family that controls Shanxi's Meijin Energy group, a coal/coking company in Taiyuan; he has served as general manager/president of the listed Meijin Energy (chairman is Yao Jinlong). Hurun listed him at ~$680m (2016-21). Meijin has repositioned itself from coke toward hydrogen energy and fuel-cell vehicles.

deep_cut_fact: In a 2021 Shanghai Securities News interview he said Meijin began exploring its transformation path back in 2016, arguing that coke-oven-gas hydrogen 'has great potential' under China's dual-carbon strategy.

The public face of the business is Yao Junliang and his son Yao Jinlong (chairman of Meijin Energy). The IR email is Meijin Energy's board-secretary address. Last appeared on Hurun in 2021.

notes: Very low profile; almost no personal coverage. name: Ma Yongsheng

profile: Ma Yongsheng (马永升; not Sinopec's Ma Yongsheng 马永生) left a prosecutor's-office job in 1988 to revive a bankrupt cement plant, then in 1998 founded Ludian Haolong Industrial, growing it into a Yunnan group in lead-zinc mining, cement, hydropower and Kunming real estate. Earlier, as a 1988 graduate, he carried cement sacks alongside workers to revive the idle Dashuijing plant.
notes: Hurun spells the company 'Haolong' (昊龙). Little coverage after the 2010s; current role and well-being unverified. Fortune shared with Suo Fang. Do not confuse with Sinopec chairman Ma Yongsheng. No published contact found; regional Yunnan private group with minimal web presence.

current_role: Founder and former chairman/CEO of Winsway Coking Coal (now E-Commodities Holdings, HKEX 1733); no current board seat found
