current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with Zhang Huanong) of Shenzhen Center Power Tech Co. / Vision Group (雄韬股份, SZSE: 002733); exact current title not confirmed
profile: Xu Kerong appears on Hurun China lists 2015-2021 jointly with Zhang Huanong as owners of Shenzhen Center Power Tech (Vision), founded in 1994 in Shenzhen and listed in 2014. Vision makes lead-acid, LFP lithium, sodium and hydrogen fuel-cell batteries for UPS/data-center, telecom, motive-power and grid-storage uses, selling in 100+ countries.
interesting_fact: Vision claims to be the world No.1 in LFP lithium UPS batteries and the top exporter of valve-regulated lead-acid batteries for 10 straight years; in 2026 it launched an 800V HVDC architecture and battery backup units (BBU) aimed at AI data centers, and has supplied a large Malaysian AI data center four times.
deep_cut_fact: Vision was among the first Chinese companies to build lead-acid and lithium battery factories overseas (Vietnam plant 2007, Vietnam lithium plant 2018) and among the first listed companies to invest in hydrogen, launching its fuel-cell unit Hydrogen Xiong in 2014.
notes: Very low personal profile; Zhang Huanong (chairman) is the public face. Strong data-center angle (UPS/BBU/HVDC for AI data centers). Deep-cut fact is about the company she co-owns, not her personally. Outreach via company.

name: Zhao Guoguang
current_role: Vice Chairman and General Manager (CEO), Bestechnic (Shanghai) Co. (恒玄科技, 688608.SH)
profile: Zhao Guoguang (b. 1977), a former RDA Microelectronics operations VP, co-founded Bestechnic in 2015 with Liang Zhang. Bestechnic makes low-power Bluetooth/Wi-Fi SoCs for earbuds, smartwatches, smart glasses and smart-home devices and listed on the STAR Market in 2020. He has been GM since 2022 and holds about 10%.
interesting_fact: Bestechnic's chips sit inside earbuds and smart devices from Samsung, OPPO, Xiaomi, Honor and vivo, audio brands such as Harman, Anker, Edifier and Shokz, and internet firms including Alibaba, Baidu, ByteDance and Google.
deep_cut_fact: Before Bestechnic he spent years at RDA Microelectronics, rising from design manager to operations director and then VP of operations. He was Bestechnic's first executive director and general manager (June 2015 to January 2016) before the company took its current shape.
notes: Source is the Bestechnic 2024 annual report. Chairman is Liang Zhang; Zhao is No. 2 and runs operations. Low personal media profile. Board director Tang Xiaodong is the company's PR director and is the formal press route.

name: Zhang Yigui
current_role: Former vice chairman & president and No. 2 shareholder of Zhongrong Xinda Group (中融新大集团, Qingdao); current role unknown
profile: Zhang Yigui (张亿贵, b. 1955, Zibo, Shandong) is a former state steel executive who bought 10% of Shandong Coking Group (later Zhongrong Xinda) for RMB30m in 2011, becoming its second-largest shareholder (8.31% in 2016) and vice chairman/president under founder Wang Qingtao. The coke-to-chemicals and logistics group entered court-supervised restructuring in 2023.
interesting_fact: He came to private coal-chemicals from state metallurgy: he ran the Shandong Zhangdian Steel Works and was deputy GM of Shandong Metallurgical Industry Corp before becoming Zhongrong Xinda's president in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a master's degree in world economics from Nankai University and is a senior economist, per the group's 2016 bond prospectus.
notes: Identity confirmed via Zhongrong Xinda bond filings on cninfo (2016 prospectus; 2015 annual report shareholder table https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2016-11-02/1202812530.PDF). Zhongrong Xinda (debts ~RMB48.8bn) entered bankruptcy restructuring in 2023 (https://hao.cnyes.com/post/49387), so the Hurun wealth is likely gone and there is no working company contact; sensitive topic. Now ~71 with no public profile.

name: Zhou Jingcai
current_role: Principal owner of Shandong Jincheng Petrochemical Group (山东金诚石化集团), Huantai, Zibo (exact title not confirmed)
profile: Zhou Jingcai (周敬才, b. c.1954, Zibo) is the main figure behind Shandong Jincheng Petrochemical, a private 'teapot' refiner founded in 1992 in Maqiao Town, Huantai, now expanding into polyolefins and propylene oxide/polyurethanes. On Hurun's lists 2010-2021, he was named Zibo's richest person on the 2025 Shandong Chuangfu list (RMB17.9bn).
interesting_fact: Jincheng is one of Shandong's big independent refiners: a 2016 NDRC review recorded 5.9m t/yr of retained crude distillation capacity after it scrapped two older units to win import-crude rights, and the plant has been running since 1992.
notes: Unlisted company; confirmed via Hurun (金诚石化, Zibo, age 67 in 2021), Shandong Business Daily's 2025 Shandong Chuangfu list (https://www.cnpp.cn/focus/3538159.html) and Hoshine IPO prospectus (he is among five individuals holding 29.13% of Shandong Jincheng Heavy Oil Chemical; https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2020-03-03/1207339738.PDF). No official website or press contact found; very low media profile.

name: Xie Qian
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Jiangsu Eazytec Co. (卓易信息, STAR 688258), Yixing
profile: Founded Jiangsu Eazytec in Yixing in May 2008 and holds about 39% of it (H1 2025). Eazytec started in government/enterprise and IoT cloud services and now centres on core firmware for cloud computing hardware: BIOS and BMC firmware for CPU makers and server builders, a niche tied to China's push for domestic data-center supply chains.
interesting_fact: Eazytec is one of the few Chinese suppliers of server BIOS and baseboard-management-controller (BMC) firmware, the low-level code that boots and remotely manages data-center servers.

public_contacts.value: wangjuan@eazytec.com (board secretary Wang Juan, published IR contact)

notes: Low public profile; no personal bio/interviews found. Very relevant to data-center theme (server firmware). Route via board secretary, tel 0510-80322888.

name: C Park Shaper
current_role: Director, Kinder Morgan Inc. (since 2007) and Service Corporation International; retired President of Kinder Morgan
profile: Houston energy executive who joined Kinder Morgan as CFO in 2000, became President in 2005 and retired in 2013 after helping build North America's largest natural-gas pipeline network. He remains a KMI director, sits on SCI's board, sat on the boards of two Star Peak energy-transition SPACs, and chaired Sunnova's board in 2025.
interesting_fact: He served as Kinder Morgan's President and in its 'Office of the Chairman' alongside Rich Kinder, joining in 2000 as VP and CFO and rising to President within five years.
deep_cut_fact: Before pipelines he was a dot-com-era operator: President and Director of Altair Corp., which distributed web-based investment research to financial firms, and earlier CFO of First Data Analytics; he also consulted at Boston Consulting Group and Andersen Consulting.
notes: Board bio confirmed in KMI 2026 proxy (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1506307/000150630726000024/kmi-20260401.htm). Avoid Sunnova topic (bankruptcy 2025). Kinder Morgan contacts reach the company, not him personally; no personal channels found.

name: Peng Xiaofeng
current_role: Founder of LDK Solar; later chairman/CEO of SPI Energy (delisted from Nasdaq Jan 2025; reported Chapter 15 filing Apr 2026) - no clear current role
profile: Jiangxi-born entrepreneur (彭小峰) who founded LDK Solar in Xinyu in 2005; it listed on the NYSE in 2007 and by 2010 was the world's largest producer of multicrystalline solar wafers, making him one of China's richest people in 2007-2011. LDK collapsed into bankruptcy in 2014-15; he later ran US-listed SPI Energy (Solar4America), which also failed.
interesting_fact: In 2010 LDK, then the world's largest multicrystalline wafer maker, signed an $8.9bn five-year strategic financing deal with China Development Bank and an R&D MoU with the US National Renewable Energy Laboratory.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar he built Suzhou Liouxin (founded 1997), a maker of gloves and other personal protective equipment with ~12,000 staff; he moved into wafers after noticing no Chinese company made them, putting $30m of his own money in alongside $80m of VC.
notes: Wealth listing is stale (Hurun 2007-2011); he is no longer a billionaire. Journalist should be aware of a history of bankruptcies (LDK, SPI Energy) and a 2020 Chinese insider-trading conviction reported in Chinese media. No current published contact.

name: John-Paul Backwell
current_role: Director, Quality Industrial Corp. (OTC: QIND); former CEO of Fusion Fuel Green (Nasdaq: HTOO), which he left as CEO and chairman in April 2026
profile: Backwell led Quality Industrial Corp, an industrial and energy holding company that owns Dubai-based industrial-gas firm Al Shola Gas. When Fusion Fuel, a Portuguese green-hydrogen company, bought 70% of QIND in late 2024, he became Fusion Fuel's CEO and repositioned it as a multi-energy engineering and gas platform. He stepped down as CEO of both companies in April 2026 and remains a QIND director.
interesting_fact: On becoming Fusion Fuel CEO he set out to build 'a world-class platform for engineering and advisory services across energy and industrial sectors', moving a struggling electrolyser maker into industrial gases and advisory work through the QIND/Al Shola Gas deal.
notes: The $550m figure is an SEC-holdings artefact. HTOO and QIND are micro-caps, so he is unlikely to be a true UHNW individual. He resigned as CEO in April 2026, citing personal and health reasons (don't raise this). Fusion Fuel is now led by CEO Frederico Figueira de Chaves and chairman James Passin, with a uranium-royalty pivot. Little public biography exists.

name: Tony Buckingham
current_role: Owner (reported CEO), Albion Energy Ltd, holder of Malta offshore exploration study licence for Areas 2 and 7 (2023); founder & ex-CEO of Heritage Oil
profile: Tony Buckingham, a former British SAS officer, founded Heritage Oil in 1992 to explore in Angola; Heritage later made big finds in Uganda's Lake Albert basin and Iraqi Kurdistan, listed in London in 2008 and was sold in 2014. He now explores via privately owned Albion Energy, which won a Maltese offshore licence in 2023.
interesting_fact: Heritage Oil found hundreds of millions of barrels in Uganda and up to ~3bn barrels recoverable in Kurdistan; Heritage's prospectus says he advised Angola's government from 1989 and helped set up Sonangol, the national oil company.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in the oil industry as a North Sea diver in the 1970s before launching Heritage Oil in 1992.
notes: Very private; no website or published contact found for Albion Energy (UK Companies House: Albion Energy Limited 09187547). Press coverage routinely references his past links to private military firms Executive Outcomes/Sandline - sensitive; avoid in outreach. Alive status inferred from 2023 Malta licence news; no death reports found.

name: Claiborne P Deming
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Murphy Oil Corporation (since 2012); Director, Murphy USA Inc.
profile: Louisiana-born lawyer (Tulane BA 1976, JD 1979) and nephew of Murphy Oil's longtime head Charles H. Murphy Jr. He joined Murphy Oil as a staff attorney and was President & CEO from 1994 to 2008, tripling production and reserves, expanding into Malaysia and starting the Walmart gas-station tie-up that became Murphy USA. He is now board chair of Murphy Oil and a Murphy USA director.
interesting_fact: He conceived the El Dorado Promise, a $50M Murphy Oil-funded pledge (2007) covering in-state college tuition for every El Dorado (Ark.) High graduate. By 2016, 84% of eligible students went to college and AP offerings grew from 3 to 19 classes.
deep_cut_fact: After Hurricane Katrina in 2005 he had Murphy hire a security firm to rescue employees trapped in its flooded New Orleans office; 83 people were brought out that Friday. Earlier, Murphy's exploration under him found the ~500M-barrel Kikeh field off Borneo (2002), the largest reserve add in company history.
notes: Inducted into the Arkansas Business Hall of Fame. Former chair of the National Petroleum Council. Also a senior advisor to TPH Partners (energy PE). Wealth estimate comes from SEC insider holdings. Approach via Murphy Oil corporate communications/IR in Houston.

name: Gao Zhendong (高振东, Don Gao)
current_role: Founder and CEO/president, Positec Group (宝时得, Suzhou), maker of WORX, Rockwell and Kress tools (latest confirmed reporting ~2016)
profile: Founder of Suzhou-based Positec (Chinese name 宝时得), started in 1994 as a power-tool exporter. He opened a Suzhou factory in 1995 making OEM tools for Sears, B&Q, OBI and Black & Decker, then built own brands: WORX (launched 2004) and the acquired US brand Rockwell. Positec, a major cordless and robotic-mower player, sells via Home Depot, Lowe's, Walmart and Costco.
interesting_fact: He chose to build Chinese-owned global brands rather than stay an OEM, deciding in 1999 to launch his own brand even though old customers would become competitors; WORX products were later reported to outsell Bosch in some German categories.
deep_cut_fact: The name 'Positec' is a play on 'Positive Technology'. To launch WORX he hired Vicenza-based Italian designer Paolo Andriolo for ergonomic products; the flagship was the WORX GT trimmer. He has said: 'Consumers don't care about the technology you put into products. They only care about whether it works well.'
notes: Identity: Hurun lists 高振东 of 宝时得 (Positec); English sources call Positec's founder 'Don Gao'. Same company, very likely the same person, but the Chinese/English name link isn't explicitly confirmed. Private company, little recent press; current title and status not confirmed after ~2016. Quote is from China Daily (2016). Energy angle: cordless battery platforms (Power Share).

name: Zhu Long
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and largest shareholder, YITU Technology (依图科技), Shanghai
profile: Computer-vision scientist (Leo Zhu) who co-founded YITU Technology in Shanghai in 2012. YITU became one of China's 'four AI dragons' in face recognition and later moved into medical AI and AI chips (its QuestCore inference chip) and large models. He holds a statistics PhD from UCLA under Alan Yuille and was a postdoc at MIT's AI lab before teaching at NYU.
interesting_fact: YITU's early break came from recognising cars with cloned licence plates before faces. Staff photographed about 50 vehicles a day on Shanghai streets to build a vehicle database, which won the company its first police client in Suzhou.
deep_cut_fact: He and YITU co-founder Lin Chenxi (an ACM ICPC world champion and Alibaba Cloud architect) were childhood friends. Both were born in 1978 and attended the same primary, middle and high school, Fuzhou's Yinghua school, for 12 years, then reconnected at a class reunion in late 2011.
notes: Keeps a low public profile. YITU is on the US Entity List (since 2019) over surveillance in Xinjiang, which makes outreach sensitive. Its STAR Market IPO was suspended and a Hong Kong IPO has been mooted. No sourced 2025-26 update on his role.

name: Sun Yanbin
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2020-2021) as sharing a fortune with Feng Kang from Aofei Data (奥飞数据, Shenzhen 300738), a Guangzhou-based IDC/data-center operator. Aofei's controlling shareholder and chairman is Feng Kang; no public role for Sun Yanbin at Aofei could be found in filings or press.

public_contacts.value: liuhy@ofidc.com (Aofei Data board secretary Liu Haiyan; securities rep fangmh@ofidc.com)

notes: Could not confirm who Sun Yanbin (孙彦彬) is or their link to Aofei Data beyond the Hurun joint listing with Feng Kang; possibly a family co-holder. Not in current management. If pursuing the Aofei story, Feng Kang (chairman/GM) is the relevant person, via the board secretary.

name: Jin Yong
current_role: Majority limited partner (55.33%) of Tianjin Xundu Venture Capital, a founding shareholder of Maxscend (卓胜微, SZSE 300782)
profile: Jin Yong (金勇) is a private investor whose Maxscend wealth comes through Tianjin Xundu Venture Investment Partnership, in which he held 55.33% as LP. Xundu co-founded Maxscend's Jiangsu operating company with Xu Zhihan and Yao Lisheng and held 7.77% before the 2019 IPO; the RF front-end chip stock's surge put him on Hurun's 2020-2021 lists.
interesting_fact: Tianjin Xundu was one of the three original cash investors that set up Jiangsu Maxscend (卓胜有限), alongside chairman Xu Zhihan and Yao Lisheng; it still held 1.81% of Maxscend at end-2025.
notes: Identified via Maxscend's 2019 IPO prospectus (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2019-06-03/1206323462.PDF) and Xundu's 2020 equity-change report: Jin Yong = 55.33% LP of Tianjin Xundu (GP: Wuxi Yuandu Venture Consulting, rep Wang Xuefeng). Hurun 2020-21 matches. Purely a financial investor with no public profile or role at Maxscend; not the novelist Jin Yong. Maxscend contact is only an indirect route.

name: Luo Chuankui
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Shanghai Nenghui Technology Co., Ltd. (能辉科技, SZSE ChiNext: 301046)
profile: Luo Chuankui (罗传奎, b. Sept 1966) is a Tsinghua-trained environmental engineer who founded Shanghai Nenghui in 2009, building it into a new-energy engineering and products firm (solar, wind, storage, EV heavy-truck battery swapping, power-plant environmental systems). He controls it via Shanghai Nenghui Investment Holding and holds ~35.4m shares directly.
interesting_fact: Nenghui's founding team all came from provincial power design institutes; the company has recently added data-centre infrastructure operation and AI/computing services to its registered business scope alongside storage and battery-swap equipment.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a PhD in environmental engineering from Tsinghua and is a professor-level senior engineer; before founding Nenghui he was chief design engineer and branch GM at the Zhejiang Electric Power Design Institute (1995-2002), then VP of Shandong Sanrong Environmental Engineering (2002-2008). He is rotating chairman of the Shanghai New Hushang Federation.
notes: Chinese-language outreach via company email/board secretary (罗联明) is the realistic route. Good fit for energy-storage and data-centre-power angle.

name: Shen Xueru
current_role: Chairman, Aoyang Group Co. (Zhangjiagang, Jiangsu); former actual controller of Jiangsu Aoyang Health (002172.SZ)
profile: Shen Xueru (沈学如, b. 1954) built Zhangjiagang-based Aoyang Group from wool textiles into viscose fibre (Aoyang Technology, listed 2007), hospitals and pharma logistics (now Aoyang Health). In Sept 2025 Aoyang Group agreed to sell 20% of Aoyang Health to a Zhangjiagang development-zone vehicle, handing control to local government.
interesting_fact: In 2007 he took Aoyang Technology public on the Shenzhen exchange, making viscose staple fibre the core of the 'Aoyang system', which later pivoted into private hospitals and healthcare.
notes: Aged ~72 and stepping back from the Aoyang listed companies (control of Aoyang Health passing to Zhangjiagang ETDZ). No personal/public channels found; the only route is Aoyang Health's board-secretary office via its Shenzhen exchange filings (cninfo). Low relevance to energy/data centers beyond Aoyang Shunchang link.

name: Shen Qing
current_role: Shareholder and acting-in-concert party to her father Shen Xueru in the Aoyang group; has worked in Aoyang Group's financial management centre
profile: Shen Qing (沈卿, b. 1979) is the daughter of Shen Xueru, founder of Zhangjiagang-based Aoyang Group (chemical fibres/viscose, later healthcare via Aoyang Health, SZSE: 002172). Hurun listed the family's wealth from 2011 to 2020. In September 2025 the family sold a controlling 20% stake in Aoyang Health to a Zhangjiagang ETDZ-backed vehicle, and control passed to the zone's management committee.
interesting_fact: The Aoyang group grew from viscose fibre in Zhangjiagang into listed businesses in healthcare (Aoyang Health) and metals and logistics (Aoyang Shunchang, 002245, now Shunchang). In 2025 the family handed control of Aoyang Health to the local development zone.
notes: Private family member with no public profile or interviews found. Weak fit for the podcast: textiles and healthcare, despite the data_center_ai tag. The IR email belongs to Aoyang Health, which the family no longer controls. Her father Shen Xueru (b. 1954) is the public figure.

name: Chen Haoyue
current_role: Early individual shareholder of Maxscend Microelectronics (卓胜微, SZSE 300782); holds no position at the company
profile: Chen Haoyue (陈皞玥, male, b. 1975) was an early shareholder of Maxscend's Cayman holding company and in 2015 moved his stake onshore, buying 4.5% of Jiangsu Maxscend for RMB500,000 at par. He held 4.09% before the 2019 Shenzhen IPO; the RF chipmaker's rise put him on Hurun's 2021 list (~US$530m).
interesting_fact: His roughly 4.5% Maxscend stake was acquired for just RMB500,000 in 2015 as part of the company unwinding its offshore Cayman structure, years before Maxscend became one of China's most valuable chip designers.
notes: Confirmed via Maxscend IPO prospectus and lawyer's work report on cninfo (listed as a natural-person shareholder, 'no position held'). Not in Maxscend's 2025 top-10 holders, so he has likely sold down. No public profile, background or role found; passive investor. Low priority for outreach.

name: Liang Dazhong
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Chippacking Technology / Qipai Technology Co. (SSE STAR: 688216), Dongguan
profile: Liang Dazhong, a veteran chip-packaging engineer, is the controlling shareholder of Qipai (Chippacking) Technology, an integrated-circuit packaging and testing company headquartered in Shipai, Dongguan and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market. He built it with Bai Ying (fellow director and co-holder) through a series of Shenzhen chip firms from 1997 onward.
interesting_fact: In late 2024 he sold a 5% block of Qipai and pledged to lend the after-tax proceeds back to the company to fund its development.
deep_cut_fact: He started as an engineer at Huayue Microelectronics (1984-1990), then spent seven years trading in the Shenzhen electronics market before founding Shenzhen Tianguang Microelectronics in 1997 - the forerunner of Qipai.
notes: Bai Ying (listed as co-holder) also worked at Huayue Microelectronics and the Shenzhen electronics market and is a Qipai director. IR email is the board secretary's (Wen Zhengguo). Small-cap; Hurun listing only in 2021.

name: Bai Ying
current_role: Non-independent Director, China Chippacking Technology (Qipai Technology, 688216.SH); director of its Hong Kong subsidiary
profile: Bai Ying co-controls Shenzhen-founded China Chippacking Technology (气派科技) with husband Liang Dazhong (chairman/GM). It is one of South China's largest domestic IC packaging-and-test firms and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021. She has been a director since 2013.
interesting_fact: Qipai defined its own chip package formats (Qipai and CPC series, and CDFN/CQFN) that shrink traditional DIP/SOP/SOT packages, and developed plastic packaging for GaN RF power amplifiers used in 5G MIMO base stations.
deep_cut_fact: Her chip career began in September 1983 at Huayue Microelectronics, where she worked until 1992 (her husband was an engineer there too) before the couple moved into sales in Shenzhen's electronics market and later founded their own packaging businesses.
notes: Low profile; husband Liang Dazhong is the public face. Company board secretary: Wen Zhengguo. Wealth is shared with Liang Dazhong. Contacts sourced from Eastmoney's F10 company data (exchange-filed info).

name: Tan Guanghua
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Hangzhou Raycloud Technology (光云科技, SSE STAR: 688365)
profile: A Central South University software-engineering graduate (class of 2004) and ex-Alibaba software engineer (2008-09), Tan Guanghua co-founded Raycloud in 2009 as one of China's first e-commerce SaaS vendors. Its tools (Chaoji Dianzhang, Kuaidi Zhushou, Kuaimai ERP) serve 4M+ merchants on Taobao, Tmall, JD, Pinduoduo and Douyin, and it is building DingTalk-based enterprise SaaS.
interesting_fact: When Raycloud listed on 29 April 2020 it was the 100th company on Shanghai's STAR Market, billed as A-shares' first e-commerce SaaS stock, and at 35 Tan became the STAR Market's youngest chairman.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2015, years before the IPO, his company gave RMB 1 million to his alma mater Central South University to set up the 'Raycloud Fund' at its School of Software, backing students in tech competitions and entrepreneurship.
notes: Only on Hurun lists in 2021; wealth now likely below the original threshold. IR email from company filings (via Eastmoney F10); board secretary Liu Yu.

name: Xing Libin
profile: Deceased. Xing Libin, the former coal magnate of Liulin, Shanxi, who controlled Liansheng Energy/Group, died in Shanghai in January 2023, according to Jiemian News. Liansheng filed for bankruptcy restructuring in 2013 and was reorganised as Jinliu Energy.
notes: Died January 2023 in Shanghai (source: https://m.jiemian.com/article/11268445.html). His former company was restructured as Jinliu Energy, and the remaining coverage is mostly negative (bankruptcy, detention, litigation). Not a podcast candidate.

name: Song Yuqing
current_role: Founder of Zhongdeng Group (中登集团), Xi'an; formally exited the group's shareholding and board in 2015 but reported to still run it; current status unclear
profile: Song Yuqing (宋玉庆, b. c.1960-62, Nantong, Jiangsu) started in petrochemicals and moved Zhongdeng into Xi'an real estate in 2001, building a 'petrochemicals + property' group that later spread into finance, tourism and film. A Hurun regular 2009-2015 and often in Shaanxi's top ten, he saw the group hit a debt crisis after taking on four urban-village redevelopment projects.
interesting_fact: Zhongdeng's first big Xi'an move was winning a 71-mu plot in the Economic & Technological Development Zone at auction in 2003 for RMB98m, billed then as 'the north city's first auction'; it became the Zhongdeng Jiayuan estate.
notes: Sensitive: NBD (Nov 2018) reports Zhongdeng became a court-listed defaulter (30+ enforcement cases, >RMB2bn) and Xi'an Intermediate Court searched its HQ in Oct 2018; in 2015 Song and family transferred group shares to his brother Song Yu (88%) and Shen Weiding (12%). Wealth likely much reduced. Searches found no recent (post-2018) news or official contact. Avoid as outreach target or approach with care.

name: Xun Jianhua
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of EGing PV (亿晶光电, 600537.SH); co-controller with family of Huayao PV (华耀光电)
profile: Xun Jianhua (荀建华, b. 1962) founded Changzhou-based EGing Photovoltaic in 2003, building an integrated wafer-cell-module chain and taking it public via a 2011 backdoor listing billed as one of the first A-share solar plays. He sold control in 2017 to Shenzhen property developer Gu Yaoming for a reported ~3bn yuan; his family now runs solar maker Huayao PV.
interesting_fact: He entered solar after China's 2001 'Brightness Program' rural electrification push, putting in 30m yuan in 2003 to found EGing, which added wafer (2005), cell (2006) and module (2007) lines in quick succession.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar, he took over a struggling local enterprise, overhauled its equipment, talent and products, and grew annual sales to nearly 100m yuan by 1999, earning a local reputation as a turnaround 'nengren' (go-getter).
notes: Off Hurun lists since 2017. Alive status not explicitly confirmed (no reports of death; family co-controls Huayao PV per its 2023 ChiNext prospectus, which named him a co-controller). Was publicly reprimanded by regulators in 2018 over EGing disclosures; avoid. No published personal/office contact found.

name: Zhu Danfeng
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2010-2012 jointly with Qiu Yibo, with wealth attributed to Hengyi Group (Hangzhou; polyester, PTA and petrochemicals; listed arm Hengyi Petrochemical, SZSE 000703, now chaired by Qiu Yibo). No filing, news or profile naming her in connection with Hengyi could be found, so her role and relationship to the Qiu family are unconfirmed.
notes: Probably a Qiu family member or relative (Hengyi's controlling shareholder in filings is Qiu Jianlin), but this is unverified, so do not assume it. She has not appeared on rich lists since 2012. Approach Hengyi via Qiu Yibo or company IR instead.

name: Dong Li
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Executive Director, Leoch International Technology (HKEX: 842)
profile: Dong Li founded Shenzhen-born battery maker Leoch in 1999 and listed it in Hong Kong in 2010. Leoch is China's top lead-acid battery exporter (100+ countries, ~$1.4B+ turnover) and has added lithium and energy-storage products for telecom, data-centre and grid use; he was re-elected executive director in 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2019 he announced a 4GW/yr lithium battery factory in Anhui aimed partly at telecoms and data centres, while backing bipolar lead technology via US startup Gridtential - insisting lithium 'will not kill lead.'
deep_cut_fact: At the gala of Leoch's first Global Battery Innovation Conference in Zhaoqing (Oct 2024, 1,500+ attendees) he surprised delegates by singing 'Auld Lang Syne' on stage, as reported by Batteries International.
notes: Strong fit for energy/data-center podcast (data-centre UPS batteries, UL 9540 energy storage). Frequent speaker at industry conferences (Asian Battery Conference, BCI) - conference organisers are a good route. enquiry@leoch.com is the general company enquiry address; IR site leochir.com.

name: Guo Jinglin
current_role: Minority shareholder (about 25%) of Nanjing Gpro (Jinpu) Investment Holding Group; no confirmed current executive role
profile: Guo Jinlin (郭金林; Hurun romanises it 'Guo Jinglin') and his brother Guo Jindong built Nanjing Gpro (Jinpu) Group, with interests in petrochemicals, titanium dioxide (listed Gpro Titanium) and real estate. He held about 25% of the group holding company. He last appeared on the Hurun China list in 2013.
interesting_fact: Through Gpro Investment the brothers were co-controllers of the Shenzhen-listed titanium dioxide maker Gpro Titanium; Gpro Investment owned 37.3% of it.
notes: Very little public information, and none recent. Press coverage centres on a past shareholder dispute between the brothers; avoid it in outreach. The group has also had recent debt-enforcement news. I found no published contact. Low priority.

name: Gao Zhu
current_role: Legal representative of Mengfa Energy Holding Group (蒙发能源控股集团), Ejin Horo Banner, Ordos, Inner Mongolia
profile: Inner Mongolia coal entrepreneur behind Mengfa Energy Holding Group, which started in 1998 by building the first local coal loading/dispatch station in the Shenfu-Dongsheng coalfield and grew into coal mining (e.g. Huhewusu mine), processing, transport and sales, plus agriculture, finance and newer carbon-fibre and hydrogen ventures. Listed on Hurun China 2012-2018.
interesting_fact: Mengfa's founding business was not a mine but a coal loading and dispatch station - the first locally built one in the Shenfu-Dongsheng coalfield, one of the world's largest coal basins.
notes: Identity based on business-registry info (cnpp.cn) naming 高柱 as Mengfa's legal representative; source is a user-compiled brand directory, so verify. No personal profile, press office or IR contact found (private company). Off Hurun list since 2018.

name: Zhang Zhenwu
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List 2008-2018 with wealth from 'Eastar' (petrochemicals and energy-saving equipment). An 'Eastar Holding Group' operates a refinery near Guangrao/Dongying, Shandong, but no source tying Zhang Zhenwu (张振武) to it, or to any named company, was found.
notes: Could not confirm the company's Chinese name or his role. Possible lead (unverified): Eastar Holding Group's refinery in Dongying, Shandong. Not to be confused with Dongguan-based Oriental Energy (东华能源). Needs Hurun's Chinese company name to research further.

name: Wu Shirong

No web source tying this name to a specific company could be found; a similarly named Henan Wanzheng Group (河南万政集团, Nanyang, founded 1995, real estate and road/bridge construction) exists, but no link to him could be confirmed.

He dropped off Hurun after 2018. Candidate company (unverified): Henan Wanzheng Group, profile at https://regional.chinadaily.com.cn/nanyang/2018-10/25/c_573007.htm. Not recommended for outreach without further verification.

name: Fan Jiangang
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder, Changshu Fengfan Power Equipment Co. (601700.SH); control sold to Tangshan Industrial Holding in 2024-2025
profile: Fan Jiangang built Changshu Fengfan Power Equipment in Jiangsu into a leading maker of power-transmission towers and steel structures for State Grid and China Southern Grid, later adding solar wafers. In 2024 he and his concert parties sold control to Tangshan's state-owned industrial holding group and in late 2025 agreed to sell their remaining 17.32% for about RMB 989M.
interesting_fact: Transmission towers and steel structures still make up over 84% of Fengfan's revenue, and the company is a regular winner of State Grid and China Southern Grid tenders - a play on China's ultra-high-voltage grid build-out.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 Fengfan co-founded China-Pakistan Energy (Suzhou) with Sichuan Energy Investment to develop and operate hydropower projects in Pakistan as a Belt and Road platform; a company he controlled also held a stake in the venture.
notes: No longer runs the company (chairman is now Wang Jianxiang per May 2026 board notice); alive per recent filings - he signed a share-transfer agreement on 13 Nov 2025 (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202512291810619356_1.pdf). Very private; no personal contacts or interviews found.

name: Zhang Guoqiang
current_role: Chairman (founder, legal representative), Beijing SinoHytec Co. (SSE STAR 688339 / HKEX 2402); deputy to China's National People's Congress
profile: Zhang Guoqiang co-founded SinoHytec in 2012 after working at Tsinghua-linked Beijing Qingneng Huatong; it became a leading Chinese maker of hydrogen fuel-cell engines for buses and trucks, partnering with Toyota, BAIC and FAW. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market (2020) and in Hong Kong (2023); as an NPC deputy he lobbies for hydrogen-highway pilots.
interesting_fact: SinoHytec was a key supplier for the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics; Zhang said ~1,200 hydrogen vehicles and 20 refuelling stations were used during the Games, logging 3.75 million km.
deep_cut_fact: Under his leadership SinoHytec co-launched the world's first fuel-cell tram in 2014 and China's first fuel-cell logistics vehicle in 2015, and in 2018 initiated the China Hydrogen Alliance; it joined the global Hydrogen Council in 2019.
notes: Public-facing as an NPC deputy; regularly speaks at hydrogen forums - conference appearances may be a good route. Tsinghua MPA (2010) and CAS PhD (2017) appear in an executive-resume listing but not fully verified.

name: Yogesh Mehta
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Petrochem Middle East (Dubai); son Rohan Mehta is Managing Director
profile: Mumbai-born chemistry graduate Yogesh Mehta moved to Dubai in 1990 and co-founded Petrochem Middle East with British partner David Lubbock, building the region's largest independent petrochemical distributor (~$1.5-2bn turnover). Since 2025 he is chairman while son Rohan runs the firm; in Jan 2026 it opened an AED300m Jebel Ali terminal with DP World.
interesting_fact: Petrochem's new ~US$82m Jebel Ali terminal and headquarters, inaugurated with DP World in January 2026, consolidates its storage and logistics under Dubai's D33 economic agenda.
deep_cut_fact: He landed in Dubai on March 15, 1990, aged 29, on a Dh2,000 monthly salary at a small chemicals business; before launching Petrochem he compiled a 'business file' on which chemicals the UAE imported and exported to pitch investors. He has called partner David Lubbock 'like a brother'.
notes: Gives regular media interviews (Gulf News, CNBC Arabia, Arabian Business). No official company website/contact could be verified (petrochemme.com is parked). Day-to-day leader is now Rohan Mehta; CEO listed as Venu Nayar in Jan 2026.

name: Scott D Sandell
current_role: Executive Chairman & Chief Investment Officer, New Enterprise Associates (NEA); director, Cloudflare and Coursera
profile: Joined venture firm NEA in 1996, ran its tech practice for a decade, then served as Managing General Partner (2017-23) and CEO (2023-24); now Executive Chairman and CIO. He led or backed Bloom Energy, Cloudflare (board since 2010), Robinhood, Salesforce, Tableau and Workday.
interesting_fact: He was an early backer and board member of fuel-cell maker Bloom Energy - now a major on-site power supplier to AI data centres - as well as of Cloudflare, whose network sits in front of a large share of the web.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond investing he is an adjunct lecturer at Stanford, teaching a course on 'principled entrepreneurship', and a founding director of Venture Forward, the NVCA's nonprofit; asked what keeps him grounded, he answered 'My regular failures as an investor'.
notes: Net worth is SEC-insider-derived (largely fund-held). NEA's media contact is the cleanest route. Ex-NVCA chairman (2014-15). A Stanford NVCA speaker bio (https://conferences.law.stanford.edu/vcs2020/speakers/scott-sandell/, blocked here) reportedly lists BCG, C-ATS Software Europe and Microsoft PM (Windows 95) - verify first.

name: Wen Kezhon
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2008-2012 as Wen Kezhong (温克忠), coal, 'Golden Rock Group'. I couldn't confirm the person or the company in public sources. The likeliest match is the Xiaoyi (Shanxi) 'Golden Rock' (金岩) coal/coal-chemical group (e.g. 孝义市金岩电力煤化工有限公司), but no source names him.
notes: Name spelled 'Wen Kezhon' in input (likely Wen Kezhong). Several Chinese and English searches turned up nothing linking him to Golden Rock/金岩. The Shanxi coal sector was heavily consolidated by the state after 2009, and he has been off the lists since 2012. Not a viable outreach target without local-language company-registry research.

name: Meng Kai
current_role: No current public corporate role; former founder/chairman of Xiang E Qing (later renamed Cloud Live Technology / 中科云网, SZ002306)
profile: Meng Kai (孟凯), from Ezhou, Hubei, grew Xiang E Qing from a tiny 1994 Shenzhen eatery into a high-end restaurant chain that in 2009 became the first private Chinese restaurant firm on the A-share market. After 2012 austerity rules hit banqueting, he renamed it Cloud Live (中科云网) in a failed 2014 big-data pivot and later lost control of it.
interesting_fact: On its 2009 listing day Xiang E Qing closed with a market value above RMB 5.3bn, making Meng Kai, with about RMB 3.94bn, China's richest restaurateur at the time.
deep_cut_fact: Xiang E Qing ('Hunan-Hubei love') was named for the romance between Meng, a Hubei native, and his Hunanese wife; it began in 1994 as a 40-sq-m, four-table shop in Shekou with a stove he built himself, and he used a computer to tally dish sales daily, dropping the five worst sellers every month.
notes: Listed under data_center_ai only because of the 2014 'Cloud Live' big-data rebrand; he is really a restaurateur. Career includes a 2015 bond default, a CSRC investigation and loss of his shares: sensitive, likely a poor fit for the podcast. No published contacts found.

name: Zheng Xiongbin
current_role: Unknown
profile: Listed once on the 2014 Hurun China Rich List (RMB-equivalent ~$500m) with wealth attributed to CEFC China Energy (华信能源), the Shanghai oil-trading and finance conglomerate founded by Ye Jianming. No public source found confirming his role at CEFC or any current activity.
notes: Could not verify identity beyond the Hurun listing; searches (English/Chinese) returned nothing on 郑雄斌. CEFC China Energy collapsed in 2018 after its founder was detained and its units entered liquidation, so there is no live corporate channel. Low priority.

name: Jia Lingxia
current_role: Executive Director and Chief Operating Officer, Boer Power Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 1685)
profile: Jia Lingxia (b. c.1973) is a co-controlling shareholder and executive director of Wuxi-based Boer Power, a maker of electrical distribution equipment and power-efficiency solutions. She joined the founding Wuxi Boer business in 1995 and, as COO, oversees sales and marketing; chairman/CEO Qian Yixiang is her husband.
interesting_fact: She has been on Boer Power's board since February 2010, ahead of its Hong Kong IPO, and has spent three decades in China's electrical-distribution equipment business.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Wuxi Boer in August 1995 she briefly headed the accounts department at Wuxi Special Ventilation Machine Factory, having just earned a business-management diploma from Jiangnan University that year.

public_contacts.value: Financial PR (HK) Limited (Boer Power's investor and media relations consultant)
ron.chan@boerpower.com (company secretary, published for shareholder correspondence)

notes: Not chairwoman: husband Qian Yixiang is chairman/CEO and the company's public face. Hurun listing only 2014-15; wealth likely well below that peak now. The company-secretary email is published for shareholder matters; use the IR/PR consultant for media requests.

name: Qian Yiqing
current_role: Likely = Qian Yixiang (錢毅湘), Chairman and CEO of Boer Power Holdings (HKEX: 1685)
profile: Hurun's 'Qian Yiqing' of Boer Power appears to be Qian Yixiang, who chairs and runs Wuxi-based Boer Power, a maker of electrical distribution equipment and intelligent power-distribution solutions listed in Hong Kong in 2010. He joined predecessor Wuxi Boer Power Instrumentation in 1995 and runs it with his wife Jia Lingxia (COO) and father Qian Zhongming, a founding member.
interesting_fact: Boer Power is a family-run grid-edge business: father (a founding member of Wuxi Boer), son (chairman/CEO) and daughter-in-law (COO) all sit on the board as executive directors.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Wuxi Boer in July 1995, the same year he finished a business-management diploma at Jiangnan University, and was made general manager in January 1998 while still in his mid-20s.
notes: Name mismatch: no 'Qian Yiqing' found in Boer filings; the chairman is Qian Yixiang (aged 52 per 2025 annual report) - treat identity as probable, verify before outreach. Only on Hurun China 2014-15; fortune much reduced since. No published email found in the annual report.

name: Ge Yuesheng
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, BIT (formerly Matrixport), Singapore
profile: Ge Yuesheng (John Ge) joined Bitmain in 2015 as investment director (blockchain/AI deals, IR, strategy). In 2019 he co-founded Matrixport with Bitmain co-founder Jihan Wu; the Singapore digital-asset firm (custody, trading, wealth management, tokenised RWA) rebranded as BIT in March 2026 and is exploring a US listing.
interesting_fact: BIT (ex-Matrixport) is a unicorn managing over US$6B in assets, with licensed entities spanning Singapore, Hong Kong, Switzerland, the UK, the US and Bhutan; Ge says the name stands for 'Bridge into Tomorrow'.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto he started out in venture capital: after graduating in business administration from Hangzhou Dianzi University in 2013, he worked as an investment analyst at Beijing's Aowen Venture Capital (2013-14), then joined Bitmain in January 2015.
notes: Goes by John Ge in English. Fit: crypto-mining hardware (Bitmain) background; BIT also references mining infrastructure. press@bit.com is the newest contact (Mar 2026); pr@matrixport.com used through 2025. Early-career details come from IQ.wiki, a crypto wiki; Bitmain internship claim from bnext.com.tw (https://www.bnext.com.tw/article/73543/matrixport-web3).

name: Fu Qiming
current_role: Chairman, Sino Wealth Electronic Ltd. (中颖电子, SZSE ChiNext 300327); control transferring to Shanghai Zhineng Industrial Electronics after 2025 share sale
profile: Hong Kong-citizen chip designer (b. 1958) who built Shanghai-based Sino Wealth, founded in 1994 and listed on ChiNext in 2012, into a supplier of MCUs, lithium-battery management chips and display drivers used in smart meters for China's State Grid, appliances and e-bikes. He held ~18.5% via Weilang International; in 2025 he agreed to sell control (~RMB 1.25B) to state-backed Zhineng Industrial Electronics.
interesting_fact: Sino Wealth's smart-meter chips are widely used across China's State Grid and China Southern Grid, and its battery-management chips go into phones, earbuds, power tools and e-bikes; it has paid dividends every year since its 2012 IPO, distributing over half its cumulative profit.
deep_cut_fact: A chip designer since 1983: after a telecom-engineering degree from Taiwan's National Chiao Tung University he worked as an IC design engineer at UMC, then as a senior engineer in Philips' IC design group, before returning to UMC as an IC design project manager. He once said a good boss just keeps the company stable, staff happy and shareholders rewarded.
notes: Low media profile. Following the 2025 control transfer he may step back from Sino Wealth; check current board status. Chips angle fits data-center/AI focus only loosely (MCUs/BMS, not AI accelerators).

name: Lu Guojian
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Chipsea Technologies (Shenzhen) Corp. (芯海科技, SSE STAR: 688595)
profile: Lu Guojian (卢国建) is a former Huawei chip engineer who founded Shenzhen-based Chipsea in 2003 to build domestic high-precision ADC (analog-to-digital) chips; it now designs full signal-chain chips - ADCs, MCUs and health-measurement AIoT chips - and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020. He remains chairman (still active in 2026).
interesting_fact: Chipsea first broke through by supplying chips for smart body-fat and weighing scales to Huami (Xiaomi ecosystem) and Huawei, and in 2021 became one of the first HarmonyOS Connect ISV partners signed by Huawei; he said a third of its health-AIoT revenue came from HarmonyOS.
deep_cut_fact: At Huawei he was deputy chief engineer of the Basic Research Department and director of the digital-analog products department - the unit that became HiSilicon; Chipsea's first 24-bit high-precision ADC took three years of R&D to ship.
notes: Gives occasional interviews to Chinese financial press (NBD). Chipsea site blocks automated access, so IR email not captured - check the 'Investor Relations' page or SSE filings (board secretary office) manually. Analog/MCU focus rather than data-center chips.

name: Jim Justice II
current_role: U.S. Senator (R) for West Virginia since January 2025; former two-term Governor of West Virginia (2017-2025)
profile: Jim Justice inherited and grew his family's coal business (Bluestone), which still owns mines in several states, and bought the Greenbrier Resort out of bankruptcy in 2009. Elected WV governor in 2016 as a Democrat, he switched to the GOP in 2017 and won a U.S. Senate seat in 2024; he sits on the Energy & Natural Resources Committee.
interesting_fact: He has coached the Greenbrier East High School girls' basketball team since 2003, continuing while governor and as a senator; the team won the 2012 state title under him (and, per the West Virginia Encyclopedia, again in 2026).
deep_cut_fact: At Marshall University, where he earned a B.A. and MBA, he captained the golf team; his English bulldog Babydog, introduced at his 2021 inauguration, is described on his official Senate bio as 'the state's most famous four-legged celebrity'.
notes: Sitting U.S. senator; for an interview pitch, use the Senate press office (newsroom at justice.senate.gov) or the meeting-request form. His coal companies' unpaid debts and liens are widely reported, so avoid wealth topics. Senate Energy & Natural Resources Committee seat is the obvious podcast hook.

notes: Identity unconfirmed: 'Erdos' may refer to a different Ordos-based (coal/energy) business or a romanisation mismatch. Erdos controller data: https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/600295/company.html. Kept minimal.

name: Cao Jianjun (曹建军)
current_role: Listed (2010) as head of Huifeng Xingye Investment Group (汇丰兴业投资集团), a Shanxi coal group; current role unverified

The related Shanxi Huifeng Xingye Coking Coal Group (Lüliang, founded 2008) mines and washes coking coal and runs coal-bed methane, logistics and tourism businesses. He has been off Hurun lists since 2013.

Common name; treat identity details beyond the Hurun listing as unconfirmed. Low priority.

name: Hu Yishuo
current_role: Unknown; former Bitmain founding-team member, shareholder (~4.18%) and member of its board of supervisors
profile: Hu Yishuo (胡一说) was one of Bitmain's early founding-team members and, per its 2018 Hong Kong IPO prospectus, its sixth-largest shareholder with ~4.18%, which put him on Hurun's China list in 2018-19. He later resigned from Bitmain's board of supervisors in a board reshuffle; his current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Bitmain's 2018 IPO filing showed a tight founder group: Micree Zhan ~36%, Jihan Wu ~20%, then Zhao Zhaofeng 6.26%, Ge Yuesheng 4.18% and Hu Yishuo 4.18%.
notes: Extremely low profile; virtually no public statements, interviews or social accounts found. Only verifiable traces are Bitmain shareholder/supervisor disclosures. Identity as the Bitmain shareholder is consistent with the listing, but nothing personal could be confirmed; no reachable public contact.

name: Manuel Alba
current_role: Independent Chair of the Board, Astera Labs (NASDAQ: ALAB), since March 2018
profile: Veteran semiconductor founder and board member (also listed as Manuel Alba-Marquez). Co-founded Galileo Technology in Israel and was its President 1994-2001 (sold to Marvell), then sat on Marvell's board. He later served on boards of Annapurna Labs (acquired by Amazon) and Habana Labs (acquired by Intel), and has chaired AI-connectivity chipmaker Astera Labs since 2018.
interesting_fact: He has been on the board of three Israeli chip startups bought by tech giants — Galileo (Marvell), Annapurna Labs (Amazon, whose chips became AWS Graviton/Nitro) and Habana Labs (Intel) — before chairing Astera Labs through its 2024 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: Before Astera, he was a co-founder, director and President of Israeli networking-chip company Galileo Technology (1994-2001); he has also been a director of Canadian asset-management software firm Copperleaf Technologies since 2010.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Very strong fit for data-center/AI topic (PCIe/CXL retimers, Scorpio fabric switches). Company emails are named IR/PR contacts as published in Astera press releases; verify before use. ir.asteralabs.com blocks automated fetches.

name: Michael Truett Tate
current_role: Former CFO of Astera Labs (ALAB), retired as CFO 2 Mar 2026; strategic advisor to CEO Jitendra Mohan through 1 Sep 2026
profile: Veteran Silicon Valley semiconductor CFO (Cal Poly SLO accounting grad) who joined Astera Labs, maker of PCIe/CXL connectivity chips for AI data centres, as CFO in July 2020 and took it public in March 2024. Earlier CFO roles: Galileo Technology, interim CFO at Marvell, NetLogic (sold to Broadcom for $3.7bn) and Annapurna Labs. Handed the CFO job to Desmond Lynch in 2026.
interesting_fact: He has been finance chief through three notable chip exits: Galileo Technology (acquired by Marvell in 2001), NetLogic Microsystems (sold to Broadcom for $3.7bn after 400%+ revenue growth on his watch) and Annapurna Labs, before helping take Astera Labs public.
deep_cut_fact: He was CFO of Israeli chip start-up Annapurna Labs from June 2014 to January 2015 - the company Amazon acquired in 2015 and that went on to design AWS's Graviton and Trainium chips - and spent 2015-2020 as an angel investor/adviser to early-stage companies before joining Astera.
notes: Now effectively retired from Astera (advisor role ended Sept 2026), so company PR may not forward. Reportedly a member of Cal Poly's Center for Innovation & Entrepreneurship (unverified). Low social-media presence. Astera contact emails were confirmed via search snippets of press releases, not fetched directly.

notes: Can't identify. 'Yuantong' may be 远通 or 源通 (e.g. an Inner Mongolia company named 内蒙古源通长富煤业 exists in Wuhai, but no link to him was found). Dropped off Hurun after 2021. Needs a Chinese business-registry lookup by the journalist before any outreach. Low priority.

name: Li Xinhua
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Henan Lantian Gas Co. (SH: 605368) and Henan Lantian Group
profile: Born in Aug 1975, Li built Zhumadian-based Henan Lantian Group into a regional natural-gas business spanning long-distance pipelines (Yunan pipeline) and city gas distribution in southern Henan. He has chaired Lantian Group since 2006 and took Henan Lantian Gas public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in Jan 2021. A senior economist with an EMBA, he was a deputy to the 12th National People's Congress.
interesting_fact: He became chairman of Lantian Group in 2006 at about 31, and controls the listed gas company through Lantian Investment and Lantian Group (together roughly half the shares).
deep_cut_fact: Before entering the gas business he worked at the Zhumadian Public Security Bureau, then became a business supervisor at a liquefied-gas company and general manager of the Yunan (southern Henan) gas pipeline company.
notes: Regional player; Chinese-language outreach via the listed company's securities affairs office is the only realistic route. 2026 filings note heavy share pledges by the controlling holders - be aware of financial pressure. NPC deputy detail from third-party bio (maigoo), not an official filing.

name: Zhang Yinrong
current_role: Former vice chairman, Inner Mongolia Erdos Resources (SSE 600295) and VP of Erdos Group (left May 2014); no current role found
profile: Zhang Yinrong (张银荣, b. c.1953) is a long-time Erdos Group executive who ran the group's power company, then served as vice chairman of listed Erdos (cashmere, power, ferroalloy smelting) and group VP from 2011 until May 2014. He held 18.46% of Erdos Investment Holding Group, the controlling holder, around 2014-15. By 2019 he was no longer a shareholder.

deep_cut_fact: Before becoming vice chairman, he was general manager of the Erdos group's power company (电力公司), the arm behind its move from cashmere into electricity and metallurgy (per Erdos's 2013 annual report).
notes: Identity confirmed via cninfo filings of Erdos (600295): vice chairman 2011-2014 and an 18.46% holder of the parent in 2014 (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2015-04-02/1200779862.PDF). Replaced as parent shareholder by 2019 (Zhang Yiling). Contacts are the company's board-secretary IR emails, not his own. A different Zhang Yinrong was a director at GCI Science & Technology (002544). Retired and private.

name: Jiao Yun
current_role: Founder, actual controller and honorary chairman (since June 2026), Baotailong New Materials (SSE: 601011), Qitaihe, Heilongjiang
profile: Jiao Yun founded Baotailong, a Qitaihe, Heilongjiang coal-chemical company (coking coal, coke and derived new materials) that he co-established as a listed vehicle in 2003 and long chaired. In June 2026 the board named him honorary chairman, a non-director advisory role on strategy and industrial upgrading, as Jiao Qiang took over as chairman; he remains the actual controller.
interesting_fact: Baotailong's board describes Jiao as the founder who spent years 'deep in the coal-chemical industry' and notes he is a deputy to China's National People's Congress.

name: Tang Guoqiang
current_role: Former chairman (2011-2013) of Shunfeng Photovoltaic International (HKEX: 1165, now Shunfeng International Clean Energy); no current role found
profile: Tang Guoqiang (汤国强, b. c.1957), from Liyang, Jiangsu, chaired Shunfeng Photovoltaic International when it listed in Hong Kong in July 2011. Through his company Peace Link he owned about 29.65% of the solar-cell maker. He left the chair in mid-2013, before the group's 2014 takeover of Wuxi Suntech, and has kept no public profile since. Hurun listed him once, in 2014.
interesting_fact: He came to solar late. His earlier jobs were running Liyang Economic Development Corp (metals wholesale, 1990-96), deputy GM of a Liyang fine-chemicals maker (1996-2003) and a director of a Zhenjiang property developer (2003-07). He joined Jiangsu Shunfeng PV's board only in April 2010.
deep_cut_fact: Per the company's 2011 annual report, his formal education ended with a high-school diploma from Jiangsu Province Liyang Middle School in 1977, the year China restored the national college entrance exam.
notes: Identity confirmed from Shunfeng PV's 2011 annual report on HKEX (chairman; 100% owner of Peace Link, which held 29.65%). MarketScreener shows his chairmanship ending 1 Jul 2013. No current activity or published contact found. Not the actor Tang Guoqiang. The '1977 college-exam' note is historical context, not a claim about him.

name: Huang Mingsong
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (about 24.6%), CSG Smart Science & Technology (科大智能, 300222.SZ), Shanghai
profile: Huang Mingsong (黄明松), born 1971, holds a master's degree. He leads CSG Smart Science & Technology, founded in Shanghai in 2002 with links to the University of Science and Technology of China. Listed in 2011, it makes smart power-distribution automation, EV charging and energy management systems, industrial robots and logistics automation; JD Logistics is a strategic investor.
interesting_fact: CSG Smart combines grid tech (distribution automation, EV energy management) with industrial robots and logistics automation; JD Logistics invested about RMB 618m as a strategic investor in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Before scaling CSG Smart he ran a cluster of USTC-linked ventures, including Anhui Keda Luneng Technology and Anhui Keda Smart Grid Technology. He also sits on the board of the Shanghai Fuke Intelligent Robot Research Institute.
