A 2026 report says Wang Tingting succeeded him as president (CEO) ahead of a Hong Kong listing application; he remains chairman per the latest board filings we found. IR email is the board-secretary address from the Jan 2025 board-election notice.

name: Zhang Yaping
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Shanxi Donghui Energy Group (coal, coking, non-ferrous metals, new materials, cultural tourism)
profile: Shanxi entrepreneur Zhang Yaping (张亚平) started in coal trading and mine acquisitions, then founded Donghui in 2003. It was once China's largest stamp-charged coke producer and now has about 19bn yuan in assets. The group spans coal, non-ferrous metals, new materials and tourism, and holds 7.5% of Shanghai-listed Kexin Development.
interesting_fact: In 2013 Donghui paid A$160M for an Australian copper-gold miner, making it the first private Shanxi company to buy mines overseas. The group has since added Wutai Mountain tourism, a Marriott hotel, EV in-wheel motors and modern agriculture.
deep_cut_fact: Hurun's 2017 business-jet owners report listed him with an Embraer Legacy 650, then the only private jet owned by a Shanxi tycoon. He first built capital as a coal trader and by buying the Dengjiazhuang mine in Liulin county.
notes: Very private; no official group website or press contact found. In June 2026 Shanxi securities regulators fined Donghui's investment arm over undisclosed share buying in Kexin Development. Approach cautiously, in Chinese. Hurun's 'Donghui Coal Coking & Chemicals' (2010-12) now trades as Shanxi Donghui Energy Group.

name: Yan Shengjun
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, China Tianying Inc. (000035.SZ)
profile: Yan Shengjun (严圣军) built Tianying from Jiangsu into a listed environmental-energy group (China Tianying, Shenzhen-listed) focused on waste-to-energy incineration, sludge and food-waste treatment. Under him it has pivoted into new energy, licensing Energy Vault's technology to build a 25MW/100MWh gravity energy storage plant in Rudong, Jiangsu, connected to the grid in 2024.
interesting_fact: China Tianying's Rudong plant is billed as the world's first commercial-scale gravity battery: cranes lift composite blocks made partly from waste (soil, coal ash, fibreglass from retired wind blades) when power is cheap and lower them to generate power later.
deep_cut_fact: At the March 2022 groundbreaking Yan said the project would help Rudong become a Yangtze Delta 'zero-carbon industrial centre'; Tianying's deal with Rudong county also covers tidal-flat solar, offshore wind, hydrogen and a zero-carbon data centre.
notes: Strong energy/data-center fit (gravity storage, zero-carbon data centre plans). Low personal media profile; no personal channels found. Company site ctyi.com.cn was unreachable from here; route via China Tianying IR / board office. Hurun listed wealth jointly with Mao Hongju.

name: Mao Hongju
current_role: Director and Vice President, China Tianying Inc. (SZSE: 000035), Hai'an, Jiangsu; joint actual controller with husband Yan Shengjun
profile: Mao Hongju (b. 1968) and husband Yan Shengjun, the chairman, control China Tianying via two Nantong holding companies. Tianying grew from waste-to-energy and environmental services into a 2014 reverse-merger listing spanning wind, solar, green hydrogen/ammonia and gravity storage. She has been a director and VP since 2014.
interesting_fact: China Tianying is Energy Vault's partner on the 25 MW/100 MWh gravity energy storage system in Rudong, Jiangsu, next to a wind farm; it was connected to the State Grid in Dec 2023 and billed as the first commercial utility-scale non-pumped-hydro gravity storage plant.
deep_cut_fact: Unlike many founder-spouses listed as passive shareholders, she holds professional titles as a senior engineer and senior economist, and has served as Tianying's vice president since its 2014 listing (per her 2026 board nomination resume).
notes: Husband Yan Shengjun (chairman) is the public face. IR email is that of board secretary Lu Ping as published in the 2026 interim report (securities rep: zhangmma@cnty.cn). IR email is the reliable route.

name: Lu Hongping
current_role: Major individual shareholder (~2.35% at end-2025) of GoodWe Technologies (688390.SH); controller of Kunshan-based precision-electronics firms
profile: Lu Hongping (卢红萍, b. 1969) is a passive top-10 shareholder of GoodWe, the Suzhou maker of solar inverters and energy-storage systems founded in 2010. Her stake came largely from husband Tu Haiwen, one of GoodWe's five founding shareholders, who transferred his 8.76m shares to her in 2018. She also controls precision-electronics and investment firms in Kunshan and Shenzhen.
interesting_fact: GoodWe was set up in November 2010 by five individuals including chairman Huang Min and Tu Haiwen (who put in 4m yuan for 20%), and grew into one of China's leading PV inverter and home energy-storage brands, listing on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond GoodWe, GoodWe's IPO prospectus lists her as actual controller of Kunshan Tianyaze Precision Electronics, Shenzhen Tianyaze Precision Electronics and Anhui Deying Electrical Technology, plus investment vehicles Kunshan Hanzetai and Kunshan Handing.
notes: Not an executive or director of GoodWe; a passive investor with no public profile. GoodWe chairman/CEO Huang Min is the more relevant guest for an energy podcast. She has been reducing her GoodWe stake (sold ~3.6m shares in 2025). Only route found is GoodWe IR.

name: Shen Jie
current_role: Largest shareholder (about 8.75%, about 10.7% with concert party Beijing Hongyu Rongji VC) of Jiangsu Nata Opto-electronic Material Co. (南大光电, SZSE: 300346)
profile: Shen Jie (沈洁) is a pre-IPO investor and the largest shareholder of Nata Opto-electronic, a Jiangsu maker of MO sources, electronic specialty gases (e.g. phosphine/arsine) and ArF photoresists for chipmakers. Nata has no controlling shareholder. She appears to be a passive investor rather than an executive.
interesting_fact: Nata, where she is the top shareholder, said its ArF photoresist was the first domestically made one to pass customer certification (tested on 50nm flash memory, 2020), challenging an import-dominated market.
notes: Very private; no interviews or bio found. Exchange filings (June 2026, https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202606291826547570_1.pdf) confirm her as Nata's largest 5%+ shareholder. Common name, so be careful with other 'Shen Jie's. The company website lists a general inbox, natainfo@natachem.com, which is a company contact, not hers.

name: Zhu Guangping
current_role: Private investor based in Shenzhen; actual controller of Dangtu Xinshi Emerging Industry Fund, an early ~4.25% shareholder of Trina Solar (688599.SH)
profile: Zhu Guangping (朱广平) is a Shenzhen businessman and investor. Trina Solar's 2021 convertible-bond prospectus names him as actual controller of Dangtu Xinshi Emerging Industry Fund, which held about 4.25% of Trina after its 2020 STAR Market listing. That stake explains his single 2021 Hurun listing. Filings link him to duty-free retail, Guowei Electronics, microfinance and food-import companies in Shenzhen.
interesting_fact: His Trina stake came through a private fund, not a solar company. Trina's prospectus lists more than 20 firms he controlled or helped run, from China Duty Free joint ventures in Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Urumqi to Comvita Food (China), the mainland arm of the New Zealand manuka-honey brand.
deep_cut_fact: For years he was listed as the legal representative of Shenzhen China Duty Free Merchandise Co. and Zhuhai China Duty Free Merchandise Co., joint ventures in which state-owned China International Travel Service (now China Tourism Group Duty Free) held 30-50%.
notes: Identity resolved via cninfo filings. Not a Trina executive; he was a financial investor whose fund had sold down to under 5% by 2021. Other filings (Focus Media 2025-26 deal documents) show him as an indirect LP investor via Shenzhen Guangliwei Investment. Very private; no personal or office contact published. Common name: check before outreach.

name: Luo Jianqiang
current_role: Chairman & GM of Zhejiang Xinghuo Chemical; chairman of Zibo Zhongda Chemical; majority LP of Shanghai Chenxiang Investment Center (per 2015 filing)
profile: Luo Jianqiang (骆建强, b. 1965) is a Hangzhou chemicals entrepreneur and investor. He held 61.3% of Shanghai Chenxiang Investment Center (上海辰祥投资中心), which took 300 million shares (11.89%) in the 2014 court-led rescue of bankrupt Shanghai Chaori Solar. Chaori was relaunched under GCL as GCL System Integration (002506.SZ), which explains Hurun's 2015 solar listing.
interesting_fact: His vehicle was the second-biggest investor, after GCL, in the nine-member consortium that rescued Shanghai Chaori Solar. Chaori's March 2014 missed coupon was China's first onshore corporate bond default.
deep_cut_fact: His day job is chemicals, not solar: GCL System's 2015 filing lists him since 2012 as chairman and general manager of Zhejiang Xinghuo Chemical Co. and chairman of Zibo Zhongda Chemical Co. in Shandong.
notes: Resolved via cninfo: Hurun's 'Chenxiang' is 上海辰祥投资中心 (not 晨祥). Chaori default background: https://thediplomat.com/2014/03/its-official-chinas-chaori-defaulted. Other filings show a 骆建强 as a 2011 Joyson Electronics (600699) asset vendor and a shareholder of Haixing (603115); not confirmed as the same man. Private; no published contact.

name: Frank Hurst Lin
current_role: General Partner, DCM (venture capital); independent director of Vipshop; board/major holder positions in 51Talk and GigaCloud
profile: Hurst (Frank) Lin, 林欣禾, co-founded SINA (now Weibo) and served as its COO, then joined VC firm DCM as a general partner in 2006. His investments include Kuaishou, Vipshop, 58.com, GigaCloud (US IPO 2022), QuantaSing and 51Talk; he now focuses on AI and consumer-internet companies, splitting time between the US and Asia.
interesting_fact: SINA, which he co-founded and ran as COO, was the first venture-backed Chinese internet company to go public in the US; he oversaw its global business development and M&A.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in New York City, earned an engineering degree at Dartmouth, worked as an Ernst & Young management consultant in Silicon Valley, and co-founded SINA's predecessor SinaNet in 1995 after his Stanford MBA.
notes: Goes by Hurst Lin professionally (SEC filings: Frank Hurst Lin). Data-center/AI angle: DCM AI investing; GigaCloud is B2B e-commerce logistics. Best route via DCM or LinkedIn.

name: Zhang Xinming
current_role: Formerly chairman, Shanxi Jinye Coal Coking Group (山西金业煤焦化集团); no verified current role
profile: Zhang Xinming was chairman of Shanxi Jinye Coal Coking Group and was described as Shanxi's richest energy tycoon, appearing on Hurun China from 2005 to 2010. Reports since 2010 concern legal matters rather than business activity.
notes: Do not approach. Chinese media reported in Oct 2010 that he fled and was wanted by police (https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2010-10-26/400513.html); later reports cite organised-crime allegations. Off rich lists since 2010; current status unverified.

name: Luo Lin
current_role: Founder and chairman, Anton Oilfield Services Group (3337.HK)
profile: Petroleum engineer (Southwest Petroleum University; Tsinghua MBA, per MarketScreener) who left a secure job at state-owned CNPC in 1999 to found Anton Oilfield Services in the Tarim Basin. Anton grew into one of China's largest private oilfield-service firms, once dubbed 'China's Halliburton', and listed in Hong Kong in 2007. It now works for international clients in Iraq and elsewhere.
interesting_fact: Caixin reported that Anton was once dubbed 'China's Halliburton' and was a major player during the 'golden decade' of China's petroleum sector.
deep_cut_fact: He started out as an employee of state oil giant CNPC. In 1999 he gave up that 'iron rice bowl' job to start a private company selling services to CNPC itself, one of the first private entrants into China's state-dominated oilfield-services market.
notes: IR email from irasia.com (2015) and a 2011 company release; antonoil.com did not load, so currency is unverified. Hurun listing (2013-14) is old; his stake is now far smaller (~$90M per MarketScreener). Good oilfield-services angle; the 'China's Halliburton' line comes from a sector ups-and-downs piece, so keep framing positive.

name: An Yong
profile: Hurun China listed An Yong (安勇) in 2014-2017 at about $450M, with wealth from 'Tianyu' (coal and property). Searches in Chinese and English could not establish which Tianyu company this is (Shaanxi Tianyu Mineral Industry Group is one candidate) or confirm his role there.
notes: Identity unresolved and no public footprint found. He has not been on Hurun since 2017, possibly because coal-sector wealth fell. Not a viable outreach target without more identifying information.

name: An Mei
current_role: Private investor; former 5%+ shareholder of Beijing Ultrapower Software (神州泰岳, 300002.SZ)
profile: An Mei (安梅) is a private shareholder of Ultrapower, a Beijing IT-operations and software company founded in 1998 and listed on ChiNext in 2009. Her stake (6.47% in 2016) came from a 2013 property-division agreement, and its voting rights were entrusted to chairman Wang Ning. She sold down in 2016-2018 and fell below 5% in June 2018. She has no known operating role.
notes: Private individual, not an entrepreneur or executive, and her wealth derives from a personal settlement. I would not recommend outreach. Her only appearance on a rich list is Hurun China 2015. Not a fit for an entrepreneurship podcast.

name: Howard S Jonas
current_role: Chairman, IDT Corp; Chairman, Genie Energy; Executive Chairman, CEO & President, Rafael Holdings; director, Zedge
profile: Bronx-born serial entrepreneur (b. 1956, Harvard '78) who founded IDT in 1990 as an international call-back service and spun off Genie Energy (retail energy/solar), Zedge, Rafael Holdings and Straight Path (sold to Verizon for $3.1B in 2017). He chairs the group and leads Rafael's pharma efforts.
interesting_fact: He sold Straight Path Communications, a long-struggling spectrum company spun out of IDT, to Verizon for $3.1 billion in 2017 after a bidding war over its 5G-suitable millimeter-wave licenses.
deep_cut_fact: Asked about his first job, he said he had little jobs at the Bronx Zoo and a butcher shop, but his first real 'business' was a hot dog stand he opened at 14 near a local hospital - the origin of his 1998 memoir 'On a Roll: From Hot Dog Buns to High-Tech Billions'.
notes: Author of 'On a Roll' (1998) and 'I'm Not the Boss, I Just Work Here' (2006); generally open to media. Genie Energy is the energy hook (retail power/gas, solar). IDT contact emails are general corporate inboxes.

name: Sushil Kumar Kalyanji Parekh
current_role: Promoter-family shareholder of Pidilite Industries; director of family holding companies (e.g., Pidichem, Pargro Investments)
profile: Younger brother of Pidilite founder Balvant Parekh and part of the promoter family that controls Pidilite Industries, maker of Fevicol, M-Seal and Dr. Fixit. He worked with Balvant in the family's early dye and chemicals trading and served as Pidilite's Vice Chairman from 1969 to 2014. He now holds directorships in family investment companies.
interesting_fact: Pidilite's Fevicol, launched in 1959, became so widespread that 'Fevicol' is effectively India's generic word for white glue.
deep_cut_fact: He served as Vice Chairman of Pidilite Industries for 45 years, from 1969 to 2014.
notes: Elderly and very low-profile. No death report found, but there are no recent public appearances, so his status is unconfirmed. Sources disagree on whether he co-founded Pidilite in 1959 or joined early. The Pidilite investor-relations inbox is a company channel, not his own; Narendrakumar and Apurva Parekh are the family's public faces.

name: Cui Lianguo
current_role: Chairman, Inner Mongolia Jiutai Group (last confirmed 2013; current status not verified)
profile: Cui Lianguo (崔连国) heads Jiutai Group, an Inner Mongolia coal-chemicals company producing methanol and downstream materials in Ordos and Hohhot. He appeared on Hurun's China rich list 2009-2020 for the petrochemical business. Little recent English or Chinese coverage of him personally was found.
interesting_fact: In 2013 Jiutai chose GE's high-pressure coal gasification technology to double methanol capacity at its Ordos (Zhungeer Banner) plant to 1.5 million tonnes a year, which Cui pitched as a cheaper, cleaner way to make methanol.
notes: Very low profile; no official website or IR contact found for him (Jiutai Group is unlisted; HK-listed 2798 is a different company, Perennial/Jiutai Bangda coal). Current role and status should be checked before outreach.

name: Keith Kepler
current_role: Vice President (副总经理) & Head of Research Institute, Farasis Energy (Ganzhou) Co. (SSE STAR: 688567); director & CTO of Farasis Energy USA
profile: US battery scientist (b. 1967) who co-founded Farasis Energy in California in 2002 with Yu Wang and served as its CTO; the company moved manufacturing to Ganzhou, China, and became a major pouch-cell supplier for EVs (Daimler/Mercedes was an anchor customer), listing on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020. He was reappointed VP and head of Farasis' research institute in May 2025.
interesting_fact: Farasis started in Silicon Valley in 2002 and is now a Chinese STAR Market-listed EV battery maker; Kepler is a named inventor on many of its lithium-ion cell patents.
deep_cut_fact: Before Farasis he was a scientist at Argonne National Laboratory (1996-98) and then senior R&D director and scientist at early lithium-ion startup PolyStor Corp (1999-2001); he holds a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
notes: US citizen despite 'China' country tag. In 2025 he and co-founder entities agreed to sell a combined 5% Farasis stake to Guangdong state investors (Hengjian/Guangzhou Industrial). Technical, low-profile; IR route via board secretary Pan Lian.

name: Xu Zhiming
current_role: Chairman, Hong Kong Jiahao (Ka Ho) Group; former chairman and controlling shareholder of Sino Union Petroleum & Chemical (HKEX 346, later Sino Union Energy Investment) (last reported)
profile: Xu Zhiming (许智明), born 1964 in Gaozhou, Guangdong, moved to Hong Kong in the late 1980s and built Jiahao Group in property, finance and trade, then became an oil tycoon via Sino Union Petroleum & Chemical ('Sunpec'), which bought overseas oilfields. In 2009 he bought five coal mines for HK$3.66B, steering it toward coal and chemicals.
interesting_fact: A major poverty-relief donor (over HK$300M per his profile), he was honoured by China Post with a 7-envelope commemorative cover set, 'Xu Zhiming and China's Guangcai poverty relief', and received Hong Kong's Gold Bauhinia Star.
deep_cut_fact: He single-handedly financed the development of Fangji Island (放鸡岛), dubbed the 'Pearl of the South China Sea' off Guangdong, and was awarded an honorary doctorate and the Lomonosov Medal by the Russian Academy of Sciences.
notes: 'Sunpec' appears to be the abbreviation of Sino Union Petroleum & Chemical (中联石化). Little news after ~2010; last on Hurun list 2021. No published contacts found. Former CPPCC national committee member and Hong Kong JP.

name: Chen Guangbiao
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Jiangsu Huangpu Renewable Resources (Nanjing)
profile: Born 1968 to a farming family in Sihong, Jiangsu, Chen trained in Chinese medicine, patented a medical device, then in 2003 found he could profit from reselling steel from a demolition job. That became Jiangsu Huangpu Renewable Resources, a demolition and construction-waste recycling firm. He is best known as a flamboyant, highly publicized philanthropist.
interesting_fact: After the 2008 Sichuan earthquake he arrived early with 100+ staff and 60 excavators and hoists, personally rescued 13 survivors, and was named one of Forbes Asia's 48 leading Asia-Pacific philanthropists in 2008 and 2009.
deep_cut_fact: His first business, at age 10, was selling water in his village, earning about 0.3 yuan a day (nearly half an adult's daily wage at the time); at 13 he moved on to selling frozen food.
notes: Highly media-seeking (stunts like a 2014 bid to buy The New York Times); his philanthropy has been questioned by Chinese media, so vet claims. Last on Hurun lists in 2019. No verified official contact found; he historically courts press via his company in Nanjing. Recycling/demolition is only loosely related to energy.

name: Guo Xiangwen
current_role: Founder and former chairman/Party secretary of Shanxi Kangwei Group (Qinyuan County coal and coke); 65% sold to Yongtai Energy (600157.SH) in 2012; current role unverified
profile: Guo Xiangwen (郭向文) built Shanxi Kangwei Group from Qinyuan Kangwei Coal & Coke, set up in 2000 with him as legal representative. In 2012 Yongtai Energy paid RMB 2.895bn for 65% of Kangwei (a RMB 1.5bn capital injection plus RMB 1.395bn for 31% from Guo and employee share funds). He then held Yongtai shares (about 70m in 2014), and still appeared in its top-10 holders in 2020.
interesting_fact: Kangwei was a rural collective turned private company. Until 2012 three employee share-fund associations, one with about 420 worker members, owned about 36% of the group alongside Guo.
deep_cut_fact: Kangwei began as the Nanshan coal mine in Baizi town, Qinyuan County. It was restructured in 2000 into Qinyuan Kangwei Coal & Coke with registered capital of only RMB 820,000. Twelve years later Yongtai valued the group at billions.
notes: Identity confirmed via Yongtai Energy filings on cninfo (2012 acquisition report; 2015 notice that Guo personally paid the 2014 profit-guarantee shortfall: https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2015-06-24/1201186581.PDF). That payment is neutral but avoid it in outreach. Very local, low-profile Shanxi coal owner; no published contact. Kangwei is now a Yongtai subsidiary.

name: Pan Huarong
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Focus Lightings Technology (聚灿光电, SZSE: 300708), Suzhou
profile: Pan Huarong (潘华荣) built Focus Lightings from a small plant in Suzhou Industrial Park (founded 2010, ChiNext IPO 2017) into a leading LED epitaxial-wafer and chip maker, expanding counter-cyclically through three downturns. He is steering it toward a compound-semiconductor platform: Mini/Micro LED, auto lighting, AR, optical interconnect and space PV.
interesting_fact: Focus Lightings has taped out prototype Micro LED CPO (co-packaged optics) array chips with a strategic customer; Pan says AI data-center expansion will accelerate commercial optical interconnects.
deep_cut_fact: Known for a low-key, almost obsessive 'product-first' style, he told Shanghai Securities News in 2026: 'We don't chase being No. 1 in scale, but we pursue leadership in profitability' (我们不追求规模上的第一，但追求盈利能力上的领先).
notes: Good data-center angle (CPO/optical interconnect Micro LED chips; joint lab with CAS Suzhou Nano institute on optical interconnect and space PV). Company email is a general corporate address; IR materials at stocknotice.asp. Chinese-language approach advised.

name: Xie Yunkai
current_role: No current listed-company role found; formerly director of Dalian Energas Gas-System Co. (派思股份, SSE: 603318), now Shuifa Energas
profile: Xie Yunkai (谢云凯) was a board director of Dalian Energas Gas-System (natural-gas processing and gas-system equipment maker) from 2014 to 2019 and again 2020-2021, alongside chairman Xie Bing (谢冰). Hurun counted him among China's rich in 2015-2016, around Energas's 2015 Shanghai listing; control of the company later passed to Shandong's Shuifa Group.
notes: Low-profile; little coverage beyond board records (source: https://vip.stock.finance.sina.com.cn/corp/go.php/vCI_CorpManager/stockid/603318.phtml). Family relationship to chairman Xie Bing not verified. The Energas business is now under state-owned Shuifa Group, so there is no obvious current corporate route. Low priority.

name: Marc Murphy
current_role: Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Micron Technology
profile: Mark Murphy (listed here as 'Marc') has been Micron's CFO since 2022, running finance, treasury, tax, audit and investor relations as AI-driven demand for high-bandwidth memory pushed Micron to record results. He was previously EVP and CFO of Qorvo and held senior roles at Delphi Automotive, MEMC Electronic Materials and Praxair; his wealth stems from Micron equity.
interesting_fact: His career has spanned nearly every layer of the chip supply chain: semiconductor materials (MEMC), capital equipment, fabrication, and assembly and test, before landing at memory maker Micron.
deep_cut_fact: He is a U.S. Marine Corps veteran (Marquette BBA in finance, Harvard MBA) and serves on the Advisory Council of Boise State University's College of Business and Economics, in Micron's hometown.
notes: Name is spelled Mark Murphy by Micron. The 'Hurun Unicorn founders (2021)' tag in the input likely belongs to a different Marc Murphy; ignore. Press/IR contacts are Micron's media (Mark Plungy) and IR (Satya Kumar) leads named in the Sept 2026 earnings release.

name: Daniel Levy
current_role: Co-founder, Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI), Palo Alto / Tel Aviv (assumed match for the AI-unicorn listing)
profile: This record merges two different men. The AI-unicorn Daniel Levy is a former OpenAI researcher (led its Optimization team) who co-founded Safe Superintelligence (SSI) with Ilya Sutskever and Daniel Gross in June 2024; SSI reached a $30B valuation in March 2025 and announced a long-term compute partnership with Nvidia in July 2026. The 'Football' / Sunday Times 2020 entry is ex-Tottenham Hotspur chairman Daniel Levy (b. 1962).
interesting_fact: SSI calls itself the 'world's first straight-shot SSI lab' with one product (a safe superintelligence) and no product cycles; it uses Google Cloud TPUs and, from 2026, a strategic Nvidia partnership.
deep_cut_fact: (SSI Levy) He did the French prepa at Lycee Louis-le-Grand, then Ecole Polytechnique (applied maths/CS), an MS at Stanford with Stefano Ermon and a PhD with John Duchi on optimization and privacy; in 2017 he interned at Google Brain with Jascha Sohl-Dickstein and Matt Hoffman.
notes: IDENTITY MERGE: Sunday Times 2020 'Football' wealth (GBP ~421M) belongs to Tottenham's Daniel Levy, while the Hurun AI-unicorn listing is SSI's Daniel Levy; the profile above covers the SSI one given the data-center/AI focus. SSI is very low-profile; comms@ssi.inc is the only published press route. The Stanford email is self-published but from his PhD days and may be stale.

name: Shi Zhengrong
current_role: Founder, Sunman Energy (上迈新能源, Shanghai), maker of ultra-light flexible solar modules; founder and former chairman/CEO of Suntech Power
profile: Shi Zhengrong (施正荣, b. 1963, Yangzhong, Jiangsu) earned a solar PhD at UNSW, became an Australian citizen and returned to Wuxi in 2001 to found Suntech Power; its 2005 NYSE listing briefly made him China's richest man and helped spark China's solar boom. After leaving Suntech in 2013 he built Sunman Energy, which makes ultra-light solar panels, and still speaks widely on PV.
interesting_fact: Academic Lan Xiaohuan argues Shi's overnight wealth after Suntech's 2005 NYSE IPO had a 'strong demonstration effect' that prompted local governments across China to pour money into solar - seeding the industry China now dominates.
deep_cut_fact: He did his doctorate at UNSW's School of Photovoltaic and Renewable Energy Engineering under Professor Martin Green, the 'father of photovoltaics'; in 2009 he was elected a Fellow of the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering and won the Oslo Business for Peace Award.
notes: Great podcast fit (solar pioneer, Australia-China story) and historically media-friendly. Avoid Suntech's 2013 bankruptcy in outreach. No published email found (Sunman site is JS-only); route via Sunman's website contact page or conference organisers where he keynotes. Holds Australian citizenship.

name: Ma Guoli
current_role: Legal representative and controller, Shanxi Chenggong (Success) Investment Group; chairman, Shanxi Chenggong General Aviation (NEEQ: 834916)
profile: Ma Guoli (马国利, b. Oct 1967) is a Changzhi, Shanxi entrepreneur. Hurun's 'Victory' is a mistranslation of his Chenggong ('Success') Group. He made his money in coal (Changzhi Liansheng Xizhang Coal, Changzhi County Xishan Coal) and built 'one body, two wings': coal as the core, with Chenggong Auto (mini-trucks, plants in Changzhi and Zunyi) and Chenggong General Aviation as the wings. He still chairs the aviation arm.
interesting_fact: Chenggong General Aviation, which he founded in 2010, says it was the first fixed-wing general-aviation company listed on China's NEEQ (2015). It flies cloud-seeding and emergency-rescue missions with a 16-aircraft fleet that includes Y-12s, King Airs and Airbus H225 heavy helicopters.
deep_cut_fact: Before coal, he served in the People's Armed Police Changzhi detachment (Oct 1985-Nov 1988), then ran Changzhi Dafa Industrial Co. as general manager from 1991, per his official biography in Chenggong Aviation's 2024 annual report.
notes: Hurun lists him as 马国利 | 成功集团 | 原煤、汽车、航空 (2010 list: https://finance.ifeng.com/money/special/hurun2010/20101012/2698001.shtml). The email is the Chenggong Aviation board office (board secretary Xu Huating). 'Alive: yes' because he signed the 2024 annual report in April 2025. An aviation and EV-truck angle could interest the podcast.

name: Yu Nirong
current_role: Executive director of Shanghai Shengtian Enterprise Development; former chairman (2018-Nov 2022) and actual controller of Shanghai Topcare Medical Services (ex-600532.SH, delisted 2023)
profile: Yu Nirong (俞倪荣, b. c.1978) and Xie Yutong took control of Shanghai Hongda Mining (600532) in late 2017, when their Shanghai Shengtian bought its parent Shanghai Jingci. He chaired it from 2018 and renamed it Shanghai Topcare Medical Services, a mix of medical services and coal trading. That is the source of their 2021 Hurun listing. He resigned as chairman in Nov 2022, and the shares were delisted in June 2023.
interesting_fact: The listed shell he bought has had three identities: Shandong Huayang Technology, then Hongda Mining (iron ore), then Topcare Medical, which he steered toward healthcare.
notes: Identity confirmed via Topcare's 2022 annual report on cninfo (chairman; he and Xie Yutong named as actual controllers via Shanghai Shengtian). Caution: Topcare was delisted in 2023 after an audit disclaimer. SSE disciplined the company and Yu as controller/chairman ([2025] No. 21). Filings also record a debt settlement with Shennong (300189), now repaid. Not recommended for outreach; no positive deep-cut found.

name: Xie Yutong
current_role: No public role found; listed by Hurun (2021) jointly with her husband Yu Nirong as owner of Shanghai Topcare Medical Services (未来股份, SSE 600532, now delisted)

name: Jim Hay
current_role: Founder and chairman, JMH Group (Dubai-based private family business)
profile: Glasgow-born Dr James 'Jim' Hay (b. 1950) spent 27 years at BP, rising to senior executive, then in 2002 founded JMH Group and bought BP's construction-chemicals business Fosroc, later adding Savile Row tailors and wife Fitri's fashion label. Fosroc is now part of Saint-Gobain Construction Chemicals. Based in Dubai, the Hays are major racehorse owners.
interesting_fact: The Hays co-owned Ascot Gold Cup winner Fame and Glory (2011), and on that day were invited to join the Queen's royal procession in open carriages from Windsor Castle; in 2011 they also bought Birch Grove, Harold Macmillan's former Sussex home.
deep_cut_fact: A chemist by training (BSc and PhD in applied chemistry, University of Strathclyde), he effectively bought a piece of his old employer: JMH Group acquired Fosroc from BP in 2002, and Fosroc later built a technology centre in Bangalore (2007). Strathclyde inducted him into its Academy of Distinguished Entrepreneurs in 2013.
notes: Wealth listed jointly with wife Fitri Hay (major UK Conservative Party donor). No published personal, press or family-office contact found; JMH Group website did not load. Very private; racing connections (Uplands yard, Lambourn) are the most public facet. Fosroc ownership now Saint-Gobain.

name: Fitri Hay
current_role: Racehorse owner and co-owner (with husband Jim Hay) of Dubai-based JMH Group; founder of the Fitriani fashion label
profile: Fitriani 'Fitri' Hay, born in Jambi, Sumatra (Indonesia), is the wife of Glasgow-born ex-BP executive Dr Jim Hay, whose Dubai-based JMH Group owns construction-chemicals maker Fosroc and luxury brands (Ray Ward, Bernard Weatherill). The couple's wealth comes from oil-industry careers and JMH; they are major Flat and jumps racehorse owners and run Uplands yard in Lambourn.
interesting_fact: In 2011 the Hays bought shares in Irish Derby winner Cape Blanco and Fame and Glory; Fame and Glory won the 2011 Ascot Gold Cup on a day the couple were invited to ride in the Queen's royal carriage procession.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond racing, she has her own women's fashion design and retail label, 'Fitriani', which sits inside the family's JMH Group alongside Savile Row tailor Bernard Weatherill.
notes: Based in Dubai. Prominent Conservative Party donor (largest single donor to Liz Truss's 2022 leadership bid) - politically visible, handle accordingly. Rich List entry is joint with Jim Hay (oil/Fosroc). Best approach likely via racing circles or JMH Group; no published contact verified. Profile interview: Ccercle, Dec 2019 'Racing's Golden Couple'.

name: Wei Wenyuan
current_role: Retired; founding general manager of the Shanghai Stock Exchange and former chairman/acting president of Sinovel Wind (Huarui Fengdian)
profile: Wei Wenyuan (尉文渊) built the Shanghai Stock Exchange and was its first general manager when it opened on 19 Dec 1990, pushing electronic matching, paperless shares and T+0 trading. His rich-list wealth came from an early stake in wind-turbine maker Sinovel (via Tibet Xinmeng), which he briefly chaired in 2012-13. Retired as of 2020.
interesting_fact: At 35, with no finance background, he volunteered to build the Shanghai Stock Exchange in six months, insisted on computer-matched trading instead of open outcry, and personally struck the opening gong in 1990.
deep_cut_fact: He came up with Shanghai's famous '6'-prefixed stock codes on the spot, copying how Shanghai phone numbers had just gone from six to seven digits by adding a leading 6; he also says the idea for paperless shares came to him one morning while brushing his teeth.
notes: Retired and private; gave a long interview to Shanghai Securities News in Nov 2020 for the market's 30th anniversary. Sinovel stake via Tibet Xinmeng per bjnews (https://www.bjnews.com.cn/detail/155147330514089.html). Avoid Sinovel's later troubles. No contact route found.

In 2017 he founded Vista, the first NYSE-listed independent focused on Argentina's Vaca Muerta shale, which he still runs.
interesting_fact: He was tapped to run YPF on the day of its renationalization in May 2012, steering the push to develop Vaca Muerta, one of the world's largest shale plays, before leaving to found Vista and becoming an SLB board member.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond oil, he co-founded and chairs GridX, a Buenos Aires science-based incubator that creates and invests in biotech startups spanning health, food, agriculture, energy and materials.
notes: Well-known public figure in Argentina; Vista IR is the cleanest corporate route. GridX is a strong rapport angle beyond energy.

name: Jack Hightower
current_role: Founder and former Chairman/CEO, HighPeak Energy (NASDAQ: HPK); retired 15 Sept 2025, remains a major shareholder
profile: Texas oilman with 50+ years in E&P who founded HighPeak Energy, a Midland Basin (Permian) producer formed in 2020 via his SPAC Pure Acquisition Corp. He serially built and sold E&P companies: Enertex (1991-94), Titan Exploration (1995), which became Pure Resources (taken in by Unocal in 2002), Celero Energy I and II, and Bluestem Energy. He retired as CEO/chairman in Sept 2025.
interesting_fact: Pure Resources, which grew out of the Titan Exploration he founded in 1995, became the 11th-largest publicly traded independent E&P company in North America before Unocal bought out minority shareholders in 2002.
deep_cut_fact: A 1970 Texas Tech graduate (BBA degrees in Administrative Finance and in Money, Banking & Investments), he chaired both Pure Resources (until Unocal's 2002 buyout) and, 15 years later, Pure Acquisition Corp. (2017), the SPAC that took HighPeak public.
notes: Retired from HighPeak in Sept 2025 (CEO now Michael Hollis). No personal public channels found; company contact is the only published route and may not forward. Not to be confused with the late Texas congressman Jack Hightower (d. 2013).

He became a non-executive director in 2018 and is now Vice Chairman.
interesting_fact: As President of International Business, IT, HR and Chemicals he led Asian Paints' digital transformation and its entry into home improvement, and was instrumental in restructuring its joint ventures with US coatings giant PPG Industries.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an MBA and a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from the University of Houston; a recognised IT leader, he has served on the advisory boards of IBM and SAP and is an active angel investor.
notes: Data said 'Chemicals/Petrochemicals'; his wealth is from Asian Paints (paints/coatings). Angel investor and IT/digital background make him a decent podcast fit. Route via Asian Paints investor relations / company secretary.

current_role: Founder & Chairman (since Oct 2025), Sinofibers Technology Co., Ltd. (中简科技, SZSE: 300777), Changzhou

He was deputy director of its carbon-materials key lab and of China's National Engineering Laboratory for Carbon Fiber Preparation Technology.
notes: Hurun's 'Sinofibers' is 中简科技 (carbon fiber), which serves aerospace and defense more than data centers or energy. name: Mark Getty
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Getty Images (NYSE: GETY); chairman of ecotourism company andBeyond
profile: Mark Getty (b. 1960, Rome), grandson of oil baron J. Paul Getty, left banking (Kidder Peabody, Hambros) to co-found Getty Images with Jonathan Klein in 1994, and it became the world's top stock-imagery firm. He chairs Getty Images and ecotourism firm andBeyond, and chaired the National Gallery trustees 2008-16.
interesting_fact: The oil heir turned image mogul is credited with the line 'Intellectual property is the oil of the twenty-first century', and he argues that today's fortunes come from IP rather than natural resources. He now speaks out against AI firms training on copyrighted images without paying.
deep_cut_fact: Italian was his first language (he grew up between Rome and a house near Siena). He called the 1984 sale of Getty Oil the most important moment of his working life because 'it freed me from the need to feel that I had to join the family business.' Getty Images started from a small office in Camden.
notes: Honorary KBE; Irish citizen since 1995. Also chairman of the British School at Rome. Best route is Getty Images corporate communications or IR (the investors.gettyimages.com pages blocked automated fetches, so no email was verified). Do not raise family history (the 1973 kidnapping of his brother).

name: Charles H Giancarlo
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Everpure (formerly Pure Storage); director, Arista Networks and Zscaler
profile: Charlie Giancarlo (b. 1957) co-founded several 1980s networking startups, joined Cisco in 1994 via the Kalpana Ethernet-switching acquisition and rose to CTO/chief development officer, then spent a decade at Silver Lake. CEO of Pure Storage since 2017, he rebranded it Everpure in Feb 2026 to pivot from all-flash storage to AI-era data management for data centers.
interesting_fact: He was a founding investor in data-center giant Equinix, and Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings' first job was at Adaptive, a startup Giancarlo co-founded in 1988; he later sat on Netflix's board (2007-2012).
deep_cut_fact: Before he was a CEO he was a chip designer: in his first engineering job at Siemens he developed and patented the world's first functioning digital codec filter, a mixed-signal CMOS chip. He also holds a Brown BA in Classics alongside his engineering degree.
notes: Pure Storage renamed Everpure (Feb 2026); site moved to everpuredata.com. Older pr@purestorage.com still appears on the page. Strong data-center/AI angle; Brown's Giancarlo Engineering Laboratories are named for him.

notes: Very low profile, regional; no personal channels. Route via board secretary. Company is family-controlled (do not reference family members).

name: Zhao Shanqi
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Jiangsu Macmic Science & Technology Co. (SSE STAR: 688711), Changzhou
profile: Power-semiconductor engineer (PhD) who founded Macmic in Changzhou in August 2006 and remains its chairman, GM and largest individual shareholder (~14-18%). Macmic designs and makes IGBT and FRED power chips and modules for EVs, wind/solar/storage and industrial drives, and is now expanding into AI data-center power (GaN chips, UPS and server power).
interesting_fact: In Sept 2026 he said Macmic's GaN 650V 30mΩ chip had passed certification with AI data-center power-supply customers and it is working with a leading North American power-equipment company on UPS, server-power and solid-state-transformer (SST) products.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Macmic he was deputy chief engineer at the Beijing Power Electronics Center (to 1994), then a postdoc (1994-95) and visiting associate professor (1995-96) at INSA de Lyon in France.
notes: Strong fit for energy/data-center angle (power semiconductors for AIDC). Jilin University graduate per profiles. No published IR email captured; Macmic's securities office is reachable via SSE e-interaction (sns.sseinfo.com) and the company website. Chinese name 赵善麒.

name: Shi Zhengmin
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder (~42%, acting in concert with chairman Shi Yimin) of Hangzhou Innover Technology (先锋电子, SZSE: 002767)
profile: Shi Zhengmin (石政民, b. 1946) founded Hangzhou Innover Technology, a smart gas-meter and 'smart gas' solutions maker set up in 1991 and listed in Shenzhen in June 2015. He held ~65% at incorporation and still holds ~42%, acting in concert with chairman Shi Yimin. Innover serves 1,200+ gas utilities and 50m+ online meters.
interesting_fact: Innover was one of the first companies certified as a high-tech enterprise by Zhejiang's science commission, and now runs a smart-gas big-data centre and a 5-million-unit-per-year smart manufacturing base in Hangzhou.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he began his career at the China Meteorological Administration before becoming deputy GM of Beijing Haidian Xianfeng (Pioneer) Industry and president of Dongguan Xianfeng, the group that seeded the Hangzhou gas-meter business in 1991.
notes: Age ~80 and not in day-to-day management (chairman is Shi Yimin, GM Shi Yang). Alive status inferred from a Sept 2026 SZSE filing listing him as current shareholder; not otherwise confirmed. Very low public profile; Chinese-language approach via the company.

name: Zhang Mingzhu
profile: Listed once on the Hurun China Rich List (2017, ~US$390M) with wealth from 'Dide Energy' (张明珠). No public source could be found identifying the company 'Dide Energy' or this person's role, so identity could not be confirmed.
notes: English and Chinese searches for 张明珠 with 迪德/帝德/德迪 能源 and Hurun 2017 found nothing; company name may be a romanization of a small private (unlisted) energy firm. Not to be confused with Gree's Dong Mingzhu. Would need the Chinese company name from Hurun to proceed.

name: Shawn Marie Soderberg
current_role: Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary, Bloom Energy Corp. (NYSE: BE), since January 2016
profile: Shawn Soderberg has led Bloom Energy's legal, regulatory and compliance work since 2016, through its 2018 IPO and its rise as an on-site fuel-cell power supplier for AI data centers. She was previously EVP and General Counsel at Bio-Rad (2013-15) and held GC roles at Aricent, H&Q Asia Pacific and Oak Technology.
interesting_fact: She has more than 20 years as a general counsel, mostly in tech and life sciences. Her Bloom stock has turned a legal career into a fortune as Bloom became a go-to supplier of on-site power for AI data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Her first general counsel job, from 1994 to 1996, was VP and General Counsel of Microtec Research, a publicly traded maker of software tools for embedded systems. Later she was GC at Asian private-equity firm H&Q Asia Pacific.
notes: In-house lawyer with no media profile, so she is unlikely to be a podcast guest on her own. Route through Bloom press (press@bloomenergy.com). Bloom's data-center power story is the hook; CEO KR Sridhar is the natural guest.

name: Douglas R Bettinger
current_role: EVP & CFO, Lam Research (since 2013); director of Lattice Semiconductor (since Dec 2022) and Marvell Technology (since Nov 2026)
profile: Veteran semiconductor finance executive who has been CFO of wafer-fab equipment maker Lam Research since 2013, through its AI-driven boom in etch and deposition tools. Before that he was CFO of Avago Technologies (now Broadcom), VP finance/corporate controller at Xilinx, CFO of 24/7 Customer, and spent about 11 years in finance roles at Intel.
interesting_fact: Joined Marvell's board in November 2026 while still Lam's CFO, so he now sits close to both the chip-equipment and the AI data-centre silicon sides of the industry.
deep_cut_fact: A UW-Madison economics graduate (MBA, Michigan), he sits on the Industrial Advisory Board of the University of Wisconsin College of Engineering and previously served on the SEMI Board of Industry Leaders.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder, so the best route is Lam IR or media relations (https://newsroom.lamresearch.com/media-contacts). Education per Lattice/Fintool profiles (https://fintool.com/app/research/companies/LRCX/people/douglas-r-bettinger).

name: Gao Wenzhi
current_role: Unknown; Hurun China (2010-2015) listed him with 'Xingguang' (coal)
profile: Gao Wenzhi appeared on the Hurun China Rich List from 2010 to 2015 with an estimated $380m fortune from coal company 'Xingguang'. The company is likely Inner Mongolia Xingguang Coal Group (formerly Otog Banner Xingguang Coal Group, Ordos), but no public source confirming his role was found.
notes: Very private; dropped off rich lists after 2015. Company identification (Inner Mongolia Xingguang Coal Group vs Shanxi Lu'an Xingguang Coal Power) is unconfirmed - would need Chinese business registry records. Low-priority target.

name: Wang Lubao
current_role: Founder and Chairman/President, Jiangsu Huantai Group (solar silicon wafers), Yangzhong, Jiangsu (latest confirmation 2018-19)
profile: Wang Lubao founded Jiangsu Huantai Group, established in 1988 in Yangzhong, Jiangsu, and grew it into a photovoltaic silicon wafer maker (mono and multi-crystalline slicing, ingot pulling) with a photoelectric business line. Huantai partnered with SunEdison in 2014 on up to 1.7GW of Chinese solar projects and supplied wafers to Tongwei from 2015.
interesting_fact: In 2018 Huantai signed a 1.5B-yuan, 3GW monocrystalline ingot-pulling project in Baotou, Inner Mongolia, sited there for cheap electricity, designed to produce ~17,000 tonnes of mono-silicon rods a year.
deep_cut_fact: In 2014 Huantai struck a deal with US firm SunEdison, which agreed to supply polysilicon for Huantai's wafers as part of a partnership to build up to 1.7GW of solar projects in China.
notes: Very low profile; little English or recent (post-2019) coverage found, so current role/status should be reconfirmed. Input lists 'Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)' but I could not identify which unicorn. No published contact found.

name: Wang Weijie
current_role: Executive at Zhongrong Xinda Group (中融新大集团, Qingdao/Zibo coal-chemical group); registry-listed executive director and GM of group subsidiary Binzhou Youkang Building Materials. Current title not confirmed.
profile: Wang Weijie (王维杰) is one of several Zhongrong Xinda Group executives/shareholders whom Hurun listed alongside chairman Wang Qingtao in 2017 (RMB 2.5bn) and 2018 (RMB 2.6bn). Zhongrong Xinda, formerly Shandong Coking Group, grew from coking coal into coal chemicals, mining, glass/building materials and logistics. He is legal representative of its Binzhou subsidiary.
interesting_fact: Zhongrong Xinda put six people on the 2018 Hurun list: Wang Qingtao plus Zhang Yigui (RMB 8.1bn), Liang Kai, Tian Tongbao, Guo Yan and Wang Weijie. That made the company a 'rich-list factory' for Qingdao.
notes: Hurun's 'Zhongrong Xinda' = 中融新大 (not 中融信达). Wealth listing confirmed on the Hurun 2017 Qingdao list (https://m.sohu.com/a/198071714_99904077/). The court record that names him as exec director/GM of 滨州市友康建材 (in Binzhou's Beihai zone) is the 2024 Zibo court ruling that put 128 Zhongrong Xinda companies into consolidated restructuring, so his Hurun-era wealth has likely evaporated; avoid the topic. Common name: do not confuse him with namesakes. The website is the group's, not his.

name: Damodar Prasad Choudhary
current_role: Co-founder and promoter-family member of Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd (Kolkata). He holds no current board position; MarketScreener lists him as chairman 2010-2013.
profile: Damodar Prasad Choudhary co-founded Himadri Speciality Chemical (formerly Himadri Chemicals & Industries) in Kolkata in 1987 with six other family members. Himadri began as a coal-tar pitch maker and has grown into specialty carbon black, naphthalene derivatives and lithium-ion battery materials. The company is now run by Chairman/MD/CEO Anurag Choudhary.
interesting_fact: The company he co-founded has turned a steel-industry byproduct (coal tar) into an energy-transition business, making advanced battery materials such as anode materials and LFP cathode chemicals. Its CMD was named BT India's Best CEO 2026 in chemicals.
notes: I found no recent news on him personally and no obituary, so alive is marked unknown. He appears to have stepped back years ago, and Anurag Choudhary (CMD) is the public face and better podcast guest. He was on the Hurun India list only in 2017-18.

name: Manish Satyanarayan Nuwal
current_role: Managing Director & CEO, Solar Industries India Ltd (Nagpur)
profile: Son of founder Satyanarayan Nuwal; joined the family explosives business in the mid-1990s when it began manufacturing, and has been MD & CEO since ~2012. He has steered Solar from bulk/packaged explosives for mining into defence: propellants, warheads, ammunition, 'Nagastra' loitering munitions and counter-drone systems, with a large new defence/aerospace hub in Nagpur.
interesting_fact: Solar supplies 'Nagastra' loitering-munition drones to the Indian Army, and PM Modi inaugurated its loitering-munition test range in Nagpur in March 2025.
deep_cut_fact: A qualified chartered accountant, he says Solar's defence breakthrough was multi-mode hand grenades co-developed with DRDO over nearly three years, which he calls a watershed for private-sector defence in India; asked if 'playing with fire' is fun, he laughed.
notes: Hurun net-worth figure is from 2019 and well out of date; the Nuwal family is now multi-billionaire as Solar's market cap soared on defence orders. Strong energy/defence-manufacturing angle. Chartered-accountant credential per company website.

name: Ni Kailu
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Shanghai Chaori Solar (超日太阳, 002506.SZ), now GCL System Integration; no current role found
profile: Ni Kailu (倪开禄) founded Shanghai Chaori Solar Energy, a solar-module maker that listed in Shenzhen in 2010 with him and his daughter Ni Na as major holders. After Chaori's 2014 debt crisis, a GCL-led consortium restructured it and renamed it GCL System Integration (协鑫集成), keeping code 002506; Hurun's listing reflects his pre-2016 stake.
interesting_fact: The company he founded, Chaori Solar, was taken over in restructuring by a GCL-led consortium in 2014 and reborn as GCL System Integration, still trading under the same Shenzhen ticker 002506.
notes: Dropped off Hurun after 2016. Chaori was the issuer in China's first onshore corporate bond default (2014) and reports in 2015 said he faced travel restrictions over unpaid debts; not a positive outreach angle and likely unreachable. No public contact or current activity found.

name: Ni Na
current_role: No current public role found (former director and shareholder of Shanghai Chaori Solar, now GCL System Integration, SZSE 002506)
profile: Daughter of Ni Kailu, founder of Shanghai Chaori Solar, a solar-module maker that listed in Shenzhen in 2010. She was a director and related-party shareholder at the IPO. Chaori was restructured in 2014 and taken over by GCL, becoming GCL System Integration, which is why Hurun lists her wealth under that name. She has no identifiable public role since.
notes: Not recommended for outreach: the family company went through China's first onshore bond default and a 2014 bankruptcy restructuring, and 2015 reports say she and her father faced court enforcement (finance.ifeng.com/a/20151208/14114590_0.shtml). Hurun wealth (2011-16) is likely stale. An unrelated SJTU professor shares her name.

name: Tang Faling
current_role: Founder of Wuxi Qiaolian Group (无锡桥联集团), maker of wind-turbine castings and components, Huishan, Wuxi; handed day-to-day control to son Tang Ming in 2008
profile: Tang Faling (唐法林) founded Wuxi Qiaolian (Hurun's 'Qiaolian'), a hardware maker that switched to wind-turbine components in 2004: hubs, nacelles, bearing housings and main shafts for 1.5-2.4MW turbines. He and his son Tang Ming were on Hurun's list in 2011-2013. Registry data still show him as legal representative of several Wuxi machinery companies; no recent press coverage found.
interesting_fact: In 2007 Qiaolian Wind raised US$70m from foreign funds including Avenue Capital, France's NBP and Tsing Capital, aiming for a New York listing. That took a family firm with RMB 20-30m in sales past RMB 1bn within a few years.
deep_cut_fact: Before building Qiaolian he had farmed, worked as a carpenter, designed furniture and made hardware; his son described him as a '拼命三郎' (workaholic) always travelling to scout markets.
notes: Hurun's 'Qiaolian' = 桥联 (Wuxi Qiaolian Wind Power Technology / Qiaolian Group), not 侨联. The planned US IPO never happened, and there is no news coverage after about 2013. Private company with no IR channel; no published contact found. Very low profile.

name: Tang Ming
current_role: Chairman of Wuxi Qiaolian Wind Power Technology Group (无锡桥联风电科技集团), as of last press coverage; legal representative of Wuxi Qiaolian Investment
profile: Tang Ming (唐明), son of founder Tang Faling, took over Wuxi Qiaolian Group in 2008 after it pivoted from hardware to wind-turbine castings and components in 2004 (Qiaolian Wind was set up in Nov 2006). He brought in US$70m of foreign private equity in 2007 and pursued a planned New York IPO; Yicai put his wealth at RMB 1.7bn in 2011.
interesting_fact: Tang rejects the label 'fu er dai' (rich second generation): 'to be precise, I'm a chuang er dai (second-generation founder)', saying he earned it through 20 years of his own hard work.
deep_cut_fact: To pick investors for the 2007 round he set criteria: a mature US fund for a New York listing (Avenue), a fund with clean-energy listing experience (France's NBP), and Tsing Capital for its government background. More than 200 VCs had been tracking the company.
notes: Hurun's 'Qiaolian' = 桥联 (not 侨联). In 2009, as chairman, he signed a RMB 2bn deal in Deyang, Sichuan to expand component supply to Dongfang Electric (https://mobile.epaper.routeryun.com/index.php/home/article/index/appkey/192/date/2009-06-23/page/390414/aid/1924365.html). No news coverage after about 2013; the company is private and no published contact was found.

name: Li Yuchi
current_role: Co-founder and founding shareholder of Zhongman Petroleum & Natural Gas Group (ZPEC, 603619.SH); acts in concert with controller Zhu Fengxue
profile: Early partner in Shanghai-based oilfield-services and upstream group Zhongman Petroleum (ZPEC), which grew from drilling services into an integrated driller, equipment maker and oil producer with overseas assets, listing in Shanghai in 2017. He was one of the joint-stock company's founding promoters with about 8% of shares and is named in 2024 filings as a concert party of the controlling group led by Zhu Fengxue. No current executive role found.

notes: Only on Hurun 2018; minimal public profile. Has sold down shares (2024 block/agreement transfers). Better interview targets at ZPEC: chairman Li Chundi or controller Zhu Fengxue; route via board secretary office (Shi Mingxin).

name: Liu Fahe
current_role: Founder and chairman/legal representative of Zouping Sanli Group (邹平县三利集团) and its parent Zhongrong Shuangchuang (Beijing) Technology Group (中融双创), Zouping, Binzhou, Shandong
profile: Liu Fahe (刘法合, b. Aug 1959) built Sanli Group in Matou town, Zouping (Shandong) into a family conglomerate spanning cotton, compact/ring spinning, home textiles, petroleum refining, chemicals, feed, logistics and coal. He controls it with his brothers. Hurun listed the Liu Fahe family at RMB 2.3bn in 2012-2013 for 'Sanli textiles and petrochemicals'.
interesting_fact: Sanli is a rare cotton-to-oil combination: the four Liu brothers own a group that runs cotton, compact and ring spinning, eco home textiles, edible oil and feed alongside petroleum, chemicals, logistics and coal.
deep_cut_fact: Sanli's company profile describes him as a native of Shaodian village (邵店村), Matou town, Zouping, a university-educated engineer and Party member who had run the business continuously since 1985.
notes: Hurun 'San Li' = 三利集团. Caution: in 2021 the CSRC penalised Zhongrong Shuangchuang and him over bond disclosure, and 2025-26 court and asset-manager notices list him and group firms as debtors. The group appears financially distressed, so frame outreach carefully. Alive inferred from 2026 court notices naming him. No published contact.

name: Du Ligang
current_role: Former co-founder and Executive Vice Chairman of WM Motor (威马汽车, 'Weltmeister'); reported to be leaving in Dec 2022. Current role unknown
profile: Du Ligang (杜立刚) co-founded Shanghai EV maker WM Motor with CEO Shen Hui, a former colleague, in late 2015. He joined as CFO and later became executive vice chairman, overseeing fundraising, new business development, legal and internal control during WM's rise to unicorn status. Media reported in Dec 2022 that he was leaving after seven years.
interesting_fact: One account says WM Motor's roots trace to an electric-drivetrain ('three-electric' battery/motor/control) R&D company Du founded in 2012, which later merged with Shen Hui's venture; other reports say he joined at Shen's invitation.
notes: No public profile or contact channels found since he left WM Motor; WM later went through bankruptcy restructuring (2023), so the Hurun wealth figure (2021) is likely stale. Low priority for outreach.

profile: Li Lifeng (b. Oct 1971) is a Yuyao, Zhejiang entrepreneur who rose through family-run Ningbo Shimao Copper (supervisor 2001, GM 2009, chairman 2016) and has chaired Ningbo Shimao Energy since 2018. Shimao Energy runs waste-to-energy incineration plants selling power and industrial steam in Yuyao; it listed in Shanghai in 2021. Unrelated to developer Shimao Group.

deep_cut_fact: Li is a deputy to the 14th Zhejiang Provincial People's Congress, vice-chair of Yuyao's federation of industry and commerce, and was named a 'Yuyao Model Worker' and one of Ningbo's outstanding entrepreneurs (16th edition).

name: Alasdair Locke
current_role: Non-executive chairman & major shareholder, Well-Safe Solutions; chairman, First Property Group; chairman of the Scottish Conservative Party (since Nov 2024)
profile: Oxford-educated ex-Citigroup shipping/oil banker (b. 1953) who founded Aberdeen oil-services firm Abbot Group in 1992, floated it in 1995 and sold it in 2008 in a deal valuing it at GBP 906m. He then founded Motor Fuel Group, built into the UK's largest forecourt owner, and since 2017 has backed well-decommissioning specialist Well-Safe Solutions.

deep_cut_fact: In 2019 he and his stepson co-founded Glenrinnes Distillery in Speyside, launching Organic Speyside Vodka and Organic Speyside Gin backed by a GBP 4m investment.
notes: Now politically prominent as Scottish Tory chairman; keep outreach business-focused (oil services, decommissioning/energy transition). Routes: Well-Safe Solutions or First Property Group (fprop.com).

name: Huang Litai
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu LAD (Li'anda / 利安达) Group, Jiangyin, Jiangsu (per older profiles; current status unverified)
profile: Huang Litai (黄丽泰) founded the forerunner of Jiangsu Li'anda (LAD) Group in Jiangyin in 1991-93, growing it into one of China's notable casual-wear makers and exporters, with fabric weaving, dyeing and garment bases and 13 subsidiaries, selling ~90% of output to Japan, Europe/US and Hong Kong. deep_cut_fact: She was a medical doctor before business: she gave up her beloved career as a physician to open Jiangyin Fenghua Garment Co. (LAD's predecessor) and began full-time entrepreneurship in January 1993.
notes: Sparse, dated public info; gas/energy link listed by Hurun could not be verified (sources only show apparel). Not on Hurun since 2021. No official website or contact found. Low relevance for an energy/data-center show.

name: Zhang Ruiling
current_role: Non-executive director and Chairman, MIE Holdings Corporation (HKEX: 1555) as of March 2025 (spelled Zhang Ruilin / 张瑞霖 in filings)
profile: Controlling shareholder of MIE Holdings (MI Energy), an HK-listed independent upstream oil and gas firm that ran Chinese oilfields such as Moliqing under PSCs with PetroChina and held Kazakh fields.
