name: Wei Zhenyu
current_role: No current listed-company role found. Formerly chairman (2014-2018) and actual controller of Gosun Holdings (高升控股, SZSE: 000971), and board chairman (2015-16) and 16.91% holder of HK-listed China Soft Power Technology
profile: Wei Zhenyu (韦振宇, b. Oct 1984) holds a bachelor's degree from Cal Poly and an EMBA from Nankai. He was one of Hurun's youngest rich-listers (2016 post-80s list). Through Beijing Yuchi Ruide and Landing Industrial he controlled Gosun Holdings, a cloud-infrastructure provider (IDC, CDN, VPN, data-center interconnect), and held a stake in China Soft Power (Hurun's 'Soft Power'). He exited Gosun's control in 2020.
interesting_fact: Data-center angle: under his control Gosun repositioned itself as a full-stack cloud-infrastructure provider, offering IDC, VPN, CDN and APM plus multi-active data centers, hybrid cloud and DCI services.
deep_cut_fact: Before the Gosun deal he ran a cultural company: from Jan 2011 he was executive director and GM of Beijing Shenzhouqing Culture (北京神州情文化), and from 2013 a director of Beijing Dingjiu Information Engineering Research Institute.
notes: CAUTION: in 2019 the Hubei CSRC bureau fined him and imposed a 5-year market ban over undisclosed guarantees at Gosun (http://www.csrc.gov.cn/hubei/c104396/c1351576/content.shtml). Control of Gosun passed to Zhang Dai/Tianjin Bairuoke in 2020, and the company was later delisted. The Gosun IR channel no longer reaches him; no published personal contact. Low suitability for outreach.

name: Ma Changjiang
current_role: Chairman and president of Yuncheng Polytechnic University (运城职业技术大学); supervisory-board chairman and ~78% owner of Shanxi Hongyuan Group (山西宏源集团), Linfen, Shanxi
profile: Ma Changjiang (马长江, b. 1967, Xiangning county, Linfen) managed coal mines in Hejin and Puxian before founding Hongyuan Coal/Shanxi Hongyuan Group in the 1990s. The group now spans clean energy (coal), vocational education, cultural tourism and elderly care. He stepped back from the group chairmanship in 2022 and now leads the private Yuncheng Polytechnic University; he also chairs Shanghai Gaijing New Energy Technology.
interesting_fact: A coal boss turned educator: he founded and chairs Yuncheng Polytechnic University, one of China's first private vocational universities. He presided over its 2024 graduation as 'Dr. Ma Changjiang' and its 2026 ceremony as president.
deep_cut_fact: He studied Chinese literature at Shanxi Normal University (class of 1994) and later earned a Tsinghua EMBA and a doctorate in global management from the University of Minnesota. Early on he ran the Dujiawan mine in Hejin and the Beiyu mine in Puxian.
notes: Hurun 'Hongyuan Coal' = 蒲县宏源煤业 / 山西宏源集团 (Linfen), not the Shenzhen-listed Hongyuan Securities. Alive and active as of the June 2026 graduation ceremony. The best route is probably via the university, which publishes a leadership page; no personal email found. Energy angle: in 2023 he became chairman of Shanghai Gaijing New Energy and acquired a Guizhou anthracite mine. Avoid the group's 2024 tax-penalty and mine-accident news.

name: Zeng Li
current_role: Legal representative and 97.86% owner of Shanghai Yaoxin Information Technology LP, a major AtHub shareholder; formerly vice chairman & president of Shanghai AtHub (数据港, 603881.SH) - current board role not confirmed
profile: Zeng Li (曾犁, b. 1968) was vice chairman and president of Shanghai AtHub (数据港), a Shanghai-listed (2017) developer of customised wholesale data centers, and a major shareholder through Shanghai Yaoxin, which held 26.19% after the IPO and 18.44% by April 2022. AtHub's board is now chaired by Sun Zhongfeng.
interesting_fact: AtHub builds customised data centers for large cloud customers, bundling the power infrastructure and data-center infrastructure management alongside the buildings.
notes: Shareholding source: AtHub 2022 equity-change notice https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202204121558875314_1.pdf. Very low public profile; no interviews or personal channels found. Relevant for the data-center angle; AtHub IR is the only published route and may not reach him if he has left management.

name: Chen Guohua
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder/director-level insider of Hangzhou Silan Holdings, controlling shareholder of Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics (SSE: 600460); one of Silan's seven actual controllers
profile: Chen Guohua (陈国华) is one of seven co-founders who jointly control Silan Microelectronics, a Hangzhou chipmaker founded in 1997 that runs its own fabs making power semiconductors, MEMS, LEDs and analog ICs. He holds a small direct stake plus part of Silan Holdings (~31% owner); in 2008 he was a Silan supervisor.
interesting_fact: Silan is controlled by a group of seven founders acting in concert (Chen Xiangdong, Fan Weihong, Zheng Shaobo, Jiang Zhongyong, Luo Huabing, Song Weiquan and Chen Guohua), an unusual collective-ownership structure among Chinese chipmakers.
notes: Very low profile; chairman Chen Xiangdong is Silan's public face. Current personal title not confirmed (2008 filings: Silan supervisor, Silan Holdings supervisor, VP of Youwang Technology). Common name: many unrelated academics named Chen Guohua. Hurun listing only 2021.

name: Ding Ran
current_role: Director and Vice President, Allwinner Technology (Zhuhai; SZSE ChiNext: 300458)
profile: Born 1973, Ding Ran co-founded Zhuhai fabless chip designer Allwinner (Quanzhi) in September 2007 and holds ~77.5m shares; he was re-elected a director and reappointed VP in July 2026. Allwinner makes ARM-based SoCs for tablets, OTT boxes, smart home, automotive and edge-AI devices.
interesting_fact: Allwinner's cheap ARM chips (A10/A13/A20) briefly made it the world's No. 1 supplier by units of Android-tablet application processors in 2012-13, and powered open-hardware boards like the Cubieboard.
deep_cut_fact: Allwinner was started by a group of senior engineers who left Zhuhai's Actions Semiconductor; per Allwinner's 2026 filing, Ding Ran has been a co-founder since the company's creation in September 2007.
notes: Low public profile; holds Macau permanent residency per filing. Board secretary is Cai Xiaopeng (IR). Edge-AI chip angle fits the data-center/AI focus loosely.

name: Ge Wenzhi
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hangzhou MDK Opto Electronics (SSE STAR: 688079)
profile: Ge Wenzhi (葛文志, b. 1970) founded and controls Hangzhou MDK Opto Electronics, which makes optical and optical-semiconductor components (precision optics, filters, ultra-precision machining) for consumer electronics and imaging. Founded in 2010, the company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in March 2021; he has been chairman and GM since 2018.
interesting_fact: At MDK's 2021 STAR Market IPO, Ge, the largest shareholder and chairman, personally raised his own funds to take part in the IPO's strategic placement, an unusual vote of confidence by a founder.
deep_cut_fact: He learned the optics trade at Zhejiang Crystal Electronic Group (forerunner of optical-components maker Crystal-Optech), where he worked from 1992 to 1999 before starting his own optics business, Zhejiang MDK, in 2001.
notes: Low public profile; no interviews found. Route via the company's board-secretary/IR office (ipo@chinamdk.com, listed in the 2023 annual report). Tie to data-center/AI is indirect (optical semiconductor components).

name: Shen Haibo
current_role: General Manager of Huichuang New Energy and Dongguan Ganfeng; heads battery recycling at Ganfeng Lithium (left Ganfeng board Oct 2026, remains in other roles)
profile: Born 1968, Shen Haibo is a Ganfeng Lithium veteran who joined in 2005 as marketing director and served as a director from 2007 and director/vice president from 2010, holding ~15.3M Ganfeng shares directly. He now runs Ganfeng's battery subsidiaries Huichuang New Energy and Dongguan Ganfeng and oversees the group's battery recycling business; he stepped off the board in Oct 2026 for work reasons but stays with the company.
interesting_fact: He was among the earliest executives at Ganfeng, now one of the world's largest lithium producers, joining in 2005 years before its 2010 Shenzhen IPO and helping build its sales operation.
deep_cut_fact: Lithium was his trade before Ganfeng: from 1996-2002 he was lithium-products manager at the Beijing office of China Nonferrous Metals Import & Export Xinjiang Corp; he studied industrial engineering management at North China University of Technology (class of 1991).
notes: Ganfeng lists a named 'Media Cooperation' contact (Evan Sun) - best route. Battery recycling/second-life angle is relevant to energy storage. Board exit Oct 2026 reported by rccaijing; confirm his current title before outreach.

name: Song Weiquan
current_role: Co-founder and one of seven ultimate controlling shareholders of Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics (士兰微, SSE: 600460); no board/executive title found
profile: Song Weiquan (宋卫权) is one of the seven natural persons - with chairman Chen Xiangdong, Fan Weihong, Zheng Shaobo, Jiang Zhongyong, Luo Huabing and Chen Guohua - who jointly control Silan Microelectronics via Hangzhou Silan Holdings. Silan is a Hangzhou-based integrated device manufacturer of power semiconductors, MEMS sensors and LED chips; Hurun listed him at ~$360M (2021).
interesting_fact: Silan has been controlled by the same seven-founder group for decades - its 2025 half-year report still names all seven as the company's ultimate controlling parties, a rare example of a stable founder collective in Chinese semiconductors.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal biography found online. Best route is Silan's board-secretary office (Chen Yue). Chairman Chen Xiangdong is the group's public face. No reports of death; alive status unconfirmed.

name: Wei Xiaolin
current_role: Chairman & General Manager and controlling shareholder, Chengdu Xiling Power Science & Technology (西菱动力, SZSE: 300733)
profile: Born in 1956, Wei Xiaolin founded Chengdu-based Xiling Power in 1999; it makes engine components such as camshafts, pulleys and crankshaft dampers for automakers and has expanded into aviation and defense parts. He and his wife are the company's controlling shareholders, and he runs it as chairman and general manager.
interesting_fact: Xiling Power started in auto parts but now runs a separate aviation and military components division, putting the Chengdu firm in aerospace supply chains as well as automotive.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 17 years (1975-1992) as a worker in Workshop 82 at Chengdu Aircraft Company, then in 1992 founded a small auto-parts factory in Qingyang district before creating Xiling in 1999.
notes: Contacts are the board secretary (Yang Hao) and securities rep from the 2024 annual report. The board term expired in Jan 2026; re-election outcome not checked. Low public profile; only on Hurun China 2021.

name: Xu Huadong
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Power HF Co., Ltd. (Huafeng Power, SSE: 605100), Weifang, Shandong
profile: Chinese industrialist (b. 1968) who founded Huafeng Power in April 2004; with partner Chui Lap Lam he controls it via Engineus Power Holding. The company makes diesel-engine blocks/heads, small multi-cylinder diesel engines and generator sets (10kW-2,400kW), and is pushing gas gensets as prime power for data centers, including in the US market.
interesting_fact: Huafeng says its natural-gas generator sets can serve as primary (not just backup) power for data centers and it is pursuing US certification and orders; it earlier won diesel-genset tenders for China Unicom's Langfang and Hohhot data-center bases.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding the engine maker he worked in trade, at Changzhou Garment Import & Export Co. and Changzhou International Economic & Technical Cooperation Group; he holds a master's degree and is also listed as one of the company's core technical personnel.
notes: Chinese name 徐华东. No published email found; company switchboard/IR via board secretary Liu Xiang per filings. Data-center backup/prime power angle is a strong podcast hook, though gensets are still a small share of revenue.

name: Chui Lap Lam
current_role: Co-actual controller (with Xu Huadong) of Power HF Co., Ltd. / Huafeng Power (SSE: 605100), Weifang, Shandong
profile: Hong Kong-linked investor disclosed, with chairman Xu Huadong, as an actual controller of Power HF (Huafeng Power), holding ~8.6% indirectly via offshore vehicles (Engineus Power Holding). Power HF makes diesel engines for backup power, data centers, trucks, construction and marine use; listed in Shanghai in 2020. No public biography found.
interesting_fact: Power HF's diesel engines are sold for stationary power generation including data-center backup, linking this low-profile fortune to the data-center buildout.
notes: Ownership/controller status from 10jqka shareholder data (https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/605100/holder.html). Holds no visible executive role; Xu Huadong is chairman. Route only via company IR.

name: Yang Xiaoqi (杨小奇)
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Shanghai Fullhan Microelectronics (富瀚微, SZSE: 300613)
profile: Shanghai Jiao Tong University graduate (b. 1963) who founded fabless chip designer Fullhan in 2004. Fullhan makes image-signal-processing and video SoC chips for security cameras, smart-home devices and in-car cameras, and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2017. He leads the largest shareholder group (~25% with concert parties) and is pursuing a Hong Kong dual listing.
interesting_fact: Fullhan's ISP and IP-camera chips are a key domestic supplier for China's video-surveillance industry; its 2025 chips integrate on-chip NPUs for AI detection.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Fullhan he was a department manager at China Kejian Co. (1987-92), general manager of Shenzhen Silicon Valley Electronic Systems (1994-2000) and COO of Wuhan Hanwang High-Tech (2000-03).
notes: Low English-language profile. Chips focus is edge video/AI vision rather than data-center compute. Best route: Fullhan investor services (stock@fullhan.com).

name: Kavita Saraf
current_role: Promoter-group shareholder of Vinati Organics Ltd (via Kavita Vinod Saraf Family Trust, ~12%); former director (ceased 2019 per MCA records)
profile: Kavita Vinod Saraf is part of the promoter family of Mumbai-listed specialty-chemicals maker Vinati Organics, founded in 1989 by Vinod Saraf; she holds her stake mainly through the Kavita Vinod Saraf Family Trust. Vinati makes isobutyl benzene (IBB, the key ibuprofen raw material), ATBS monomers and butyl phenols. She keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Vinati Organics is the world's largest - and lowest-cost - producer of IBB, the key raw material for the painkiller ibuprofen, and the global leader in ATBS monomers used in water treatment and paints.
deep_cut_fact: The Mrs. Kavita Vinod Saraf Foundation (KVSF), a registered public charitable trust bearing her name, is consolidated into Vinati Organics' financial statements and is a vehicle for the company's CSR work.
notes: Not an operating executive; the public faces of Vinati are founder-chairman Vinod Saraf and MD Vinati Saraf Mutreja. The listed email is Vinati's general corporate inbox. Industry tag 'petrochemicals' fits only loosely (specialty chemicals). Alive status not confirmed by a dated source.

name: Rahul Dhanuka
current_role: Managing Director, Dhanuka Agritech Ltd (NSE: DHANUKA), since August 2024
profile: Second-generation leader of Gurugram-based crop-protection company Dhanuka Agritech, on its board since 2002 and previously COO; became MD in Aug 2024 as the company was handed to him and Harsh Dhanuka. Dhanuka's model relies on tie-ups with Japanese and US agrochemical majors to bring patented and exclusive molecules, and increasingly biologicals, to Indian farmers.
interesting_fact: As COO he committed Dhanuka to launching two new exclusive products every year, built on licensing partnerships with Japanese and American agrochemical firms.
deep_cut_fact: In a Sept 2026 interview he said Dhanuka was launching a new range of crop-nutrition products to help farmers recover from El Niño stress and depleted soil moisture, with the goal of 'making 2027 a more resilient and healthier year' for Indian agriculture.
notes: Agrochemicals rather than energy despite the 'Chemicals & Petrochemicals' tag; weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Gives trade-press interviews (AgroPages, Indian Chemical News). Company also publishes groupchairmanoffice@dhanuka.com, which serves the group chairman rather than him.

name: Ayman Asfari
current_role: Co-founder, The Asfari Foundation (London); former CEO (2002-2020) of oilfield-services group Petrofac
profile: Syrian-born British engineer (b. 1958; Villanova, Penn, Wharton MBA) who joined Petrofac in 1991, bought it out in 2001 and floated it in London in 2005, building a major oil & gas engineering contractor. He stepped down as CEO at end-2020. Since Assad's fall he has become a prominent diaspora investor and philanthropist re-engaging with Syria.
interesting_fact: In April 2026 he returned to Syria via Idlib and laid the foundation stone for the Dr. Mohammad Adeeb Asfari Maternity and Children's Hospital, named after his father; in 2025 he met Syria's energy minister about oil and gas investment and was floated as a possible transitional PM.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was in Oman as a consulting engineer doing soil testing; when he joined Petrofac in 1991 it was essentially a single plant in Tyler, Texas. He won the UK EY Entrepreneur of the Year award in 2011.
notes: Sensitivities: he was questioned in the SFO's Unaoil-related inquiry (Petrofac itself pleaded guilty in 2021; he was not charged) and was a large Conservative donor - avoid. His personal site aymanasfari.com (listed on Wikipedia) did not load. Great angle: post-war Syrian energy reconstruction. Foundation is the cleanest route.

name: Brian P Friedman
current_role: President and Director, Jefferies Financial Group (NYSE: JEF); Director, Vitesse Energy (NYSE: VTS)
profile: Brian P. Friedman (70) has been President and a director of Jefferies Financial Group since 2013, after joining legacy Jefferies Group in 2005. A former Wachtell Lipton lawyer, he spent 17 years at Furman Selz (head of investment banking) and ran Jefferies Capital Partners. He sits on the board of Vitesse Energy, the oil and gas company Jefferies spun off in 2023.
interesting_fact: About 70% of his pay since joining Jefferies has come in equity; counting all earned and unearned deferred shares and options, he would own about 6.8 million Jefferies shares, roughly 3.2% of the firm.
deep_cut_fact: He is co-chairman of the board of Strive, a workforce-training nonprofit, and a board member of the HC Leukemia Foundation. He graduated summa cum laude in economics from Wharton, also took a Wharton M.S. in Accounting, and holds a Columbia Law J.D.

public_contacts.value: https://www.jefferies.com/contact-us/ (directs investor, media and general inquiries to Jefferies Investor Relations)

notes: Energy angle: Vitesse Energy (non-operated oil and gas interests, spun off by Jefferies in 2023). Jefferies' IR pages are behind a bot wall, so no published email was captured. Route via Jefferies IR/corporate communications.

name: Sun Gengwen
current_role: Former chairman (until Dec 2018) of LandOcean Energy Services (SZ: 300157, now renamed New JCM Group); current role unclear - listed as director of some former subsidiaries
profile: Founder and long-time chairman of Beijing-based LandOcean Energy Services (Hengtai Aipu), a ChiNext-listed provider of oil and gas exploration software, geophysical services and oilfield equipment, which put him on the Hurun China list in 2011-2014. He stepped down as chairman in Dec 2018; the company was later renamed New JCM Group under new management (chairman Wang Lifei since 2022).
interesting_fact: LandOcean was among the early oilfield-technology companies listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext growth board (2010) and expanded through acquisitions such as Jinzhou New JCM Machinery and Sichuan Chuanyou Engineering Survey & Design.
notes: Low public profile; no verifiable biography or personal contacts found. No longer runs the listed company, so its IR channel is not a route to him. ChiNext listing year from general knowledge of ticker 300157 - verify. Consider low priority.

name: Rakesh Malhotra
current_role: Co-founder and head of SAR Group (Livguard, Livfast, Livpure, Lectrix EV, Ncubate), Gurugram
profile: Engineer-entrepreneur who founded Luminous Power Technologies in 1988 and built it into one of India's leading home inverter/UPS and battery brands before selling it to Schneider Electric (74% in 2011, the rest later). He then relaunched SAR Group around clean energy, founding Livguard (inverters, batteries, solar, storage) in 2014, plus EV and venture-incubation arms.
interesting_fact: He started Luminous at 26 with just Rs 40,000 in a 600 sq ft workshop in South Delhi; after the Schneider exit he built a second energy company, Livguard, reported to be worth about Rs 3,500 crore.
deep_cut_fact: Luminous's first big break was an order from Modi Xerox for 28 UPS units worth Rs 4.2 lakh; the company closed its first year with just Rs 8 lakh in revenue.
notes: SAR Group co-founded with Navneet Kapoor (per Livguard 'About us'). Good fit for an energy-storage / Indian power-backup episode. No personal social accounts verified; Livguard's published mailbox is marketing, so it is a fallback rather than a press desk.

name: Chimanlal Khimchand Mehta
profile: Deceased: C.K. Mehta, founder and chairman emeritus of the Deepak Group (Deepak Nitrite, 1970; Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals, 1979), died on 3 July 2023 at age 91 in Vadodara.
notes: Died 3 July 2023 (sources: Business Today; Deepak Fertilisers BSE filing https://bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/695923ed-fd4a-490e-b542-8873a97405a4.pdf). His son Sailesh C. Mehta (P14423) chairs Deepak Fertilisers.

name: Muhammad Raghib Hussain
current_role: CEO, Altera (Intel's FPGA business, majority-owned by Silver Lake) since May 2025; director, Cirrus Logic
profile: Pakistani-American chip executive who co-founded Cavium (networking/security processors) with Syed Ali in 2000, took it public in 2007 and sold it to Marvell for ~$6bn in 2018. He then ran Marvell's products and technology as president, helping build its data-center/custom AI silicon business, before being named Altera CEO when Silver Lake bought 51% of the FPGA maker from Intel.
interesting_fact: Intel picked him to lead Altera as part of the April 2025 deal valuing the FPGA pioneer at $8.75bn, making him the first CEO of Altera as a standalone, PE-backed company.
deep_cut_fact: A NED University (Karachi) computer-systems engineering grad, he began his career at Karachi firms Zelin (Pvt.) Ltd. and ITIM Associates before moving to Silicon Valley (Cisco, Cadence); he later earned an MS from San Jose State.
notes: Input lists him as Marvell president, but he moved to Altera in May 2025. Strong fit for data-center/AI theme (FPGAs, AI infrastructure). Altera media contact is Stephen Gabriel via the newsroom email. NED University awarded him a citation (neduet.edu.pk).

name: Miao Liansheng
current_role: Founder and former chairman/CEO of Yingli Green Energy (Baoding); no current role confirmed after the 2020-21 court restructuring
profile: Miao Liansheng (苗连生), from Hebei, left the military, ran a cosmetics trading business in Baoding, and in 1998 founded Yingli, which became one of the world's largest solar module makers and listed on the NYSE in 2007. Heavy debts led to a 2020-21 court restructuring in which the Baoding government became the largest shareholder; his role since then is not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Under Miao, Yingli became the first Chinese company to sponsor the FIFA World Cup (2010, renewed for Brazil 2014), and by 2013 it was described as the world's largest PV module maker.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar he was in the military, then ran the 'Yingli' cosmetics trading company in Baoding. The solar business took the same Yingli name when it was founded in 1998.
notes: Yingli went through court restructuring in 2020-21 and is now controlled by Baoding state investors, so Yingli company channels are probably not a route to him. No personal or office contact found. He last appeared on Hurun in 2011. Avoid the debt and restructuring history in outreach. Living status is unconfirmed: no recent coverage found either way.

name: Sun Hongyuan
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2008-09) as the owner behind Qinxin Group (Shanxi Qinxin Energy Group); current role not verified
profile: Sun Hongyuan (孙宏原) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List in 2008-09 as the owner behind Qinxin Group: Shanxi Qinxin Energy Group, a private coal, coke, power and materials group founded in 1995 in Qinyuan county, Changzhi, Shanxi. No current public information about him personally could be found.
interesting_fact: Qinxin has grown into one of Shanxi's key private energy groups, spanning eight sectors from coal and coke to power and materials, with more than 12,000 employees and 9.8bn yuan revenue in 2024.
notes: Searches could not link Sun Hongyuan's name to Qinxin in any current source, so treat his identity and role as unverified. He has not appeared on rich lists since 2009. Confirm via the Chinese business registry before any outreach. GEM lists Qinxin's coal mine parent as Hainan Hexinyuan Investment, so ownership may have changed.

name: Cao Mingfang
current_role: Founder of Jiangyin Mould & Plastic Group (Jiangnan Mould & Plastic Technology, 000700.SZ); historically chairman, current role unconfirmed
profile: Cao Mingfang (曹明芳, b. 1944, Jiangyin, Jiangsu), a former township official, founded Jiangnan Mould & Plastic in 1984 as a $320k joint venture with a Hong Kong plastics firm. It became a major supplier of car bumpers to Shanghai VW, Citroen and GM and listed in Shenzhen in 1999. Wealth listed jointly with Cao Kebo, who has chaired the listed company.
interesting_fact: The company that became a leading bumper maker started out making decorative candles; its break came in 1988 with an order for front and rear bumpers for 30,000 Santana sedans.
deep_cut_fact: A farmer's son with a middle-school education, he started in 1960 as an apprentice at the township-run Jiangyin No. 2 Textile Machinery Factory and by 25 had risen to head its technical section.
notes: Input's SEC link (TSMC VP) is a mismatch; unrelated person. Industry tag 'wooden floor' also seems wrong (auto parts/moulding). Born 1944; last on Hurun 2020; no death notice found but current status unconfirmed. Very low profile; route only via the listed company's board office. Weak fit for energy/data-center podcast.

name: Chen Zhongxiao
current_role: Unknown; listed as head of Changping Group (常平集团), a Shanxi coal and steel business
profile: Chen Zhongxiao (陈忠孝) appeared on Hurun China lists 2006-2016 via Changping Group (常平集团), coal and steel. In Hurun's 2010 Shanxi rich list he ranked 21st with 1.5B yuan. No further public biography, company website or recent coverage could be found.
interesting_fact: He was one of a cluster of Shanxi coal and coke fortunes on Hurun's 2010 Shanxi list, where Changping Group was listed under coal and steel.
notes: Very obscure private Shanxi businessman; no online presence found and the company name is often confused with Beijing's Changping district. Shanxi coal consolidation after 2009 may have changed the business. Recommend deprioritising.

name: Zhou Licheng
current_role: Legal representative / head of New United Group (新誉集团有限公司), Changzhou, Jiangsu
profile: Zhou Licheng (周立成) heads New United Group, a private equipment-manufacturing group founded in 2002 in Wujin, Changzhou, listed by Hurun together with Ge Yaqin. The group makes rail-transit traction and electrical systems (a key supplier to China Railway rolling stock), wind-power equipment, CNC machines, office equipment, aerospace parts and logistics, with 4,000+ staff and about 10.3bn yuan in assets.
interesting_fact: New United runs a provincial wind-power equipment research institute and a ground test bench that can full-performance test wind turbines up to 3.8 MW before they leave the factory, plus a 3 MW traction-drive lab and a national-level EMC lab.
notes: 'New United' = 新誉集团 (Xinyu Group). Hurun listed him 2009-2021 jointly with Ge Yaqin. Very little personal information online; no recent personal news found, so alive status marked unknown. Email is the group's general address published on its own website.

name: Li Fengyi
profile: Li Fengyi (李凤义) appeared on Hurun China lists 2007-2013 as an Ordos (Inner Mongolia) entrepreneur in cashmere and electro-metallurgy/smelting (also coal). The 2010 Hurun table lists him under 'Ordos | cashmere, electric smelting'. I could not confirm his company or current role.
notes: Identity unconfirmed: 'Erdos' here likely means the city of Ordos rather than necessarily Erdos Group (whose leaders are Wang Linxiang/Wang Zhen). Not on lists since 2013. No public bio, interviews or contacts found. Low priority.

name: Ge Yaqin
profile: Hurun China (2012-2021) lists Ge Yaqin (戈亚琴) with Zhou Licheng as owners of 'New United', i.e. New United Group (新誉集团), a private Changzhou, Jiangsu group founded in 2002. It makes rail-transit traction/equipment and wind-power equipment, plus CNC and aerospace businesses. No public source describing Ge Yaqin's own role was found.
interesting_fact: New United Group, founded in 2002 in Wujin, Changzhou, is a key supplier of locomotive and rolling-stock components to China's national railway and has been recognised as a national 'single-champion' manufacturer, with about 4,000 staff.
notes: Wealth is shared with Zhou Licheng, New United's founder/chairman, who is the more public figure. Her personal role is unconfirmed. The company website (newunited.com.cn) was unreachable during research. A third-party brand directory lists nug@newunited.com.cn, but that listing is unclaimed and not official, so it is not included as a contact. She dropped off Hurun after 2021.

name: Ding Wenxiang
profile: Appeared on the Hurun China Rich List in 2014-2015 with coal wealth attributed to 'Tehong' (est. ~$340m). Chinese and English searches found no public source tying Ding Wenxiang (丁文祥) to a company named Tehong/特弘 or any coal business, so identity and current status could not be confirmed.
notes: Could not identify; 'Tehong' may be a romanisation of a different company name. Needs Chinese business-registry lookup. Dropped off rich lists after 2015 (coal downturn). Low priority.

name: Zhou Lixin
current_role: Listed by Hurun as owner of New United Group (新誉集团), Changzhou; exact current title not confirmed
profile: Hurun China (2015-2021) attributes his wealth to New United Group (新誉集团有限公司), a private Changzhou, Jiangsu equipment group founded in 2002 that makes rail-transit traction, air-con, gearbox and signalling systems, wind turbines and other new-energy kit, CNC machine tools, office shredders and logistics parks (4,000+ staff, ~RMB10bn assets).
interesting_fact: New United runs a 3.8 MW wind-turbine full-performance factory test rig and a 3 MW traction-drive lab, and has diversified into general aviation and even rainbow-trout/salmon aquaculture.
notes: Company match confirmed (New United = 新誉集团). But the group's registered legal representative is shown as 周立成 (Zhou Licheng) on a brand-directory page (cnpp.cn/pinpai/4084356.html) and the chairman's name on the official site is an image; could not confirm whether 周立新 is the same person, a relative, or a Hurun romanisation variant. Very low profile.

name: Yang Delin
current_role: Legal representative and company head (chairman), Jiangsu Changhai Composite Materials (长海股份, SZSE ChiNext: 300196), per its 2026 interim report (under the name 杨国文 / Yang Guowen)
profile: The input's Chinese name, 杨国文 (Yang Guowen), matches the head of Jiangsu Changhai Composite Materials, a fiberglass and composite-materials maker in Yaoguan, Wujin district, Changzhou. He and Yang Pengwei (listed by Hurun as co-holder) are the company's actual controllers. He signed Changhai's 2026 half-year report as company head.
interesting_fact: Changhai is a vertically integrated fiberglass group, making glass-fibre yarn, mats and fabrics plus composite products and resins, at its base in Changzhou's Wujin district.
notes: Name mismatch: input pinyin 'Yang Delin' does not match the Chinese 杨国文 (Yang Guowen). The Changhai and Yang Pengwei details fit Yang Guowen, so this profile is of him; verify before outreach. Very low media profile.

name: Yang Pengwei
current_role: Director and general manager, Jiangsu Changhai Composite Materials (300196.SZ); co-actual controller with his father Yang Guowen (chairman)
profile: Second-generation owner and largest shareholder (~41.7%) of Changhai Composite Materials, a Changzhou fiberglass and glass-fibre composites maker (founded 2000, ChiNext-listed 2011). He runs it as GM while father Yang Guowen chairs the board; products serve rail, aerospace, electrical and telecom uses.
interesting_fact: Father and son together control more than half of Changhai: Yang Pengwei holds about 41.7% and Yang Guowen about 10.6%. Filings name them as acting in concert.
notes: Hurun lists him with 'Yang Delin', but filings name his father, the chairman and co-controller, as Yang Guowen (杨国文); Yang Fengqin (杨凤琴) is also named as a controller in older commitments. The IR email is from the 2024 annual report summary (April 2025). Very low public profile and no interviews found. Fibreglass maker, so the data-center link is weak.

name: Ma Chengzhang
current_role: No current role found (former founding shareholder of Hongli Opto-Electronic / Hongli Zhihui Group, SZSE: 300219)
profile: Ma Chengzhang (马成章) was a founding (promoter) shareholder of Guangzhou LED-packaging maker Hongli Opto-Electronic, now Hongli Zhihui Group. Company-registry data show him holding 4.74%, equal to co-founder Li Guoping's stake, when the company restructured in 2011. Hurun listed him from 2015 to 2021. Control of Hongli has since passed to Sichuan Jinduo Investment, and he is not named in its 2026 disclosures.
notes: Very little public information; his only trace is shareholder-registry data (https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1679829948404482). He holds no current board or management position at Hongli, whose chairman is Li Jundong. Company IR is not a route to him. Low priority.

name: Cao Qidong
current_role: Honorary Chairman, Ningbo Yongxin Optics Co. (603297.SH); stepped down as chairman in 2026 after 19 years
profile: Hong Kong industrialist and son of Ningbo-born tycoon Cao Kuang-piu (Novel Enterprises), whose 1997 investment created Yongxin Optics. He became chairman in 2007 and took it public in Shanghai in 2018. Yongxin makes high-end microscopes and precision optics. In 2026, aged 75, he became honorary chairman.
interesting_fact: Yongxin built China's first space microscope, installed on the Tianhe core module. It was used in the February 2022 'Tiangong classroom' broadcast to show beating heart-muscle cells in orbit. Yongxin also made camera lenses for the Chang'e-2, -3 and -4 lunar missions.
deep_cut_fact: The company name honours his father's Hong Kong group, Novel (永新). In Chinese it means 'forever innovating', and the English word deliberately evokes a long, legendary story. From 2005 Cao spent about two years acting as the bridge that completed Yongxin's acquisition of Nanjing Jiangnan Yongxin.
notes: Recently retired to an honorary role (Securities Times, stcn.com/article/detail/4058883.html). He announced the succession in a letter to all shareholders on Yongxin's official WeChat account. Formal route: the Yongxin Optics board secretary office.

name: Han Yu
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Shenzhen Hopewind Electric Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603063)
profile: Power-electronics engineer (b. 1964, PhD, senior engineer) who joined Shenzhen Hopewind Electric in 2009 and chairs it; he holds ~87m shares via Shenzhen Pingqi Technology.
