interesting_fact: Jiangsu Fasten, which he co-controls, was recognized by China's MIIT as a national 'specialized and sophisticated little giant' in 2021 and again in 2024 for its specialty steel wire.
notes: Listed company chairman is Chen Mingjun (since 2018); Zhou Jiang holds no executive role at the listed company. Only appeared on Hurun 2012-2013. Company websites (chinafasten.com/.cn) unreachable; no published contact verified. Web search budget exhausted, so his exact title at Fasten Hongsheng Group is unconfirmed.

name: Hou Lirong
current_role: Shareholder of Allwinner Technology (全志科技, SZSE ChiNext: 300458), per Hurun; title/role not confirmed
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List 2021 (est. ~US$330M) with wealth from Allwinnertech, the Zhuhai-based fabless chip designer founded in 2007 that makes application-processor SoCs, analog/power and wireless chips for tablets, set-top boxes, smart home, automotive, robotics and industrial control; listed in Shenzhen in 2015. Her personal role at the company could not be verified.
notes: Appeared on Hurun only in 2021 (Allwinner share-price peak). Not named on the company website. Company IR details are in its annual reports on cninfo.com.cn. Web search budget exhausted mid-lane, so role unconfirmed.

name: Ji Xinhua
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, UCloud Technology (优刻得, 688158.SH)
profile: Ji Xinhua (b. 1979), a noted Chinese white-hat hacker, ran security at Huawei, Tencent and Shanda before founding UCloud in 2012. UCloud's 2020 STAR Market IPO was China's first public-cloud listing and first dual-class A-share. He is now steering it toward AI compute and overseas expansion.
interesting_fact: In June 2026 UCloud opened an availability zone in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, its 36th worldwide across 28 regions. Ji's stated rule: 'we will build in every country with more than 30 million people,' as part of a 'Digital Silk Road' strategy.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup, 'Ala Shanghai' (阿拉上海), launched in 1998 while he was an electrical-automation student at Tongji University. It was a local-life site that predated Dianping by years and failed for being too early. In 2012 he sold an apartment in Shenzhen to fund UCloud after more than 100 investors turned him down.
notes: Accessible and media-friendly: he gives frequent interviews to Chinese financial press. Strong fit for a data-center/AI-compute episode (UCloud runs large intelligent-computing centres, e.g. in Ulanqab). He was early in his career as Tencent Security Center deputy GM.

name: Li Shijun
current_role: Top-10 shareholder and long-time director/general manager (from 2011 per research reports) of Shenzhen S.C New Energy Technology (捷佳伟创, SZSE: 300724); current title not confirmed
profile: Li Shijun (李时俊) is an early partner in S.C New Energy, China's leading maker of solar-cell manufacturing equipment (wet benches, diffusion furnaces, PECVD, etching). He joined around 2008-2010 bringing a semiconductor-equipment team that moved the firm into dry-process tools; it listed in Shenzhen in 2018 and he remains a top-10 shareholder (2026).
interesting_fact: S.C rode the solar industry's shift from BSF to PERC cells to become China's top PV-cell equipment supplier, holding 196 patents by 2018.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 22 years (1985-2007) at the Electronics Ministry's 48th Research Institute, a pioneer of Chinese semiconductor and PV equipment, rising from head of its Ion Beam Technology Lab to assistant director before joining S.C.
notes: 'S.C' = Shenzhen S.C New Energy Technology (捷佳伟创); despite the 'semiconductor equipment' tag, its core business is solar PV cell equipment. Controllers are Liang Meizhen, Zuo Guojun and Yu Zhong; Li is a significant shareholder. Very low public profile; route via company board office.

name: Li Xiaodan
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder and co-actual controller (with chairman Xing Meizheng) of Shenzhen Jufei Optoelectronics (SZSE ChiNext: 300303).
profile: Li Xiaodan is one of two actual controllers of Jufei Optoelectronics, a Shenzhen SMD LED packager (founded 2005) supplying phones, PCs, TVs, displays, auto electronics, sensing and optical comms. She holds ~3.05% and acts in concert with chairman Xing Meizheng (together ~10.8%), renewing their agreement on 27 Oct 2026.
interesting_fact: Jufei's 2025 revenue rose 13% to about RMB 3.45bn; the company's product range now spans optical sensing and optical-communication components alongside display backlight LEDs.
notes: No personal biography published; she holds no disclosed executive post. Relationship to Xing Meizheng not stated in filings. Only route is Jufei securities/board office email.

name: Xing Meizheng
current_role: Chairman (company head) and co-controlling shareholder, Shenzhen Jufei Optoelectronics (聚飞光电, SZSE 300303)
profile: Co-controlling shareholder (with Li Xiaodan) and head of Shenzhen Jufei Optoelectronics, founded in 2005 and listed on ChiNext in March 2012. Jufei is one of China's leading makers of LED backlight components for phones, TVs and displays, and has expanded into lighting, automotive and optical-device products.
interesting_fact: Jufei grew from a 2005 Shenzhen start-up with RMB59.5m registered capital into what Chinese industry press calls the country's leading backlight-LED maker within seven years of founding.
notes: Low profile; no personal interviews found. Best route is Jufei's securities/IR office (jfzq@, tel 0755-29646311).

name: Corbin J Robertson Jr
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Natural Resource Partners L.P. (NYSE: NRP); director, Quintana Minerals and KLX Energy Services
profile: Houston-born (1947) grandson of oilman Hugh Roy Cullen, founder of Quintana Petroleum. He started in the family business at 15, inherited oil holdings and in the 1980s moved into coal royalties, amassing one of the largest private U.S. coal reserves. He leads NRP, a Houston partnership owning mineral and royalty interests (coal, soda ash, carbon-neutral initiatives).
interesting_fact: He was an All-American linebacker at the University of Texas who captained the Longhorns to victory in the 1969 Cotton Bowl Classic.
deep_cut_fact: Racing as 'Saron Stable', he bred Turkoman (by Alydar), voted 1986 Eclipse Award U.S. Champion Older Male, and raced Hall of Fame filly Bold 'n Determined (inducted 1997).
notes: Goes by 'Corby'. Serves on University of Houston Energy Advisory Board; UH has a Corbin J. Robertson Society. Major GOP donor and coal-industry figure: politically sensitive topics. NRP IR contact is the only published route.

name: Steven Ferguson
current_role: Principal of Linton Investments, the Ferguson family investment office (Aberdeenshire, Scotland)
profile: Aberdeenshire entrepreneur who built Kintore-based Ferguson Group (offshore containers, accommodation modules) into a global offshore rental business over three decades, selling it to Brambles in 2014 for ~£320m. Now invests via family office Linton Investments, incl. North Sea services firm Centrifuges Un-Limited (2020).
interesting_fact: Ferguson Group grew from a small North Sea container firm into a global business with a fleet of 16,000+ offshore containers, tanks and baskets, and in 2011 launched its own 220-berth accommodation service vessel, ASV Pioneer.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 the Ferguson family set up the Inverurie Youth Sports Foundation, which has funded 61 young athletes across 34 sports in the Garioch area - including freestyle skier Kirsty Muir (2022 Winter Olympian) and Tokyo Paralympic finalist swimmer Conner Morrison.
notes: Private family-office figure; best route is Linton Investments' published admin email. Sale-to-Brambles detail per Energy Voice (https://www.energyvoice.com/?p=64838, not directly fetchable here). Energy angle: North Sea services and decommissioning (Centrifuges).

name: Michael Gregory
profile: A UK businessman listed on Hurun Global (2015–2019) and the Sunday Times Rich List (about £295–320m) with wealth from engineering services and electric power. An East Midlands rich-list ranking places a Michael Gregory at £295m, but I couldn't confirm his company from public sources.
notes: Ambiguous common name. A Michael Gregory appears at £295m in an East Midlands rich-list ranking (https://www.hinckleytimes.net/news/local-news/triumph-rich-list-john-bloor-9151652), but no industry is given. Do not confuse him with Michael John Gregory of Amber Infrastructure or Prof. Sir Mike Gregory of Cambridge. The Sunday Times Rich List entry text is needed to identify his company.

name: Li Ruijie
current_role: Chairman, Shenzhen Power Leader Investment Holding (宝德集团); actual controller of Power Leader Computer Systems (server maker)
profile: Li Ruijie (b. 1967, Jieyang, Guangdong) co-founded server maker Power Leader (宝德) with his wife Zhang Yunxia in 1997, listed it in Hong Kong in 2002, and pushed it into online-game servers and games, which became Shenzhen-listed Zhongqingbao (中青宝). He has handed Zhongqingbao's chair to the next generation while controlling Power Leader Computing, a domestic server/PC maker.
interesting_fact: His Power Leader Computing, a Chinese server maker, unveiled a custom 'PowerStar' CPU in May 2023, produced by Intel specially for Power Leader and aimed at commercial branded PCs.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in the early 1990s selling sound cards before moving into server after-sales and then manufacturing, riding Intel's rise; Power Leader went public in Hong Kong within about three years of being founded.
notes: No published contact found (powerleader.com.cn blocked automated fetch). Sensitive: in Mar 2025 Shenzhen CSRC bureau issued administrative penalties to Zhang Yunxia and Li Ruijie over disclosure violations; the 2023 PowerStar chip launch drew 'rebadged Intel' criticism. Avoid these in outreach.

name: Zhang Yunxia
current_role: Co-founder and co-controller of PowerLeader (宝德) group, Shenzhen; legal representative and head of Shenzhen Zhongqingbao Interactive Network (ZQGame, SZ:300052)
profile: Tianjin-born, Nankai University computer-software graduate who co-founded Shenzhen PowerLeader (宝德) in 1997, now a top domestic Chinese server/cloud-hardware brand. The group also controls listed online-game and cloud-services company Zhongqingbao (ZQGame), where she was GM 2008-2012 and is now legal representative. Wealth shared with co-controller Li Ruijie.
interesting_fact: PowerLeader, which she co-founded in 1997, describes itself as one of China's top 5 domestic server brands and No. 9 in the Asia-Pacific server market. It now builds AI/GPU servers and cloud solutions.
deep_cut_fact: Before PowerLeader she co-founded Shenzhen Lehe Electronics (乐和电子) in 1991. In 2018 she was elected executive president of the Shenzhen Women Entrepreneurs' Chamber of Commerce.
notes: Sensitive. A Shenzhen CSRC penalty (Mar 2025) says she was detained on 29 Dec 2023 on suspicion of refusing to carry out a court judgment and released on bail the same day; disclosure was delayed. Investor suits are ongoing (https://www.163.com/dy/article/KU4B2AE70519BOCB.html). The deep-cut source is a user-uploaded profile site. Best route is ZQGame IR.

name: Yuan Huaidong
current_role: Executive director & GM, Juning Group (巨凝集团, Changzhou building materials/property); early investor and former 5%+ shareholder of Sinofibers (中简科技, 300777.SZ)
profile: Changzhou businessman (b. 1965) who built Juning Group, a ready-mix concrete, property and venture-investment group, with his wife Shi Qiufang. The couple were founding backers of carbon-fibre maker Sinofibers and together held 12% at its 2019 ChiNext IPO, which put them on the Hurun list in 2020. They have since sold down and are no longer top-10 holders (Q1 2026).
interesting_fact: Sinofibers' IPO prospectus lists him as a 6.1% holder and his wife Shi Qiufang as a 5.9% holder. It also names him as a director of Donghai Securities and of Jiangsu Gaojin Venture Capital.
deep_cut_fact: He sat on the board of Sinofibers' predecessor (中简有限) as one of its original investors' representatives. His building-materials company 巨凝建材 (now Juning Group) was an investor when the carbon-fibre maker was set up in 2008.
notes: Identity confirmed from the Sinofibers IPO prospectus (2019), which identifies Yuan Huaidong and Shi Qiufang as husband and wife. He is a private Changzhou investor, not a company executive. In 2021 Sinofibers issued a notice on a disclosure lapse when the couple sold shares. They no longer appear among the top-10 holders in the Q1 2026 report. No personal channel was found. The Sinofibers IR email only reaches the company; a better route is Juning Group in Changzhou.

name: Shi Qiufang
current_role: Co-owner (49%) of Juning Group, Changzhou; executive director & GM of its concrete subsidiaries; former 5%+ shareholder of Sinofibers (中简科技)
profile: Changzhou businesswoman (b. 1962) and wife of Yuan Huaidong. She co-owns Juning Group (concrete, property, education) with him and runs several of its ready-mix concrete and trading companies. The couple were early investors in carbon-fibre maker Sinofibers and held a combined 12% at its 2019 IPO, which put them on Hurun's 2020 list. They have since sold down.
interesting_fact: At Sinofibers' 2019 IPO she held 21.17m shares (5.88%) in her own name, almost as many as her husband's 6.12%, making her one of the carbon-fibre maker's largest individual shareholders.
deep_cut_fact: Besides the Sinofibers stake, she is executive director and GM of several Juning companies: Changzhou Juning Yongheng Concrete, Changzhou Juning Concrete, Juning Decoration Engineering and Benlong Materials.
notes: Identity confirmed from the Sinofibers IPO prospectus, which shows her as Yuan Huaidong's wife and acting-in-concert party. She is a passive investor in Sinofibers and very private. In 2021 the company issued a notice on a disclosure lapse when the couple sold shares. She is not among the top-10 holders as of Q1 2026. Best route is via Juning Group.

name: Steven Lamprell
current_role: Founder of Lamprell (UAE-based energy fabrication/rig services group); not involved in day-to-day management
profile: British-born (1950) entrepreneur who moved to the UAE with his family and founded Lamprell in 1976, growing it from rig maintenance into jack-up rigs, FPSO modules and offshore-wind structures. He sold a majority stake in its 2006 London AIM float (reported GBP 265M); Lamprell marked its 50th anniversary in 2026.
interesting_fact: For Lamprell's 50th anniversary (2026) he said: 'What I am most proud of is not the scale Lamprell has reached, but the culture that remains... It has been a privilege to pioneer Lamprell and witness its 50-year success story.'
deep_cut_fact: He is a keen polo player with his own entry in Horace Laffaye's 'The Polo Encyclopedia', and a racehorse owner.
notes: Private; Dubai/UAE-based. Lamprell is no longer London-listed. Energy-transition angle: Lamprell now builds offshore wind foundations as well as oil & gas structures. Approach via company communications.

name: Manish H Bhatia
current_role: President and Chief Operating Officer, Micron Technology (previously EVP Global Operations); Independent Director, Quantinuum
profile: Joined Micron in 2017 as EVP Global Operations; now President & COO, running its business units, fabs, supply chain, IT/AI and government affairs (the HBM/DRAM build-out behind the AI data-center boom). Previously led silicon operations at Western Digital and SanDisk after McKinsey and Matrix Semiconductor. Quantinuum board member.
interesting_fact: He was awarded Singapore's Public Service Medal (Friends of Singapore) in 2024 for contributions to the country's semiconductor industry, and sits on the Singapore Economic Development Board and the U.S.-Japan Business Council.
deep_cut_fact: An MIT mechanical engineer (BS and MS), he did his MBA at MIT Sloan as a Leaders for Manufacturing fellow, and early on worked at Matrix Semiconductor, the 3D one-time-programmable memory startup later bought by SanDisk.
notes: Title has changed: Micron's site now lists him as President & COO (input shows EVP Global Operations). Chairs Quantinuum's nominating & governance committee. Matrix Semiconductor detail: Micron bio confirms he worked there; the 3D-memory/SanDisk description is general background on that company. Route via Micron corporate communications (media contact Mark Plungy).

name: Thomas E Jorden
current_role: Non-Executive Chair of the Board, Devon Energy (since the May 2026 Devon-Coterra merger)
profile: Geophysicist and shale-era E&P chief: he joined Key Production in 1993 as chief geophysicist, became CEO (2011) and chairman (2012) of Cimarex Energy, then led Coterra Energy (Cimarex + Cabot, 2021) as chairman, CEO and president. After Devon's all-stock ~$58bn combination with Coterra closed on 7 May 2026, he became Devon's non-executive board chair.
interesting_fact: He steered two big shale mergers in five years - Cimarex/Cabot into Coterra (2021) and Coterra into Devon (2026) - ending up chairing one of the largest US independent oil & gas producers.
deep_cut_fact: He earned both his bachelor's and master's in geophysics at the Colorado School of Mines, later chaired its Board of Trustees, and started his career at Superior Oil Company and Union Pacific Resources before joining Key Production as chief geophysicist in 1993. He is also a Tulane University trustee.
notes: SEC-derived wealth (~$316m). Devon media contact is Michelle Hindmarch (phone only published). Known as a thoughtful, technical speaker on shale and capital discipline - a good podcast guest candidate via Devon communications.

name: Jack A Fusco
current_role: Chairman (since May 2026), President and CEO (since May 2016), Cheniere Energy, Inc. (NYSE: LNG)
profile: A 40-year power and gas veteran, Fusco runs Cheniere, the largest US LNG exporter (Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi). Earlier he cofounded Goldman-backed Orion Power (CEO 1998-2002), ran Texas Genco to a 5x+ return on its 2006 merger with NRG, and as Calpine CEO (2008-14) led it out of bankruptcy to become America's largest gas-fired power generator.
interesting_fact: Named 2025 Chief Executive of the Year at the Platts Global Energy Awards and repeatedly Institutional Investor's best natural-gas CEO (2020, 2022-2025); in 2012 he was its best electric-industry CEO.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in 1984 as a mechanical engineer at Pacific Gas & Electric straight out of Cal State Sacramento; 13 years later he moved to Goldman Sachs as a VP trading wholesale electricity, which led to founding Orion Power. He sits on the board of the American-Italian Cancer Foundation.
notes: Very relevant: gas-to-power and LNG exports tie into data-center power demand; frequent CERAWeek/Gastech speaker, so conference-stage interviews are a realistic route. Media requests via Cheniere newsroom/IR.

name: Gyan M Swarup
current_role: Director (listed from 2012), Paharpur Cooling Towers Ltd., Kolkata (role not confirmed as current)
profile: Gyan Mahendra Swarup is listed as a director of Paharpur Cooling Towers, a family-owned Kolkata maker of cooling towers, air-cooled condensers and heat exchangers incorporated in 1949. Hurun India listed him in 2018-19. Day-to-day leadership is held by Gaurav Swarup (Co-Chairman & MD) and Vikram Swarup (MD).
interesting_fact: Paharpur is one of the world's largest cooling-tower makers, with offices across India plus Europe and Turkey operations. Its heat-rejection technology matters for thermal power and, increasingly, data-center cooling.
notes: Almost no public biographical information; his relationship to Gaurav and Vikram Swarup is unverified. Whether he is alive and still on the board is unconfirmed; check MCA filings. The listed email is Paharpur's general company address, not a personal one. Gaurav Swarup is the more public family member.

name: Deming Xiao
current_role: EVP, Global Operations, Monolithic Power Systems (Nasdaq: MPWR)
profile: Process engineer turned operations chief who joined power-semiconductor maker MPS in May 2001 as Foundry Manager, led MPS Asia Operations from 2008, and now runs global operations. MPS power-management chips are key to AI server and data-centre power delivery. Earlier he worked at Chartered Semiconductor and Fairchild Imaging Sensors.
interesting_fact: An early MPS employee (joined 2001, three years before its 2004 IPO), he built out the fabless company's Asian foundry and manufacturing base as MPS grew into a major supplier of power chips for AI accelerators.
deep_cut_fact: He studied semiconductor physics at Sichuan University in Chengdu (B.S.), earned an MSEE at Wayne State University in Detroit, and spent six years managing process integration engineering at Fairchild Imaging Sensors before joining MPS.
notes: Low public profile operations executive (age 62 per the FY2024 10-K). Best route is MPS investor relations. Bio also on the MPS management page (https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/about-mps/managementteam.html), which is JS-rendered.

name: Lian Guangming
current_role: Unknown; Hurun China (2007-2015) listed him with 'Simon' (coal and real estate)
profile: Lian Guangming appeared on the Hurun China Rich List from 2007 to 2015 with an estimated $310m fortune from coal and real estate via a company Hurun calls 'Simon'. No public English- or Chinese-language source identifying the company or his current role was found.
notes: Very private; not found in web searches. Company name 'Simon' (possibly a transliteration such as Ximeng) unverified. Would need Chinese business registry research. Low-priority target.

name: Li An’min
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller, Shanxi Antai Group (600408.SH); no longer chairman (chairman since June 2025 is Li Meng)
profile: Li Anmin founded the Anmin coking plant in Jiexiu, Shanxi in 1984 and from 1993 led Shanxi Antai Group as chairman and GM, expanding from a single coking plant into coal washing, coke, steel rolling, power and building materials; the company listed in Shanghai in 2003. He remains its controlling shareholder (~31.6%) per 2025-26 filings.
interesting_fact: Antai built a state-approved national eco-industrial demonstration park (2006) and is a national circular-economy pilot, recovering coke-oven by-products and using dry coke quenching; it now pursues a Shanxi near-zero-carbon industrial park pilot.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in 1984 as factory director of the Anmin Coking Plant he founded, the business that grew into Antai Group.
notes: Poor podcast fit: past exchange censure (2015) and CSRC penalty (2016) over related-party disclosures; his shares were frozen/pledged in a bank dispute settled Jan 2026. Fortune listing is dated (Hurun 2007-2015). Coal/coke rather than clean energy. Referenced as living controlling shareholder in Feb 2026 share-unfreezing filings.

name: Li Jiankang
profile: Appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2008-2021 (~USD 310M) with wealth attributed to 'Taxin' in petrochemicals and baijiu (white spirit). Chinese and English searches did not surface a verifiable record linking a Li Jiankang (李健康) to a 'Taxin' group, so identity and current status are unconfirmed.
notes: Company Chinese name not found ('Taxin' may be a Hurun romanisation); needs a Hurun-profile or business-registry lookup to disambiguate. Not to be confused with Baota Petrochemical (chairman Sun Hengchao).

name: Zhang Yanfu
profile: He appeared on the Hurun China list in 2009-2011 (with Zhang Jiefu), linked to the 'Xinjiang Foreign Economic & Trade Group' with interests in coal, real estate and mining. I could not find any current, verifiable information on him or his role at the group in English or Chinese sources.
notes: Not verifiable online; the last list appearance was in 2011. The journalist should deprioritise him. Note that any Xinjiang coal or mining business may carry supply-chain and reputational sensitivities (Xinjiang-related US import restrictions).

name: Zhang Jiefu
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2009-2011 (with Zhang Yanfu) for Xinjiang Foreign Economic & Trade Group (新疆对外经济贸易集团), coal, real estate and mining. No current public information found confirming his role or the group's status.
notes: Could not verify identity or current status via Chinese/English searches; off the Hurun list since 2011. Xinjiang business exposure may carry sanctions/forced-labour sensitivities for a US podcast. Low priority.

name: Chen Niandai
current_role: Founder, Chairman & President of Huiren Group (汇仁集团), Nanchang, Jiangxi (latest available; current status unverified)
profile: Chen Niandai (陈年代) founded Huiren Pharmaceutical in Nanchang in 1992 as a Sino-foreign joint venture and built it into Huiren Group, known for mass-market TCM tonic brands such as Huiren Shenbao, later adding investments. He appeared on Hurun's China Rich List 2005-2015; no recent public activity was found.
interesting_fact: He was elected a deputy to China's National People's Congress in 2003 and named one of Jiangxi's first 'Top 10 Economic Figures' that year.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in 1984 at Nanchang Shuanghuan Industrial; he set up Huiren in Sept 1992 and in 2002 received China's national May Day Labour Medal.
notes: Listed industry 'data_center_ai' focus seems a dataset artefact; he is a pharma entrepreneur. Off Hurun since 2015; sources are dated (2000s). Company website not reachable in this pass; no published contact found.

name: Xu Lianguo
current_role: Board chairman, Zonda Group (中大集团), Yancheng, Jiangsu (as of 2008; current status unconfirmed)
profile: Co-leader, with Xu Liankuan (group president), of Zonda Group, a private Jiangsu manufacturer founded in 1994 whose Zonda Bus unit makes coaches, city buses and commercial vehicles, later including new-energy buses, plus auto-maintenance equipment. He appeared on Hurun China 2006-2011. Little has been published about him since about 2008.
interesting_fact: In Jan 2008, as Zonda board chairman, he signed a cooperation agreement in Yancheng with the US company CD3I, part of Zonda's push abroad; Zonda buses were exported to Asia-Pacific, Africa, Latin America, the Middle East, Australia and the EU.
notes: Sparse, dated coverage, and the chinabuses.com source page could not be loaded directly (fact taken from the search snippet). Brother/associate Xu Liankuan was the group's public face (EU business week 2007, Beijing NEV base). No live company website or contact found. Low priority.

name: Xu Liankuan
current_role: Founder/chairman (historically), Zonda Industrial Group, Yangzhou, Jiangsu; current status unclear
profile: Xu Liankuan built Zonda (中大) Industrial Group in Jiangsu, spanning buses and coaches (Zonda Bus), new-energy vehicles and battery storage, with a Hong Kong-listed arm (China Zhongda). In the 2000s-2010s he pushed electric buses and planned an NEV base in Beijing. Little reliable recent information is available.
interesting_fact: Under him Zonda was an early Chinese mover in electric buses and power-battery storage; he planned to expand Zonda's new-energy vehicle base in Beijing.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he was elected deputy chairman of the first board of the China Power Supply Association, a national body focused on battery energy-storage and power-system equipment.
notes: CAUTION: Hong Kong's SFC lists Xu Lian Kuan (徐连宽) as a 'person of interest' it has been unable to contact since 2019 regarding Zhongda and subsidiaries (https://www.sfc.hk/en/Regulatory-functions/Enforcement/Have-you-seen-these-people/Persons-of-interest/Xu-Lian-Kuan). Whereabouts/current role unknown; not a recommended outreach target.

name: Gao Huaixue
current_role: Former controlling shareholder and founder-chairman of GI Technologies (吉艾科技, SZ:300309); no current public role found
profile: Gao co-founded Beijing-based GI Technologies with Xu Bo. The company made oilfield logging and well-service equipment and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2012. Gao was its controlling shareholder until 2020, when he agreed to sell a 19.66% stake to Qingke Chuang Industrial Group, changing control. The company was later delisted (2023).
interesting_fact: GI Technologies was one of the early private Chinese oilfield-logging-equipment makers on ChiNext; Gao and Xu Bo controlled it as concert parties for about a decade after listing.
notes: Very private, with no recent public profile. He has exited the company, and the listed entity has since been delisted, so there is no corporate channel. Low priority.

name: Liu Chenglin
profile: Listed on Hurun China (2011-2021) with wealth attributed to 'MEC' (coal and air-charter services). Searches in English and Chinese (刘丞霖) did not identify the company behind 'MEC' or any verifiable profile.
notes: Could not confirm identity or company; 'MEC' should not be assumed to be HK-listed Mongolia Energy Corp (whose chairman is a different person). Needs the Hurun entry's Chinese company name to research further.

name: Yang Jianzhong
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder and director-level family principal of Juli Sling Co. (巨力索具, SZSE: 002342) / Juli Group, Xushui, Baoding, Hebei; chaired the listed company through its 1st-6th boards (to ~2022)
profile: Born 1965, Yang Jianzhong has run the family rigging business in Xushui, Hebei since 1992, building Juli Group and its SZSE-listed unit Juli Sling (wire-rope slings, rigging and hoisting gear, incl. for energy projects). He chaired Juli Sling for its first six board terms; brother Yang Jianguo has chaired it since ~2022. Hurun listed the family wealth jointly.
interesting_fact: He served as a deputy to China's 11th and 12th National People's Congress and has been named a National Model Worker and Hebei Outstanding Entrepreneur.
deep_cut_fact: His official honours include serving as a 'Baoding Image Ambassador' (保定形象大使) for his home city, alongside the 5th Hebei Province Entrepreneur award; he holds a master's degree and the professional title of senior business manager (高级经营师).
notes: IR email is the board secretary's as published in Dec 2019; may be stale, check latest cninfo filings. Per mid-2026 press, Juli Sling disclosed a CSRC investigation (May 2026) and Juli Group had management changes; tread carefully and confirm his current title. Hurun pairs him with 'Yang Xiang'.

name: Cheng Zhishan
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2011-2015) as Cheng Zhishan (程志山), with wealth from Sinovel Wind Group (华锐风电), the Beijing wind-turbine maker founded in 2005 by Han Junliang that listed in Shanghai in 2011. No public source naming him as a Sinovel executive or disclosed shareholder was found; he was likely an indirect, IPO-era investor.
notes: Identity could not be verified in English or Chinese web sources. Sinovel's IPO-era backers held their stakes through investment vehicles (e.g. Xizang Xinmeng, Ruihua Fengneng), so he may have held through one of these. Hurun dropped him after 2015 and Sinovel's value has fallen sharply since, so the listed wealth is stale. Not recommended for outreach.

name: Zhu Fengxue
current_role: Co-actual controller and major shareholder, ZPEC - Zhongman Petroleum and Natural Gas Group (603619.SH), Shanghai
profile: Zhu Fengxue is, with chairman Li Chundi, a controlling shareholder of ZPEC, a Shanghai private oil and gas group founded in 2003 and backed early by Sequoia. ZPEC grew from drilling contractor and rig maker into upstream production, working in Iraq, Pakistan and its own Tenge oilfield in Kazakhstan. He has been selling down shares since late 2025.
interesting_fact: ZPEC, a private Chinese driller, won a $526.6M Iraqi government contract to drill 66 production wells at the giant West Qurna 2 oilfield, and in 2019 entered Kazakhstan to develop its own Tenge oilfield.
notes: Almost no personal public profile: no interviews or bio found, appears only in shareholder filings (e.g. https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2024-08-16/1220882095.PDF). Chairman Li Chundi is the company's public face. Company contact is the only route.

name: Gong Hui
current_role: Founder, Zhuhai Miaocun Technology (NAND flash storage-controller chips); co-founder and >5% shareholder of Allwinner Technology (SZSE: 300458)
profile: Zhuhai chip veteran Gong Hui co-founded fabless SoC designer Allwinner Technology in 2007, serving as director and VP for manufacturing and quality; Allwinner listed in Shenzhen in 2015 and its low-cost processors power tablets and smart devices. In 2017 he founded Miaocun Technology, which develops NAND flash controllers and error-correction tech.
interesting_fact: Allwinner's 2015 IPO prospectus is described as 'half a history of Zhuhai's chip industry': many of its original shareholders, including Gong, went on to found their own chip startups in edge AI, RISC-V, storage and power management.
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1993 as an engineer at Zhuhai Yali Electronics, then from 2002 ran manufacturing at Actions Semiconductor (Zhuhai Juli) before leaving to co-found Allwinner in 2007.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal channels found. Route would be via Allwinner (allwinnertech.com) or Miaocun Technology. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Huang Xueliang
current_role: Founder, Chairman, Executive Director and CEO, SMIT Holdings Ltd (国微控股, 2239.HK), Shenzhen
profile: Huang Xueliang (黄学良) is a veteran Chinese IC designer with 40+ years in the industry. He chaired Shenzhen State Micro (国微) from 1993 to 2022, founded SMIT Holdings (HK-listed maker of digital-TV conditional-access modules and security chips), and chaired EDA/FPGA-prototyping firm S2C until 2022. He was deputy director of the China Semiconductor Industry Association's IC Design Branch, 2005-2023.
interesting_fact: He helped build China's chip-design ecosystem: besides SMIT he chaired S2C (上海思尔芯), a pioneer in FPGA-based prototyping tools used to verify chip designs before tape-out.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a semiconductor degree at Xidian University (then the North-western Telecommunications Engineering School) in 1984 and an EE master's at Southeast University in 1989, then started at China National Electronic Devices Corp.'s Shenzhen branch distributing computer components before launching State Micro in 1993.
notes: Identity partly uncertain: input lists 'Sunmoon Microelectronics' (Hurun 2021), which we could not match; Huang Xueliang of State Micro/SMIT is the best-matching semiconductor billionaire of this name. Marketing@ is a general marketing inbox, not a dedicated press office.

name: Jiang Guibin
current_role: Founder, Chairman and legal representative, Zhuhai Enpower Electric Co. Ltd. (英搏尔, SZSE: 300681)
profile: Electrical-engineering PhD (b. 1975) who founded Zhuhai Enpower Electric in 2005 and controls ~21%. Enpower is a Tier-1 supplier of EV powertrain electronics - drive motors, motor controllers, on-board chargers, DC-DC converters and multi-in-one assemblies - and is expanding into eVTOL electric propulsion.
interesting_fact: Enpower has used its in-house 'integrated core' (集成芯) technology - originally for multi-in-one EV powertrains - to develop electric propulsion systems for eVTOL aircraft and drones, positioning a car-parts maker in China's 'low-altitude economy'.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his engineering PhD in electrical engineering at Xi'an Jiaotong University in 2003, spent 2004-06 as chief engineer of Zhuhai Haibo Electronics, and founded Enpower in 2005 at age 29-30 while still in that job; he is also listed as one of the company's core technical staff.

public_contacts.value: xuhuidong@enpower.com (board secretary Xu Huidong, as published in 2025 annual report)
enpower@vip.163.com (company email listed in 2025 annual report)

notes: Hurun listing (2021) only; wealth tied to Enpower share price. Engineer-founder with little English-language press; approach via board secretary in Chinese. Energy angle is EV/eVTOL power electronics rather than grid/data centres.

name: Lam Yee Chun
current_role: Founder, executive director and CEO, VPower Group International Holdings (HKEX: 1608); stepped down as executive chairman Dec 2023
profile: Hong Kong entrepreneur (born c.1972, also known as Samson Lam) who founded VPower, a designer and integrator of engine-based electricity generation units and distributed power plants in Hong Kong, mainland China and Southeast Asia (listed 2016). His Hurun wealth (2021 only) comes from his and Chan Mei Wan's VPower stake.
interesting_fact: VPower builds gas- and diesel-engine generation units and operates distributed power plants, a modular approach to fast-track power supply for emerging markets.
notes: Hurun lists him under China; VPower is Hong Kong-based. Role per MarketScreener and the VPower executive-changes announcement. Simply Wall St also links 'Samson Lam' to Paka Capital, unverified. I couldn't find a sourced biography detail for a deep-cut fact. Fortune and share price have fallen sharply since 2021; don't mention.

name: Chan Mei Wan
current_role: Director of various subsidiaries of VPower Group International Holdings (HKEX: 1608); resigned as non-executive director and vice chairwoman in Dec 2023
profile: Chan Mei Wan (陈美云) is the wife of VPower founder and CEO Lam Yee Chun (Samson Lam) and helped found the Hong Kong-based engine-based distributed power generation group, which designs, builds and operates gas/diesel-engine power plants and listed in Hong Kong in 2016. She served as its vice chairwoman and a non-executive director, advising on HR and finance, until stepping off the board in December 2023.
interesting_fact: She joined VPower in June 2001 and, according to the company, supported Lam's power-generation systems business from its founding, helping set up its operating system, corporate reorganisation and staff welfare scheme.
notes: Behind-the-scenes co-founder; her husband Samson Lam (VPower CEO) is the more natural podcast guest. Board resignation announced Dec 2023 (https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2023/1205/2023120500101.pdf).

name: Pan Feng
current_role: Co-actual controller (with spouse Zhong Wangjun) of Tianjin Jieqiang Equipment (捷强装备, 300875.SZ); chairman/GM 2015-July 2024, no longer in management
profile: Pan Feng (潘峰, b. 1968) led Jieqiang Equipment, a maker of nuclear-biological-chemical (NBC) defence and safety equipment, as chairman and general manager from 2015 until July 2024, taking it public on Shenzhen's ChiNext. He stepped down from management in 2024 and remains a co-controlling shareholder.
notes: NOT a suitable outreach target: per company disclosure he was placed under investigation in June 2024 and criminally detained in June 2025 on suspicion of unit bribery (https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2025-06-26/3922472.html). Defence/military-equipment business, not energy. Recommend skipping.

name: Zhong Wangjun
current_role: Co-founder and one of five actual controllers (~7.4% holder) of Tianjin Jieqiang Power Equipment Co., Ltd. (捷强装备, SZSE: 300875); no current board/executive title confirmed
profile: Zhong Wangjun (钟王军) was a founding cash investor when Tianjin Jieqiang was set up in 2005 and remains one of its five acting-in-concert controllers alongside largest holder Pan Feng. Jieqiang makes nuclear-biological-chemical (NBC) detection, protection and decontamination equipment for China's military, plus new-materials products; it listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2020.
interesting_fact: Jieqiang's core business is NBC security gear (radiation monitors, biological detectors, decontamination systems), and the 'Power' in its name comes from its origins in mobile power-supply vehicles.
deep_cut_fact: Jieqiang was founded on 1 Nov 2005 with RMB 3m of capital: Beijing Jieqiang contributed a utility-model patent for 'a power-supply vehicle' (一种电源车) valued at RMB 2.4m, and Zhong Wangjun put in RMB 444,000 in cash, the largest individual contribution.
notes: Defense-sector company; very low profile. Hurun 'Jieqiang Power' = 天津捷强动力装备. Chairman since July 2024 is Pan Qijing. Energy link is weak (power-supply vehicles origin). Approach via company general email.

name: Wu Wenqing
current_role: Unverified - listed by Hurun China 2021 under 'Anhui Guoxuan' (batteries, real estate, screen culture)
profile: Appears once on the Hurun China Rich List (2021) with wealth attributed to Anhui Guoxuan, the Hefei group behind battery maker Gotion High-Tech (founded by Li Zhen), which also has real-estate and other interests. Searches of Gotion filings and press found no public role or shareholding for a Wu Wenqing, so the link and current role could not be confirmed.
notes: Identity could not be confirmed; kept minimal. Gotion High-Tech's chairman and controlling holder is Li Zhen; Wu Wenqing may be a family member or partner in the private Guoxuan holding group - verify via Hurun 2021 entry or company registry before any outreach.

name: Yang Xiang
current_role: Shareholder and concerted party of the controlling Yang family of Juli Sling Co. (SZSE: 002342), Baoding, Hebei
profile: The Chinese name on file, 姚香 (Yao Xiang), matches the wife of Yang Jianzhong, one of the controlling Yang siblings of Juli Sling (巨力索具), China's leading maker of slings and rigging for lifting, construction and energy projects, based in Xushui, Baoding. She holds shares directly and acts in concert with the family; Hurun listed the couple's wealth in 2015.
interesting_fact: Juli Sling describes itself as the leader of China's rigging industry, running a national-level enterprise technology center and the Hebei provincial sling and rigging engineering innovation center, with 247 valid patents as of 2021.
notes: Romanization 'Yang Xiang' looks wrong: the name is 姚香 (Yao Xiang), spouse of Yang Jianzhong per Juli's 2021 annual report, hence identity 'uncertain'. Not an operating executive; no public profile. IR emails are the board secretary and securities rep from the 2021 report (may be out of date). Juli came under a CSRC investigation in May 2026 (https://stock.10jqka.com.cn/20260519/c676796665.shtml).

name: Guo Jun
profile: Listed once on the Hurun China Rich List (2015, ~US$310M) with source 'Chenxiang investment' in solar equipment. Searches in English and Chinese could not identify the company (辰祥/晨祥投资) or tie it to a specific Guo Jun (郭军 is a very common name), so no profile is given.
notes: Ambiguous common name and unidentifiable source company; would need the Hurun 2015 list entry (Chinese company name/city) to research further. Low priority.

name: Zhang Guoan
current_role: Controlling shareholder, Tong Petrotech / Tongyuan Petroleum Technology Group (通源石油, SZSE ChiNext: 300164), Xi'an
profile: Zhang Guoan (张国桉) is the controlling shareholder of Xi'an-based Tongyuan Petroleum (Tong Oil Tools), an oilfield-services firm founded in 1995 specialising in perforation technology, with fracturing, drilling/completion, coalbed-methane and enhanced-recovery services. It was among the first oilfield-services companies listed on ChiNext (2011). Day-to-day leadership is with chairman Ren Yanzhong.
interesting_fact: Tongyuan was one of the first oilfield-services companies to list on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in 2011 and positions itself as China's perforation-technology leader.
notes: Hurun-listed only in 2015 (~$310M). Confirmed as controlling shareholder in a May 2025 exchange filing (cninfo). No personal bio, interviews or published company IR email retrieved (company site unreachable); IR contact should be in Tongyuan's annual report on cninfo.com.cn. Low public profile.

name: Ding Yuxin
current_role: None public; former chairwoman of Beijing Boyou (Broad-union) Investment Management; sentenced in Dec 2014 to 20 years in prison
profile: Ding Yuxin (also Ding Shumiao), a Shanxi businesswoman, made her fortune in coal transportation and hotels and chaired Beijing Boyou Investment Management (Broad-union). In Dec 2014 a Beijing court sentenced her to 20 years and a 2.5bn yuan fine for bribery and illegal business tied to railway contracts under ex-minister Liu Zhijun.
interesting_fact: According to Caixin, she built her fortune in the coal transportation business before moving into hotels and investment management.
notes: Not a suitable outreach target: she was convicted in the Liu Zhijun railway graft case (20-year sentence, Dec 2014) and is presumably still in prison. Listed only on Hurun China 2010. Recommend dropping from the guest list.

name: Yan Tangfeng
current_role: President, Sinolion Holdings Pte Ltd (Singapore investment firm); independent director, China Sunsine Chemical Holdings (SGX), appointed 2019
profile: Singapore-based financier (b. ~1970, Shandong). He was the ultimate controlling shareholder (about 60%, through BVI vehicle Aceplus) and non-executive chairman of Shengli Oil & Gas Pipe Holdings (HKEX:1080), a maker of spiral-welded oil and gas line pipe that listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2009. He now runs the investment firm Sinolion and sits on the board of an SGX-listed rubber-chemicals maker.
interesting_fact: In 2009, the year his pipe company listed in Hong Kong, it reported revenue of about RMB3.0bn, nearly triple the RMB1.07bn of 2008, and profit of RMB336m.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in academia, not business. After graduating in engineering from Shandong University of Technology in 1994, he worked there until 2003, including as Communist Youth League committee secretary. He then moved to Singapore's ICH Capital as a VP and rose to senior VP of investments.
notes: Identity confirmed via HKEX filings (2009 annual report: 閆唐鋒, non-exec chairman and 60.21% holder via Aceplus) and a 2019 SGX announcement that cites his Shengli chairmanship. He lives in Singapore. He is no longer on Shengli's board; its 2025 report names Wei Jun as chairman. No published personal contact was found. Possible routes are Sinolion Holdings (Singapore) or the China Sunsine company secretary. SGX bio: https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/X0NGZVPH1N35T92M/f9db018c1a9524b7f6b46655c40a5b2ed4a7588d6d7e4e0d56f3b17f

name: Todd J. Kantor
current_role: Founder, Portfolio Manager and Managing Member, Encompass Capital Advisors LLC; Director of T1 Energy Inc. (NYSE: TE) since April 2024
profile: New York hedge-fund manager who launched Encompass Capital Advisors in 2012, an energy-focused fund investing across oil and gas, renewables and battery technology. Encompass is a 10%+ holder of T1 Energy (formerly FREYR Battery), the US solar-module and cell manufacturer, and Kantor sits on its board.
interesting_fact: Before starting Encompass he was a portfolio manager on Citadel's PioneerPath platform (2008-2012) and a senior analyst at Touradji Capital, a commodities-focused fund.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a senior research analyst and equity trader at Solstice Equity Management (2002-2005) after earning a BBA in finance from Emory University's Goizueta Business School.
notes: Low media profile; best route is Encompass's published office email. T1 Energy press releases also list an investor contact (EVP IR) and media contact (EVP Strategic Communications) - see ir.t1energy.com releases. Background from proxy-derived profile (fintool) and SEC 13D filings.

name: Robert Madison Murphy
current_role: Chairman, Murphy USA Inc. (NYSE: MUSA); Director, Murphy Oil Corp. (NYSE: MUR); President, The Murphy Foundation (El Dorado, Ark.)
profile: R. Madison Murphy is a scion of the El Dorado, Arkansas oil family; his father Charles H. Murphy Jr. built Murphy Oil. He is a longtime Murphy Oil director and has chaired fuel retailer Murphy USA since its 2013 spin-off. He also runs The Murphy Foundation and owns The Sumac Company, Arc Vineyards and Presqu'ile Winery.
interesting_fact: He has served as chairman of the Arkansas Highway Commission. He also bought ~$1.8M of Murphy USA stock in August 2025.
deep_cut_fact: His family's Santa Maria Valley (California) winery, Presqu'ile, is named after the Murphy family's longtime Gulf Coast gathering spot at Henderson Point near Pass Christian, Mississippi. 'Presqu'ile' is a Creole word meaning 'almost an island'.
notes: Still listed as Murphy USA Chairman in the 2026 proxy (https://s22.q4cdn.com/506259022/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/2026-Proxy-Statement.pdf). The IR email belongs to Murphy USA's VP of Investor Relations (company-published). Energy angle: Murphy Oil (E&P) plus Murphy USA (fuel retail).

name: Han Junliang
current_role: Unknown; former founder, chairman and president of Sinovel Wind Group (华锐风电) - left management in 2012-13
profile: Han Junliang (韩俊良) was deputy GM of a Dalian Heavy Industry equipment unit when he moved into wind power in 2004, licensing Fuhrländer's 1.5 MW turbine design and founding Sinovel (registered Feb 2006). Sinovel briefly became China's largest and the world's No.2 turbine maker and listed in Shanghai in 2011. He stepped down as president in 2012 and chairman in 2013; his current activity is not public.
interesting_fact: Sinovel went from incorporation in 2006 to the world's second-largest wind turbine maker in about four years, largely by localising a single licensed 1.5 MW German design at enormous scale.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Sinovel he was deputy general manager of Dalian Heavy Industry's mechanical & electrical equipment complete-sets company; his first move into wind (2004) was securing a production licence for Fuhrländer's FL1500 turbine series.
notes: Out of public life since ~2013. Sensitive history: CSRC penalised Sinovel and 15 individuals including Han over overstated 2011 revenue (https://www.csrc.gov.cn/csrc/c101928/c1042913/content.shtml); Sinovel (the company, not Han personally) was convicted in the US in 2018 over AMSC trade secrets. No public contact route found; likely unsuitable/unreachable.

name: Qu Naijie
current_role: Founder, Haichang Group / Haichang Ocean Park Holdings (HK: 2255); chairman and CEO as of March 2023 — current role unclear after Xiangyuan Holding became the largest shareholder
profile: Dalian entrepreneur who started in oil trading and marine shipping in 1992, set up Dalian Haichang Group in 1998, and from 1999 moved into ocean theme parks, building 11+ cultural-tourism projects across China (Dalian, Shanghai, Sanya, Zhengzhou etc.). Haichang Ocean Park listed in Hong Kong; a later share placement handed control (~38.6%) to Xiangyuan Holding.
interesting_fact: His fortune began in petrochemical trading and shipping in the early 1990s; property development then funded his theme parks, a model the company later moved away from in favour of 'asset-light' IP deals such as Ultraman-themed pavilions.
deep_cut_fact: In 2002 he led the construction of the Polar Aquarium at Dalian Laohutan Ocean Park, China's first polar aquarium, which became a national 5A attraction in 2007; in 2015 he received China's 'Feima Award' for outstanding contribution to tourism.
notes: Last on Hurun in 2019; Haichang has faced heavy debt and a control change, and press reports cite legal issues in France — handle with care. Alive status not verified by a recent source (aged 62 in the 2022 annual report). Weak fit for energy topic today (theme parks).

name: Wu Jialing
current_role: Unknown
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2009-2012 only) jointly with Wu Jie, whose wealth came from Fujian Yango (阳光) Group, parent of property developer Yango Group (阳光城, formerly 000671.SZ) with interests in real estate and power. Wu Jie is Yango Group's legal representative/controller; no public record found identifying Wu Jialing or her role.
notes: Could not identify this person beyond the Hurun co-listing with Wu Jie (presumably a relative). Yango's listed arm was moved to the delisting board in Oct 2023 after the property downturn, so outreach on this lead is not recommended. Recommend dropping.

name: Xu Ling
current_role: Actual controller of Geo-Jade Petroleum (洲际油气, Shanghai 600759) via Guangxi Zhenghe Industrial Group; also controls Sino-Science Netherlands Petroleum B.V. (中科荷兰石油)
profile: Xu Ling (许玲, also written HUI LING in filings) indirectly owns 100% of Guangxi Zhenghe Industrial Group, controlling shareholder of Shanghai-listed Geo-Jade Petroleum, an oil producer with upstream assets in Central Asia. She also indirectly holds 70.04% of Sino-Science Netherlands Petroleum ('Zhongke'), controlling holder of Sozak Oil & Gas LLP.
interesting_fact: Her 'Zhongke' vehicle, Sino-Science Netherlands Petroleum B.V., is the controlling shareholder of Sozak Oil & Gas LLP, in which Geo-Jade was set to hold an indirect 17.859% stake after a 2025 share-for-debt swap between her two companies.
notes: Identity match via Hurun's 'Zhongke' + oil exploitation/trading = Sino-Science Netherlands Petroleum, which Geo-Jade filings say she controls. Very private, no interviews found. Heads-up: Geo-Jade got an adverse internal-control audit opinion for 2025, was renamed 'ST Zhouji' from April 2026, and has had exchange inquiries about guarantees. Off Hurun since 2019.

name: Wu Mingting
current_role: Chairman (and founder/initiator), Ruiqi Holding Co. / KEN power tools (SZ ChiNext: 300126), Shanghai
profile: Born in 1966, Wu co-founded Shanghai-based Ken (Ruiqi) in 2000 to make professional-grade electric power tools for industry, shipbuilding, auto, aerospace and construction. He took it public on ChiNext and remains chairman (signing its April 2026 articles as chairman).
interesting_fact: KEN is one of the few Chinese brands positioned in high-end professional power tools, a field long dominated by Bosch, Makita and Hilti; the company offers 20+ product series and 100+ specifications for industrial and infrastructure users.
deep_cut_fact: A senior economist who studied at Shanghai Jiao Tong University and CEIBS's general-manager program, he has received the 'Shanghai Science & Technology Entrepreneur Innovation Award' and was named an 'Outstanding Chinese Private Science & Technology Entrepreneur'.
notes: Chairman role confirmed by company articles signed Apr 2026 (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202604221821456686_1.pdf). Hurun lists him in 'energy' focus but business is power tools - limited fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Bio details from a third-party brand site (CNPP).

name: Liu Dongliang
current_role: Director and controlling shareholder (~22.6%), Shanxi Yongdong Chemistry Industry (永东股份, SZSE: 002753)
profile: Founder (b. 1969) of Shanxi Yongdong, a Jishan County, Shanxi producer of carbon black and refined coal-tar products, which he grew from Jishan Yongdong Chemical Co. and took public in Shenzhen in 2015. He was GM and later chairman; his brother Liu Dongjie now chairs the company and Liu remains a director and, with Jin Caihong, actual controller.
interesting_fact: Yongdong runs an integrated coal-tar-to-carbon-black model: it refines coal tar into naphthalene, wash oil and other products, then blends the residue into feedstock oil for carbon black used in tyres.
deep_cut_fact: Outside chemicals, he has also served as general manager of a tea company, Wuzhishan Wuchuang Tea Co. (五指山五创茶业) in Hainan's Wuzhishan tea region.
notes: Input lists co-holder as 'Jing Caihong'; company filings spell it 靳彩红 (Jin Caihong), co-actual controller and director. Low media profile; only one Hurun appearance (2017). Route via securities office mailbox.

name: Jing Caihong
current_role: Co-actual controller and major shareholder, Shanxi Yongdong Chemistry Industry (SZSE: 002753), Jishan, Yuncheng, Shanxi
profile: Jing (Jin) Caihong (靳彩红) and her husband Liu Dongliang are the actual controllers of Shanxi Yongdong Chemistry, a coal-tar processor and carbon-black maker in Shanxi's Jishan county. She remains a top-10 shareholder per the 2025 annual report; the company has been squeezed by weak carbon-black prices.
interesting_fact: Yongdong runs a circular model: it distills coal tar into naphthalene and wash oil, turns the residue into carbon-black feedstock, and burns the carbon-black tail gas to generate power.
notes: Hurun romanises 靳 as 'Jing'; standard pinyin is Jin Caihong. Shared Hurun entry with husband Liu Dongliang. No executive role or public profile found; only route is the company securities office. Alive status inferred from her listing as a shareholder in the April 2026 annual report.

name: Sun Yang
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2019) under Zhongrong Xinda Group (coal/coking, Qingdao); exact role not verified
profile: Appears on the 2019 Hurun China Rich List (~$300m) under Zhongrong Xinda, a Qingdao-headquartered group (formerly Shandong Coking Group, founded 2003) with coking/coal, logistics (Shandong Logistics Group) and financial (Zhongrong Financial Holding) arms. No public biography linking a Sun Yang to the group was found; not the Olympic swimmer.
interesting_fact: Zhongrong Xinda began life as Shandong Coking Group before rebranding and expanding into logistics and financial holdings.
notes: Very common name; identity could not be confirmed against the company in English or Chinese searches. Verify via Hurun 2019 Chinese list and company registry (Qichacha) before outreach.

name: Hrishikesh A Mafatlal
current_role: Chairman and Promoter Director, Mafatlal Industries Ltd; Chairman and Promoter Director, NOCIL Ltd (Arvind Mafatlal Group)
profile: Hrishikesh A. Mafatlal, son of industrialist Arvind Mafatlal, heads the Arvind Mafatlal Group, whose holdings include Mafatlal Industries (textiles, founded 1913) and NOCIL (India's largest rubber-chemicals maker), and historically Navin Fluorine International. He chairs Mafatlal Industries and NOCIL, with his son Priyavrata as MD of Mafatlal Industries.
interesting_fact: He leads one of India's oldest business houses: Mafatlal Industries was incorporated in 1913 in Gujarat, and the group spans textiles, rubber chemicals (NOCIL) and, historically, fluorochemicals (Navin Fluorine).
deep_cut_fact: A 1975 commerce honours graduate of Mumbai's Sydenham College and a 1993 Harvard Business School AMP alumnus, he served 12 years on IIM Ahmedabad's Board of Governors and was vice-chairman of the Cotton Textiles Export Promotion Council (TEXPROCIL).
notes: Navin Fluorine is now chaired by cousin-branch member Vishad P. Mafatlal (Padmanabh Mafatlal Group); Hurun's link to Navin Fluorine reflects older group holdings. The best route is Mafatlal Industries' corporate contact (Mafatlal House, Mumbai). He is also on the board of BAIF (sustainable livelihoods), which could be an angle.

name: Marcos Marcelo Mindlin
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Pampa Energía (NYSE: PAM); co-founder of Grupo EMES; 2026 Chair of the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance
profile: Argentine economist who co-founded investment firm Grupo EMES in 1989 and was IRSA's vice-chairman and CFO (1990-2003). He founded Pampa Energía in 2005: a top Vaca Muerta shale producer, Argentina's largest independent power producer, and co-controller of Transener and TGS. In 2025 EMES took over Intercement/Loma Negra.
interesting_fact: In 2026 he was appointed Chairman of the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA), an intergovernmental body: an unusual role for a sitting energy CEO. He has received EY's CEO of the Year (2017) and the 2025 Apertura/PwC CEO Achievement Award.
deep_cut_fact: Since 2016 he has been president of the Holocaust Museum of Argentina (Buenos Aires), overseeing a US$7M full renovation of the building and exhibitions. His Pampa Energía Foundation has put about US$30M into education and employability over two decades.
notes: Gives long-form interviews to Argentine business press (e.g. El Cronista on Pampa's 20 years and the Loma Negra deal), so he is approachable on energy and Vaca Muerta topics. Best route is Pampa IR or corporate communications. 'Marcos Marcelo' is his formal SEC name; he goes by Marcelo Mindlin.

name: Ye Fang
current_role: Unconfirmed; listed by Hurun (2013-2020) against Landbridge Group (山东岚桥集团, Rizhao)
profile: Hurun listed a Ye Fang (叶芳) for Landbridge Group, the Rizhao-based petrochemicals, trading and ports group founded in 2001 by Ye Cheng (叶成), which holds the 99-year Port of Darwin lease. No filing or news source was found that states Ye Fang's role or her relationship to Ye Cheng.
notes: Chinese searches tried: 叶芳+岚桥集团, 叶芳+岚桥 董事/监事/股东, and bond-prospectus shareholder searches. English searches tried: Ye Fang Landbridge Hurun. Every 叶芳 found was an unrelated person (an AllBright lawyer, a Huaqiao Univ. professor). She may be a relative or co-owner of Ye Cheng, but this is unverified. A 2024 CSRC penalty notice (csrc.gov.cn) names Ye Cheng as actual controller and records Landbridge's missed bond disclosures. Low priority.

name: Zhao Zhaofeng
current_role: Early shareholder/member of founding team, Bitmain Technologies (current title not publicly disclosed)
profile: A low-profile member of Bitmain's early team. The September 2018 Hong Kong IPO filing showed him with 6.26% of the bitcoin-mining-chip maker, the third-largest individual stake after co-founders Micree Zhan (36%) and Jihan Wu (20.25%). That stake put him on the Hurun China list from 2018 to 2020. No public executive role or later stake has been disclosed.
interesting_fact: In Bitmain's 2018 HKEX application his 6.26% holding ranked third among individuals, ahead of fellow early team members Ge Yuesheng (葛越晟) and Hu Yishuo (胡一说), at 4.18% each.
notes: Identity confirmed via the 2018 Bitmain prospectus coverage (NBD/券商中国) and Blockmedia's Hurun report (https://www.blockmedia.co.kr/archives/49046). He has almost no web footprint in Chinese or English. MarketScreener's 'Zhao Feng Zhao' entry is probably him but is unsourced. No personal channels were found. The only route is Bitmain corporate.

name: Guo Yan
current_role: Unverified; listed by Hurun China (2017-2019) as associated with Zhongrong Xinda (中融信达), coal
profile: Listed on Hurun China Rich List 2017-2019 with wealth of about 2.9bn yuan from coal via 'Zhongrong Xinda'. Searches in Chinese and English found no reliable public source linking a Guo Yan (郭岩) to a coal company of that name, so identity and current role could not be confirmed.
notes: Common name; could not disambiguate. Company name may be a Hurun transliteration or a holding company. Would need Chinese corporate-registry checks (not done, per rules) or the original Hurun list entry to identify. Low priority.

name: Li Renchao
current_role: Former chairman and president of Huaxi Energy Industry Co. (华西能源, SZSE: 002630), Zigong, Sichuan; resigned May 2025
profile: Li Renchao (黎仁超), nicknamed the 'boiler king', built Zigong-based Huaxi Energy into a maker of power-station and waste-to-energy boilers and an EPC/energy investor. He chaired it from Nov 2007 and was also president from April 2024 until he stepped down in May 2025.
interesting_fact: Chinese media nicknamed him the 'boiler king' (锅炉大王) for building one of Sichuan's leading industrial-boiler groups, listed in Shenzhen in 2011.
notes: Not suitable for outreach: in May 2025 he resigned all Huaxi Energy posts, and the company disclosed a detention (liuzhi) and case-filing notice against him from a Suining district supervisory commission. No longer an active executive; current status unknown.

name: Lyu Rengao
current_role: Former founder and chairman of Zhejiang Julong Pipe Industry (巨龙管业, 002619.SZ); current role unknown
profile: Lyu Rengao (吕仁高, b. Nov 1961, from Dongyang, Zhejiang) built Jinhua-based Zhejiang Julong Pipe, a maker of large concrete water-transmission pipes (PCCP) for water-diversion projects, and listed it in Shenzhen in 2011 holding about 54%. The listed company later did a reverse takeover with game developer Aigelasi and was renamed (艾格拉斯). His current activities are not public.
interesting_fact: Julong Pipe's listed shell later became Aigelasi (艾格拉斯), a mobile-game company, through a reverse takeover: a concrete-pipe maker turned into a games stock.
deep_cut_fact: Julong began in January 1996 as a small private cement-products works Lyu set up in Bailongqiao, Jinhua county (later the Jinhua County Cement Pipe Factory). He spent nearly 30 years in cement products and won Jinhua's 'Golden Bull' outstanding entrepreneur award in 2010.
notes: 'Dragon Pipe Manufacturing' = 巨龙管业 (Julong = 'giant dragon'). He was on Hurun only 2015-2018. After the 002619 reverse takeover the listed company is unrelated to him (IR ir@egls.cn belongs to the games company, not him), so there is no current published contact. Status after about 2018 is unknown.

name: Xu Jianmin
current_role: Actual controller (~30.9%) of Xi'an Huaxin New Energy Co., Ltd. (西安华新新能源, ex-NEEQ 834368 '华新能源'), per exchange data; likely match
profile: Probable match: Xu Jianmin (许建民) is listed as actual/ultimate controller of Xi'an Huaxin New Energy, a Shaanxi firm doing engineering, EPC and energy-management contracts for industrial waste-heat/waste-pressure power plants and biomass power. It traded on China's NEEQ board (834368), consistent with Hurun's 2016-18 'HuaXin, new energy' entry; it has since been delisted.
interesting_fact: Xi'an Huaxin specialises in turning industrial waste heat (e.g. coke dry-quenching, ferroalloy and yellow-phosphorus furnaces) into electricity, and is a registered NDRC energy-service company.
notes: Tie to Hurun entry is inferred (name + 'Huaxin' new-energy company + NEEQ listing timing), not confirmed by a Hurun source. Chairman/legal rep is Wang Jihua, not Xu. Company delisted from NEEQ; 2019-21 broker/company notices cite court-enforcement (失信) issues for the company and Xu - treat outreach with caution. Chinese web search tools were weak; Baidu/cninfo unreachable.
