name: Sun Yanlong
current_role: Chairman, General Manager and actual controller, Hangzhou Arcvideo Technology (当虹科技, SSE STAR: 688039)
profile: Sun Yanlong (b. 1976) is a video-compression engineer who founded Hangzhou Arcvideo, a STAR Market-listed maker of AI-driven video encoding, ultra-HD (4K/8K) broadcast and streaming systems. He has been GM since 2013 and chairman since 2016, and controls the company through holding partnerships.
interesting_fact: For the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics, CCTV used Arcvideo's 8K AVS3 encoders to compress the 8K feed to a 120 Mb stream. Arcvideo also helped build the broadcaster's 8K ultra-HD IP distribution platform.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Arcvideo he was R&D director at InterVideo Inc. (maker of WinDVD) from 2002 to 2005, then vice president of ArcSoft (Hangzhou) from 2005 to 2012.
notes: Engineer-founder with a modest public profile; IR mailbox is the formal route. The deep-cut career history comes from a secondary profile site (maigoo), so confirm it against Arcvideo's prospectus if possible.

name: Li Yueling
current_role: Board secretary and CFO, Nanjing Develop Advanced Manufacturing (迪威尔, 688377.SS); co-actual controller with chairman Zhang Li
profile: Co-founder and co-controller, with chairman and GM Zhang Li, of Nanjing Develop Advanced Manufacturing. Founded in 2009 and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market, it forges and machines pressure-control parts for oil and gas wellheads, blowout preventers and subsea Christmas trees, sold mainly to large international oilfield-service companies. She serves as board secretary and heads the accounting function.
interesting_fact: Develop calls itself a pioneer in parts for deep-sea subsea Christmas trees and a 'one-stop shop' supplying everything from the forged material to finished assemblies, built to API standards for subsea conditions.
deep_cut_fact: She was one of the original founding investors in 2009, when the company was set up by Nanjing Develop Industrial, Li Yueling and Zhang Hong. It has since been building a multi-directional die-forging plant to make high-end valve and piping components.
notes: Hurun's 'Develop' is Nanjing Develop (迪威尔); Hurun's 'Zhang Li' is chairman Zhang Li (张利). The founding detail comes from the 10jqka company page (https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/688377/company.html) via search, and the plant detail from the 2024 interim report. As board secretary she personally handles the zqb@ IR mailbox, which makes it a reasonably direct route. Subsea oil-and-gas equipment angle.

name: Rajendra Vallabhaji Gogri
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman (from Oct 1, 2026; previously Chairman & MD), Aarti Industries Ltd. (NSE: AARTIIND)
profile: Rajendra Gogri is a founding member of Aarti Industries, the Mumbai-based benzene-chemistry specialty chemicals group incorporated in 1984 and started by his brother Chandrakant Gogri. He was managing director for about two decades and became chairman in 2012. In a planned succession he moved to non-executive chairman on Oct 1, 2026, with professional CEO Suyog Kotecha (ex-McKinsey) now running the company.
interesting_fact: In 2019 he won both ICC's Lala Shriram National Award and Hurun India's Most Respected Entrepreneur of the Year award.
deep_cut_fact: He was a rank holder in chemical engineering at UDCT Mumbai (now ICT), earned a master's in chemical engineering in the US, and received UDCT's Distinguished Alumnus Award in 1995, the same honour his brother Chandrakant received.
notes: He just moved to a non-executive role (Oct 2026) and may have more time for long-form conversations. Aarti also has a media kit page: https://www.aarti-industries.com/media-kit. Some aggregators say his US master's is from Iowa State; the company site says only 'USA'.

name: Mark S Comora
current_role: Chairman of the Board, OPAL Fuels (Nasdaq: OPAL); Founder and President, Fortistar LLC
profile: CPA with a Columbia MBA who founded Fortistar, a White Plains investment firm, in 1993. He led its growth in decarbonising power, transport fuels and industry. Fortistar controls OPAL Fuels, a renewable-natural-gas producer listed via SPAC in 2022, and he has chaired OPAL since 2020. He is 84 per the 2026 proxy.
interesting_fact: He has long been in independent power. He sat on the board of the Independent Power Producers of New York and the Equipment Leasing Association. Fortistar's portfolio has run from power plants to landfill-gas and dairy RNG.
deep_cut_fact: Outside energy, he is an officer and board member of the American Museum of Fly Fishing in Manchester, Vermont.
notes: Good fit for the energy angle (RNG, independent power). The general Fortistar inbox is the most direct published route. The OPAL IR contact appears in older press releases. OPAL's media contact is handled by ICR.

name: Hu Shiyong
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with brothers Hu Shiqing and Hu Shifa) of Jiangsu Huahong Industrial Group / Huahong Technology (SZSE: 002645); chairman of Huahong Technology 2008-2023, director until May 2026
profile: Jiangyin, Jiangsu industrialist (b. 1949) who built Huahong Group from a Zhouzhuang village enterprise into a chemical-fibre, plastics and copper group, and listed Huahong Technology (scrap-metal recycling equipment, resource and rare-earth recycling). He chaired it 2008-2023; on Hurun China lists 2008-2012.
interesting_fact: Huahong Group grew out of Mengxiang village in Zhouzhuang town, Jiangyin - the village was later renamed 'Huahong Village' after the company he led as village party secretary from 1992.
deep_cut_fact: With only a junior-high education, he spent 1969-72 in Guizhou working on the 'Third Front' industrial construction drive, then ran the Zhouzhuang sheet-metal welding works as factory director before founding the group.
notes: Elderly (77), stepped off the listed company's board in May 2026 (per lixinger); no personal media presence. IR mailbox is the listed company's securities office. Weak fit for data-center focus; recycling/metals angle instead.

name: Graham Peacock
current_role: Owner, TG Convenience Stores (UK forecourt/convenience operator)
profile: British forecourt entrepreneur who cofounded MRH (GB) in 1997 and built it into the UK's largest independent fuel retailer (~450 sites plus a fuel-distribution arm), selling to Lone Star Funds in 2016 after a 2008 Barclays PE stake sale. He remains in the sector via TG Convenience Stores.
interesting_fact: The 2016 sale of MRH to US private-equity firm Lone Star Funds was reported as a roughly £2bn forecourt deal, putting him among the UK's super-rich.
deep_cut_fact: MRH was born in 1997 when Peacock and several colleagues set up on their own after their employer, forecourt operator Oakstead, buckled under the 'Esso Pricewatch' price war.
notes: Low public profile, covered mainly by trade press (Forecourt Trader, The Grocer), which has given him a lifetime-achievement award. No published personal or company contact found. Forecourt Trader returns 405 to scripted fetches, so award details are unverified.

name: Meeta Dhingra
current_role: Berger Paints promoter-family member (no executive role found)
profile: Meeta Dhingra is the wife of Kuldip Singh Dhingra, who with his brother Gurbachan bought Berger Paints India from Vijay Mallya's UB Group in 1991 and built it into India's second-largest paint maker. She appeared on Hurun India 2018-2019 as part of the Dhingra promoter holdings; no public business role for her was found.
interesting_fact: The Dhingra brothers acquired Berger Paints India in 1991 from the UB Group; it is now India's No. 2 paint company, chaired by Kuldip's daughter Rishma Kaur.
notes: Very private; identified only as Kuldip Singh Dhingra's wife (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuldip_Singh_Dhingra). IR email belongs to Berger's company secretary (Arunito Ganguly) and is for shareholder matters, so it is a weak route. Paint/chemicals, so a loose fit for an energy podcast.

name: Konstantin Grigorishin
current_role: Head/majority investor, Energy Standard Group; founder and president, International Swimming League (ISL)
profile: Zaporizhzhia-born (1965) theoretical physicist (MIPT, PhD 1991) who made money in 1990s metals trading, then bought Ukrainian machine-building, river-shipping (Ukrrichflot) and regional power-distribution (oblenergo) assets via Energy Standard Group (est. 2005). Best known internationally for bankrolling the professional International Swimming League; currently outside Ukraine.
interesting_fact: He founded and funded the International Swimming League (~$20m first-season budget), a team-based pro swimming circuit, and in January 2026 the ISL won a US jury verdict in its antitrust case against World Aquatics (damages: $1).
deep_cut_fact: A master-class swimmer himself, he trained in Landau's theoretical-physics group at MIPT and defended a 1991 PhD on 'light propagation in nonlinear disordered media'; his first company (1992) was an IT firm called AragornSoft.
notes: HIGH RISK: Ukraine sanctioned/blocked his assets (Jan 2025 presidential decree) and as of May 2026 is reportedly seeking an international arrest warrant; Russia also issued an in-absentia warrant (2016, tax case) and sanctioned him in 2018. Net worth figure is dated. No published contact found; journalist should weigh suitability carefully.

name: Susan Tobbell
current_role: Co-founder, SGN Retail (Essex forecourt operator; sale of 100% to Essar's EET Retail agreed Sept 2026); director, TG Convenience Stores and Starbridge Property Investment
profile: Susan Margaret Tobbell is a UK fuel-retail entrepreneur. After serving as a director of forecourt group MRH (GB) in 2011-2016, she co-founded SGN Retail with Graham Peacock in 2016 and grew it to 118 petrol stations. In Sept 2026 Essar's EET Retail agreed to buy all of SGN, reportedly for about £400M, to create a 235-site refinery-to-pump network.
interesting_fact: SGN Retail reached 118 sites in a decade in a UK market where total forecourt numbers have been falling for fifty years; Essar is buying it to send Stanlow-refined fuel straight to its own pumps.
deep_cut_fact: Before SGN she was a director of MRH (GB), the forecourt operator later bought by Lone Star (2016) and Motor Fuel Group (2018, £1.2B); she has also been a significant shareholder (about 7%) in AIM-listed bus operator Rotala.
notes: Very private; not quoted in the 2026 deal announcement and no interviews, website or social accounts found. Sunday Times Rich List 2020 entry for fuel distribution. Approach via SGN Retail/EET Retail press channels if needed.

name: Nikolaos Tsakos
current_role: Founder, President and CEO, TEN Ltd (Tsakos Energy Navigation, NYSE: TEN)
profile: Born 1963 in Athens into a Chios shipping family, Nikolas Tsakos (Columbia BA, London MA in shipping finance) founded Tsakos Energy Navigation, listed in Oslo in 1993 and on the NYSE since 2002, the longest-established listed Greek shipping company. TEN runs a fleet of crude and product tankers, LNG carriers and shuttle tankers chartered to oil majors and refiners.
interesting_fact: He chaired INTERTANKO, the global independent tanker owners' association, from 2014 to 2018, and was Lloyd's List Greek Shipping Newsmaker of the Year in 2015.
deep_cut_fact: He has spent a total of two years at sea and served as an officer in the Hellenic Navy in 1988; in 2026 he was named Grand Marshal of the Greek diaspora parade in New York.

public_contacts.value: Capital Link, Inc. (Nicolas Bornozis / Markella Kara), ten@capitallink.com

notes: Usually spelled Nikolas P. Tsakos. Media-friendly and a frequent speaker at shipping conferences (Capital Link forums). Capital Link handles TEN's IR/media; COO George Saroglou is the company's named press-release contact. Energy-shipping (oil, LNG) angle.

name: Ni Yunda
current_role: Founder/president of Jiangsu Shunda Group (Yangzhou polysilicon, ingot and wafer maker); current role not verified
profile: Ni Yunda (倪云达) built Yangzhou-based Jiangsu Shunda Group into one of China's larger early solar raw-material suppliers, producing polysilicon (~1,500 t/yr by 2009), monocrystalline ingots and wafers. Shunda drew $82m led by Actis in 2006-07; Suntech bought into Shunda Holdings in 2008 with a 13-year ~7GW wafer supply deal. He was on Hurun lists 2007-2010.
interesting_fact: In 2008 Suntech paid ~$99m for a stake in Shunda Holdings and signed a 13-year wafer supply contract totalling roughly 7GW, one of the largest PV supply deals of that era.
deep_cut_fact: In April 2009 Ni ('Mr. Yunda Ni, President of Jiangsu Shunda') became chairman of Shunda-SolarE Technologies, a US joint venture with Menlo Park-based Solar EnerTech aimed at the US solar market; he said the goal was to 'build market share in the U.S.'
notes: Identity confirmed via SEC filing (Solar EnerTech 8-K, 2009). No current information found on Ni or Shunda after ~2012 polysilicon downturn; no published contacts. Low public profile.

name: Yang Rongchun
current_role: Co-founder and former vice-president of Hengan Group (Hengan International, HKEX 1044); no current executive role found
profile: Yang Rongchun (杨荣春, b. ~1950), an engineer from Anhai, Jinjiang (Fujian), co-founded Hengan in 1985 with Sze Man Bok, Hui Lin Chit and Hung Ching Shan, pooling RMB1.36m to start one of China's first sanitary-napkin makers. Hengan grew into China's leading tissue and hygiene group (HK-listed 1998). He later served as Hengan Group VP and a director of Shanghai Jahwa.
interesting_fact: Hengan's 1998 Hong Kong IPO set that year's records for the highest P/E and the highest subscription multiple on the HK exchange.
deep_cut_fact: Hengan's origin story starts with him: in Nov 1984, as a technician at the Anhai General Machinery Factory, Yang showed Hui Lin Chit a Taiwanese sanitary-napkin machine manual, said to promise payback within three months of production - which led to Hengan's founding.
notes: Low-profile co-founder; a 2018 Jiemian piece says only Sze Man Bok and Hui Lin Chit remain in management, so Yang appears retired from executive roles. Email is Hengan Group's general website mailbox (footer), not a personal route. Sina Finance lists him as engineer, b. 1950, ex-director of Shanghai Jahwa (600315).

name: Dmytro Lider
current_role: Co-founder, Grammarly (now part of Superhuman Platform Inc.); current operating role not confirmed
profile: Ukrainian software entrepreneur who co-founded Grammarly in 2009 with Max Lytvyn and Alex Shevchenko. The writing assistant, built largely in Kyiv, reached a $13B valuation in 2021; in 2024-25 Grammarly bought Coda and the Superhuman email app and rebranded its parent company as Superhuman.
interesting_fact: Grammarly started as a subscription grammar checker for students and grew into an AI writing assistant used as a browser extension and Google Docs add-on; the company keeps a major engineering office in Kyiv.
notes: Least public of the three Grammarly co-founders; no own website or verified social accounts found. Web search budget ran out before checking his current role or a Superhuman press contact. Alive status assumed, no reports otherwise.

name: Sherif Foda
current_role: Chairman and CEO, National Energy Services Reunited Corp. (NESR, Nasdaq), Houston
profile: Egyptian-born oilfield-services executive who spent ~25 years at Schlumberger (SLB), rising to President of the Production Group and senior advisor to the chairman. In 2017 he started NESR as a SPAC, rolling up MENA oilfield-service firms into the region's largest Nasdaq-listed energy services company; NESR recently signed with Aramco on the region's first direct lithium extraction project.
interesting_fact: He built NESR from a blank-check company in 2017 into what it calls the first and largest MENA-region energy services company listed on Nasdaq.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil, he spent two years in the IT and computer industry after earning a double major in electronics engineering and automatic control at Ain Shams University in Cairo; he then joined Schlumberger in 1993 working offshore fields in the Red Sea.
notes: Frequent conference speaker and member of the Oxford Energy Policy Club, so likely receptive to podcast invitations; also chairs WDVG Engineering and GLC Energy. Route via NESR IR or info@nesr.com.

name: Carl Ledbetter
current_role: Independent director, Cloudflare (since Nov 2009; chair of compensation committee); Chairman, CEO and CTO of SimpleRose, Inc.
profile: Dr. Carl Ledbetter (76) is a mathematician-turned-tech executive and VC. As a Managing Director of Pelion Venture Partners (2003-2018) he joined Cloudflare's board in November 2009, and his long-held stake is the source of his SEC-listed wealth. He has sat on four other public-company boards and 30+ private boards, and since 2018-19 leads SimpleRose, an optimization/mathematical-programming software company.
interesting_fact: He has been on Cloudflare's board since November 2009, one of its longest-serving directors, and is designated an 'audit committee financial expert'.
deep_cut_fact: He is a career mathematician: B.S. in Mathematics from the University of Redlands, M.S. from Brandeis and a Ph.D. in Mathematics from Clark University. Fittingly, his current company SimpleRose sells optimization software for supply-chain, scheduling and even sports scheduling.
notes: Low public profile; best routes are via SimpleRose (his own company, website contact page) or Cloudflare's press office (company-level). Wealth figure is from SEC insider holdings of Cloudflare stock.

name: Jyotsna Ramesh Shah
current_role: Promoter-family shareholder of Fine Organic Industries Ltd (Mumbai; NSE/BSE: FINEORG), per Hurun India 2018-2019; no executive role found
profile: Hurun India (2018-2019) listed Jyotsna Ramesh Shah (Mumbai) with INR 1,300-2,100 crore from Fine Organic Industries, the oleochemical-additives maker founded in 1970 by Mumbai chemical trader Ramesh Shah and ICT-trained technocrat Prakash Kamat. Her name suggests she belongs to Ramesh Shah's family, but her exact relationship and current holding could not be verified.
interesting_fact: Fine Organics pioneered plant-derived oleochemical additives (for plastics, food, cosmetics, etc.) in India and now sells to customers in over 110 countries.
notes: Private individual with no public profile; only on Hurun India 2018-19. Contacts are the company's, not hers. Weak fit for an energy podcast (specialty chemicals). Web-search quota ran out before her family role could be confirmed; company's public face is CMD Mukesh Shah.

name: Ramprakash V Bubna
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Sharda Cropchem Ltd (NSE/BSE listed, Mumbai)
profile: IIT Bombay-trained chemical engineer who founded Sharda International in 1987, growing it into Sharda Cropchem, a global generic agrochemicals company. Its asset-light model centres on preparing dossiers and winning product registrations in high-barrier markets (Europe, US, LATAM), then selling formulations via distributors and its own sales forces.
interesting_fact: Sharda Cropchem does not need to own big factories: its core competence is regulatory, compiling registration dossiers for off-patent fungicides, herbicides and insecticides and sourcing from a global supplier network; it also sells conveyor belts and V-belts.
deep_cut_fact: The business began as two sole proprietorships, Sharda International (1987) and Bubna Enterprises (1989), exporting dyes, dye intermediates, pesticides and V-belts, before being rolled into Sharda Worldwide Exports in 2004 and renamed Sharda Cropchem in 2013 ahead of its IPO.
notes: Agrochemicals, not energy, so a weak fit for the podcast theme. Company secretary Jetkin Gudhka handles investor contact. Low media profile; no personal accounts found.

name: Song Dianquan
current_role: Founder & chairman, Coslight Technology International Group (光宇国际; ex-HKEX 1043) / Harbin Coslight group (batteries, power supplies)
profile: Song Dianquan (宋殿权), an electrochemical engineer from Harbin Institute of Technology, founded the Coslight battery group in Harbin in 1994 (with Li Kexue), making lead-acid and lithium rechargeable batteries and power-supply products for telecom, power and EV markets. Coslight Technology listed in Hong Kong and he chaired it through its 2022 delisting; he was on Hurun lists 2001-2010.
interesting_fact: Song signed Coslight's HKEX filings as chairman for more than two decades, from its early-2000s annual reports through the last 2022 filings before the shares were delisted.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from Harbin Institute of Technology in 1982 with a bachelor's in electrochemical engineering, and by 2004 had 20+ years in rechargeable-battery R&D - an engineer-founder rather than a trader.
notes: Coslight Technology's HK listing was cancelled 4 Apr 2022 under Rule 6.01A after a long suspension (2021 HKEX censure of company and directors also on record) - be tactful. coslight.com currently a parked page; no published IR/press email found. Route would be via Harbin Coslight Group.

name: Randall S. Wade
current_role: President, EIG (EIG Global Energy Partners, Washington DC); was an EIG-affiliated director of Diversified Energy (NYSE/LSE: DEC) per SEC filings Dec 2025-Jan 2026
profile: Randall 'Randy' Wade is President of EIG, a ~40-year-old institutional investor focused on energy and infrastructure credit and equity, and has been on its team since 1996. He joined Diversified Energy's board as a director tied to EIG funds that received DEC shares when Diversified bought EIG-backed Maverick Natural Resources in 2025. The ~$250M figure reflects EIG fund holdings he reported, not personal wealth.
interesting_fact: In Oct 2026 EIG and Saudi power developer Acwa announced Plenum Power, a partnership targeting ~$4B of initial equity to invest in US power infrastructure, squarely aimed at AI/data-center-driven demand.
deep_cut_fact: He is one of EIG's longest-serving leaders: EIG says he has been a member of the team since 1996, two years before CEO R. Blair Thomas joined in 1998.

public_contacts.value: FGS Global (Kelly Kimberly / Brandon Messina), EIG@fgsglobal.com

notes: Wealth figure is misleading: the SEC 'holdings' are ~7.5M DEC shares held by EIG funds (indirect). He no longer appears on Diversified's current board page (Nov 2026), so the seat may have ended. Strong energy-finance/AI power-demand guest; route via EIG's PR firm FGS Global.

name: Vincent D Foster
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Main Street Capital Corp (NYSE: MAIN), Houston; founding director of Quanta Services 1998-2025
profile: Vince Foster, a CPA and former Arthur Andersen partner who ran its Southwest corporate-finance/M&A practice, co-founded the Main Street predecessor funds in 1997; they co-founded Quanta Services, now the leading builder of grid and power infrastructure. He was Main Street's CEO 2007-2018 and has chaired its board since 2007, after 27 years on Quanta's board.
interesting_fact: Main Street's predecessor funds co-founded Quanta Services (NYSE: PWR), the specialty contractor that has become a key builder of transmission lines and power infrastructure for the AI data-center boom; Foster sat on its board from its 1998 IPO until 2025.
deep_cut_fact: At Arthur Andersen he specialised in 'roll-ups' - companies consolidating fragmented industries - the playbook behind Quanta; he was a founding director of the Texas TriCities chapter of the National Association of Corporate Directors and won EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2008 (Houston, financial services). He holds a JD from Wayne State.
notes: Main Street publishes his direct work email on its board page - the best route. Strong podcast angle: the origin story of Quanta Services, now central to US grid and data-center power build-out. Michigan State BBA.

name: Michael E. Hurlston
current_role: President & CEO and director, Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ: LITE); board member of Flex Ltd. and Astera Labs
profile: Michael Hurlston (59) is a semiconductor/optics executive who became CEO of Lumentum - a key supplier of lasers and optical transceivers for AI data-center interconnect - in February 2025. He was previously CEO of Synaptics (2019-25) and Finisar (2018-19), after 16 years at Broadcom running its wireless connectivity division and later worldwide sales. He also sits on the boards of Flex and AI-connectivity chipmaker Astera Labs.
interesting_fact: He has now run three public tech companies; at Finisar he led the agreed sale to II-VI (now Coherent) - Lumentum's chief optical rival - before moving to Synaptics and then Lumentum.
deep_cut_fact: He is a triple UC Davis Aggie - BS and MS in electrical engineering plus an MBA - and spent the 1990s in marketing and engineering roles at small chip firms including Exar, MicroPower Systems, IC Works, Avasem and Oren Semiconductor before joining Broadcom in 2001.
notes: Highly relevant to the data-center/AI optics theme; regularly speaks on earnings calls and at investor conferences. SEC insider wealth ~US$248M. Best route is Lumentum IR/communications.

name: Jack M Huynh
current_role: Senior Vice President and General Manager, Computing and Graphics Group, AMD
profile: AMD lifer who joined in 1998 and now runs the Computing and Graphics Group (PC, Radeon graphics and semi-custom businesses), responsible for strategy, business and engineering for CPUs, GPUs and NPUs in end-user devices. He previously led AMD's semi-custom group as SVP/GM and was CVP/GM of the mobile business unit. Wealth (~$240M) is from AMD equity per SEC insider filings.

interesting_fact: Acteon grew by acquisition into a group of specialist subsea businesses (moorings, cables, survey, decommissioning) serving both oil and gas and offshore wind; in 2024 it was acquired by Buckthorne and One Equity Partners.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the business in 1989, when it was still UWG Group, and led it for three decades through its 2004 rebranding as Acteon and its shift to a subsea focus.
notes: The Sunday Times 2020 entry only says 'oil and gas services'; the link to Acteon is my inference (no other UK oil-services Richard Higham found), so verify before outreach. The UWG/1989 detail rests on secondary profiles. No published personal contact found; route via Acteon.

name: Daniel S Shugar
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Nextpower Inc. (Nasdaq: NXT; formerly Nextracker)
profile: Solar pioneer who co-founded PowerLight (sold to SunPower for $332M in 2007; he became SunPower president), then co-founded Nextracker in 2013 as its CEO. It became the top utility-scale solar tracker maker, IPO'd in 2023 and rebranded as Nextpower in 2025, adding power conversion and battery storage.
interesting_fact: Under Shugar the company had shipped trackers for 100+ GW of solar capacity in 40 countries by 2024, and in Dec 2024 shipped the first US-made solar trackers with 100% domestic content after reshoring manufacturing.
deep_cut_fact: An RPI electrical-engineering grad from New Jersey, he started in the late 1980s in PG&E's R&D department; in 2023 the American Solar Energy Society gave him its Hoyt Clarke Hottel Award, and S&P Global Platts named him Chief Trailblazer of the Year.
notes: Very media-friendly CEO and frequent conference speaker; excellent fit for an energy podcast. Pitch via media@nextpower.com (global media contact Brandy Lee).

name: Mark Allen McFarland
current_role: President and CEO, Talen Energy Corp. (NASDAQ: TLN) since May 2023; Director, California Resources Corp.
profile: Known as 'Mac', a veteran power-industry executive who has run Luminant (2013-16), GenOn Energy (2017-18) and California Resources Corp. (2020-23) before taking over Talen Energy. At Talen he pivoted the independent power producer toward data centers, selling the Cumulus campus beside the Susquehanna nuclear plant to AWS and signing a large nuclear power deal with Amazon.
interesting_fact: In March 2024 Talen sold its 960 MW Cumulus data-center campus next to the Susquehanna nuclear station to AWS for $650m - one of the first big nuclear-to-data-center co-location deals; McFarland argued 'around-the-clock nuclear power matches very well with around-the-clock data center power needs.'
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer: a B.S. in Civil Engineering with an environmental concentration from Virginia Tech (plus an MBA from the University of Delaware), and spent 1999-2008 at Exelon, rising to SVP of Corporate Development.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast (nuclear + hyperscaler deals). Media contact is Talen's Director of Corporate Communications as listed in 2026 press releases.

name: Gary Dutton
current_role: Retired founder of Synseal Extrusions (UK PVC-U window, door and conservatory-roof systems); no current executive role found
profile: Gary Dutton MBE founded Synseal in 1980 and built it into a leading UK maker of conservatory roof kits and PVC-U window/door profiles, run from a 34-acre site in Sutton-in-Ashfield, Nottinghamshire, with 500+ staff. He exited in 2010 when H.I.G. Europe backed a management buyout, retiring after a two-year wind-down 'to pursue his hobbies'.
interesting_fact: Synseal's turnover reached £76.3M in the year to March 2009, shortly before its private-equity sale.
deep_cut_fact: As Synseal chairman he was ranked Britain's 23rd best entrepreneur by Management Today, on the strength of 200% turnover growth in five years to £66M.
notes: Private retired individual; no published contact found. Weak fit for energy/data-center focus (window/insulation products only). Last rich-list appearance was 2020; no recent public information.

name: Nandlal Valecha
current_role: Co-founder of Regent Group / Regent Gas (London commercial gas supplier); stepped down from all group directorships in June 2019
profile: Nandlal Mulchand Valecha (b. 1938), a British Indian entrepreneur, co-founded Regent Gas in 1995 with his son Deep Valecha; the Acton-based group supplies natural gas, connections and metering to businesses across Great Britain and has expanded into water and power. He resigned his Regent directorships in 2019; Deep now runs the group as CEO.
interesting_fact: In 2024 the Valecha-owned Regent Group agreed to take private TClarke - the 1889-founded building-services firm that once wired Windsor Castle and lit up the Shard - for £90.56m, after building a ~21.5% stake from 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Regent Gas Ltd was incorporated in October 1995; Companies House shows Nandlal Valecha appointed a director in January 1996 and serving for more than 23 years until June 2019.
notes: Shared fortune with son Deep Valecha (Sunday Times Rich List 2020). Nandlal is ~88 and no longer active; status since 2019 not publicly confirmed. Deep Valecha (CEO, Regent; director of TClarke) is the realistic interview target. Email is Regent Gas's general company inbox.

name: Deep Valecha
current_role: Owner of Regent Group (Regent Gas); director, Regent Gas Ltd and Regent Acquisitions Ltd; non-executive director of TClarke plc since June 2024
profile: UK businessman behind Regent Gas, a family-owned supplier of gas and metering services to industrial and commercial customers, set up in 1995 (with family incl. Nandlal Valecha) and trading as a licensed supplier since 1996. After building a ~21.5% stake from 2018, Regent bought London building-services/electrical contractor TClarke for ~£90m in 2024, taking it private.
interesting_fact: Regent's 2024 takeover of TClarke — an electrical and building-services contractor founded in 1889 that works on data centres and large commercial buildings — moved a gas-supply family business into construction services.
deep_cut_fact: Regent Gas started trading as a licensed gas supplier in April 1996, an early independent entrant in the newly liberalised UK gas market, and remains privately owned.
notes: Private; no personal or press contacts published (Regent Gas website unreachable from this session). Route via TClarke corporate office or Regent Gas. TClarke angle (data-centre electrical contracting) is a good podcast hook.

name: Brian Long
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Partner, Atlantic Bridge (growth-equity tech investor, Dublin/London/Palo Alto); director of Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS) since ~2015
profile: Irish engineer-entrepreneur (Trinity College Dublin, BA/MSc in electronic engineering and semiconductor microelectronics) who founded chip-IP firm Parthus in 1993 and ran it until 2003, taking it public on Nasdaq and London. In 2004 he co-founded Atlantic Bridge, now managing over EUR 1bn across eight funds, which backed GaN/SiC power-chip maker Navitas from early on.
interesting_fact: Navitas, the GaN/SiC power-chip company whose board he sits on, is supplying devices for NVIDIA's 800 VDC power architecture for next-generation AI-factory data centres; Atlantic Bridge's fund fully exited its Navitas stake in Dec 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before VC, he built Dublin's Parthus Technologies (founded 1993), a chip-IP licensor for mobile/Bluetooth/GPS that floated on Nasdaq and the LSE in 2000 and became today's CEVA after merging with DSP Group's Ceva unit.

public_contacts.value: https://www.abven.com (Atlantic Bridge; contact page lists offices)

notes: Investor rather than operator - good guest on European deep-tech / power-semis for AI. Navitas board status in late 2026 not re-verified after Atlantic Bridge's exit. Common name: confirm via Atlantic Bridge. Parthus->CEVA merger detail is from general knowledge plus Navitas bio (which says 'Parthus-CEVA').

name: Charles Alvin Meloy
current_role: Director, Diamondback Energy (Nasdaq: FANG) since September 2024; retired President & CEO, Endeavor Energy Resources
profile: Charles A. 'Chuck' Meloy (65) is a Permian Basin veteran. He ran Kerr-McGee's exploration and production as a VP, was EVP of US Onshore E&P at Anadarko until 2015, and was President & CEO of Endeavor Energy Resources from 2016 to 2020. After Diamondback's 2024 merger with Endeavor he joined Diamondback's board as one of four directors designated by Endeavor's Stephens family stockholders.
interesting_fact: He is one of four Diamondback directors whom the Stephens family stockholders, legacy owners of Endeavor, have the right to designate under the 2024 Endeavor-Diamondback merger, which created one of the largest Permian Basin producers.
deep_cut_fact: He is an engineer by training: a 1982 Texas A&M chemical-engineering graduate and member of the Society of Petroleum Engineers and Texas Professional Engineers. He was also on the API Upstream Committee and the boards of Western Gas Equity Partners and the Independent Producers of America Association.
notes: Retired executive, now a board member; no personal public channels found. Diamondback's own IR pages block automated access. Its quarterly press releases list an investor-relations contact, so check the latest release for the current address. Route via Diamondback IR (Midland, TX).

name: Marshall S McCrea Iii
current_role: Co-CEO and director, Energy Transfer LP (NYSE: ET); retiring as co-CEO at end of 2026, remaining on the board (Tom Long becomes sole CEO)
profile: Known as Mackie McCrea, he has spent ~30 years at Energy Transfer, joining its predecessor in 1997 as SVP of business development and producer services, then serving as president of ETP (2008), group COO/chief commercial officer (2015-18), president and CCO (2018-20) and co-CEO since Jan 2021. He has led ET's commercial push into supplying gas to AI data centers (e.g. CloudBurst in Texas).
interesting_fact: On AI-driven gas demand he said: 'The data centers - especially around AI - it's going to happen... We're believers like everybody else,' and after the CloudBurst deal noted that tech companies 'are in a hurry.'
deep_cut_fact: He joined Energy Transfer's predecessor in 1997 - when it was a small Texas gas gatherer - and has served on the partnership's board since December 2009, making him one of the longest-tenured executives in its rise to a top US midstream company.
notes: Goes by 'Mackie'. Retirement as co-CEO announced June 2026 (8-K), effective ~Dec 31 2026 - post-retirement he may be freer for a podcast. Energy Transfer media relations is by phone (Vicki Granado, 214-840-5820) per 2026 press releases; no current published email confirmed. Strong data-center/gas angle.

name: N Jagan Mohan Reddy
current_role: Vice Chairman, Rain Industries Ltd (Hyderabad; NSE: RAIN) and CEO of Rain Carbon Inc.
profile: Hyderabad industrialist (Jagan Mohan Reddy Nellore - not the Andhra politician Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy) who built Rain from an Indian calcined-petroleum-coke maker into Rain Carbon, a global producer of calcined pet coke, coal-tar pitch and advanced carbon materials for aluminium smelting, batteries and chemicals, via acquisitions of US-based CII Carbon (2007) and Germany's RÜTGERS (2013).
interesting_fact: Rain is one of the world's largest producers of calcined petroleum coke and coal-tar pitch, two key inputs for aluminium smelter anodes; he addresses shareholders as Vice Chairman at its AGMs.
deep_cut_fact: A Purdue University industrial-engineering graduate, he was founder-MD of Rain Calcining, which began producing calcined petroleum coke in Visakhapatnam in 1998, before leading its globalisation through the CII Carbon buyout (renamed Rain CII Carbon).
notes: Name collision risk with Andhra Pradesh politician Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy - always use 'Jagan Mohan Reddy Nellore / Rain Carbon'. Purdue degree field comes from Crunchbase (secondary); confirm before quoting. Only published company channel is the company secretary mailbox.

name: Sailesh Chimanlal Mehta
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals Corp. (DFPCL), Pune; chairman, Fertiliser Association of India (elected 2025)
profile: Sailesh C. Mehta, son of founder C.K. Mehta, has run Deepak Fertilisers since the 2010s (chairman since 2012/13), steering it from commodity fertilisers and chemicals toward ammonia self-sufficiency (a new greenfield ammonia plant), technical ammonium nitrate for mining, and branded crop nutrition. He was elected chairman of the Fertiliser Association of India in June 2025.
interesting_fact: He was a winner in the Natural Resources category of the 2024 BT-PwC India's Best CEOs ranking, credited with a strategy shift 'from customer to consumer' and backward integration into ammonia instead of relying on Middle East imports.
deep_cut_fact: Explaining DFPCL's move into branded crop nutrition, Mehta cited the insight that a 1% rise in sugarcane sucrose content is worth about Rs 35 crore to a sugar mill: 'If people see value, they will not speak about the price.'
notes: Accessible, media-friendly CEO (Zee Business, Outlook Business, Business Today interviews). Best route: Anuradha Bose, EVP Group Branding & Corporate Communications, listed as media contact in the Q1 FY27 results (July 2026); CFO Subhash Anand is the IR contact. His father C.K. Mehta (P11922) died in July 2023.

name: Jigish Shailesh Choksi
current_role: Managing Director, ELF Trading & Chemicals Manufacturing Ltd; Asian Paints promoter-group member (non-executive director of Asian Paints 2019-2025)
profile: Member of the Choksi family, one of the four founding promoter families of Asian Paints (est. 1942), India's largest paint maker; his wealth stems mainly from that inherited stake. He runs agro-chemical trader ELF Trading & Chemicals, works in the family's Navbharat Packaging corrugated-box business, and oversees a family office investing in equities, debt and startups.
interesting_fact: Despite being a promoter heir, he started at Asian Paints in 2010 as a regular sales hire and served on the company's board from April 2019 until 2025.
deep_cut_fact: An RIT (Rochester Institute of Technology) business grad, he spent three years as an Area Manager in project sales at Asian Paints, then moved to marketing, where he was in charge of several product launches in the waterproofing range; his board profile also calls him a sports enthusiast.
notes: Low-profile heir; no personal channels found. Asian Paints IR email is a weak route since he left the board in 2025 (email appears in the filing footer, OCR-garbled as 'mvestor.relations'). Industry tag in input (petrochemicals) is loose; paints/chemicals.

name: Varun A Vakil
current_role: Chairman and Non-Executive Director, Elcid Investments Ltd; Assistant General Manager - Supply Chain New Products, Asian Paints Ltd (promoter group)
profile: Varun Amar Vakil is a member of the Vakil family, one of the four founding promoter families of Asian Paints, and is in its promoter group. He chairs Elcid Investments, a Vakil-family holding company whose main asset is an Asian Paints stake, and works in Asian Paints' supply-chain function for new products.
interesting_fact: Elcid Investments, which he chairs, became India's most expensive stock overnight in October 2024: a special price-discovery auction re-rated it from about Rs 3.53 to roughly Rs 2.36 lakh per share, reflecting the value of its Asian Paints stake.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a BBA from Michigan State University and an MBA in entrepreneurship and global marketing from Babson's F.W. Olin Graduate School. He began with an internship at Asian Paints, then worked at Piramal Glass before rejoining Asian Paints in supply chain.
notes: vakilgroup@gmail.com and the Worli office are Elcid Investments' published company contact (also the Vakil group office). He is a working manager rather than a public-facing founder, so keep the outreach low-key. His link to energy/chemicals is weak (paints). His father Amar Vakil, a former Asian Paints promoter director, died in 2021/22.

name: Shyam Sunder Jindal
current_role: Promoter and head (described in group materials as chairman) of the B.C. Jindal Group (Jindal Poly Films, Jindal India, Jindal India Thermal Power); not on the current Jindal Poly Films board
profile: Shyam Sunder Jindal leads the Delhi-based B.C. Jindal Group, founded in 1952 as a steel-pipe maker; Hurun India listed him in 2016-17 via Jindal Poly Films. The group expanded into polyester yarn, BOPET and BOPP packaging films (it bought ExxonMobil's BOPP business in 2013) and a 1,200 MW coal power plant in Angul, Odisha.
interesting_fact: Jindal Poly Films runs what the group calls the world's largest single-location plant for polyester (PET) and polypropylene (OPP) films, at Nashik, Maharashtra, and in 2013 bought ExxonMobil's BOPP films business.
notes: Do not confuse him with the O.P. Jindal/JSW family. Very low media profile. Several unofficial 'personal' sites (odoo.com, netlify) appear in search but are unverified or offline, so ignore them. The group's energy angle is Jindal India Thermal Power (2x600 MW, Odisha). Approach via the group's corporate office.

name: Matthew J Murphy
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Marvell Technology (MRVL)
profile: Matt Murphy spent 20+ years at Maxim Integrated, rising to EVP of business units, sales and marketing, before becoming Marvell's CEO in 2016 (chairman since 2023). He turned Marvell from a storage/consumer chip vendor into a data-infrastructure company built around custom AI silicon, optical DSPs and data-center connectivity for hyperscalers.
interesting_fact: He is the first executive to have chaired both the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA, 2018) and the Global Semiconductor Alliance (GSA), and sat on eBay's board 2019-2022.
deep_cut_fact: Not an engineer by degree: he holds a BA from Franklin & Marshall College, and outside chips he is a Trustee of the U.S. Olympic & Paralympic Foundation; he also set up Marvell's formal global philanthropy program.
notes: Excellent fit for data-center/AI angle (custom AI accelerators, optical interconnect). Frequent conference/podcast speaker (e.g. OFC 2026 Optica Executive Forum). Net worth in input is from SEC holdings only. Franklin & Marshall BA per https://www.semiconductors.org/board/matt-murphy/.

name: James Richard Perry
current_role: Co-founder and Director, Fermi Inc. (Fermi America, Nasdaq: FRMI); Director, Energy Transfer LP
profile: Rick Perry, longest-serving Texas governor (2000-2015) and US Secretary of Energy (2017-2019), sits on Energy Transfer's board and co-founded Fermi America. Fermi is building Project Matador, a planned 17 GW private 'HyperGrid' power and AI data-center campus on ~8,400 acres in the Texas Panhandle mixing gas, nuclear and other generation; it listed on Nasdaq in 2025.
interesting_fact: Fermi bills Project Matador as the world's largest private HyperGrid campus, with ~6 of 17 GW already permitted, aimed at hyperscalers who face 3-7 year waits for public grid power.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in tiny Paint Creek, Texas, by dryland cotton farmers, he traces his interest in politics to November 1961, when his father took him to Sam Rayburn's funeral. He was an Eagle Scout, a Texas A&M yell leader, and flew C-130s for the US Air Force.
notes: Highly on-topic (energy + AI data centers) and media-friendly; Fermi actively courts press. Best route: Fermi media team. Former Energy Secretary, so expect political framing; keep the pitch on energy/data centers.

name: Eran Zinman
current_role: Co-Founder and Co-CEO, monday.com Ltd. (NASDAQ: MNDY)
profile: Israeli software entrepreneur who co-founded monday.com (originally dapulse) with Roy Mann in 2012, serving as CTO until 2020 and then Co-CEO. He helped turn an internal team-management tool into a work OS / AI work platform used by 60%+ of the Fortune 500, through the 2021 NASDAQ IPO and past $1bn ARR.
interesting_fact: The company launched as 'dapulse' and rebranded to monday.com in 2017, a repositioning that preceded its fastest growth; Zinman has said nearly all investors turned the company down early on.
deep_cut_fact: Before monday.com he was co-founder and CEO of a small startup called Othersay, then part of the leadership team at Conduit Mobile (now Como), where he managed R&D; on 20VC he discussed the role video games played in his path as a founder.
notes: Accessible, podcast-friendly founder (has appeared on 20VC and SaaStr). Fit for data-center/AI angle is indirect (AI software, not infrastructure). Press inquiries via press@monday.com per monday.com press kit.

name: Gao Jinghai
profile: Gao Jinghai (高靖海) appeared on Hurun China lists only in 2009-2010, tied to 'G-Ocean Energy Group' (likely Shanxi Jinhaiyang/Golden Ocean Energy), a Shanxi coke and coal business. Golden Ocean Energy was later renamed China Coal Group Shanxi Huayu Energy after consolidation into state-owned China Coal.
notes: Identity unconfirmed: no source tying Gao Jinghai to the company was found, and the link to Golden Ocean is inferred from the company name. Off the lists since 2010, likely after Shanxi's 2009-10 coal consolidation. No public bio or contacts. Low priority.

notes: Unverifiable from open web sources. He has been off rich lists since 2010. The chemical-fibre focus suggests Zhejiang or Jiangsu, but that is unconfirmed. Would need a Chinese corporate registry lookup. Low priority.

He left the board in 2019; data aggregators also list a directorship at Hi-Think Technology.

notes: Identity matched via MarketScreener insider profile (secondary source; reports Tsinghua graduate degree and a 2002 Rutgers MBA - unverified in primary filings). Very low public profile; no direct contact route. Weak fit for energy focus.

Could not confirm his role at the company.

name: Wang Xiangwu
current_role: Founder and chairman, Nanchang Kaixun Photoelectric (南昌凯迅光电) per 36Kr; former chairman and GM of Xiamen Changelight (乾照光电, SZSE: 300102)
profile: Wang Xiangwu is a semiconductor-optoelectronics engineer who was director, GM and later chairman of Xiamen Changelight, an LED epitaxial-wafer and chip maker founded in 2006. He appeared on Hurun China in 2010. 36Kr now lists him as founder and chairman of Nanchang Kaixun Photoelectric.
interesting_fact: 36Kr describes him as a well-known technical expert in China's semiconductor-optoelectronics field, an engineer-founder rather than a financier, who built Changelight around compound-semiconductor epitaxy.
notes: Thinly documented; only on Hurun 2010. Current status and the Kaixun role are unverified beyond 36Kr's company page. Low priority.

name: Jennifer D. Saavedra
current_role: Chief Human Resources Officer, Dell Technologies (leads global HR and facilities)
profile: Organisational psychologist (PhD, Tulane) who consulted before joining Dell in 2005. She rose through talent development, culture, learning and HR business-partner roles, including SVP of HR for Sales, and became Dell's CHRO around 2021. Her wealth comes largely from Dell stock, and she sits on BetterUp's CHRO Growth Advisory Council.
interesting_fact: She runs people strategy for Dell during its AI-server boom, overseeing both HR and global facilities for one of the largest suppliers of AI data-center infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: Before Dell she spent several years as an external HR consultant; a SHRM speaker bio says her clients included Fortune 50 companies and the US armed forces. She has served on the executive boards of many of Dell's Employee Resource Groups, and says her passion is 'understanding the psychology of human behavior'.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; best angle is AI-era workforce and culture at Dell. Dell press and IR emails appear in Dell press releases (e.g. May 2026), found via search. The investor pages now return 404 or 403, so I could not re-open them. dell.com blocks scripted access. The armed-forces client detail comes from a SHRM session bio (sessions-cron.shrm.org/node/19709) seen via search only.

name: Mala Madhukar Parekh
current_role: Promoter-group shareholder, Pidilite Industries Ltd. (about 1.04% stake); no executive or board role
profile: Mala Parekh is the wife of Pidilite chairman Madhukar Parekh and a member of the promoter family behind Pidilite Industries, maker of Fevicol, M-Seal and Dr. Fixit, founded by Balvant Parekh. She holds about 10.6M shares (about 1.04%) directly. She keeps a private profile and appears mainly in Pidilite's own publications.
interesting_fact: She wrote a personal tribute in Pidilite's 2025-26 annual report to ad legend Piyush Pandey, creator of the famous Fevicol campaigns. She called him a brother-like friend and credited him with helping her husband grow Pidilite.
deep_cut_fact: At her 40th wedding anniversary in Udaipur, Piyush Pandey, who had said he couldn't come, surprised the family by arriving disguised as the leader of a Rajasthani folk-singer troupe, shawl over his face. She calls it a memory she cherishes.
notes: Very private, non-executive family shareholder. Pidilite's published press contact (Hiral Jani Vasani) is the only formal route. She is only loosely tied to the energy theme: Hurun classes Pidilite under chemicals.

name: Anurag Choudhary
current_role: Chairman, Managing Director and CEO, Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd (Kolkata; NSE: HSCL)
profile: He leads the Choudhary family's Kolkata company Himadri and has turned it from a coal-tar-pitch maker into a speciality-chemicals group (carbon black) that is building lithium-ion battery materials (LFP cathode, anodes). It has invested in Australia's Sicona and bought Birla Tyres. Target: a ₹30,000 crore battery-materials business by about 2032.
interesting_fact: Himadri calls itself India's first producer of both anode and cathode materials for lithium-ion batteries. It has an exclusive licence to commercialise Sicona's SiCx silicon-carbon anode technology in India, and Choudhary sits on Sicona's board.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Himadri at 18 and has spent three decades there. In a December 2023 interview he predicted that 'in 5 years [Himadri] will be a totally different company', an early signal of its pivot to battery materials.
notes: Wealth is shared with his brother Amit Choudhary (Hurun India 2019). Strong fit for the energy/battery-supply-chain angle. He speaks regularly on earnings calls and to Indian business media. info@himadri.com is a corporate inbox, not a personal office.

name: Amit Choudhary
current_role: Executive Director and promoter, Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd (NSE: HSCL), Kolkata
profile: Promoter of Kolkata-based Himadri Speciality Chemical, where he has worked since 1994 (brother Anurag is Chairman, MD & CEO). He runs operations, plant commissioning, safety and HR as Himadri grew from a coal-tar-pitch maker into a carbon black/specialty chemicals group exporting to 56 countries, now entering battery materials.
interesting_fact: Himadri is pivoting a coal-tar chemicals business into EV/energy-storage supply chains: it now markets battery anode materials, LFP cathode materials, lithium refining and battery recycling alongside its carbon black lines.
deep_cut_fact: A commerce graduate of St. Xavier's College, Kolkata with executive education at IESE Business School (Spain), he personally drives Himadri's safety push - the company won the IOD Golden Peacock Award for Occupational Health & Safety (2025), chosen from 573 nominations.
notes: Hurun India listing shares wealth with brother Anurag Choudhary (the company's public face; better podcast guest for battery-materials story). Company has its own profile page for Amit - operations/people/safety focus.

name: Naresh Chander Oberoi
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Powerica Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Founder-promoter of Powerica, which he started in 1984 as a diesel generator-set business; it has been a Cummins India genset OEM since 2004. In 2008 Powerica moved into wind power, co-developing farms with Vestas and later GE, and it is now both a genset maker and a wind IPP/EPC player. Powerica launched a roughly ₹1,400 crore IPO in March 2026; family trusts hold the shares.
interesting_fact: Powerica's medium-speed large generators are used in critical infrastructure. In 2019 it agreed with HD Hyundai Heavy Industries to supply generator sets for nuclear power plants in India, a relevant angle for data-center backup power.
deep_cut_fact: Powerica signed a joint-venture agreement with Vestas in 2016 for about 750 MW of wind projects, after installing its first co-developed wind farm with Vestas in 2014. By 2023 it had executed 398 MW of wind as IPP and balance-of-plant contractor.
notes: Strong fit for energy and data-center topics: backup gensets plus wind. His son Bharat Oberoi (Joint MD) is the more media-facing family member and has given CEO Magazine interviews. Company emails sit behind Cloudflare obfuscation on the site; decoded values are listed.

name: Scott J Deboer
current_role: President and Chief Technology and Products Officer, Micron Technology (since Aug 26, 2026)
profile: Dr. Scott DeBoer joined Micron in 1995 as a process technology engineer and rose through Process R&D and Technology Development to run its technology and products organisation, leading delivery of 15 memory technology nodes. notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (distributed solar + storage + EV charging). hello@ is Altus's general company inbox. Altus no longer files with the SEC after the TPG take-private.

name: Jayendra H Kharawala
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Jay Chemical Industries Pvt Ltd (JCIL), India (listed as chairman on the company website)
profile: Founder of Jay Chemical Industries, started in 1967 as a small dye and dye-intermediate unit. JCIL is now one of the world's top reactive-dye producers, with more than 15% of India's market, sales in over 40 countries and revenue above $200M. It has expanded into digital textile inks, construction chemicals and garments.
interesting_fact: JCIL makes more than half of its own raw-material inputs (over 50% backward integration). That is a deliberate self-reliance strategy that Kharawala built into a dye business started when international firms dominated Indian dyes.
deep_cut_fact: Jay Chemicals marked its 50th anniversary on 9 March 2017. The company credits its founding to Kharawala's vision 'to do business that would not only provide for his family but would better society as well'.
notes: Private company with a low profile. Day-to-day operations are run by Managing Director Greeven Kharawala. Alive status is not independently confirmed (the company site still lists him as chairman). The links are corporate, not personal. Industry is textile dyes, so the fit with energy and data centers is weak.

name: Ramesh Vinayak Vaze
current_role: Not on the current board of S H Kelkar and Company (Keva); current status unconfirmed
profile: Member of the Vaze promoter family behind S H Kelkar and Company (now branded Keva), a Mumbai fragrance, flavour and aroma-ingredients maker that began as an industrial perfume manufacturer in British India and is now one of India's largest fragrance companies. The family's third generation, Kedar Vaze, is Group CEO; Prabha Vaze is a non-executive director.
interesting_fact: Keva started as S H Kelkar & Company, a maker of industrial perfumes in British India, and grew organically and via acquisitions into an Indian fragrance multinational.

name: Bharat Naresh Oberoi
current_role: Joint Managing Director and Promoter, Powerica Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Bharat Oberoi is a promoter and Joint MD (since 2003) of Powerica, the Mumbai power-solutions firm his father Naresh Chander Oberoi founded in 1984. Powerica builds diesel generator sets and medium-speed large generators for standby/prime power (a key data-center backup market) and since 2008 has been a wind IPP and wind EPC/O&M contractor. He joined in 1994 and leads its marketing side.
interesting_fact: Powerica began as a diesel-generator business in 1984, added medium-speed large generators in 1996, and in 2008 moved into wind energy as an independent power producer, later adding wind EPC and O&M services.
notes: Low public profile; last on Hurun India in 2018. Backup-power gensets for Indian data centers plus wind IPP make a natural energy/data-center angle. Route via company. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so no sourced personal deep-cut.

name: Vasant Laxminarayan Rathi
current_role: Promoter and Non-Executive Director, Advanced Enzyme Technologies Ltd (NSE: ADVENZYMES); heads its US subsidiaries
profile: V. L. Rathi, a pharmacist turned enzyme entrepreneur, co-founded Rathi Papains (1978), set up Cal-India Foods in the US (1985) and has been with Advanced Enzyme Technologies since 1993. The Thane-based enzyme and probiotics maker listed in India in 2016; from the US he runs its American subsidiaries.
interesting_fact: Advanced Enzymes grew from a family papain business into one of India's largest enzyme makers, with US and European arms. It owns Germany's evoxx technologies in Monheim am Rhein.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture, Rathi Papains (1978), made enzymes from papain, the protein-digesting enzyme taken from papaya latex. He trained as a pharmacist (B.Pharm, Nagpur University) and earned an MS at the University of Hawaii.
notes: Categorized as Chemicals/Petrochemicals 'energy', but the business is industrial and nutritional enzymes, so the fit for an energy podcast is weak (enzymes are used in biofuel/biogas, which could be an angle). Low media profile; route via the US subsidiaries (Cal-India Foods / AST Enzymes in California) or the company's general email.

name: Suresh Harakchand Parakh
current_role: Chairman, Parakh Agro Industries Ltd (Samrat flour brand), Parakh Group, Pune
profile: Younger son of Parakh Group founder Harakchand K. Parakh (1930-2015), Suresh Parakh is a flour-milling veteran who chairs Parakh Agro Industries, maker of Samrat atta, besan and oil. The family's Parakh Foods built the Gemini edible-oil brand, sold to Cargill in 2004-05; the Pune group now spans FMCG, flexible packaging, real estate (Gemini Housing) and wind power.
interesting_fact: Parakh Group's energy arm, Parakh Energy, runs 8.3 MW of wind turbines (4 Suzlon, 2 Vestas) in Dhule, Maharashtra, feeding the western regional grid.
deep_cut_fact: He drove the adoption of Swiss Bühler milling technology in the group's flour mills, which combine traditional stone chakkis with Bühler machinery, and personally heads the bulk flour sales business, with some customers loyal for 25+ years. B.Com, Maharashtra Mandal College, Pune.
notes: Primarily a food/FMCG businessman; the energy link is the family's wind assets and former edible-oil refining (Gemini sold to Cargill: https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2011/03/29/Acquisition-boosts-Cargill-brand-portfolio-in-India). Elder brother Prakash Parakh led group expansion. Low-fit for energy podcast.

name: Sureshbhai Jayantibhai Patel
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Bodal Chemicals Ltd (NSE: BODALCHEM), Ahmedabad.
profile: Suresh J. Patel founded Bodal Chemicals in Ahmedabad around 1989-90 as a small vinyl sulphone maker and built it into a vertically integrated producer of dye intermediates, textile/leather/paper dyestuffs and basic chemicals (sulphuric acid etc.), exporting to 40+ countries. He has been chairman & MD since 2006, the year the company went public.
interesting_fact: Bodal is one of very few dye makers integrated from basic chemicals through intermediates to finished dyestuffs; by 2015 it ran eight Gujarat plants with ~2,500 staff and sales above Rs 1,000 crore, exporting 80% of its dyestuff output.
deep_cut_fact: Bodal began in 1989 as 'JK Pharma', a two-man partnership of Suresh Patel and Ramesh Patel with capacity of just 60 tonnes a year of vinyl sulphone; it became Bodal Chemicals Pvt Ltd in 1994.
notes: Chemicals, not energy/data-center; modest wealth (Hurun India 2017 only). Director Bhavin Patel runs the dyestuff division. Best route: company secretarial/info email.

name: Madan Mohan Dhanuka
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, I G Petrochemicals Ltd (Dhanuka Group), Mumbai (per Simply Wall St/Investing.com; some sites list Nikunj Dhanuka as chairman)
profile: Senior figure of the Dhanuka Group and a director of I G Petrochemicals since its incorporation in October 1988. IGPL, set up in technical collaboration with Germany's Lurgi, is India's largest maker of phthalic anhydride (used in plasticisers, paints and resins), with plants at Taloja, Maharashtra; he also sits on the board of Mysore Petro Chemicals.
interesting_fact: He has served on IGPL's board for more than 35 years, since the company's founding in 1988, as it grew into India's largest phthalic anhydride producer.

public_contacts.value: ssingh@igpetro.com (Company Secretary Sudhir R Singh, published company contact)

notes: Chairman title conflicts across data sites; confirm in latest IGPL annual report. Day-to-day leadership by younger family members (Nikunj, Mayank Dhanuka). Low public profile.

name: Abhay Vithaldas Udeshi
current_role: Chairman, Jayant Agro-Organics Ltd (Mumbai; BSE/NSE listed)
profile: Mumbai industrialist who succeeded his father Vithaldas Udeshi as chairman of Jayant Agro-Organics, a castor-oil and castor-derivatives company with an estimated 35-40% share of the global castor oil market. The group runs JVs with France's Arkema and a Japanese partner, plus hybrid castor seed and pharma-grade oil operations.
interesting_fact: He notes India produces nearly 90% of the world's castor oil; Jayant says it was the first company in India to process castor seeds into oil, starting in 1952.
deep_cut_fact: He helped create the Sustainable Castor Association (with Arkema, BASF and NGO Solidaridad), which runs a sustainable castor farming code and certification for Indian farmers and had grown to 31 global members by 2024.
notes: University of Baroda graduate; director of the Sustainable Castor Association. Energy relevance is modest (company has a power-generation segment; castor-based bio-chemicals). Family-run board.

name: Brij Bhushan Agarwal
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Shyam Metalics and Energy Ltd (and subsidiary Shyam SEL and Power); President, Indian Chamber of Commerce
profile: Kolkata-based industrialist (B.Com, University of Calcutta) who has led Shyam Metalics since its inception in 2001, building it into an integrated metals producer (ferroalloys, iron and steel, aluminium foil) with captive power plants in West Bengal and Odisha; listed on NSE/BSE in 2021. He owns roughly 9.5% directly, with the promoter family holding the majority.

deep_cut_fact: He chaired the Indian Chamber of Commerce's National Expert Committee on Minerals and Metals in 2019 and that October won Zee Business's 'Inspirational Leader of the Year' award in the 'Dare to Dream' category, before rising to ICC Senior VP and then President.
notes: Hurun India figure ($132m, 2019) is stale; promoter-family stake is worth much more today. Head of IR Pankaj Harlalka appears on earnings calls; IR partner is EY (per call transcripts). ICC presidency gives a second route via Indian Chamber of Commerce, Kolkata.

name: Russell Craig Ellwanger
current_role: CEO (since May 2005) and director, Tower Semiconductor Ltd (Nasdaq/TASE: TSEM), Migdal HaEmek, Israel
profile: An American-born semiconductor veteran, Ellwanger spent 1980–92 at Philips Semiconductors and 1992–96 at Novellus. He then held senior roles at Applied Materials from 1996 to 2005, including running its Metal CVD, CMP/electroplating and global services units. Since 2005 he has turned Tower into a profitable specialty foundry; it now has big silicon-photonics and SiGe contracts for AI data-centre optical modules, including work with NVIDIA.
interesting_fact: Tower reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $460m (+24%), and Ellwanger raised the 2028 target to $3.6bn revenue and $1.2bn net profit. Growth is driven by silicon photonics for data-centre optics; Tower signed customer contracts for about $1.3bn of 2027 silicon-photonics revenue.
deep_cut_fact: He started wrestling at 11 and his family picked a Las Vegas high school for its wrestling programme. While studying physics at BYU he joined Philips Semiconductors' Utah site, partly because it was one of the few companies offering students health insurance, and was later sent to Philips' main lab in the Netherlands.
notes: Articulate and quotable: Globes says he quotes management gurus, William Faulkner and Alice in Wonderland. A strong data-centre/AI-optics guest. The IR contact is Liat Avraham (+972-4-6506154). A media contact (oritsha@towersemi.com) appears in some releases but I didn't verify it. The $1.3bn photonics-contracts figure comes from a Finviz headline.

name: Li Shujun
current_role: Founder, Trustbridge Partners (挚信资本), Shanghai-based China-focused private equity firm
profile: Li Shujun (Shujun Li) is the former CFO of Shanda Interactive who founded Trustbridge Partners in 2006. current_role: Co-owner of Jinglong Group (BVI), a founding shareholder group of JA Solar (Ningjin, Hebei); limited partner in JA Solar investor vehicle Xingtai Jingjun Ningyu

He held 9.58% of Jinglong Group BVI, the joint-largest stake after Jin, which held JA Solar shares through its 2007 Nasdaq IPO, 2018 take-private and 2019 Shenzhen relisting (JA Solar Technology, 002459).

Earlier pass missed him because Chinese web search yields nothing; SEC full-text search on 'Binguo Liu' does.

name: Stefan A Dyckerhoff
current_role: Managing Director, Sutter Hill Ventures; independent director, Astera Labs (NASDAQ: ALAB) since Nov 2019
profile: Networking executive turned VC. He ran Cisco's Edge Routing unit and Juniper's Platform Systems Division before joining Sutter Hill Ventures in 2012. An early backer and director of AI-connectivity chipmaker Astera Labs (IPO 2024), he also has board seats at SiFive and Enfabrica.
interesting_fact: His board seats cover much of the AI data-center 'plumbing' stack: Astera Labs (PCIe/CXL retimers and scale-up switches), Enfabrica (AI networking silicon) and SiFive (RISC-V processor IP).
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he ran routers himself. From 2007 to 2009 he was VP & GM of Cisco's Edge Routing Business Unit, and he then ran the Platform Systems Division at rival Juniper. He has a Duke BSE in electrical engineering and computer science and a Stanford MSEE.
notes: Low public profile. Sutter Hill is famously quiet, and its website is a placeholder with no contact details. The Astera Labs media contact reaches the company, not him. A warm intro through the Astera Labs or Sutter Hill network is likely the best route.

name: Jack Hartung
current_role: Independent director, Tesla (since 2025, Audit Committee); also on boards of The Honest Company, Portillo's, Wonder Group and ZocDoc. Retired from Chipotle March 2026
profile: John R. 'Jack' Hartung, 68, spent 18 years at McDonald's before joining Chipotle in 2002 as CFO (20 years), later CFAO and President & Chief Strategy Officer. He delayed retirement after Brian Niccol left for Starbucks, retired as senior advisor in March 2026, and now sits on the boards of Tesla, Honest Company, Portillo's and others.
interesting_fact: He was persuaded to delay his retirement when CEO Brian Niccol made a surprise move to Starbucks in 2024; he has been named 'CFO of the Year' by the Orange County Business Journal and 'Best CFO' (restaurants) by Institutional Investor.
deep_cut_fact: Portillo's 2026 proxy lists his favorite menu item as the Italian Beef with Hot Peppers. He holds a B.S. in accounting and economics and an MBA from Illinois State University, and is a (non-practicing) CPA and CMA.
notes: Tesla board seat gives an energy/AI angle (Tesla Energy, Megapacks). Low social-media profile; route via board/IR channels or Chipotle alumni network.

name: Theodore Blegen
current_role: Retired EVP & CFO (Feb 2026), Monolithic Power Systems; remains with MPS in a transition role
profile: T. Bernie Blegen joined power-chip maker Monolithic Power Systems in 2011 as corporate controller and served as CFO from 2016 until retiring after the FY2025 10-K in Feb 2026, a decade in which MPS grew into a major supplier of power-management chips for AI servers and data centers. deep_cut_fact: Before semiconductors he worked in publishing and software finance, including at Times Mirror's higher-education group, Shutterfly and Micro Focus, per his executive profile; his 10-K bio cites 25+ years across the semiconductor, software and publishing industries.
notes: Goes by 'Bernie'. Now retired as CFO, so the company IR route is indirect; Rob Dean is interim CFO. Specific employers Times Mirror/Shutterfly/Micro Focus come from MarketScreener profiles (not the 10-K, which confirms only the publishing/software background).

name: Joseph W Gorder
current_role: Retired; former Chairman & CEO of Valero Energy (CEO 2014-June 2023, Executive Chairman until 31 Dec 2024)
profile: Joe Gorder ran Valero, the largest US independent refiner, as CEO (May 2014-June 2023) and chairman (from end-2014), then executive chairman until retiring at end-2024. He rose through Diamond Shamrock/Ultramar Diamond Shamrock (sales, treasury, IT, business development) before Valero's 2001 acquisition of UDS.

deep_cut_fact: A Pattonville High School (Maryland Heights, Mo.) grad, he chose UMSL because he could work 30-40 hours a week and still graduate on time (BSBA, marketing, 1979). His leadership line: 'I believe that a leader is one who serves... give them the latitude to do their jobs without micromanaging them.'
notes: Retired from Valero's board at end-2024, so Valero IR is only an indirect route; no personal social accounts found. SEC-derived wealth (~$125m). UMSL alumni network is a possible warm connection.

name: Dan O Dinges
current_role: Former Chairman, President and CEO of Cabot Oil & Gas (2002-2021); Coterra Energy director until the May 2026 Devon-Coterra merger
profile: Dan Dinges ran Cabot Oil & Gas for about 20 years. He took over in 2002 after more than 20 years at Noble Energy/Samedan and built Cabot into a leading Marcellus Shale gas producer. He led the 2021 merger with Cimarex that created Coterra Energy and then served on Coterra's board. Coterra merged into Devon Energy in May 2026, and Dinges was not named to the combined board.
interesting_fact: He chaired the American Exploration & Production Council, the trade group of the largest US independent oil and gas producers, from 2015. He has also served on the boards of U.S. Steel and the American Petroleum Institute.
deep_cut_fact: Dinges started out as a Mobil Oil landman covering Louisiana, Arkansas and the central Gulf of Mexico. He holds a BBA in Petroleum Land Management from the University of Texas, a niche degree. He is a member of the All-American Wildcatters and served on the executive committee of UT Austin's Kay Bailey Hutchison Center for Energy, Law and Business.
notes: Retired from executive roles and Houston-based, with no personal website or social accounts found. Coterra no longer exists independently (merged into Devon, May 2026), so there is no current corporate press route. Industry associations (AXPC, All-American Wildcatters) or UT's KBH Energy Center are possible intro paths.

name: Michael C Morgan
current_role: Co-founding partner & Chairman, Triangle Peak Partners; Lead Director, Kinder Morgan Inc.
profile: Former president of Kinder Morgan (pipelines and energy infrastructure) who co-founded Triangle Peak Partners, a venture/growth investor in energy and technology, and runs the Portcullis Partners investment partnership. He is lead director at Kinder Morgan and has served on the boards of residential-solar firm Sunnova and AI-driven storage company Stem.

deep_cut_fact: A 2022 Stanford Distinguished Careers Institute fellow (billed as 'Energy & Technology Geek/Investor'), he co-chaired the Precourt Institute for Energy's advisory council, won the Stanford Associates Governors' Award, and once taught as an adjunct professor at Rice's Jones School.
notes: Kinder Morgan contacts are corporate routes, not personal. No working Triangle Peak website found. Sunnova filed for Chapter 11 in 2025, so avoid that topic. Education: Stanford BA econ & MA sociology, Harvard MBA. Stanford energy-network ties could make a warm intro.

name: Xue Yongmin
current_role: Chairman of the supervisory board (earlier chairman), Shanxi Dongfang Resources Development Group (山西东方资源, ex-Dongfang Ferro Alloy), Jishan, Shanxi; head of the manganese committee of China's ferroalloy industry association
profile: Xue Yongmin (薛永民) built Shanxi Dongfang Resources Development, founded in 2002 in Jishan county, Yuncheng, Shanxi, into China's largest high-carbon ferromanganese producer. It is an integrated 'circular economy' plant covering coal washing (1.2 Mt), coking (0.6 Mt), sintering, blast-furnace smelting and power generation. By 2016 it had about 550,000 t/yr of ferromanganese capacity, which it put at over half the national market.
interesting_fact: In 2016 the company lit what it called China's largest-volume, highest-output high-carbon ferromanganese blast furnace (No. 6, 120m yuan). It said it carried no bank debt even in that downturn and had been Jishan county's top taxpayer for 13 straight years.
deep_cut_fact: Under his leadership the company publicly adopted a 'low-key, rigorous, frugal' (低调、严谨、节约) management creed, and in Jan 2016 he personally lit the ceremonial 'blessing fire' to start the No. 6 ferromanganese furnace.
notes: Hurun 'Dongfang Ferro Alloy' matches the company's own domain (dongfangferroalloy.com) and Xue Yongmin as chairman. The site couldn't be reached from here; a search snippet says it lists him as 监事长 and head of the ferroalloy association's manganese committee. Company GM in 2016 was Xue Guodong. The interesting fact relies on a reposted trade-press (thjb.net) article on Sina Blog. Hurun's 'iron mine' line was not confirmed; the business is coal and ferromanganese.

current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, Vikram Solar Ltd (NSE/BSE); Director, Vikram (India) Ltd; chairman of the Kolkata-based Vikram Group

deep_cut_fact: The family's solar business grew out of tea: he is a director of Vikram (India) Ltd, a Kolkata company founded in 1974 that makes tea-processing machinery, the original business of the Vikram Group.

current_role: Retired as Chairman of Kirloskar Oil Engines on 31 Mar 2026 (age 70); remains on boards incl. Kirloskar Industries and Kirloskar Pneumatic (non-executive)

deep_cut_fact: Before Bloom he spent 22 years in semiconductor and electronics operations - process engineering, quality, product and program leadership - and holds a mechanical engineering degree plus an MBA in operations.

name: Pablo Manuel Vera Pinto

current_role: Co-founder, CEO and director, indie Semiconductor (NASDAQ: INDI), since 2012

name: Ryan Fukushima
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Data, Tempus AI (Nasdaq: TEM), since February 2026; board member and advisor, Pathos AI
profile: Ryan Fukushima (40) was a founding-era executive at Tempus AI, Eric Lefkofsky's Chicago precision-medicine company that pairs clinical/molecular data with AI. name: John P Surma
current_role: Independent Lead Director, Marathon Petroleum (director since 2011; also MPLX GP board); director, Trane Technologies; former Chairman & CEO, U.S. Steel

Now lead independent director of refiner Marathon Petroleum (since Aug 2024) and a director of HVAC/data-center-cooling maker Trane Technologies.

name: Victor K Lee
current_role: Independent director (audit committee financial expert), Monolithic Power Systems (Nasdaq: MPWR), since Sept 2006

He was CFO of video-chip maker Ambarella (2007-2011), served on the MoSys board (2012-2016), and has sat on the board of power-chip maker MPS since 2006; his wealth comes largely from MPS stock, whose power ICs are now key in AI data-center servers.

current_role: Chairman, CEO & President, Plains All American Pipeline (PAA) / Plains GP Holdings (PAGP), Houston; director, Delta Air Lines
profile: Willie Chiang (65) is a career oil and gas operator: 16 years at ConocoPhillips (1996-2012, ending as SVP Refining, Marketing, Transportation & Commercial), then EVP Operations at Occidental (2012-15). name: Mark Edwin Jensen
current_role: Independent director, Lattice Semiconductor (since 2013) and Wolfspeed (since May 2025); retired Deloitte partner

Since then he has been a professional director at tech companies including Lattice, Wolfspeed, ForeScout, Control4 and Exabeam.

current_role: Angel investor; Independent director at Arista Networks (since 2011), lead director of Zoom Communications and lead independent director of SentinelOne
