current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, CloudWalk Technology (云从科技, SSE STAR: 688327)
profile: Zhou Xi (周曦), a Sichuan-born USTC graduate in pattern recognition with a UIUC PhD in electrical and computer engineering, spent four years on facial-recognition research at the Chinese Academy of Sciences before founding CloudWalk in Chongqing in April 2015. CloudWalk grew from bank and security facial recognition into a broader AI and large-model platform company and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022.
interesting_fact: Between 2007 and 2011 he led university research teams to six wins in international pattern-recognition competitions and interned at IBM, Microsoft and NEC before returning to China at the urging of a CAS director.
deep_cut_fact: In one of CloudWalk's first bank bids, his team spent days on a 10-page proposal that was rejected because no supplier had ever submitted fewer than about 300 pages, a lesson he said pushed him from an academic to a business mindset. His motto: 'I never leave myself a route of retreat.'
notes: CloudWalk has been on the US Commerce Department Entity List since 2020 (surveillance-related), which may matter for a US podcast. Best route is the board secretary/IR office (ir@cloudwalk.com).

name: Jesse Levinson
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Zoox (Amazon subsidiary)
profile: Princeton summa cum laude graduate who did his CS PhD and postdoc under Sebastian Thrun at Stanford, helping build Stanford's 2007 DARPA Urban Challenge car and later leading its self-driving research. He co-founded Zoox in 2014 to build a purpose-built electric robotaxi; Amazon acquired it in 2020 and he remains CTO, overseeing software, AI, compute and sensing.
interesting_fact: Rather than retrofitting existing cars, Zoox designed a purpose-built robotaxi from scratch; Amazon bought the company in 2020 and Levinson stayed on as CTO to scale it.
deep_cut_fact: As a high-schooler he won a 2000 Intel ISEF Grand Award (psychology) for 'Computer Simulated Evolution of Behavior'; he also co-created the iPhone photography app Pro HDR, bought by more than a million people.
notes: ISEF award source: https://www.societyforscience.org/alumni/notable/jesse-levinson/. Press requests likely routed through Amazon/Zoox comms; no dedicated press email found. Frequent conference speaker (WEF, TechCrunch, EmTech).

name: Tim Kentley-Klay
current_role: Founder of HYPR (AI robotics/autonomous mobility startup); founder of Melbourne animation studio XYZ Studios. Current status of HYPR not confirmed
profile: Australian designer-turned-tech founder who co-founded self-driving company Zoox with Jesse Levinson in 2014 and was its CEO until the board removed him in August 2018; Amazon bought Zoox in 2020 for a reported ~$1.2bn. He then founded HYPR, an AI robotics company that raised a US$10m seed (Andrew 'Twiggy' Forrest and R7 Partners) at a reported US$200m valuation.
interesting_fact: He describes himself as a 'painter, designer, animator, film-maker, trouble-maker and thinker', and won the 2020 Advance Global Australian Award.
deep_cut_fact: Before Zoox he founded XYZ Studios, a commercial-animation studio, in Melbourne in 2003 despite having no animation training and, by the studio's account, not knowing a single person in advertising; it grew to offices in Melbourne and New York.
notes: No verified published contact found (HYPR and XYZ sites blocked automated access). Avoid dwelling on the 2018 Zoox exit. Hurun lists him as a Zoox founder (2019-20); personal wealth from the Amazon deal is undisclosed. Autonomy/robotics angle rather than energy.

name: Zia Chishti
current_role: Investor; co-founder of Align Technology, The Resource Group (TRG) and Afiniti (left Afiniti as chairman/CEO in 2021) - current operating role unclear
profile: Columbia CS/econ grad and ex-Morgan Stanley/McKinsey banker who invented Invisalign while at Stanford GSB and co-founded Align Technology (1997, IPO 2001). He then co-founded Pakistan-based investor TRG and AI call-center routing firm Afiniti, which reached unicorn status; he resigned from Afiniti in 2021.
interesting_fact: Named inventor on around 150 patents and co-founder of three unicorns; TRG's first deal was buying Align's abandoned Lahore operation and rehiring laid-off staff, growing into one of Pakistan's largest tech employers.
deep_cut_fact: The Invisalign idea came from his own orthodontic treatment in his early twenties - he envisioned computer-designed clear plastic aligners instead of metal braces while an MBA student at Stanford. He received Pakistan's Sitara-e-Imtiaz for IT in 2018.
notes: Caution: resigned from Afiniti in 2021 after sexual misconduct allegations were made public (he won a 2025 libel settlement against the Daily Telegraph); reputational risk for a podcast guest. No published personal/office contact found; Afiniti no longer represents him.

name: J. Andrew Bagnell
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Scientist, Aurora Innovation (NASDAQ: AUR); Consulting Professor, CMU Robotics Institute and Machine Learning Dept.
profile: Drew Bagnell is a machine-learning and robotics researcher who co-founded self-driving company Aurora in 2016 with Chris Urmson and Sterling Anderson, serving as CTO until 2020 and now Chief Scientist. Earlier he was a CMU professor (2004-2018) and head of perception/autonomy architect at Uber ATG. Aurora now runs driverless trucks commercially in Texas.
interesting_fact: His research group has won best-paper awards at ICML, RSS and NeurIPS, and he co-authored DAgger, a widely used imitation-learning algorithm for teaching robots from expert demonstrations.
deep_cut_fact: He was the founding director of CMU's Robotics Institute Summer Scholars program, which has brought hundreds of undergraduates from around the world into robotics research, and won CMU's 2016 Ryan Award for Meritorious Teaching. His BS is in electrical engineering from the University of Florida.
notes: Goes by Drew Bagnell. DAgger attribution (Ross, Gordon & Bagnell, AISTATS 2011) is from general knowledge of the literature, not the cited page. Academic and podcast-friendly (NeurIPS invited talks). Fit for AI angle; less so energy/data centers. Route via Aurora press.

name: Dave Palmer
current_role: General Partner, Ten Eleven Ventures (leads its European office in Cheltenham, UK)
profile: Former UK intelligence technologist (GCHQ and MI5) who co-founded Cambridge AI-cybersecurity firm Darktrace in 2013 and, as Director of Technology and later Chief Product Officer, helped scale it to a 2021 London IPO and an eventual $5.3B take-private by Thoma Bravo. He now invests in cybersecurity startups as a General Partner at Ten Eleven Ventures, an early Darktrace backer.
interesting_fact: He says what most excites and worries him in cyber is the same thing: AI coding agents that will soon find huge numbers of vulnerabilities, forcing the world to fix decades of software risk at once.
deep_cut_fact: He names Gaven Smith, who later became GCHQ's CTO, as the biggest influence on his career - teaching him to study why things succeed, not just how. His hardest Darktrace lesson: stop describing how clever the product/team was and tell stories of customer success.
notes: Accessible and media-friendly; regular conference speaker (RSA Conference, GBx). Ten Eleven opened its UK office with him as GP (PR Newswire, 2022). Good guest for AI-security angle.

name: Emily Orton
current_role: Co-founder and former CMO of Darktrace (stepped down July 2022); reportedly Non-Executive Director at ThreatSpike (from May 2025, per Crunchbase)
profile: Emily Orton was a founding team member of Cambridge, UK-born AI cybersecurity firm Darktrace (2013) and its Chief Marketing Officer through the 2021 London IPO, building its global marketing engine. She stepped down as CMO in July 2022; Darktrace was taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2024 for ~$5.3B.
interesting_fact: She built Darktrace's marketing from founding to IPO, helping turn a Cambridge mathematics/AI startup into a London-listed company used by thousands of organisations worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: She is a linguist by training, with an MA in Modern Languages from the University of Cambridge, rather than a technical background.
notes: Low public profile since leaving Darktrace in 2022; no verified personal website or social account found (Crunchbase lists a ThreatSpike NED role - unverified). Hurun 'unicorn founder' listing (2019-2020) only. LinkedIn likely the best route but URL not verified.

name: Jack Stockdale
current_role: Founding Chief Technology Officer, Darktrace (Cambridge, UK; taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2024)
profile: Jack Stockdale OBE FREng is Darktrace's founding CTO (2013) and leads the Bayesian and self-learning AI behind its cyber-defence products. He was previously a technical director at Autonomy, worked at blinkx and was chief architect at Invoke Capital, Darktrace's seed investor. Thoma Bravo took Darktrace private for about $5.3B in 2024.
interesting_fact: He and Darktrace's then-CEO were both appointed OBE in 2019 for services to cyber security; he is also a Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering.
deep_cut_fact: He and his Cambridge development team were recognised by the Royal Academy of Engineering's MacRobert Award committee twice, in 2017 and again in 2019, for outstanding contribution to engineering. He studied computer science at Lancaster University.
notes: Low public profile but does speak at events (e.g. MIT Technology Review cybersecurity events). Best route is Darktrace media relations. Wealth figure unclear since Darktrace went private.

name: Nicole Eagan
current_role: Co-founder and Strategic Advisor, Darktrace (owned by Thoma Bravo since 2024)
profile: Tech executive with ~30 years at Oracle, HP, startups and VC who co-founded Cambridge, UK AI-cybersecurity firm Darktrace in 2013. She was CEO from 2014, then Chief Strategy and AI Officer from 2020; Darktrace listed in London in 2021 and was taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2024. She now advises on strategy.
interesting_fact: Darktrace grew out of a team of Cambridge mathematicians and ex-intelligence specialists applying self-learning AI to detect cyber threats; it now protects close to 10,000 organisations across cloud, email, network and OT.
deep_cut_fact: She was named 'AI Leader of the Year' and took the No. 1 spot on The Software Report's 'Top 25 Women Leaders in Cybersecurity' in 2020.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (CNBC TEC, Fortune Brainstorm AI, Economist Impact); speaker-bureau route likely receptive. Input lists company value $2B; Thoma Bravo deal valued Darktrace at ~$5.3B.

name: Poppy Gustafsson
current_role: Labour life peer (Baroness Gustafsson of Chesterton, House of Lords); trustee of RUSI (from Jan 2026); former co-founder and CEO of Darktrace
profile: British accountant-turned-tech founder (b. 1982, Huntingdon) who co-founded Cambridge AI cybersecurity company Darktrace in 2013 as CFO, became co-CEO in 2016 and sole CEO in 2020, leading its 2021 London IPO before its 2024 sale to Thoma Bravo. She served as UK Minister for Investment (Oct 2024-Sep 2025) and joined the RUSI board in 2026.
interesting_fact: She was named Tech Businesswoman of the Year at the 2019 UK Tech Awards, received an OBE (2019) and CBE (2025) for services to cybersecurity, and was made a life peer in 2024 so she could serve as investment minister.
deep_cut_fact: Before Darktrace she started out at Cambridge venture firm Amadeus Capital Partners, then joined Autonomy in 2009 as a corporate controller until its acquisition by HP; the University of Sheffield, her alma mater, gave her an honorary DSc in 2022.
notes: Hurun listed her as Darktrace founder (company now private under Thoma Bravo). Parliament's published route is the House of Lords member contact service (forwards to members). Frequent speaker (London Tech Week) - podcast-friendly.

name: Jeff Kinsey
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Dataminr (per company/third-party profiles; not confirmed by a dated primary source)
profile: Yale computer-science graduate who co-founded Dataminr in New York in 2009 with Ted Bailey and Sam Hendel. Dataminr's AI platform detects breaking events from public data (originally Twitter) in real time for corporations, newsrooms and governments; Hurun lists it at a ~$4B valuation. In 2025 it agreed to buy cyber-threat-intelligence firm ThreatConnect for $290M.
interesting_fact: Dataminr first drew wide notice when its system flagged the death of Osama bin Laden 23 minutes before major news organizations reported it.
deep_cut_fact: Dataminr's three founders (Kinsey, Ted Bailey and Sam Hendel) were Yale undergraduate roommates.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Ted Bailey is the company's public face. No published press email verified (dataminr.com was bot-blocked on direct fetch). Net worth not quantified; Hurun unicorn-founder listing only.

name: Theodore Bailey
current_role: Founder, CEO & Chairman, Dataminr (New York)
profile: Ted Bailey founded Dataminr in 2009 with Yale roommates Sam Hendel and Jeff Kinsey to detect breaking events from Twitter and other public data in real time. It grew into an AI real-time event-detection and risk platform for corporations, newsrooms and governments (valued ~$4bn), and in 2025-26 expanded into cyber defense (ThreatConnect) and large defense contracts.
interesting_fact: In August 2026 the Pentagon awarded Dataminr a $318m, five-year contract (through 2031) for AI-powered alerting from publicly available information across all US military branches and combatant commands.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his Yale BA in American Studies with a concentration on technology's impact on society, and says that academic interest was the direct inspiration for Dataminr; before founding it he worked in social-media-analytics strategy/product roles for public-sector agencies and NYC start-ups.
notes: Legal first name appears as Edward/Theodore in some databases; goes by Ted. Speaks at AI and journalism conferences (HumanX, ONA, Imagination in Action, WEF) - conference circuit is a natural route. Press email cited across 2025-26 Dataminr releases.

name: Yet-Ming Chiang
current_role: Kyocera Professor of Materials Science and Engineering, MIT; co-founder and Chief Scientist of 24M Technologies and Form Energy
profile: Taiwan-born MIT materials scientist (b. 1958), serial climate-tech founder with 100+ patents. Co-founded American Superconductor, A123 Systems (LFP batteries), 24M (semi-solid Li-ion), Form Energy (iron-air long-duration storage), Sublime Systems (electrochemical cement) and Desktop Metal; since 2023 has started more, incl. Propel Aero (electric aviation).
interesting_fact: LFP, the cathode chemistry his lab and A123 helped commercialize, has become the dominant battery chemistry in EVs and grid storage worldwide; the Boston Globe has named him a Tech Power Player in energy three times.
deep_cut_fact: He arrived at MIT as a freshman in 1976 and 'never left' (SB 1980, ScD 1985, faculty since). As a junior professor he was told to keep his startup work quiet because academic entrepreneurship wasn't well regarded. Of his work he says: 'Climate is the biggest problem that I could think of tackling with the skill set that I have.'
notes: Excellent podcast fit (batteries, long-duration storage for grid/data centers via Form Energy). Accessible academic who gives interviews (Cipher, MIT Tech Review ClimateTech). No published email confirmed; best via MIT DMSE or Form Energy/24M press teams.

name: Nigel Toon
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Partner, BlankPage Capital (deep-tech VC); stepped down as Graphcore Executive Chair on 31 Jul 2026
profile: British semiconductor entrepreneur who co-founded AI-processor maker Graphcore with Simon Knowles in 2016 (idea born 2012), raised over $600m and sold it to SoftBank in 2024; Graphcore now has ~1,000 staff. Earlier he was a founder/CEO of Icera (bought by Nvidia) and a long-time Altera executive. He now co-runs BlankPage Capital to back European deep-tech chip and AI firms.
interesting_fact: Graphcore's first chip, the Colossus MK1 - named after Bletchley Park's wartime Colossus computer - shipped to Microsoft in 2018 and, with 1,200+ cores and 23.6bn transistors, was then the world's most complex CMOS chip. His 2024 book 'How AI Thinks' (Penguin/Torva) became a Times bestseller.
deep_cut_fact: Graphcore was conceived not in a garage but over lunch at the Marlborough Tavern pub in Bath in January 2012; he and Knowles then spent 2012-14 touring the world meeting AI pioneers, many of whom became friends-and-family investors.

public_contacts.value: press@graphcore.ai (Graphcore press office; he remains a supporter 'from the sidelines')

notes: Very media-friendly and a published author - strong podcast candidate (AI chips, UK/EU sovereign compute, energy efficiency of AI). BlankPage Capital (co-founded with Ekaterina Almasque) had no verifiable website found; publisher publicity or LinkedIn are likely better routes than Graphcore now.

name: Simon Knowles
current_role: Co-founder, CTO and EVP Engineering, Graphcore (Bristol, UK; acquired by SoftBank in 2024)
profile: Simon Knowles is a Cambridge-trained British chip architect who has designed processors for over 30 years. He co-founded Element-14 (DSL chips, sold to Broadcom), Icera (cellular basebands, sold to Nvidia in 2011) and, with Nigel Toon, Graphcore, whose Colossus IPU he architected for AI workloads. He was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in 2024.
interesting_fact: Graphcore's first Colossus IPU held 24 billion transistors, a record for logic-chip complexity in 2018; its 60-billion-transistor successor (2020) was the first wafer-stacked 3D logic chip.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup, Element-14 (founded 1998), made DSL processors to bring broadband over old copper phone lines. The Royal Society says those designs still power most DSL infrastructure worldwide. He is an Engineering (EST) graduate of Churchill College, Cambridge.
notes: Strong fit for the AI/data-center theme (AI accelerator architect, three-time chip founder). Graphcore is now part of SoftBank. Best route is Graphcore press. He sits on a Royal Society Industry Fellowships panel (2026-2028).

name: Moshe Yanai
current_role: Founder and former chairman/CEO of Infinidat (stepped down as CEO 2020; Infinidat agreed to be acquired by Lenovo in 2025); storage-industry inventor
profile: Israeli electrical engineer (b. 1949, Technion 1975) and one of enterprise storage's legends: he led development of EMC's Symmetrix from the late 1980s to 2001, then founded XIV (sold to IBM in 2008 for ~$300m) and in 2011 Infinidat, which reached unicorn status after a TPG-led $150m round in 2015. He is an EMC Fellow, IBM Fellow and holds ~40 US storage patents.
interesting_fact: The Symmetrix remote replication (SRDF) his team built was called 'the true hero of 9/11' by Barron's, because it kept NYSE and bank data intact after the attacks - EMC had 25 customers in the World Trade Center.
deep_cut_fact: He is a licensed helicopter pilot - in 2010 TheMarker reported his 'new job' was flying businessmen by helicopter; he also won the 2010 IEEE Reynold B. Johnson Information Storage Systems Award.
notes: No longer runs Infinidat; no published personal contact found. Blocks and Files (Jan 2026) reported personal insolvency proceedings in Tel Aviv - Hurun 'unicorn founder' wealth is likely outdated; be sensitive. Former IDF tank commander per storage press.

name: David Elkington
current_role: Founder & CEO, Atonom (AI 'Cloud Employees' for sales, support, marketing and HR), Silicon Slopes, Utah
profile: Utah entrepreneur who founded InsideSales.com in 2004 (rebranded XANT, later back to InsideSales), an AI sales-acceleration platform that raised nearly $400M from backers incl. Salesforce and Microsoft, reached a ~$2B valuation and 1,000+ staff. He now runs Atonom, building autonomous AI agents that do full jobs, and is a co-founder of the Silicon Slopes tech community.
interesting_fact: InsideSales' 'Neuralytics' self-learning engine had analysed more than 80 billion sales interactions by 2016, the year he was named one of Utah's top 10 entrepreneurs in the Peak 100 awards.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a BA in Philosophy from BYU with minors in business, history, Japanese and Hebrew, and is also founder/CEO of Elkington Electric, building an electric vehicle called the e1 designed 'from first principles'; he spends spare time in the mountains on foot, skis and rock.
notes: Accessible, public-facing founder who keynotes Utah events (Silicon Slopes STACKED, Aug 2026); Atonom PR contact is Pete Ketchum via the EIN Presswire release form. X/LinkedIn listed are Atonom company accounts, not personal. Good AI-agents angle.

name: Ken Krogue
current_role: Co-founder, InsideSales.com (later XANT); current role not confirmed
profile: Ken Krogue co-founded InsideSales.com (later XANT) in Provo, Utah in 2004 with Dave Elkington and served as president; it became an AI sales-acceleration platform valued at about $2bn. Profiles list a later venture, Mobaliz International (2017-2020), and a board seat through 2020; nothing more recent was found.
interesting_fact: InsideSales.com, which he co-founded, was named to CNBC's 2016 Disruptor 50 list, crediting founders Dave Elkington and Ken Krogue.
deep_cut_fact: Krogue was a regular Forbes.com contributor writing on sales and lead-generation, and was billed as 'President & Co-founder' on InsideSales' own ebooks about building inside-sales teams.
notes: Public footprint goes quiet after ~2020; current activity unverified (Crunchbase/Village.ai aggregator data only). LinkedIn would be the natural channel but no verified profile URL was confirmed.

name: Rob Christensen
current_role: Unverified; profiles list a Rob Christensen as former Chief Predictive Architect at InsideSales.com and, since 2021, CTO at Destination Pet (same person not confirmed)
profile: Named by Hurun (2019-20) and some startup databases as a co-founder of InsideSales.com (Provo, Utah; later XANT), the AI sales-acceleration platform founded in 2004 and valued around $2bn at its peak. Most primary sources credit Dave Elkington and Ken Krogue as founders; Christensen appears as an early technical lead.
interesting_fact: InsideSales.com grew out of Dave Elkington's senior thesis on organising large volumes of information and became one of Utah's 'Silicon Slopes' unicorns before rebranding as XANT.
notes: Founder status only supported by Seedtable (lists founders as Elkington, Krogue, Rob Christensen, Chris Harrington). Common name; current role and wealth unverified. XANT was later broken up/sold, so the $2bn valuation is stale. Low priority.

name: Gerald Blackie
current_role: Former CEO and co-founder of Kaseya; later launched Pilixo (MSP remote-control software), reportedly in a chairman role. No current role confirmed.
profile: Gerald Blackie became CEO of Kaseya in 2003, merging in his own startup. Kaseya, founded in 2000 by Mark Sutherland and Paul Wong, created the remote-monitoring and management category for managed service providers (MSPs). Kaseya counts him as a founder. He left after Insight Venture Partners took control in June 2013 and named Yogesh Gupta CEO; he then launched Pilixo.
interesting_fact: Kaseya's own release credits Blackie, Sutherland and Wong with having 'defined the MSP IT management market'. Kaseya's VSA remote monitoring platform became core infrastructure for thousands of IT service providers, and the company later became a multi-billion-dollar business under Insight.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving Kaseya he started again: in 2013 he launched Pilixo, a remote-control tool aimed at MSPs, later taking a chairman role while a new CEO ran day-to-day operations.
notes: Sources conflict on whether he co-founded Kaseya: Wikipedia says he joined as CEO in 2003, while Kaseya calls him a founder. No current public profile, website or published contact found. ChannelE2E/Channel Futures pages could not be fetched (Cloudflare), so the Pilixo detail rests on search snippets.

name: Wang Yulin
current_role: Former founding president/CEO of Kingsoft Cloud (Nasdaq: KC; HKEX: 3896), stepped down in 2022; current role not found
profile: Wang Yulin (王育林) built Kingsoft Cloud within Lei Jun's Kingsoft group from 2012, growing it into one of China's largest independent cloud providers. As CEO he led its May 2020 Nasdaq IPO (about $510M raised). He left the CEO post and board in 2022, and vice-chairman Zou Tao succeeded him. No current public role found.
interesting_fact: He took Kingsoft Cloud public on Nasdaq in May 2020, mid-pandemic, raising about US$510M at $17 per ADS. 36Kr called it Lei Jun's fourth listed 'Kingsoft' (金山, 'gold mountain').
deep_cut_fact: Kingsoft Cloud grew out of the roughly 40-person team behind Kingsoft's Kuaipan personal cloud-drive, reaching 200 staff within about a year. In 2013 he said Kingsoft needed a new market worth at least 10bn yuan beyond games, WPS Office and antivirus, and that market was cloud.
notes: He is no longer at Kingsoft Cloud, so the IR address reaches the company, not him. He has been out of public view since 2022. Do not raise his departure circumstances. Kingsoft Cloud is now chaired by Zou Tao (Lei Jun stepped down as chairman in March 2026).

name: Paolo Cerruti
current_role: Northvolt co-founder; stepped down as CEO of Northvolt North America in Jan 2025 (stayed chairman of the Canadian entity); current main role not publicly confirmed
profile: Italian engineer-executive Paolo Cerruti co-founded Swedish battery maker Northvolt with Peter Carlsson in 2016 after four years at Tesla, serving as COO and later leading Northvolt North America and its planned Quebec gigafactory (Northvolt Six). He was also an external director of Japanese grid-battery startup PowerX until March 2026.
interesting_fact: Before Northvolt he spent about 15 years at Renault-Nissan in France, Japan and India, then ran supply chain and purchasing at Tesla (VP Global Supply Chain & Operations Planning, 2015-16) during the Gigafactory build-out.
deep_cut_fact: He served as an external director of PowerX, the Japanese startup building battery-carrying ships to move offshore wind power and rack-mounted storage for data centers, stepping down when his term ended in March 2026.
notes: Northvolt went through Chapter 11 / Swedish bankruptcy in 2024-25, so avoid framing around it; his Tesla/Renault supply-chain and gigafactory-building experience is the strong angle. No verified personal channels found. Step-down source: https://northvolt.com/articles/leadership-transition-canada/

name: Peter Carlsson
current_role: Co-founder and chairman, Aris Machina AB (agentic AI operating system for manufacturing, Sweden); former co-founder and CEO of Northvolt
profile: Swedish supply-chain executive (CPO at Sony Ericsson, NXP and Tesla) who co-founded Northvolt in 2016 to build Europe's largest lithium-ion battery factory, raising billions (Hurun valued it at ~$20B). He stepped down as CEO in Nov 2024 when Northvolt entered restructuring. In 2025 he co-founded Aris Machina with Northvolt's former AI lead Siddharth Khullar.
interesting_fact: He left Tesla at the end of 2015 as Chief Procurement Officer and Head of Supply Chain to become an entrepreneur and angel investor, then founded Northvolt in 2016 to build Europe's largest lithium-ion battery factory.
deep_cut_fact: Before Tesla he was Chief Procurement Officer at NXP (ex-Philips Semiconductors), based in Singapore and also country manager for Singapore, Malaysia and the Philippines; before that he was CPO at Sony Ericsson from 2005.
notes: Northvolt went bankrupt in Sweden (Mar 2025); handle tactfully, though he has discussed the lessons publicly (e.g. MCJ 'Inevitable' podcast). Hurun valuation figure is stale. Aris Machina's general contact is a sales inbox. A sodium-ion venture (Sonder Labs) is also linked to him in Swedish press (unverified).

name: Daisuke Okanohara
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, Preferred Networks, Inc. (since Nov 2025); CEO, Matlantis Inc.
profile: University of Tokyo computer-science PhD (2010) who co-founded Preferred Infrastructure as a grad student in 2006 and Preferred Networks (PFN) in 2014 with Toru Nishikawa. As CTO he led generative AI, the PLaMo LLM and Matlantis atomistic simulator; became CEO in Nov 2025. PFN builds the full stack from apps and models down to its own MN-Core AI chips, and agreed a capital alliance with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries in 2026.
interesting_fact: PFN designs its own AI processors: its MN-3 supercomputer, powered by the in-house MN-Core chip, topped the Green500 list of the world's most energy-efficient supercomputers three times; next-gen MN-Core L1000 targets generative-AI inference (planned 2027).
deep_cut_fact: He is a prolific author and explainer: he wrote 'Diffusion Models: The Mathematics of Data Generation' (Iwanami Shoten, Feb 2023), one of the first books worldwide on diffusion-model theory, and posts paper summaries as @hillbig, the handle on his talk slides.
notes: Excellent fit for data-center/AI-chip angle (energy-efficient AI chips, sovereign Japanese AI stack). Contact form is PFN's official Media/PR inquiry form (also handles speaker requests). Active on X (@hillbig), mostly in Japanese.

name: Toru Nishikawa
current_role: Co-Founder and Chairman, Preferred Networks Inc. (PFN), Tokyo (Daisuke Okanohara is now CEO)
profile: Toru Nishikawa co-founded Preferred Infrastructure (2006) and then Preferred Networks (2014) with Daisuke Okanohara. PFN is one of Japan's most valuable AI startups, working on deep learning, its own MN-Core AI accelerator chips and supercomputers, and LLMs (PLaMo), with partners such as Toyota, Fanuc and Mitsubishi. He led PFN as president/CEO and is now its chairman.
interesting_fact: PFN's in-house MN-3 supercomputer, built on its own MN-Core deep-learning chip co-designed with Kobe University, ranked #1 on the Green500 energy-efficiency list three times (June 2020, June 2021, Nov 2021).
deep_cut_fact: Nishikawa is a competitive programmer who reached the ICPC (International Collegiate Programming Contest) World Finals as a student. PFN recruits heavily from competitive programmers, and staff cite working alongside world-class coders as a reason they joined.
notes: PFN's contact page has a dedicated Media/PR form that covers speaker requests, which is the best route for a podcast invite. Hurun lists the company valuation at $2B. PFN's company page lists him as Co-Founder, Chairman.

name: Louay Eldada
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Quanergy Systems (stepped down Jan 2020); current role not publicly confirmed
profile: Louay Eldada, a Columbia electrical-engineering PhD, is a photonics and solar technologist. He built telecom photonics at Honeywell/AlliedSignal, founded Telephotonics (bought by DuPont), was CTO at thin-film solar maker HelioVolt and chief science officer at SunEdison, then co-founded lidar company Quanergy in 2012, which was valued around $2B. He left Quanergy in 2020.
interesting_fact: Under Eldada, Quanergy developed what its later CEO called the industry's only 100% solid-state lidar sensor, making it one of the first lidar 'unicorns' of the self-driving boom.
deep_cut_fact: Before lidar, Eldada was an energy technologist: in 2008 he joined Austin thin-film CIGS solar startup HelioVolt as CTO. By then he had published 170+ technical papers, filed 39 patents and won 43 technical awards, starting at Honeywell, where he launched the Telecom Photonics unit later acquired by Corning.
notes: Lebanese-born (per LIDAR Magazine interview with his co-founder) and speaks Arabic and French. Quanergy has since gone through bankruptcy, so avoid it as a topic in outreach. No verified personal site or social accounts found. LinkedIn would likely be the route but was not verified. Interesting angle for the podcast: solar (HelioVolt/SunEdison) plus sensing.

name: Yu Tianyue
current_role: Founder and CEO, Q3D Sensing (Silicon Valley mobile 3D reality-capture startup)
profile: Dr. Tianyue Yu co-founded lidar maker Quanergy Systems in 2012 (with Louay Eldada and Angus Pacala), serving as CTO/Chief Development Officer and leading its solid-state optical-phased-array lidar; Quanergy was once valued at ~$2B. She left in early 2023, advised Artilux, and founded Q3D Sensing, maker of AuraGO, a pocket 3D scanner that clips onto a smartphone.
interesting_fact: In 2017 CNN Money featured her among the rare women co-founders of U.S. 'unicorn' startups, for Quanergy's ~$2B valuation.
deep_cut_fact: She holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) and a Ph.D. from Cornell; in Feb 2026 she spoke at Geo Week on 'Reimagining Mapping with AI and Scalable Technologies'.
notes: info@q3dsensing.com is the company's general inbox. Avoid dwelling on Quanergy's post-SPAC outcome; frame around solid-state lidar and 3D sensing. Hurun listing reflects Quanergy's past unicorn valuation, not current net worth.

name: Sumant Sinha
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, ReNew (ReNew Energy Global plc, Nasdaq: RNW)
profile: Sumant Sinha founded ReNew in 2011 after serving as CFO of the Aditya Birla Group, founding CEO of Aditya Birla Retail and COO of Suzlon. ReNew is one of India's largest clean-energy firms (solar, wind, storage, manufacturing, green hydrogen; ~28 GW pipeline). He co-chairs the WEF Alliance of CEO Climate Leaders and is part of a take-private consortium.
interesting_fact: Named to the TIME100 Most Influential Climate Leaders (2024) and Forbes Global Sustainability Leader (2025); he formerly chaired the board of US think tank Rocky Mountain Institute (RMI) and was the first Indian business leader recognised as a UN SDG Pioneer.
deep_cut_fact: In 2025 he was elected a Fellow of the Indian National Science Academy (INSA), a rare honour for a business founder; he is also the author of 'Fossil Free', a book on India's clean-energy transition.
notes: Very media-friendly and a frequent speaker (WEF, COP, Climate Week NY); strong podcast candidate. The office email is for Mr Dinesh Kumar, Executive Secretary, Chairman's Office, as published on his own site. ReNew take-private process ongoing (Masdar-led bid withdrawn Dec 2025).

name: Bradley Keywell
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Gigawatt AI (AI-native operating system for energy and water utilities); director, TKO Group
profile: Serial Chicago founder (b. 1969): co-founded Groupon, Echo Global Logistics, MediaBank/Mediaocean and the VC firm Lightbank, then industrial-AI company Uptake (2014), which Bosch acquired in 2026. Founding investor in Tempus AI. In Aug 2025 he founded Gigawatt AI to build AI software for utilities.
interesting_fact: He was the 2019 EY World Entrepreneur of the Year, chosen from 44 country winners, and signed The Giving Pledge in 2015. He also teaches as an adjunct professor at Chicago Booth.
deep_cut_fact: He started his first business at age 7, a greeting-card company called 'Key Creations'. He met Sam Zell as a Michigan freshman and interned at Zell's Equity Group Investments; Zell mentored him for 35 years.
notes: Ideal guest: AI for utilities and grid is squarely on-topic, and he is media-friendly (has his own podcast, press kit on his site). Gigawatt AI or his website/LinkedIn is the best route. The site's /contact page currently returns 404.

name: Ji Xiaochen
current_role: Founder, CEO and legal representative, Beijing Moviebook Technology (影谱科技)
profile: Ji Xiaochen (姬晓晨) founded Moviebook in Beijing in December 2009 and is its largest shareholder, with about 43.9%. Moviebook applies AI and computer vision to video, for example inserting products and ads into existing film and TV footage. It raised several hundred-million-RMB rounds in 2019-21 (TR Capital, Yuexiu Industrial Fund and others) and was listed by Hurun as a roughly $2B unicorn in 2019-22.
interesting_fact: Moviebook's core idea is AI 'virtual product placement': using computer vision to insert brands and content into already-filmed video across the production-to-distribution chain. The World Economic Forum listed it as an AI-plus-entertainment company.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Moviebook, Ji was deputy general manager of 'The Wonder' (北京泽万达), the visual-effects production house founded by famed TV director Zhang Jizhong. There Ji gathered the film VFX and R&D talent who formed Moviebook's early team.
notes: The Zhang Jizhong/The Wonder detail comes from 36Kr's project page as surfaced by search; it was not visible in the fetched page text. I found no news on Moviebook since about 2022, so check whether the company is still active. moviebook.cn did not resolve. Search results refer to Ji as female (她). I found no verified contacts.

name: Eugenio Pace
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Auth0; retired as Okta's President, Business Operations at the end of March 2025 (no new role found)
profile: Argentine-born Eugenio Pace co-founded developer-focused identity platform Auth0 in 2013 with Matías Woloski, after more than a decade at Microsoft. He became CEO in 2017, made Auth0 an Argentine-rooted unicorn, and sold it to Okta for about $6.5B in 2021. He then served as Okta's President, Business Operations, and retired in March 2025.
interesting_fact: Outside work he rows, rides bikes and restores a 1970 Volkswagen Karmann Ghia. He has also visited more than 35 countries.
deep_cut_fact: He quit as a Principal Lead Program Manager at Microsoft to start Auth0. Six months later, in July 2013, the startup landed its first paying customer, at US$27 a month.
notes: Retired from Okta in 2025, so the corporate press route no longer applies. His X account, linked from his official Auth0 author page, is the best published channel. He blogs and has spoken publicly about company values and culture. Based near Seattle.

name: Matias Woloski
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO, Auth0; product advisor via Shipit Partners (e.g. OpenZeppelin, 2023); angel investor
profile: Argentine engineer who co-founded identity platform Auth0 in 2013 with Eugenio Pace and served as CTO. Okta bought Auth0 for $6.5B in 2021, and he then led R&D for Okta's Customer Identity Cloud. Since 2023 he has advised companies such as OpenZeppelin through Shipit Partners, and he is an angel investor.
interesting_fact: Auth0 was designed as global and remote from day one, with Pace in Seattle and Woloski in Buenos Aires. More than half its staff, mostly engineers, worked remotely, which made it a model for Argentine tech.
deep_cut_fact: He studied systems engineering at the University of Buenos Aires (UBA). He met Pace by doing consulting work for him while Pace was at Microsoft Argentina, and through Pace became a major Microsoft contractor on joint projects before the two founded Auth0.
notes: I found no published email, and could not verify his social handles from an official source (he is known as 'woloski' online). He has done Spanish-language podcasts (Startupeable) and Latitud's podcast, so he is podcast-friendly. His current full-time role after Okta is unclear.

name: Hao Fei
current_role: Co-CEO, Banma Zhixing / Banma Network Technology (Alibaba-SAIC smart-cockpit JV, Shanghai) - as of June 2025
profile: Automotive software executive and member of Banma's founding team; Banma, set up by Alibaba and SAIC around 2015, builds the AliOS-based smart-cockpit operating system and now 'Yuanshen AI' (built on Alibaba's Qwen LLM) used by 60+ automakers including VW, BMW, SAIC and FAW. He was CEO by 2019 and co-CEO in 2025 as Banma pursued a Hong Kong IPO (refiled March 2026).
interesting_fact: Banma is one of the 'Big Dipper Seven' flagship AI companies of Shanghai's Xuhui district, alongside MiniMax, SenseTime and StepFun; Hao argues intelligent driving will standardise while the AI cockpit will become ever more personalised.
deep_cut_fact: Before Banma he worked inside a carmaker, where - in his words - he was responsible for the vehicle electrical architecture, vehicle systems and software development, which is why he talks fluently about OTA security at the whole-vehicle level.
notes: The listed email is Banma's published 'market cooperation' contact (not strictly press). Leadership has shifted (Alibaba VP Dai Wei named CEO/executive director in 2025 filings) - confirm Hao Fei's current title before outreach. 'Founder' label comes from Hurun.

name: Patricia House
current_role: Cofounder of C3 AI and Siebel Systems; Chairman, Mary Mae Foundation (left the C3 AI board in Feb 2023)
profile: Pat House cofounded Siebel Systems with Tom Siebel in the 1990s, building it into a ~$2B-revenue CRM pioneer and serving as Vice Chairman and EVP until the 2006 Oracle merger. She then cofounded C3.ai (enterprise AI) and was its board Vice Chairman from 2009 until resigning in February 2023. Her wealth comes mainly from her C3 AI stake.
interesting_fact: Before Siebel she held managerial and executive roles at Verbatim, Oracle and Frame Technology. Fortune named her one of its 50 Most Powerful Women.
deep_cut_fact: She trained as a teacher, with a BA in Education from Western Michigan University, and chairs the Mary Mae Foundation, a nonprofit that provides affordable housing for teachers.
notes: Her C3 AI board resignation (Feb 24, 2023) is documented in an 8-K: https://sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1577526/000162828023006047/ai-20230224.htm. She has served on the Hewlett Foundation and Carnegie Endowment boards. No published personal or office contact found; low public profile since leaving C3.

name: Dave Baxter
current_role: Co-founder and VP Hardware Engineering, ChargePoint (per company leadership page; current status not re-verified)
profile: Dave Baxter co-founded Coulomb Technologies in 2007 in Campbell, California, alongside Richard Lowenthal, Harjinder Bhade and others; it became ChargePoint, one of the largest EV-charging networks, and went public via SPAC in 2021. He has led hardware engineering for the charging stations and is a named inventor on many Coulomb/ChargePoint patents.
interesting_fact: ChargePoint started in 2007 as Coulomb Technologies, years before mass-market EVs, betting on networked public charging stations.
deep_cut_fact: A Cornell engineering grad, before ChargePoint he was VP of Engineering at Jetstream Communications, where he led work on an early carrier-grade voice-over-DSL system, after engineering roles at 3Com and Adept Technology.
notes: Low-profile engineer co-founder; no personal socials found. Deep-cut source is Crunchbase (summarised via search, page paywalled) so verify before use. ChargePoint leadership page (https://www-aws.chargepoint.com/at-de/node/2548) lists him but is undated.

name: Harjinder S. Bhade
current_role: Chief Technology Officer, Blink Charging (Nasdaq: BLNK) (appointed April 2021; still listed on Blink's site)
profile: Silicon Valley networking engineer who co-founded Coulomb Technologies (now ChargePoint) in 2007 with Richard Lowenthal and Dave Baxter, serving as VP of Software Engineering and helping develop the IP behind networked EV charging. He then spent 6+ years as CTO/SVP Engineering at ENGIE Storage (built its GridSynergy battery-storage platform) before joining Blink as CTO.
interesting_fact: He is credited with helping create the intellectual property behind networked EV charging infrastructure at ChargePoint, now one of the world's largest charging networks.
deep_cut_fact: At ENGIE Storage (formerly Green Charge Networks) he built the GridSynergy behind-the-meter battery storage software platform from the ground up, and he is named inventor on roughly 28 US patents from his ChargePoint/Coulomb days.
notes: Patent count from patentleaderboard.com (https://www.patentleaderboard.com/chargepoint/harjinder-bhade/225012). Gave a 2024 interview to Renewable Energy World on EV charging infrastructure - useful hook. Hurun unicorn-founder listing; personal wealth not disclosed. Current 2026 role not re-confirmed via filings.

name: Milton T. Tormey
current_role: Co-founder of ChargePoint (founded 2007 as Coulomb Technologies); current role not publicly documented
profile: Milton 'Tom' Tormey is one of five co-founders (with Richard Lowenthal, Harjinder Bhade, Praveen Mandal and Dave Baxter) of Coulomb Technologies, launched in 2007 in Campbell, California, to build networked EV charging before many EVs were on the road. Renamed ChargePoint, it became one of the largest EV charging networks and went public via SPAC in 2021.
interesting_fact: Stanford GSB's ChargePoint case credits the five founders with seeing the need for an expansive charging network 'even before many electric vehicles were on the road'; early backers included Voyager Capital and Rho Ventures.
deep_cut_fact: He is a named inventor on ChargePoint's networked-charging patents, including 'Authorization in a networked electric vehicle charging system' (US 12,068,620, issued Aug 2024), and an early Coulomb patent on a self-powered charging-connector locking system.
notes: Lesser-known co-founder (Wikipedia lists only three founders). Very low public profile; no interviews, website or social accounts found. ChargePoint's public face is co-founder Richard Lowenthal.

name: Praveen Mandal
profile: Listed by Hurun's Global Unicorn founders lists (2019-2020) as a founder of EV-charging network ChargePoint (founded 2007 as Coulomb Technologies, Campbell, CA; NYSE: CHPT since 2021). Wikipedia names the founders as Richard Lowenthal, Dave Baxter and Harjinder Bhade, so his founding role and current position could not be confirmed.
notes: Low public footprint; not named as a founder in ChargePoint's Wikipedia entry (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChargePoint) or on its current about page. Web search budget was exhausted before further verification; treat Hurun attribution as unconfirmed. Likely no longer at ChargePoint.

name: Richard Lowenthal
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of ChargePoint (founded as Coulomb Technologies); former ChargePoint director - current role not verified
profile: Co-founded Coulomb Technologies in 2007 with Dave Baxter and Harjinder Bhade and led it as CEO; Coulomb's 'ChargePoint Network' of smart public charging stations became ChargePoint, one of the largest EV-charging networks, which went public via SPAC in 2021 (NYSE: CHPT). He remained on the board and as a shareholder through the 2021 listing.
interesting_fact: In 2010, as Coulomb's CEO, he won a federal stimulus-backed program to give away free home and public chargers - about 11,200 across nine U.S. regions - to seed EV adoption.
deep_cut_fact: Coulomb's very first chargers (July 2008, from an office in Campbell, CA) were called 'Smartlets' and used 802.15.4 mesh wireless; his launch pitch was that the U.S. had 247M cars but only 54M garages, so most drivers would need public charging.
notes: No longer appears to be a ChargePoint officer/director, so the company press team is an indirect route; I couldn't verify a personal site or social accounts (web-search quota exhausted). He is widely reported to be a former Cupertino mayor, but I couldn't source it. Good EV-infrastructure/grid founder story.

name: Lee Holloway
current_role: Cloudflare cofounder and original lead engineer; no longer with the company (left in 2015)
profile: Lee Holloway cofounded Cloudflare on July 26, 2009 with Matthew Prince and Michelle Zatlyn and was its original technical lead, building much of the early network that became one of the internet's largest edge/CDN and security platforms (NYSE: NET, IPO 2019). He stepped away from the company in 2015.
interesting_fact: Before Cloudflare, Holloway and Matthew Prince collaborated on Project Honey Pot, an anti-spam effort by Unspam Technologies that partly inspired the idea for Cloudflare.
notes: Do not approach: he left Cloudflare in 2015 because of a serious illness that was widely reported (Wired, 2020) and is not a viable interview subject; current status not verified. For the Cloudflare story, approach Matthew Prince or Michelle Zatlyn instead.

name: Kris Gale
current_role: Co-founder of Clover Health (left the company in 2017); current role not verified
profile: Kris Gale co-founded Clover Health, a data- and software-driven Medicare Advantage insurer, with Vivek Garipalli in 2014, leading its technology side. He left in 2017; Clover later went public via a SPAC in 2021.
interesting_fact: Clover's pitch was to use data analytics and software to spot health risks early and cut costs for Medicare Advantage members, including a home-based primary-care program for homebound members launched in 2017.
notes: Left Clover nearly a decade ago; no verified current role, website or social accounts found, and the web search budget ran out before more could be checked. 'Artificial Intelligence' industry tag is loose (health-insurance tech). Low priority for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Vivek Garipalli
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairperson, Clover Health (Nasdaq: CLOV); runs family-office investment arm Wormhole Capital
profile: Vivek Garipalli (47) co-founded Medicare Advantage insurer Clover Health in 2014 and was CEO until Dec 2022, taking it public via SPAC in 2021; he has been Executive Chair since Jan 2023. Earlier he co-founded New Jersey hospital system CarePoint Health and Ensemble Health, and after finance roles at CSFB, J.P. Morgan Partners and Blackstone became an early backer of Flatiron Health.
interesting_fact: Clover pitches itself as a tech company first: its in-house clinical software gives doctors data-driven prompts at the point of care, e.g. for earlier detection of diabetes and chronic kidney disease.
deep_cut_fact: He was an early investor in Flatiron Health, advised on its business model, led its acquisition of the Altos data platform and sat on its board from 2012 until Roche bought it in 2018; he holds a BBA in entrepreneurship from Emory.
notes: Input tag 'Artificial Intelligence' reflects Clover's AI-assisted care software; weak fit for an energy/data-centre podcast unless angled on healthcare AI. Route via Clover press inbox.

name: Jeremy Achin
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO, DataRobot (Boston); current role not verified
profile: Jeremy Achin co-founded Boston-based DataRobot in 2012 with Tom de Godoy; both came from insurance-industry predictive modelling. He led the company as CEO as it built an automated machine-learning ('AutoML') platform and reached a ~$6B valuation (Hurun unicorn list 2019-2024), before Dan Wright took over as CEO around 2020. He no longer appears on DataRobot's site.
notes: Thin record: web-search quota ran out mid-lane and DataRobot's site has no founder bio, so the profile rests on the lane data plus well-known company history and should be checked before use. No published contact found; he keeps a low public profile since leaving DataRobot. Avoid the 2022 DataRobot executive share-sale controversy as an outreach topic.

name: Thomas DeGodoy
current_role: Co-founder, DataRobot (Boston enterprise AI platform, founded 2012); current role not verified
profile: Hurun's Global Unicorn Index (2019-2025) lists Thomas (Tom) DeGodoy as the founder of DataRobot, the Boston-based enterprise AI/AutoML company valued at about US$6.3B. DataRobot, founded in 2012, pioneered automated machine learning and MLOps and now sells an agentic-AI platform to regulated enterprises. His current involvement with the company could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: DataRobot, which he co-founded in 2012, pioneered AutoML (automated machine learning) and MLOps before pivoting to a platform for building and governing agentic AI at enterprise scale.
notes: Web-search quota ran out and DataRobot's site no longer lists founders, so his bio/current role are unverified; widely reported (not checked here) as co-founder alongside Jeremy Achin. Not on DataRobot's current leadership pages. Verify via LinkedIn before outreach; data-center angle is weak (AI software).

name: Solomon Hykes
current_role: Co-founder of Dagger (dagger.io), a programmable CI/CD and AI-agent workflow engine; Docker founder
profile: New York-born, France-raised engineer (b. 1983) who co-founded dotCloud in Paris in 2008, went through Y Combinator in 2010, and open-sourced Docker in 2013, popularising Linux containers that now underpin cloud and data-center software. He left Docker's CTO role in 2018 and launched Dagger in 2022.
interesting_fact: Docker was first shown publicly in a roughly five-minute lightning talk, 'The future of Linux Containers', at PyCon 2013 in Santa Clara, and was open-sourced that same month.
deep_cut_fact: He moved to France at age 4, entered the Epitech coding school in 2001, started his career in 2006 at an IT-security firm, and in 2008 set up dotCloud as a small SARL in Montrouge with fellow Epitech alum Sébastien Pahl. His story was cited around François Hollande's 2014 Silicon Valley 'brain drain' visit.
notes: Approachable, active in open-source communities and on conference stages (KubeCon keynote, Dagger blog demos). His personal X handle is widely known as @solomonstre but I could not verify it from an official page here; company X/Discord are verified. Docker 'valued $2B' refers to Hurun unicorn list.

name: Wu Jingzhuan
current_role: CEO (co-founder), Dtdream / Hangzhou Dtdream Technology (数梦工场), per 36Kr company profile; current status not re-confirmed
profile: Wu Jingchuan (吴敬传; Hurun romanises as 'Wu Jingzhuan') is a veteran Chinese networking executive: ~7 years at Huawei, then a founding executive of H3C, where she became CEO in 2012 before leaving in Feb 2015. She is listed as CEO of Dtdream, the Hangzhou digital-government cloud/data platform company set up in 2015 by ex-H3C staff with Alibaba ties.
interesting_fact: Dtdream was founded in March 2015 in Hangzhou's Yunqi (Cloud Town) by a team of ex-H3C executives led by Wang Wei, shortly after the H3C leadership exodus; it focuses on 'digital government' platforms, e.g. Zhejiang's 'run at most once' reform.
deep_cut_fact: In China's IT industry she was nicknamed the 'Iron Lady' (铁娘子); before taking over as H3C CEO from Zheng Shusheng in 2012 she ran H3C's global marketing, sales and channels, and at Huawei had been VP of domestic marketing and head of datacom marketing.
notes: Chinese name 吴敬传 (Wu Jingchuan). 36Kr PitchHub (https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1678465091859458) lists her as Dtdream CEO and Wang Wei (王巍) as founder; no 2024-26 news found confirming she is still CEO. dtdream.com was unreachable from this session, so no published press contact captured. Low public profile; approach via Dtdream corporate channels.

name: Zhai Xuehun
current_role: Founder & CEO, G7 E6 (G7易流; formed from the 2022 merger of G7 and E6/易流), Beijing
profile: Zhai Xuehun (翟学魂), a Tsinghua physics graduate, founded G7 around 2010 to put IoT devices and a SaaS platform into Chinese truck fleets; by 2018 it had raised 500M+ USD and connected 800k+ vehicles. After merging with E6 it became G7易流, a digital-logistics/IoT platform serving tens of thousands of SME carriers, now pushing hard into logistics AI.
interesting_fact: In April 2018 G7 co-founded an autonomous-trucking company together with NIO Capital and GLP (Inceptio Technology), as Zhai pursued his vision of logistics becoming a self-operating, algorithm-driven industry.
deep_cut_fact: Despite running a 'dirty, hard work' logistics business, he studied physics at Tsinghua and has said he still regrets not pursuing theoretical physics; on stage he introduces himself simply as 'G7's Lao Zhai' (老翟). In 2017 he set a target of one logistics manager per 50 trucks, vs. the industry's 1:5.
notes: Chinese name 翟学魂. Frequently speaks at TMTPost ITValue / T-EDGE and G7's annual Digital Logistics Conference (2025 launch of logistics AI hardware; 2026 talk on token usage) - conference/media route is the most realistic. g7.com.cn was unreachable from this session so no published press email captured. 36Kr interview: https://www.36kr.com/p/1721664929793

name: Kathryn Petralia
current_role: Board director and fintech investor (boards: PadSplit, Cloverly, Castle Creek Capital, Woodruff Arts Center); 'Scaling Outcomes' at QMD Scientific; co-founder and former President of Kabbage
profile: Atlanta-based fintech entrepreneur who co-founded Kabbage in 2008 with Rob Frohwein and Marc Gorlin; its data-driven automated lending served ~500,000 small businesses, reached a $1.2B valuation in 2017 and was acquired by American Express in 2020. She now serves on several boards and invests in fintech and climate-related startups.
interesting_fact: Forbes ranked her the 98th most powerful woman in the world in 2017; Kabbage originated over $16B in small-business working capital, often funding loans in minutes.
deep_cut_fact: An English-literature major at Furman who got hooked on tech after her parents gave her a TRS-80 computer at age nine; before Kabbage she co-founded WorthKnowing.com, which let consumers see their credit scores before bureaus were required to provide them (sold to CompuCredit and TransUnion).
notes: Her personal site says to make inquiries via LinkedIn - best route. Frequent podcast guest (e.g. Altar.io, Regulation Innovation). Note: Kabbage's non-acquired remnant (K Servicing) went through a 2022 bankruptcy related to PPP loans - avoid in outreach. Fit is fintech/AI more than energy.

name: Marc Gorlin
current_role: Founder and CEO, Roadie (crowdsourced same-day delivery, a UPS company since 2021) - latest confirmed 2022
profile: Atlanta serial entrepreneur (five startups) and UGA journalism graduate (ABJ '95). He co-founded small-business lender Kabbage in 2009 with Rob Frohwein and Kathryn Petralia (sold to American Express in 2020), then founded Roadie in 2014, which matches shippers with drivers already heading their way. UPS, an early investor, acquired Roadie in 2021 and he kept running it.
interesting_fact: Roadie's pitch: 250 million U.S. passenger vehicles hit the road daily with almost 4 billion cubic feet of empty space - more capacity than UPS, FedEx, the Post Office and all couriers combined. EY named him a 2021 Entrepreneur of the Year.
deep_cut_fact: When Roadie partnered with Waffle House as 24-hour drop-off points in 2015, a tired Gorlin ad-libbed to a reporter that in the South 'you can't throw a dead cat without hitting a Waffle House' - the line reached Jimmy Kimmel, who ran a segment on Roadie. He credits Grady professor Conrad Fink for his storytelling.
notes: Natural storyteller who enjoys press and podcasts (e.g., This Is Capitalism ep. 002). Current role after 2022 not re-verified. Avoid Kabbage's post-sale K Servicing/PPP bankruptcy topic. No press email found on roadie.com.

name: Rob Frohwein
current_role: Founder building Quest (collect.quest, a card-collecting app) and author of The Expert Novice Substack; co-founder and former CEO/Chair of Kabbage
profile: Atlanta lawyer-turned-entrepreneur who co-founded Kabbage in 2008 to automate small-business lending using real-time transaction data via APIs; it served ~500,000 businesses, originated $16bn+, hit a $1.2bn valuation (2017) and was acquired by American Express in 2020. He then co-founded Keep Financial (sold 2025) and now builds Quest while writing about building with AI.
interesting_fact: He is the named inventor on 25 U.S. patents, spanning automated lending, ML classification, optical transaction verification and even conferencing technology.
deep_cut_fact: Before Kabbage he wrote three books in Penguin/Putnam's 'Pocket Idiot's Guide' series - to Patents, Trademarks and Copyrights (2004) - and earlier was VP Business Development and General Counsel at Security First Network Bank, the world's first internet bank. He also holds a lifetime donor pass to the Baseball Hall of Fame.
notes: Very reachable: his site says 'For inquiries, connect via LinkedIn'. Natural AI/data angle (writes about building with AI as a non-expert). Kabbage itself is not a data-center company, so pitch around AI/fintech entrepreneurship.

name: Liu Ye
current_role: Legal representative, China Fusion Energy Co. (中国聚变能源有限公司, 'CFEC', Shanghai, CNNC subsidiary); Party Secretary, CNNC Southwestern Institute of Physics (SWIP)
profile: Liu Ye (刘叶) is a CNNC (China National Nuclear Corp.) executive, not a private founder: he is legal representative of China Fusion Energy Co., the state fusion-power company launched in Shanghai in July 2025 with RMB 15B registered capital, and Party Secretary of SWIP in Chengdu, China's oldest magnetic-confinement fusion institute. Hurun lists him against CFEC on its 2026 unicorn index.
interesting_fact: CNNC paid for its stake in China Fusion Energy partly in intellectual property (valued at nearly RMB 3B), believed to come from SWIP's fusion team, whose HL-3 tokamak hit 117M-degree ion and 160M-degree electron temperatures in 2025; PetroChina Kunlun Capital and Zhejiang Energy are co-investors.
notes: Chinese name 刘叶. Matched via Hurun 2026 Global Unicorn Index (刘叶 / 聚变能源 CFEC / Shanghai, New Energy, US$2.2B). He holds the role as a state-enterprise appointee, so he has no personal wealth from it; outreach would go through CNNC / China Fusion Energy official channels. The '2019-2026' Hurun span in the input is odd since CFEC was only renamed and launched in 2025; the earlier years may be a different Liu Ye merged on name. Day-to-day GM is Zhang Libo (张立波). No personal bio found.

name: Amit Goldstein
current_role: Co-founder, Lightricks (current role unverified - not listed in Lightricks' current founders & management page)
profile: Amit Goldstein is one of five Hebrew University PhD students who founded Lightricks in 2013 (maker of Facetune, Photoleap, Videoleap). Lightricks was valued at $1.8B in 2021 and has pivoted to generative AI with its open-source LTX video models, now being spun out as a separate company.
interesting_fact: Lightricks bootstrapped its early growth - the subject of a Harvard Business School case study, 'Bootstrapping at Lightricks' - and Facetune became Apple's most downloaded paid app of 2017.
notes: Low-profile co-founder; no personal public channels found and the web-search budget ran out before his current activity could be checked. He does not appear on Lightricks' current management page, so he may have stepped back from operations. Company press email is a weak route; LTX (AI video models, GPU-heavy) is the data-center-relevant angle.

name: Itai Tsiddon
current_role: Co-founder, Lightricks (Jerusalem); current operating title not verified
profile: Itai Tsiddon co-founded Lightricks in January 2013 with four Hebrew University PhD students. The company built Facetune (200M+ downloads) and other creator apps, was valued at about $1.8B in 2021, and has pivoted toward generative video with LTX Studio and the open-source LTX Video model.
interesting_fact: Lightricks' Facetune was Apple's most-downloaded paid app of 2017; the company later released LTX Video, an open-source text/image-to-video model, as it moved into generative AI.

notes: Zeev Farbman (CEO) is Lightricks' public face; Tsiddon keeps a low profile. Verify his current role before outreach (shared web-search budget exhausted).

name: Nir Pochter
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Marketing Officer, Lightricks (Jerusalem)
profile: One of five Hebrew University PhD-student co-founders of Lightricks (2013), maker of Facetune, Photoleap and Videoleap and now the LTX Studio / LTX Video generative-AI video models. Bootstrapped at first (subject of a Harvard Business School case), the company raised $335M and was valued at $1.8B in 2021; it reached ~$250M ARR by mid-2025. He leads its marketing.
interesting_fact: Facetune, launched in March 2013, was Apple's most downloaded paid app of 2017 and has been downloaded over 200 million times; Lightricks' marketing under Pochter has been showcased by Meta and Instagram as case studies.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a Master's in artificial intelligence from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and his company bio lists his hobbies as Brazilian jiu-jitsu and gardening - and says he'd spend more free time playing computer games.
notes: Generative-AI video angle (open LTX Video models). CEO Zeev Farbman is the usual public spokesperson; route via press@lightricks.com. No personal verified accounts confirmed.

name: Yaron Inger
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Lightricks (Jerusalem)
profile: Yaron Inger cofounded Lightricks in 2013 with four fellow Hebrew University PhD students/alumni; the company built Facetune (200M+ downloads), Videoleap and Photoleap and was valued at $1.8B in 2021. As CTO he now leads its pivot to generative video: the LTX Studio platform and the open-source LTX Video / LTX-2 models, including work with Nvidia.

notes: Quoted in Lightricks' LTX product announcements - an accessible technical founder for an AI/compute episode (GPU-heavy video models). Route via press@lightricks.com.

name: Zeev Farbman
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Lightricks (Jerusalem)
profile: Ukrainian-born Israeli computer-graphics PhD (Hebrew University) who co-founded Lightricks in 2013 with four fellow students; it built hit photo app Facetune and was valued at $1.8B in 2021. Under Farbman it has pivoted toward generative AI with LTX Studio and its open-weights LTX Video text-to-video models; he was named to the 2026 ADWEEK Innovator 50.

notes: Lightricks' open-source LTX video models make GPU compute a natural podcast angle. Company contact email is the only published one; his own social accounts were not verified.

name: John Hering
current_role: Co-Founder, Coalition (cyber insurance); Founding Partner, Vy Capital
profile: Serial security entrepreneur who co-founded mobile-security company Lookout (protecting 100M+ users) and then co-founded Coalition, the 'active insurance' cyber-insurer valued around $5B. He is also a founding partner of Vy Capital, a technology investor with more than $7.5B under management.

notes: Hurun industry/focus tag 'energy' looks wrong - he is a cybersecurity/insurtech founder. Best route is Coalition press or via Vy Capital. Personal social accounts not verified (search budget exhausted).

name: Thomas Rebaud
current_role: Co-founder of Meero (now Diffusely), Paris; current role not verified (company now led by Gaetan Rougevin-Baville)
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Meero in 2014 with Guillaume Lestrade, a platform linking businesses with freelance photographers plus AI-powered photo post-processing. Meero's June 2019 EUR205M round was then a French Tech record and made it a unicorn. After COVID hit, the marketplace shut in February 2023 and the company was rebranded Diffusely, an AI visual-content software firm.

The 'AI' tag reflects automated photo editing, not data centers.

name: Xiao Diaokun
current_role: Early executive / COO and key shareholder, Microvast (NASDAQ: MVST; China arm Microvast Power Systems, Huzhou) - current title not re-confirmed after 2022
profile: Diaokun 'Jack' Xiao is a long-serving Microvast executive, listed as COO since the company's 2006 start and named among the 'Key Company Holders' (with founder-CEO Yang Wu) who backed Microvast's 2021 SPAC merger with Tuscan Holdings. Microvast makes fast-charging lithium-ion battery systems for commercial vehicles and energy storage, with its main plant in Huzhou, Zhejiang.

Chinese characters for his name not confirmed (some pages render 'Xiao Kun'). He does not appear in 2023+ EDGAR full-text results, so his current role is unverified. Approach via Microvast media contact.

name: Wu Minghui
current_role: Founder, CEO and CTO, Mininglamp Technology (明略科技), Beijing
profile: A serial founder with math, software and electronics degrees (BA to PhD) from Peking University, Wu founded marketing-data platform Miaozhen Systems in 2006, Mininglamp Data in 2014 and Mininglamp Technology Group in 2019, which sells enterprise AI and data-intelligence software (knowledge graphs, marketing analytics, on-device agent models).

He also won an outstanding master's thesis award at Peking University's AI Lab.

name: Li Zhifei
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Mobvoi (出门问问; HKEX: 2438)
profile: Li Zhifei is a speech/NLP scientist with a Johns Hopkins PhD who worked at Google on machine translation before founding Mobvoi in Beijing in Oct 2012. Mobvoi started with Chinese voice search (first inside WeChat), then made TicWatch smartwatches with Google, and now sells generative-AI products such as AI voice/dubbing (Moyin) and AIGC tools. It listed in Hong Kong in 2024.
interesting_fact: Google invested in Mobvoi in 2015 and partnered with it to bring Wear OS to China; Mobvoi's TicWatch S/E Kickstarter raised over $3M from 19,000+ backers.
deep_cut_fact: As a Johns Hopkins PhD student he was lead author of 'Joshua: An Open Source Toolkit for Parsing-Based Machine Translation' (WMT 2009, with Chris Callison-Burch, Chris Dyer, Sanjeev Khudanpur and others), a widely used open-source statistical MT system.
notes: Active public speaker in China on AI and LLMs; good AI-founder guest. No published personal or press email found; Mobvoi annual report (HKEX) has the IR details but its Chinese text could not be extracted. Route via Mobvoi IR/communications.

name: Cao Xudong
current_role: Founder and CEO, Momenta Global Ltd (SEHK: 6880), Beijing/Suzhou
profile: Cao Xudong is a computer-vision researcher who left Microsoft Research and SenseTime (where he was executive director of R&D) to found Momenta in September 2016. Momenta sells intelligent-driving software to automakers including Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Toyota, GM, SAIC, Nissan and Honda, runs robotaxi programmes with Uber and Grab, and listed in Hong Kong on 8 July 2026, raising ~HK$5.89bn.
interesting_fact: Daimler's 2017 investment in Momenta was the German automaker's first-ever investment in a Chinese startup; in 2021 Momenta became China's first self-driving unicorn, and by 2025 its driver-assist stack was going into BMW's entire new China lineup.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Momenta, Cao was a research scientist at Microsoft Research and then executive director of R&D at SenseTime - one of the few Chinese AV founders to come straight out of deep-learning computer-vision research rather than the auto industry.
notes: Hurun listed him as a unicorn founder; Momenta is now listed (HK, July 2026), so his stake is now publicly valued. contact@momenta.ai is the general company inbox (shown alongside its Abu Dhabi office). For press, check Momenta's HKEX filings for an IR contact.

name: Kabir Barday
current_role: Founder & Board Member, OneTrust (Atlanta); stepped down as CEO in February 2026
profile: Founded OneTrust in Atlanta in 2016 to help companies comply with new privacy laws such as GDPR and CCPA. He grew it into a large privacy, security and AI-governance software company with more than 14,000 customers and over 300 patents. In February 2026 he handed the CEO role to John Heyman and stayed on the board in a strategic-advisory role.

No sourced personal background found because the web-search budget ran out; check pre-OneTrust history (often reported as AirWatch/VMware) before using it. The Hurun valuation tag ($4B) is dated.

name: Yang Sinan
current_role: Founder, CEO & CTO, ProLogium Technology (Taoyuan, Taiwan)
profile: Vincent Yang (Yang Sinan/楊思枬) founded ProLogium in 2006 to develop solid-state/lithium-ceramic batteries; it runs a GWh-class gigafactory in Taoyuan, has shipped 800,000+ cells, and opened an R&D centre in Paris-Saclay in 2024. name: Alex Timm
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Director, Root, Inc. (Nasdaq: ROOT), Columbus, Ohio
profile: Alex Timm, a credentialed actuary, co-founded Root in March 2015 after working at Nationwide (2011-15), on the idea that car-insurance rates should rest on how people actually drive, measured by smartphone telematics, rather than demographics. Root went public in 2020 (Ohio's largest IPO, after a $3.65B private valuation) and is now pushing embedded insurance sold through partners' checkouts.
interesting_fact: Root says it has gathered ~20 billion miles of smartphone telematics driving data to price policies, and was the first U.S. licensed insurance carrier run entirely on mobile.
deep_cut_fact: Timm triple-majored at Drake University (actuarial science, accounting and mathematics), is a Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society, and is a 2023 Aspen Institute Henry Crown Fellow.
notes: Hurun's $4B figure is Root's former valuation, not his net worth. Classified as AI because of Root's ML pricing; topic fit for an energy/data-center podcast is weaker (telematics/data-science angle). Root has a Chief Communications Officer (Kelly Ruoff) - press@ is the route.

He left Root around 2021 and founded RWX, a cloud platform where engineers and AI coding agents build, test and validate software, with fast reproducible environments, flaky-test quarantine and parallelized CI.
interesting_fact: He has been CTO at two big exits back to back: Braintree, acquired by PayPal in 2013 (the deal that brought Venmo to PayPal), and Root, which IPO'd in 2020 at a multibillion-dollar valuation.

name: Alex Jacobs

Sila makes silicon-based anode materials (Titan Silicon) that replace graphite to boost lithium-ion energy density, and is scaling production at a plant in Moses Lake, Washington.

current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Sila Nanotechnologies (Alameda, CA; Moses Lake, WA plant).
profile: Ukrainian-born Stanford engineer (BS ME, MS Eng) who was Tesla's seventh employee and principal engineer on the Roadster battery. He cofounded Sila in 2011 to replace graphite anodes with Titan Silicon, now made at its Moses Lake, Washington plant for EVs, devices, aerospace and data-center/robotics batteries.

As a Stanford freshman he joined the solar-car team, helping build an all-carbon-fibre chassis for a 4,000 km Chicago-to-LA race car; he later designed his own energy-engineering master's curriculum.

name: Gleb Yushin
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Sila Nanotechnologies; Professor, School of Materials Science & Engineering, Georgia Tech; co-Editor-in-Chief, Materials Today
profile: Materials scientist who co-founded Sila Nanotechnologies in 2011 with Gene Berdichevsky and Alex Jacobs, spinning out his Georgia Tech work on silicon-carbon anodes. Sila's Titan Silicon anode replaces graphite to raise battery energy density for EVs, devices and data centers; valued at $3.3bn+ in 2021, it is scaling a plant in Moses Lake, WA.

notes: Accessible academic; Georgia Tech email is the most direct published route, but for Sila-related podcast requests go via Sutherland Gold.

name: James Hom
current_role: Co-Founder, Chief Product Officer and Interim CFO, SoundHound AI (Nasdaq: SOUN)

As CPO he leads product development for the SoundHound AI platform, SoundHound services and consumer apps reaching hundreds of millions of users; the company listed via SPAC in 2022.

name: Keyvan Mohajer
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, SoundHound AI (Nasdaq: SOUN)
profile: Iranian-born, Canada-raised engineer with a Stanford PhD in electrical engineering who co-founded SoundHound in 2005 from his Stanford dorm. Known first for its music-recognition app, SoundHound now sells voice and agentic AI to carmakers, restaurants (e.g. Five Guys), insurers and telcos, and went public via SPAC in 2022.

notes: Frequent podcast guest (Voicebot, Fox News Radio, Stratospheric Leaders), so receptive to audio interviews. PR email appears in 2026 press releases (IR site blocked direct fetch here; confirmed via search snippet). Edge-AI/on-device angle (NVIDIA GTC 2026).

name: Majid Emami
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Science Officer and SVP Engineering, SoundHound AI (Nasdaq: SOUN)
profile: Majid Emami co-founded SoundHound in 2005 with Keyvan Mohajer and James Hom; the three met in Stanford's electrical-engineering PhD programme. He was VP of Engineering from the founding and became Chief Science Officer and SVP Engineering in 2022. SoundHound, known for its music-recognition app and the Houndify voice-AI platform, now sells voice and agentic AI to carmakers, restaurants and enterprises.

deep_cut_fact: He holds a Stanford PhD in electrical engineering and is named on 16 patents in voice AI, per SoundHound's investor-relations biography.
notes: A technical, low-profile co-founder; CEO Keyvan Mohajer is the public face. Some sources say his undergraduate degree is from the University of Toronto, but I couldn't verify this. The Hurun listing is as a unicorn founder; SoundHound is now public. A good angle is on-device and edge voice AI versus data-centre inference.

name: Cristina Fonseca
current_role: Co-founder of Talkdesk (left operations 2016); last confirmed role Head of AI at Zendesk (2023); also linked to Lisbon VC Indico Capital Partners (venture partner from 2018)

name: Tiago Paiva
current_role: Founder & CEO, Talkdesk (AI-powered cloud contact-center software, San Francisco/Lisbon)
profile: Portuguese engineer who built the first Talkdesk prototype in 10 days in 2011 for a Twilio hackathon, won TwilioCon, joined 500 Startups' third batch and moved to the US. He grew Talkdesk into a contact-center-as-a-service leader valued at $10B in 2021, now centred on AI agents for customer service, and remains CEO.
interesting_fact: He entered Twilio's 2011 contest because, aged 24 with an old PC and no money, he wanted the MacBook Air prize. He won it, then won TwilioCon's $10,000 first prize, which started Talkdesk.

With no passport, he fast-tracked one and flew to San Francisco Monday night. Earlier he had a part-time job at Procter & Gamble, which convinced him he 'wasn't built for the 9-5 life.'
notes: Accessible, story-friendly founder with frequent interviews (SaaStr, CEO Magazine). Talkdesk has had layoffs and valuation pressure since 2022, so avoid valuation talk. The $10B figure is the 2021 Series D valuation. Strong AI angle (agentic customer service).

profile: IIT Kharagpur/Stony Brook-trained engineer who worked at VMware and Google (2007-12), then co-founded ThoughtSpot (search/AI analytics, valued ~$4B) as VP Engineering. He then co-founded NetSpring (warehouse-native analytics, acquired by Optimizely 2024) and reportedly now leads compute-platform engineering at Databricks.

current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, ThoughtSpot
profile: Serial enterprise-software founder. He co-founded Nutanix as Chief Products Officer (its 2016 IPO was the largest tech IPO that year), then co-founded ThoughtSpot in 2012. ThoughtSpot pioneered search-based analytics and has since moved into AI agents for data analysis (Spotter, AgentSpot). He moved from CEO to executive chairman and remains its public face on AI analytics.

profile: IIT Kanpur (B.Tech) and Stanford (MS CS) engineer who worked on search and ads technology at Google before co-founding search-driven analytics company ThoughtSpot in 2012 (valued ~$4B). current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Revefi (AI data-operations / data observability startup, founded 2021)

current_role: Cofounder and CTO, Revefi (AI/data FinOps and observability); cofounder of ThoughtSpot
profile: IIT Delhi / UT Austin-educated engineer who cofounded search-driven analytics firm ThoughtSpot in 2012, building its search engine and leading engineering for three years. After leading data quality for Meta's exabyte-scale warehouse, he cofounded Revefi in 2021 with ThoughtSpot cofounder Sanjay Agrawal to cut AI and cloud-data spend.
interesting_fact: Revefi's RADEN agent targets AI/data cost control across Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery and LLM apps; in Nov 2026 it launched closed-loop 'AI FinOps' to budget and enforce enterprise AI spend.
