deep_cut_fact: While working on an EdTech startup venture, he went back to school for a master's degree in education to understand learners from the inside; earlier he worked on distributed systems and search at Amazon and Yahoo.
notes: Revefi media contact is Girish Bhat (published on press releases). Revefi runs its own 'Deep Dive' podcast. Good AI-cost/compute-efficiency angle.

name: Vijay Ganesan
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of NetSpring (acquired by Optimizely, 2024); now leads NetSpring analytics within Optimizely (exact current title unverified)
profile: Vijay Ganesan, an IIT Madras graduate, co-founded AI-search analytics firm ThoughtSpot (2012; valued at about $4.2bn) and led product there until 2019. He then co-founded NetSpring, a warehouse-native analytics platform, which Optimizely acquired in late 2024. He now works on bringing that analytics across Optimizely One.
interesting_fact: Before founding companies he spent eight years at Oracle as technical lead for its flagship business-intelligence product. He has now built two analytics startups on that foundation: ThoughtSpot and NetSpring.
deep_cut_fact: NetSpring was built on his thesis that 'event data' from sensors, devices, phones and product instrumentation was outgrowing traditional reporting tools. Its answer was analytics that sit directly on the customer's data warehouse rather than copying data out. Dell Technologies Capital backed it at seed and led its Series A.
notes: The press contact is Optimizely's VP of Global Communications as listed on the 2024 NetSpring acquisition release, so it may be outdated. He appears on marketing and analytics podcasts (e.g. Agile Brand), so he is open to podcast appearances. Not a billionaire; the Hurun unicorn-founder listing relates to ThoughtSpot.

name: Hao Jianan
current_role: Co-founder, COO & Director, CreateAI Holdings (formerly TuSimple; OTC: TSPH); legal representative of Beijing TuSimple
profile: NTU PhD in parallel/distributed systems and ex-Temasek Labs researcher who cofounded autonomous-trucking firm TuSimple in 2015 as COO, running its China engineering. After TuSimple froze US operations and delisted, it rebranded in Dec 2024 as CreateAI, pivoting to generative AI for games and animation.
interesting_fact: CreateAI open-sourced its 'Ruyi' image-to-video model (Ruyi-Mini-7B, a DiT model trained on ~200M clips) on Hugging Face and licensed Jin Yong's martial-arts IP and The Three-Body Problem for AI-made games and animation.
deep_cut_fact: Before TuSimple he was a supercomputing researcher: in 2007 he designed a parallel pi-calculation system that broke the world record for computing digits of pi.
notes: Sensitive context: TuSimple co-founder disputes and a 2025 report on data transfers to China (TechCrunch); avoid. COO/director role per https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/tsph/company. No working CreateAI/TuSimple press or IR email found (ir.tusimple.com returns 403; createai.com unreachable from here). The pi record claim comes from the company's own 36Kr team bio.

name: Sebastian Thrun
current_role: Co-founder, Cresta (AI for contact centers); founder, Sage AI Labs; adjunct professor, Stanford University
profile: Sebastian Thrun (b. 1967, Solingen) led Stanford's Stanley to win the 2005 DARPA Grand Challenge, led Google's self-driving project (now Waymo) and co-founded Google X. He co-founded Udacity, ran eVTOL firm Kitty Hawk, co-founded $2bn AI contact-center unicorn Cresta (2017) and recently founded agentic-AI start-up Sage AI Labs.
interesting_fact: Larry Page reportedly disguised himself to watch a driverless-car race in order to scout and recruit Thrun to Google, where he went on to found the moonshot lab Google X.
deep_cut_fact: Long before self-driving cars he built museum tour-guide robots: Rhino at the University of Bonn (1994) and Minerva, which guided thousands of visitors at the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History in 1998 - the same museum that now houses his DARPA-winning car Stanley.
notes: Hurun lists him for Cresta. Very accessible public speaker and podcast guest (recent appearances on AI, flying cars, education). Active on X (posted 2025 about hiring for an agentic-AI start-up) but handle not verified here.

name: Liang Jia'en
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CTO, Unisound AI Technology (HKEX: 9678)
profile: Liang Jia'en (梁家恩), a USTC graduate with a CAS Institute of Automation PhD, led speech-recognition R&D at CAS before co-founding Unisound in 2012. Unisound makes voice AI, AI chips and its 'Shanhai' large model for IoT and healthcare, and listed in Hong Kong on 30 June 2025.
interesting_fact: Unisound's work on what it called the world's first AI chip for IoT voice interaction won the Wu Wenjun AI Science & Technology Progress Award; its medical knowledge-graph work won a Beijing Science & Technology Progress first prize.
deep_cut_fact: At CAS in 2008-2010 his biggest project put machine scoring into the English oral middle-school entrance exams for all of Jiangsu province and Wenzhou, reaching millions of students. He calls it China's first large-scale AI scoring deployment; it was hard to commercialise inside CAS, which pushed him toward entrepreneurship.
notes: Self-described 'engineer at heart': all four Unisound founders are AI PhDs, and he is the one who stayed on R&D. Quote: tech founders must not 'succeed by technology and then fail by technology', since tech is only a third of the business chain. CEO Huang Wei is the commercial face. Mostly Chinese-language media.

name: Paul Nguyen
current_role: Unknown; co-founder of View, Inc. (formerly eChromics/Soladigm), no longer with the company
profile: Paul Nguyen co-founded electrochromic smart-glass maker eChromics with Mike Scobey in April 2007 in Santa Rosa, California; it became Soladigm and in 2012 View, Inc., whose dynamic glass tints to cut building heat and glare. Rao Mulpuri took over as CEO in 2008. View reached a $1B+ valuation, listed on Nasdaq via SPAC (2021) and went private again in 2024. No public record of Nguyen's current role was found.
interesting_fact: The company he co-founded makes 'dynamic' electrochromic windows that tint electronically to control sunlight and heat, an energy-efficiency play for buildings; it was valued above $1 billion in 2017.
notes: Common name — don't conflate with other Paul Nguyens. His exit from the company led to a 2010 lawsuit/arbitration (ruled in his favour in 2015); avoid the topic. View itself had financial trouble and went private in 2024. Current whereabouts unknown; very low profile.

name: Craig Ramsey
current_role: Co-founder and former chairman/board member of Vlocity (acquired by Salesforce in 2020); former Salesforce director (to 2014)
profile: Craig D. Ramsey is a veteran enterprise-software sales executive. He worked at Oracle (1986-94), nCUBE and Siebel Systems, where he became SVP Worldwide Operations in 1996, and sat on Salesforce's board until 2014. In 2014 he co-founded Vlocity, an industry-specific cloud CRM built on Salesforce, which Salesforce bought for about $1.33B in 2020.
interesting_fact: He was part of the Oracle-to-Siebel-to-Salesforce sales lineage that built the enterprise CRM industry. He sat on Salesforce's board in its early public years, then co-founded Vlocity, which Salesforce later acquired.
deep_cut_fact: Siebel's 1996 IPO filing shows he joined from parallel-computing pioneer nCUBE, where he was SVP of worldwide sales, marketing and support. Before that he spent eight years at Oracle, rising to VP of US Commercial Sales. He holds a BA in economics from Denison University.
notes: Low public profile, with no published contact or social accounts found. MarketScreener lists a Glide Foundation (San Francisco) directorship. He has been out of the news since the 2020 Vlocity sale; alive status not confirmed. Fit with the podcast theme is weak (cloud CRM, not infrastructure).

name: David Schmaier
current_role: President & Chief Strategy Officer, Salesforce (per Salesforce media bio, June 2025)
profile: Founding executive and EVP at Siebel Systems, then co-founder/CEO of Vlocity (industry cloud apps on Salesforce), sold to Salesforce for $1.33B in 2020. At Salesforce he ran Salesforce Industries, then was Chief Product Officer driving agentic AI, and now oversees strategy, M&A, Salesforce Ventures and philanthropy.
interesting_fact: Salesforce acquired Vlocity for about $1.33B in 2020 and immediately made Schmaier CEO of the new Salesforce Industries division.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a mechanical engineer (B.S., Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute) before his Harvard MBA, and today sits on the cabinet board of Harvard's Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences and on Genstar Capital's strategic advisory board.
notes: Title has shifted several times (CEO Industries -> President & CPO -> President & Chief Strategy Officer); confirm current title before outreach. Also oversees Salesforce's Office of Ethical and Humane Use of technology.

name: James Ramsey
current_role: Co-founder & former board member, Vlocity (acquired by Salesforce 2020); LP at Stage 2 Capital; private investor
profile: James (Burr) Ramsey co-founded Vlocity in 2014 with Craig Ramsey, David Schmaier, Mark Armenante and Young Sohn to build industry-specific cloud CRM apps on Salesforce. Salesforce bought Vlocity in 2020 for about $1.33bn in cash. A long-time enterprise-software sales executive, he sat on SPS Commerce's board 2014-May 2025 and is now an LP with go-to-market VC Stage 2 Capital.
interesting_fact: Vlocity was built entirely on top of Salesforce's own platform, and Salesforce ended up acquiring it for ~$1.33bn in 2020, folding it into Salesforce Industries.
deep_cut_fact: Before Vlocity he was SVP of Worldwide Sales & Distribution at NetSuite, after starting out at Oracle, and he served about 11 years as an independent director of supply-chain software firm SPS Commerce, leaving in May 2025.
notes: Do not confuse with co-founder Craig D. Ramsey (Vlocity chairman, ex-Salesforce director). SPS board exit confirmed in SPS 2026 proxy: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1092699/000109269926000029/spsc-20260413.htm. Data-center angle is indirect (cloud software).

name: Young Sohn
current_role: Founding Managing Partner, Walden Catalyst Ventures; Chairman, HARMAN International; Chairman, Samsung Semiconductor Advisory Board
profile: Seoul-born, Maryland-raised Silicon Valley executive (Penn EE, MIT Sloan). Intel, Quantum, Agilent Semiconductor and Oak Technology, then took Inphi public in 2010 as CEO. As Samsung President/CSO (2012 on) he drove the $8B HARMAN deal and created the Samsung Catalyst Fund. He now invests in deep tech, AI and semis at Walden Catalyst (with Lip-Bu Tan).
interesting_fact: He has been a seed investor in Zoom, Ring, Noom, SambaNova, AI21 Labs and Berkeley Lights, and has sat on the boards of Arm, Cadence and Cymer (ASML).
deep_cut_fact: Early at Intel, as director of new business development, he oversaw the creation of Intel's PC chipset business and formed Intel's first joint venture with Samsung, decades before becoming a Samsung president. He also co-founded the Extreme Tech Challenge, a startup competition tied to the UN SDGs.
notes: Identity is clear (well-known executive), but Hurun's label 'Vlocity founder' could not be verified. Vlocity's known founders are other people, so he may have been an early investor or board member; avoid calling him its founder. Strong fit for an AI/semis/data-center podcast and a frequent conference speaker (CES, Web Summit).

name: David A. Steinberg
current_role: Co-Founder, Chairman & CEO, Zeta Global (NYSE: ZETA)
profile: Serial entrepreneur who spent ~17 years in wireless (Sterling Cellular, then InPhonic) before co-founding XL Marketing - now Zeta Global - with former Apple CEO John Sculley in 2007. Zeta, an AI/data-driven marketing cloud, listed on the NYSE in 2021; he now pushes its 'Athena' AI agent, including a partnership with OpenAI.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Zeta Global (originally XL Marketing) with former Apple CEO John Sculley shortly after leaving InPhonic.
deep_cut_fact: His first real company, at 16 or 17, was a nightclub production business in New York City and the Hamptons; after college (1990) Goldman and Morgan Stanley turned him down, so he worked on telecom issues on Capitol Hill before entering wireless.
notes: Very media-friendly; does many podcasts/interviews (Adam Mendler, ICE House, Alejandro Cremades). Best route: press@zetaglobal.com. Zeta's valuation is now well above the $1B in the source field.

name: Wang Xiaogang
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director, CTO and EVP, SenseTime (HKEX: 0020); Chairman, ACE Robotics (since Dec 2025)
profile: Computer-vision scientist who co-founded SenseTime in 2014 from Tang Xiaoou's CUHK lab, whose DeepID face recognition beat human accuracy. SenseTime became one of China's largest AI firms and runs big AI compute (SenseCore). Since Dec 2025 he has also chaired ACE Robotics, a SenseTime embodied-AI spinout behind the open 'Kairos' world model.
interesting_fact: DeepID, from his CUHK team, was the first method to exceed 99% face-verification accuracy on the Labeled Faces in the Wild benchmark, beating human performance. That result helped launch SenseTime.
deep_cut_fact: He studied in USTC's famous 'Special Class for the Gifted Young' (BEng 2001), took an MPhil at CUHK under Tang Xiaoou, and on Tang's recommendation did his PhD at MIT (2009). He returned that year to teach electronic engineering at CUHK.
notes: Strong fit for AI and data-center topics: SenseTime runs large AI compute (SenseCore AIDC), and he is now leading on embodied AI and world models. He speaks often to media (Yicai, CnTechPost); in 2026 he predicted robotics' 'ChatGPT moment' is about two years away. SenseTime is on the US Entity List.

name: Uber Technologies
profile: Not a person: this Hurun Unicorn (2020) entry lists Uber Technologies itself as the 'founder' of Uber ATG, its self-driving unit. Uber sold ATG to Aurora Innovation in an all-stock deal announced in December 2020 (ATG valued at ~$4bn), keeping about a 26% stake in Aurora.
interesting_fact: As part of the ATG sale, Uber invested $400m in Aurora, valuing Aurora at about $10bn, and Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi joined Aurora's board.
notes: Data artifact - corporate parent recorded as founder. No individual to profile; suggest dropping, or re-targeting Uber ATG's leaders/Aurora founders (Chris Urmson, Sterling Anderson, Drew Bagnell) if relevant.

name: Tang Wenbin
current_role: Founder & CEO, Yuanli Lingji (原力灵机 / Dexmal), embodied-AI robotics startup founded March 2025; co-founder and long-time CTO of Megvii
profile: Zhejiang-born member of Tsinghua's elite Yao Class who co-founded Beijing computer-vision company Megvii (Face++) in 2011 with classmates Yin Qi and Yang Mu, serving as CTO through ~14 years of the 'AI 1.0' wave. In March 2025 he launched Yuanli Lingji, focused on embodied intelligence, deliberately keeping its scope narrow.
interesting_fact: He says his main lesson from Megvii is not to over-expand: focus all effort on the one business where you have the greatest advantage, a philosophy he is applying at his robotics startup.
deep_cut_fact: A competitive-programming star, he won Tsinghua's 'Yao Award' (given to one student a year) in 2009 and spent seven years coaching China's national Olympiad in Informatics training team.
notes: Now focused on embodied AI rather than Megvii. Gives interviews to 36Kr; Chinese tech-media route likely best. No published press email found (site is a JS app). The dexmal.com site is titled 原力灵机, but no third-party source checked here confirms 'Dexmal' as the English brand.

name: Yang Mu
current_role: Co-founder and executive director, Megvii Technology (旷视科技, Beijing); earlier titled co-founder and senior vice president
profile: Yang Mu (杨沐) is one of Megvii's three co-founders, with Yin Qi and Tang Wenbin, all classmates in Tsinghua University's elite 'Yao Class' computer-science programme (2006 intake). They founded Megvii in 2011, building the Face++ computer-vision platform into one of China's 'AI four little dragons'. He remains on the company's board.
interesting_fact: Megvii's founders are known in China as the 'three musketeers of the Yao Class', the programme created in 2005 by Turing Award winner Andrew Chi-Chih Yao that also produced Pony.ai co-founder Lou Tiancheng.
deep_cut_fact: Yang, Yin Qi and Tang Wenbin were all in the Yao Class's 2006 cohort. They started Megvii in 2011, the same year Yin Qi left for a PhD at Columbia University in New York.
notes: Lowest-profile of the three Megvii founders; few interviews. Megvii is under US Entity List restrictions, which may matter for a US podcast. Executive-director title comes from a 10jqka company profile (https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/A04701/company.html) and the date is unverified. Chinese-language outreach recommended.

name: Wen Hao
current_role: Founding-team member / employee, CloudWalk Technology (云从科技, SSE STAR: 688327), Guangzhou/Chongqing; exact title not disclosed
profile: Wen Hao (温浩) is one of the early CloudWalk team who, like founder-chairman Zhou Xi, came from the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Chongqing Institute of Green and Intelligent Technology. CloudWalk, set up in 2015, grew into one of China's 'AI four dragons' in face recognition and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in May 2022. He is not a director or senior officer in its 2025 annual report.
interesting_fact: CloudWalk spun out of a CAS research institute: its 2022 IPO prospectus lists nine staff, including Zhou Xi and Wen Hao, who previously worked at CAS Chongqing Institute, and records the institute's written confirmation that it had no IP dispute with the company.
notes: Hurun lists him as a CloudWalk founder, but company filings name Zhou Xi (周曦) as the founder and actual controller; Wen Hao appears only as an ex-CAS Chongqing employee in the 2022 prospectus and is not in the 2025 annual report's director/officer table. Very low public profile (no interviews found; search hits for 温浩 are mostly an unrelated artist). Route via CloudWalk IR.

name: Yao Zhiqiang
current_role: Co-founder and head of strategic planning, CloudWalk Technology (SSE STAR: 688327) (role as of 2022 interviews)
profile: Yao Zhiqiang co-founded CloudWalk in 2015 with Zhou Xi, spinning the team out of a Chinese Academy of Sciences lab in Chongqing; it became one of China's 'AI Four Dragons' in computer vision (face recognition for banks, airports, cities). CloudWalk listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in May 2022; Yao champions its 'human-machine collaboration' operating system strategy.
interesting_fact: Yao describes the ideal AI system as like Iron Man's J.A.R.V.I.S.: it lays out options, but the human makes the final call - the thinking behind CloudWalk's human-machine collaboration OS (CWOS).
deep_cut_fact: Early on, the team camped at a bank client in Guangzhou for 1-2 weeks and proudly submitted a few-dozen-page PPT bid - only to be told vendors normally submitted at least 300 pages. He earned bachelor's, master's and PhD at USTC, where he was Zhou Xi's senior.
notes: Described as low-key and shy, a classic technical founder. No personal channels found; route via CloudWalk corporate communications. Current title should be rechecked in latest annual report.

name: Huang Chang
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and Chief Technology Officer, Horizon Robotics (地平线, 9660.HK)
profile: Dr. Huang Chang (黄畅, Chang Huang) co-founded Beijing-based Horizon Robotics with Kai Yu in July 2015 after both worked at Baidu's deep-learning effort. As CTO he leads R&D on Horizon's 'Journey' automotive AI chips and its BPU architecture; Horizon listed in Hong Kong in October 2024 and supplies assisted-driving chips/software to most major Chinese automakers.
interesting_fact: Horizon's founding team came out of NEC Labs America and Baidu's Institute of Deep Learning; the company's investors include SAIC, FAW, VW's CARIAD, BYD, Dongfeng and CATL.
deep_cut_fact: He took all three degrees in computer science at Tsinghua (BS 2003, MS 2005, PhD 2007), did a postdoc in the US, was a research staff member at NEC Laboratories America (2010-12) and principal architect at Baidu before co-founding Horizon; there he led in-house research on its BPU chip architecture.
notes: Horizon is now a listed company (~$9bn unicorn valuation is outdated). Huang is technical and less media-facing than CEO Kai Yu; English-language international PR team exists. horizon.auto was unreachable from our network, contacts taken from search-indexed company pages.

name: Yang Ming
current_role: Reportedly Head of Multi-Modality Cognition, Ant Group (since 2023, per an unverified profile); co-founder and former VP of Software, Horizon Robotics
profile: Computer-vision researcher (Tsinghua; PhD Northwestern), ex-NEC Labs and a founding member of Facebook AI Research, who co-founded Horizon Robotics with Kai Yu and Chang Huang in 2015 and was VP of software until ~2019. Profiles then place him at xForwardAI and, since 2023, Ant Group.
interesting_fact: He was a founding member of Facebook AI Research (FAIR) before leaving Silicon Valley to co-found Horizon Robotics, now one of China's leading makers of AI chips for driver-assistance systems.
deep_cut_fact: He is the second author of Facebook's landmark 2014 'DeepFace' paper (with Taigman, Ranzato and Wolf), which hit 97.35% accuracy on the Labeled Faces in the Wild benchmark - closely approaching human-level face verification.
notes: Identity 'uncertain' only because the Hurun record is name-only; Ming Yang is the Horizon co-founder per MarketScreener/Crunchbase, so the match is likely. Current role is from aggregator profiles (alphaXiv/Village), not confirmed by Ant Group. No published contact; he appears to have left Horizon.

name: Tao Feiwen
current_role: Co-founder, Horizon Robotics (HKEX: 9660); former COO and executive director (left the board Aug 27, 2025)
profile: Feiwen 'Annie' Tao (陶斐雯) co-founded Horizon Robotics in 2015 with ex-Baidu colleagues Yu Kai and Huang Chang. The company makes AI chips and driver-assistance software for Chinese automakers and listed in Hong Kong in Oct 2024. As COO and executive director she ran operations; she held ~7% of the company as of 2024 and stepped off the board in Aug 2025.
interesting_fact: Horizon's Journey chips and software power driver-assistance in many Chinese EVs, making it one of China's most valuable AI-chip companies after its 2024 Hong Kong IPO.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Horizon she spent nearly four years at Baidu, after an undergraduate degree from Nanjing University (2007) and a graduate degree from Northwestern University (2008).
notes: Resigned as executive director effective 27 Aug 2025 (HKEX announcement 2025082701309); it gave a personal reason, which should not be raised. Unclear whether she keeps an operating role. Low-profile; route via Horizon IR/PR. The Baidu tenure is from TheOrg/MarketScreener, a secondary source.

name: Feng Shicong
current_role: Founder and CEO, Bailian Intelligence (百炼智能, AI-driven B2B marketing/lead generation); co-founder and former President/CTO of Mininglamp (明略)
profile: Feng Shicong (冯是聪) earned a Peking University computer science PhD (2003) under Prof. Li Xiaoming, worked at Lucent and HP Labs China, then joined Wu Minghui's AdMaster/Miaozhen as tech director and VP and co-founded Mininglamp Data as CTO. In 2018 he left to found Bailian Intelligence, which raised a 100M+ RMB Pre-B in 2022; Mininglamp listed in Hong Kong in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: He was a core developer of 'Peking University Tianwang', one of China's first general web search engines; teammates from that project went on to co-found Baidu with Robin Li, while he chose Lucent instead, which he called 'following the crowd'.
deep_cut_fact: Before leaving HP Labs China he did a formal SWOT analysis to decide whether to start a company; he introduced his PKU junior Yao Conglei to HP Labs, and Yao later became Bailian's CTO. He holds 50+ patents and studied at Hundun and Cheung Kong business schools to go from CTO to CEO.
notes: Hurun lists him as a Mininglamp unicorn founder, but his current company is Bailian Intelligence; in May 2026 he spoke publicly about AI shifting B2B SaaS from 'selling tools' to 'selling results' (https://cj.sina.com.cn/articles/view/2311077472/89c03e6002002khka). No published contact found; route via Bailian Intelligence.

name: Kunle Olukotun
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technologist, SambaNova Systems; Cadence Design Systems Professor of EE and CS, Stanford University
profile: London-born Nigerian computer architect known as the 'father of the multi-core processor' for Stanford's Hydra chip-multiprocessor project. His startup Afara Websystems (2000) was bought by Sun in 2002 and became the Niagara/UltraSPARC T1 line. In 2017 he co-founded AI-chip company SambaNova (dataflow RDU chips for inference), which raised $1B at an $11B valuation in July 2026.
interesting_fact: The Niagara multicore design from his startup Afara went on to power Oracle's SPARC servers and generate billions of dollars of revenue; he was an architect of Sun's 2005 UltraSPARC T1.
deep_cut_fact: He did his undergraduate degree at Calvin College in Grand Rapids, Michigan, before a Michigan PhD (1991) under Trevor Mudge; his mid-1990s paper 'The Case for a Single-Chip Multiprocessor' argued for multicore years before industry adopted it. He won the 2023 Eckert-Mauchly Award.
notes: Funding source: https://www.ai-infra-summit.com/press-releases/ai-chip-startup-sambanova-valued-at-11-billion-in-1-billion-funding-round. Intel's ~$1.6B acquisition talks collapsed in early 2026, replaced by an Intel partnership/investment. Academic, approachable; Stanford route also possible.

name: Rodrigo Liang
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, SambaNova Systems (AI inference chips and systems, Palo Alto)
profile: A chip executive from Sun/Oracle, Rodrigo Liang co-founded SambaNova in 2017 with Stanford professors Kunle Olukotun and Christopher Ré to build dataflow AI chips. In 2026 it launched the SN50 chip with Intel collaboration and closed a $1B round led by General Atlantic at an $11B valuation, selling inference racks for power-constrained data centres.
interesting_fact: In April 2026 SambaNova partnered with TEPCO Systems to supply energy-efficient AI infrastructure to Japan's power sector, squarely at the energy/data-centre intersection.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Taipei but raised in Brazil, Liang chose the company's name himself: SambaNova is Portuguese for 'new dance'. 'It's time for us to do something new in the world of technology,' he told SoftBank Vision Fund.
notes: Very media-friendly; frequent podcast/conference speaker (Bloomberg Open Interest, theCUBE, HumanX). Strong fit for the AI data-centre/energy angle. Intel acquisition talks reportedly stalled in early 2026; Intel remains investor/partner.

name: Daniel Yanisse
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Checkr (San Francisco)
profile: French-born engineer who co-founded Checkr with Jonathan Perichon in 2014 (YC) after seeing, at delivery startup Deliv, how slow background checks held up gig hiring. Checkr's API-first, AI-assisted screening platform serves thousands of employers and was valued at $4.6bn in 2021.
interesting_fact: Checkr launched Checkr.org in 2022 to push 'fair chance' hiring of people with criminal records, a mission Yanisse says crystallised from the founders' first conversations with job applicants.
deep_cut_fact: Before Checkr he was a software engineer who helped develop prototypes of the Mars rover for NASA; he was also on Forbes 30 Under 30.

public_contacts.value: Guest on 20VC (Harry Stebbings) discussing hiring and fundraising

notes: Podcast-friendly founder (20VC, SafeGraph, Battery Ventures interviews). Best route: Checkr press team. AI/HR-tech angle rather than energy/data-center.

name: Jonathan Perichon
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO of Checkr (San Francisco); reported as board director
profile: Jonathan Perichon is a software engineer who co-founded Checkr in 2014 with Daniel Yanisse, building an API-first background-check platform that took off with gig-economy customers. Checkr went through Y Combinator (S14), was valued at $5B in 2022 and reported about $800M in 2025 gross revenue with 120,000+ customers. Recent research profiles list him as former CTO.
interesting_fact: Checkr was born from a hiring bottleneck: at on-demand delivery startup Deliv, the founders couldn't onboard drivers fast enough because background checks were slow and manual, and incumbent vendors had no proper APIs, so they built their own.
deep_cut_fact: He and Yanisse met in 2012 as coworkers at LA startup Mogreet; when it failed less than a year later they moved together to Deliv, where the Checkr idea emerged. At Y Combinator they landed Checkr's first 10 customers.
notes: Very low public profile; current title uncertain (sources say co-founder/former CTO or director). Reported French background is from an aggregator only (unverified). Checkr is HR-tech/AI rather than energy/data centers; weak podcast fit.

name: Lin Chenxi
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Architect, Yitu Technology (依图科技), Shanghai; leads its technology organisation
profile: Lin Chenxi co-founded computer-vision company Yitu in 2012 with his high-school classmate Zhu Long, building one of China's 'AI four dragons' (with SenseTime, Megvii, CloudWalk). After Yitu withdrew its 2021 STAR Market IPO and restructured, he took over its overall technology work; he says Yitu has been profitable and cash-flow positive for several years via security/smart-city work and is exploring spatial intelligence/world models.
interesting_fact: In his first media interview in five years (Jan 2025) he argued China's six LLM start-up 'tigers' are retracing the AI-four-dragons path at triple speed, reaching ~RMB 20B valuations in 1-2 years versus Yitu's 7-8 - and that 'technology is not a friend of time; commercial value matters more.'
deep_cut_fact: Before Yitu he was a senior expert at Alibaba Cloud, helping build the Apsara (飞天) distributed cloud operating system under Wang Jian, and earlier did machine-learning, computer-vision and distributed-systems research at Microsoft Research Asia. He and Zhu Long were classmates at the High School Affiliated to Fujian Normal University.
notes: Rarely speaks to media (the 2025 TMTPost interview broke a ~5-year silence). Yitu has been on the US Commerce Entity List since 2019 - consider sensitivity for a US podcast. Strong cloud-infrastructure background (Apsara) fits data-center angle.

name: Dai Baojia
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Chief Strategy Officer, ASR Microelectronics (翱捷科技, SSE STAR: 688220)
profile: Dai Baojia (戴保家, b. 1956, Hong Kong citizen) is a serial chip entrepreneur: he founded RDA Microelectronics in 2004 (Nasdaq-listed, sold to Tsinghua Unigroup in 2013), then founded Shanghai-based ASR in 2015, which bought Marvell's mobile-communications unit in 2017 and makes cellular baseband/IoT chips. ASR listed on the STAR Market in 2022 and filed for a Hong Kong listing in 2026; he controls ~21.9%.
interesting_fact: After acquiring Marvell's mobile business in 2017, ASR became the only Chinese baseband company other than Huawei's HiSilicon with full multi-mode ('all-network') cellular technology.
deep_cut_fact: Long before RDA he was a Silicon Valley founder: Georgia Tech-trained electrical engineer and University of Chicago MBA who started Excel rep firm, was GM of UMAX Technologies in the US, and co-founded linear power-amplifier developer USI.
notes: Input lists 'ASR (founder; company valued $2B)' - now a listed company (~RMB 43B market cap in 2026). Pending Hong Kong dual listing may make IR team responsive to media. Two-time founder story (RDA -> ASR) is a good podcast hook.

name: Ai Yu
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Terminus Group (特斯联 / Chongqing Terminus Smart Technology)
profile: Ai Yu (Victor Ai, b. 1983) founded Terminus in 2015, an AIoT company building smart-building and 'AI City' infrastructure, including the Cloud Valley AI City project in Chongqing; backers include JD.com and Investcorp. Before that he was a managing director at China Everbright Limited, running new-economy investing. Terminus filed for a Hong Kong IPO in September 2024.
interesting_fact: He is credited with coining 'AIoT' (AI + IoT) in 2017, and Terminus was a technology partner of Expo 2020 Dubai, where it showcased its AI City concept.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech he was a finance man: Simon Fraser University economics grad with a finance master's from Washington University in St. Louis, he worked at JPMorgan and Lehman Brothers and was a core co-founder of Everbright Ashmore (光大安石), described as China's largest real-estate fund.
notes: Media-friendly: frequent speaker at Web Summit, CLSA forums and Economist events. HK IPO status after the 2024 filing not confirmed. The pedaily source supports the AIoT claim; the Expo 2020 detail is from Gulf News/Global Times coverage.

name: Lin Yaona
current_role: Early shareholder and employee of Tuya Inc. (NYSE: TUYA; HKEX: 2391); director of Tuya's onshore VIE entity (Zhejiang/Hangzhou Tuya Technology)
profile: Yaona Lin is one of the five original onshore shareholders of Tuya's VIE, Hangzhou Tuya Technology, alongside co-founders Jerry Wang, Leo Chen and Ruixin Zhou, under contracts dating to December 2014. Tuya's 2021 IPO prospectus describes him as an employee holding about 4.5% of Tuya after the IPO; he reported 25.2M Class A shares (4.99%) via Anywink Limited at end-2023. Tuya runs an IoT cloud platform for smart devices.
interesting_fact: Lin held 11.5% of Hangzhou Tuya Technology, the onshore entity behind Tuya's structure, making him the third-largest holder after Jerry Wang (60.7%) and Leo Chen (13.1%) - more than CTO Ruixin Zhou (9.8%).
notes: Confirmed via SEC filings (F-1/424B4 2021; Schedule 13G 2022 and 13G/A 2024, CIK 0001909014; Tuya 2025 annual report calls him 'Mr. Lin Yaona', a director of Zhejiang Tuya). Chinese characters not confirmed. No public profile, interviews or social accounts found; he isn't on Tuya's board or senior management list. Route via Tuya IR.

name: Dror Feldheim
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Trax (retail computer-vision company); stepped back from day-to-day operations in May 2024
profile: Israeli-born, Singapore-based co-founder of Trax, which he started in 2010 with Joel Bar-El to apply computer vision and AI to store shelves, giving consumer-goods brands and retailers real-time data on availability, pricing and shelf share. Trax raised ~$1.2bn and peaked above a $3bn valuation; Feldheim served as CCO/president before stepping back to the board in 2024.
interesting_fact: Trax raised about $1.2 billion over its life - roughly half in secondary transactions - and was valued at more than $3 billion at its 2021 peak, making it one of Israel's best-known retail-tech unicorns.
deep_cut_fact: Before Trax he spent more than 15 years in business development in the FMCG (consumer packaged goods) sector launching brands - the shelf-level problem Trax was built to solve - and became Trax's CCO in January 2015 after running global sales and BD.
notes: Low public profile; LinkedIn (as linked from his TechAviv founders-club profile) is the best direct route. No published press email found on Trax's site.

name: Joel Bar-El
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman (non-executive since mid-2024), Trax Ltd.
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Trax with Dror Feldheim in 2010 to digitize retail shelves with computer vision. As CEO for ~8 years he built a Singapore-based unicorn that raised $640M at a $2.25B valuation in 2021 (SoftBank VF2-led). He became non-executive chairman in 2024; Trax sold its image-recognition unit to Gemspring in 2025.
interesting_fact: Trax deliberately insisted on a multinational as its first customer: founded at the end of 2010, it landed its first recurring client, Coca-Cola, only in mid-2013.
deep_cut_fact: Before Trax he was CEO of Sentry, a wealth-management software company sold to Australia's IRESS after four years, and he co-founded Tersus Software.
notes: Stepped back from operations in May 2024 to pursue 'innovative initiatives' (https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/ryp6iv8na). No published personal or press contact verified. Retail AI/computer vision is only a loose fit with the data-center theme. Deep-cut source is TheOrg (secondary); the company name appears there as 'Sentryi Limited'.

name: Laurent Simoneau
current_role: Chief Executive Officer (since April 2025) and co-founder, Coveo Solutions Inc. (TSX: CVO), Quebec City
profile: Quebec tech executive who, as CTO and COO of desktop-search pioneer Copernic, spun its enterprise-search division out as Coveo in 2005. He was Coveo's first CEO (2004-11), then President & CTO under Louis Têtu while Coveo became an AI search, relevance and generative-answering platform for enterprises and listed on the TSX (2021); he returned as CEO in April 2025.
interesting_fact: Coveo was born as a 2005 spin-off of Copernic, one of the early desktop-search pioneers of the dot-com era, and has since grown into a TSX-listed AI-relevance company serving large enterprise websites and support portals.
deep_cut_fact: Before Coveo he was Copernic's CTO, personally directing R&D of its core desktop-search technology, and as Copernic's COO he orchestrated the 2005 spin-off of the enterprise-search unit that became Coveo; he holds an MBA from the Université du Québec.
notes: French-speaking Quebecer; writes on Coveo's blog (coveo.com/blog/author/laurent-simoneau). CEO change announced Feb 2025 (effective 1 Apr 2025), with Louis Têtu as Executive Chair. Media enquiries go via Coveo corporate communications (Kiyomi Harrington named in releases; email not verified).

name: Marc Sanfaçon
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Coveo (TSX: CVO), since February 2025
profile: Quebec City software engineer who co-founded AI-search company Coveo (spun out of Copernic in 2004/05) and led its technology as SVP Technology for two decades, including its cloud operations, before being promoted to CTO in Feb 2025 when co-founder Laurent Simoneau became CEO. Coveo sells AI-relevance and generative search for commerce, service and workplace and listed on the TSX in 2021.
interesting_fact: Coveo grew from Copernic's enterprise search unit into a Hurun-listed $1bn+ unicorn; in 2025 the co-founders took over the top tech and CEO roles as Louis Têtu moved to Executive Chair.
deep_cut_fact: Before Coveo he was Director of Technologies at Copernic, an early desktop-search pioneer, and before that a senior software developer at Berclain Group, a Quebec supply-chain software firm; he has 30+ years in application development, mostly search.
notes: Technical, low-profile co-founder; writes occasionally on Coveo's blog. Good fit for AI-infrastructure/search topics. Route via Coveo IR or comms.

name: Richard Tessier
current_role: Co-founder and (as of latest available bios) SVP Products, Coveo Solutions (TSX: CVO), Quebec City
profile: Quebec engineer (B.Sc. electrical engineering, Universite Laval) who ran software development for Copernic's enterprise-search division and in 2005 co-founded Coveo as its spin-off with Laurent Simoneau and Marc Sanfacon. Coveo grew into an AI-powered search and relevance platform for e-commerce and customer service, reaching unicorn status and listing on the TSX in 2021.
interesting_fact: Before Coveo, he was Director of Software Development at Copernic, an early desktop-search leader, overseeing its enterprise-search division; in 2005 he played a key role in spinning that division out as Coveo, and has run Coveo's product organisation since 2008.
notes: Low public profile compared with CEO Laurent Simoneau; current title only confirmed via Coveo blog bio and TheOrg (may be dated). Hurun lists him as a unicorn founder (no personal net-worth figure).

name: Almog Cohen
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO, SentinelOne (left the company a few years after its 2013 founding); current role not publicly confirmed
profile: Almog Cohen co-founded Israeli-American cybersecurity company SentinelOne in 2013 with childhood friend Tomer Weingarten (and Ehud Shamir), serving as CTO through its early growth. SentinelOne built an AI-driven endpoint-protection platform and listed on the NYSE in 2021. He appears to have stepped back from day-to-day roles; no newer venture is publicly confirmed.
interesting_fact: In 2017, as CTO, he said SentinelOne aimed to bring 'the first revolution in the end-points and servers security market in four decades' and had turned down exit offers; Ashton Kutcher and Guy Oseary's Sound Ventures was an early investor and Kutcher visited the Palo Alto office.
deep_cut_fact: He and CEO Tomer Weingarten have been friends since second grade. Before SentinelOne, Cohen spent seven years at Check Point, and he told Globes neither founder went to university: 'We skipped it. We felt we didn't need it.'
notes: Left SentinelOne a few years after founding, per Calcalist 2021 (https://www.calcalistech.com/ctech/articles/0,7340,L-3917654,00.html); low public profile since. No verified personal channels found. Hurun lists the company as an AI unicorn. Weak fit for the podcast (cybersecurity).

name: Ehud Shamir
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Architect, Cylake (AI-native, data-sovereign cybersecurity startup launched March 2026)
profile: Ehud 'Udi' Shamir co-founded endpoint-security company SentinelOne in 2013 with Tomer Weingarten and Almog Cohen and helped grow it for 5+ years (it IPO'd on NYSE in 2021). He later became a distinguished engineer at Palo Alto Networks, and in 2026 co-founded Cylake with Palo Alto founder Nir Zuk and Wilson Xu, launching with a $45m Greylock-led seed.
interesting_fact: Cylake targets organisations that cannot use public-cloud security products for regulatory or security reasons - building AI-native security that runs on-premises or in private clouds with total data sovereignty.
deep_cut_fact: After co-founding SentinelOne, he went on to work as a distinguished engineer at Palo Alto Networks - the rival founded by Nir Zuk, with whom he then started Cylake.
notes: Hurun listing (SentinelOne unicorn, 2020) is dated; he is no longer at SentinelOne. Engineer-type founder with a low media profile; route via Cylake. Data-sovereign/on-prem AI security angle ties to data-center theme.

name: Chen Yuqiang
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director & Chief Research Scientist, 4Paradigm (第四范式, HKEX: 6682), Beijing
profile: Machine-learning scientist who co-founded enterprise-AI company 4Paradigm with CEO Dai Wenyuan after helping build Baidu's Phoenix Nest (凤巢) ad system - described as the first commercial deep-learning system - and Toutiao's feed recommendation and ads system. 4Paradigm sells AutoML/decision-AI platforms to banks and enterprises and listed in Hong Kong in 2023.
interesting_fact: He led the team behind 4Paradigm's AutoML algorithms; 4Paradigm AutoML was cited among Gartner's Top 10 Strategic Technology Trends for 2020.
deep_cut_fact: As a transfer-learning researcher he introduced 'heterogeneous transfer learning', won the APWeb 2010 Best Paper Award (work covered by MIT Technology Review), and placed in the top three of KDD Cup 2011; he was also the first winner of the WAIC 'Yunfan' (云帆) award for young AI talent.
notes: Technical, research-oriented co-founder; CEO Dai Wenyuan is the usual media face. KDD Cup 2011 top-three detail is from Chinese media (36kr) summaries rather than the company page - verify before quoting.

name: Hu Shiwei
current_role: Co-founder and chief architect, 4Paradigm (renamed Phancy Group / 范式智能 in Jan 2026; HKEX: 6682) - last confirmed in 2023 materials
profile: Hu Shiwei (胡时伟) co-founded 4Paradigm with Dai Wenyuan and Chen Yuqiang, building it into an enterprise machine-learning/AI platform company that listed in Hong Kong in 2023 and was renamed Phancy Group in 2026. A systems architect by background, he led R&D on the company's flagship 'Prophet' (Sage) AI platform.
interesting_fact: The team he led built 4Paradigm's 'Prophet' (先知), billed as China's first end-to-end AI platform, which won first prize for innovation at the 2016 Wu Wenjun AI Science & Technology Awards.
deep_cut_fact: At Baidu he was the systems architecture lead on core commercial systems including the Phoenix Nest (凤巢) ad-monetization platform and the Aladdin ecosystem, then joined the founding team of property platform Lianjia, designing its new main site and agent work systems.
notes: Technical co-founder, comfortable speaking at conferences (TMTPost T-EDGE, IWRA 2023). Not shown as a director in recent filings; current title should be re-checked against Phancy Group's 2025 annual report. Company PR mailbox is the best route.

name: Yang Qiang
current_role: Chief AI Officer, Director of the Academy for AI and Chair Professor of AI, Hong Kong Polytechnic University (since April 2025); Professor Emeritus, HKUST
profile: Prominent AI scientist (Qiang Yang) known for pioneering transfer learning and federated learning; co-founder of 4Paradigm (HKEX: 6682), the enterprise-AI platform valued ~$3bn at its unicorn peak. He was founding director of Huawei's Noah's Ark Lab, chief technology advisor at WeChat and Chief AI Officer of WeBank (2018-2025) before joining PolyU.
interesting_fact: He led development of the first international standard on federated learning (IEEE) and launched the first open-source federated-learning platform (FATE), letting banks and hospitals train models without sharing raw data.
deep_cut_fact: Before computer science, his undergraduate degree at Peking University was in astrophysics; he then did his PhD at the University of Maryland (1989), which inducted him into its CS Alumni Hall of Fame in 2017. He also was founding editor-in-chief of both ACM TIST and IEEE Transactions on Big Data.

public_contacts.value: qyang@cse.ust.hk (published as 'qyang at cse ust hk')

notes: Highly accessible academic with published university emails; good podcast fit for AI/data-center angle (privacy-preserving AI, enterprise AI). 4Paradigm's founder-CEO is Dai Wenyuan (Yang's former student); Yang is co-founder. Wealth figure from Hurun unicorn list is approximate.

name: Joseph Chen
current_role: Co-founder, Anduril Industries; current operating role not confirmed
profile: Joe (Joseph) Chen co-founded Anduril Industries in 2017 with Palmer Luckey, Trae Stephens, Matt Grimm and Brian Schimpf, after working as a producer and product lead at Oculus VR. Anduril builds autonomous defence systems (drones, counter-drone, Lattice software, sentry towers), reported about $2.2B revenue in 2025 and was valued at $61B after a $5B raise in 2026.
interesting_fact: He was one of the original Oculus team members who left with Palmer Luckey to start Anduril, which went from a placeholder website in 2017 to a $61B defence-tech company with about 7,000 staff by 2026.
deep_cut_fact: After about 10 years in engineering and product development, he enlisted in the US Army National Guard as a paratrooper, an unusual path for a Silicon Valley hardware product lead.
notes: Lowest-profile Anduril co-founder; no personal site or verified social accounts found. The paratrooper detail comes from his self-description on The Org (marked 'unverified'), so confirm before using. Some aggregator pages mix him up with a different Joseph Chen (Fairway Health CPO). Best route is via Anduril's corporate contact or Palmer Luckey/Trae Stephens.

name: Matt Grimm
current_role: Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer, Anduril Industries
profile: Co-founded defense-tech company Anduril in 2017 with Palmer Luckey, Brian Schimpf, Trae Stephens and Joe Chen. As COO he runs procurement, manufacturing, supply chain, facilities, security, people and finance. Before Anduril he was an early Palantir hire, a Mithril Capital principal and a Booz Allen consultant to the DIA and US Navy.
interesting_fact: As an early Palantir employee he deployed to both Iraq and Afghanistan to get software into the hands of US forces. Trae Stephens later recruited him to Anduril, calling him 'the best person I know at starting a company'.
deep_cut_fact: As Cornell classmates, he and now-Anduril CEO Brian Schimpf co-founded Cornell's autonomous-vehicle entry in the DARPA Grand Challenge and Urban Challenge. The 2007 car, a modified Tahoe called 'Skynet', finished the Urban Challenge. He holds a BS in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering and an MEng in Systems Engineering from Cornell.
notes: Does occasional long-form media: a Sourcery HQ tour (Dec 2025) and a 20VC interview. Best route is Anduril communications or the general contact address. The 'podcast' entry is an interview appearance, not his own show. Strong angle for an energy/data-center podcast: manufacturing scale-up (Arsenal factories) and supply chain.

name: Huang Xiaoqing
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, CloudMinds / Dataa Robotics (达闼机器人), Shanghai
profile: Bill Huang (黄晓庆) is a telecom veteran: AT&T Bell Labs project manager (1990-94), co-founder and CTO of UTStarcom, then head of China Mobile Research Institute (2007-15). In 2015 he founded CloudMinds, a 'cloud robotics' company whose robots run on a cloud-hosted AI 'brain'; it is now refocusing on humanoid robots.
interesting_fact: He is often called the 'father of cloud robots': CloudMinds' core idea is to keep robots' intelligence in the cloud, connected over secure networks, rather than on the device.
deep_cut_fact: He studied electrical engineering at Huazhong University of Science & Technology, earned an EECS master's at the University of Illinois, and as UTStarcom CTO led work credited with the first mobile softswitch and first carrier-class IPTV system.
notes: Goes by Bill Huang. Company has been through heavy restructuring (US Entity List 2020, 2024-25 layoffs, new JV with Guohua Group 'Gangzai Robot' in 2025), so avoid financial framing. Good fit for AI/cloud-robotics angle; he speaks often at MWC Shanghai/WAIC.

name: Zhang Zhe
current_role: Unknown
profile: Listed by Hurun's Global Unicorn Index (2020-2024) as a founder of CloudMinds (达闼科技), the Beijing/Shanghai cloud-robotics and embodied-AI company valued around $2B. Public sources name Bill Huang (黄晓庆, ex-UTStarcom co-founder/CTO, ex-China Mobile Research Institute) as founder and CEO; no source linking a 'Zhang Zhe' to CloudMinds' founding team was found.
notes: Could not verify that this person exists as a CloudMinds co-founder; possibly a Hurun data error or a minor co-founder with no public footprint. 'Zhang Zhe' is a very common name. If CloudMinds is wanted, the public face is founder/CEO Bill Huang. Recommend dropping or re-checking with Hurun.

name: Chen Lucheng
current_role: Chairman (and general manager), Kaos IoT Technology Co., Ltd. (卡奥斯 / COSMOPlat), Haier Group's industrial-internet platform
profile: Chen Lucheng (陈录城), a Qingdao native, co-founded Haier's COSMOPlat industrial internet platform and chairs its operating company Kaos IoT Technology, founded in 2017. COSMOPlat sells mass-customization, connected-factory, IoT and industrial-AI solutions; it says it has helped light up 20 WEF 'Lighthouse' factories. Kaos filed for a Hong Kong IPO in July 2026 (CICC, HSBC as sponsors).
interesting_fact: At WAIC in July 2026 he launched the 'ONE-COSMO Rainforest Ecosystem Plan' with partners incl. Shanghai Jiao Tong University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Huawei and China Mobile to scale industrial AI.
deep_cut_fact: Besides running COSMOPlat, he heads the Haier Industrial Intelligence Research Institute and sits on China's national intelligent-manufacturing expert advisory committee, as well as being vice-chairman of the Alliance of Industrial Internet.
notes: Corporate executive within Haier rather than an independent founder-owner; 'founder' wealth reflects Hurun unicorn listing. Email is COSMOPlat's published marketing/business address (no dedicated press email found); Haier Group also has a media-contact page on haier.com. HK IPO pending as of late 2026.

name: Sashi Narahari
current_role: Founder, President and CEO, HighRadius (Houston-based AI finance/order-to-cash SaaS)
profile: Sashi (Sashidhar) Narahari, a former SAP developer/consultant, co-founded master-data firm Riversand before founding HighRadius in 2006 to automate accounts receivable and treasury. HighRadius grew to a roughly $3B valuation, about 3,300 employees and $300M+ ARR, and now pitches 'autonomous finance' AI agents for CFO offices.
interesting_fact: HighRadius bootstrapped for over a decade, then raised a $50M Series A in 2017 (a cheque the size of a typical Series C) and a $125M Series B that made it a unicorn, and later reached a $3.1B valuation.
deep_cut_fact: An SAP developer from a middle-class Chennai family, Narahari built HighRadius in accounts-receivable automation, a category 'nobody was excited about'. He self-funded it for about 12 years and now says openly that he waited too long to raise outside capital.

public_contacts.value: Has appeared on SaaSBoomi and Kalaari 'SaaS from Scratch' podcasts

notes: Does founder podcasts regularly (SaaSBoomi, Kalaari, Sramana Mitra), so he is a good podcast prospect. Education is reported inconsistently across aggregators (IIT Madras vs Osmania), so don't cite it.

name: Li Hao
current_role: Founding shareholder of CalmCar (Tianjin/Suzhou Tiantong Weishi, 天瞳威视); current title not disclosed
profile: A Li Hao (李皓) is one of six founding shareholders of CalmCar, an autonomous-driving perception and software company set up in March 2016 by founder/CEO Wang Xi, holding 5% at incorporation. CalmCar sells L2-L2+ driver-assistance software and L4 robotaxi systems and filed for a Hong Kong IPO in May 2026. No public bio or current role for Li Hao was found.
interesting_fact: CalmCar says it was the first company to mass-produce an L2-L2+ driving software solution outside China, and it is delivering 1,000 robotaxis to Lenovo Connect over two years.
notes: Identity is only partly confirmed. The HKEX draft prospectus lists Li Hao (李皓) as a 5% founding shareholder (2016) who in 2018 moved part of his stake to the founder's platform, Tiantong Zhilian. He is not named among the directors. CEO and public face is Wang Xi. Low priority.

name: Anant Bhardwaj
current_role: Founder and CEO, SuperApp, Inc. (formerly Instabase, Inc.), San Francisco
profile: Anant Bhardwaj came from Pune to Stanford for an MS in CS (2010), then pursued a PhD at MIT CSAIL, where a research project became Instabase (2015), an AI platform for turning unstructured documents into usable data for banks and Fortune 100 firms; it was valued at ~$2B. In Aug 2026 the company renamed itself SuperApp and launched a multi-model AI collaboration app.
interesting_fact: Instabase's breakthrough came after landing Standard Chartered, which opened the door to other big banks; the company is backed by a16z, Greylock, Index, NEA, Spark, Tribe and QIA.
deep_cut_fact: He says he never expected Stanford to admit him ('Stanford claims that they don't make mistakes. That year, they did') after rejections from peer schools; he interned at Oracle and Google, and chose an MIT PhD because someone told him a PhD is a 'failsafe environment' to try ideas.
notes: Instabase rebranded to SuperApp, Inc. on Aug 18, 2026 - use the new name in outreach. Fit is AI/data infrastructure rather than energy. Older Instabase press addresses may be stale.

name: Sun Weilin
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Newlink (能链); director of NaaS Technology (Nasdaq: NAAS) per insider records
profile: Sun Weilin co-founded Beijing-based Newlink (Newlinks Technology) in May 2016 with Wang Yang and Dai Zhen, growing it from a fuel-station digital platform into an energy-services and EV-charging group. Subsidiary NaaS Technology listed on Nasdaq in 2022; in 2024 he signed a planned RMB1bn new-energy infrastructure JV in Foshan.
interesting_fact: NaaS describes itself as the first US-listed EV charging service company in China, and its JV with Chancheng City Construction Group covers charging stations, PV and energy-storage projects plus charging-safety testing.
notes: Press email is the media contact (Sabrina Wang) named in a Feb 2024 NaaS/PRNewswire release; may be outdated. Co-founder status supported by NaaS SEC Schedule 13D/A (2024) listing Weilin Sun as a Newlink director/executive. Low personal profile; route via Newlink/NaaS communications.

name: Chakri Gottemukkala
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, o9 Solutions (Dallas)
profile: Chakri Gottemukkala (IIT Madras BE, UCLA MS) spent his early career at i2 Technologies, then co-founded o9 Solutions with i2 founder Sanjiv Sidhu in 2009. o9's AI 'Digital Brain' platform handles supply-chain, revenue and integrated business planning for large enterprises. The company now has 2,500+ staff and was most recently valued at about US$3.7bn.
interesting_fact: He built o9 from two founders to profitability without outside investment before later bringing in investors such as KKR. The company also hosts its own annual planning conference, aim10x.
deep_cut_fact: i2 Technologies, the company that pioneered advanced-planning software, was his first job after UCLA. Its founder Sanjiv Sidhu, his old boss, became his o9 co-founder and chairman. His motto on o9's site: better decision-makers are 'better stewards of the earth's precious resources'.
notes: Gives interviews regularly (Authority Magazine, D Magazine Dallas 500, aim10x keynotes), so media-friendly. Agentic AI for planning is a good podcast angle. The 'first job at i2' detail comes from an interview cited by search results; the o9 bio confirms the i2 background.

name: Sanjiv S. Sidhu
current_role: Co-founder and board member (long styled chairman) of o9 Solutions, Dallas
profile: Hyderabad-born chemical engineer who worked in Texas Instruments' AI lab, then co-founded supply-chain software pioneer i2 Technologies in 1988. At i2's peak his stake was worth $6.5B and Forbes ranked him the world's 109th-richest person in 2001. In 2009 he co-founded o9 Solutions with Chakri Gottemukkala; o9 makes an AI planning platform (the 'Digital Brain') and has been valued at about $3.7B.
interesting_fact: He is often called the father of modern advanced planning systems. In the 1980s his software at TI's AI lab used simulation to plan chip production, years before 'AI for supply chain' was a category.
deep_cut_fact: As a young man in India he was a member of the national sailing team. His father was a chemist who oversaw India's national laboratories.
notes: o9's About page now lists him as 'Board Member & Cofounder', with Chakri Gottemukkala as Executive Chairman and CEO (July 2026 release); his bio page still says Chairman. Strong AI/enterprise-software and supply-chain story. He mentors executives and is passionate about sustainable supply chains.

name: Hao Zheng
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, PlusAI (autonomous trucking; Santa Clara, CA)
profile: Hao Zheng co-founded PlusAI (formerly Plus.ai) in 2016 with David Liu, Shawn Kerrigan and Tim Daly. The company builds the SuperDrive Level 4 'AI driver' for heavy trucks, partnering with Traton and IVECO. As CTO he leads its AI and ML stack. PlusAI agreed to list on Nasdaq (ticker PLS) through a merger with Churchill Capital Corp IX.
interesting_fact: In May 2021 Plus ran a 4,000-mile autonomous truck test drive from Suzhou to Dunhuang along China's Silk Road.
deep_cut_fact: Before PlusAI he founded Ztelic, a social-network data analytics startup that Yahoo acquired. At Yahoo he became Distinguished Architect and head of its Beijing Research Lab, and he was later CTO for Asia at Zynga. He holds an MS in EECS from UW-Madison.
notes: Technical founder with a low media profile; CEO David Liu is the usual spokesperson. I could not confirm whether the Churchill IX SPAC deal had closed (it was targeted for Q1 2026). The media contact is Lauren Kwan (pr@plus.ai).

name: Shawn Kerrigan
current_role: Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer, PlusAI (Santa Clara, CA)
profile: Shawn Kerrigan co-founded PlusAI, a developer of autonomous-trucking software (SuperDrive), in 2016 with Stanford classmate David Liu, and serves as COO. PlusAI works with OEMs such as IVECO and Traton. Its planned Nasdaq listing via Churchill Capital Corp IX was terminated in April 2026 because of market conditions, and the company is raising private capital instead.
interesting_fact: In January 2026 PlusAI launched Southern Europe's first autonomous-trucking program with IVECO, adding to its US driverless-truck commercialisation plans.
deep_cut_fact: Before autonomous trucks he was in energy. He co-founded Locus Energy, a solar-monitoring and analytics company where he was CTO, and earlier worked at Bridgewater Associates and McKinsey. He holds a BS from UIUC and an MS and PhD in engineering from Stanford.

public_contacts.value: https://www.plus.ai/contact (form; fallback email info@plus.ai, which the page says is for investors and journalists)

notes: The Locus Energy (solar) background makes a good energy angle. The plus.ai contact page explicitly invites journalists to use the form or info@plus.ai.

name: Tim Daly
current_role: Co-Founder and Chief Architect, PlusAI (Plus Automation), Santa Clara, CA
profile: Software architect and AI/search expert who co-founded autonomous-trucking company Plus in 2016 with David Liu and Hao Zheng. He leads the architecture of PlusAI's SuperDrive virtual driver, built for factory integration with truck OEMs, and its 'AV 2.0' end-to-end approach. PlusAI is going public via a merger with Texas Ventures Acquisition III Corp (S-4 filed).
interesting_fact: He holds 41 granted patents with 40+ more pending in autonomous driving and AI, and is a recipient of the KDD award (the top data-mining conference).
deep_cut_fact: Long before self-driving trucks, as a Roadsend employee he came up with the idea of writing their own PHP implementation that compiled PHP to native binaries - the origin of the Roadsend PHP Compiler, later open-sourced - before moving to Yahoo! search.
notes: Engineer, not the public face (CEO David Liu is). PlusAI's contact form explicitly invites journalists; info@plus.ai is the fallback. 'AI/data center' angle: physical-AI/autonomy compute (NVIDIA DRIVE-based).

name: Eldad Farkash
current_role: Co-Founder, Firebolt (cloud data warehouse); Benjamin Wagner is now CEO
profile: Israeli data-infrastructure entrepreneur who cofounded BI company Sisense and was its CTO for about 14–15 years. In 2019 he cofounded Firebolt, a high-performance cloud data warehouse, with former Sisense colleagues Saar Bitner and Ariel Yaroshevich. He led it as CEO to a ~$1B+ valuation; Firebolt's site now lists Benjamin Wagner as CEO and Farkash as co-founder.
interesting_fact: He has built two data unicorns back to back, Sisense and Firebolt, and won a World Technology Award for inventing Sisense's 'In-Chip' analytics engine.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career at 16 as a developer at Gilon Systems, then Israel's largest database integrator. Working on MDX compilers there, he foresaw columnar in-memory databases becoming pervasive, the idea behind Sisense's technology.
notes: The CEO handover to Benjamin Wagner is per Firebolt's current About page; the date was not verified. He appeared on the Zero Prime podcast (E32, 'Lightning strikes twice'), useful prep. Firebolt publishes no press email; the contact form is the official route.

name: Liang Jiadong
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CTO, Unisound (云知声, HKEX: 9678) [assuming 'Liang Jiadong' = Liang Jia'en 梁家恩]
profile: Unisound's co-founders are CEO Huang Wei and Chairman/CTO Dr. Liang Jia'en (梁家恩); 'Liang Jiadong' appears to be a mis-romanisation of the latter. A USTC graduate, Liang spent five years at the CAS Institute of Automation and joined Shanda Innovation Institute before co-founding the speech-AI company in 2011-12. Unisound listed in Hong Kong on June 30, 2025.
interesting_fact: A Guangxi native, in 2025 he was appointed to Guangxi's AI strategy advisory expert committee, and Unisound signed to set up an 'ASEAN headquarters' project with the Nanning government.
deep_cut_fact: In March 2013 Unisound beat iFlytek to supply voice control for Luo Yonghao's Smartisan 'Hammer ROM' launch; though live demos failed amid venue noise, Liang thanked Luo for putting Unisound 'on the big screen of the National Convention Center.'
notes: Name in input ('Liang Jiadong') does not match any Unisound founder exactly; the closest is co-founder Liang Jia'en (梁家恩). Confirm before outreach. He has worked on speech recognition since 2001 and is a USTC alumnus like iFlytek founder Liu Qingfeng.

name: Li Xiaohan
current_role: Executive Director & Vice President of R&D, Unisound AI Technology (云知声, HKEX: 9678)
profile: Li Xiaohan (李霄寒) is a founding-team member of Unisound, the Beijing speech-recognition and AI company started in 2012 by Huang Wei, Liang Jia'en and others, which makes voice AI for smart devices, healthcare and its 'Shanhai' large language model. Unisound listed on the Hong Kong main board on 30 June 2025; he is an executive director overseeing R&D.
interesting_fact: Unisound, which once powered many of China's smart speakers, listed in Hong Kong on 30 June 2025 after more than a decade as a voice-AI unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: Before Unisound he spent 2005-2009 at Motorola China Research Center developing AI for embedded devices (after a stint as a tech manager at Motorola Mobile), and holds both a BS and PhD from USTC; in 2023 the Chinese Academy of Sciences certified him a senior engineer.
notes: Correct Chinese name is 李霄寒 (not 李晓汉). Technical, low public profile; route via Unisound IR. marketing@ is the company's general marketing inbox, not a dedicated press line.

name: Kang Heng
current_role: Executive Director and Vice President (IoT), Unisound AI Technology (HKEX: 9678)
profile: Dr. Kang Heng (康恒) is a member of the founding team of Unisound, the Beijing speech-recognition and AI company founded in 2012 that listed in Hong Kong on June 30, 2025. He is an executive director and runs its IoT business (voice AI chips and smart-device solutions). He holds a PhD in pattern recognition from the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Automation.
interesting_fact: Unisound was among China's early voice-AI unicorns and became one of the first Chinese AI speech companies to list in Hong Kong (June 2025).
deep_cut_fact: Before Unisound he spent 2007-2011 as a researcher at Canon Information Technology (Beijing), working on multilingual speech synthesis and multimodal interaction; his undergraduate degree (Tsinghua, 2000) was in mechanical engineering.
notes: Technical co-founder, not the public face (CEO Huang Wei and chairman/CTO Liang Jia'en are). No personal public channels found; IR email not verified, so route via company contact page or HKEX-filed company secretary.

name: Zhi Zhengchun
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder (~72.7%) of Beijing Shanyin Qiyi Technology (Wecash/闪银); listed as founder of the affiliated Jingsuan (鲸算) group; left the operating entity's management roster in 2022
profile: George Zhi Zhengchun (支正春) founded Wecash (闪银) in Beijing in 2013, an AI/big-data credit-scoring and online lending platform that raised a US$80M Series C in 2017 from investors including IDG and 9F. Before that he ran mobile-internet business at 9F Group (玖富). Wecash later moved into tech-export services under the Jingsuan (鲸算) brand.
interesting_fact: At 32, Zhi was driving a joint bid by Wecash and partners for one of Hong Kong's first virtual-bank licences in 2018, after pitching Wecash as China's first online credit-evaluation platform.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from Peking University in 2009 with a double bachelor's degree in physics and economics, and from August 2013 led 9F's whole mobile-internet business before going full-time on Wecash.
notes: Chinese name 支正春; English name George Zhi. Per Lanjinger (Mar 2022, https://www.lanjinger.com/d/179878) the Wecash app and official WeChat account were taken offline and he and other directors left the operating company's management list, though he remains controlling shareholder. Current activity unclear; the business is effectively dormant. No published contact found.

name: Zhao Guoqing
current_role: Chairman, Beijing Zhongguancun Kejin Technology (ZKJ, 中关村科金); founder, chairman and (since May 2026) again legal representative of Mashang Consumer Finance (马上消费), Chongqing
profile: Zhao Guoqing (赵国庆) is a former JD.com vice chairman and chief strategy officer who left before JD's 2014 IPO and founded Mashang Consumer Finance in 2015, now one of China's largest consumer-finance firms (200M+ users). He also chairs ZKJ, a Beijing enterprise-AI company whose Dezhu (得助) LLM platform sells AI agents to banks and other industries. He holds a Nankai BA, a Tianjin University PhD and a CEIBS EMBA.
interesting_fact: He was named one of the 'Top 10 Chongqing Economic Figures of the Year' in 2018 and again in April 2025, and is the only person from a financial institution picked as a national 'Ten Thousand Talents' sci-tech entrepreneurship leader.
deep_cut_fact: Known for 'entrepreneurial asceticism': he has walked 100+ km across desert carrying his own pack with no resupply, flies about 10 laps of the earth a year but stays in budget or even capsule hotels, and quoted Jobs' 'Stay Hungry, Stay Foolish' in Mashang's 8th-anniversary staff letter.
notes: Chinese name 赵国庆. The ZKJ link is confirmed by The Paper/Economic Observer (May 2026, https://m.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_33274084), which lists him as chairman of Mashang and of Beijing Zhongguancun Kejin, and by 36Kr's ZKJ business-registration data. Don't confuse him with academics of the same name. The contact is Mashang's published business-cooperation inbox, not a press office; zkj.com was unreachable from this session. Caixin forum bio: https://www.caixinglobal.com/2024/1980/102236444/

name: Amit Bendov
current_role: CEO and Co-Founder, Gong (Revenue AI platform)
profile: Israeli software executive who co-founded Gong in 2015 with Eilon Reshef and has led it as CEO since. Gong records and analyzes sales calls, emails and deals with AI to guide revenue teams; it serves 5,000+ customers and is now pushing AI agents that take actions, not just surface insights. Hurun lists him among unicorn founders (company valued ~$4B+).
interesting_fact: Bendov frames Gong's next phase as AI agents that 'don't just surface insights, but take action and deliver results at enterprise scale' (2026 press release).
deep_cut_fact: Before Gong he was CEO of BI company SiSense and earlier CMO of Panaya, giving him 20+ years in hyper-growth enterprise software before founding Gong.
notes: Accessible, media-active founder-CEO; best route is Gong PR (press@gong.io) or LinkedIn, where he posts regularly. Fits AI/entrepreneurship themes more than energy/data centers.

name: Eilon Reshef
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Gong
profile: Israeli software entrepreneur who co-founded Gong with CEO Amit Bendov in 2015 and leads its product and engineering. Gong's AI records and analyses sales calls and emails to give revenue teams insights, forecasts and automated next steps; it was valued at about $7B+ at its 2021 peak. He previously co-founded Webcollage, an e-commerce content SaaS platform.
interesting_fact: Gong grew from a 2015 seed round to 1,000 customers by 2020 and added Gong Forecast and Gong Engage by 2023; Gartner named it a Leader in its 2026 Magic Quadrant for Revenue Action Orchestration.
deep_cut_fact: Gong's origin: Bendov was CEO of another company that had just had its worst quarter ever with no idea why, so he called his friend Reshef to explore using AI to understand what customers were actually saying, which became Gong.
notes: Hurun's '$4B valuation' is dated; Gong's last priced round (2021) was about $7.25B. Note: the $7B+ valuation is from widely reported 2021 funding news, not the cited Gong page. Route via Gong PR.

name: Erik Bernhardsson
current_role: Founder and CEO, Modal Labs (serverless GPU cloud for AI inference, training and sandboxes), New York
profile: Swedish-born engineer (KTH physics MSc) who spent six years at Spotify, building the first version of its music recommendations (Related Artists, Radio, Discover Weekly), then ran Better.com's 300-person tech team (2015-21). He founded Modal, which lets developers scale from zero to thousands of GPUs with usage-based pricing; it says it has raised over $1.2B.
interesting_fact: At Spotify he open-sourced Luigi, a workflow engine with 10,000+ GitHub stars, and Annoy, an approximate-nearest-neighbour library that predates today's vector databases.
deep_cut_fact: He has a gold medal from the International Olympiad in Informatics, competed twice at the ACM-ICPC world finals, and in high school won both the Swedish physics and Swedish programming competitions; he has also never had a driver's license and played piano for 10+ years.
notes: Very public and approachable: long-running blog (erikbern.com), active on X, gives talks. Strong data-centre/GPU-capacity angle. LinkedIn listed is Modal's company page.

name: Jean-Philippe Fricker
current_role: Co-founder and Chief System Architect, Cerebras Systems (Nasdaq: CBRS)
profile: J.P. Fricker is one of five Cerebras co-founders (2015) who previously worked together at SeaMicro (sold to AMD for $334M in 2012). Cerebras builds wafer-scale AI chips and systems; it signed a 750MW, $10B+ compute deal with OpenAI in Jan 2026 and IPO'd on Nasdaq in May 2026, raising $5.55B. He is one of the four 'Founders' holding high-vote Class B stock.
interesting_fact: To make wafer-scale chips work, the founders had to invent custom cooling, defect-routing software and even a machine that drives 40 screws into the wafer simultaneously without cracking it. The May 2026 IPO was the largest U.S. tech IPO since 2019.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cerebras he was Senior Hardware Architect at rack-scale flash startup DSSD (bought by EMC) and at SeaMicro designed three generations of fabric-based computers; earlier he ran hardware engineering at Riverstone Networks and Alcatel-Lucent. He holds an MS in EE from EPFL (Lausanne) and is named on 42 patents.
notes: Engineering-focused co-founder with little press presence; CEO Andrew Feldman is the public face. Natural fit for a data-center/AI hardware podcast (wafer-scale systems, cooling, power). Route via Cerebras corporate/communications; no personal contact published.

name: Michael James
current_role: Co-founder of Cerebras Systems (Nasdaq: CBRS); named as one of four 'Founders' holding Class B stock in the May 2026 IPO prospectus (not listed as an executive officer or director)
profile: One of five engineers who founded Cerebras in 2015 (with Andrew Feldman, Gary Lauterbach, Sean Lie and Jean-Philippe Fricker) to build wafer-scale AI chips. Cerebras' WSE chips and CS systems power AI training/inference data centers and cloud; it IPO'd on Nasdaq in May 2026, raising $5.55B at $185/share - the largest US tech IPO since 2019 - opening at a ~$95B valuation.
interesting_fact: Building a dinner-plate-sized wafer-scale chip forced the founders to invent new cooling, software that routes around manufacturing defects, and even a machine that drives 40 screws into the wafer simultaneously without cracking it.
deep_cut_fact: Cerebras was a reunion: all five co-founders had worked together at SeaMicro, the energy-efficient microserver startup Feldman and Lauterbach founded in 2007 and sold to AMD in 2012 for $334 million.
notes: Common name - ensure outreach targets the Cerebras co-founder. Founder status confirmed by Cerebras' own timeline (https://www.cerebras.ai/company) and the 424B4 prospectus. Technical, low-profile founder; his exact current title (reportedly a chief-architect role) was not verified this session. Strong data-center fit; CEO Andrew Feldman is the public voice.

name: Bradley Mascho
current_role: Unverified; a 2026 Mortgage Bankers Association speaker page reportedly lists him as Chief Digital Officer at BWE (not opened)
profile: Columbus, Ohio entrepreneur who founded CrossChx (2012), the healthcare-AI company that built the 'Olive' automation product and later rebranded as Olive (once valued ~$4B). In 2018 he became the first Chief AI Officer in the government-tech industry at contractor NCI Inc.; NCI's AI unit later became Empower AI. Olive itself wound down in 2023.
interesting_fact: NCI created the chief AI officer role for him in Jan 2018, months after partnering with CrossChx to pilot its Olive automation product with the U.S. Army and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services.
notes: Not a current billionaire: Olive shut down and oliveai.com now redirects to waystar.com. Later served as CMO/communications chief at Empower AI (2023, per WashingtonExec). Current role unverified. No published contact found.

name: Sean Lane
current_role: Founder, Ghostdog Inc. (incorporated July 2023); former founder & CEO of Olive AI (wound down Oct 2023)
profile: Sean Lane is a Columbus, Ohio serial founder. He co-founded CrossChx in 2012, which he rebuilt in 2017 as Olive, an AI 'digital workforce' that automated hospital revenue-cycle and admin work. Olive raised over US$850M and hit a ~US$4B valuation in 2021 before winding down in late 2023 and selling its product lines. He then set up a new company, Ghostdog.
interesting_fact: Olive became one of Ohio's best-known unicorns (~US$4B valuation in 2021) by selling healthcare systems AI 'employees' to handle repetitive revenue-cycle tasks; before that Lane had founded technology companies in Ohio, Maryland and Virginia.
deep_cut_fact: He met his CrossChx co-founder Brad Mascho at Miami University (Ohio), where both were in the Air Force ROTC programme, before they went on to separate careers in the Baltimore-Washington area.
notes: Becker's says Lane incorporated Ghostdog Inc. in July 2023, months before Olive's shutdown (https://beckershospitalreview.com/digital-health/olive-ai-founder-has-a-new-startup.html); what Ghostdog does isn't public. Olive's collapse is a sensitive subject, so frame outreach around his founder journey and healthcare AI. No verified personal site or social account captured.

name: Yang Hongxin
current_role: Chairman (and CEO), SVOLT Energy Technology (蜂巢能源), Changzhou, Jiangsu
profile: Yang Hongxin (杨红新) leads SVOLT, the battery maker that grew out of a power-battery project team formed in 2012 inside Great Wall Motor's orbit and was incorporated in 2018 in Changzhou. SVOLT makes EV cells/packs and grid and home energy-storage systems (14 production sites, 13,000+ staff) and is a three-time BNEF Tier 1 storage supplier; Hurun valued it at about $4B as a unicorn.
interesting_fact: In Oct 2026 SVOLT began volume production in Changzhou of its 100kWh 'Dragon Armor' (龙鳞甲) hybrid solid-liquid fast-charge pack: 900V, 6C charging, ~500 km of range in 12 minutes, 3,000+ cycle life.
deep_cut_fact: He is a public contrarian on solid-state hype: he argues hybrid solid-liquid batteries are not a stopgap but will persist long-term as one of the mainstream routes, especially for ternary (NCM) EV chemistries.
