notes: Good energy-storage angle (BNEF Tier 1 storage, overseas expansion). Contact is company-level only. His exact title mix (chairman/CEO) and Great Wall Motor background were not re-verified because the search quota ran out; the SVOLT site confirms him as chairman (董事长).

name: Ariel Berkman
current_role: Co-founder and founding CTO of OwnBackup / Own Company (acquired by Salesforce, Nov 2024); later listed as Chief Product Security Officer; post-acquisition role not public
profile: Israeli engineer Ariel Berkman co-founded OwnBackup around 2014-15 as a part-time project to back up SaaS data, and served as founding CTO. Renamed Own, it grew to US$170M+ ARR protecting Salesforce and other SaaS data and was bought by Salesforce for about US$1.9B in cash, completed 18 Nov 2024. He had earlier co-founded Recover Information Technologies.
interesting_fact: Own was one of Salesforce's largest-ever acquisitions (about US$1.9B net of its existing stake) and one of Israel's notable SaaS exits of 2024.
deep_cut_fact: The company found its CEO by accident: at a Herzliya coffee-shop meeting in 2014 with Berkman and his co-founders, Sam Gutmann (on holiday in Israel) tagged along to Ori Yankelev's 'job interview'; halfway through, the founders told Ori to stop selling himself and asked Sam to be CEO.
notes: Co-founder status confirmed by Salesforce Ventures' portfolio page (https://salesforceventures.com/?p=1675), which lists Berkman, Daniel Gershuni and Ori Yankelev. No 2025-26 news of a new venture. Very low public profile; no verified personal site or social account captured.

name: Daniel Gershuni
current_role: Co-founder, OwnBackup / Own Company (acquired by Salesforce 2024); now reportedly a serial entrepreneur and startup advisor
profile: Daniel Gershuni is one of the Israeli co-founders of OwnBackup (later Own Company), the SaaS data backup and recovery platform that Salesforce bought for about US$1.9B in 2024. Third-party profiles list him as Chief Product Officer / VP Sales & Product in the early years and as a co-founder of website-monitoring firm Uptime.com; he now advises early-stage startups.
interesting_fact: OwnBackup started as a part-time side project that backed up data from several platforms (Facebook, Google, Twitter, LinkedIn, Gmail, Salesforce) before narrowing its focus to Salesforce, which took it to US$100M+ ARR.
notes: Co-founder status confirmed by Salesforce Ventures' portfolio page (https://salesforceventures.com/?p=1675) and Crunchbase. The Uptime.com and Sodyo roles come only from aggregators (TheOrg, Happenstance), so verify before using. Very low public profile; no verified contacts found.

name: Eran Cohen
current_role: Co-founder of OwnBackup (now Own Company, part of Salesforce); no active role there since at least 2020 - current role unknown
profile: One of the 2015 co-founders of OwnBackup, alongside Sam Gutmann (CEO), Ariel Berkman (CTO) and Ori Yankelev, per Globes. The Israeli-founded, New Jersey-headquartered SaaS backup company grew to nearly 7,000 customers, was renamed Own Company, and was bought by Salesforce for about $1.9B in cash (closed Nov 2024). Globes reported in 2020 he no longer had an active position.
interesting_fact: Own started as a backup tool for Salesforce data and was bought by Salesforce itself for ~$1.9B after Salesforce Ventures had already taken ~10%.
deep_cut_fact: OwnBackup began as a part-time project; its founders recruited their CEO, Sam Gutmann, at a Herzliya coffee shop where he had tagged along on Ori Yankelev's job interview while on vacation - they told Yankelev to stop pitching himself because they were really hiring a CEO.
notes: Founder identity confirmed via Globes (https://en.globes.co.il/en/article-1001334990), but very common name and no current role or public channels found - verify the right Eran Cohen (e.g., LinkedIn) before outreach. The coffee-shop story is from Gutmann's account and is about the company, not Cohen personally.

name: Ori Yankelev
current_role: Partner & CRO (Operating Partner, Platform CRO), Team8, Israeli venture-creation firm
profile: Ori Yankelev was a founding member of OwnBackup/Own, joining as VP Sales and rising to CRO and Chief Business Officer; under him Own's ARR grew 100%+ a year to over US$170M with 800+ staff before Salesforce bought it for about US$1.9B in 2024. He now runs go-to-market support and business development across Team8's portfolio. He has a BBA (magna cum laude) from UMass Amherst.
interesting_fact: Before Own he worked in venture capital and on go-to-market at Intronis (acquired by Barracuda Networks), and he was the friend who brought future CEO Sam Gutmann to the coffee-shop meeting that created Own's leadership team.
deep_cut_fact: He walked into Own's founding meeting in Herzliya treating it as his own 'unofficial job interview'; the founders told him 'Please stop selling yourself. We're not hiring a sales guy', then offered the CEO job to his friend Sam Gutmann. Ori had personally lost Salesforce data while consulting, one reason the team believed in the problem.
notes: Full name appears as Ori Baruch Yankelev on Team8. Salesforce Ventures lists him as 'CRO & Founder' (https://salesforceventures.com/?p=1675). He left Own around May 2024, before the Salesforce deal closed. Best route is via Team8, where he manages business development.

name: Sam Gutmann
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of OwnBackup / Own Company (acquired by Salesforce, Nov 2024); current position not verified
profile: Sam Gutmann co-founded and led OwnBackup (renamed Own Company), a cloud data backup, recovery and data-management provider that began as a Salesforce AppExchange partner in 2012 and reached a ~$3B private valuation. Salesforce, already a ~10% holder via Salesforce Ventures, agreed to buy Own for about $1.9B in cash in Sept 2024 and closed the deal on 18 Nov 2024.
interesting_fact: By the time of the Salesforce deal, Own was trusted by nearly 7,000 customers to safeguard mission-critical SaaS data; Gutmann said its mission had expanded 'from preventing data loss in the cloud to helping customers ... accelerate AI-driven innovation.'
notes: Unicorn founder rather than billionaire; post-acquisition role (Salesforce or new venture) not confirmed - web-search quota ran out mid-lane, so check LinkedIn before outreach. Salesforce PR is only a corporate route. Fit: SaaS data protection / data for AI, not energy.

name: Tony Han
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, WeRide Inc. (Nasdaq: WRD; HKEX: 800)
profile: Tony Xu Han (49) was a tenured University of Missouri professor in computer vision/ML, then Chief Scientist of Baidu's autonomous-driving unit (2014-17), before founding WeRide in 2017. WeRide runs robotaxis and robobuses with driverless permits in ~9 countries (often with Uber); it listed on Nasdaq in 2024 and Hong Kong in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: He voluntarily committed to a three-year lock-up on all his WeRide shares from October 2025, around the Hong Kong dual listing.
deep_cut_fact: Han was an original contributor to Baidu's DeepSpeech2 speech-recognition system, which MIT Technology Review counted among its 10 Breakthrough Technologies of 2016; he earned degrees from Beijing Jiaotong (1998), the University of Rhode Island (2002) and a UIUC PhD (2008).
notes: WeRide is a heavy AI-training compute user; strong angle on autonomous driving + AI infrastructure. Press route via pr@weride.ai.

name: Jason F. VandeBoom
current_role: Founder & CEO, ActiveCampaign (Chicago)
profile: VandeBoom founded ActiveCampaign in Chicago in 2003 as on-premise email-marketing software, then shifted it to a cloud SaaS marketing-automation/CRM platform for small and mid-size businesses (150,000+ customers). It took no outside money until a 2016 Series A and hit a $3B+ valuation in a 2021 Tiger Global-led round.
interesting_fact: ActiveCampaign was bootstrapped for about 13 years: its first external investment was a $20M Series A from Silversmith Capital in 2016, followed by $100M (2020) and $240M (2021, $3B+ valuation).
deep_cut_fact: To make the jump to SaaS, ActiveCampaign cut its product line from eight on-premise solutions down to one, focused on marketing automation, a pivot the company credits for its later growth.
notes: No published press email found on the company site (only sales/help inboxes). Infra/AI angle is modest; he's a bootstrapping-to-unicorn founder story.

name: He Xianhan
current_role: Representative Director, President & Group CEO, Ferrotec Holdings (Tokyo; TSE) - Ferrotec's equity affiliate Hangzhou Zhongxin Wafer (FTWafer) is the Hurun-listed unicorn
profile: Chinese-born executive (賀賢漢) who heads Ferrotec, a Japan-listed group supplying semiconductor-equipment parts, quartz, ceramics, silicon wafers, power-semiconductor substrates and thermoelectric modules, with large operations in China. Hurun credits him as founder of FTWafer, i.e. Hangzhou Zhongxin Wafer Semiconductor, a Ferrotec-affiliated 8/12-inch silicon wafer maker valued at ~$2B.
interesting_fact: Ferrotec's core technologies - magnetic fluid (ferrofluid) and thermoelectric modules - trace back to the Apollo program; the company began in 1980 as the Japanese subsidiary of a US firm, went independent in 1987 and in 1999 bought its former Nasdaq-listed US parent via a friendly tender offer.
deep_cut_fact: In his CEO message he calls Ferrotec's origin story 'a bit unusual': the child company ended up acquiring its parent, reversing the parent-child relationship 12 years after independence.
notes: Identity mapping FTWafer = Hangzhou Zhongxin Wafer (Ferrotec equity affiliate) is inferred, not confirmed by a source read here; He Xianhan as Ferrotec President/Group CEO is confirmed (board list as of 26 Jun 2026). Japanese/Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Yang Yongzheng

profile: Hurun credits Yang Yongzheng as founder of Mattson Technology (valued ~$3B). Mattson, a Fremont, CA wafer-processing equipment maker, was founded in 1988 by Brad Mattson and acquired in 2016 by Beijing E-Town Dragon; parent Beijing E-Town Semiconductor (BEST) listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in July 2025. name: Liu Qi
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, PingCAP (maker of the TiDB distributed SQL database), known in English as Max Liu
profile: Infrastructure engineer who co-founded PingCAP in Beijing in 2015 with Dongxu Huang and Qiu Cui after working on Redis infrastructure at Wandou Labs. PingCAP built the open-source TiDB database and TiKV storage engine (a CNCF project), was valued at about $3B in 2021, and is now headquartered in Sunnyvale, pitching TiDB as infrastructure for AI agents.
interesting_fact: PingCAP's TiKV storage engine was accepted into the Cloud Native Computing Foundation in 2018, and TiDB is now pitched as AI-agent infrastructure, with Moonshot's Kimi AI announced as a customer.
deep_cut_fact: Before PingCAP, he and his co-founders built Codis, an open-source clustering solution for Redis, while working on Redis infrastructure at Chinese internet company Wandou Labs (Wandoujia).
notes: Publicly goes by Max Liu; Chinese name 刘奇. Active in open-source community talks. PR agency contact is the published media route for PingCAP/TiDB.

name: Wojciech Zaremba
current_role: Co-founder, OpenAI
profile: Polish computer scientist (b. 1988, Kluczbork) who co-founded OpenAI in 2015 after a PhD at NYU under Yann LeCun and Rob Fergus, with research stints at Google Brain and Facebook AI Research. At OpenAI he first led robotics, including a robot hand that solved a Rubik's Cube, then led teams on GPT models, GitHub Copilot and Codex.

deep_cut_fact: He earned both his bachelor's (1991) and master's (1995) in electronic engineering at Tsinghua University. He joined OmniVision in June 1997, when it was still a young image-sensor startup, and stayed until founding Black Sesame in July 2016.

name: Krste Asanovic
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Architect, SiFive; Chief Architect, RISC-V International; Professor Emeritus, UC Berkeley EECS
profile: Computer architect (born 1965; Berkeley PhD 1998; MIT faculty 1998-2007) who has led Berkeley's open RISC-V instruction-set project since its 2010 start. He co-founded the RISC-V Foundation (now RISC-V International) and in 2015 SiFive to commercialize RISC-V cores. He co-directs Berkeley's SLICE lab (Chipyard, FireSim, Gemmini).
interesting_fact: RISC-V, the free and open instruction set he co-created at Berkeley in 2010, is now a global alternative to Arm and x86, used from microcontrollers to AI accelerators. He was elected an ACM Fellow in 2018 for 'the open RISC-V instruction set and Agile hardware'.
deep_cut_fact: His 1998 Berkeley PhD thesis, under John Wawrzynek, was titled 'Vector Microprocessors', foreshadowing the RISC-V vector extension. He was tenured at MIT in 2005 before returning to Berkeley in 2007 to co-found the Par Lab, the parallel-computing lab where RISC-V was born.
notes: His university email is published on his own Berkeley page as 'krste at berkeley dot edu'. SiFive PR is an alternative route. A strong fit for a data-center/AI-silicon episode (RISC-V in AI accelerators).

name: Yunsup Lee
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Technology Officer, SiFive
profile: Yunsup Lee co-created the open RISC-V instruction set and the first RISC-V processors as a UC Berkeley PhD student, then co-founded SiFive in 2015 with Andrew Waterman and Krste Asanovic to commercialize RISC-V core IP. SiFive's cores ship in 2B+ devices; it raised a $400M Series G in 2026 (~$3.65B valuation) to push into AI data centres, including NVIDIA NVLink Fusion support.
interesting_fact: He was one of the original authors of the RISC-V spec 'from Day 1' and co-designed the first RISC-V microprocessors at Berkeley; SiFive is now targeting AI data-centre CPUs.
deep_cut_fact: His 2016 Berkeley PhD thesis introduced the Hwacha 'decoupled vector-fetch' architecture (committee included David Patterson), and at Hot Chips 2015 he presented Raven3, a 28nm RISC-V vector chip with on-die switched-capacitor DC-DC converters.
notes: Strong data-center fit (RISC-V for AI data centres, $400M 2026 round). Press email is SiFive Corporate Communications (David Miller) as listed on 2026 press releases. Hot Chips slides: https://old.hotchips.org/wp-content/uploads/hc_archives/hc27/HC27.25-Tuesday-Epub/HC27.25.70-Processors-Epub/HC27.25.731-RISC-V-Lee-UCB-V4.with-backup.pdf

name: Joshua Motta
current_role: CEO & Co-Founder, Coalition, Inc. (cyber insurance / 'Active Insurance')

Coalition pairs cyber insurance with continuous risk scanning and incident response, was valued at $5B in 2022, and partners with Allianz for capacity.

name: Alexi Robichaux
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, BetterUp (digital and AI-powered coaching platform)
profile: USC political-science graduate who worked as a product manager at Socialcast and became a VMware product executive at 25 after its 2011 acquisition. In 2013 he co-founded BetterUp with Eduardo Medina to bring evidence-based professional coaching to whole workforces; it reached a ~$4.7-5B valuation in 2021 and now pairs human coaches with AI coaching.

name: Eddie Medina
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer, BetterUp
profile: Eduardo 'Eddie' Medina cofounded BetterUp, the coaching and 'human + AI' leadership-development platform, with CEO Alexi Robichaux in 2013. As COO he runs coaching, operations and delivery for enterprise clients; BetterUp was valued at ~$4.7B in 2021 and now sells AI coaching, incl. inside Microsoft 365 Copilot. name: Cliff Click
current_role: CTO, CRATUS Technology (lidar machine perception / industrial IoT automation), since Feb 2019; co-founder of H2O.ai
profile: Compiler engineer Cliff Click (Texas A&M BS/MS, Rice PhD 1995) was primary architect of Sun's HotSpot JVM server compiler (C2), co-founded Azul Systems (2002), and co-founded H2O.ai (2012), designing its distributed in-memory math engine. He later was CTO of fintech Neurensic and since 2019 CTO of CRATUS; he also hosts the open 'Coffee Compiler Club'.
interesting_fact: His Rice PhD work produced the 'sea of nodes' intermediate representation, which became the basis of HotSpot's C2 JIT - code that still optimizes much of the world's Java.
deep_cut_fact: He describes himself as having been 'writing compilers since age 15', holds 20+ patents, and runs a weekly 'Coffee Compiler Club' video call open to anyone interested in language design.
notes: Hacker/engineer personality, approachable in the compiler/PL community; technical deep-dives (JIT, GC, sea of nodes, ML infra) would land well. Coffee Compiler Club recordings are on YouTube (link via https://lists.puremagic.com/pipermail/digitalmars-d-announce/2021-December/058199.html).

name: Sri Satish Ambati
current_role: Founder and CEO, H2O.ai (Mountain View, CA)
profile: Sri Ambati co-founded H2O.ai in 2012 (originally 0xdata, with Java veteran Cliff Click) to build the open-source H2O ML platform, later adding Driverless AI and enterprise GenAI/agent products. He earlier co-founded Platfora and led engineering at DataStax. In 2026 H2O launched the tabH2O tabular foundation model and expanded an AI lab in Singapore.

name: Augusto Marietti

name: Brad Goldoor
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Employee Experience Officer, Phenom (Ambler, PA) - most recent reported title (formerly Chief People Officer)

public_contacts.value: jennifer.lyons@phenompeople.com (Phenom Director of PR, media inquiries)

name: Mahe Bayireddi
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Phenom (Phenom People), Ambler/Philadelphia
profile: Co-founded Phenom around 2010-11 with Hari Bayireddy and Brad Goldoor to build an AI-powered talent-experience platform for hiring, employee development and retention. name: Liu Yong
current_role: Founder, Chairman & President, DAS Solar (一道新能源), Quzhou, Zhejiang
profile: Solar-industry veteran who founded DAS Solar in Quzhou in August 2018, betting early on N-type TOPCon cells; it reached ~9th in global module shipments in 2024 (InfoLink). interesting_fact: DAS Solar positions itself as an N-type TOPCon pioneer (lab cell efficiency >26%) and runs flagship 'scenario' projects such as desert ecological restoration in Gansu and fishery-PV integration in Hainan.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding DAS Solar he was a senior executive at two other leading PV makers, JA Solar and Jolywood (中来股份); company filings list his name in passport form as 'LIUYONG'.
notes: Common name - confirm via DAS Solar. Active on the conference circuit (Boao Forum 2024, Global Green Energy Leaders Dialogue) with English-language PR, so reachable via DAS Solar's international PR. Company now state-controlled (Quzhou Industrial Holding); unicorn valuation dates from Hurun 2021-25.

name: Yin Jing
current_role: Founder and CEO, Cloudwise (云智慧, Beijing) - AIOps / IT operations and observability software
profile: Listed by Hurun as 'Yin Jing', the Cloudwise founder is Yin Jin (殷晋, 'Andy Yin'), CEO since 2010. Cloudwise began with the Jiankongbao (监控宝) website-monitoring SaaS for small businesses and grew into an AI-driven IT-operations platform for large enterprises; Sequoia China led its US$150m Series E in 2021, valuing it at about US$1bn.
interesting_fact: Cloudwise now pitches itself as 'Reliability for AI Infrastructure', selling AI agents for alert triage and autonomous incident resolution to 2,000+ enterprises.

name: Lv Shijie
current_role: Founder, Cloudwise (云智慧), Beijing-based AIOps/observability software company
profile: Lv Shijie (吕士杰, Shijie Lyu) founded Cloudwise in Beijing in 2009, starting in application performance monitoring and growing into an AI operations platform (observability, incident resolution, ITSM/CMDB) used by 2,000+ enterprises. name: Ren Yuancheng
current_role: Executive director (formerly chairman and CEO), Xinmai Semiconductor Technology (Hangzhou) Co. (芯迈半导体), which is seeking a Hong Kong IPO
profile: Ren Yuancheng (任远程), about 50, a power-electronics engineer, founded Xinmai Semiconductor in Hangzhou in 2019-20: a 'virtual IDM' power-chip firm backed by CATL and Xiaomi and valued around RMB 20bn (~$3bn). He was chairman/CEO until June 2025 (now executive director); the firm filed for a Hong Kong IPO a third time in July 2026.

He ran a China subsidiary of Monolithic Power Systems (2006-13), then was VP at JoulWatt, and was named a provincial 'leading talent' by Hangzhou's Binjiang high-tech zone in 2014.

I could not confirm 'Jupiter' as Xinmai's English name, so verify before outreach. No published contact found; the HKEX prospectus would list company contacts.

name: Kannan Muthukkaruppan
current_role: Co-founder and President of Yugabyte (distributed PostgreSQL database); some profiles list him as co-CEO with Karthik Ranganathan
profile: Database engineer. He spent 13 years on Oracle's PL/SQL compiler, then at Facebook built the HBase storage behind Messages, then worked on distributed storage at Nutanix. In 2016 he co-founded Yugabyte, maker of the open-source distributed SQL database YugabyteDB, with ex-Facebook colleagues Karthik Ranganathan and Mikhail Bautin, and was its founding CEO.
interesting_fact: He was the founding CEO of Yugabyte. In 2020 he handed the CEO role to Pivotal's ex-president Bill Cook and moved to President, Product Development. Before Yugabyte he spent about 13 years on Oracle's PL/SQL compiler and virtual machine team.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote Facebook's 2010 engineering post 'The Underlying Technology of Messages'. It explained why the team picked HBase over MySQL and Cassandra after weeks of benchmarking, to serve 350M users sending 15B+ messages a month.
notes: A technical founder who speaks at developer conferences (QCon, AsiaTechX). Sources conflict on his title (President vs co-CEO) and on whether Karthik Ranganathan is now sole CEO (May 2026 release), so confirm before outreach. The PR address was found through search excerpts of Business Wire releases; the pages themselves were blocked.

name: Karthik Ranganathan
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, Yugabyte (previously CTO)
profile: Karthik Ranganathan (BS IIT Madras, MS UT Austin) was one of Facebook's early database engineers from 2007, working on Cassandra and as an Apache HBase committer. In 2016 he co-founded Yugabyte with ex-Facebook colleagues Kannan Muthukkaruppan and Mikhail Bautin to build YugabyteDB, an open-source, Postgres-compatible distributed SQL database for cloud-native and AI workloads.
interesting_fact: When he joined Facebook in 2007 it had roughly 30-40 million monthly users; by the time he left about six years later it had passed one billion, an experience that shaped YugabyteDB's focus on scale.
deep_cut_fact: He worked on Facebook's inbox-search store before it was open-sourced and is credited with naming it 'Cassandra'; he has been quoted saying he was 'fortunate enough to have given it its name'.
notes: Very accessible technical founder; frequent conference speaker (QCon, PGConf, Postgres Conference) and podcast guest (Last Week in AWS). Cassandra-naming claim comes from secondary profiles, so verify or soften before quoting it to him. Good data-infrastructure fit.

name: Mikhail Bautin
current_role: Engineer at Google Cloud (Cloud SQL), reportedly since Nov 2024; co-founder and former software architect of Yugabyte
profile: Stony Brook CS PhD and Apache HBase committer at Facebook (ran HBase for Facebook Messages and search indexing). Co-founded Yugabyte in Feb 2016 with Kannan Muthukkaruppan and Karthik Ranganathan; YugabyteDB is an open-source, PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL database (unicorn in 2021). After ~8 years building it he reportedly joined Google Cloud to work on Cloud SQL in Nov 2024.
interesting_fact: Called the quietest of Yugabyte's three ex-Facebook founders, he was the architecture-focused one who understood at code level where HBase and Cassandra diverged and broke under load, knowledge that shaped YugabyteDB.
deep_cut_fact: Before databases he worked on NLP: as a Stony Brook PhD student he co-authored 'International Sentiment Analysis for News and Blogs' (ICWSM 2008, with Lohit Vijayarenu and Steven Skiena), machine-translating news in nine languages and scoring entity sentiment with the Lydia text-analysis system.
notes: Low public profile; per a 2025/26 origin-story article he left Yugabyte in Nov 2024 for Google Cloud (Cloud SQL) via a LinkedIn update only (not independently confirmed). Yugabyte's PR agency (Inkhouse) is listed but is unlikely to route to him now. Hurun lists no net worth for him.

name: Mike Murchison
current_role: Co-founder of Ada; becoming Chief AI Officer of the combined Dialpad-Ada company (deal announced Nov 4, 2026, expected to close ~Nov 12, 2026)
profile: Toronto serial entrepreneur (U of T cognitive science/HCI) who co-founded Ada with David Hariri in 2016 after their previous startup, Volley, was swamped by support requests. As CEO he built Ada into a $1bn+ AI customer-service agent platform (clients incl. Pinterest, Square, monday.com). In Nov 2026 Ada agreed to combine with Dialpad; Craig Walker becomes CEO and Murchison Chief AI Officer.
interesting_fact: Before building Ada, he and co-founder David Hariri worked as customer-service reps at several fast-growing tech companies to understand the problem first-hand; Ada then went through the AI stream of the Creative Destruction Lab at U of T's Rotman School.
deep_cut_fact: As a U of T cognitive-science and human-computer-interaction student he was regularly inspired by Geoffrey Hinton's research and by Steve Mann's wearable-computing lab; he was also in an early cohort of The Next 36 entrepreneurship program and is a Forbes 30 Under 30 alum.
notes: Role change: as of mid-Nov 2026 Ada is merging into Dialpad; use 'co-founder of Ada, Chief AI Officer at Dialpad' once closed. pr@ada.cx and PAN agency contact came via search of Ada's media center (site blocks scripted fetch); pr@dialpad.com verified on the deal release. Articulate, podcast-friendly AI-agents founder.

name: Aaron Kalb
current_role: Co-founder, Alation (data catalog / data intelligence); recent profiles list him as Chief Strategy Officer (title unconfirmed for 2026)
profile: Aaron Kalb co-founded Alation in 2012 with Satyen Sangani, Venky Ganti and Feng Niu, bringing design and linguistics to a team of database/ML researchers. The company pioneered the modern enterprise data catalog and reached unicorn status. Kalb has been Alation's head of product, its first Chief Data Officer (2019) and Chief Data & Analytics/Innovation Officer.
interesting_fact: In 2019 Kalb became Alation's first Chief Data Officer, a co-founder 'drinking his own champagne' by running the company's internal data governance and analytics, and he went on a global tour to collect best practices from other CDOs.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alation, Kalb was a designer and researcher in Apple's Siri Advanced Development Group. He studied Symbolic Systems (BS and MS) at Stanford, and Alation's own history describes him as the 'designer and linguist' of its founding team.
notes: Current title is inconsistent across sources (CSO vs CDAO vs Chief Innovation Officer; one profile says the CDAO role ended Aug 2023), so confirm on LinkedIn before outreach. Also linked to Alchemist Accelerator as a partner/mentor. Alation's media center lists marketingwebrequest@ for marketing/media requests.

name: Feng Niu
current_role: Co-founder of Alation (2012) and Lattice Data (acquired by Apple); current role not confirmed from a primary source
profile: Feng Niu is a database and machine-learning researcher (Tsinghua CS; UW-Madison PhD) who co-founded data-catalog company Alation in 2012 with Satyen Sangani, Venky Ganti and Aaron Kalb. Alation reached about a $1.7-2B valuation. He also co-founded Lattice Data (DeepDive-based dark-data extraction) with Chris Ré, which Apple acquired in 2017; profiles say he then worked at Apple.
interesting_fact: Niu is a co-author, with Ben Recht, Chris Ré and Stephen Wright, of 'Hogwild!' (2011), the lock-free parallel SGD paper that won the NeurIPS 2020 Test of Time Award and shaped how large ML models are trained.
deep_cut_fact: Hogwild! was written while Niu was a UW-Madison PhD student in the optimization group of the Wisconsin Institute for Discovery, which was in its first months of operation at the time. Alation's founding story credits him and Ganti with seeing data-discovery problems first-hand in research and at Google.
notes: Low public profile, with no verified personal site or social accounts. Secondary profiles claim Apple Research Scientist (2017-2020) and later CEO of a startup called Evidently, but neither is verified. The Alation founding-team description is at https://www.alation.com/about. Good AI-infrastructure/data angle for the podcast.

name: Satyen Sangani
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Alation, Inc. (Redwood City, CA)
profile: Satyen Sangani, an economist by training and former Oracle VP for financial-services analytical applications, co-founded Alation in 2012 with Aaron Kalb (ex-Apple Siri), Feng Niu and Venky Ganti. Alation pioneered the enterprise data catalog and was valued around $1.7-2B; in 2026 it relaunched its platform as AIOS, aimed at governing data and AI agents.
interesting_fact: Alation's founding idea combined Sangani's economics/Oracle view that big-company users can't find or trust data with Kalb's Siri-era natural-language work; its first 2015 product let employees query enterprise data in plain English.
deep_cut_fact: He has hosted Alation's podcast since 2022: launched as 'Data Radicals', it was relaunched in July 2026 as 'AI Radicals' for its fourth season, with biweekly interviews of data and AI leaders.

name: Venky Ganti
current_role: Snowflake (Head of Migrations, per Snowflake blog author page, 2026); co-founder of Alation
profile: Venky Ganti co-founded data-catalog company Alation and served as CTO, helping define the 'data catalog' category. He later co-founded Mesh Dynamics, worked at Google, and was SVP Product & Engineering at AI startup Numbers Station (acquired by Alation in 2025). He now works on data migrations at Snowflake.
interesting_fact: Before Alation he worked on Google's Dynamic Search Ads, building web-scale ML/data-enrichment pipelines, and at Microsoft Research he initiated and productized several projects.

He later founded Cocoon (acquired by Substack in 2021), designed the Substack and Linear mobile apps, and now leads generative-AI design at Meta.

name: Brian Peterson
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Dialpad
profile: Software engineer who co-founded Dialpad (originally UberConference) in 2011 with CEO Craig Walker, after both worked on Google Voice. He led engineering as SVP and in April 2021 became Dialpad's first CTO, overseeing its AI-powered calling, meetings and contact-center platform. In November 2026 Dialpad agreed to combine with the AI customer-service firm Ada in an all-share deal.

deep_cut_fact: Before Dialpad he was a senior software engineer at Google and built the front end of Google Voice, the product that grew out of Craig Walker's startup GrandCentral, which Google acquired.
notes: Hurun lists him as a Dialpad unicorn co-founder. The Dialpad-Ada merger was announced on 4 Nov 2026 (https://www.dialpad.com/press/dialpad-and-ada/), so his title may change. The HumanX page now returns 404; the AI-mandate detail is from search snippets. Common name: be sure to reference Dialpad. A good engineering-leader guest on AI adoption.

name: Craig Walker
current_role: Founder and CEO, Dialpad (AI-powered business communications / contact center)
profile: Craig Walker is a former M&A lawyer turned three-time founder. He ran the first Dialpad Communications (sold to Yahoo) and co-founded GrandCentral, which Google bought in 2007 and relaunched as Google Voice. After leaving Google he founded today's Dialpad in 2011, an AI-native communications and contact-center platform valued at about $2B with roughly 1,500 staff. It is now pushing agentic AI with Google Gemini integrations.
interesting_fact: He co-founded GrandCentral, the startup Google acquired in 2007 that became Google Voice.
deep_cut_fact: His career started in door-to-door dictation-equipment sales, which he credits for his grit. He then worked at Apple, went to law school, and did M&A at Wilson Sonsini before becoming a founder.
notes: A frequent podcast guest and open about founder lessons, so likely receptive. A June 2026 Dialpad release also lists pr@dialpad.com. His LinkedIn is linked from his official Dialpad author page.

profile: Listed as a technical co-founder of Dialpad (founded around 2011 as UberConference/Switch, with Craig Walker and Brian Peterson), where he was VP Engineering (telephony) and a board director. name: Jia Jiaya
current_role: Founder and Board Chairman, SmartMore (思谋科技); Chair Professor, HKUST and Dean of its von Neumann Institute
profile: Hunan-born computer-vision scientist (b. 1978; PhD HKUST 2004), ex-CUHK tenured professor and head of Tencent YouTu X-Lab, who founded SmartMore in 2019. SmartMore sells AI vision 'industrial agents' for inspection in EV batteries, autos, rail and electronics; a unicorn within two years, it filed for a Hong Kong IPO in March 2026.
interesting_fact: His lab produced LongLoRA (2023), a widely used technique for extending LLM context length, and the open-source multimodal model DreamOmni2 (2025); he has 200+ papers and over 100,000 citations.
deep_cut_fact: A keen photographer, in 2002 as an HKUST student he spent scholarship money on one of the early digital cameras; frustrated by the image quality, he wondered if algorithms could dehaze, deblur and denoise photos - the question that launched his computer-vision career.
notes: Accessible academic-founder; day-to-day SmartMore CEO is co-founder Shen Xiaoyong. SmartMore is in an HKEX IPO process (filed Mar 2026) - may limit what he can say. global@smartmore.com is a general company inbox; academic route via HKUST also possible.

name: Shen Xiaoyong
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, SmartMore (思谋科技)
profile: Chinese AI entrepreneur and CEO of SmartMore, an industrial machine-vision and AI company founded in 2019 with his former CUHK doctoral supervisor, Prof. Jia Jiaya, and a core team from Tencent's YouTu Lab. SmartMore sells AI inspection and smart-manufacturing systems to clients such as Bosch, Canon and P&G. It raised about US$200M in 2021 and reached a ~$1B+ valuation.
interesting_fact: SmartMore's founding team largely came from Tencent YouTu Lab, which Jia Jiaya joined from CUHK in 2017; Shen was one of Jia's CUHK students before becoming CEO of the spin-out.
notes: global@smartmore.com appears on the company's international site and is a general company inbox, not his personal one; sales@ and product@ are on smartmore.com/contact. Sources differ on whether Jia Jiaya or Shen is called 'founder'. Mostly covered in Chinese media (36Kr, QbitAI).

profile: Liu Shu (刘枢) co-founded Shenzhen/Hong Kong industrial-AI company SmartMore with CUHK professor Jia Jiaya and Shen Xiaoyong, and leads its R&D, including the IndustryGPT multimodal industrial model and AI visual-inspection equipment for manufacturing. SmartMore became a unicorn after large early funding rounds; he was named to Hurun's Under-30 entrepreneurs lists in 2020 and 2021.

notes: 'Co哥' nickname and 5-title claim from Shenzhen Special Zone Daily (sznews, May 2025; page not directly fetchable here, quoted via search). PANet authorship/COCO 1st place verified on arXiv. global@smartmore.com is a general company inbox on the site, not specifically press. Chinese outreach preferred.

profile: Hurun names Li Ruiyu among the founders of SmartMore, the Hong Kong/Shenzhen industrial-AI unicorn founded in 2019 by CUHK professor Jia Jiaya with former students including CEO Shen Xiaoyong, which sells machine-vision and AI inspection systems to manufacturers. name: Wu Gansha
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, UISEE Technology (驭势科技; listed in Hong Kong, 2026)
profile: Wu Gansha (吴甘沙), born 1976 in Nantong, Jiangsu, holds a Fudan CS master's and spent 16 years at Intel, ending as head of Intel Labs China, before co-founding UISEE in 2016. UISEE skipped robotaxis to focus on L4 autonomy in closed sites like airports, factories and mines, and listed in Hong Kong in 2026 at ~RMB 10B.
interesting_fact: UISEE's contrarian bet on commercial vehicles in closed scenarios paid off: H1 2026 revenue was about RMB 163M (+64.9% YoY) with a ~53% gross margin; Wu says his main daily question is simply how to 'stay alive'.
deep_cut_fact: He likes to argue autonomy in unit economics: how expensive a driver is in Europe and how many drivers one unmanned vehicle replaces, pitching the near-zero marginal cost of an 'AI driver' sold like software.
notes: Articulate, media-friendly founder who speaks at conferences (World Robot Conference etc.); good fit for AI/autonomy angle. UISEE's site lists pr@uisee.com for media and an IR site (ir.uisee.com).

name: Peng Jinzhan
current_role: Co-founder, deputy general manager and head of innovation business division, UISEE Technologies (驭势科技, HKEX: 1511)
profile: Peng Jinzhan (彭进展) is one of five co-founders of UISEE (驭势科技), a Beijing L4 autonomous-driving company focused on closed scenarios such as airports and factories. UISEE listed on HKEX (1511.HK) in May 2026; Peng is a controlling shareholder (~2% stake) and part of the acting-in-concert founder group.

notes: Chinese name 彭进展. Identity confirmed via HKEX prospectus (May 12, 2026), Directors and Senior Management section. Not a board director; low public profile. Spoke at TIC 2021 as co-founder/chief system architect. Business contact on site: winfuture@uisee.com.

profile: Hurun's unicorn-founder lists (2021-2025) name Jiang Yan as a founder of UISEE Technology, the Beijing autonomous-driving company led by co-founder, chairman and CEO Wu Gansha. name: Hitesh Sheth
current_role: President and CEO, Vectra AI (San Jose, CA)
profile: Networking veteran who leads AI threat-detection company Vectra AI (formerly Vectra Networks) as president and CEO, building it into a $1B+ unicorn. Previously COO of Aruba Networks, EVP/GM of switching at Juniper, and a senior switching executive at Cisco (metro Ethernet), after roles at Liberate Technologies and Oracle.
