Common name, so make sure you have the Austin-based CloudBees/Liquibase Ryan Campbell. No personal contact published; LinkedIn is the likely route but no verified URL found. He was likely a minority co-founder, so 'unicorn founder' wealth is probably modest.

name: Sacha Labourey
current_role: Co-founder and board member, CloudBees (stepped back from day-to-day role as Chief Strategy Officer in Feb 2025).
profile: Swiss software entrepreneur (b. Neuchâtel 1975, EPFL) who was CTO of open-source middleware firm JBoss through its 2006 sale to Red Hat, then GM of Red Hat middleware. In 2010 he founded CloudBees (enterprise Jenkins CI/CD, DevOps), serving as CEO then CSO; since 2025 he is a board member and advisor.
interesting_fact: CloudBees became the main commercial company behind Jenkins, the open-source CI/CD automation server, and appointed Jenkins creator Kohsuke Kawaguchi as its Chief Technology Officer.
deep_cut_fact: Before JBoss he founded Cogito Informatique, a Swiss consultancy specialising in application servers and middleware; at JBoss he wrote the first implementation of load-balancing/fail-over (clustering) for the JBoss application server and ran JBoss Europe before becoming CTO.
notes: Based in Neuchâtel, Switzerland; frequent conference speaker and blogger. Now off day-to-day CloudBees duties (new CEO Moritz Plassnig, June 2026), so reach him personally via LinkedIn rather than company PR. Cloud/DevOps rather than energy.

name: Vivek Pandey
current_role: Engineering executive; reportedly at Mirantis since Dec 2022 (unverified); previously VP Engineering at Shipa.io
profile: Software engineer who was one of CloudBees' founding team in 2010 (with Sacha Labourey, Francois Dechery and others), the Jenkins-based CI/CD company that reached unicorn status with a $150m raise in Dec 2021. Earlier he held engineering roles at Sun Microsystems and VMware; after CloudBees he was VP Engineering at cloud-native app platform Shipa.io.
interesting_fact: CloudBees, which he helped found, became a unicorn in Dec 2021 after raising $150m from Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Morgan Stanley, Bridgepoint, HSBC and others.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding CloudBees he was an engineer at Sun Microsystems and VMware, then later took his DevOps experience to Shipa.io, an 'application-as-code' platform for Kubernetes.
notes: Hurun 'founder' wealth figure is likely overstated: CloudBees' own pages name only Labourey and Dechery as co-founders; third-party profiles list Pandey among the 2010 founders. Common name; no verified personal channels found. Not a public-facing executive.

name: Guang Zhou
current_role: Founder and CEO, DeepRoute.ai (Shenzhen)
profile: Guang 'Maxwell' Zhou (周光) is a Tsinghua-educated AI researcher with a PhD from UT Dallas who worked on autonomous driving at Baidu USA before founding Shenzhen-based DeepRoute.ai in 2019, his second self-driving startup. DeepRoute builds map-free assisted/autonomous driving software for Chinese automakers (backed by Great Wall Motor and others) and pitches itself as 'AI infrastructure of the physical world'.
interesting_fact: He argues general-purpose AI models will let one self-driving system work in any city without HD maps: 'Waymo can only drive in a few places like Phoenix or San Francisco... The power of the new AI technologies... gives us the potential to drive everywhere.'
deep_cut_fact: He studied in Tsinghua University's 'Talent Class' undergraduate program, and before autonomous driving worked on IoT projects at Texas Instruments in Dallas while doing his AI PhD at UT Dallas.

public_contacts.value: Guest appearance: China EVs & More, Episode 3 (not his own show)

notes: Goes by Maxwell Zhou in English. Avoid his first startup Roadstar.ai (ended in a 2019 founder dispute). Gives English-language interviews; no published press email found (site is JS-rendered).

name: Hillel Kobrinsky
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Strategy Officer, DriveNets (Ra'anana, Israel)
profile: Former IDF brigadier general who founded Interwise (sold to AT&T in 2007), then co-founded DriveNets with Ido Susan in 2015 to replace proprietary routers with disaggregated white-box networking. DriveNets now sells Ethernet AI fabric for GPU clusters and raised a $410m Series D in June 2026.
interesting_fact: DriveNets, built to displace Cisco in telcos like AT&T, has pivoted into AI data-center networking as an Ethernet alternative to Nvidia's fabrics - it reports $1bn+ in secured business and has been cash-flow positive since 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech he was a brigadier general in the IDF Armored Corps; after selling Interwise he built and ran AT&T's Israeli R&D center, and from 2013-2015 was a senior adviser to Israel's Minister of Finance.
notes: Globes notes both founders 'recoil from media interviews' - expect a hard get. Also a co-founder and early secretary-general of Yair Lapid's Yesh Atid party (Globes). Press releases list agency contacts (Crystal Monahan, Martin Perlin) but emails are obfuscated. Strong AI data-center networking angle.

name: Ido Susan
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, DriveNets (Ra'anana, Israel)
profile: Serial Israeli founder Ido Susan co-founded Intucell, which invented self-optimising network (SON) software, and sold it to Cisco in 2013 for $475m after raising only $6m. He then spent about two years at Cisco. In 2015 he co-founded DriveNets with Hillel Kobrinsky to replace carrier routers with disaggregated, cloud-native software. DriveNets now also sells Ethernet fabrics for AI clusters and raised a $410m Series D in 2026.
interesting_fact: DriveNets, started to take on Cisco and Juniper at telecom operators, now competes with Nvidia in AI-factory networking. Globes reported a roughly $1bn five-year order book in 2025, and in 2026 it announced the first commercial long-distance 'scale-across' AI supercluster deployment.
deep_cut_fact: He never earned a university degree. He founded Intucell at about 24 and sold it to Cisco at 26, then founded a company to compete with his acquirer.
notes: Globes says both founders 'recoil from media interviews', so pitch through the PR agency with a data-centre and AI-networking angle. He has spoken at Calcalist's Tech TLV and on the DealMakers podcast (Alejandro Cremades).

name: Eli Harris
current_role: Co-founder & Partner, One Dream Ventures (venture studio for SaaS/AI tools for real estate & construction); co-founder of EcoFlow and R-Zero
profile: Eli Harris, a former DJI strategic-partnerships lead, co-founded portable power-station maker EcoFlow with DJI battery engineer Lei 'Bruce' Wang (co-founder/CEO c.2016-2020). He then co-founded R-Zero (disinfection/building air quality) and Honor Pet, and now runs venture studio One Dream Ventures.
interesting_fact: He got the idea for EcoFlow at DJI, where disaster-relief and emergency projects showed him how critical portable batteries were; EcoFlow's pitch was to 'replace fuel generators and provide clean personal energy storage.'
deep_cut_fact: EcoFlow's first product, the 412-watt River 'personal grid', launched on Indiegogo and raised over $157,000 from 267 backers within days (523% of its $30k goal); early on EcoFlow also worked with an anti-poaching group in Kenya.

public_contacts.value: Guest appearance: Tangent podcast (Nov 2024) on One Dream Ventures

notes: Forbes 30 Under 30 alum; podcast-friendly (has done several). Fits energy/climate-tech angle (portable storage, building energy). Some role dates come from profile aggregators. Note: the 'podcast' entry is a guest appearance, not his own show.

name: Hannah Sieber
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Artyc PBC (battery-powered cold-chain shipping for healthcare); co-founder of EcoFlow
profile: Mandarin-speaking, Stanford-educated co-founder of Shenzhen-based EcoFlow, the portable-power and home-battery unicorn, and a Forbes 30 Under 30 Energy honoree (2018). She now runs Artyc, which makes reusable, battery-powered, sensor-tracked coolers (Medstow) for shipping medical samples. It had raised about $14M by mid-2024.
interesting_fact: Artyc grew out of her Stanford research on California's wildfire power shutoffs. Seeing small businesses lose refrigerated stock in a 56-hour outage led her to ask 'Could we electrify the cold chain?'
deep_cut_fact: Artyc's first product, the hand-sized Medstow Micro, uses a USB-C-charged lithium battery and a solid-state heat pump to hold up to four vials at 3°C for at least 56 hours, matching the length of the shutoff that inspired it. She has lived in Shenzhen, Shanghai, Hangzhou and Beijing.
notes: No longer at EcoFlow. A great podcast guest with a hardware/battery founder story from Shenzhen to San Francisco. She has appeared on My Climate Journey and speaks at conferences. Artyc's domain is shipartyc.com (artyc.com is parked). Nationality not confirmed.

name: Lei Wang (Bruce Wang, 王雷)
current_role: Founder and CEO, EcoFlow (Shenzhen portable power stations and home energy storage)
profile: HK PolyU mechanical engineering graduate (BEng 2010) with a PhD in battery technology who set up DJI's battery R&D department, then founded EcoFlow in Shenzhen (2016-17). Its RIVER and DELTA portable power stations, launched via crowdfunding, made EcoFlow a ~$2B unicorn in portable and home battery storage and solar generators.
interesting_fact: EcoFlow's DELTA power station sold US$2.8M on Kickstarter in 48 days; its first product, the RIVER, raised ~US$1M on Indiegogo and within six months topped Tmall's outdoor-power category.
deep_cut_fact: Before EcoFlow he established DJI's battery R&D department, and in about three years his team doubled the battery life of DJI's drones. He later completed CKGSB's Master of Entrepreneurship and Technology Innovation (METI) programme.

public_contacts.value: media.na@ecoflow.com (North America PR; regional media.eu@ / media.apac@ also listed)

notes: Goes by 'Bruce Wang' in English and is profiled by PolyU as an alumnus (polyu.edu.hk/alumni ... bruce-wang-lei). Good energy-storage and home-backup-power angle. CKGSB dates EcoFlow's founding to 2016; most other sources say 2017.

name: Joel Hyatt
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Globality (stepped down as CEO in late 2026, per Procurement Magazine)
profile: Serial entrepreneur. He co-founded Hyatt Legal Services (1977), which brought affordable legal services to middle-income families, and Hyatt Legal Plans (later sold to MetLife). With Al Gore he co-founded Current TV (2004; sold to Al Jazeera in 2013). In 2015 he co-founded Globality, an AI platform for enterprise procurement and sourcing backed by SoftBank, and led it as CEO until 2026.
interesting_fact: He was the face of his own firm's nationwide TV ads, which always ended with the line: 'I'm Joel Hyatt and you have my word on it.'
deep_cut_fact: He co-authored the 2000 book 'The Long Boom' with futurists Peter Schwartz and Peter Leyden. He taught entrepreneurship at Stanford GSB from 1998 to 2003 and was founding chairman of VideoSurf, a computer-vision video search engine that Microsoft acquired in 2011.
notes: An experienced public figure: 1994 Democratic Senate nominee in Ohio, 2000 DNC national finance chair, former HP director, RAND trustee. He does podcasts readily. His personal site links to his X and LinkedIn, and he is reachable through Globality. The CEO handover is reported only by procurementmag.com, so confirm his current title.

name: Lior Delgo
current_role: Co-founder, Globality (AI platform for enterprise services procurement, Menlo Park/Palo Alto); listed as co-founder & president
profile: Israeli-American serial entrepreneur. Co-founded travel meta-search engine FareChase (acquired by Yahoo, 2004) and computer-vision video search company VideoSurf (acquired by Microsoft in 2011, reportedly ~$70M, for Xbox LIVE), then worked on Xbox at Microsoft. In 2015 he co-founded Globality with Joel Hyatt; the AI-driven sourcing platform for services spend reached unicorn status (~$1B).
interesting_fact: His VideoSurf technology used computer vision to 'see' frames inside videos, identifying people and moments rather than relying on text tags; Microsoft bought it in 2011 to power video search and Kinect voice search on Xbox LIVE.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded VideoSurf with applied mathematician Prof. Achi Brandt (a pioneer of multigrid methods), Dr. Eitan Sharon and Shai Deljo; its computer-vision engine analyzed video about 10x faster than playback speed.

public_contacts.value: slafferty@roundearthconsulting.com (Sarah Lafferty, Round Earth Consulting; Globality media contact)

notes: Jared Hyatt succeeded Joel Hyatt as Globality CEO; Delgo remains co-founder. PR contact is from a Mar 2026 Business Wire release seen via search (page not directly fetchable; verify). FareChase/Yahoo link per Globality's own bio. Low personal media profile.

name: Ran Harpaz
current_role: Founder and CEO, Lettuce Financial (AI operating system for solopreneurs)
profile: Israeli-born tech executive who was founding CTO of procurement-AI unicorn Globality (2015-2019), then CTO/COO of Hippo Insurance and COO of Noname Security, after strategy roles at PayPal. In 2023 he founded Lettuce Financial, an AI platform handling accounting, tax, payroll and benefits for solopreneurs; it has raised $28M+ and bought Besolo and Carry's retirement platform.
interesting_fact: He has helped scale three unicorns (Globality, Hippo, Noname Security) and now says Lettuce aims to put at least $50 billion back into solopreneurs' businesses through smarter tax and accounting.
deep_cut_fact: Before Silicon Valley he was CIO of Israeli ISP Netvision/Cellcom and worked at security firms Skybox Security and Sanctum; he holds an MBA, a BA in economics and an LLB in law, all from Tel Aviv University.
notes: Active founder who gives press interviews; LinkedIn is linked from his official Lettuce author page. The X account is the company's (@joinlettuce), not his personal account. Unit 8200 veteran per aggregator profiles (unverified).

name: Jonathan Ross
current_role: Founder of Groq; since Dec 2025 at NVIDIA (reported as Chief Software Architect) under Nvidia's ~$20bn non-exclusive Groq inference-technology licensing deal
profile: Chip architect who started Google's TPU as a '20% project', left in 2016 with much of the TPU team and founded Groq (LPU inference chips, GroqCloud; $6.9bn valuation in 2025). In Dec 2025 Nvidia licensed Groq's tech (~$20bn) and Ross and president Sunny Madra joined Nvidia; Groq continues under CEO Simon Edwards.
interesting_fact: Groq's tech is credited as one of the few credible challengers to Nvidia in inference - so much so that Nvidia ultimately paid ~$20bn to license it and bring Ross and his team in-house.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of high school because he 'was bored', taught himself programming, did a stint at Hunter College, then got into NYU where he took PhD classes (incl. under Yann LeCun) as an undergrad before dropping out again: 'I didn't want to cap my earning opportunity by graduating from something.'
notes: Very podcast-friendly historically (Chamath, 20VC etc.), but now an Nvidia employee, so requests likely route through Nvidia PR. 'Chief Software Architect' title comes from reports quoting his LinkedIn; not confirmed on nvidia.com. LeCun detail per Groq's former leadership bio (via search). Hurun $7bn valuation figure is outdated.

name: Tian Dihong
current_role: Cofounder and former director of Intellif (Shenzhen Intellifusion, SSE STAR: 688343); sole owner of NaitMind, Inc. (current active role not published)
profile: Tian Dihong (田第鸿) cofounded Shenzhen Intellifusion (Intellif), an AI vision and AI-inference chip company, with Chen Ning in August 2014, holding 30% at founding. He later left the board for personal reasons and sold part of his stake in 2019; his company NaitMind, Inc. provided technical consulting to Intellif. Intellif listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023.
interesting_fact: Intellif's founding capital was largely intellectual property: Chen and Tian contributed a non-patent technology package for 'extracting crowd feature values through video analysis', valued at RMB 4.7M, in 70/30 proportion.
notes: Very low profile; no interviews or bio found. Possibly US-based (owns US-registered NaitMind, Inc.) but unconfirmed. Not to be confused with Intellif CEO Chen Ning. Intellif IR is the only published channel and he is no longer a director there.

name: Alex Dulin
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Morning Consult (Washington, DC)
profile: Alex Dulin co-founded Morning Consult in 2014 with Michael Ramlet and Kyle Dropp and has been CTO since. The firm grew from online political polling into a $1bn+ 'decision intelligence' company. Dulin leads engineering and product technology, from daily survey data collection to the AI systems built on top of it.
interesting_fact: Morning Consult started in political polling, where forecasts are tested against election results. Its tracking data is now used by Federal Reserve researchers, and the company says it ranked first for accuracy among alternative datasets in forecasting public-company earnings.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a CTO, Dulin's degree is not in computer science: he holds a bachelor's in political science from the University of Rochester. He built the tech stack of a billion-dollar data company from a polling and politics background.
notes: Behind-the-scenes technical co-founder; CEO Michael Ramlet is the usual spokesperson. Go through press@morningconsult.com. The AI-native data pipeline is a good podcast angle.

name: Kyle Dropp
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Research Officer (formerly President), Morning Consult, Washington DC
profile: Milwaukee-born political scientist (UW-Madison; Stanford PhD 2013) who worked in the Washington Post's polling unit, then cofounded Morning Consult in 2014 with Michael Ramlet and Alex Dulin. The firm became a $1B+ global data-intelligence company tracking public and consumer opinion in real time and increasingly AI-driven. He also taught at Dartmouth (2016-18).
interesting_fact: While building Morning Consult he was also an assistant professor in Dartmouth's Department of Government, leading its Washington program (2016-18) and teaching persuasion and applied data science; he was on Ad Age's 40 Under 40 (2020).
deep_cut_fact: He co-wrote the viral April 2014 Monkey Cage study (with Joshua Kertzer and Thomas Zeitzoff) that asked Americans to find Ukraine on a map: only about 1 in 6 could, and the farther off their guess, the more they backed US military intervention.
notes: Title has varied across sources (President vs Chief Research Officer); the IDFA bio says Chief Research Officer. Active in DC civic/business networks (Economic Club of Washington, Aspen Vanguard, Public Affairs Council board). No published press email found on the Morning Consult site.

name: Michael Ramlet
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Morning Consult (Washington, DC)
profile: Michael Ramlet (University of Minnesota Carlson School, BSB 2009) co-founded Morning Consult around 2013-14 with Kyle Dropp and Alex Dulin. It grew from a healthcare-policy newsletter into a global survey-based business-intelligence firm polling tens of thousands of people daily, valued at ~$1bn, and is now repositioning as an 'AI-native' intelligence company.
interesting_fact: Morning Consult's daily consumer-confidence tracking became a real-time economic indicator during the 2020 pandemic, with data shared with the Federal Reserve and Germany's central bank; he co-founded the firm before he was old enough to rent a car.
deep_cut_fact: Morning Consult started as a daily healthcare newsletter he launched while still a Carlson student; its very first poll asked whether young, uninsured people would sign up for insurance on the new ACA marketplaces. He was named UMN Entrepreneur of the Year in 2024.
notes: Grew up outside Madison, Wisconsin; worked at Purple Strategies before Morning Consult. Frequent conference speaker (Adweek, Cannes). AI angle: company pitching 'AI-native' market intelligence.

name: Wang Yongfeng
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Neusoft Reach (东软睿驰), automotive software and AI-vehicle platforms
profile: Wang Yongfeng is a long-time Neusoft Group executive (former VP, president and rotating CEO of Neusoft, 600718.SH) who now chairs and runs Neusoft Reach, Neusoft's intelligent-vehicle spin-off and a Hurun-listed unicorn. Neusoft Reach supplies automotive base software (NeuSAR OS), AI computing platforms, driver-assistance stacks and EV power electronics (BMS) to carmakers.
interesting_fact: Neusoft Reach's NeuSAR automotive OS has been adapted to more than 100 mainstream domestic and international chips; Wang calls the car OS 'the strategic commanding height' of intelligent vehicles (Beijing Auto Show 2026).
deep_cut_fact: He trained in AI long before the current boom: he holds a master's in computer applications (artificial intelligence) from Jilin University, and was named an outstanding young talent of China's software industry.
notes: He stepped down as Neusoft Group rotating CEO in 2025 and appears as Neusoft Reach chairman/CEO in April 2026 coverage. Gives interviews at auto shows (Chinese-language media). Data-center/AI angle: car-cloud AI computing platform. 'Founder' label in input is loose; Neusoft Reach was founded by Neusoft Group.

name: He Dongdong
current_role: Co-founder, Vice Chairman and General Manager/CEO, Rootcloud (树根互联 / 树根科技), Guangzhou
profile: He Dongdong (b. 1967; SJTU industrial-management engineering, CEIBS EMBA) spent 2003-2017 at construction-equipment giant SANY, rising to senior VP and head of process IT. In 2016 he launched SANY's spin-out Rootcloud, an industrial-internet (IIoT) platform connecting factory and machinery data; it filed for a STAR Market IPO in 2022 and in 2026 was on Hurun's Global Unicorn list for the sixth year running.
interesting_fact: Rootcloud grew out of SANY's own effort to connect its excavators and cranes worldwide and became one of China's flagship industrial-internet platforms, recognised as a Hurun global unicorn six years in a row (2026).
deep_cut_fact: At SANY he ran businesses abroad, serving as general manager of SANY India and chairman of SANY Germany before becoming SANY's CIO-style process-IT chief; he is also vice president of the Chinese Society of Vocational and Technical Education.
notes: Company now brands itself 树根科技 (Rootcloud Technology); still unlisted as of 2026. Frequent speaker on industrial internet/AI in manufacturing. No press email found (site lists only a partner@ address).

name: Andrew Reiter
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO of Shield AI (left 2022; remains an adviser). Contrary Research reports he moved to ThorCon US (molten-salt nuclear) in 2023; I could not confirm his title there.
profile: Andrew Reiter (Northwestern '10, Harvard MS robotics '12) is a perception and sensor-fusion engineer. He co-founded San Diego defense-autonomy company Shield AI in 2015 with Ryan and Brandon Tseng and was its first CTO; Shield AI makes the Hivemind AI pilot and the V-BAT drone. He left in fall 2022 to pursue decarbonization, and Contrary Research says he joined nuclear developer ThorCon US in 2023.
interesting_fact: Shield AI was born when ex-Navy SEAL Brandon Tseng and his brother Ryan flew from San Diego to Boston to meet him at Draper. 'After eight hours, we had the loose strings of Shield AI in place,' Reiter recalled. The company grew from three people in a garage to more than 500 staff.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Northwestern as a chemical engineering major, but robotics hooked him when he won the 2009 McCormick Autonomous Robot Design Competition with classmates Andrew Dai and Eric West. At Draper he led teams building a handheld 3D-scanning system and a fully autonomous exploration quadrotor.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast: in 2023 he said his next move targeted decarbonization via nuclear energy or energy storage ('The climate emergency waits for no one'). He has no published email or verified social handle; try LinkedIn or Northwestern Engineering alumni channels. Shield AI's press office is not a good route since he left.

name: Brandon Tseng
current_role: Co-founder and President, Shield AI
profile: Former Navy SEAL officer and surface warfare officer (7 years; deployed to Afghanistan and the Pacific) who co-founded Shield AI in 2015 with his brother Ryan Tseng and Andrew Reiter. Shield AI builds the Hivemind AI-pilot software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft and (via Aechelon) simulation tech; it was valued at ~$12.7B in 2026 and is a leading US defense-autonomy startup.
interesting_fact: His thesis is that the AI pilot matters more than the airframe; in 2026 he said he now expects autonomous defense systems to be ubiquitous by 2040-45, not his original 2035 forecast, because procurement moved slower than he expected.
deep_cut_fact: In August 2015 he and his co-founders pitched 30 Silicon Valley investors and all said no; the next year they met 25 more and two said yes. a16z's Peter Levine, a board member, likened defense tech then to Uber or Airbnb: 'ideas that look dumb until they don't.'
notes: Frequent podcast/op-ed guest (Masters of Scale, War on the Rocks), so receptive to media. AI/autonomy plus defense angle; adjacent rather than core to energy/data centers. Shield AI's own site blocked automated fetch; personal social handles not verified.

name: Ryan Tseng
current_role: Co-founder & President (strategic growth), Shield AI; CEO 2015-May 2025
profile: Ryan Tseng co-founded San Diego-based Shield AI in 2015 with his brother Brandon (an ex-Navy SEAL) and Andrew Reiter to build AI pilots for military aircraft and drones (Hivemind software, V-BAT drone). He was CEO until former Splunk chief Gary Steele took over in May 2025; Ryan now focuses on senior government and industry engagement as president. Shield AI raised a $1.5bn Series G at a $12.7bn valuation in March 2026.
interesting_fact: Shield AI's founding idea came from Brandon Tseng's SEAL deployments: small autonomous drones that could clear buildings ahead of troops; it grew into Hivemind, an AI pilot for aircraft from quadcopters to F-16s.
deep_cut_fact: Before defense tech he was a wireless-power entrepreneur: as founder/CEO/CTO of WiPower he developed wireless charging technology and sold the company to Qualcomm in 2010. He studied electrical engineering at the University of Florida and earned an MBA at MIT.
notes: Leadership change confirmed by Shield AI release (12 Mar 2025). Titles vary (President / President & Chief Strategy Officer / President, Strategic Growth). Defense-AI focus rather than data centers. Frequent speaker (CSIS, Sedona Forum, AIAA), so open to media; route via Shield AI communications (shield.ai blocked from this session, so no press email captured).

name: David Durrleman
current_role: Co-founder, Shift Technology (Paris); former CTO (current title unconfirmed)
profile: Co-founded Shift Technology in Paris in 2014 with Jeremy Jawish and Eric Sibony. Shift sells AI for insurance (claims-fraud detection, claims automation) and became a $1B+ unicorn in 2021. As CTO he built a 100+ engineer tech organisation. Marc Jones has been CTO since Oct 2022, and Durrleman remains a co-founder.
interesting_fact: Shift Technology is one of France's AI unicorns, selling AI for insurance fraud detection and claims decisions to insurers worldwide.
notes: Low public profile; his pre-Shift background and education could not be verified. Shift lists marketing@ as its 'Press & Media' contact. CEO Jeremy Jawish is the company's main spokesperson.

name: Eric Sibony
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Science Officer, Shift Technology (Paris)
profile: Polytechnique-trained mathematician who co-founded Shift Technology in 2013 with Jeremy Jawish and David Durrleman. Shift sells AI for insurance claims fraud detection, underwriting and claims automation; it became a unicorn in 2021 with a $220M Series D led by Advent. He leads its data science and now its agentic-AI push for insurers.
interesting_fact: Shift Technology raised $220M in May 2021 at a $1B+ valuation, becoming one of France's insurtech unicorns; its AI scores insurance claims for fraud for insurers worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: While building Shift as CSO, he completed a PhD at Telecom ParisTech (2016) titled 'Multi-resolution analysis of ranking data', on machine learning over permutations and rankings, co-authoring work on ranking aggregation with Stephan Clemencon.
notes: marketing@shift-technology.com is listed under 'Press & Media' on Shift's contact page. He appears in Shift content ('Four questions with Eric Sibony') and trade press commentary on AI in insurance. Less direct energy/data-center fit; AI/entrepreneurship angle.

name: Jeremy Jawish
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Shift Technology (Paris)
profile: Polytechnique-trained French entrepreneur who co-founded Shift Technology in 2014 with Eric Sibony and David Durrleman. Shift sells AI for insurers, starting with fraud detection and now claims and underwriting decision automation and AI agents. It became a unicorn after a $220m Series D (2021) and earns about half its revenue in the US.
interesting_fact: Shift says its fraud-detection AI saves insurers over EUR 5bn a year. By late 2021 it had analysed nearly two billion claims for 100+ insurers in 25 countries.
deep_cut_fact: He met cofounder Eric Sibony at Ecole Polytechnique, and their first calling was 'more mathematical'. The idea for Shift came during his internship at a big insurer, where experts reviewed claims by hand despite all the maths that could be applied. He says he became an entrepreneur mainly 'to work with Eric on something that was ours.'

public_contacts.value: Safia Danger, Public Relations Europe (in-house): safia.danger@shift-technology.com

notes: An approachable, media-friendly French Tech CEO who writes bylines for American Banker and similar outlets. He is an AI-applications person rather than energy or data-center. The PR contact is Shift's in-house European PR lead, as named on its press releases.

name: Cui Dong
current_role: Founder, chairman & CEO of SJ Semiconductor (盛合晶微, formerly SMIC-Changdian / 中芯长电), Jiangyin
profile: Born 1971, Cui Dong worked in government and then as a senior executive at Hua Hong and SMIC, rising to SMIC executive VP for investment and strategy. In 2014 he led the founding of SMIC-Changdian, a JV incubated by SMIC and JCET, which became SJSemi - a leader in bumping, wafer-level and 2.5D/3D advanced packaging for AI chips. SJSemi has cleared review for a STAR Market IPO.
interesting_fact: SJSemi has no controlling shareholder (top holder under 11%), but Cui controls the votes of all 11 employee shareholding platforms; revenue grew from about RMB1.6bn to RMB6.5bn on AI-chip packaging demand, fastest among the global top-10 packaging/test firms.
deep_cut_fact: Before entering the chip industry he worked as a secretary in the General Office of China's Ministry of Electronics Industry, which commentators credit for his feel for national industrial policy.
notes: Strong AI/data-center angle (advanced packaging for AI accelerators; heavy customer concentration in a large domestic AI-chip client). Media differ on his title (chairman vs CEO); profile details are from media reports, not the prospectus.

name: Abraham Bachrach
current_role: Co-Founder & CTO, Skydio (autonomous drones, San Mateo, CA)
profile: Abe Bachrach (BS UC Berkeley; MS/PhD MIT) led MIT's autonomous-flight research from 2007 in Nick Roy's Robust Robotics Group, then joined Google's Project Wing drone effort. In 2014 he co-founded Skydio with Adam Bry and Matt Donahoe; it builds AI-driven autonomous drones and docks for enterprise, utilities/infrastructure inspection, public safety and defense.
interesting_fact: Skydio grew out of MIT research on drones that fly themselves without GPS; Bachrach and Bry built a fixed-wing drone with a laser rangefinder that autonomously navigated around a parking lot.
deep_cut_fact: As an MIT grad student he led the Robust Robotics Group team whose GPS-denied quadrotor won the 2009 International Aerial Robotics Competition: it entered an unknown building through a window, explored without GPS and found a target. It was the first time a new IARC mission was solved in its first year.
notes: Technical founder with a low media profile (CEO Adam Bry is the usual spokesperson). Energy angle: Skydio drones and docks are used for utility and energy-infrastructure inspection. Press route: press@skydio.com.

name: Adam Bry
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Skydio (largest US drone maker, San Mateo, CA)
profile: MIT CSAIL roboticist (SM '12) who helped lead research on autonomous high-speed flight, then co-founded Google X's Project Wing delivery-drone effort. Co-founded Skydio in 2014; it pivoted from consumer selfie drones to autonomous drones and docks for public safety, infrastructure inspection and defence, has delivered over 60,000 drones to 3,800+ organisations, and raised at a ~$4.4B valuation in 2026.
interesting_fact: Skydio is the largest drone manufacturer in the US, with more than 60,000 autonomous drones flying thousands of daily missions in public safety, critical-infrastructure inspection and national security.
deep_cut_fact: He started building things that fly at age five and had won two US national championships in radio-controlled airplane aerobatics by 18. At MIT he co-captained the cycling team and led it to a 2012 national title.
notes: Experienced public speaker (congressional testimony, MIT fireside chats, FAA Drone Advisory Committee). Energy angle: drones for grid and utility infrastructure inspection. Best route is press@skydio.com.

name: Matt Donahoe
current_role: Cofounder, Skydio (autonomous drones), San Mateo, CA - current exec title not confirmed
profile: Matt Donahoe (MIT Media Lab SM '11) cofounded Skydio in 2014 with MIT roboticists Adam Bry and Abe Bachrach. Skydio began with the R1 'selfie drone' (13 cameras, full autonomy) and became the largest US drone maker, selling to the military, police and utilities; it raised a Series F at a $4.4B valuation in 2026 and plans $3.5B of US manufacturing.
interesting_fact: Skydio's first product, the 2018 R1 'selfie drone', used 13 cameras and deep neural networks to follow and film a person while dodging obstacles with no pilot - which CEO Adam Bry likened to a driverless car with level-four autonomy.
deep_cut_fact: For Skydio's first year the three cofounders worked out of Abe Bachrach's dad's basement, getting free rent in exchange for yard work; their first prototype was a quadcopter with a media-center PC and USB camera held together with duct tape - yet it won a $3M seed round.
notes: Lowest-profile of the three cofounders (CEO Adam Bry is the public face). Third-party sites give conflicting titles (COO / CRO / chief experience officer); verify before addressing him. Skydio is on China's sanctions list (relevant to supply chain stories, not to outreach).

name: Li Yang
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Guangzhou Smarter Microelectronics (Smarter Micro / 慧智微, SSE STAR: 688512)
profile: Li Yang (b. ~1974) is an RF engineer who spent years in the US chip industry before founding Smarter Micro in Guangzhou in November 2011. The company designs RF front-end modules (power amplifiers etc.) for 4G/5G phones and IoT using a reconfigurable RF front-end architecture, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023; he holds ~9.5% directly.
interesting_fact: Smarter Micro bet on a 'reconfigurable' RF front-end architecture - one adaptable PA design covering many frequency bands - as China's answer to the Skyworks/Qorvo-dominated discrete-module approach.
deep_cut_fact: Before returning to China he worked in US RF/semiconductor firms: Principal Engineer at Millennial Net (2004-06), Staff Engineer at Peregrine Semiconductor (2006-08) and Principal Engineer at Skyworks (2008-11), founding Smarter Micro three months after leaving Skyworks.
notes: Common name - identity confirmed via Smarter Micro annual report. Fit is semiconductors (RF for handsets), not data-center power directly.

name: Mike Pittaro
current_role: SnapLogic co-founder; last publicly listed as Distinguished Engineer, Cloud and Big Data Solutions, Dell EMC (current role unverified)
profile: Mike (Michael) Pittaro co-founded SnapLogic in 2006 with Informatica co-founder Gaurav Dhillon, serving as chief community officer while it ran as an open-source data-integration project; SnapLogic later became an iPaaS unicorn. He came from Informatica (customer services/strategic support) and later worked as a principal engineer at La Honda Research Center and a distinguished engineer at Dell EMC.
interesting_fact: SnapLogic launched in 2007 as open-source data-integration software under a GPL-style licence, with Pittaro as chief community officer building the developer community, long before it became a commercial AI-integration platform.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 he was an active member of BayPIGgies, the San Francisco Bay Area Python users' group, answering members' data-pipeline questions and signing off as 'Co-Founder, Snaplogic, Inc.'; SnapLogic's early engine was built in Python.
notes: Founder status per Golden wiki, MarketScreener and a 2009 Sramana Mitra profile; current role from Crunchbase (may be outdated). Low public profile; no current published contact found. Old snaplogic.org address in 2008 list posts is obsolete and should not be used. He left SnapLogic around 2010, so his stake in the unicorn is probably small.

name: Alexander Ratner
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Snorkel AI (Redwood City/SF); Affiliate Assistant Professor of Computer Science, University of Washington
profile: Stanford CS PhD (advisor Christopher Re) who started and led the open-source Snorkel project for programmatic data labelling, then spun it out as Snorkel AI in 2019. The unicorn now focuses on expert data, evaluations and benchmarks for frontier AI labs and enterprises. He is also affiliate faculty at the University of Washington.
interesting_fact: Snorkel grew from his 2016 NeurIPS paper 'Data Programming: Creating Large Training Sets, Quickly', which showed models could be trained without hand-labelled data by writing noisy 'labeling functions' and modelling their accuracies - the weak-supervision idea behind the company.
deep_cut_fact: As a PhD student he co-authored AMELIE, a Stanford tool that speeds diagnosis of patients with rare Mendelian genetic diseases by mining the primary medical literature directly (with Gill Bejerano's lab).

public_contacts.value: ajratner at gmail.com (self-published on his academic homepage, last updated ~2020)

notes: Accessible, academically minded founder who speaks often at AI events (Snorkel hosts its own Frontier Data Summit). For a business/podcast request, media@snorkel.ai is the most appropriate route; the gmail address is from his older academic page.

name: Braden Hancock
current_role: Research Partner, Laude Ventures and Laude Institute (since Jul 2025); co-founder and advisor, Snorkel AI
profile: BYU mechanical-engineering valedictorian turned Stanford CS PhD (under Chris Ré) who co-founded Snorkel AI from Stanford weak-supervision research; it reached a $1.3B valuation (Series D, May 2025). He then founded Meta's GenAI Evaluations org for Llama (2024-25), and since mid-2025 is a Research Partner at Laude.
interesting_fact: At Meta he founded the centralized evaluation org responsible for all eval work on Llama 3, 3.1 and 3.2, the most-downloaded open LLM family.
deep_cut_fact: Before AI he was a mechanical engineer: in summer 2011 he worked in the Air Force Research Laboratory's Turbine Engine Division on evolutionary algorithms for turbine-engine simulation, and he graduated BYU (2015) as valedictorian.
notes: Very accessible: maintains a personal site, posts on X/LinkedIn and does podcasts (e.g. The SaaS CFO, Aug 2025; Practical AI #117). Good guest for AI data/evals and research-to-startup topics. No published email; X or LinkedIn is the best route.

name: Chris Re
current_role: Professor of Computer Science, Stanford (Stanford AI Lab / Hazy Research); co-founder of Together AI
profile: Christopher Re is a Stanford CS professor and MacArthur Fellow whose machine-learning systems research has spun out multiple companies: Lattice (DeepDive) and Inductiv (HoloClean), both acquired by Apple, plus Snorkel AI, SambaNova Systems and Together AI, the AI-cloud/open-model infrastructure company co-founded in 2022. His lab now focuses on AI kernels (ThunderKittens) and AI efficiency.
interesting_fact: He has co-founded companies straight out of his research, including SambaNova and Snorkel, and his lab says over a dozen of its members have gone on to become professors; his students also run the MLSys podcast.
deep_cut_fact: In Nov 2025 he co-authored 'Intelligence Per Watt' with John Hennessy, arguing that, as with mainframes to PCs, efficiency gains could shift AI inference from power-constrained data centers to local devices; they found local LMs could answer 88.7% of single-turn chat and reasoning queries.
notes: Excellent fit for a data-center/energy podcast given his 'intelligence per watt' work. The email is his Stanford work address, published on his own homepage. The X account is the lab's (Hazy Research), not personal.

name: Henry Ehrenberg
current_role: Co-founder, Snorkel AI (technical strategy and engineering)
profile: Yale applied-math grad with a Stanford MS who was a core member of the Snorkel project in the Stanford AI Lab, then tech lead of Facebook Applied AI's representation-learning team. He co-founded Snorkel AI (spun out 2019 with Alex Ratner, Chris Ré and others), which sells programmatic data-labeling and expert-data tooling for enterprise and frontier AI.
interesting_fact: Snorkel's core idea, 'programmatic labeling' or weak supervision, lets teams write labeling functions instead of hand-labeling data; it began as an open-source Stanford research library he helped build.
deep_cut_fact: He is a co-author of the original 2017 paper 'Snorkel: Rapid Training Data Creation with Weak Supervision' and of 'Learning to Compose Domain-Specific Transformations for Data Augmentation' (2017), the research that seeded the company.
notes: Lower profile than CEO Alex Ratner but does public talks (theCUBE + NYSE Wired 'Robotics & AI Infrastructure Leaders' 2025: https://snorkel.ai/press/henry-kiss-ehrenberg-snorkel-ai-robotics-ai-infrastructure-leaders/). Snorkel press list mentions a 2026 RIF - avoid as an angle.

name: Paroma Varma
current_role: Co-founder and Head of Research, Snorkel AI
profile: Paroma Varma earned an EE PhD at Stanford, where her weak-supervision research in the Stanford AI Lab became Snorkel, spun out as Snorkel AI (valued ~ $1bn). Snorkel has pivoted toward expert-curated datasets, benchmarks and evaluation for frontier AI labs, and she leads its research (e.g. 2026 work on rubric-based LLM evaluation).
interesting_fact: Snorkel started as a Stanford AI Lab research project in 2015 to give ML a 'higher-level interface' through training data; she describes Snorkel Flow as the first data-centric platform built on programmatic labelling.
deep_cut_fact: Her first exposure to machine learning was as a UC Berkeley undergrad working in a neuroscience lab, and during her PhD she collaborated with radiologists, applying weak supervision to medical imaging.
notes: Researcher-founder; accessible via Snorkel media. Some third-party profiles list her as Head of Solutions, but Snorkel's own author page says Head of Research.

name: Idit Levine
current_role: Founder and CEO, Solo.io (cloud-native application networking / agentic AI infrastructure)
profile: Israeli-born engineer who held roles at Verizon, CloudSwitch, DynamicOps and VMware before serving as CTO of EMC's Cloud Management Division (2014-17). She left in 2017 to found Solo.io, which built the Gloo API gateway and Istio/Ambient-mesh products, raised a $135m Series C at a $1bn+ valuation, and now ships agentic-AI infrastructure such as kagent and agentgateway.
interesting_fact: Before tech she played professional basketball in Israel for about seven years (Elitzur Holon), juggling up to six hours of practice a day with mandatory military service.
deep_cut_fact: She left Dell EMC in 2017 to start a company without yet knowing what she would build; she credits basketball for her style: 'Basketball is a small team, no politics whatsoever, that's going to the same goal.'
notes: Very podcast-friendly (InfoQ, The New Stack, Spot.io 'Cloud Control' appearances). Agentic-AI/cloud infra angle fits data-center/AI theme. Some 2026 releases also list media@solo.io via a third-party republisher - unverified.

name: Brandon Ogle
current_role: Co-founder of Standard AI (formerly Standard Cognition), San Francisco; listed as Head of Machine Learning
profile: Brandon Ogle is one of seven co-founders of Standard AI (Standard Cognition), a Y Combinator company founded in 2017 to build camera-based, cashierless checkout for retailers using computer vision, which reached a ~$1-2B valuation. He is listed as the company's machine-learning lead. Standard AI later pivoted toward retail computer-vision analytics.
interesting_fact: Standard's system tracked shoppers with overhead cameras that identify people by shape and movement rather than facial recognition, pitching itself as a privacy-friendlier rival to Amazon Go.
notes: Very low public profile: role known only from aggregator profiles (MarketScreener: Head of Machine Learning since 2017). Current status at the company unverified. No published personal or press email found.

profile: Co-founder and former Director of Research of Standard AI (Standard Cognition), the San Francisco computer-vision startup that came out of Y Combinator's Summer 2017 batch to build camera-based autonomous checkout for retailers and reached a ~$1B+ valuation. In March 2024 he, Jordan Fisher and co-founder Brandon Ogle joined DoorDash with part of Standard's engineering team to build an AI phone-ordering product for restaurants.

profile: David Valdman (PhD) co-founded San Francisco-based Standard Cognition in 2017 (Y Combinator S17) with Jordan Fisher, Michael Suswal, John Novak and others to build camera-based, cashierless 'autonomous checkout' for retail; it reached unicorn status (~$1B+; Hurun lists $2B) and later rebranded as Standard AI, pivoting toward AI/edge vision analytics for stores.

current_role: Co-founder, Tenstorrent Inc. (Toronto/Santa Clara AI-chip and RISC-V company); current title not publicly confirmed (profiles describe a system/foundational software role)

Tenstorrent builds AI accelerators (Grayskull, Wormhole, Blackhole) and licenses RISC-V CPU and chiplet IP; Jim Keller became CEO and it has raised at multi-billion valuations. Hamer works on the company's low-level software stack.

name: Ljubisa Bajic
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Taalas (Toronto) — being acquired by AMD (announced Aug 2026); he and his team are to join AMD's AI Group under SVP Vamsi Boppana
profile: Toronto chip architect who founded AI-chip company Tenstorrent in 2016 (bringing in Jim Keller as CTO, later CEO) and served as its CEO/CTO/president. He then co-founded Taalas, which hard-wires a specific AI model into silicon (its HC1 runs Llama 3.1 8B at ~17,000 tokens/s per user, per the company). Taalas raised ~$219m before AMD agreed to buy it in Aug 2026.
interesting_fact: Taalas customises only the top two metal layers of its chip for each new model, which it says lets it turn a new AI model into dedicated silicon in about two months.
deep_cut_fact: The AMD deal is a homecoming: before Tenstorrent he was an ASIC architect at ATI/AMD (an ATI patent filed in 2006 names him as co-inventor of a method to cut GPU power consumption), a senior architect at Nvidia, and AMD's director of IC design and architecture, where he first worked with Jim Keller.
notes: Excellent podcast fit (AI inference silicon, data-center efficiency). Has done long-form interviews (AnandTech with Jim Keller, MIT Tech Review Future Compute). Once the AMD deal closes, route through AMD corporate PR; the AMD release also names specific PR contacts.

name: Milos Trajkovic
current_role: Co-founder and Senior Fellow, Systems Engineering & Software, Tenstorrent (Toronto/Santa Clara)
profile: Belgrade-educated chip engineer who co-founded Toronto-born AI/RISC-V processor firm Tenstorrent in 2016 with Ljubisa Bajic and Ivan Hamer. He has worked on every stage of its Tensix processor (architecture, RTL, verification, post-silicon) and now leads systems engineering and the low-level software stack at the Jim Keller-led company.
interesting_fact: Tenstorrent, the company he co-founded, announced a $1.5bn Series E at a $6.2bn valuation in October 2026, positioning its open RISC-V + Tensix hardware and fully open-source software stack as an alternative to Nvidia for AI inference.
deep_cut_fact: Before Tenstorrent he managed AMD's firmware design engineering team for power management across graphics, CPU and data fabric - dynamic voltage/frequency scaling, power and clock gating, thermal monitoring - and was IP lead for RTL blocks in AMD's System Management Unit, working on perf-per-watt of GPU compute units.

public_contacts.value: Salient PR (Justin Mauldin), media contact on 2026 Tenstorrent releases

notes: Engineer-founder with a low public profile; his AMD power-management background is a great hook for an energy/data-centre podcast. Route via Tenstorrent PR. Note co-founder Ljubisa Bajic has left to found another company; don't conflate them.

name: Alexandre Dalyac
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Tractable (London); stepped down as CEO (per a Tractable announcement; date unconfirmed)
profile: Alex Dalyac co-founded Tractable in 2014 at Entrepreneur First with CTO Razvan Ranca (later joined by Lazada co-founder Adrien Cohen). Tractable uses computer vision to appraise vehicle and property damage for insurers and to value cars for recycling. It became a $1bn unicorn in 2021, and Dalyac led it as CEO before moving to chairman.
interesting_fact: He got into deep learning in 2013 through Geoffrey Hinton's Coursera course 'Machine learning with neural networks', months before the field took off. At Imperial he helped build a plant-recognition app that his professor tested on flowers in Hyde Park.
deep_cut_fact: Tractable's first paying customer had nothing to do with cars: the first use case was AI inspection of plastic pipe welds in water and gas lines. Dalyac had been rejected by Entrepreneur First once 'for not knowing anything about tech' before getting in, and the name comes from Ranca's webpage line about 'currently intractable problems'.
notes: Writes publicly about building Tractable (TechCrunch essay republished on tractable.ai), so a good podcast fit for the AI-founder story. CEO-to-chairman move reported via a Tractable post now offline and a Jan 2026 profile; confirm before outreach. No published press email found.

Tractable uses computer vision to assess car and property damage for insurers, and in 2021 became EF's first company valued above $1bn.
interesting_fact: Tractable went from Entrepreneur First idea to $1bn 'unicorn' valuation in about six years (2014-2021), using AI that estimates vehicle repair costs from photos within seconds.

profile: Israeli lawyer-turned-entrepreneur who co-founded Verbit in 2016 with Eric Shellef and Kobi Ben Tzvi, building an AI-plus-human transcription and captioning platform (acquired VITAC and others) valued at ~$2bn in 2021.
