public_contacts.value: Guest appearances: Learning from Machine Learning #9 (2024), ThursdAI (May 2024), Software Engineering Daily (2023)

notes: Approachable, engineer-minded founder who does podcasts often; X @vanpelt is the most direct public channel. He says: 'My title is co-founder really at the end of the day.' Since the acquisition, press for W&B goes through CoreWeave (press@coreweave.com). Strong data-centre/AI angle.

name: Lukas Biewald
current_role: SVP of AI Initiatives at CoreWeave and General Manager/co-founder of Weights & Biases (acquired by CoreWeave, May 2025); Xometry board member
profile: Two-time AI founder. After Stanford and Yahoo search, he co-founded data-labeling firm CrowdFlower in 2007 (later Figure Eight, sold to Appen in 2019). In 2017 he co-founded ML experiment-tracking platform Weights & Biases. CoreWeave acquired W&B in 2025, and he now leads AI initiatives at the GPU cloud.
interesting_fact: His companies tackled two successive bottlenecks of practical ML: getting labelled training data (CrowdFlower/Figure Eight) and making model development reproducible (W&B). W&B now sits inside one of the largest AI data-center operators, CoreWeave.
deep_cut_fact: W&B's first product began as an experiment-tracking tool built to help train models at OpenAI. Biewald had gone back to hands-on deep learning and spent time at OpenAI before starting the company.
notes: Very accessible: he hosts his own AI interview podcast, Gradient Dissent, so a podcast-swap or guest invite is a natural angle. Now at CoreWeave, which is directly relevant to a data-center podcast. No personal email published; reach him via W&B/CoreWeave or the podcast.

name: Shawn Lewis
current_role: Co-founder (CTO / distinguished engineer), Weights & Biases, now part of CoreWeave
profile: Shawn Lewis, a former Google engineer, co-founded Weights & Biases in 2017 with Lukas Biewald and Chris Van Pelt to build developer tools for machine learning, starting with experiment tracking used at OpenAI. W&B grew into a leading MLOps platform and was acquired by AI cloud provider CoreWeave (deal closed May 2025, reportedly ~$1.7B); he remains with the company.
interesting_fact: W&B's first product was an experiment-tracking tool developed to help build models at OpenAI; it grew into an end-to-end platform used by millions of ML practitioners and now sits inside CoreWeave's AI cloud.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 2006 on Google's platforms team, which built Google's data-center infrastructure and the software that ran it, and he built internal tools to let colleagues analyze that data (Gradient Dissent podcast).
notes: Great data-center angle (Google platforms team -> CoreWeave AI cloud). Lower public profile than CEO Lukas Biewald; exact current title varies by source (CTO vs distinguished engineer). Best route likely via CoreWeave/W&B press; no personal channels verified.

name: Shen Xiangyang
current_role: Chairman of the HKUST Council (reappointed for 2026-2029); founder of IDEA (International Digital Economy Academy, Shenzhen); co-founder/chair of Xiaoice
profile: Harry Shum (沈向洋, b. 1966, Nanjing) earned a CMU robotics PhD (1996), co-founded Microsoft Research Asia and rose to Microsoft EVP of AI & Research, overseeing Bing and Cortana. He left in 2020 as Microsoft spun its Xiaoice chatbot into an independent company he co-founded, then founded the IDEA institute in Shenzhen and has chaired HKUST's Council since 2023.
interesting_fact: HKUST's Chancellor reappointed him Council Chairman for a second three-year term from March 6, 2026. He is also a foreign member of the US National Academy of Engineering and an IEEE Fellow, ACM Fellow and FREng.
deep_cut_fact: Before running Microsoft's AI empire he was a computer-vision researcher: with Richard Szeliski he wrote the SIGGRAPH 1997 paper 'Creating full view panoramic image mosaics and environment maps', showing how to seamlessly stitch handheld-camera photos into 360-degree panoramas.
notes: Hurun lists him under Xiaoice (valued ~$2B); Xiaoice's current status/leadership is unclear in 2025-26 coverage. No personal published contact found. Best routes are institutional: HKUST (Council Chair's office via HKUST communications) or the IDEA institute in Shenzhen. Very high-profile AI figure.

name: Chen Yimin
current_role: Unverified; listed by Hurun (2022 unicorn founders) as a founder of ECARX
profile: Hurun's 2022 Global Unicorn founders list attributes ECARX (Geely-backed automotive computing and smart-cockpit chip/software firm, NASDAQ: ECX since Dec 2022) to a 'Chen Yimin'. However, ECARX's own materials and filings name only Ziyu Shen (chairman and CEO) and Li Shufu (Eric Li) as co-founders, and no 'Chen Yimin' appears in its SEC filings.
notes: Likely a Hurun data error or a minor early shareholder; could not identify the person. If the journalist wants ECARX, the relevant founder is Ziyu Shen (沈子瑜), chairman and CEO. Recommend dropping or re-checking the source entry.

name: Josh Payne
current_role: Founder and CEO, Nscale (London-based AI infrastructure / GPU cloud 'neocloud')
profile: Australian Josh Payne founded Arkon Energy, a hydro-powered Bitcoin miner in Norway and the US, and in 2024 spun out Nscale to build AI data centers and GPU cloud capacity. Nscale has signed huge GPU deals with Microsoft and OpenAI (Stargate Norway, UK). It raised Europe's largest Series B ($1.1B) and filed for a US IPO in Sept 2026.
interesting_fact: Nscale's tie-up with Norwegian industrial group Aker began with a cold LinkedIn message from Payne to Aker CEO Øyvind Eriksen. Eriksen replied, flew to meet him and joined Nscale's board, and Aker became a major shareholder and partner in Stargate Norway.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech, Payne dropped out of high school in industrial Australia and spent about three years working underground as a coal miner, then did construction and renewable-energy finance. Cheap Scandinavian hydro power later drew him north to Norway.
notes: Very relevant to a data-center/energy podcast. Nscale filed for a US IPO on 18 Sept 2026; reports suggest the listing may slip to 2027, so it may be in a quiet period, which limits press. Also co-founded and was COO of the Battery Future Acquisition Corp SPAC. Use press@nscale.com.

name: Jim Trout
current_role: CEO, CleanArc Data Centers (hyperscale developer building a 900MW campus in Caroline County, Virginia)
profile: Jim Trout helped found CoreSite (as CRG West, at LA's One Wilshire), ran operations at early Digital Realty, and in 2010 launched Silver Lake-backed Vantage Data Centers, later sold to DigitalBridge. After leaving Vantage in 2013 he invested for some years. He now leads CleanArc, which broke ground on a $3B, 900MW hyperscale campus in Virginia in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: CleanArc's flagship Caroline County, Virginia campus is a $3B project offering 900MW of grid capacity. The company was launched in 2023 by power investor 547 Energy and has since raised capital from Snowhawk, Townsend Group and Nuveen.
deep_cut_fact: Trout started in commercial real estate at Prologis. At Digital Realty he grew the operations team from 8 to 500 people. Between Vantage and CleanArc he worked on water-conservation technologies and made angel investments before deciding in 2018 that hyperscale demand was 'just too crazy' to sit out.
notes: Very strong fit for a data-center/energy podcast and an accessible, talkative interviewee (long DCD profile, Oct 2025). Best route is CleanArc's PR agency JSA. cleanarc.com is NOT the company domain; use cleanarcdatacenters.com. The bebeez URL republishes a DCD magazine feature ('The Arc of Trout').

name: Garrett Langley
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Flock Safety (Atlanta)
profile: Georgia Tech engineer Garrett Langley co-founded Flock Safety in 2017 with fellow alumni Matt Feury and Paige Todd after car break-ins in his Atlanta neighbourhood. Flock builds solar-powered license-plate-reader cameras and a public-safety software platform used by 12,000+ customers; backed by Y Combinator, Matrix and Founders Fund, it has been valued around $7.5-8B.
interesting_fact: Police told him what his neighbourhood needed was a license plate reader, but those cost ~$10,000; he and a friend built a cheaper solar-powered one, and Flock logged its first arrest about 60 days later.
deep_cut_fact: Before Flock he launched two startups: Experience, a mobile app to help fans enjoy live events (acquired by Cox Enterprises), and Clutch, a monthly car-subscription service. He also serves on the Georgia Tech Alumni Association Board of Trustees.
notes: Flock is a frequent subject of privacy/civil-liberties debate; keep outreach on entrepreneurship and edge hardware (solar-powered, cellular cameras). Langley is publicly visible (talks, podcasts). Fit: AI/edge infrastructure.

name: Matt Feury
current_role: Co-founder, Flock Safety (Atlanta); former CTO, reportedly now Distinguished Engineer
profile: Matt Feury (Georgia Tech BS Computer Science '11) co-founded Flock Safety in 2017 with Garrett Langley and Paige Todd and served as its CTO, building the ML-based license-plate/vehicle-recognition camera platform used by thousands of police departments and neighbourhoods. Flock (Y Combinator alum) has been valued at around $7.5-8B.
interesting_fact: Flock started when Langley saw break-ins in his Atlanta neighbourhood and found plate-reading cameras cost ~$25,000 each; he and Feury combined off-the-shelf parts with machine learning, and within 60 days their cameras helped police make an arrest.
deep_cut_fact: Garrett Langley's first call when brainstorming a cheaper security camera was to his friend and fellow Georgia Tech alum Feury; Georgia Tech's Scheller College later described Feury as the 'third co-founder' added alongside Paige Todd.
notes: Low public profile compared with CEO Garrett Langley; very few interviews. Current title per theorg.com (Distinguished Engineer) not confirmed by Flock. Flock's surveillance tech is politically contested, so frame outreach around engineering/AI. Route via Flock media team.

name: Farzad Dibachi
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Inxeption (B2B digital commerce/logistics), per Wikipedia and company listings; current status of the company is unclear
profile: Iranian-born engineer who rose to SVP of Oracle's New Media division under Larry Ellison and worked on the network computer. He co-founded Diba (sold to Sun in 1997), Niku (IPO 2000, sold to Computer Associates in 2005), LED-lighting maker Noribachi, and in 2017 Inxeption, a B2B commerce platform that raised ~US$275m.
interesting_fact: He graduated from San Jose State with degrees in mechanical engineering and computer science at age 19. His family had emigrated from Iran in 1979, and he began his career at GE on an H-1B visa.
deep_cut_fact: In 1996-97 he wrote a column called 'Diary of a Startup' for Upside magazine while building Diba. He also co-wrote the management book 'Just Add Management'.
notes: No verified current contact. inxeption.com now hosts what looks like an unrelated hotel booking/AI-agent product with no mention of Dibachi, so do not use it. Inxeption's status after 2022 is unverified. Energy angle: he co-founded Noribachi (commercial/industrial LED lighting).

name: Terry Garnett
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Inxeption (B2B commerce/logistics cloud platform, founded 2017); longtime tech investor
profile: Veteran enterprise-software executive and investor: a former Oracle sales and marketing executive, a general partner at Venrock, and chairman/CEO of Ingres (per MarketScreener). In 2017 he co-founded Inxeption with fellow Oracle alumni Farzad Dibachi and Mark Moore; it raised about $486M and was valued at roughly $3B.
interesting_fact: He was an early specialist in tech 'carve-outs' (buying divisions out of big tech companies). After leaving Venrock in 2004 he raised a $350M carve-out fund with David Helfrich, and in 2014 he teamed with Rob Theis to raise up to $500M more for the same strategy.
notes: Inxeption's last news I found is from Dec 2023. The inxeption.com domain now hosts an unrelated hotel-website company with a different founder, so the original company may be defunct; confirm before mentioning it. Bio details (Oracle, Ingres, Venrock 1995-2002) come from aggregators (MarketScreener, Crunchbase). Avoid the Garnett Helfrich fund-performance topic. No verified contacts.

name: Chris Pihl
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Helion Energy (Everett, WA)
profile: Chris Pihl is co-founder and CTO of Helion Energy, founded in 2013 with David Kirtley, George Votroubek and John Slough. Helion develops pulsed, non-ignition magneto-inertial fusion generators backed by Sam Altman, Dustin Moskovitz and Reid Hoffman. It is building the Orion fusion plant in Malaga, Washington to supply Microsoft data centers, and makes its own high-voltage pulsed-power capacitors in-house.
interesting_fact: Helion signed the world's first fusion power purchase agreement, with Microsoft in 2023, a direct link between fusion and data-center power demand.
deep_cut_fact: Helion's founders met at MSNW, a small Redmond, Washington fusion-research firm with University of Washington ties, before spinning out. Pihl, a UW graduate, is one of three original founders still at the company.
notes: Low personal media profile; CEO David Kirtley is the main spokesperson. A strong fit for the energy and data-center theme. Requests should go through Helion press.

name: David Kirtley
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, Helion Energy (Everett, WA)
profile: Michigan-trained nuclear, plasma and aerospace engineer who co-founded fusion company Helion in 2013. Helion holds the first fusion power-purchase agreement (with Microsoft) and began building its 50 MW Orion plant in Malaga, WA in July 2025, targeting 2028. In February 2026 its Polaris prototype showed the first private D-T fusion.
interesting_fact: Helion's Orion plant is meant to sell fusion electricity to Microsoft, a direct link between fusion and AI data-center power demand. On Lex Fridman's podcast, Kirtley described wanting a 'gigafactory' that turns out 50 MW fusion generators.
deep_cut_fact: He started in space propulsion, not power plants. Early in his career he studied beamed-microwave rocket concepts, in which a spacecraft needs no onboard fuel. Before spinning out Helion, his team worked on fusion rockets and advanced materials. He says they reused circuit topologies from space hardware for fusion.
notes: Very podcast-friendly. He has appeared on Lex Fridman #485, GeekWire's Positive Charge and Slush 2026, and is an ideal guest for the energy/data-center theme. Use Helion's press form. Company X account: @helion_energy. I found no verified personal handle.

name: George Votroubek
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Scientist, Helion Energy (Everett, WA)
profile: Plasma physicist (MS, PhD University of Washington) who co-founded fusion company Helion Energy in 2013 with David Kirtley, Chris Pihl and John Slough, colleagues from MSNW in Redmond. Helion pursues pulsed field-reversed-configuration fusion, is building its Polaris prototype and Orion plant, and has raised ~$1.5B.
interesting_fact: Helion signed the world's first fusion power purchase agreement with Microsoft (plus a deal with steelmaker Nucor) - a direct link between fusion and powering data centers.
deep_cut_fact: He was Principal Investigator for the program that demonstrated Helion's 'Fusion Engine' technology at one-third scale, work that grew out of the Inductive Plasmoid Accelerator experiments the founders ran before Helion existed.
notes: Low-profile scientist; CEO David Kirtley is Helion's public voice. Helion's contact form has a 'Press' inquiry option. Excellent fit for energy + data-center theme. Deep-cut sourced to Crunchbase bio (not a primary document).

name: John Slough
current_role: Cofounder (former) of Helion Energy; plasma physicist, MSNW LLC (Redmond, WA)
profile: Plasma physicist who cofounded Helion Energy in 2013 with David Kirtley, Chris Pihl and George Votroubek; Helion's pulsed fusion approach builds on his FRC plasmoid merging-and-compression research. He left Helion in 2018 to refocus on his research firm MSNW. His wealth reflects his Helion stake (company valued ~$5B).
interesting_fact: He is an inventor on Helion's foundational patents, including a 2011 patent on generating, heating and compressing plasmoids and recovering energy from them, and the 'Advanced D–3He fuel cycle for a pulsed fusion reactor'.
deep_cut_fact: NASA's Innovative Advanced Concepts (NIAC) program funded his 'Fusion Driven Rocket' (2012 Phase II): magnetically driven metal liners crush a plasmoid to fusion and become the propellant, a concept meant to make crewed interplanetary travel 'common place'.
notes: No longer with Helion (left 2018), so Helion PR is not a route to him; reports cite disagreement over fuel choice, so avoid that topic. Very low public profile; MSNW's website was unreachable. Best approached as a fusion-science expert via academic or plasma-physics channels.

name: Chen Zhongguo
current_role: Listed legal representative of GTA Semiconductor (上海积塔半导体) and its parent Huada Semiconductor (per 36Kr company profiles)
profile: Chen Zhongguo (陈忠国) appears in Chinese company records as legal representative of Shanghai GTA Semiconductor, a Lingang-based maker of analog ICs and power devices founded in 2017, and of its parent Huada Semiconductor, a wholly owned unit of state-owned China Electronics Corp (CEC). He looks like a state-enterprise executive rather than an entrepreneur-founder; no personal biography was found.
interesting_fact: GTA Semiconductor raised about RMB13.5B ($1.8B) in one funding round, one of China's largest for a specialty chip fab; industry veteran Zhang Rujing (SMIC founder) joined it as executive director.
notes: Hurun 'unicorn founder' tag is likely misleading: GTA is a CEC (state-owned) subsidiary. Sources: https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/2144877428720901 and https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/2012741344921093 . Low priority; identity/role not independently confirmed.

name: Itai Lahan
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Cloudinary
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Cloudinary in 2012 with Tal Lev-Ami (CTO) and Nadav Soferman (CPO), whom he met in the IDF's 8200 unit. Its API-based image/video management platform grew for years without VC before Bessemer invested; Hurun values it at ~$2bn, and it now ships AI agents for visual media.
interesting_fact: Cloudinary had paying customers within months of formation and grew organically for years without venture capital, before Bessemer Venture Partners invested to fund expansion.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cloudinary he was an executive at Israeli anti-spam startup Blue Security and at Collactive, founded news aggregator Newsodrome, and in 2009 co-founded Ndivi, a tech consultancy for start-up founders - the gap he noticed there sparked the Cloudinary idea.
notes: Press contact on Cloudinary newsroom: Juli Greenwood, Senior Director Global Communications. Has done developer-podcast interviews (Software Engineering Daily, 'Bootstrapping a SaaS for Developers') - receptive to podcast format.

name: Nadav Soferman
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Cloudinary
profile: Israeli engineer Nadav Soferman co-founded Cloudinary in early 2012 with Itai Lahan (CEO) and Tal Lev-Ami (CTO), whom he met in the IDF's 8200 unit. Cloudinary's API-first platform optimises, transforms and delivers images and video for the web; it bootstrapped for years before taking growth capital (~$2B valuation). As CPO he leads product.
interesting_fact: Cloudinary was a rare bootstrapped Israeli startup: five years in (2017) it had raised no venture capital, yet had 220,000 developers on its free tier and 5,000 paying customers including eBay and Sky News.
deep_cut_fact: Cloudinary's first version took just four months to build and launched quietly in mid-2012; the idea came from the founders' consulting firm Ndivi, where every new social-network client struggled to render images well on every device and resolution.
notes: Low-profile product-side founder (CEO Itai Lahan is the usual spokesperson). Press contact is Cloudinary's Senior Director of Global Communications (Juli Greenwood) as listed on the newsroom page. He has written for Smashing Magazine on responsive images.

name: Tal Lev-Ami
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Cloudinary
profile: Israeli developer who co-founded Cloudinary in 2012 with Itai Lahan and Nadav Soferman to fix the tedious work of uploading, transforming and delivering images and video online. The API-first media platform grew profitably without venture funding; a 2022 Blackstone-led secondary deal valued it at $2B. He remains CTO, focusing on AI-powered visual media at scale.
interesting_fact: Cloudinary bootstrapped its way to a $100M annual revenue run rate (2021) without venture capital, before Blackstone's $100M+ secondary investment valued it at $2B.
deep_cut_fact: Cloudinary worked with Google researchers to create the JPEG XL image format, and has since championed JPEG XL support across browsers and Apple devices.
notes: Press contact is Juli Greenwood, Senior Director Global Communications, as listed on the Cloudinary newsroom. He gives technical interviews (e.g. TechDogs Dec 2025). Deep-cut fact is about the company he co-founded, not him personally. Fit is CDN/media infrastructure rather than energy.

name: Ouyang Jian
current_role: CEO, Kunlunxin (昆仑芯, Beijing) - Baidu's AI-chip spin-off (CEO since June 2021; 2026 status per company news, not independently re-verified)
profile: Ouyang Jian (欧阳剑) was Baidu's chief chip architect and led its Kunlun AI-chip program. When Baidu spun Kunlun out in June 2021 (valued ~CNY 13B after a CPE-led round), he became CEO and legal representative. Kunlunxin sells AI accelerator cards and 'supernode' clusters for data centers and large models.
interesting_fact: Kunlunxin's spin-off entity was actually a 2011-registered Baidu shell company (星云融创) renamed in June 2021; at launch Baidu still owned ~76% and Ouyang framed it as building on 'Baidu's 10 years of accumulation in compute chips'.
deep_cut_fact: At the 2021 launch he said compute and semiconductor technology faced 'an unprecedented opportunity for change', and Kunlun's team presented at chip-design's top conference ISSCC 2021 just before the spin-off.
notes: Strong data-center/AI-chip fit. Company publishes only a business/cooperation mailbox (marketing@kunlunxin.com); no personal social accounts found. Speaks at Baidu/WAIC events; interviews mostly in Chinese. Web-search quota ran out, so his current title rests on the company's own news pages.

name: Jeff Elton
current_role: Vice Chairman and Founding CEO, ConcertAI (oncology real-world data and AI)
profile: Dr. Jeff Elton was founding CEO of ConcertAI, backed by founder/executive chairman Romesh Wadhwani, which combines oncology real-world data, clinical expertise and applied AI for pharma and providers (CancerLinQ, TeraRecon). After an April 2025 leadership transition Eron Kelly became CEO and Elton moved to vice chairman.
interesting_fact: ConcertAI now runs ASCO's CancerLinQ oncology quality platform and in 2025 launched a generative and agentic AI 'Precision Suite' that automates ASCO guidelines and clinical-trial matching.
notes: No longer CEO (vice chairman since 2025). Frequent podcast/interview guest (e.g. 'Cracking the Clinical Trial Code', AITech interview) so open to media; route via Treble PR. No sourced deep-cut found (web-search budget exhausted). Healthcare-AI angle rather than energy/data centers.

name: Chase Lochmiller
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chairman, Crusoe
profile: Co-founded Crusoe with Cully Cavness in 2018 to turn flared, otherwise-wasted natural gas into power for on-site computing. Crusoe has since become a vertically integrated AI-infrastructure company (energy, data centers, cloud) building campuses in Texas, Wyoming and beyond; in 2026 it raised a $3.9B Series F at a $30.9B valuation.
interesting_fact: Crusoe's origin was its patented 'Digital Flare Mitigation' technology: putting modular data centers at oil fields to burn stranded gas for computing instead of flaring it. It now reports 6GW+ of contracted capacity.
deep_cut_fact: On the Series F he framed Crusoe's strategy as 'controlling the infrastructure from electrons to tokens', saying AI 'will usher in an era of abundance'.
notes: Top-priority fit for an energy + data-center podcast. The Hurun '$10B valuation' is stale (now $30.9B). No published press email found; use the contact form or company socials. Web search budget ran out before personal background (education, earlier career) could be sourced.

name: Cully Cavness
current_role: Co-Founder, President and Chief Strategy Officer, Crusoe (AI data-centre / 'AI factory' developer and cloud), Denver
profile: Cully Cavness co-founded Crusoe with CEO Chase Lochmiller after leadership roles in upstream oil and gas, geothermal energy and energy investment banking (Middlebury and Oxford alum). Crusoe began by using stranded, flared natural gas to power bitcoin mining in oilfields, then pivoted to energy-first AI data centres, including the flagship campus for OpenAI's Stargate project.
interesting_fact: Crusoe's origin pitch: pay oil producers for gas they would otherwise flare for zero, and burn it in on-site generators to power computing; Cavness told Insider it was one of North America's biggest bitcoin miners, with units in North Dakota, Colorado and Montana.
deep_cut_fact: Before Crusoe he worked in the geothermal energy industry as well as upstream oil and gas, an early clean-energy thread that shows up in Crusoe's internal rule to pick projects only if they are net reducers of greenhouse gases.
notes: Perfect fit for an energy + data-centre podcast; frequent conference speaker (e.g., FII Riyadh). Title changed over time (President, COO, now President & Chief Strategy Officer per crusoe.ai). Route via media@crusoe.ai.

name: John Street
current_role: Founder and Chairman of the Board, Pax8 (Greenwood Village, Colorado); former CEO
profile: Denver native John Street is a serial Colorado founder who started Pax8 in 2012 as a cloud-commerce marketplace that lets managed service providers buy and bill Microsoft and other cloud/security products. Pax8 grew to ~2,000 employees and a multi-billion valuation; Street handed the CEO role to Scott Chasin and now chairs the board as Pax8 pushes into 'managed intelligence' AI agents.
interesting_fact: He received the 2023 Colorado Governor's Citizenship Medal for Growth and Innovation from Gov. Jared Polis and CTA's Bob Newman Lifetime Achievement Award in 2025, after being named CTA CEO of the Year in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: Pax8 is his fourth Colorado start-up: before it he launched Telephone Express, USA.Net (an early web-based email provider) and MX Logic (email security).
notes: Accessible, community-minded Colorado founder who does podcasts and local tech events (e.g. FirstMile Ventures 'Four Minute Founder', Colorado Voices on Tech). Route via Pax8 media relations. Note: the descriptions of USA.Net and MX Logic in parentheses are general knowledge; the source only lists the company names.

name: S. Zayd Enam
current_role: Co-founder of Cresta (enterprise contact-center AI, San Francisco); former CEO (Ping Wu became CEO in 2023); current title not verified
profile: Zayd Enam co-founded Cresta in 2017 out of Stanford's AI Lab with Sebastian Thrun and Tim Shi (an early OpenAI researcher). Cresta sells real-time AI agent-assist and AI agents to contact centers at Fortune 500 firms, backed by Greylock, a16z, Sequoia and Tiger Global (Series D $125M in 2024). Ping Wu replaced him as CEO in 2023.
interesting_fact: Cresta's first customer, in 2018, was Intuit, where it deployed a transformer-based real-time Agent Assist model - years before transformer-powered chat became mainstream with ChatGPT.
deep_cut_fact: Cresta was 'born at Stanford's AI Lab' in 2017 and co-founded with Sebastian Thrun, the Stanford professor behind Google's self-driving car project and Udacity.
notes: Web-search quota ran out, so his personal accounts/current title were not verified (verify LinkedIn/X before outreach). Thrun's Google/Udacity background is general knowledge, not from the cited page. Company-level contacts only; no press email published on cresta.com/press. Weak data-center fit (AI software); good AI-entrepreneurship guest.

name: Tim Shi (Tianlin Shi)
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Cresta (enterprise contact-center AI); formerly CTO
profile: Stanford AI Lab PhD researcher and early OpenAI researcher who co-founded Cresta in 2017 with Sebastian Thrun and Zayd Enam. Cresta builds real-time AI agent-assist and AI agents for customer-service teams (first customer Intuit), is backed by Greylock, a16z, Sequoia and Tiger Global, and serves Fortune 500 firms; Ping Wu became CEO in 2023.
interesting_fact: In 2018 Cresta deployed a transformer-based model for real-time agent assist at Intuit, years before the ChatGPT wave; the company emerged from stealth in 2020 with Greylock and a16z backing.
deep_cut_fact: As an OpenAI researcher he was first author, with Andrej Karpathy and Percy Liang, of 'World of Bits' (ICML 2017), a platform where AI agents complete web tasks using raw keyboard and mouse actions, an early precursor of today's computer-use agents.
notes: Technical founder; the World of Bits paper is a strong hook for an AI/data-center audience. LinkedIn is the one personal channel Cresta itself links to. No published press email found on the press page.

name: Xu Zhiqun
current_role: Founder, Gokin Solar Co., Ltd. (高景太阳能股份有限公司), Zhuhai, Guangdong
profile: Founder of Gokin Solar, set up in 2019 in Zhuhai, which grew within a few years into a top-3 global monocrystalline silicon wafer shipper and later added BC/high-efficiency modules and solar power plants. The company reports 6,000+ employees, bases in Guangdong, Qinghai and Sichuan, and sales in 30+ countries; it was valued around $2B as a Hurun unicorn.
interesting_fact: Gokin went from founding in 2019 to a top-3 global silicon-wafer shipper and reports five consecutive years of profitability, despite the solar industry's brutal price downturn.
deep_cut_fact: In a July 2026 company-blog essay ('To boil, first understand the fire') he recalls heating water in a big iron wok on a village stove as a child and quotes his mother: 'People should be loyal-hearted; a fire should be hollow-hearted' (人要忠心，火要空心), using it as a metaphor for Gokin's patience in the downturn.
notes: Writes reflective essays on the company's blog column (signed by him) - good conversation hook. His exact title and background not verified this pass (search budget exhausted).

name: Arthur Macedo
current_role: Listed as CloudWalk co-founder (chief commercial officer 2013-2018 per MarketScreener); current role unknown
profile: Arthur Macedo is listed by MarketScreener as one of five 2013 co-founders of CloudWalk, the Brazilian payments fintech behind InfinitePay (with Luis Silva, Behzad Malek, Bruno Freitas and Eliezer Pimentel), serving as chief commercial officer from 2013 to 2018. No independent press, company or filing source confirming his role or background was found.

name: Assaf Resnick
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, BigPanda (agentic AI for IT operations / AIOps)
profile: UC Berkeley Haas graduate who started at Moody's on Wall Street, then invested for Sequoia Capital (Israel) before co-founding BigPanda in 2012 with Elik Eizenberg. BigPanda, a unicorn, correlates IT monitoring alerts and automates incident response; in 2025-26 it repositioned around 'agentic ITOps' and an IT knowledge graph.
interesting_fact: He got the idea for BigPanda while at Sequoia, where he saw that as companies moved to the cloud, IT Ops teams were overwhelmed by alert noise from fragmented monitoring tools.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he began his career on Wall Street at Moody's. He says he left to 'marry my passion for tech with my background in investments', and that the 'courage and conviction' of Sequoia's founders inspired him to start BigPanda.

public_contacts.value: jbarbour@bigpanda.io (Jenne Barbour, Head of Corporate Marketing, listed as BigPanda contact on July 2026 release)

notes: Active speaker in 2026 (Emerj AI in Business podcast, July 2026; BigPanda 26 keynote, Atlanta, April 2026). Earlier 2026 releases list Adam Blau (VP Product Marketing) as media contact. bigpanda.io blocked automated fetches (403), so the leadership-page URL is from search results. Data-center angle: IT ops reliability and incident automation.

name: Wang Donglin
current_role: Founder and Chief Scientist, Smartlogic Technology (思朗科技), Beijing/Shanghai; STAR Market IPO application accepted July 2026
profile: Chip architect and former director of the CAS Institute of Automation. In 2016 he founded Smartlogic to commercialise his reconfigurable MaPU processor architecture, used in 5G small-cell, edge-AI and energy-management chips. Backed by CATL Capital, Smartlogic filed for a roughly RMB 4.4bn STAR Market IPO in 2026.
interesting_fact: CATL, the world's largest battery maker, led Smartlogic's D round. Investors cited MaPU's efficiency for AI inference and smart battery and energy-storage management, a link between AI chips and the energy sector.
deep_cut_fact: He invented the MaPU (Mathematics Processing Unit) architecture, described as the world's first reconfigurable chip architecture built on 'software-defined hardware'. It won a first-class Technology Invention Award from the Chinese Institute of Electronics, and he is a recipient of China's National Science Fund for Distinguished Young Scholars.
notes: The Hurun 'Smart Logic' entry maps to 思朗科技 (Smartlogic). The founder is written 王东琳 in Chinese media. He is described as founder and chief scientist; Zha Hao has been chairman and CEO since 2019. Wang directly holds about 19% and controls about 34%. Sources give different dates for his CAS posts. No public contact found; the company's IR office will open once the IPO proceeds.

name: Chris Mansi
current_role: CEO and co-founder, Viz.ai (AI disease detection and care coordination, San Francisco)
profile: Newcastle-raised, Cambridge-trained neurosurgeon who operated at Queen Square and King's College hospitals in London before moving to the US for a Stanford MBA. In 2016 he co-founded Viz.ai with ML postdoc David Golan; it won the first FDA clearance for an AI triage platform (stroke) and by its 10th anniversary (July 2026) was in 2,000 hospitals covering ~230M patients with 50+ AI care pathways.
interesting_fact: Viz.ai's software now 'helps one patient every six seconds'; Mansi calls it 'an AI safety net that works consistently across hospital settings'. The idea came from seeing surgeries go well yet patients die or end up disabled because getting them to the OR took too long.
deep_cut_fact: In 2012, while still a neurosurgeon, he started Edusurg, an online exam-prep business for junior surgeons; at Stanford he tinkered with 'every technology I could find', including 3D-printing brains for surgical practice and a cranial-nerve stimulation device.
notes: Frequent conference speaker and WEF contributor; accessible via PR agency. Healthcare AI rather than energy; angle could be AI deployment at scale in hospitals.

name: David Golan
current_role: Co-founder and board director, Viz.ai (former CTO); current operating role not found
profile: Israeli machine-learning researcher (PhD in statistics & ML, Tel Aviv University) who, as a Fulbright postdoc at Stanford applying deep learning to medical imaging and genetics, co-founded Viz.ai in 2016 with Chris Mansi and served as CTO. Viz.ai built the first FDA-cleared AI triage system for stroke (2018), now installed in 800+ hospitals in the US and Europe; he remains on the board.
interesting_fact: Viz.ai's software was the first AI-powered automatic stroke-triage system cleared by the FDA, alerting specialists directly so patients can be treated faster; it runs in 800+ hospitals.
deep_cut_fact: Before academia he founded the machine-learning team at Israeli startup b-hive Networks, acquired by VMware in 2008, and later co-authored 20+ scientific papers including three in the journal Science.
notes: Podcast entry is a past guest appearance (Brains Behind AI episode on building Viz.ai), not his own show; useful as prep. Left day-to-day role at Viz.ai; member of TechAviv founders club. No published personal/press email found; Viz.ai media inquiries via company site.

name: Manoj Ramachandran
current_role: Co-founder of Viz.ai; Consultant Orthopaedic & Trauma Surgeon (and reported Director of Innovation) at Barts Health NHS Trust, London; CEO & co-founder of halfloop (per profiles)
profile: London paediatric/young-adult orthopaedic surgeon who co-founded Viz.ai in 2016 with Chris Mansi and David Golan; its FDA-cleared AI care-coordination tools (stroke first, now cardio, vascular, oncology) made it a ~$1bn+ unicorn. He combines NHS practice at Barts with ventures, most recently halfloop (patient data for implant recipients).
interesting_fact: Viz.ai was his fourth business venture; in 2016 he described operating on children on Mondays and 'switching on in the evenings when Silicon Valley wakes up on the West Coast' to build the company.
deep_cut_fact: He became an orthopaedic consultant at a very young age (his self-described career highlight), has a keen interest in medical history - arguing most health solutions 'have been explored at some point in history but now we are adding a technological layer' - and is lead author of a Hodder Arnold basic orthopaedic sciences guide for fellowship exam candidates.
notes: Not a Viz.ai executive (CEO is Chris Mansi), so Viz.ai is an indirect route; halfloop or Barts Health innovation channels may be better. Titles (Professor, Director of Innovation, halfloop CEO) come from aggregator profiles - verify. Textbook detail via search results, not read directly. Personal wealth unconfirmed.

name: Fangjin Yang
current_role: Cofounder and CEO, Imply Data (Apache Druid-based real-time analytics / observability warehouse)
profile: Canadian engineer (Waterloo BASc EE, MASc CompE) who worked at Cisco and was a lead engineer at adtech startup Metamarkets, where he co-created open-source real-time database Apache Druid. In 2015 he cofounded Imply with Gian Merlino and Vadim Ogievetsky; it now sells Imply Lumi, an 'observability warehouse' for security and log data.
interesting_fact: He is one of the original authors of open-source real-time database Apache Druid, built at Metamarkets (acquired by Snap in 2017); Imply, founded by Druid's creators, is backed by a16z, Bessemer and Thoma Bravo.
deep_cut_fact: In April 2023 he returned to his alma mater to give a University of Waterloo Engineering talk, 'Getting out of the garage', on taking a startup from idea to scale.
notes: Accessible, technical founder who speaks at conferences (Data Council, O'Reilly, Waterloo). Real-time data infrastructure angle fits data-center/AI theme. Press via Imply's PR agency INK Communications.

name: Gian Merlino
current_role: Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer, Imply Data
profile: Gian Merlino is an original author of Apache Druid, the open-source real-time analytics database built at Metamarkets, where he led data ingestion after senior roles at Yahoo. In 2015 he co-founded Imply with Fangjin Yang and Vadim Ogievetsky to commercialise Druid (a16z-backed, about $1bn valuation) and remains its CTO.
interesting_fact: Druid powers real-time analytics at large internet companies. Merlino was the Apache Druid project's first PMC (Project Management Committee) chair after it entered the Apache Software Foundation.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a B.S. in Computer Science from Caltech. He still gives hands-on technical talks, for example 'Swimming in the Data River, or When Streaming Analytics Isn't' at Data Council 2025, about where streaming analytics fits.
notes: Engineer-founder who speaks regularly at data conferences (Data Council/AI Council, Strata, Databricks Data+AI Summit), so he is likely open to technical podcasts. No published press email found on imply.io; the contact form and the company X account are company channels, not personal.

name: Vadim Ogievetsky
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Experience Officer (CXO), Imply Data
profile: Stanford CS master's graduate who, at Metamarkets (later acquired by Snap), was one of the original authors of the Apache Druid real-time analytics database. In 2015 he cofounded Imply with Fangjin Yang and Gian Merlino to commercialise Druid; it became a $1B+ unicorn backed by a16z. As CXO he leads Imply's product experience and UI, including its Druid console.
interesting_fact: He is one of the original authors of Apache Druid, the open-source real-time analytics database used by companies like Netflix, Airbnb and Salesforce.
deep_cut_fact: Before databases, he was in Stanford's Data Visualization group, where he contributed to Protovis and was one of the co-authors of D3.js, the JavaScript library behind much of the web's interactive data journalism.
notes: Strong data-infra/visualisation podcast angle (D3 + Druid). No press email found on imply.io (press/contact pages timed out). Fallback is Imply's site contact form. Druid's named enterprise users are commonly cited in Druid materials and were not separately verified here.

name: Balaji Srinivasan
current_role: Founder, The Network School; founder, Balaji Fund; author of 'The Network State'
profile: Balaji S. Srinivasan (b. 1980; Stanford EE PhD) co-founded Counsyl (sold to Myriad for $375m), was an a16z general partner, co-founded 21 Inc/Earn.com (sold to Coinbase in 2018, where he became first CTO) and relocation start-up Teleport (2014, sold to Topia). He now runs the Network School (now in Kazakhstan) and the Balaji Fund.
interesting_fact: His self-published 2022 book 'The Network State: How To Start a New Country' hit No. 2 on the Wall Street Journal's e-book bestseller list, and in 2017 the Trump administration considered him for FDA Commissioner.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he taught Stanford's 'Startup Engineering' online course, which Business Insider ranked in 2014 as the sixth most popular free online course for professionals; his genomics papers have 5,000+ citations.
notes: IDENTITY CAVEAT: Hurun lists him as founder of a $1bn cloud unicorn 'Teleport' - that is almost certainly Gravitational/Teleport (founders Ev Kontsevoy et al.), not Balaji's 2014 relocation start-up teleport.org (sold to Topia). Treat the Hurun attribution as an error. Very active on X; reachable publicly. Renounced US citizenship in 2023.

name: Silver Keskküla
current_role: CEO, ScamGuardian.AI (deepfake-scam defence); also runs trackAIanswers.com; CDL-Estonia associate
profile: Estonian engineer-entrepreneur Silver Keskküla was the first researcher on Skype's core team, then co-founded Teleport (2014, with Sten Tamkivi and Balaji Srinivasan), a data-driven relocation search engine for 'digital nomads' later acquired by MOVE Guides/Topia (2017). He then founded AI startup Supervaisor and now builds AI-safety and LLM-brand-monitoring tools.
interesting_fact: Teleport, which he co-founded with ex-Skype executive Sten Tamkivi and Balaji Srinivasan, began as a search engine to help people pick cities to live and work in, and was acquired by global-mobility firm MOVE Guides (now Topia).
deep_cut_fact: At Skype he used machine learning to optimise the peer-to-peer network topology, shipping neural networks to hundreds of millions of computers years before the deep-learning boom; he says he is most inspired by bio-mimetic algorithms, from evolutionary computation to neural nets.
notes: Identity confirmed as Teleport co-founder, but the input's claim that Teleport was a $1B 'unicorn' is doubtful: it was a modest exit to MOVE Guides/Topia, so the Hurun listing may be an error. Not a UHNW profile. Approachable startup founder; also raised what was described as Estonia's largest solo-founder angel round for Supervaisor.

name: Sten Tamkivi
current_role: Partner, Plural (European founder-led VC platform); Founding Partner, Creative Destruction Lab Estonia
profile: Estonian entrepreneur and investor who spent 8+ years as an early Skype executive through its $8.5B sale to Microsoft. As an EIR at Andreessen Horowitz he co-founded Teleport, a tool for remote workers and digital nomads that pivoted to B2B and was acquired by Topia in 2017; he stayed as Topia's CPO through a $48M Series C. He now invests as a partner at Plural.
interesting_fact: Teleport was co-founded while he was an entrepreneur-in-residence at Andreessen Horowitz, after his Skype years spanning startup to the $8.5B Microsoft exit.
deep_cut_fact: He started his entrepreneurial career in 1996, aged 18, by founding the first digital media agency in Estonia.
notes: Very accessible and public: active on X and LinkedIn, gives interviews (ERR, Estonian World, Seedcamp). Founders Pledge member. Hurun lists him via Teleport, but his wealth is mainly from Skype/Teleport exits. Good podcast guest candidate.

name: Gu Jing
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Viewtrix Technology Co., Ltd (云英谷科技 / Yunyinggu, HKEX: 3310)
profile: Dr. Gu Jing founded Shenzhen-based fabless chip designer Viewtrix (Yunyinggu) in 2012. It is China's leading AMOLED display-driver IC supplier for smartphones and, per Frost & Sullivan, No. 2 globally in micro-OLED backplanes for AR/VR, with a ~40.7% share. Viewtrix listed on the Hong Kong Main Board on 27 May 2026, and in September 2026 it began preparing an A-share listing.
interesting_fact: Viewtrix shipped 51.4 million AMOLED driver ICs in 2024, up from 14.1 million in 2022, with revenue near $130M. Its micro-OLED backplanes go into the near-eye displays used in AR/VR headsets.
deep_cut_fact: Gu is personally the named inventor on a string of Yunyinggu patents covering subpixel rendering and display-driving methods, the image-processing tricks that let OLED panels look sharper with fewer physical subpixels.
notes: 'Viewtrix' is 云英谷 (Yunyinggu), not the similarly named Hefei micro-OLED maker SeeYA (视涯, founder Gu Tie). A Harvard engineering PhD is claimed only by Dealroom (unverified). I found no published IR email; check the forthcoming 2026 interim report on HKEXnews for the IR contact. A good fit for AI-hardware and AR themes.

profile: Listed by Hurun (2022-2025 unicorn founders) as a founder of Viewtrix. Viewtrix (云英谷科技 / Yunyinggu, Shenzhen) makes OLED display-driver ICs and micro-OLED microdisplays for AR/VR and listed in Hong Kong in May 2026 (03310.HK). Public sources name Dr. Gu Jing (Tsinghua; Harvard PhD) as founder, chairman and CEO; no public mention of Xue Wenxiang found.

name: Lin Yuanqing
current_role: Founder & CEO, Aibee (爱笔智能), Beijing
profile: Lin Yuanqing (Yuanqing Lin) is a computer-vision researcher who led media analytics at NEC Labs America, then directed Baidu's Institute of Deep Learning (2015-2017) under Andrew Ng. He left in late 2017 to found Aibee, raising $25m within a month; Aibee sells AI 'total solutions' (footfall analytics, navigation, parking, face access) for malls, retailers, banks and airports and was valued at ~$1bn.
interesting_fact: He was featured as one of the 'Heroes of Deep Learning' interviewees in Andrew Ng's deeplearning.ai course, reflecting his time running Baidu's Institute of Deep Learning.
deep_cut_fact: He is first-listed on the NEC-UIUC team that won the very first ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge in 2010, two years before AlexNet made the contest famous.
notes: Baidu appointment source: https://sg.news.yahoo.com/finance/news/baidu-appoints-yuanqing-lin-computer-010000604.html ; Aibee founding/funding: https://syncedreview.com/2018/01/19/life-after-baidu-yuanqing-lins-ai-startup-moves-fast-on-funding-and-b2b-opportunities/. Aibee website footer dated 2019, so confirm company's current status. Technical founder; good for an AI-infrastructure conversation.

name: John de Souza
current_role: Co-founder and President, Ample (modular EV battery swapping; San Francisco)
profile: Serial entrepreneur (MIT SB/SM in EECS) who co-founded Smartleaf, Flash Communications and MedHelp before co-founding Ample with MedHelp's CTO, Khaled Hassounah. Ample's robotic stations swap modular EV batteries in about five minutes. It raised $330M+ and ran pilots with Uber drivers, Stellantis/Fiat in Madrid and Mitsubishi Fuso/Yamato in Tokyo.
interesting_fact: Ample's stations swap an EV's modular battery in about five minutes. Investors had been scared off by the failure of Better Place, but the founders still raised over $275M by 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Born and raised in Ethiopia, he moved with his family to Dubai in the 1970s, then came to the US at 16 on a full university scholarship. He later co-founded Flash Communications, a real-time two-way messaging startup acquired by Microsoft.
notes: Ample filed for Chapter 11 in Dec 2025 (Electrek, CCJ), so its unicorn status is stale; be tactful. No press email was found (ample.com contact/press pages return 404). The podcast entry is a past guest spot, not his own show. The Microsoft acquisition of Flash comes from profile summaries; TechCrunch confirms only that he co-founded Flash.

name: Khaled Hassounah
current_role: Co-Founder & CEO, Ample (San Francisco EV battery-swapping company)
profile: Jordan-trained electrical engineer (University of Jordan, 1998) who co-founded Ample with John de Souza in 2014 to build robotic, modular EV battery-swapping stations. Ample has run stations for Uber drivers in the Bay Area, expanded to Japan with ENEOS and partnered with Stellantis; its newest stations swap a battery in about five minutes.
interesting_fact: TIME named Ample to its TIME100 Most Influential Companies list in 2023 (Disrupters); Hassounah argues Ample's real competitor is gasoline, not charging.
deep_cut_fact: Before Ample he was co-founder and CTO of MedHelp, an online health community, and sat on the board of KarmSolar, Egypt's first private off-grid solar power company.
notes: Strong energy fit (EV infrastructure, solar background). Has appeared on climate podcasts (MCJ 'Inevitable' - https://mcj.vc/inevitable-podcast/ample), so podcast-friendly. No published press email found on ample.com (contact page is JS-only); LinkedIn link is the company page, not personal. Deep-cut source is a third-party bio aggregator; KarmSolar board role may be past.

name: Michael I. Jordan
current_role: Directeur de Recherche, Inria and ENS Paris; Pehong Chen Distinguished Professor Emeritus, UC Berkeley; co-founder of Anyscale and Arena Intelligence
profile: Among the most influential figures in machine learning and statistics, he was an MIT professor (1988-98) and then at Berkeley, where his RISELab students created Ray and spun out Anyscale, the distributed-AI-compute company he co-founded. He went emeritus in 2024, now researches at Inria Paris, and won the 2025 BBVA Frontiers of Knowledge Award.
interesting_fact: In 2016 an article in Science, using Semantic Scholar rankings, named him the 'most influential computer scientist' in the world.
deep_cut_fact: His degrees are not in computer science: a master's in mathematics from Arizona State and a 1985 PhD in cognitive science from UC San Diego. Beyond AI startups, he sits on the board of UnitedMasters, the independent-music distribution company.
notes: This is the Berkeley ML professor, not the basketball player. The email is his academic address, published on his own homepage; he is now based mostly in Paris (Inria). He is an outspoken critic of 'AI' hype who favours framing it as economics plus ML. Strong guest for AI-infrastructure topics: Ray and Anyscale underpin large-scale AI compute.

name: Philipp Moritz
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Anyscale (Ray) - being acquired by AI cloud/data-center operator Nscale (deal signed July 2026)
profile: Computer scientist who did his PhD at UC Berkeley's RISELab, where he co-created the open-source distributed computing framework Ray with Robert Nishihara and Ion Stoica. The trio founded Anyscale in 2019 to commercialize Ray, now a standard for scaling AI training/inference (used by OpenAI among others). In July 2026 London-based Nscale agreed to buy Anyscale to add orchestration software to its power-data-center-GPU stack.
interesting_fact: Nscale's acquisition makes Anyscale the software layer of a vertically integrated AI cloud spanning power, data centers and compute; Anyscale's ~200 staff will join Nscale while keeping the Anyscale brand.
deep_cut_fact: Before Ray, he co-authored the landmark 2015 reinforcement-learning paper 'Trust Region Policy Optimization' (TRPO) with John Schulman, Sergey Levine, Michael I. Jordan and Pieter Abbeel - a precursor to PPO.
notes: Ideal data-center/AI-infra guest given the Nscale deal. Education details (Würzburg physics BSc, Cambridge Part III maths) come only from aggregators - not used. PR contact predates the Nscale deal; may now route via Nscale comms. Ray paper: arxiv.org/abs/1712.05889.

name: Robert Nishihara
current_role: Co-Founder, Anyscale (CEO until July 2024; now leads customer engagement and helps shape product roadmap/strategy)
profile: Harvard math grad and UC Berkeley CS PhD who co-created the open-source distributed-computing framework Ray with Philipp Moritz and Ion Stoica in Berkeley's RISELab, then co-founded Anyscale to commercialize it. Ray has become a standard way to scale AI training and inference across clusters; Nishihara handed the CEO role to Keerti Melkote in 2024.
interesting_fact: Anyscale's open-source Ray is a 'picks-and-shovels' layer of the generative-AI boom, used by OpenAI among others to train and deploy models at scale; by 2024 it had 50,000+ developers and was growing 6x a year.
deep_cut_fact: Ray began as a side effort during his Berkeley PhD: he and Moritz were doing theoretical ML research (reinforcement learning, optimization) and, rather than cobble together yet another single-purpose system to scale their experiments, built a general framework instead.
notes: Frequent conference and podcast guest (Ray Summit, Gradient Dissent, Python Podcast, Data Council), so a likely yes for a podcast on AI compute and data centers. PR agency LaunchSquad handles Anyscale media (as of the July 2024 release).

name: Orral Nadjari
current_role: Founder of an unnamed battery-cell venture based in Abu Dhabi, UAE (as of Aug 2025); former founder and CEO of Britishvolt
profile: Swedish financier (formerly at Gothenburg corporate-bond house Jool Capital) who co-founded Britishvolt in 2019 to build a UK gigafactory at Cambois, Northumberland, briefly valued at about $1B. He stepped down as CEO in Aug 2022, and the company closed in 2023 after failing to raise capital. He is now building, from Abu Dhabi, a venture to make battery cells for high-end EVs, robots and flying taxis.
interesting_fact: On moving his battery ambitions to the Gulf, he said: 'The leadership in the GCC, the monarchs, have a get-it-done ethos which I believe to a certain degree we might be lacking in Europe.'
notes: Sensitive: Britishvolt's collapse was a high-profile UK failure, so frame any outreach around his new Gulf battery venture. He declined to name the new company, its 50,000 sq m factory location or its funders (Sifted, Aug 2025: https://sifted.eu/articles/britishvolt-founder-orral-nadjari-gulf). No published contact channels found; the Hurun $1B figure is stale.

name: Martin Greenwald
current_role: Cofounder, Commonwealth Fusion Systems; Research Affiliate (former deputy director), MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center
profile: Martin Greenwald is a plasma physicist (MIT BS, Berkeley PhD) who spent 43 years at MIT's Plasma Science and Fusion Center, rising to deputy director and leading physics on the Alcator tokamaks. In 2018 he cofounded Commonwealth Fusion Systems, the MIT spinout building the compact SPARC tokamak, and headed SPARC's physics group. He stepped back in 2022.
interesting_fact: He discovered the 'Greenwald density limit', a tokamak scaling law showing plasma fuel density can rise with magnetic field and smaller machine size - a key reason CFS's compact, high-field SPARC design can reach high fusion power density.
deep_cut_fact: His first claim to fame, as a Berkeley grad student, was building diagnostics whose measurements shut down the TORMAC fusion concept he worked on ('It didn't work out very well,' he laughs). At MIT he later fuelled Alcator C by firing frozen fuel pellets into the plasma - 'snowballs in hell'.

public_contacts.value: g@psfc.mit.edu (MIT PSFC work email, listed on his faculty page)
rivenberg@psfc.mit.edu (Paul Rivenberg, MIT PSFC press contact)

notes: Academic scientist rather than a typical billionaire-founder; very approachable and has given NPR and National Academy of Engineering interviews. Excellent podcast fit for fusion/energy. Hurun 'founder' listing reflects CFS cofounder status, not disclosed wealth.

name: Robert Mumgaard
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS)
profile: Omaha-born Bob Mumgaard (UNL mechanical engineering & physics; MIT nuclear engineering MS, plasma physics PhD) co-founded MIT spinout CFS in 2018 to build compact tokamaks with high-temperature superconducting magnets. CFS is finishing its SPARC demo in Massachusetts (to turn on in 2027) and plans its first ARC power plant in Virginia for the early 2030s.
interesting_fact: In June 2025 Google agreed to buy 200 MW - half the output - of CFS's first ARC fusion plant in Virginia, the first direct corporate PPA for fusion power, and increased its equity stake in CFS.
deep_cut_fact: He has joked that Nebraska mechanical engineers 'are very talented, but they end up building things like combines and tractors' - not what he wanted - and that he 'fell in love with physics late'; growing up in Nebraska, he says, 'you grow up knowing about weather and climate.'
notes: Top-tier fit for energy + data-center podcast (fusion power for Google data centers; testifies to Congress on fusion policy). Very media-active (Masters of Scale, MCJ podcast). Route: press@cfs.energy.

name: Alexander Mans
current_role: Founder and CEO, FLYR (FLYR Labs), AI-driven revenue-management and Offer & Order platform for airlines and travel
profile: Dutch-born Alex Mans moved to Silicon Valley in 2013 to build FLYR, starting as CTO and becoming CEO in 2020. FLYR pivoted to B2B AI forecasting and pricing for airlines (JetBlue, Avianca, Air New Zealand, Virgin Atlantic), added hotels via Pace Revenue, raised $500m+ (WestCap, BlackRock) and now powers Offer & Order retailing, e.g. for Riyadh Air.
interesting_fact: FLYR's ambition is a 'Commercial Operating System' for transportation: replacing decades-old airline revenue-management and reservation systems with AI-native retailing (Offer & Order), with rail, rental cars and cruise lines next.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in the Netherlands, he taught himself to write software around age 10 and has been building startups ever since finishing high school; a self-described lifelong aviation enthusiast, he founded FLYR specifically to combine his two fascinations, AI and aviation.
notes: Regular conference speaker (Skift, World Aviation Festival) and podcast guest (PhocusWire 'How I Got Here'). FLYR is private; $1bn unicorn valuation dates from 2022.

name: Cyril Guiraud
current_role: Co-founder (original CMO), FLYR Labs; current role not confirmed - a San Francisco-based Cyril Guiraud is listed as co-founder of music start-ups doubleOone and everwave
profile: Co-founded FLYR in San Francisco in 2013 with Alex Mans and Jean Tripier as a consumer airfare-prediction start-up, joining as CMO. FLYR later pivoted to AI revenue-management and offer/order software for airlines (e.g. Riyadh Air). He no longer appears among FLYR's executives.
interesting_fact: FLYR started life as a consumer app that predicted airfares and let travellers lock in prices, before pivoting to selling deep-learning revenue-management systems to airlines themselves.
notes: FLYR co-founder/CMO role reported by PhocusWire and MarketScreener (blocked to direct fetch). A French-born SF saxophonist/producer named Cyril Guiraud (founder of music start-up doubleOone; https://www.syos.co/en/artists/cyril-guiraud) is likely the same person but unconfirmed - verify first. No published contact; weak energy/AI-infra fit.

current_role: Co-founder, FLYR Labs (FLYR Inc., travel/airline AI); current title unconfirmed
profile: French-born, ESCP Europe and Harvard MBA-educated tech executive who co-founded FLYR (c. 2013) with Alexander Mans and Cyril Guiraud. FLYR is a San Francisco-based AI platform for airline revenue management and offer/order retailing, backed by Vista Equity Partners and valued at ~$1B+. Earlier he was chief executive of WorldMate, a mobile travel-itinerary app company.
interesting_fact: FLYR applies deep learning to airline pricing and revenue management, and now runs the native offer-and-order platform for new Saudi carrier Riyadh Air.

name: Pranay Agrawal
current_role: Co-founder; Non-Executive Director and CEO, Fractal USA, Fractal Analytics (NSE/BSE listed)
profile: Pranay Agrawal co-founded Fractal Analytics in Mumbai in 2000 with Srikanth Velamakanni and others, after working as a manager at ICICI Bank (1998-2000). Group14 makes silicon-carbon anode material (SCC55) that boosts lithium-ion energy density by up to 50%, has factories in Washington state and Sangju, South Korea (EV-scale production from 2026), and closed a EUR 150M Series D extension in Oct 2026.

profile: Shenzhen-born founder of Infervision, a Beijing medical-imaging AI company started in 2016 whose deep-learning tools help radiologists screen CT scans for lung cancer, stroke and other conditions across hospitals in China, Europe, Japan and the US. name: Abhinai Srivastava
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Mashgin (AI computer-vision self-checkout, Palo Alto)
profile: IIT Delhi CS graduate who co-founded Mashgin (founded 2013; YC W15) with dorm-mate Mukul Dhankhar. Its barcode-free computer-vision kiosks let customers pay in about 10 seconds in stadiums, cafeterias and convenience stores. A 2022 $62.5M Series B led by NEA valued Mashgin at $1.5B.
interesting_fact: Mashgin says its system rings up multiple items in half a second with 99.9% identification accuracy, making checkout four times faster than cashiers.
deep_cut_fact: Mashgin began with a lunch line: co-founder Mukul Dhankhar, then working on Toyota computer-vision research, kept losing 30-40 minutes a day in a corporate cafeteria queue. He flew to California, reconnected with Srivastava (his dorm-mate at IIT Delhi), and his early demo convinced Srivastava to join.
notes: contact@mashgin.com is Mashgin's general company inbox (not personal). Prior employers (Yahoo/Microsoft/Facebook) come only from aggregator profiles and are unverified. Edge-AI/computer-vision angle rather than data center.

name: Mukul Dhankhar
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Mashgin (computer-vision self-checkout, Palo Alto/San Francisco)
profile: IIT Delhi-trained computer-vision engineer who worked on camera-based perception for Toyota before co-founding Mashgin in 2013 with his IIT dorm-mate Abhinai Srivastava (YC W15). Mashgin's kiosks recognise multiple items without barcodes in about half a second; its 2022 NEA-led Series B valued it at $1.5bn, with kiosks in stadiums, airports, convenience stores and corporate cafeterias.
interesting_fact: Mashgin's kiosks ring up multiple items in roughly half a second with ~99.9% identification accuracy and no barcodes, and are installed at venues such as Madison Square Garden, Citi Field and Arrowhead Stadium.

name: Anand Babu (AB) Periasamy
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO (with Garima Kapoor), MinIO, Inc. (Redwood City, CA)
profile: Free-software developer (Annamalai University CS) who co-founded Gluster (open-source distributed file system, sold to Red Hat in 2011 for a reported ~$136m), then MinIO in 2014 with Garima Kapoor and Harshavardhana. MinIO's S3-compatible object storage (AIStor) is a common data layer for AI and private-cloud infrastructure.
interesting_fact: He says he built Gluster 'accidentally' while trying to solve storage for supercomputing clusters; Red Hat's acquisition made Gluster the basis of Red Hat Storage.
deep_cut_fact: In 2004, as CTO of California Digital Corp., he led development of Lawrence Livermore's 'Thunder', then the world's second-fastest supercomputer; he also wrote GNU FreeIPMI and GNU FreeTalk and sat on the board of Free Software Foundation India.
notes: Very accessible and podcast-friendly: has guested on Last Week in AWS 'Screaming in the Cloud' and speaks at open-source conferences. Strong data-center/AI-storage fit. MinIO's site offers only a generic contact form; X handle is self-published in his SCALE speaker bio.

name: Frederick Kautz
current_role: Cloud-native security / zero-trust architect and open-source leader; SPIFFE Steering Committee member (current employer not confirmed; TheOrg lists HumanForm Technologies)
profile: Software engineer named among MinIO's co-founders in 2015 coverage (Nov 2014 founding, after he was a senior principal engineer at Red Hat and CTO of GridX); MinIO's own site now credits three other founders. He went on to co-found Network Service Mesh, co-create OmniBOR and ProtoBOM, lead architecture at Elevance Health and co-chair KubeCon + CloudNativeCon.

name: Noam Ben-Zvi

name: Miri Ratner
current_role: Co-Founder and VP R&D, Vayyar Imaging (Yehud, Israel)
profile: Israeli R&D executive with 20+ years in wireless and telecom engineering who co-founded Vayyar Imaging in 2011 with Raviv Melamed and Naftali Chayat. Vayyar builds single-chip 4D mmWave imaging radar used in automotive in-cabin sensing, eldercare fall detection, smart home and industrial applications, and raised $108m in a Koch-led Series E in 2021, reaching unicorn valuation.

Her BSc is in maths and computer science from Bar-Ilan.
notes: Low public profile; the CEO, Raviv Melamed, is Vayyar's usual spokesperson. No current published press email found (older releases list agency/individual contacts from 2020-22). Vayyar's press page is https://vayyar.com/press/. Fit with data-center/AI focus is limited (sensing chips).

name: Naftali Chayat
current_role: Co-Founder and CTO, Vayyar Imaging (Yehud, Israel)
profile: Naftali Chayat co-founded Vayyar in 2011 with Raviv Melamed and Miri Ratner to put 3D/4D imaging radar on a single chip. Vayyar's radar-on-chip is used for elder-care fall detection (Vayyar Care), in-car occupant and child-presence sensing, and robotics. He brings over 30 years in signal processing, radio systems and antennas.

Before Vayyar he was Chief Scientist of BreezeCOM/Alvarion, an early broadband-wireless pioneer, and represented it in IEEE 802.16 (WiMAX) work.

name: Raviv Melamed
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chairman, Vayyar Imaging (Yehud, Israel)
profile: Raviv Melamed (BSc/MSc EE, Ben-Gurion University) joined Intel through its acquisition of startup Envara and rose to VP of the Intel Architecture Group and GM of its mobile wireless group. In 2011 he co-founded Vayyar, which makes low-cost 4D mmWave radar-imaging chips for in-cabin automotive sensing, elder care and more. It became a unicorn after its Series E.
interesting_fact: Vayyar began as a breast-cancer imaging project: Melamed asked why radio waves couldn't look inside the body if cheap RF silicon and MIMO radar made imaging affordable. The same sensor then spread to in-wall imaging, food contaminant detection, cars and elder-care fall detection.
deep_cut_fact: Melamed says he 'started life as an engineer at 13', building electronics and trying to sell them. Vayyar's core idea came from his army work using radio waves to see through walls, which he later reapplied to medical imaging.
notes: Israeli. Vayyar has had layoffs and a strategic shift amid cash burn (Calcalist); avoid that topic. Best route is press@vayyar.com. Sensing and radar fit less directly with energy and data centers, but his chip and wireless background (Intel) is a good angle.

name: Lu Chuan
current_role: Chairman, Chint Anneng Digital Energy; Chairman & President, Chint New Energy Technology (Astronergy); Chairman, Chint New Energy Development; Chairman, Chint Power; director, Chint Group
profile: Born 1981, Lu Chuan leads Chint Group's new-energy arm: module maker Chint New Energy Technology (Astronergy, ~6th largest module shipper globally), residential-PV leader Chint Anneng (valued ~$4B by Hurun), project developer Chint New Energy (40+ countries), and inverter/storage maker Chint Power, where he became chairman in May 2026.

name: Casey Morrison
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Astera Labs (NASDAQ: ALAB)
profile: Casey Morrison (MSEE, Univ. of Florida) was a systems engineering leader at Texas Instruments. In 2017 he co-founded Astera Labs with TI colleagues Jitendra Mohan and Sanjay Gajendra. Astera makes PCIe/CXL/Ethernet retimers, smart-cable modules and switches linking AI accelerators in hyperscale data centers; it IPO'd in March 2024 and he runs its product organization.
interesting_fact: He and his two co-founders were named EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2025 award winners. EY notes Astera hires only about 2% of the candidates it interviews.
deep_cut_fact: The three founders met while working at Texas Instruments, where Morrison was a systems engineering manager and member of the group technical staff, before leaving in late 2017 to start Astera in the Bay Area.
notes: Highly on-topic (AI data-center connectivity). He speaks at industry events (OCP, Hot Chips-type venues). Route via Astera IR/corporate marketing. TI tenure dates conflict across profiles (2005 vs 2012 start). The TI titles come from Crunchbase/TheOrg, not the EY page.

name: Yu Huigen
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Beijing WeLion New Energy Technology (卫蓝新能源)
profile: Lanzhou University chemistry graduate and former EV-maker chief battery engineer (BAIC New Energy) who co-founded WeLion in 2016 with academician Chen Liquan and Li Hong, spun out of CAS's Institute of Physics. WeLion makes semi/all-solid-state batteries; backers include Huawei Hubble, Xiaomi, NIO and Geely; valued ~RMB18.5B at its Dec 2025 ChiNext IPO tutoring.
interesting_fact: WeLion supplied the cells in NIO's 150kWh semi-solid-state pack, on which NIO founder William Li drove 1,044 km on one charge in a late-2023 livestream. Yu says WeLion's first all-solid-state cells will reach 400Wh/kg, with small-batch vehicle installation planned for 2027.
deep_cut_fact: He was one of China's earliest EV drivers. In winter 2010, as a carmaker's chief battery engineer, he drove its first-generation electric car daily between central Beijing and the suburbs, and watched the range drop from 150km to just over 70km in the cold. That range anxiety drives his solid-state work.
notes: The contact form has an 'I am a media' option. WeLion is preparing a ChiNext IPO (CITIC Securities tutoring from Dec 2025, per Jiemian), billed as the potential 'first solid-state battery stock'. Excellent energy and battery-storage guest. The BAIC detail comes from search snippets of the 36Kr project page.

name: Li Di
current_role: Founder, Nextie (明日新程), a 'collective intelligence and cognitive large model' AI startup; former CEO of Xiaoice (left April 2025)
profile: Li Di (李笛), known as the 'father of Microsoft Xiaoice', led the Xiaoice chatbot team at Microsoft from 2014 and also oversaw Bing China. He became CEO when Xiaoice was spun out of Microsoft in July 2020 and was its second-largest shareholder (about 25%). He left in April 2025 and in December 2025 unveiled Nextie, a MiraclePlus-backed startup of about 30 people, mostly from the original Xiaoice team.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Xiaoice grew from a Microsoft chatbot into a global product line covering China, Japan, the US, India and other markets, and became one of China's first AI unicorns after the 2020 spin-out.
deep_cut_fact: A Tsinghua graduate, he joined Microsoft's Asia internet engineering academy in September 2013, where he pioneered Microsoft's AI emotional-computing framework. He later became the academy's executive vice president.
notes: Xiaoice is no longer the right route. He debuted Nextie at MiraclePlus (奇绩创坛) Demo Day on Dec 7, 2025, and Nextie was planning a ~$10M funding round. No published Nextie press contact was found. English coverage: https://news.aibase.com/news/23484. He gives long-form interviews to Chinese tech media (36Kr, ifanr).

name: Li Lianrong
profile: Listed by Hurun (Unicorn founders 2023-2025) as founder of 'Spiche', a new-energy company valued at about $2B. Searches in English and Chinese (李连荣) did not identify the company or the person, so nothing further is recorded.
