name: Joo-Wan Lee
current_role: Founder and Chairman of the Board, MegazoneCloud (Seoul); handed CEO role to ex-AWS executive Yeom Dong-hoon in Jan 2025
profile: Korean entrepreneur who founded Megazone in 1998 as a web agency/hosting business, pivoted to cloud and spun off MegazoneCloud in 2018 - Korea's largest cloud MSP and first MSP unicorn (2022), with 2023 revenue of ~KRW 1.5tn. As chairman he now focuses on IPO preparation, new businesses and investments.
interesting_fact: Megazone was an early AWS partner in Korea and MegazoneCloud went on to win AWS's APJ Consulting Partner of the Year award in back-to-back years (incl. 2025).
deep_cut_fact: He started Megazone in 1998 while still a university student majoring in computer programming; its first businesses were classic first-generation internet services - web agency work, online shopping malls and hosting.
notes: MegazoneCloud is preparing an IPO (valuation talk ~KRW 3tn). cloud@megazone.com is the general business inquiry inbox. Founding detail cross-checked with Dealroom (1998 web agency/hosting origins); student detail comes from a blog - moderate confidence.

name: Yao Xing
current_role: Founder, XVERSE (元象, Shenzhen) — AI/3D and large-model company
profile: Former Tencent Group VP (姚星) who joined Tencent in 2004, ran its architecture, infrastructure and search-technology units, and in 2016 built Tencent AI Lab. He left in early 2021 to found XVERSE (元象唯思), first aimed at AI-generated 3D worlds and later at open-source LLMs (XVERSE-13B, MoE models) and entertainment AI apps. The company is valued at ~$2B.
interesting_fact: XVERSE-13B, its open-source multilingual LLM trained on 1.4 trillion tokens with a free commercial license, topped Hugging Face's trending chart about a week after release in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: As head of Tencent AI Lab he assembled the team behind the Go AI 'Fine Art' (绝艺), which won the 10th UEC Cup computer-Go tournament in Japan in March 2017; he appears in the winning team photo.
notes: opensource@xverse.cn is XVERSE's published inbox for open-source questions and collaborations, not a press line. Mostly covered in Chinese media (36Kr, Huxiu, QbitAI); founding reported by 36Kr: https://www.36kr.com/p/1144447936185737.

name: Jack Kokko
current_role: Founder and CEO, AlphaSense
profile: Finnish-born Jaakko 'Jack' Kokko was a Morgan Stanley tech/telecom M&A analyst in London and Menlo Park, then co-founded AlphaSense with Wharton classmate Raj Neervannan (founded 2008, launched 2011) to fix the research pain he felt as a banker. The AI market-intelligence platform bought rival Tegus for $930M in 2024 and in June 2026 raised $350M at a $7.5B valuation, passing $600M ARR.
interesting_fact: He talked Morgan Stanley into transferring him from London to Silicon Valley specifically so he could meet a future co-founder after his banking stint.
deep_cut_fact: Between Morgan Stanley and AlphaSense he spent about eight years (2000-08) building a semiconductor company, Silecs, with a friend from undergrad; it was acquired in 2014. He started his Wharton MBA in 2006 while still running it.
notes: Good podcast guest: has done Ted Seides' Capital Allocators podcast (https://www.alpha-sense.com/resources/research-articles/scaling-alphasense-jack-kokko-ted-seides-podcast). $7.5B round: https://alpha-sense.com/press/alphasense-raises-350m-at-7-5b-valuation-and-surpasses-600m-in-annual-recurring-revenue/

name: Raj Neervannan
current_role: Chief Technology Officer & Co-Founder, AlphaSense
profile: BITS Pilani-trained technologist who served as CEO/CTO at several software startups before a Wharton MBA, where he met ex-Morgan Stanley analyst Jack Kokko. In 2011 they co-founded AlphaSense, an AI/NLP-powered market-intelligence search platform for financial and corporate researchers, now valued in the multi-billions; he leads its technology and AI as CTO.
interesting_fact: AlphaSense grew out of the founders' own frustration at Wharton piecing together facts from scattered filings and reports - their benchmark question was always whether the product beat 'the next best thing, which is Google'.
deep_cut_fact: He has said that when he graduated from BITS Pilani he 'didn't know a lot about computing', but became hooked after spending weeks on a single algorithm problem - the lesson he took was that persistence on one problem unlocks a whole family of solutions.
notes: Title confirmed on AlphaSense About page (2026). Earlier roles per aggregator profiles: CTO at ePolicy Solutions (sold to ChoicePoint) and MajescoMastek, CEO of Framesoft - unverified by primary source. Good AI-search angle; route via AlphaSense media team.

name: Ruan Chenjie
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, Southchip Semiconductor Technology (Shanghai) Co. (SSE STAR: 688484)
profile: Ruan Chenjie (阮晨杰) founded Shanghai-based power-management chip designer Southchip in 2015 after leaving Texas Instruments. Southchip makes fast-charging, charge-pump, buck-boost and battery-management ICs for phones, laptops and cars, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023. Ruan is the controlling shareholder (~17%) and still runs the company.
interesting_fact: Southchip's customers include Xiaomi, Honor, OPPO, Vivo, Lenovo, Samsung and DJI, and it has joined Apple's supplier list. It is one of the few Chinese firms offering end-to-end fast-charging solutions.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Southchip, Ruan worked at Richtek and Texas Instruments. Within a year, Southchip shipped the SC8801, billed as the industry's first buck-boost charging chip supporting USB Type-C Power Delivery. Lei Jun's Shunwei Capital led its 2018 Series A, its first-ever chip-design investment.
notes: Hurun listed Southchip as a unicorn, but it has since listed publicly (STAR Market, 2023). There is no personal social presence; the best route is the company IR mailbox / board secretary's office. Chinese-language outreach is advisable.

name: Dave Rogenmoser
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Jasper (AI marketing platform), Austin TX
profile: Kansas-raised serial founder who co-founded Jasper, a generative-AI writing/marketing platform, in 2021; it hit unicorn status within ~18 months (valued $1.5B in 2022). He was CEO for its first two years, handed the CEO role to ex-Dropbox president Timothy Young in Sept 2023, and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Before Jasper, he co-founded Proof (YC W18), a 'social proof' widget that reached ~$220K in monthly recurring revenue and raised $2.2M before stalling; the same team pivoted into Jasper.
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Kansas, the biggest businessman he knew was 'a guy that owned a few Wendy's franchises.' He got into software after meeting future co-founder Chris Hull at a wedding, and his early ventures included fraternity-recruitment software and marketing agencies.
notes: No longer CEO since Sept 2023 (Timothy Young is CEO); chairman per Jasper's CEO announcement. Active on X and podcasts; X/LinkedIn is the most direct route.

name: Chris Hull
current_role: Co-founder, Jasper (Austin-based generative-AI marketing platform); exact current title unclear (variously listed as VP Customer Success / COO / strategic advisor)
profile: Chris Hull co-founded Jasper (originally Conversion.ai, then Jarvis) in January 2021 with Dave Rogenmoser and JP Morgan after years of small ventures together, including a marketing agency and the YC-backed social-proof tool Proof. Jasper built an early GPT-3 copywriting business that reached a ~$1.5B valuation; since 2023 it has been run by CEO Timothy Young with an enterprise focus.
interesting_fact: Jasper was originally named 'Jarvis' and had to rename after receiving a 'communication' from Disney (the 'Mouse House') over the Marvel-related name; the founders tell the story in a deleted scene from HubSpot/LinkedIn's 'Spiraling Up' documentary series.
deep_cut_fact: At 26 Hull was living in Atlanta in a $500-a-month internship, working through an online course on starting a software company; he reconnected with Rogenmoser at a rural Arkansas wedding among hay bales, and early on worked mornings at a Restoration Hardware warehouse while building their first businesses.
notes: Lower-profile than co-founder Dave Rogenmoser (the public face). Do not confuse with a different Chris Hull who co-founded Chicago ed-tech company Otus; some aggregators merge them. Best route is Jasper's press team.

name: J.P. Morgan
current_role: Co-founder of Jasper (AI marketing content platform, Austin TX); served as CTO, stepped back from the CTO role in Sept 2023 (current title unconfirmed)
profile: John Philip 'JP' Morgan co-founded Jasper (launched Feb 2021 as Conversion.ai, then Jarvis) with Dave Rogenmoser and Chris Hull, and built its technical architecture as CTO. Jasper raised $125M at a $1.7B valuation in Oct 2022. The trio previously co-founded YC-backed Proof (W18). Reports say he and Rogenmoser stepped back from day-to-day roles in Sept 2023.
interesting_fact: Before Jasper, Morgan, Rogenmoser and Hull set three goals: start a company (any company), make $6k/month to support their families, and keep their friendship above both. They shut down two failed SaaS companies before finding traction.
deep_cut_fact: The founders' digital marketing agency's very first client paid $300/month for SEO for a porta-potty rental company; they then spent three years running a marketing course business before going to YC with Proof.
notes: Not related to the bank J.P. Morgan; name searches are swamped by JPMorgan Chase results. Low public profile; current role after Sept 2023 not confirmed (Contrary Research: https://research.contrary.com/company/jasper). Best route likely via Jasper or co-founder Dave Rogenmoser.

name: Rob McGinnis
current_role: Founder & CEO, Prometheus Fuels (Santa Cruz, CA)
profile: Robert L. McGinnis is a scientist-inventor who founded Prometheus Fuels in 2019 to make carbon-neutral e-fuels from air-captured CO2 and renewable power. Previously co-founder/CTO of desalination startup Oasys Water and founder of Mattershift. In 2025 Prometheus pitched its tech as turning cheap solar into 24/7 baseload power for AI data centers.
interesting_fact: He is credited as co-inventor of the ammonia–carbon dioxide draw solution for forward-osmosis desalination, developed during his Yale PhD under Menachem Elimelech.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an engineer he was a playwright: he started at Cabrillo College and earned a Yale B.A. in Theater (2002) before switching to environmental engineering (M.S. 2007, Ph.D. 2009). Science profiled him as 'this former playwright'.

notes: info@ is the company's general inbox (no dedicated press email found); X/LinkedIn are company accounts. Very on-topic for energy + data centers: Prometheus now markets e-fuel-based baseload power for AI. US Navy EOD veteran per YC profile.

name: Gao Shixing
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, AISpeech (Suzhou)
profile: Cambridge-educated co-founder (2007, with Yu Kai and Lin Yuandong) of AISpeech, a Suzhou-based conversational-AI company whose voice tech runs in cars, smart offices and IoT devices. AISpeech refiled for a Shanghai STAR Market IPO in 2026 seeking ~1.56bn yuan, after a Jan 2026 share transfer valued it at ~6.4bn yuan; it also builds its own DFM large language models.
interesting_fact: AISpeech was among the first in China to target in-car voice: Gao predicted in 2018 that 30-50% of vehicles would have voice recognition by 2022, and smart mobility is now about 40% of AISpeech revenue.
deep_cut_fact: AISpeech was actually founded in the UK, and its first project was an intelligent computer terminal to help foreigners learn Chinese; it failed because the market was small and voice tech immature, before the team moved back to Suzhou.
notes: Born 1976; master's degrees from Cambridge (sources cite business management and computer science). Company is mid-IPO (STAR Market refiling, May 2026), so it may route media requests carefully. marketing@ is the general company email on the English site, not a personal one.

profile: Wang Pengcheng co-founded HiTHIUM in Xiamen in December 2019 and is its President and an executive director. The company makes LFP energy-storage cells and BESS systems; HiTHIUM says it ranked second globally in energy-storage battery shipments in 2025, delivering to 40+ countries. He leads its global expansion and Hong Kong IPO effort.

deep_cut_fact: On 11 April 2025 he was invited to speak as the energy-storage industry representative at Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez's meeting with Chinese entrepreneurs in Beijing, then held a closed-door session with Spain's ICEX trade agency.

Very relevant for energy-storage/data-center power angle. Best route: HiTHIUM media form.

current_role: Shareholder associated with HiTHIUM (Xiamen Hithium Energy Storage); spouse of founder/chairman Jeff Wu (Wu Zude)
profile: Lin Xiuhua (林秀華) is listed by Hurun as a founder of HiTHIUM, the Xiamen battery energy-storage maker founded in 2019. HiTHIUM's Hong Kong IPO filing describes her as the spouse of founder Jeff Wu; she held 82% of predecessor entity Zhuhai Haiheng at its 2019 formation before transferring her stake to Wu in 2021. name: Xu Xiaohua
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Anhui Huasun Energy Co. (Huasun)
profile: Xu Xiaohua (Jimmy Xu) is a former vice president and executive director of Hanergy Thin Film Power Group who founded Huasun Energy in Xuancheng, Anhui in 2020. He bet the company on heterojunction (HJT) solar cells; within about three years Huasun raised over RMB 5bn in 2023 and became the world's youngest PV unicorn and a leading HJT maker.
interesting_fact: Chinese media nicknamed him the 'HJT madman' (异质结狂人) for staking Huasun entirely on heterojunction technology while most of the industry chose TOPCon; Huasun ranked 12th on TIME's World's Top GreenTech Companies of 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He studied in the physics department of Beijing Normal University before entering solar at Hanergy, where he was named executive director of Hanergy Thin Film in 2016 after Li Hejun stepped down.
notes: Uses English name Jimmy Xu in Huasun press releases. Only general company inboxes found; no dedicated press email. Huasun is preparing an IPO.

name: Jiang Wenwu
current_role: Vice Chairman, Jiangsu Xinhua Semiconductor Technology Co. (鑫华科技); was Chairman from March 2022 to September 2025
profile: Jiang Wenwu (蒋文武) is a longtime GCL polysilicon executive who led Xinhua Semiconductor, China's largest maker of electronic-grade polysilicon for chip wafers. GCL's Zhongneng Silicon and China's Big Fund set up the company in 2015. Hurun valued it at about $1.16B in 2024. It filed for a STAR Market IPO in February 2026, and Jiang moved from chairman to vice chairman.
interesting_fact: Xinhua says it is the only domestic supplier delivering electronic-grade polysilicon at scale for 12-inch wafers. Its purity is 11N+ (only a handful of impurity atoms per trillion silicon atoms), and it holds about 62% of China's IC-grade market (2025).
deep_cut_fact: Jiang worked his way up inside GCL from senior manager to production VP, GM and then chairman of Zhongneng Silicon, and later president of GCL Tech's polysilicon division. Under his leadership, Xinhua's team ran 317 production trials and made 629 technical/equipment tweaks, using 70% domestic equipment, to solve impurity release.
notes: Hurun's 'founder' label is loose: Xinhua was incubated by GCL and the national Big Fund and has no controlling shareholder. Jiang is a professional manager whose personal stake is unclear. Since 2025, Nie Wei (CNBM-linked) is chairman and Tian Xin is GM/legal rep. No published contact found; the IPO prospectus on the SSE site is the place to look.

name: Zhuang Dan
current_role: Chairman, Changfei Advanced Semiconductor (YASC, Wuhan SiC power chips); Executive Director & President, Yangtze Optical Fibre and Cable (YOFC)
profile: A trained accountant who joined Wuhan-based YOFC's finance department in 1998, became CFO in 2001 and has been president since 2011. He chairs YOFC's silicon-carbide spinout Changfei Advanced Semiconductor (YASC), founded 2018, which raised a record CNY 3.8B round in 2023 for SiC power devices used in EVs and energy.
interesting_fact: YASC's CNY 3.8 billion (~US$519M) financing in June 2023 was reported as the largest private-equity round ever for SiC devices; YOFC itself is now pitching an 'AI-2030' strategy of fibre for AI data centres.
deep_cut_fact: He is a career finance man, not an engineer: bachelor's in auditing (1992) and master's in accounting (1995) from Wuhan University, a doctorate in accounting from Zhongnan University of Economics and Law (1998), then joined YOFC as assistant finance manager that same year.
notes: Hurun lists him as YASC founder; he is a professional manager at state-linked YOFC (Hong Kong/Shanghai listed). 'YASC' = Changfei Advanced (长飞先进) per CB Insights/Chinese press (chairman per cls.cn/10jqka reports). Best route is YOFC IR/media. Low public profile in English media.

name: Chen Nanxiang
current_role: Chairman (and CEO since Sept 2022) of Yangtze Memory Technologies Corp. (YMTC) and chairman of YMTC Holding; chairman of the China Semiconductor Industry Association since Oct 2023
profile: Chen Nanxiang is a veteran Chinese chip executive who spent about 18 years at China Resources Microelectronics (Wuxi) and was co-president of Tsinghua Unigroup before becoming chairman of Wuhan-based 3D NAND maker YMTC in 2021 and acting CEO in 2022. He has steered YMTC through US blacklisting in late 2022 and a 2025 holding-company restructuring ahead of a planned IPO amid AI-driven memory demand.
interesting_fact: Speaking as head of China's chip industry association in 2024, Chen predicted China's chip sector would see 'explosive growth' within three to five years and argued that advanced packaging may soon matter more than foundry technology.
notes: Listed as 'founder' but he is not YMTC's founder (founded 2016 under Tsinghua Unigroup; Simon Yang was founding CEO); he is chairman/CEO and a professional manager, so personal stake unclear. YMTC's contact page lists a general corporate inbox YMTC@ymtc.com (not a press-specific address). YMTC is on the US Entity List; consider compliance implications. Reported early career abroad (Fraunhofer, Max Planck) seen only on aggregators - unverified, not used.

name: Ma Daojie
current_role: Chairman, Unisoc (Shanghai) Technologies; Executive VP, New Unigroup (Tsinghua Unigroup); Vice Chairman, Unigroup Guoxin Microelectronics
profile: Ma Daojie (b. 1964) is a telecoms industry veteran appointed by Tsinghua Unigroup as chairman of Unisoc, China's largest mobile/IoT chip designer (ex-Spreadtrum), in June 2023, succeeding Wu Shengwu. He is a professional manager rather than Unisoc's founder; he previously held roles at China Unicom, China Telecom and Lenovo (VP) before joining Unigroup.

deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, senior engineer, DBA), Ma spent his early career in carrier operations, including deputy general manager of China Unicom's Guangxi branch, before moving to Lenovo as a vice president.
notes: Dataset label 'founder' is inaccurate: Ma is Unisoc's appointed chairman (since June 2023), not its founder; Unisoc is controlled by state-linked New Unigroup, so no personal stake/wealth confirmed. current_role: Chairman & CEO, xFusion Digital Technologies (超聚变), Zhengzhou, China
profile: Liu Hongyun (刘宏云; English materials call xFusion's chairman/CEO 'Jeffrey Liu') heads xFusion, the AI/x86 server maker spun out of Huawei in 2021 when Huawei transferred its x86 server R&D, patents and customers to it. He has led it from launch to reported 2025 revenue of RMB 58.2B; it hired CITIC Securities in 2025 to prepare an IPO.

deep_cut_fact: Before xFusion he ran Huawei's server business for the Asia-Pacific region, becoming general manager when xFusion was set up in September 2021 (it 'set sail' on Nov 5, 2021).

name: Li Ying
current_role: Former CEO, Xiaodu Technology (Baidu); reported to have left in Oct 2026. Previously Baidu Group VP and CIO
profile: Li Ying is a career Baidu technologist who joined via campus hiring in 2004. She worked on search NLP, then ran recommendation, knowledge graph and Baidu Maps, became Group CIO (2020) and VP, and in Oct 2023 took over Baidu's smart-device arm Xiaodu (valued ~$5B). She was hired, not a founder. Chinese media reported in Oct 2026 that she had left Xiaodu and Ruan Yu replaced her.
interesting_fact: She holds 30+ patents and won a first-class Science and Technology Progress Award from the Chinese Institute of Electronics. As Xiaodu CEO she pushed a 'scenario + AI + hardware' strategy built on Baidu's ERNIE models.
deep_cut_fact: In her first years at Baidu (2004-2011) she worked in the web search department on natural language processing, search relevance and even the 'spider' web crawler, before running Baidu Maps from March 2018.
